rows.original:
As hard as you fight back against the endless wave of elementals pouring out from the air above the old altar, you're steadily losing ground and the front is being pushed back closer and closer to Barney. No matter how fast the old wizard works, he simply isn't able to finish stabilising the area in time — seeing that you're about to be overrun, Cait is the first to break ranks, grabbing her father by the scruff of his neck and dragging him away from his instruments. [party.manyCompanions
        |[comp2.name] and you are
        |You're
    ] quick to follow, beating a fighting retreat to buy time for Cait to shepherd both Barney and Salwah out of the immediate area. The unstable elementals don't appear interested in Barney's arcane devices in the slightest, instead pursuing the lot of you and herding away from the temple ruins. As they reach the edges of the crumbled walls and fallen debris, though, the amorphous blobs of portal-power simply wink out of existence, there one moment and gone the next. Seeing the threat vanish, the lot of you lean again one of the many broken columns around and catch your breaths.
    
    "They must've run out of energy," Barney surmises in between wheezing and coughing. Walking he's good at, running less so. "Did you see how prone they were to exploding? Ah, the term 'unstable' doesn't even begin to do them justice — once they strayed too far from their source of sustainment, they just fizzled out like a light."
    
    "It's not going to stay that way, is it, Dad?"
    
    "No, no. My preliminary readings suggest their range will grow, first beyond the ruined temple and then... further. Yes, indeed. Though I can't say how far they'll ultimately be able to travel, it will certainly consume the village someday very soon." Regaining his composure, Barney fumbles for his pipe and lights it with the accompanying scent of spice smoke. "We'll have to try again."
    
    The old man's right — it's not something you can leave alone indefinitely and hope the problem goes away on its own. You'll have to come back up here sometime and finish the job... just not today. [party.names] are all tuckered out.
    
    "Come on, let's pick up Mr. Zethra's stuff and head back to the Hound," Salwah says, throwing one arm each over you and Cait. "We'll rest, have some fun... and then when we're all freshened back up we can head back here and complete the job for good. Right?"
    
    Right.
    
    Barney claps you on the back, although it's less than what you know he's capable of. "That's the spirit! Why don't Cait and you come and find me again when you're less scuffed-up and we'll come up again for another go? For now, though... there's still a whole mess to pick up. Can't leave all my tinkerings out in the open, I'm afraid..."
rows.translation:
尽管你竭力抵抗从古老祭坛上空不断涌出的那些元素生物，但你的防线仍在不断后退，前线正被一步步逼向巴尼所在的位置。无论那位老巫师动作多快，他都无法及时完成对该区域的稳定——眼看你们即将被彻底冲垮，凯特第一个脱离了阵型，她抓住父亲的后颈，把他从那些仪器旁拖走。 [party.manyCompanions
        |[comp2.name]和你都
        |你们
    ]迅速跟上，且战且退，为凯特争取时间，好让她把巴尼和萨尔瓦带离这片区域。那些不稳定元素体似乎对巴尼的奥术装置毫无兴趣，反而追着你们，把你们从神庙废墟中赶开。然而，当它们来到那些坍塌的墙壁和散落的瓦砾边缘时，那些由传送门能量构成的无定形团块却突然凭空消失了——前一刻还在那里，下一刻便不见踪影。看到威胁消失，你们一行人便又靠在周围一根断裂的柱子旁，喘着粗气。
    
    “它们的能量肯定耗尽了，”巴尼一边喘息、一边咳嗽着猜测道。走路他倒是擅长，跑步就不太行了。“你看到它们多么容易爆炸了吗？啊，‘不稳定’这个词根本不足以形容它们——一旦它们偏离维持自身的能量源头太远，就会像灯火一样噗地熄灭。”
    
    “这种情况不会一直持续下去吧，爸爸？”
    
    “不会的，不会的。我的初步读数表明，它们的活动范围会逐渐扩大，先是超出那座被毁的神庙，然后……更远。没错。虽然我说不准它们最终能走多远，但可以肯定，很快它们就会吞噬掉这个村庄。”巴尼重新镇定下来，摸索着拿出烟斗，点燃它，随之飘起一股香料烟味。“我们还得再试一次。”
    
    那位老人的说法是对的——这件事不能无限期地置之不理，指望问题会自行消失。你总有一天还得回到这里把这件事了结……只是不是今天。[party.names]都累坏了。
    
    “来吧，我们把泽特拉先生的东西拿上，然后回‘猎犬’旅馆去，”萨尔瓦说着，一只手臂搂住你，另一只搂住凯特。“我们休息一下，找点乐子……等我们都恢复精神了，再回到这里，把这件事彻底了结。对吧？”
    
    “对。”
    
    巴尼拍了拍你的背，不过这个动作其实远没有他真正有能力做到的那么用力。“就是这种精神！等你和凯特不那么狼狈了，再来找我吧，我们再一起上去试一次。不过，眼下……还有一大堆烂摊子要收拾。恐怕我不能把我捣鼓出来的那些小玩意儿就这么扔在外面……”
rows.raw:
"
    As hard as you fight back against the endless wave of elementals pouring out from the air above the old altar, you're steadily losing ground and the front is being pushed back closer and closer to Barney. No matter how fast the old wizard works, he simply isn't able to finish stabilising the area in time — seeing that you're about to be overrun, Cait is the first to break ranks, grabbing her father by the scruff of his neck and dragging him away from his instruments. [party.manyCompanions
        |[comp2.name] and you are
        |You're
    ] quick to follow, beating a fighting retreat to buy time for Cait to shepherd both Barney and Salwah out of the immediate area. The unstable elementals don't appear interested in Barney's arcane devices in the slightest, instead pursuing the lot of you and herding away from the temple ruins. As they reach the edges of the crumbled walls and fallen debris, though, the amorphous blobs of portal-power simply wink out of existence, there one moment and gone the next. Seeing the threat vanish, the lot of you lean again one of the many broken columns around and catch your breaths.
    
    "They must've run out of energy," Barney surmises in between wheezing and coughing. Walking he's good at, running less so. "Did you see how prone they were to exploding? Ah, the term 'unstable' doesn't even begin to do them justice — once they strayed too far from their source of sustainment, they just fizzled out like a light."
    
    "It's not going to stay that way, is it, Dad?"
    
    "No, no. My preliminary readings suggest their range will grow, first beyond the ruined temple and then... further. Yes, indeed. Though I can't say how far they'll ultimately be able to travel, it will certainly consume the village someday very soon." Regaining his composure, Barney fumbles for his pipe and lights it with the accompanying scent of spice smoke. "We'll have to try again."
    
    The old man's right — it's not something you can leave alone indefinitely and hope the problem goes away on its own. You'll have to come back up here sometime and finish the job... just not today. [party.names] are all tuckered out.
    
    "Come on, let's pick up Mr. Zethra's stuff and head back to the Hound," Salwah says, throwing one arm each over you and Cait. "We'll rest, have some fun... and then when we're all freshened back up we can head back here and complete the job for good. Right?"
    
    Right.
    
    Barney claps you on the back, although it's less than what you know he's capable of. "That's the spirit! Why don't Cait and you come and find me again when you're less scuffed-up and we'll come up again for another go? For now, though... there's still a whole mess to pick up. Can't leave all my tinkerings out in the open, I'm afraid..." 
    "

rows.translation: 下一步
观察者
凯特与巴纳福斯

rows.original: Time and again the elementals pouring out from the rents above the old altar beat down upon you, an endless horde of the amorphous masses of magic and lust rushing your position. [party.names] desperately hold the line, beating them back as long as your strength will hold out. All this while, Barney works away frantically, cranking his devices and fiddling with them — he said it would only take a minute or two, but as far as you're concerned fending off this onslaught might as well have taken hours. The air crackles and fills with a terrible chemical smell like Ivris's shop on a bad day, and then — — You swing your [pc.weapon] down upon empty air as the nearest unstable elemental winks out of existence. That's followed by another, and another, as the elementals are rolled back like a rug; from behind you, palpable pulses of thrumming energy surge from Barney's arcane devices, each one slamming against your back and threatening to send you stumbling forward onto your face. A quick glance over your shoulder has the elder catfolk huffing and puffing as he leans against his devices, wiping the sweat from his brow — the arcane implements are working on their own now, pulsing with esoteric magic. One by one, the orange-brown tears in the air above the old altar close up, and then the air is still save for the continuous whirring of Barney's machines. You can feel it, the tension in the air draining, and it's only now that you completely lower your weapon and rest easy. Yeah, it's finally over. "You did it, Dad!" Running up, Cait leaps into her father's arms and presses her body against his with a kitten-like nuzzle. "You're the best!" "Of course I did it," Barney replies, accepting his daughter's hug. "Am I not the most MAJOR of the minor prestidigitators, after all?" "And of course, [pc.name], Sally, [party.manyCompanions |[comp2.name], ]we couldn't have done it without you! So... the place is safe now, right Dad?" "It is, and it should stay that way for a good long time. Long enough for Garth to get some folks together and start building something proper on the site, at any rate. That's a bridge we'll have to cross when we get to it, but here and now we can start packing up and heading back to the Hound for a small celebration." The old cat-man gives you a weary nod and smile. "Thanks, [pc.name]. Thanks, Salwah. You've both been looking out for my daughter, and as her father I'm more grateful for that than you could possibly know." Hey, no sweat. You're just doing your job. "Same here!" "All right, all right. Time to start putting all this stuff away, and then a nice long drink and a smoke." Barney sighs happily. "Now, if you don't mind..."
rows.translation: 一次又一次，那些从古老祭坛上方的裂缝中涌出的元素力量不断地冲击着你，那些由魔法与欲望构成的无定形群体像无穷无尽的洪流一般，不断冲击着你的防线。[party.names]拼命坚守防线，只要还有力气，就继续击退他们的进攻。与此同时，巴尼也在疯狂地忙碌着，不停地操作他的设备、调整各种设置——他说只需要一两分钟就能完成，但对你来说，抵御这场攻势简直就像耗费了几个小时一样。空气中充满了刺耳的声响，还弥漫着一种难闻的化学气味，就像艾薇莉丝的店铺在糟糕的日子里散发出来的那种味道……然后—— ——你挥动你的[pc.weapon]一切仿佛都消失在虚无之中，因为那些最不稳定的元素们瞬间不复存在。接着，一个又一个元素也相继消失了，这些元素就像被卷起的地毯一样从你的周围消失殆尽。而从你身后，巴尼那些神秘的装置不断释放出强烈的能量波动，这些能量不断地冲击着你的背部，几乎让你踉跄着向前跌去。你随意瞥了一眼，就会看到那位年长的猫族正气喘吁吁地靠在那些装置上，擦拭着额头上的汗水——那些神秘的器具此刻正在自动运转，散发着晦涩难懂的魔力。一个接一个，老祭坛上空那些橙棕色的光点逐渐消失，空气中只剩下巴尼的机器发出的持续嗡嗡声。你能感觉到，空气中的紧张气氛正在慢慢消散，直到此刻，你才完全放下手中的武器，放松下来。是啊，终于结束了。 “你做到了，爸爸！”凯特跑过来，跳进父亲的怀里，像只小猫一样把身体贴在他身上，然后用鼻子轻轻蹭着他：“你是最棒的！” “你真的过程我做到了，”巴尼一边说，一边接受了女儿的拥抱。“我是不是最棒的主要角色毕竟，在那些水平较低的魔术师中，也是这样的吧？” “当然，[pc.name]，萨莉， [party.manyCompanions |[comp2.name]， ]没有你，我们根本不可能完成这件事！所以……现在那个地方已经安全了吧，对吧，爸爸？” “确实安全了，而且应该会保持这种安全状态很长一段时间。至少有足够的时间让加斯召集一些人，开始在那个地方真正建造一些东西。这是我们以后需要解决的问题，但现在我们可以开始收拾东西，回到‘猎犬号’去庆祝一下了。”那位老猫族疲惫地点了点头，然后笑了起来。“谢谢你们。[pc.name]谢谢你们，萨尔瓦。你们俩一直都在照顾我的女儿，作为她的父亲，我对你们的帮助感激不尽。” “别这么说，我们只是在尽自己的职责而已。” “我也是如此！” “好吧，好吧，是时候把这些东西收起来了，然后喝杯酒、抽根烟，放松一下了。”巴尼开心地叹道，“现在，如果你们不介意的话……

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original: You catch sight of a familiar portly shape standing outside Ogrish's workshop today, rustling a light-looking coinpurse back onto his belt. [party.has cait |Cait bounds over and throws her arms around her father |Cait's just coming out of the shop, too, giving her dad a big hug ], which earns his typically jovial laugh and a scritch between the ears. [party.has cait | "Daddy!" Cait giggles, giving him one more squeeze. "What're you doing at Ogrish's place?" "Ah, investigating a few potential buys," he blusters. "Nothing you need concern yourself with, my dear. Nothing dangerous!" | "What're you two up to?" you ask, nodding towards the smithy. "Oh, we were just checking some things out," Cait says coyly, lacing her fingers together behind her back. "Daddy commissioned him for some new doohickies for one of his experiments." Barney puffs out his cheeks. "A gimbal is hardly a doohickey, Caitriss!" ] You're joined a moment later by the smith himself, wiping soot from his brow on the back of a rag. The orc towers over the pair of catfolk in his door, chest and shoulders above the elder statesmen of the two, but he carries himself with an easygoing air that makes him hardly seem his size. The smith cleans his hand off before putting it on Cait's shoulder, but he addresses you all together. "Say, [pc.isFeline |kittens |[pc.name], kitten, ] I just thought a thought." Cait giggles. "Had to run all the way out here to share the news?" "Yeah, actually." He snorts, rolling his eyes at the friendly dig. "Listen, the two of you've been staying in town a while, yeah? Done a lot for the place while you've been here, with the whole logging camp thing and the crazy plant lady. Baroness [carmen.around|doesn't|never did] collect tax, really, but everybody ought to pitch in now'n then for their community I reckon." "Just so, my good lad," Barney nods. "If only more people thought that way, the world would be an eminently better place I'd say." Ogrish scratches at his cheek, glancing away. "Anyway, the wife'n I have been tinkering with some things, figured we'd offer 'em up for use. Think I've got something that looks to fit you pretty well, Cait. Might got something you'd get use outta too, [pc.name]." "Aw, that's sweet," Cait starts to say, then gasps. "Wait, wife? You never mentioned you were married!" Ogrish grins like he's about to say something crass, but a glance at Barney makes him pause. "Eh, yeah, a village can only stomach so many lonely old men, figured I ought to tie the knot. About a year 'fore you all got here. So, wanna come see, or what?" You shrug. "Sure. What've you got for us?"
rows.translation: 今天，你看见一个熟悉的圆胖身影站在奥格瑞什的工坊外，将一个看似轻飘飘的钱袋沙沙作响地重新系回腰带。[party.has cait |凯特蹦跳着跑过去，一把抱住父亲 |凯特也刚从店里出来，给父亲一个大大的拥抱 ]；巴尼发出一贯爽朗的笑声，还挠了挠她的耳间。 [party.has cait | “爸爸！”凯特咯咯笑着，又紧紧抱了他一下。“你在奥格瑞什这里做什么？” “啊，我只是在考察几件或许值得购买的东西，”他故作豪迈地说道。“没什么需要你担心的，亲爱的。没有危险！” | “你们两个在忙什么？”你朝铁匠铺点点头，问道。 “哦，我们只是来看看几样东西，”凯特故作神秘地说，双手在背后十指相扣。“爸爸委托他为某项实验制作了几件新奇玩意儿。” 巴尼鼓起双颊。“万向节才不是什么新奇玩意儿，凯特丽丝！” ] 片刻之后，铁匠本人也加入了你们；他用抹布背面擦去额头上的煤灰。兽人站在自家门口，高高耸立在两个猫族身前，胸膛与肩膀都超过两人中年长者的头顶；不过他举止随和，让人几乎意识不到他有多么魁梧。铁匠先把手擦干净，才将它搭到凯特肩上，不过他同时对你们说道：“嘿，[pc.isFeline |小猫们 |[pc.name]，还有小猫， ]我刚想到一件事。” 凯特咯咯一笑。“所以你一路跑出来，就为了宣布这个消息？” “还真是。”面对友善的调侃，他哼了一声，翻翻白眼。“听着，你们两个在镇上待了有一阵，对吧？这段时间为这里做了不少事，又是伐木营地，又是那个疯狂的植物女人。卡门女男爵[carmen.around|现在基本不|过去也从不]收税，不过我觉得每个人偶尔都该为自己的社区出份力。” “正是如此，好小伙，”巴尼点点头。“要是更多人都这么想，我敢说世界一定会美好得多。” 奥格瑞什挠着脸颊，移开视线。“总之，我和妻子一直在捣鼓些东西，想着不妨拿出来给人用。我觉得有件东西应该很适合你，凯特。或许也有东西能让你派上用场，[pc.name]。” “噢，真贴心，”凯特刚开口，随即倒吸一口气。“等等，妻子？你从没说过自己结婚了！” 奥格瑞什露出一副即将说出粗俗玩笑的坏笑，可瞥见巴尼后又停了下来。“呃，是啊，一个村子容不下太多孤单老男人，我觉得自己也该成家了。大概在你们到这里的一年前。那么，你们到底要不要进来看看？” 你耸耸肩。“当然。你给我们准备了什么？”

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original: He waves you all into the workshop, and then out the back. There's a narrow alley connecting the shops between the two main streets, and he heads for the back of Ivris's building and opens the back door up. "So," he says as you all enter. "I've let the chest of a suit of scale out to about your size, Cait, and Ivris's got a spellbook she thinks you'll be interested in. Something-" "Something I've had since a looooong time before I got to the north," the elf says, carefully descending the shop's narrow stairs. "It's not like I'm getting much use out of it, right?" She's got a pink-bound tome tucked under an arm, its cover threaded with gold and its pages looking to be done just as richly. "This belonged to my dad ages back. He used to be a lay brother of the Prince's church, actually, before he met my mom. Sort of like yourself, I understand." [var0 |"Well," Cait chuckles, "not so lay anymore. I'm a bonafide temple mistress now, thanks to [pc.name]." "Oh!" Ivris says, setting the book down. "Oggy mentioned the new temple going up. You'll forgive us if we aren't frequent parishioners, I hope, but..." "It's fine. I know it's not for everyone. And Brother Sanders keeps the village's spiritual needs tended to just as well." The elf inclines her head. Antlers brush against hanging bags of alchemical goods, jingling gaily. "Still, it's good to know that brothers and sisters of my father's faith have a place to call their own around here. But, that's not why we got you both these goodies, is it?" |"Just like," Cait smiles. "I'd have never guessed, Lady Ivris." The elf waves her hand. "Oh, don't you start 'lady'ing me too. That was a long time ago indeed." "Once a lady always a lady," Ogrish says. Ivris makes a disgruntled noise in the back of her throat. "Not you too, Oggy." "My apologies, Magistrix." "Ugh!" Ivris sets the book down on the table. "Somebody wants to sleep out in the cold tonight. Buuut that's also definitely not what we're here to talk about, is it?" ] Ivris drums her fingers on the tome, and rather than the familiar thump of a book cover, you could swear you hear the ring of glass beneath her fingers. Or maybe a gemstone. "This tome belonged to your church a long time ago, Cait, and I think it's high time it went back into service. I frankly couldn't tell you what's in it anymore, but I can say it carries an enchantment harder than diamond. Meant for a crusader's arm, I'd say. Wear some armor, and you can sling your spells in the heart of a brawl without a fear." "That's... wow," Cait says, gently picking up the book. It clearly has some heft to it, making her biceps flex as she draws it to her chest. "Thank you, L— Miss Ivris! I don't know what to say." Ivris hesitantly reaches out, finding first Cait's shoulder, and then her cheek. "Just promise you'll keep protecting this town against the demons, won't you? At least until this crisis is over with." "And as for you, [pc.name]," Ogrish says, planting a foot on Ivris's workbench and pushing himself up into her hanging inventory. "Well, Ivy's got just the thing." "Mmhm," Ivris nods, flashing you a pretty smile. "Well, it was Oggy's idea, really. I've had this sitting around for ages, and thank Nareva I've never had need of it. Goddess knows it came close a few times," she says, rubbing at her blindfold as her husband finally finds what he was looking for — a small, wooden box. "Nobody doubts your prowess around here," Ogrish says, presenting it. "But that's just another reason maybe you ought to take this. We'd all hate to have something happen to you while you're out there with your ass on the line for us." "So a little safeguard is the least we can do. It's rare as hen's teeth, though, so try not to need it!" You crack open the box, and find a philter of colorless liquid inside, in which drift flecks of radiant gold. A heaviness settles over your heart when you stare amongst them, a certainty they'll soon fade away to nothing, all that beauty callously lost to the aether — until Ogrish closes the hinge again. The sensation recedes as soon as it began. Ivris feels her way over to you and puts her hand on his atop the box. "These are said to be the tears of Sancta Kaelirra. If you believe the stories, she gave her life to protect a woman like me from a bloodthirsty mob during the Godswar, when commonfolk lashed out against anything they didn't understand like cornered hounds. True or no, this potion will snap someone back from the brink of death, preserving life from all but the most horrific wounds. It might just save your life — or a friend's."

rows.original:
"Aha, that old thing? Yes, yes indeed she did! I'm very proud of my little sunflower for having the restraint to avoid touching something as darkly twisted as it, even if it might have a little power lurking inside. I know how much you love your spells, Caitriss. And of you, my dear [pc.boyGirl], for having the same sense. Here, I understand it cost you a fair bit to acquire it in the first place, no? Allow me to cover it, at least."

    The plump cat produces a similarly rotund coin purse from his belt and plops it into your hand — one far heftier than it cost you to buy the tome. 
    
    "And as for you, sunflower," he says, turning to Cait, "let me offer you a consolation prize for the spells you'll never learn. A trinket I've been working on for a while now in my free time. I think it might just suit you."
    
    Barney's fingers wiggle, and suddenly there's a copper ring between them. Cait giggles as he deftly places it onto one of her fingers, and then her eyes go wide. "It's so warm!"
    
    "Yes, just so!" Barney laughs. "You've been complaining about the cold ever since we arrived, dear. I hope this helps to shake off the Marcher chill, just a bit!"
    
    Cait gives you a look, eyes bright. "Leave it to my dad to make a magic ring just to keep me warm. You know, most parents would just buy me a sweater!"
    
    Barney makes a dismissive gesture. "Bah, where's the fun in that? Leave that to Randa and her obsession with ugly holiday garments. I'm sure even out here in the boonies she'll find a way to get a courier to us laden down with them for the solstice festival."
    
    Cait gives her dad a big hug. "Thanks, dad." 
    
    "You should thank [pc.name] for having the good sense to cut [pc.hisHer] losses on that book," he says. 
    
    You get a big hug too.
rows.translation:
“啊哈，就是那个老东西？没错，她确实这么做了！我为我家的小向日葵感到非常骄傲——她有足够的自制力，没有去碰那种如此邪恶、扭曲的东西，尽管那东西里面可能隐藏着某种力量。我知道你有多喜欢你的法术，凯特丽丝。我也同样为你骄傲，我亲爱的[pc.boyGirl]，因为你有同样的判断力。来，我听说你当初得到它花了不少钱，对吧？至少让我替你补上这笔钱吧。”

    那只胖乎乎的猫从腰带上取出一个同样圆鼓鼓的钱包，然后把它塞到了你的手里——这个钱包的价值，远远超过了你购买那本典籍所花费的金额。 
    
    “至于你，向日葵，”他转向凯特说道，“既然你永远也学不会那些法术，那就让我送你一个安慰奖吧。这是我这些空闲时间一直在制作的小玩意儿，我觉得它可能会很适合你。”
    
    巴尼的手指动了动，突然之间，他的指间出现了一枚铜戒指。凯特咯咯笑了起来，而他熟练地将戒指戴在了她的手指上，随后她的双眼瞪得大大的：“好暖和啊！”
    
    “没错，就是这么暖和！”巴尼笑着说，“亲爱的，自从我们来到这里，你就一直在抱怨天气太冷。希望这个魔法戒指能帮你稍微驱散一些边境的寒意吧！”
    
    凯特用明亮的眼神看着你：“我爸爸果然厉害，连一个能让我保暖的魔法戒指都能做出来。你知道，大多数父母都会直接给我买件毛衣的！”
    
    巴尼不屑地摆了摆手：“哼，那有什么意思？这种事就留给兰达和她对那些难看节日服装的痴迷吧。我敢肯定，就算是在这种偏远的地方，她也会想办法让信使满载着那些衣服，赶在至日节时给我们送来。”
    
    凯特紧紧拥抱了她的父亲：“谢谢你，爸爸。” 
    
    “你该感谢[pc.name]足够明智，及时止住了[pc.hisHer]在那本书上的损失，”他说。 
    
    你也会得到一个热情的拥抱。

"That's a fun one," Berwyn chuckles, "So, I was born to a family of farmers as you often are around here. Guess what though? I was good at magic. We had some books around that used to belong to my grandpa in the old farmhouse, and they were actually spell tomes, turns out grandpa was a mage and my parents never told me. He wasn't just some ordinary hermit mage either or anything like that. He was a battlemage! Apparently, grandpa was a pretty integral part to his lord's court, but he got tired of all the fighting and politics. I even found some old rumors that he killed a dragon at some point! That's the thing though, of all the history books I've read the only things I've found about him are from my parents or rumors. My parents said once he left his lord's court, he didn't want to be a mage any more, or anyone to know who he was, and since he was friends with his lord, he had him wipe all his records clean of any mention of grandpa, so he could live as a 'normal' person." 
    
    He rolls his eyes at that and continues his story, "So naturally, after hearing all that about grandpa, I started learning magic and wanted to learn more, but mom and dad didn't approve."

    "Oh!" he suddenly interjects, "I don't know if you've figured this out or not, but my mom's lupine and my dad's [silly|a furry|human]. Anyway, I did what any self-respecting, angry, farm-raised half-breed would do and abandoned home in the night." 

    Sounds like Berwyn to you.

    "It wasn't long before Miss Matiha found me after that, and she took me in and started teaching me all I wanted to know about magic. It was always strange how I had never heard of her before, especially since I ran into her not too far from my home, but I never questioned it." He looks to you now. "Of course, you know how all of that turned out in the end, but for a while it was nice, learning and training with someone as knowledgeable as her, and as her only apprentice no less!" 

    "Beyond all that though," he continues, now counting fingers on one of his paws, "I like runes, books about boats — I hate actual boat rides though — and I like most foods with cheese melted on top. Not much else to tell."

    Well, that's a pretty succinct summary of Berwyn if you ever needed one.

    他翻了个白眼，继续讲述：“于是很自然地，听完爷爷的事以后，我便开始学习魔法，还想学得更多，可爸爸妈妈并不赞成。”

    听起来确实是贝尔温会做的事。

    “没过多久，玛蒂哈小姐就找到了我；她收留我，开始传授我想知道的一切魔法知识。我以前居然从未听说过她，这一直很奇怪，尤其是因为我遇见她的地方离家并不远，但我从未质疑。”他此刻看向你。“当然，你知道这一切最终如何收场；不过有那么一段时间，能向她那般博学的人学习、与她一同训练，感觉确实很好——而且我还是她唯一的学徒！”

    “除此之外，”他继续说，一边掰着一只爪子上的手指数起来，“我喜欢符文、有关船只的书——不过讨厌真正坐船——还喜欢大多数上面融有奶酪的食物。没有太多别的可说。”

rows.original: You give another quick look around [atCamp|the confines of your camp|the Frost Hound] one last time before you give up your search there. [atCamp|Your next best bet is to search the area immediately around your camp, and you head out into the wilderness surrounding you. Traveling outwards, you can hear something faint from behind a piece of scenery blocking your line of sight|Instead of checking the rest of Hawkethorne, you decide to check behind the bar first. To your surprise, as you near the back door away from the rabble of the inn, you can hear muffled noises coming from the other side]. Every now and then you hear what sounds like a hammer banging on an anvil, followed by a somewhat familiar voice, and from what you can tell, the voice is not a happy one. As you [atCamp|round the large boulder blocking your path|open the door and step out back], you see Berwyn. He has a small pyre of burning coals before him, a thin pillar of smoke wafting into the air. The mage curses quietly and shakes his head, then takes a deep breath. He stands up straight and holds his staff in front of him with both hands. After a moment of quiet, the air in front of the summoner begins to shift, billowing slightly and blowing his robes back. A small whirlwind slowly forms above Berwyn's pyre, whistling like a breeze. You can see something glowing at the heart of the swirling air, burning a bright orange like embers as sparks are caught in the whirlwind. Your companion's arms begin to tremble as this ritual of his continues, and his spell seems to falter. The wind begins to slow and its glowing heart grows fainter by the second. Eventually, the whirlwind dissipates with an oddly metallic sound ringing out. Berwyn drops his staff carelessly on the ground and sighs. You walk a bit closer to the distraught magician and ask him what he's doing. He jumps slightly at the sound of your voice, giving you a slightly irritated glance over his shoulder. "Practicing," he answers bluntly. Berwyn kneels down and places a couple of dry twigs on his fire. Wondering what's causing him so much trouble, you ask him what exactly he's practicing. The girly mage gives an exasperated sigh before he briefly explains himself, "Summoning ritual... for a fire elemental." Wait, you've seen Berwyn conjure not just one, but two hulking stone elementals at once. How could this spell be giving him any issues? "Getting your spirit and will to inhabit a body of fire is different," he says, his voice monotone and tired, "Earth is all around you, and it's tied to every living thing you see. So it and life are intertwined, already has a connection that makes it easier to draw an elemental away from its elemental lord." He stand back up and turns to you, "Fire is different: it feeds on life to have its own. It needs air and has its own... well... spirit that needs to be pulled and channeled and maintained." Berwyn walks his way over to a short stack of books atop a small blanket and grabs the one that's open. "These are the tomes I still have from my time with Matiha," he explains, glancing at the pages, "I figured it'd be a good idea to teach myself some more practical spells for when she comes back. I'm no prodigy though so I either need someone to teach me, or I need books, and since there's no one around Hawkethorne who could train me in what I want to know... that kind of leaves me with one option." Berwyn's demeanor seems to take a quick turn as he continues, his brow curling downwards with anger and his grip on the tome tightening. "Guess what?" he asks rhetorically, turning towards you for a moment before he continues. "All this time," he says, gritting his teeth, "She's been giving me books to impede how fast I learn spells." The half-breed begins to breathe heavily, "I don't know how I didn't see it before... all this fucking gibberish she wrote down and false information she gave... she was trying to keep me weak." He begins to shake with anger, baring his teeth so his sharp canines seems much more predatory than cute. "That fucking bitch," he murmurs, "All that time I spent in that tower doing what she said..." Your companions voice begins to rise, "That bitch..." His eyes suddenly go wide with rage as he starts screaming, almost tearing the book in half, "THAT FUCKING BITCH!" The half-breeds words soon become indecipherable grunting and yelling as he tears away at the pages of the tome. Berwyn looks like he might pass out if he keeps going like this, so you quickly step over to him and [pc.isDK|grab him by the shoulders, shaking him back and forth while telling him to snap out of it|place a hand on his shoulder and ask him to calm down]. You seem to get Berwyn out of his rage with that. He's still trembling with anger but has stopped his book-destroying rampage. [pc.isDK|Not loosening your grip on the ferocious half-breed, you tell him he needs to stop before he hurts someone|Loosening your grip on his shoulder, you ask the angry half-breed to stop before he hurts himself]. His chest heaves for a moment, his brow still furrowed with anger. He takes a deep breaths, and tosses his now unreadable tome onto the ground. You look Berwyn over quickly; he seems fine physically, but he definitely needs to take a break from this, and you tell him such. He sighs heavily, and gazes down at his discarded staff before taking it up again. The disgruntled mage looks back and forth between you and his pyre for a moment before finally speaking, "Yeah..." You tell Berwyn you'll walk with him back to his [atCamp|tent|room].

    [party.has berwyn|Berwyn is already at your side, holding your [pc.hand], running a hand [pc.hasHair|through your [pc.hair]|across your scalp] and speaking words of encouragement in your ear.]
    
    It's a painful process that almost feels like it will last forever, but with the help of Gwyn[flags.CAIT_RECRUITED| and Cait], your pain is eased. The hours are still filled with pain, grunting, strain, and more yelling that leaves all in attendance exhausted.
    
    Finally, you're informed by Gwyn a head with two fluffy ears has appeared between your legs, followed by a body, two legs, and two itty-bitty feet.
    
    You thought a modicum of relief might come to you after all that, but that's only one of your coming litter. So, you must repeat the process one[var0|, if not more] time[var0|s] to birth your children. But, after the first of your young emerges and is carefully cleaned and swaddled, the rest come easy... or easier, at least.
rows.translation:
哦不。

    你的腹部突然一阵剧痛，几乎疼得你站不起来，汗水浸湿了你的双腿。你紧紧抓住自己隆起的腹部，弯下腰来，这才意识到发生了什么。 
    
    [atFH|对你来说，幸运的是，你只需步行一小段距离就能找到格温以及她所擅长的领域。|[party.som|你设法呼救，得到了镇上一些人的帮助，一起走到了格温的育儿室。|[companion.name]注意到你的困难后，迅速前来帮助你，带你走向格温的婴儿房。|你的同伴注意到了你的困境，迅速前来帮助你，陪你走向格温的婴儿房。]]
    
    仿佛过了漫长的时间，你终于来到了产房，很快就被安置在一张舒适的床上，双腿被分开，准备开始分娩。 
    
    [party.has berwyn|贝尔温已经站在你身边，守护着你。[pc.hand]轻轻一抚[pc.hasHair|通过你的方式[pc.hair]|从头到脚]并在你耳边说着鼓励的话语。]
    
    这是一个痛苦的过程，感觉似乎会永远持续下去，但在格温的帮助下[flags.CAIT_RECRUITED| 还有凯特]你的痛苦暂时得到了缓解。然而，接下来的几个小时里，你依然会不断地感到疼痛、发出呻吟声、身体会持续处于紧张状态，而且还会有人不断地喊叫，这让在场的所有人都精疲力竭。
    
    最后，格温告诉你：在你的两腿之间出现了一个长着两只毛茸茸耳朵的小脑袋，紧接着，一个身体、两条腿以及两只小小的脚也出现了。
    
    你原本以为经历了这一切之后，自己总该得到一些缓解了吧，但实际上，这只不过是你即将迎来的一窝幼崽中的第一个而已。因此，你还得再次重复这个过程[var0|甚至更多]时间[var0|]生下你的孩子们。但是，当第一个孩子出生后，经过仔细的清洁和包裹，接下来的孩子就会变得容易多了……至少会更容易一些。

rows.original:
By the time all is said and done, you've birthed a litter of [var0] healthy pups, now quietly sleeping in your arms and swaddled and warm cloth. Berwyn sits beside you in bed, holding one of your newborn babies, smiling at it, and at you.

        "Not gonna lie," he says after minutes of silent amazement, "I was pretty nervous about all of this." He brushes a finger across his pup's sleeping face. "I'm not sure if it was just instinct or something that made me, you know, knock you up, but I'm glad I did it now, looking at these little guys." He pauses. "I think... I think it'll be nice to have something I'm fighting for now... o-other than you, I mean. I'll be thinking about all of you a lot from now on..."
        
        Berwyn lets out a long, contented sigh. "I think I'm going to move back to my parents’ farm with these guys once all this is over... if that's okay with you of course." He grins after saying that.
        
        You tell him you think that sounds wonderful, and that you might just have to go with him.
        
        Both of you smile warmly at each other's words.
        
        "Yeah... I think things are gonna turn out all right," Berwyn sighs, pressing his nose to one of his pups'. "Don't you, little guy?"
        
        Sitting here now, pups in hand with their father, you do think things will turn out okay, and you can enjoy that feeling for as long as it lasts...
rows.translation:
当一切尘埃落定之时，你其实已经生下了一窝[var0]只健康的幼崽，此刻正安静地躺在你的怀里，被柔软的布包裹着，温暖而舒适。贝林就坐在你床边，抱着你其中一个新生儿，微笑着看着它，也看着你。

        “说实话，”在静静欣赏了它们几分钟之后，他说，“我对这一切其实挺紧张的。他用手指轻轻触碰着小狗熟睡的脸庞。‘我不确定，这是出于本能还是别的什么原因，让我做出了那个决定——让你怀孕，但现在看到这些小家伙，我真的很高兴自己当时那么做了。’他停顿了一下，接着说道：‘我想是这样吧。我觉得现在有自己为之奋斗的目标会很不错……当然，除了你之外。从现在开始，我会经常想起你们所有人……”
        
        贝林长舒了一口气，脸上露出了满足的表情：“我想等这一切结束后，我就和这些朋友们一起回到我父母的农场去生活。当然，如果你没意见的话。”他说完之后露出了微笑。
        
        你告诉他，你觉得这个主意听起来很棒，或许你真的应该跟他一起去。
        
        你们俩听到对方的话后，都温暖地笑了起来。
        
        嗯……我觉得一切都会好起来的，”贝尔温叹了口气，把鼻子贴在其中一个小狗的脸上，“你说呢，小家伙？”
        
        现在，你坐在这里，手里抱着父亲的小狗们，你确实相信一切都会好起来，而且你可以尽情享受这种感觉，直到它消失为止……

卡门

rows.original:
As you march through the gates, Etheryn holds out a leather-clad hand to the air. Her great war-falcon wings down from the battlements and perches on her, shaking itself out with a particularly loud screech that echoes off the castle's old stone walls.
    
    "We finally made it, Harrick," Ryn says with a smile, running a thumb over the bird's chest. "Cross your talons that the baroness will hear me out, hmm?"
    
    [party.has atugia|"She will!" Atugia assures her, "Carmen's a reasonable gal... most of tha time..."|You put a hand on Ryn's shoulder and tell her she'll do fine.] 

    It seems like the hawk's screaming is better than knocking on the huge wooden door opposite the gate; it shudders and begins to open a scant few moments before you even reach it. [
        flags.TODO_CARMEN_MARRIED
        |Your wife saunters out with a faint smile on her lips, extending her arms to you. "Welcome back, my [pc.mascFem|husband|wife]. What brings a screeching hawk to our door now?"
        |[flags.ATUGIA_RECRUITED 
            |The baroness steps out from the shadowy hall. She is [flags.CARMEN_MET|much as you remember her from the last time you met: ]a tall and willowy woman, save for a broad set of hips, clad in an old-fashioned dress in black and red. She regards you cooly, arms folded in front of herself. 
    
            "I don't remember summoning anyone today," she says evenly. "So. To what do I owe the pleasure?"
            |Atugia steps out first, holding the door open as the baroness herself appears. She's [flags.CARMEN_MET|much as you remember her from the last time you met: ]a tall and willowy woman, save for a broad set of hips, clad in an old-fashioned dress in black and red. She regards you cooly, arms folded in front of herself. 
    
            "I don't remember summoning anyone today," she says evenly. "So. To what do I owe the pleasure?"
        ]
    ]
    
    "I, uhm," Etheryn [etheryn.lnhConfidence|shuffles her feet awkwardly, until Harrick stamps his little hawk-feet on her glove and pecks at her. "Gah! I, uh, h-hello, your ladyship... I-I am, uh, E-Etheryn of... of, uh, H-House R-R-Ridell, a-and-"

    "Get it together girl. Deep breaths," the baroness sighs. "My patience is far more limited than my time."
    
    Ryn gulps audibly. "I-I am Princess Etheryn var Ridell, of t-the Winter City. By ancient t-treaty, I humbly request sanctuary in Castle Hawkstone!"|takes a deep breath, concentrating on her words rather than the steely gaze of the noblewoman before her. "I am Etheryn var Ridell, princess of the Winter City. By a-ancient treaty, I humbly request sanctuary here at Castle Hawkstone."|takes a deep breath, steadies herself, and looks the baroness in the eye. "I am Etheryn var Ridell, princess of the Winter City. By ancient treaty, I humbly request sanctuary here at Castle Hawkstone."]
    
    The baroness raises a narrow brow. "A lady of the Ridell family this far south? I thought the boer'alvar had died out long ago. Why have you come seeking my protection, young princess. And where are your guards? I doubt your king would thrust you out all alone, even in exile."
    
    "I am [etheryn.lnhConfidence|alone," Ryn whines. "A-and we have no... no king. Just m-my sister, Alissa. And she's... she, uh... well... she's evil. I ran away.|here unescorted. M-my sister, Queen Alissa, she... she's turned evil. A wicked tyrant. I escaped south as soon as I could.|not alone!" Ryn says proudly, taking your hand in hers. "And we have no king. Just a wicked tyrant of a queen, whose heart has turned as black as soot! I ran from the city, but my people are in peril still. Please, I need your help.]"
    
    Taking a few steps closer, the baroness fixes Ryn in her gaze, eyes wandering over the princess's features. "So a runaway, then. But you're not just here as a refugee, are you — you want my help in retaking the city from your evil sister, is that right?"
    
    Ryn shuffles awkwardly.

    "Relax, child." Carmen smiles. "First, allow me to properly introduce myself; I doubt your people have seen a Belharan noble since the Godswar. I am Baroness Carmen Reverra. Unfortunately, Belhar is no more; a memory from a bygone age, and with it, much of my power. There are [flags.ATUGIA_RECRUITED|two|three] people living in this castle, and one of them is a gargoyle. I could not offer you the hospitality and comfort befitting a princess, and I certainly have no resources to put at your disposal to retake a city many miles from here. The Marcher Barons' armies were destroyed utterly in the war, and I am already resorting to mercenaries to keep the roads clear... and many of them have simply become bandits or worse anyway."

    You watch Etheryn's shoulders slump, and her hands fall to her side. Harrick screeches and flaps, catching himself before Ryn just dumps him on the cobblestones and taking wing back towards the castle tower. 
    
    Carmen sighs and takes another guarded step forward, reaching a hand out to take Ryn's cheek. "I am sorry, princess, but your four-century-old treaty was with an empire that doesn't exist anymore. And I simply haven't the power to help you, even were I to honor it. But I will not turn away a lady in need; I will talk to Garth, the man who keeps the village inn, and make sure that the best rooms he has are made available to you and all your needs are met. You may stay within my barony as long as you need. That is, I'm afraid, the only boon I can offer you."
    
    Ryn turns to you with wide, teary eyes. Oh no.
rows.translation:
当你穿过大门时，伊瑟琳将一只裹着皮革的手伸向空中。她那巨大的战鹰翅膀从城墙上展开，落在了她的肩上，伴随着一声特别响亮的尖叫，振翅抖动，声音在城堡古老的石墙上回荡。

“我们终于成功了，哈里克，”小琳微笑着说，用拇指轻轻抚摸着那只鸟的胸膛，“希望女男爵能听我讲完，嗯？
    
    [party.has atugia|她一定会做到的！”阿图吉娅向她保证，“卡门通常是个通情达理的女孩……大多数时候都是这样……|你把手放在小琳的肩上，告诉她她一定会没事的。] 

    看来，那鹰的叫声比敲击大门对面的那扇巨大的木门还要有效——在你刚刚走到门前时，那门就已经开始缓缓打开了。 [
        flags.TODO_CARMEN_MARRIED
        |你的妻子微笑着走出来，伸开双臂迎接你：“欢迎回来，我的[pc.mascFem|丈夫|妻子]现在，是什么让那只发出尖锐叫声的鹰飞到了我们的门口呢？
        |[flags.ATUGIA_RECRUITED 
            |女男爵从那阴暗的大厅中走了出来。她[flags.CARMEN_MET|无论你对她上一次见面时的印象如何： ]那是一位身材高挑、体态纤细的女性，只是臀部较为宽厚，她穿着一件红黑相间的老式连衣裙。她双臂交叉在胸前，冷冷地注视着你。

“我不记得今天召唤过任何人，”她平静地说道，“那么……我究竟有什么荣幸能见到您呢？
            |阿图吉娅首先走了出来，将门撑开，随后女男爵本人出现了。她[flags.CARMEN_MET|无论你对她上次见面时的印象如何： ]那是一位身材高挑、体态纤细的女性，只是臀部较为宽厚，她穿着一件红黑相间的老式连衣裙。她双臂交叉在胸前，冷冷地注视着你。

“我不记得今天召唤过任何人，”她平静地说道，“那么……我究竟有什么荣幸能见到您呢？
        ]
    ]
    
    我，呃……”伊瑟琳[etheryn.lnhConfidence|她尴尬地挪动着脚步，直到哈里克用他那双像鹰爪一样的小脚踩在她的手套上，还啄了她一下。“啊！我，呃，你好，夫人……我，我是里德尔家族的伊瑟琳……”

“振作点，姑娘。深呼吸。”女男爵叹了口气，“我的耐心可比时间有限多了。”

伊瑟琳明显地咽了口唾沫：“我是冬城的伊瑟琳·瓦·里德尔公主。根据古老的条约，我恳请能在霍克斯通城堡获得庇护！|她深吸一口气，努力让自己的话语更加清晰，而不是去注意站在面前的那位贵族女性那锐利的目光。“我是伊瑟琳·瓦·里德尔，冬城的公主。根据一份古老的条约，我恳请能在霍克斯通城堡获得庇护。|她深吸一口气，稳住情绪，直视着女男爵的眼睛说道：“我是伊瑟琳·瓦·里德尔，冬城的公主。根据古老的条约，我恳请能在霍克斯通城堡获得庇护。]
    
    女男爵微微挑起了眉毛：“里德尔家族的一位小姐竟然远道来到这里？我原以为那些布尔阿尔瓦尔人早就绝迹了。年轻的女士，你为何要来寻求我的保护呢？你的护卫们在哪里？我很难相信你的国王会让你独自一人来到这里，哪怕是在流亡途中。”

“我[etheryn.lnhConfidence|一个人……”小琳哀叹道，“而且我们没有……没有国王。只有我的姐姐，艾莉莎。但她……她，呃……其实很邪恶。所以我逃走了。|我孤身一人来到了这里。我……我的姐姐，艾莉莎女王，她……她已经变成了恶人，一个邪恶的暴君。我尽快逃往了南方。|不仅仅是我一个人！”小琳骄傲地说道，握住了你的手。“我们没有国王，只有一个邪恶暴虐的女王，她的心已经变得如同煤灰一般黑暗！我逃离了这座城市，但我的人民仍然处于危险之中。求你，我需要你的帮助。]她向前走了几步，将目光紧紧地锁定在小琳身上，目光仔细地打量着这位公主的容貌。“原来是个逃亡者啊。但你来这里，不仅仅是为了寻求庇护，对吧？你是想让我帮助你从你那个邪恶的姐姐手中夺回这座城市，对吗？小琳尴尬地挪动着脚步。

    “放松点，孩子。”卡门微笑着说道，“首先，让我好好介绍一下自己吧；我想你的族人们自从神战之后，应该已经很久没有见过贝拉尔的贵族了。我是卡门·雷维拉男爵夫人。遗憾的是，贝拉尔已经不复存在了——它只是过去时代留下的回忆罢了，而我的许多力量，也随着它的消失而消失了。有[flags.ATUGIA_RECRUITED|两个|三]居住在这座城堡里的人中，有一个是石像鬼。我无法为您提供公主应有的款待与舒适，更没有足够的资源来帮助你们夺回距离这里数英里之外的那座城市。那些领主们的军队在战争中遭到了彻底的毁灭，我现在不得不雇佣雇佣兵来维护道路的安全……而其中很多人，其实已经变成了强盗，甚至比强盗还要糟糕。

你看到伊瑟琳的肩膀耷了下来，她的双手也无力地垂在身侧。哈里克发出尖叫，拼命扑腾着试图保持平衡，但小琳还是将他扔在了鹅卵石铺就的道路上，然后振翅飞回了城堡塔楼。

卡门叹了口气，小心翼翼地又向前迈出了一步，伸出手轻轻触了触小琳的脸颊。很抱歉，公主，但您那份有着四百年历史条约的对象，是一个早已不复存在的帝国。即便我愿意遵守这份条约，也实在没有能力帮助您。不过，我绝不会拒绝帮助一位处于困境中的女士。我会去和经营村中旅馆的加斯谈谈，确保把他最好的房间提供给您，并满足您所有的需求。只要你需要，你就可以留在我的领地里。恐怕，这就是我能够给你的唯一帮助了。

小琳用充满泪水的眼睛看着你。哦，不。

    "I, uhm," Etheryn [etheryn.lnhConfidence|shuffles her feet awkwardly, until Harrick stamps his little hawk-feet on her glove and pecks at her. "Gah! I, uh, h-hello, your ladyship... I-I am, uh, E-Etheryn of... of, uh, H-House R-R-Ridell, a-and-"

    "Get it together girl. Deep breaths," the baroness sighs. "My patience is far more limited than my time."
    
    Ryn gulps audibly. "I-I am Princess Etheryn var Ridell, of t-the Winter City. By ancient t-treaty, I humbly request sanctuary in Castle Hawkstone!"|takes a deep breath, concentrating on her words rather than the steely gaze of the noblewoman before her. "I am Etheryn var Ridell, princess of the Winter City. By a-ancient treaty, I humbly request sanctuary here at Castle Hawkstone."|takes a deep breath, steadies herself, and looks the baroness in the eye. "I am Etheryn var Ridell, princess of the Winter City. By ancient treaty, I humbly request sanctuary here at Castle Hawkstone."]
    
    The baroness raises a narrow brow. "A lady of the Ridell family this far south? I thought the boer'alvar had died out long ago. Why have you come seeking my protection, young princess. And where are your guards? I doubt your king would thrust you out all alone, even in exile."
    
    "I am [etheryn.lnhConfidence|alone," Ryn whines. "A-and we have no... no king. Just m-my sister, Alissa. And she's... she, uh... well... she's evil. I ran away.|here unescorted. M-my sister, Queen Alissa, she... she's turned evil. A wicked tyrant. I escaped south as soon as I could.|not alone!" Ryn says proudly, taking your hand in hers. "And we have no king. Just a wicked tyrant of a queen, whose heart has turned as black as soot! I ran from the city, but my people are in peril still. Please, I need your help.]"
    
    Taking a few steps closer, the baroness fixes Ryn in her gaze, eyes wandering over the princess's features. "So a runaway, then. But you're not just here as a refugee, are you — you want my help in retaking the city from your evil sister, is that right?"
    
    Ryn shuffles awkwardly.

    "Relax, child." Carmen smiles. "First, allow me to properly introduce myself; I doubt your people have seen a Belharan noble since the Godswar. I am Baroness Carmen Reverra. Unfortunately, Belhar is no more; a memory from a bygone age, and with it, much of my power. There are [flags.ATUGIA_RECRUITED|two|three] people living in this castle, and one of them is a gargoyle. I could not offer you the hospitality and comfort befitting a princess, and I certainly have no resources to put at your disposal to retake a city many miles from here. The Marcher Barons' armies were destroyed utterly in the war, and I am already resorting to mercenaries to keep the roads clear... and many of them have simply become bandits or worse anyway."

    You watch Etheryn's shoulders slump, and her hands fall to her side. Harrick screeches and flaps, catching himself before Ryn just dumps him on the cobblestones and taking wing back towards the castle tower. 
    
    Carmen sighs and takes another guarded step forward, reaching a hand out to take Ryn's cheek. "I am sorry, princess, but your four-century-old treaty was with an empire that doesn't exist anymore. And I simply haven't the power to help you, even were I to honor it. But I will not turn away a lady in need; I will talk to Garth, the man who keeps the village inn, and make sure that the best rooms he has are made available to you and all your needs are met. You may stay within my barony as long as you need. That is, I'm afraid, the only boon I can offer you."
    
    Ryn turns to you with wide, teary eyes. Oh no.
    '

rows.translation: 感谢卡门

rows.original:
You sigh and thank the baroness for her time. At least she was willing to hear Ryn out.

        Carmen gives you an apologetic smile. "I truly am sorry, but I'm simply not in a position to do more. Would that I could. Do take care of the young princess, [pc.title]. Her path will be a long and difficult one."
        
        Ryn sniffles, a sure sign that it's time to go before she embarrasses herself. You put a hand on the elven beauty's shoulders and guide her back towards town.
rows.translation:
你叹了口气，感谢女男爵抽出时间与你交谈。至少她愿意倾听小琳的意见。

        卡门向你露出了歉意的微笑：“我真的非常抱歉，但我目前确实无能为力。要是我能帮上忙该多好……请一定要照顾好那位年轻的公主，[pc.title]。她的道路将会充满艰辛与困难。”
        
        小琳抽泣起来，这显然意味着是时候离开这里，以免她再出丑了。你伸手搭在这位精灵美女的肩上，引导她朝着城镇的方向走去。

rows.translation: 发怒吧

rows.original:
"You call yourself a noble?" you scowl, thrusting a finger into Carmen's face. "How dare you just ignore the treaties and turn her away. She needs you, damn it!"

        The baroness sighs and shakes her head. "I know [a] [pc.bg noblescion|foreign lordling|commoner] like yourself may not understand, but things are hard in the Marches. I have no soldiers to offer, no staff to wait on her in the castle... I have nothing, [pc.title]. Nothing! Now begone from here, and be thankful I do not rescind what generosity I have shown Princess Etheryn because of your outburst."
        
        You seethe, but she's right. Getting Ryn kicked out of town entirely wouldn't help. So you put a hand on the princess' shoulder and lead her back towards town.
        
        "T-thank you," she sniffles. "For standing up for me."
        
        You ruffle her hair and tell her everything's going to be okay. Guess you'll have to deal with Queen Alissa yourselves... [pc.dcb|that bitch has a rude awakening coming to her! You just... need to get into her castle. Somehow.|somehow. All you have to do is find a way into her castle, right?|As soon as, like, you can figure out how to get there!]

你自称贵族？”你怒目而视，将手指戳在卡门面前，“你怎么敢无视那些条约，拒绝帮助她？她需要你，该死的！”

        女男爵叹了口气，摇了摇头：“我知道[pc.bg noblescion|外国贵族|平民]你可能无法理解，但在边境地区，情况确实很艰难。我没有士兵可以提供，也没有工作人员可以在城堡里为她服务……我一无所有。[pc.title]没什么！现在赶紧离开这里吧，庆幸我因为你的行为而没有撤销对伊瑟琳公主的慷慨承诺吧。”
        
        你虽然愤怒，但她说的没错。把小琳彻底赶出这座城市也不会有什么帮助。于是你把手放在公主的肩上，带着她往城镇的方向走去。

rows.original: Wow, what the fuck. How dare Carmen just turn Ryn away!
rows.translation: 哇，搞什么鬼。卡门怎么敢就这样拒绝小琳！
rows.raw: "Wow, what the fuck. How dare Carmen just turn Ryn away!"

rows.translation: 安慰

rows.original:
You turn and grab Ryn's slender shoulders, pulling her into a tight hug. "There there... it's gonna be okay. Everything's gonna be okay."

        She sniffles, hugs you back, and then starts bawling. Beside you, Carmen awkwardly bites her lower lip, glances about to make sure nobody else is looking, and then rests a hand comfortingly on Etheryn's back. "I am sorry, young princess. I... I wish there was more I could do. Truly."
        
        Something tells you that you're going to be here for a bit, so you thank the baroness for at least ensuring Ryn is welcome in town. She nods sadly and withdraws, back into the dusty old keep, leaving you to gently stroke Etheryn's hair and whisper softly in her ear that it's all gonna be alright...
        
        She nuzzles herself into your chest and has herself a good, long cry.
rows.translation:
你转过身，抓住小琳纤细的肩膀，将她紧紧抱在怀里。“别担心……一切都会好起来的，真的。”

        她抽泣着，也回抱了你，然后突然放声大哭起来。站在你身边的卡门尴尬地咬着下唇，四处张望以确保没有其他人看到这一幕，随后便把手轻轻地放在伊瑟琳的背上，给予她安慰。对不起，年轻的公主。我……真希望自己能做更多的事情来帮助您。”
        
        你隐约感觉到自己还得在这里待上一阵子，因此你至少感谢了女男爵，因为她是确保小琳能够在这个小镇上受到欢迎的人。她悲伤地点了点头，然后退了回去，重新回到了那座布满灰尘的古老城堡里，留下你一个人，轻轻地抚摸着伊瑟琳的头发，在她耳边轻声安慰她，告诉她一切都会好起来的……
        
        她依偎在你的怀里，痛痛快快地哭了一场。

rows.original:
[flags.CARMEN_MARRIED
        |"Oh?" The baroness arches an eyebrow at you, then turns to Cait. "You have a proposal, kitten? One that my [pc.mf
            |husband
            |wife
        ] can't just sign off on?"
        
        Cait takes a deep breath, squares her shoulders and puffs up her already prodigious chest. "Yes, ma'am; I've spoken to [pc.name] about it at length, but you're the one who makes the pertinent decisions, aren't you? Well, I'd like to seek your approval to build a temple to Mallach on the site of the old ruins just outside your castle. You are, after all, the ruler of these lands and my would-be neighbour."
        
        "I see. A temple of Mallach, right here on my doorstep no less? Hmm. Surely you've noticed the village already has a house worship; one that, while dedicated in Velun's name, already welcomes worshippers of every faith. Wouldn't you rather speak with Ser Riordan — ah, Brother Sanders — about joining him? At his age I'm sure he'd be happy to have another priestess easing the burden of tending to his flock."
        
        "I... I want to build someplace to worship Mallach in the Jassiran way, lady baroness," Cait ventures, rubbing the red gem clasp on her cloak. "I don't think Brother Sanders would be, ah, very receptive to the idea. You see..."
        
        "Ah. It's not just a house of prayer you want to build, is it?"
        
        Cait glances at you and gulps. "N-No, ma'am. It would be a house for sacred harlots, too."
        
        The baroness folds her hands over her willowy middle and sighs. "Hmm. [pc.name], given my... appetites... you must have realized I would not be enthused by the idea of having a brothel opening up on the road between my home and the village. There'll hardly be any virgins left in town with a sacred courtesan's nest built right on the edge of it."
        
        You can see the issue, sure, but this is important to Cait. And besides, you're here to take care of Carmen's hungers personally.
        
        She sighs, curling her lips up enough to reveal a fang. "Long after you're gone, love, a temple will endure. There's a reason we build monuments in stone. Ahh... but there must be something to this proposal that impressed my spouse enough for [pc.himHer] to personally bring it to me. Why don't we all sit down by the fire, and you can explain it all to me?"
        
        Before long all of you find yourself seated in plush, if old, armchairs about a roaring hearth, being treated to sugared biscuits and hot tea, brought to the table by the baroness herself.
        
        "Back in the day, my father would welcome petitioners with more hospitality than this meager offering, but I am afraid this is about the best we can offer in the circumstances."
        
        "Oh, please, you needn't concern yourself — it's very nice. Sugar must be a bit of a luxury up in the Marches," Cait says as she reaches for a biscuit.[party.manyCompanions
            | Off by the fire, [comp2.name] looks a little uncomfortable as [comp2.heShe] tries not to make too obvious the fact that [comp2.heShe]'s playing third fiddle here.
        ]
        
        "Sugar's a luxury anywhere you go these days, dear," the baroness replies sadly, leaning back in her chair and steepling her fingers. "But to the point — this house of harlots you're looking to build?"
        
        "Right. You see..."
        
        And with that, Cait launches into the same explanation she gave you when you were discussing the topic with Salwah. The baroness looks disinterested, all but openly hostile to the idea at first, but her expression darkens and grows serious as Cait moves onto the point of Calla's potential return and her hopes of keeping Tollus and other cultists away from the site of the portal.
        
        "You... do bring up a good point," the baroness finally sighs. "The pale elves used to have druidic temples all over the Marches, and that site was one of them. It was abandoned in the darkest days of the Godswar, when the elves drew back entirely to their bastions in the Frostwood. Since they never returned, their temple fell into ruin with the passage of age. It's been that way ever since."
        
        [party.has etheryn
            |Off in her corner by the fire, Ryn squirms in her seat and tries not to look too discomfited by the recounting of her peoples' downfall. 
            
        ]
        "Was that Tollus creep the first one to try and exploit the place?" Cait asks.
        
        "Master Tollus has been interested in those ruins for... for some time. He and his cult have caused a number of problems, some very bloody, for my little town. But his group wasn't the first to be drawn to that place, either." She pauses, giving Cait small smile. "With that said... having someone I can trust occupying the seat so someone else doesn't sneak in is a fine idea. And if you can recreate the splendours of your sunny country in these cold lands, then that's another point in your favor. But you must promise me one thing."
        
        Cait leans in, tail swishing. "Yes? Of course!"
        
        "Be considerate enough to keep the more... lascivious... activities of the temple contained within its grounds. I'm not so blind as to not take notice of the way Hawkethorne has changed in the last weeks, ever since you and your friends began arriving. I can't say I am enamoured with all of those changes, but I can't deny that the good that's been done outstrips the hamlet's loss of innocence. Still, I do not want my lands to become known as a place of carnal excess... and I don't want to hear moaning whores at all hours of the night. Understood?"
        
        "We'll behave, I promise! The only thing you'll hear are the bells, and I won't be sending girls down to seduce the farmer boys, don't worry. I want to run a clean house of Mallach, one worthy of his name, not just a cathouse."
        
        Your lordly host nods. "Then you have my blessing. But you will have to raise the funding, materials and manpower yourself, kitten, and then there is the issue of safety. There has to be a reason so many madmen have tried to set down their roots on my doorstep, and if you're going to settle down in those ruins you ought to get to the bottom of it all. I'd do it myself, but— " the baroness waves a hand at the castle's empty halls.
        
        Cait's tail twitches. "What do you think could be the problem?"
        
        "I'm not entirely sure myself, to be honest. Severine has been disturbed by the ruins on and off over the years, and every time her unease has peaked, we've always found some group of ruffians squatting on the site of the old temple worshipping the portal or whipping themselves bloody. Worse than flies to honey. I... I would hate for you to refurbish the elves' old ruins only for whatever dark magic permeates the place to get the better of you, as it's done to so many before you. Powers and presences linger in such sites for centuries after the fact and still affect the world after their passing. Before erecting any structure, an architect must examine the site first and foremost. Shouldn't the same principle apply to building atop old magics?"
        
        "All right, then. I'll do just that. My father's a magician of some repute — I'm sure he'll be able to help!"
        
        With you at her side, you're sure that she'll be able to get any problems sorted out posthaste. You're very lucky to have such a magnanimous wife — other rulers might not have been so keen on a foreign faith proselytizing on their literal doorsteps.
        
        Carmen smiles and squeezes your hand. "Mmm, that you are. My concerns are purely selfish, and with a particularly lovely [pc.mf
            |husband
            |wife
        ] of my own to alleviate them... somehow, I'll manage to cope. And besides, my barony has never favored one of the Seven over the other, as Sanders' chapel down in Hawkethorne proves."
        
        Cait's certainly done enough for the local community that she's earned her place here.
        
        Your wife chuckles softly. "Finding and retaining good people is part and parcel of effective leadership; I may have money, but good hands are harder to come by these days. [pc.bg noblescion
            |I see you carry your heritage well.
            |In the old Belharan empire, you might have been looked down upon for marrying into nobility without the blood to back it up, but new families, lines and dynasties all have to start somewhere.
        ]"
        
        Indeed.
        
        "Excellent. I think this concludes our business for now — shall I show you out, kitten? This conversation has brought up some things I should discuss with Severine posthaste."
        
        [var0]
        |"Oh?" The baroness arches an eyebrow at you, then turns to Cait. "You have a proposal, kitten?"
        
        Cait takes a deep breath, squares her shoulders and puffs up her already prodigious chest. "Yes, ma'am. I'd like to seek your approval to build a temple to Mallach on the site of the old ruins just outside your castle. You are, after all, the ruler of these lands and my would-be neighbour."
        
        A faint smile plays upon the baroness's blood-red lips. "I see. A temple of Mallach, right here on my doorstep no less? Hmm. Surely you've noticed the village already has a house worship; one that, while dedicated in Velun's name, already welcomes worshippers of every faith. Wouldn't you rather speak with Ser Riordan — ah, Brother Sanders — about joining him? At his age I'm sure he'd be happy to have another priestess easing the burden of tending to his flock."
        
        "I... I want to build someplace to worship Mallach in the Jassiran way, lady baroness," Cait ventures, rubbing the red gem clasp on her cloak. "I don't think Brother Sanders would be, ah, very receptive to the idea. You see..."
        
        "Ah. It's not just a house of prayer you want to build, is it?"
        
        Cait glances at you and gulps. "N-No, ma'am. It would be a house for sacred harlots, too."
        
        The baroness folds her hands over her willowy middle and sighs. "I am not enthused by the idea of having a brothel opening up on the road between my home and the village. But, I would be a poor noble if I turned away a servant of the gods out of hand. Come, sit, tell me exactly what you're proposing."
        
        Before long all of you find yourself seated in plush, if old, armchairs about a roaring hearth, being treated to sugared biscuits and hot tea, brought to the table by the baroness herself.
        
        "Back in the day, my father would welcome petitioners with more hospitality than this meager offering, but I am afraid this is about the best I can offer. The castle's staff has been depleted since before either of you were born."
        
        "Oh, please, you needn't concern yourself — it's very nice. Sugar must be a bit of a luxury up in the Marches," Cait says as she reaches for a biscuit.[party.manyCompanions
            | Off by the fire, [comp2.name] looks a little uncomfortable as [comp2.heShe] tries not to make too obvious the fact that [comp2.heShe]'s playing third fiddle here.
        ]
        
        "Sugar's a luxury anywhere you go these days, dear," the baroness replies sadly, leaning back in her chair and steepling her fingers. "But to the point — this house of harlots you're looking to build?"
        
        "Right. You see..."
        
        And with that, Cait launches into the same explanation she gave you when you were discussing the topic with Salwah. The baroness looks disinterested, all but openly hostile to the idea at first, but her expression darkens and grows serious as Cait moves onto the point of Calla's potential return and her hopes of keeping Tollus and other cultists away from the site of the portal.
        
        "You... do bring up a good point," the baroness finally sighs. "The pale elves used to have druidic temples all over the Marches, and that site was one of them. It was abandoned in the darkest days of the Godswar, when the elves drew back entirely to their bastions in the Frostwood. Since they never returned, their temple fell into ruin with the passage of age. It's been that way ever since."
        
        [party.has etheryn
            |Off in her corner by the fire, Ryn squirms in her seat and tries not to look too discomfited by the recounting of her peoples' downfall. 
            
        ]
        "Was that Tollus creep the first one to try and exploit the place?" Cait asks.
        
        "Master Tollus has been interested in those ruins for... for some time. He and his cult have caused a number of problems, some very bloody, for my little town. But his group wasn't the first to be drawn to that place, either." She pauses, giving Cait small smile. "With that said... having someone I can trust occupying the seat so someone else doesn't sneak in is a fine idea. And if you can recreate the splendours of your sunny country in these cold lands, then that's another point in your favor. But you must promise me one thing."
        
        Cait leans in, tail swishing. "Yes? Of course!"
        
        "Be considerate enough to keep the more... lascivious... activities of the temple contained within its grounds. I'm not so blind as to not take notice of the way Hawkethorne has changed in the last weeks, ever since you and your friends began arriving. I can't say I am enamoured with all of those changes, but I can't deny that the good that's been done outstrips the hamlet's loss of innocence. Still, I do not want my lands to become known as a place of carnal excess... and I don't want to hear moaning whores at all hours of the night. Understood?"
        
        "We'll behave, I promise! The only thing you'll hear are the bells, and I won't be sending girls down to seduce the farmer boys, don't worry. I want to run a clean house of Mallach, one worthy of his name, not just a cathouse."
        
        Your lordly host nods. "Then you have my blessing. But you will have to raise the funding, materials and manpower yourself, kitten, and then there is the issue of safety. There has to be a reason so many madmen have tried to set down their roots on my doorstep, and if you're going to settle down in those ruins you ought to get to the bottom of it all. I'd do it myself, but— " the baroness waves a hand at the castle's empty halls.
        
        Cait's tail twitches. "What do you think could be the problem?"
        
        "I'm not entirely sure myself, to be honest. Severine has been disturbed by the ruins on and off over the years, and every time her unease has peaked, we've always found some group of ruffians squatting on the site of the old temple worshipping the portal or whipping themselves bloody. Worse than flies to honey. I... I would hate for you to refurbish the elves' old ruins only for whatever dark magic permeates the place to get the better of you, as it's done to so many before you. Powers and presences linger in such sites for centuries after the fact and still affect the world after their passing. Before erecting any structure, an architect must examine the site first and foremost. Shouldn't the same principle apply to building atop old magics?"
        
        "All right, then. I'll do just that. My father's a magician of some repute — I'm sure he'll be able to help!"
        
        "Excellent. I think this concludes our business for now — shall I show you out? This conversation has brought up some things I should discuss with Severine posthaste."

[flags.CARMEN_MARRIED
        |哦？”女男爵挑了挑眉毛看着你，然后转向凯特：“小猫咪，你有什么建议吗？是不是有什么办法[pc.mf
            |丈夫
            |妻子
        ]就不能直接签字同意吗？”

凯特深吸一口气，挺直肩膀，让她那本就丰满的胸部显得更加突出。“是的，女士。我已经和[pc.name]详细谈过此事，但相关决定终究还是由您来做，不是吗？我想请求您批准，在您城堡外的旧废墟上为马拉克建造一座神庙。毕竟，您是这片土地的统治者，也将是我的邻居。”我明白了。原来是在我家门口就有一座献给玛拉赫的神庙啊？嗯，你们肯定已经注意到，这个村庄其实已经有了自己的祭祀场所；虽然那个场所是献给维伦的，但它已经接纳了各种信仰的信徒们来进行祭祀活动。您难道不觉得应该先和里奥丹爵士——啊，也就是桑德斯修士——谈谈是否愿意让他加入我们吗？以他的年纪，肯定很乐意有另一位女祭司来帮助他照顾信徒们。”

“我……我想用贾西兰的方式，建立一个用来崇拜马拉克的神殿，女男爵。”凯特小心翼翼地说道，同时摩挲着披风上那颗红色的宝石扣饰。我觉得桑德斯修士应该不会太赞同这个想法的……您看……”

“啊，你想要建造的不仅仅是一座祈祷场所，对吧？”

凯特瞥了你一眼，咽了口唾沫：“不、不是这样的，女士。那也会变成一座供那些神圣的妓女们使用的房子罢了。”

女男爵将双手交叠在纤细的腰间，叹了口气：“嗯[pc.name]，考虑到我的……兴趣爱好……你们肯定已经意识到，如果在我家和村庄之间的路上开了一家妓院，我肯定不会感兴趣的。毕竟镇上本来就几乎没有处女了，而现在又在那附近建了一家“神圣的妓院”，那剩下的处女就更少了。你当然能看到这个问题，但这对凯特来说很重要。而且，你在这里不就是专门负责满足卡门的需求的吗？

        她叹了口气，嘴角微微上扬，露出了一颗獠牙。即使在你离开很久之后，爱情依然会留存，那座庙宇也会继续存在。我们之所以用石头建造纪念碑，是有着原因的……啊……这个提议中肯定有什么地方让我的配偶感到印象深刻，才会[pc.himHer]亲自把这件事告诉我吧。我们不如都坐在火堆旁，让你把一切都解释给我听。”

不久之后，你们所有人都坐在了那些虽然有些陈旧但非常舒适的扶手椅上，围坐在熊熊燃烧的火堆旁，女男爵亲自为大家端来了加糖的饼干和热茶。
        
        在过去，我父亲接待请愿者时，所提供的招待会远比这丰盛得多。不过，在目前这种情况下，我想我们能做的已经算是最好的了。”

“哦，请别担心，这样已经非常不错了。在边境地区，糖肯定算是一种奢侈品吧，”凯特边说边伸手去拿一块饼干。[party.manyCompanions
            | 靠近火堆的地方，[comp2.name]看起来有点不太舒服[comp2.heShe]尽量不让人太明显地察觉到这个事实。[comp2.heShe]在这里，它只不过是个次要的角色罢了。
        ]
        
        亲爱的，如今无论你去哪里，糖都算是一种奢侈品了，”女男爵悲伤地回答道，她靠在椅子上，双手交叉放在胸前。“不过，说到你打算建造的这家妓院……”

“没错。你瞧……”

说完，凯特便开始解释她之前在你们与萨尔瓦讨论这个话题时所讲的内容。起初，这位女男爵看起来对这件事毫无兴趣，甚至明显表现出敌意，但当凯特讲到卡拉有可能回归，以及她希望将托卢斯和其他邪教徒挡在传送门所在地之外时，她的表情变得严肃起来。
        
        你……提了一个很好的观点，”女男爵终于叹了口气说道，“那些苍白精灵曾经在边境地区建立了许多德鲁伊神庙，而那个地点就是其中之一。在神战最激烈的那些日子里，当精灵们全部撤退到霜木地的堡垒中时，那座神庙也被废弃了。由于他们再也没有回来，他们的寺庙也随着时间的流逝而逐渐荒废了。从那以后，一直保持着这样的状态。
        
        [party.has etheryn
            |坐在靠近火堆的角落里，小琳坐立不安，努力不让自己显得对听到的关于她族人衰败的故事感到太过困扰。 
            
        ]
        是那个叫托卢斯的家伙第一个试图利用那个地方的吗？”凯特问道。

“托勒斯大师对那些废墟很感兴趣……已经有一段时间了。他和他的邪教组织给我的小镇带来了很多麻烦，其中一些麻烦还非常血腥。但他的团队也不是第一个被吸引到那个地方的人。“她停顿了一下，对着凯特微微一笑，继续说道：‘话虽如此……有我可以信任的人来担任那个职位，这样就不会有人偷偷混进来了，这个主意确实不错。而且，如果你能在这片寒冷的土地上重现你那个阳光明媚的国家的辉煌，那更是你的一个巨大优势。但是你必须向我承诺一件事。
        
        凯特凑上前来，尾巴摇来摇去：“嗯？当然可以！”

“请尽量把寺庙里那些……比较……挑逗性的活动限制在寺庙的范围内。我并不是瞎子，当然注意到了在你们和你的朋友们到来之后，鹰棘镇发生了哪些变化。我必须承认，我并不是对所有这些变化都感到满意，但不可否认，这些变化带来的积极影响确实超过了它们给这个小镇带来的负面影响。不过，我绝不希望我的土地变成一个以放荡淫乱著称的地方……更不想在夜深人静的时候听到那些妓女的哀嚎声。明白了吗？
        
        我保证我们会守规矩的！你们只会听到钟声，而我也不会派女孩下去勾引那些农场男孩，放心吧。我想把马拉克的家管理得干干净净，让它名副其实，而不是变成一个肮脏的地方。你的主人点了点头说道：“那么，我赐予你我的祝福。但是，你必须自己筹集资金、准备所需的材料并招募人手，小猫。另外，安全问题也必须得到解决。既然有这么多疯子试图在我家门口安家落户，那你如果真的打算在那些废墟中定居，就必须弄清楚其中的原因。我本想自己动手做的，但是——女男爵朝城堡里空荡荡的厅堂挥了挥手。
        
        凯特的尾巴不由自主地抽动起来。“你觉得可能是什么问题呢？”

“说实话，我也不太确定。这些年来，塞弗琳一直被那些废墟所困扰，而每当她的不安情绪达到顶点时，我们总会发现有一群流氓混在那座古老寺庙的遗址上，要么崇拜着那个传送门，要么自残至血。这简直比苍蝇飞向蜂蜜还要糟糕。我……我真不希望你花费精力修复那些精灵们的古老遗迹，结果却让那里弥漫的暗影魔法伤害到你，就像之前很多人那样。这样的地方，那些力量和存在会持续存在几个世纪，即使在它们消逝之后，依然会影响着这个世界。在建造任何结构之前，建筑师首先必须对现场进行勘测。那么，对于在那些蕴含古老魔力的地方进行建造，难道不应该遵循同样的原则吗？

        ]
        是那个叫托卢斯的家伙第一个试图利用那个地方的吗？”凯特问道。

“托勒斯大师对那些废墟很感兴趣……已经有一段时间了。他和他的邪教组织给我的小镇带来了很多麻烦，其中一些麻烦还非常血腥。但他的团队也不是第一个被吸引到那个地方的人。“她停顿了一下，对着凯特微微一笑，继续说道：‘话虽如此……有我可以信任的人坐在这个位置上，这样就不会有人偷偷混进来了，这个主意确实不错。而且，如果你能在这片寒冷的土地上重现你那个阳光明媚的国家的辉煌，那更是你的一个巨大优势。但是你必须向我承诺一件事。
        
        凯特凑上前来，尾巴摇来摇去：“嗯？当然可以！”

“请尽量把寺庙里那些……比较……挑逗性的活动限制在寺庙的范围内。我并不是瞎子，当然注意到了在你们和你的朋友们到来之后，鹰棘镇发生了哪些变化。我必须承认，我并不是对所有这些变化都感到满意，但不可否认，这些变化带来的积极影响确实超过了它们给这个小镇带来的负面影响。不过，我绝不希望我的土地变成一个以放荡淫乱著称的地方……更不想在夜深人静的时候听到那些妓女的哀嚎声。明白了吗？
        
        我保证我们会守规矩的！你们只会听到钟声，而我也不会派女孩下去引诱那些农场男孩，放心吧。我想把马拉克的家管理得干干净净，让它真正配得上这个名字，而不是变成一个肮脏的地方。你的主人点了点头说道：“那么，我赐予你我的祝福。但是，你必须要自己筹集资金、准备所需的材料并招募人手，小猫。另外，安全问题也必须得到解决。既然有这么多疯子试图在我家门口安家落户，那么如果你真的打算在那些废墟中定居下来，你就必须弄清楚其中的原因。我本想自己动手做的，但是——女男爵朝城堡里空荡荡的厅堂挥了挥手。
        
        凯特的尾巴不由自主地抽动起来。“你觉得可能是什么问题呢？”

“说实话，我自己也不太确定。这些年来，塞弗琳一直被那些废墟所困扰，而每当她的不安情绪达到顶点时，我们总会发现有一群粗人蹲在那座古老寺庙的遗址上，要么崇拜着那个传送门，要么自残至血肉模糊。这简直比苍蝇飞向蜂蜜还要糟糕。我……我真不希望你花费精力修复那些精灵的古老遗迹，结果却让那里弥漫的暗影魔法伤害到你，就像之前很多人那样。这样的地方，那些力量和存在会持续存在几个世纪，即使在它们消逝之后，依然会影响着这个世界。在建造任何结构之前，建筑师首先必须对现场进行勘测。那么，对于在那些蕴含古老魔力的地方上进行建造，难道不应该遵循同样的原则吗？
        
        好吧，那我就这么办。我父亲是一位颇有名气的魔术师，我相信他一定能帮上忙！”

“太好了。我想我们现在的事情已经谈完了——需要我送您出去吗？这次谈话让我想到了一些事情，我必须尽快和塞维琳讨论一下。
        
        [var0]
    ]

'
    [flags.CARMEN_MARRIED
        |"Oh?" The baroness arches an eyebrow at you, then turns to Cait. "You have a proposal, kitten? One that my [pc.mf
            |husband
            |wife
        ] can't just sign off on?"
        
        Cait takes a deep breath, squares her shoulders and puffs up her already prodigious chest. "Yes, ma'am; I've spoken to [pc.name] about it at length, but you're the one who makes the pertinent decisions, aren't you? Well, I'd like to seek your approval to build a temple to Mallach on the site of the old ruins just outside your castle. You are, after all, the ruler of these lands and my would-be neighbour."
        
        "I see. A temple of Mallach, right here on my doorstep no less? Hmm. Surely you've noticed the village already has a house worship; one that, while dedicated in Velun's name, already welcomes worshippers of every faith. Wouldn't you rather speak with Ser Riordan — ah, Brother Sanders — about joining him? At his age I'm sure he'd be happy to have another priestess easing the burden of tending to his flock."
        
        "I... I want to build someplace to worship Mallach in the Jassiran way, lady baroness," Cait ventures, rubbing the red gem clasp on her cloak. "I don't think Brother Sanders would be, ah, very receptive to the idea. You see..."
        
        "Ah. It's not just a house of prayer you want to build, is it?"
        
        Cait glances at you and gulps. "N-No, ma'am. It would be a house for sacred harlots, too."
        
        The baroness folds her hands over her willowy middle and sighs. "Hmm. [pc.name], given my... appetites... you must have realized I would not be enthused by the idea of having a brothel opening up on the road between my home and the village. There'll hardly be any virgins left in town with a sacred courtesan's nest built right on the edge of it."
        
        You can see the issue, sure, but this is important to Cait. And besides, you're here to take care of Carmen's hungers personally.
        
        She sighs, curling her lips up enough to reveal a fang. "Long after you're gone, love, a temple will endure. There's a reason we build monuments in stone. Ahh... but there must be something to this proposal that impressed my spouse enough for [pc.himHer] to personally bring it to me. Why don't we all sit down by the fire, and you can explain it all to me?"
        
        Before long all of you find yourself seated in plush, if old, armchairs about a roaring hearth, being treated to sugared biscuits and hot tea, brought to the table by the baroness herself.
        
        "Back in the day, my father would welcome petitioners with more hospitality than this meager offering, but I am afraid this is about the best we can offer in the circumstances."
        
        "Oh, please, you needn't concern yourself — it's very nice. Sugar must be a bit of a luxury up in the Marches," Cait says as she reaches for a biscuit.[party.manyCompanions
            | Off by the fire, [comp2.name] looks a little uncomfortable as [comp2.heShe] tries not to make too obvious the fact that [comp2.heShe]'s playing third fiddle here.
        ]
        
        "Sugar's a luxury anywhere you go these days, dear," the baroness replies sadly, leaning back in her chair and steepling her fingers. "But to the point — this house of harlots you're looking to build?"
        
        "Right. You see..."
        
        And with that, Cait launches into the same explanation she gave you when you were discussing the topic with Salwah. The baroness looks disinterested, all but openly hostile to the idea at first, but her expression darkens and grows serious as Cait moves onto the point of Calla's potential return and her hopes of keeping Tollus and other cultists away from the site of the portal.
        
        "You... do bring up a good point," the baroness finally sighs. "The pale elves used to have druidic temples all over the Marches, and that site was one of them. It was abandoned in the darkest days of the Godswar, when the elves drew back entirely to their bastions in the Frostwood. Since they never returned, their temple fell into ruin with the passage of age. It's been that way ever since."
        
        [party.has etheryn
            |Off in her corner by the fire, Ryn squirms in her seat and tries not to look too discomfited by the recounting of her peoples' downfall. 
            
        ]
        "Was that Tollus creep the first one to try and exploit the place?" Cait asks.
        
        "Master Tollus has been interested in those ruins for... for some time. He and his cult have caused a number of problems, some very bloody, for my little town. But his group wasn't the first to be drawn to that place, either." She pauses, giving Cait small smile. "With that said... having someone I can trust occupying the seat so someone else doesn't sneak in is a fine idea. And if you can recreate the splendours of your sunny country in these cold lands, then that's another point in your favor. But you must promise me one thing."
        
        Cait leans in, tail swishing. "Yes? Of course!"
        
        "Be considerate enough to keep the more... lascivious... activities of the temple contained within its grounds. I'm not so blind as to not take notice of the way Hawkethorne has changed in the last weeks, ever since you and your friends began arriving. I can't say I am enamoured with all of those changes, but I can't deny that the good that's been done outstrips the hamlet's loss of innocence. Still, I do not want my lands to become known as a place of carnal excess... and I don't want to hear moaning whores at all hours of the night. Understood?"
        
        "We'll behave, I promise! The only thing you'll hear are the bells, and I won't be sending girls down to seduce the farmer boys, don't worry. I want to run a clean house of Mallach, one worthy of his name, not just a cathouse."
        
        Your lordly host nods. "Then you have my blessing. But you will have to raise the funding, materials and manpower yourself, kitten, and then there is the issue of safety. There has to be a reason so many madmen have tried to set down their roots on my doorstep, and if you're going to settle down in those ruins you ought to get to the bottom of it all. I'd do it myself, but— " the baroness waves a hand at the castle's empty halls.
        
        Cait's tail twitches. "What do you think could be the problem?"
        
        "I'm not entirely sure myself, to be honest. Severine has been disturbed by the ruins on and off over the years, and every time her unease has peaked, we've always found some group of ruffians squatting on the site of the old temple worshipping the portal or whipping themselves bloody. Worse than flies to honey. I... I would hate for you to refurbish the elves' old ruins only for whatever dark magic permeates the place to get the better of you, as it's done to so many before you. Powers and presences linger in such sites for centuries after the fact and still affect the world after their passing. Before erecting any structure, an architect must examine the site first and foremost. Shouldn't the same principle apply to building atop old magics?"
        
        "All right, then. I'll do just that. My father's a magician of some repute — I'm sure he'll be able to help!"
        
        With you at her side, you're sure that she'll be able to get any problems sorted out posthaste. You're very lucky to have such a magnanimous wife — other rulers might not have been so keen on a foreign faith proselytizing on their literal doorsteps.
        
        Carmen smiles and squeezes your hand. "Mmm, that you are. My concerns are purely selfish, and with a particularly lovely [pc.mf
            |husband
            |wife
        ] of my own to alleviate them... somehow, I'll manage to cope. And besides, my barony has never favored one of the Seven over the other, as Sanders' chapel down in Hawkethorne proves."
        
        Cait's certainly done enough for the local community that she's earned her place here.
        
        Your wife chuckles softly. "Finding and retaining good people is part and parcel of effective leadership; I may have money, but good hands are harder to come by these days. [pc.bg noblescion
            |I see you carry your heritage well.
            |In the old Belharan empire, you might have been looked down upon for marrying into nobility without the blood to back it up, but new families, lines and dynasties all have to start somewhere.
        ]"
        
        Indeed.
        
        "Excellent. I think this concludes our business for now — shall I show you out, kitten? This conversation has brought up some things I should discuss with Severine posthaste."
