rows.original:
You feel a sharp downward tug on your [pc.armor], and turn [party.has atugia
        |to your redheaded companion to see what's wrong
        |to find Atugia standing at your side
    ]. She's got a grimly serious look on her face, and you notice she's buckled up her armor and run a comb through her hair, looking downright presentable. 
    
    "Carmen's asked me to bring you up to the castle," she says, nodding her head northward to the hillside. [party.has atugia
        |"Used a spell to whisper it and all from Hawkstone, so it's gotta be important whatever it is."
        |"Said it was important. That I ought to fetch you directly."
    ]
    
    A summons directly from the town's ruler, eh? Wonder what this could be about...
    
    [pc.dcb
        |"Well, what're you waiting for then?" you snarl, pushing Tui towards the door. "Let's go."
        |"Well, let's not keep the Lady Reverra waiting," you suggest, heading for the door.
        |"Oooh, time to meet the pretty rich lady again? Let's go!"
        
        Atugia gives you a deeply unsure look before gently taking your arm and leading you towards the door.
    ]
    
    It's a quick walk up the old road, past [var0
        |Caitriss's new Mallachite sanctuary
        |the ruined temple and its otherworldly rend in space where this all started
    ] and up to the looming walls of Castle Hawkstone, perched high above the little hamlet you've come to call home. The gates are standing open in anticipation of your arrival, and Atugia marches straight for the inner keep's doors and heaves them open with a grunt of effort. The interior of the castle hall is certainly grand enough — arched and vaulted high overhead, with a great crimson carpet stretching from the eave to the stairs opposite it, and suits of old Belharan armor lining the walls between unfurled tapestries and banners. It's all so... old. Dust clings to much of it, unkept with so few people in the castle to maintain the place, and more than a few spiderwebs cling to the shadows above you. If you didn't know better, you'd hardly guess the place was inhabited at all, much less by a noblewoman. 
    
    A side door creaks open, and the baroness herself strides sharply into the hall, hands folded in front of her black dress. High heels click loudly on the stone of the floor, echoing from the arches.
rows.translation:
你感觉到有一股向下的拉力在拉着你[pc.armor]然后转身。 [party.has atugia
        |去看看你的红发同伴到底怎么了
        |发现阿图吉娅站在你的身边
    ]她的脸上带着严肃的神情，你可以看到她已经系好了盔甲，还整理了自己的头发，看起来确实非常整洁得体。
    
    “卡门让我带你去城堡，”她说着，同时朝北方的山坡点了点头。 [party.has atugia
        |一定是用了某种咒语，在霍克斯通那里悄悄传达了这个消息，所以不管这是什么，肯定非常重要。
        |他说这很重要，所以我应该直接来接你。
    ]
    
    这是镇长直接发出的召唤，嗯？不知道这次会是为了什么事情……
    
    [pc.dcb
        |那你还等什么？”你厉声说道，推着涂往门口走去，“我们走吧。
        |好吧，我们不要让雷薇拉女士等待太久了，”你说着，朝门口走去。
        |哦，又是时候去见那位富有的女士了？我们走吧！”
        
        阿图吉娅用一种充满不确定的眼神看着你，然后轻轻地挽着你的手臂，带你朝门口走去。
    ]
    
    沿着那条老路走上去，再穿过那里就行了。 [var0
        |凯特丽丝新建的马拉克信徒避难所
        |那座被毁的寺庙，以及这一切起源之处那充满超自然气息的空间……
    ]一直延伸到高耸在你们称之为家园的小村庄上方的霍克斯通城堡的墙壁旁。大门敞开着，仿佛在等待着你们的到来。阿图吉娅径直走向内堡的大门，用力一推，将它们推开了。城堡大厅的内部确实十分宏伟——高高的拱顶和穹顶令人印象深刻，一条深红色的地毯从屋檐一直延伸到对面的楼梯，墙壁上排列着古老的贝尔哈兰盔甲，而在这些盔甲之间，还挂满了展开的挂毯和旗帜。这一切都显得如此……陈旧。许多地方都积满了灰尘，因为城堡里很少有人来维护这个地方，所以到处都是蛛网。如果你不知道内情，根本不会想到这里竟然有人居住，更不会想到这里住着一位贵族女性。 
    
    一道侧门吱呀一声打开了，女男爵本人大步走进大厅，双手交叠在黑色连衣裙的前面。高跟鞋在石质地面上发出清脆的声响，回声在拱门中久久回荡。

卡门与阿图吉娅

rows.original:
"Thank you for coming, [pc.title]," the baroness says, giving you a slight nod and gesturing towards the door she'd come from. "Please, come and have a seat. We've much to discuss."
        
        Now this is starting to seem a little ominous, but one doesn't refuse the closest thing to a ruler in these parts. You follow between the baroness and Atugia up a small set of stairs and into a small fire-lit sitting room. A single glass-paned window — quite the luxury out here in the Marches, even if a bit scratched up — overlooks the castle courtyard[flags.ATUGIA_ALTPATH
            |
            | where you and the freckled knight first sparred
        ]. You're led to one of the two couches flanking a table set out with tea, while your host sweeps down into the other. [atugia.recruited|Tui awkwardly looks between her current and former employer before settling on standing at attention between the two of you|Atugia stands protectively at attention behind her mistress, just tall enough for her chin to crest the sofa's high back]. 
        
        "You've done Hawkethorne a great service, [pc.name]," the baroness starts, picking up a porcelain cup and blowing gently onto its steaming contents. "Chaos has reigned since the incident down in the temple. Longer than that, truth be told, but it very nearly came to a head that would have destroyed my little hamlet were it not for you. Centaurs rampaging in the valley, orc marauders raiding the hills, a monstrous plant-creature corrupting the forest... and you dealt with each and every one of them. The people of Hawkethorne are in your debt, truly." 
        
        She sets her cup down without drinking, iron-gray eyes searching over you. "After such efforts, I imagine you must be wondering why dealing with these wretches fell to you — that you must be asking yourself why the ruler of these lands hasn't marshalled her forces and crushed the enemies hounding our gates."
rows.translation:
“谢谢你能来，[pc.title]，”女男爵微微点头，朝自己刚刚走出的门示意。“请进来坐吧。我们有许多事情要谈。”
        
        这件事开始显得有些不祥，可没人会拒绝这片土地上最接近统治者的人。你走在女男爵和阿图吉娅之间，登上一小段楼梯，进入一间燃着炉火的小会客室。一扇装有玻璃的小窗俯瞰城堡庭院——即便表面有些划痕，在边疆地区也称得上奢侈品[flags.ATUGIA_ALTPATH
            |
            |；你和那位雀斑骑士曾在那里初次切磋
        ]。女男爵将你领到桌边两张沙发中的一张；桌上摆着茶水，而主人轻盈地坐进对面那张。[atugia.recruited|阿图尴尬地看看现任雇主，又看看前任雇主，最后在你们之间立正站好|阿图吉娅护卫般站在主人身后，身高恰好让下巴越过沙发高高的靠背]。
        
        “[pc.name]，你为鹰棘镇立下了大功，”女男爵开口说道；她端起瓷杯，轻轻吹拂其中冒着热气的饮品。“神殿里的事件发生后，混乱一直支配着这里。说实话，混乱开始得更早；但若非有你，它几乎就要酿成灾难，摧毁我的小小村镇。半人马在山谷里横冲直撞，兽人劫掠者袭击丘陵，怪物般的植物生物腐化森林……而你解决了每一个威胁。鹰棘镇的人民确实欠你一份恩情。”
        
        她没有喝茶便放下杯子，铁灰色的眼睛审视着你。“付出如此多努力后，我想你一定很好奇，为何对付这些恶徒的责任落到了自己肩上——一定在问自己，这片土地的统治者为何没有集结军队，粉碎那些逼近我们大门的敌人。”

rows.original:
The baroness's blood-red lips curl into the faintest hint of a smile. "The truth is, [pc.name], I am not much of a leader. This isn't the first time my inaction has lead to chaos within the barony. Some years ago I watched with horror from my tower as a butcher's price was paid by the townsfolk for my passivity; nearly half the young folk of the town lost their lives in a battle which I know, now, that I could have prevented had I acted. And now, again, that lack of decisive action in the past allowed 'master' — what does he call himself now, Tollus? — to breach the old portal in the temple. As events have continued to play out these last weeks, it's become gravely apparent to me that I am responsible for what has played out here."
            
            Your host sighs, closing her eyes. "So, firstly, I wish to offer you an apology for my part in all this. Or rather, lack of part. Secondly, an offer, if you would indulge me..."
            
            Before she makes her case, this might be a good time to throw any questions you've had backed up for the baroness her way. It's not every day you get an audience...
rows.translation:
男爵夫人的血红色双唇微微勾起，露出一丝微笑：“事实上，[pc.name]，我其实并不擅长领导他人。这种因为我的不作为而导致领地陷入混乱的情况已经不是第一次了。几年前，我就在塔楼上惊恐地目睹：由于我的消极态度，镇上的居民付出了惨重的代价——几乎有一半的年轻人在那场本可以避免的战斗中失去了生命。现在我终于明白，如果当时我采取了行动，这一切都是可以防止的。而如今，过去那种缺乏果断行动的做法，再次导致了那个‘大师’——他现在自称是什么来着，托勒斯吗？——得以突破寺庙里那座古老的传送门。在过去的几周里，随着事件的发展，我越来越清楚地意识到，这里发生的一切其实都应该由我来负责。”
            
            你的女主人叹了口气，闭上了眼睛。“首先，我想为我在这一切中所扮演的角色——或者更确切地说，应该是我的无所作为——向您道歉。其次，如果您愿意的话，我还有一个提议……”
            
            在她开始说明自己的理由之前，现在或许是个好时机，把你们一直想问女男爵的问题都提出来吧。能拥有这样的观众，确实不是每天都能遇到的……

rows.original: [pc.isDK |"So why have you been sitting on your ass doing nothing this whole time?" |"If you don't mind me asking... why have you not taken action?" ] The baroness glances sharply away for a moment, gazing into the fire. "Because I swore an oath, long ago." [pc.isDK |"You've got to do better than that, lady." |"I'm sorry?" ] She sighs, finally straightening in her seat. "I do not wish to speak at length about it, but in short: a long time ago, when I was young and foolish and very strong, I... I hurt people. Though I meant to act in the defense of the innocent, my recklessness blew back on the very people I tried to save. After that, I swore an oath never again to conjure spell or raise my blade to harm another. Not even... not even in defense of self." How long ago could that have been? She barely looks older than you. [pc.isDK |"So you're just going to sit here and do nothing while your people suffer?" Carmen winces as if struck. "I... for their sake, it is better that I do just that. I'm sorry. But that is why I asked you here. What I wished to discuss with you..." |"So you can't help the people of Hawkethorne?" "I... I help as I am able. But I will not fight for them again. I cannot risk it. But that is why I asked you here, [pc.name]. Because you can." ]
rows.translation: [pc.isDK |“那你这段时间为什么一直干坐着，屁事都不干？” |“恕我冒昧问一句……为什么你一直没有采取行动呢？” ] 女男爵猛地移开视线，望向了火堆。“因为很久以前，我曾立下过誓言。” [pc.isDK |“女士，这说法可不够。” |“你说什么？” ] 她叹了口气，终于在座位上坐直了身子。“我不想长篇大论地谈论这件事，但简而言之：很久以前，当我还年轻、愚蠢，而且力量强大的时候，我……我伤害了别人。虽然我的初衷是保护无辜的人，但我的鲁莽反而伤害到了那些我试图拯救的人。从那以后，我发誓再也不会施展任何法术，也不会拔剑伤害他人。哪怕是……哪怕是为了自卫也不行。” 那应该是多久以前的事了呢？她看起来几乎不比你年长多少。 [pc.isDK |“所以你就打算坐在这里什么都不做，任由你的人民遭受痛苦吗？” 卡门仿佛被击中般皱起了眉头。“我……为了他们好，我最好还是就这样什么都不做。我很抱歉。但这就是我请你来的原因。我想与你讨论的事情……” |“所以你无法帮助鹰棘镇的人们了？” “我……我会尽力帮助他们。但我不会再为他们而战了。我不能冒这个险。但这正是我请你来的原因，[pc.name]。因为你可以。” ]

rows.translation: 托勒斯？

rows.original: "It sounds like you know something about Tollus..." "I do," the baroness says. "He has haunted this part of the world for many years. Much of the Marches' instability can be traced back to his cult, one way or another. I expected him to be trouble when he first reared his bald head around here some fifteen, twenty years ago, but I never could have imagined just how right I was. First the incident with the village youths, and now this portal and demon. The brat's gone too far this time." [pc.isDK |"You've gotta give me more than that," you snap. "What do you know?" |"You know more than just his name, don't you?" ] Your host sighs, finally picking up her teacup again and taking a long sip. "The name 'Tollus' belonged to a pre-Godswar philosopher, from the eastern reaches of the empire. He wrote chiefly about the divine right of kings, very pro-Imperial despite having been born in the desert colonies. I believe it's part of Jassira now. He reasoned that only those favored by the Seven could rule successfully, and therefore wax and wane of a ruler's term was predicated on pleasing the gods, and in turn, gods well-pleased would shower riches on the empire. It all made a great deal of sense until the Godswar, I'm sure. Then again, no doubt the real Master Tollus would have said that the [silly |Grand Poobah |Emperor ] of Belhar must have committed some mortal sin in secret to unleash such calamity. Perhaps he did, at that." "But back to our Master Tollus..." "Ah," the baroness murmurs, sipping again. Atugia coughs loudly. "Carmen..." The baroness purses her lips. "I am working out how best to speak, Atugia, thank you. Ahh, this so-called 'Tollus' is by birth Michael Augustus Reverra-" "Reverra!?" "-That is to say, a cousin of mine some distance removed. His father was brother to the hero immortalized in Hawkethorne's town square, who fled south with his children when the Godswar broke out rather than stay to defend his ancestral homeland. I can... only imagine the fear in his heart, in those dark days with no ray of hope on the horizon, with no gods to turn back the tide of demons from beyond. But now that cowardly knight's descendant has returned to claim what he believes to be his birthright — the Barony of Hawkethorne, at the very least, if not the Marches as a whole." "You're joking." Carmen shakes her head. "Would that I were. Of course, his claim to the barony is rubbish — my father ruled these lands, as his mother before him did — but even when he first arrived in the Marches and I invited him in to speak, to try and work through whatever trauma had twisted him around to such delusions, he would not hear it. He claimed I was a fraudster at best and stormed out, vowing that the people of Hawkethorne would soon make it known what lord they wished to serve. Even he could not have imagined how violently his ambitions would be curtailed after that, but he has remained in the Marches causing trouble for my lands and everywhere from Tychris to Maidenbridge in the meantime." [var0|Even further than that, now, it seems...] The baroness sets her cup down and crosses a leg, looking just as grim as Atugia did when she first fetched you. "So. That's the truth of the matter, [pc.name]. The three of us and Michael himself are likely the only people in the north that know who he really is. Though what's driven my cousin to this madness, I cannot begin to imagine. I wish I could be of more help as to the why and how of his plots."
rows.translation: 听起来你对托勒斯似乎了解一些情况……” “确实如此，”女男爵说道，“多年来，他一直在这个地区活动。边境地区的诸多动荡，或多或少都与他的邪教组织有关。大约十五、二十年前，当他第一次出现在这里时，我就预料到他会带来麻烦，但没想到我的预感竟如此准确。先是那起与村中年轻人的事件，现在又是这个传送门和恶魔……这次，这个混蛋真的做得太过分了。 [pc.isDK |你给我的信息太少了，”你愤怒地说道，“你到底知道些什么？ |你知道的，可不止他的名字，对吧？ ] 你的主人叹了口气，终于重新拿起茶杯，喝了一大口。“‘托勒斯’这个名字属于一位神战之前的哲学家，他来自帝国的东部地区。他的主要研究方向是君权神授的理论，尽管他出生在沙漠殖民地，但他的观点却非常支持帝国。我认为它现在已经成为了贾西拉的一部分。他认为，只有那些受到七神青睐的人才能成功统治，因此一位统治者的统治时长会随着能否取悦神明而发生变化；而那些受到神明眷顾的统治者，必然会为他们的帝国带来繁荣与财富。在“神战”发生之前，这一切确实都显得非常合理。不过，毫无疑问，真正的托勒斯大师也会这么说吧。 [silly |大人物 |皇帝 ]贝尔哈尔肯定在暗中犯下了什么不可饶恕的罪行，才会招致这样的灾祸。也许，他确实这么做了。我们的托勒斯大师……” “啊，”女男爵边啜饮着酒边轻声说道。 阿图吉娅大声咳嗽了一声：“卡门……” 女男爵抿了抿嘴唇：“我正在思考该如何最好地表达我的意思，阿图吉娅，谢谢你。啊，这个所谓的‘托勒斯’，其实本名是迈克尔·奥古斯都斯·雷维拉…… 雷维拉！？” “——也就是说，他是我的一个远房表亲。他的父亲与鹰棘镇镇广场上那位被人们传颂的英雄是兄弟。当神战爆发时，那位英雄没有留下来保卫自己的故乡，而是带着孩子们逃往了南方。我只能……想象他在那些暗影的日子里心中所怀的恐惧。那时，天边没有一丝希望的光芒，也没有任何神明能够阻止那些来自幽冥的恶魔。但是现在，这位懦弱的骑士的后裔回来了，他要夺回他认为是自己与生俱来的权利——至少是鹰棘镇男爵爵位，如果不能夺回整个领地的话。" 你在开玩笑吧。” 卡门摇了摇头：“要是我在开玩笑就好了。当然，他声称自己拥有那个男爵爵位的说法完全是胡说八道——我的父亲曾经统治过这些土地，他的母亲之前也这么做过；但即使在他第一次来到这些地区的时候，我邀请他过来谈谈，试图帮助他摆脱那些使他产生这种错觉的心理创伤，他也不愿意听。他声称我至多是个骗子，然后怒气冲冲地离开了，还发誓鹰棘镇的人民很快就会表明他们愿意效忠于哪位领主。就连他也没想到，从那以后他的野心会遭到如此猛烈的打击。但从那以后，他一直留在那些边境地区，不断给我的领地带来麻烦，从蒂克里斯到梅登布里奇，到处都是他的捣乱行为。" [var0|更进一步来说，现在看来……] 女男爵放下杯子，交叉着双腿坐下，她的表情和当初阿图吉娅第一次带你来的时候一样严肃。“那么，事情的真相就是这样的[pc.name]我们三个人以及迈克尔本人，可能是北方唯一知道他真实身份的人。不过，究竟是什么驱使我的表弟走上这条疯狂的道路，我实在无法想象。我真希望能为他那些阴谋背后的原因和手段提供更多的帮助。

rows.original: "You know, Lady Evergreen said you two were friends..." Carmen immediately turns up her nose, revulsion plain on her face. "Oh. Her. Friend is a very strong word, [pc.name], but I do know Oxana Evergreen. The two of us served together during trying times, trying to protect the Marches — no, the whole of the north, even beyond the River Ridell when it flowed red with the blood of martyred heroes. We were both students, too, learning from the same mistress... though eventually, Lady Komari realized that our goals and hers were so far out of alignment that she cut us out completely, our knowledge left imperfect and incomplete. Where she sought balance in a time of chaos, Oxana and I both sought the power to confront the endless sea of sorrows that gripped the world and[silly |, by opposing, ] end them." The baroness's expression hardens. "Would that I could rid the world of Oxana's blight. Where Komari sought balance in all things, and I drew so fiercely on the light that it burned even those I cared for... that witch embraced the dark, sought to master it as if it were a tool. What mad hubris! Even after all these years I can still feel her festering on the edge of my senses just across the river like a wound in the soul of the world." What vitriol. "What did she do?" Carmen shakes her head. "She did what she promised. I can say that for her. The power she learned to wield from Komari was such that it dwarfed our own. But gods, the cost... no, I'll speak no more on this now. She keeps by and large to her side of the river, and so by my oath she can keep her secrets as long as she makes no threat against my people." Ominous indeed.
rows.translation: “你知道吗，常青女士说你们两个是朋友……” 卡门立即抬起鼻子，脸上嫌恶之情显而易见。“哦，她啊。[pc.name]，朋友这个词实在太过了，不过我确实认识奥克萨娜·常青。我们曾在艰难时期并肩作战，努力守护边疆——不，是守护整个北方；甚至在里德尔河被殉道英雄的鲜血染红时，我们仍战斗在河对岸。我们也曾一同求学，师从同一位导师……不过最终，麻里女士意识到我们的目标与她的理念相去太远，便彻底将我们逐出门下，令我们掌握的知识残缺不全。她在混乱年代追求平衡，奥克萨娜和我却都渴求足以对抗笼罩世界的无尽悲海，并将其[silly |以抗争的方式 ]终结的力量。” 女男爵的神情变得冷硬。“我真希望能让世界摆脱奥克萨娜的祸害。麻里追求万事万物的平衡；而我如此猛烈地汲取光芒，以至于连自己关爱的人都会被它灼伤……那个女巫却拥抱了黑暗，妄想像操纵工具一样驾驭它。何等疯狂的傲慢！即使过了这么多年，我仍能在感知边缘察觉她在河对岸溃烂滋生，如同世界灵魂上的一道伤口。” 好强烈的恨意。“她究竟做了什么？” 卡门摇摇头。“她兑现了自己的承诺，这一点我可以为她作证。她从麻里那里学会驾驭的力量，远远凌驾于我们之上。可是诸神在上，那代价……不，我现在不愿再谈。她基本待在河流自己那一侧；凭我的誓言，只要她不威胁我的人民，就可以继续保守自己的秘密。” 的确不祥。
rows.raw: ' "You know, Lady Evergreen said you two were friends..." Carmen immediately turns up her nose, revulsion plain on her face. "Oh. Her. Friend is a very strong word, [pc.name], but I do know Oxana Evergreen. The two of us served together during trying times, trying to protect the Marches — no, the whole of the north, even beyond the River Ridell when it flowed red with the blood of martyred heroes. We were both students, too, learning from the same mistress... though eventually, Lady Komari realized that our goals and hers were so far out of alignment that she cut us out completely, our knowledge left imperfect and incomplete. Where she sought balance in a time of chaos, Oxana and I both sought the power to confront the endless sea of sorrows that gripped the world and[silly |, by opposing, ] end them." The baroness's expression hardens. "Would that I could rid the world of Oxana's blight. Where Komari sought balance in all things, and I drew so fiercely on the light that it burned even those I cared for... that witch embraced the dark, sought to master it as if it were a tool. But gods, the cost... no, I'll speak no more on this now. She keeps by and large to her side of the river, and so by my oath she can keep her secrets as long as she makes no threat against my people." Ominous indeed. '

rows.translation: 常青女士？

rows.original: Evergreen called her a 'dear friend' the first time you met the witch. What's that all about?
rows.translation: 当你们第一次见到那位女巫时，常青女士称她为“亲爱的朋友”。这是怎么回事呢？
rows.raw: "Evergreen called her a 'dear friend' the first time you met the witch. What's that all about?"

rows.translation: 城堡的状况？

rows.original:
"Why don't you have people working here?" you ask. "There have to be villagers that would be willing to help here, clean the place up..."
        
        The baroness just waves a hand absently. "I am perfectly capable of keeping the castle myself. At least what parts I use. That alderman, Garth, offers every year or two to bring some men up to fix the walls. I have money, you're right, I could hire some peasant girls to come clean up, but I prefer my privacy. It's all so, so difficult now. I sleep more, as the years pass, walk fewer of the castle's rooms... what would be the point of dragging some maid up here every week to dust out a room I haven't used in — in a long time. It will just get dusty again before I need it."
        
        She suddenly seems much, much older than she looks, withdrawing into herself across the table from you and cradling her teacup. Her gray eyes are far away now, staring into the distance of time — but she shrugs it off with a little forced chuckle. "I appreciate your concern, but I am quite alright with what few companions I choose to retain here. I maybe have blue blood in my veins, but I'm a simple woman at heart, with few needs."
        
        "If you're sure..."
        
        "Quite."
rows.translation:
“为什么这里没有仆人干活？”你问道。“村里肯定有人愿意来帮忙，把这里打扫干净……”
        
        女男爵只是心不在焉地挥挥手。“我完全有能力自己照料城堡——至少是我会使用的那些部分。那个镇议员加斯每隔一两年都会提议带人上来修墙。你说得对，我有钱，也雇得起几个农家姑娘来打扫，可我更喜欢清静。如今一切都变得那么、那么艰难。年岁渐长，我睡得越来越久，走过的城堡房间却越来越少……每周硬把一个女仆拖上来，替我清扫一间我已经——已经很久没用过的房间，又有什么意义？等到我需要它时，那里早就又落满灰尘了。”
        
        刹那间，她看起来远比外表苍老得多。她坐在桌子对面，怀抱茶杯，整个人仿佛缩进了自己的世界。灰色双眼望向遥远之处，像是凝视着逝去的岁月；但她很快用一声勉强的轻笑将情绪抛开。“谢谢你的关心，不过，我很满意自己选择留在这里的寥寥几位同伴。我血管里或许流着贵族的蓝血，可归根结底，我只是个需求不多的普通女人。”
        
        “只要你确定……”
        
        “非常确定。”

rows.translation: 城堡的状况？

rows.original: So why is the castle is such a state of neglect? Surely there's some villagers that would be thrilled to come up and work as servants! She can't be lacking for money to pay them, right?
rows.translation: 那么，为什么这座城堡会落到这种被忽视的地步呢？肯定有些村民会很高兴来这里当仆人吧！她应该不缺钱来支付他们的工资吧？
rows.raw: "So why is the castle is such a state of neglect? Surely there's some villagers that would be thrilled to come up and work as servants! She can't be lacking for money to pay them, right?"

rows.translation: 她的提议……

rows.original: "So this offer you wanted to talk about...?" "Ah, yes," Carmen says, rising from her couch. Her long legs carry her to the window, heels click-clicking over the bare stone. "In my... in the old days of glory and empire, it was seen as gauche for Belharan lords to bloody their hands outside of war. Belhar was a nation of scholars and priests, brilliant craftsmen and poets... it outgrew its need for warlords. At least, that was the air the empire wished to present to what few lands lay beyond its borders. Still, a lord must have the skill and the will to resort to violence when it is called for. An agent that can handle troubles within and beyond her borders, who can dispense justice to the wicked and act as shield to the innocent. What were once judicial champions that settled disputes by armed challenge eventually grew into something much more." "I swore long ago," she continues, staring through the window, "that I would never again conjure spell or raise my blade to harm another. I thought I was protecting my barony, my people, but I see now that I cannot shield them with only money and well-wishes. They need a Champion. They need you." [var1 |"Well, I'm already the Champion of Frost..." "So I heard. A rider from the Winter City came down some time ago with the news. Another reason why I knew you were the one. If you can save a city, surely this little thorpe should be no trouble. Just a few thousand people, huddled behind their walls as the darkness encroaches. |"Me?" you ask, eyes wide. "You, [pc.name]. ] Nobody else has stood up for the people of Hawkethorne so courageously. Not Garth or his bloodthirsty family, not Brother Sanders in his old age, and certainly not me, curse my pacifism. You have already been their shield, their avenging [pc.isMage |magister |hero ]. I only wish to make it official — to let you proudly carry the hopes and dreams of this little barony on your shoulders, and to know that we all stand behind you. That is what I wish to give you." [pc.isDK |Well that doesn't sound worth very much, does it? ] [var0 |"I'm a [pc.mf |Baron |Baroness ] myself, you know," you say. "[pc.isBimbo |Isn't that like, gonna make people make fun of you and stuff? Sounds weak. |Doesn't that make you look weak? ]" Carmen smiles sadly. "I am weak, [pc.name]. I can't defend my people anymore. I am... I am so tired, [pc.name]. They need you far more than they think they want me, an impotent figurehead." ] Carmen turns back from the window, eyes warmer than you've ever seen them before. "You are the Champion the north needs, now more than ever. I only wish I could offer you more than a mere honorific to show my appreciation for what you have already accomplished."
rows.translation: 所以，你之前想谈的这个提议……是关于这个的吧？” “啊，没错，”卡门说着从沙发上站了起来。她修长的双腿将她带到了窗边，高跟鞋在光秃秃的石地上发出“咔嗒咔嗒”的声响。“在我们的……在我们那些辉煌与强盛的年代，对于贝尔哈兰的贵族们来说，在非战争场合弄脏自己的双手，被认为是很不体面的行为。贝尔哈尔是一个由学者、祭司、技艺高超的工匠和诗人组成的国家……这个国家已经不再需要军阀来统治了。至少，帝国希望向那些位于其边境之外的少数地区传达这样的信息。然而，无论如何，一位领主仍然必须具备在必要时使用暴力的能力和决心。这样一种代理人：它能够处理发生在其疆域之内或之外的各种问题，能够为恶人伸张正义，同时也能保护无辜者的安全。那些最初只是通过武力挑战来解决争端的司法捍卫者，最终已经发展成了更加重要的存在。很久以前我就发过誓，”她继续说道，目光透过窗户望着外面，“我再也不会使用魔法，也不会拔剑去伤害别人。我原以为自己在保护自己的领地、保护我的人民，但现在我明白了，仅仅依靠金钱和美好的祝愿，我是无法保护他们的。他们需要一位冠军。他们需要你。" [var1 |嗯，我已经是霜之冠军了……” “我是听说了。不久前有个来自冬城的使者带来了这个消息。这也是我确定你就是那个人选的原因之一。如果你能拯救一座城市，那么拯救这个小小的村庄应该也不是什么难事吧。不过这里只有几千人而已，他们只是躲在城墙后面，等待黑暗的降临罢了。 |我？”你瞪大了眼睛问道。 “就是你。[pc.name]。 ]没有人能像你这样勇敢地为鹰棘镇的人民挺身而出。无论是加斯和他那嗜血的家族，还是年迈的桑德斯修士，更不用说我这个总是崇尚和平的人了。你早已成为了他们的保护伞，成为了为他们报仇的人。 [pc.isMage |大师 |英雄 ]我只想正式地告诉你们——让你们能够自豪地将这个小领地的希望与梦想扛在肩上，同时也让你们知道，我们所有人都会支持你们。这就是我想要送给你们的东西。 [pc.isDK |嗯，这听起来似乎没什么价值，对吧？ ] [var0 |我是一个[pc.mf |男爵 |女男爵 ]你知道的，就是我自己，”你说。[pc.isBimbo |那样不是会让人嘲笑你吗？听起来太弱了。 |那样做难道不会让你显得软弱吗？ ]卡门悲伤地笑了笑：“我是弱小[pc.name]我再也无法保护我的人民了。我……我真的太累了。[pc.name]他们需要你的程度，远超他们想象中对自己这样的一个无能傀儡的需求。 ] 卡门从窗边转过身来，她的眼神比你以往任何时候见过的都要温暖。“你正是北方现在最需要的冠军。我只希望能给予你更多的东西，而不仅仅是一个荣誉头衔，来表达我对你已经取得的成就的感激之情。

rows.translation: 接受

rows.original:
You nod. "[pc.isDK
                |I guess another accolade in my belt can't hurt.
                |I'd be honored.
            ]"
            
            Carmen gestures to Tui, who has while you were speaking left and returned with a sword. It's a long, iron blade with a pronounced crossguard, clearly late Belharan in style. A blood-red pattern of roses have been engraved into the blade from guard to point, vines entwined around the fuller. 
            
            "Kneel, then, my Champion."
            
            You lower yourself before the baroness, and soon feel the cold metal of the sword against your shoulder as she speaks, "By the grace Seven Divines and the will of the Emperor, I — Baroness Carmen Reverra of Hawkethorne — do proclaim you as Champion of the Realm. May you be the shield of the innocent and the wrathful blade against the wicked, from this day until your last."
            
            The sword moves from one shoulder to the other as she speaks, before withdrawing at 'last.' Carmen smiles down at you, resting the blade's tip between her feet. "Rise, then, Champion of Hawkethorne. I bid you go now and serve the realm as you have been — protect us all from the demons at our doorstep."
rows.translation:
你点点头。“[pc.isDK
                |我想，腰带上再添一项荣誉也没什么坏处。
                |这是我的荣幸。
            ]”
            
            卡门朝阿图示意。方才你们交谈时，阿图已经离开，又带着一把剑返回。那是一柄修长的铁剑，十字护手格外醒目，显然采用了贝尔哈晚期的风格。剑身从护手到剑尖都刻着血红的玫瑰图案，藤蔓则缠绕着血槽。
            
            “那么，跪下吧，我的勇士。”
            
            你在女男爵面前俯身跪下，很快便感到冰冷的剑身贴上肩膀。她开口说道：“凭七神之恩典与皇帝之意志，我——鹰棘镇女男爵卡门·雷维拉——在此宣告，你将成为王国勇士。愿你从今日直至生命尽头，始终做无辜者的坚盾、斩向恶徒的怒刃。”
            
            她说话时，剑从你一侧肩头移向另一侧，直到“尽头”二字落下才收了回去。卡门微笑着俯视你，将剑尖抵在双脚之间。“那么，起来吧，鹰棘镇的冠军。我命你继续像以往那样为王国效力——保护所有人，抵御已经逼到家门前的恶魔。”

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original: A ceremonial title may still open doors, and at least let the people of Hawkethorne know that there is now someone who stands at their side as shield and sword against the demonic threat.
rows.translation: 一个象征性的头衔或许仍能打开一些门路，至少能让鹰棘镇的人们知道，现在有人愿意站在他们身边，成为抵御恶魔威胁的盾牌与利剑。
rows.raw: "A ceremonial title may still open doors, and at least let the people of Hawkethorne know that there is now someone who stands at their side as shield and sword against the demonic threat."

rows.translation: 拒绝

rows.original:
You shake your head, standing. "I'll pass."
            
            Carmen's lips draw taut. "I... I see. Go then. In my name or on your own initiative, you have served Hawkethorne. I can ask no more from the [pc.title] that's blown through my hamlet. I pray you continue your service, intentional or not. By all the gods, we would have been lost without you already."
            
            Fine, then. You turn and march off, back whence you came.
rows.translation:
你摇了摇头，站了起来：“我放弃吧。”
            
            卡门的双唇紧绷着：“我……我明白了。那你就去吧。无论是以我的名义，还是出于你自己的意愿，你都已经为鹰棘镇做出了贡献。对于你这位偶然来到我村庄的[pc.title]，我不能再要求更多了。我恳求你继续你的工作，无论你是出于有意还是无意。诸神在上，要是没有你，我们早就完了。”
            
            好吧，那你就转身回去吧，从你来的地方原路返回。

rows.translation: 神秘女郎

rows.original:
Your sleep is fitful, the roiling ache of desire in your stomach piercing the veil between wakefulness and dreams. Your body is just uncomfortable enough in your pent-up state that you can feel each rustle of fabric against your [pc.skin] as your fruitless tossing tangles your sweat-stained sheets. Eventually, you wake up — or at least, you think you do. The moon's silvery beams shine through the shutters of the Frost Hound's windows, dust particles floating softly in the light. 
    
    This moment is a rare vignette of peace for you: [pc.isDK
        |in between chasing down that demon bitch
        |in between trying to save the world from the influence of corruption
    ], you've barely had time to rest. Now, however, as you lay on your bed and look out at the inky black sky, you take a deep breath, savouring the serenity of the moment. 
    
    Something flickers in the corner of your vision, your muscles tensing[pc.hasEmoteEars

    "Thank you for that." The sun is beginning to rise behind her, and you can see it barely illuminate the bottom of her face, her plump red lips curled into an aristocratic smile. "If you ever want to visit me, [pc.name], my door is always open to you."
    
    You blink, and she's gone. You are still laying in bed, the blanket lovingly tucked over you as though you were a small child put to sleep by a parent; the sheets are as fresh and clean as they always are in the Frost Hound. Was that really just a dream? You can't think straight... sleep claws at your mind moments later, dragging you back into its dark embrace.
    
    Save for the bone-deep ache of satisfaction in your stomach, you have no proof of that strange nighttime encounter."

rows.original:
The inside of the chapel is the same bleak stone you imagine most churches to be made of, gray and weighing down on everyone inside. Vaulted arches support a roof high above you, decorated with beautiful bits of gilding and time-worn painting. The walls are draped with cloth and surrounded by candles, giving some measure of warmth to the otherwise stark place of worship. 
    
    Several semi-circular wooden pews are arranged facing a central altar in the middle of the temple, a large stone circle arrayed with statues of the seven gods and goddesses of Savarra. Each holds a colored candle and stares beatifically across the pews. [var0
        |A middle-aged human man is standing beside the altar, flipping through a huge leather-bound volume of prayers. He's wrapped in a soft white robe with dark red stripes down his arms and chest. An emerald-tipped staff leans against the stonework beside him, looking heavily worn from many years of hard use.
        |Brother Sanders is at his usual place beside the altar, white robes wrapped tight around himself and lost in contemplation of his tremendous prayer-book.
        |The church is quiet at this hour, with few supplicants to be seen. The priest has likely retired to his rectory for the night. You'll have to come back in the morning if you need his services.
        |The church appears to be empty at the moment. The priest has likely retired to his rectory for the night. You'll have to come back in the morning if you need his services.
    ]
rows.translation:
小教堂的内部采用了人们通常想象中的那种阴沉的石料建造，灰蒙蒙的颜色让身处其中的人感到压抑。高高的拱顶支撑着屋顶，上面装饰着精美的镀金纹饰和历经岁月洗礼的绘画作品。墙壁上悬挂着布幔，周围点着蜡烛，这使得这个原本显得冰冷肃穆的礼拜场所增添了几分温暖。 
    
    寺庙中央摆放着几排半圆形的木制长椅，这些长椅都朝向中央的祭坛；祭坛周围则是一个由巨石砌成的圆圈，上面刻着萨瓦拉七位神祇的雕像。每尊雕像手中都拿着一支彩色的蜡烛，凝视着对面的长椅，脸上洋溢着幸福的表情。 [var0

        |桑德斯修士像往常一样站在祭坛旁，白色长袍紧紧地裹在他身上，他正沉浸在对那本厚厚的祈祷书的沉思之中。

        |此刻，这座教堂看起来空无一人。牧师很可能已经回到他的住所过夜了。如果你需要他的帮助，就只好明天早上再来吧。
    ]

rows.original: You step through the doors of the chapel, entering a sanctuary of stone made warm and inviting by tapestries covering its stark walls and dozens of potted flowers growing in the windowsills. Several semi-circular wooden pews are arranged facing a central altar in the middle of the temple, a large stone edifice arrayed with statues of the seven Living Gods of Savarra. Each deity's statue holds a colored candle, and stares beatifically across the pews. A middle-aged man in a white and red robe is the only occupant, currently sweeping between the pews. He looks up at you with old blue eyes, and gives you a weary smile. "Ah, I'm sorry, I didn't hear you come in," he says with an apologetic smile, setting the broom aside and smoothing out his dusty robes. Now that he's turned to face you, you can see the priest is a very weathered man, with deep-set eyes and a full beard. His hair is cropped close to his skull, revealing a prominent widow's peak and receding temples all flecked with gray. You'd put him at about fifty years old, most of them hard. "I am Brother Riordan Sanders, of the Brothers of Ancient Velun. I manage the temple here, by the grace of the gods and our noble baroness. Is there anything I can do for you, my friend[party.som|||s]?" You introduce yourself, [pc.bg acolyte |and find yourself adding that you grew up in a monastery. It feels very... different... to finally find a temple again after so long on the road. "Ah, a [pc.mf |brother |sister ] of the faith," he smiles. "Likewise, it's very refreshing to see a [pc.mf |lad |lass ] of the cloth this far from the light of civilization. Please, stay awhile[silly | and listen |, I'd love to chat for a bit ]." Brother Sanders extends a calloused hand to you, which reveals him to be a surprisingly strong man when you shake it. |taking Sanders' hand once offered. His grasp is surprisingly strong for a village priest, [pc.bg barbarian soldier hunter |and he clasps your wrists in a warrior's shake, not that of a backwoods farmer |reminding you of a mercenary more than a backwoods farmer ]. ] "So," he says, "you must be Garth's long-slumbering guest! You had us all worried there, young [pc.mf|man|lady]." [party.has cait|"None more than me," Cait says, taking a seat in a pew beneath the statue of Mallach, god of passion and beauty. "But I never doubted."] You are glad to be in the land of the living once again. Sanders gives you a warm chuckle and a pat on the shoulder, leading you to a seat. "I can imagine. Sister Caitriss tended to you well, but I can safely say that even when I served the Order of the Oriflamme I never encountered such a flash of magic that could lay a [pc.mf|man|woman] out for a solid week. If you find yourself in need of further healing, please don't hesitate to come to me. My services I offer to any man or woman that walks through my door; Velun offers succor to all who enter his embrace. Further, if you can provide for the costs of ritual herbs and incense, I am also privy to many rites of blessing, and I know a few holy spells I can share, if you're of a mind to learn." Very useful indeed. What would you ask of the priest?

rows.translation: “[party.isJustPC|我|我们][pc.dcb| 需要治疗，牧师。现在就需要。|如果您能帮忙治愈的话，我将不胜感激。 [party.isJustPC|我的|我们的]伤口。|真的非常希望能有一些治愈魔法啊！]” 当然，当然。桑德斯微笑着，用他的手杖轻敲地面。请稍等片刻。让维伦的力量在你体内开始发挥作用，就像冬天让位于春天一样。 他闭上双眼，牧师法杖的翡翠尖端开始散发淡绿色的光芒。你感受到一股微弱的力量与热量从那光芒中传来，它们包围着你，让你沐浴在白色魔法的舒缓光芒之中。 [party.isJustPC|伤口带来的持续疼痛逐渐减轻，让你感觉身体恢复了许多。|你眼睁睁地看着你的同伴[party.oneCompanion|的|s]伤痕在桑德尔的魔法作用下逐渐消失了。] 就在那里。片刻之后，牧师睁开了眼睛，将手中的法杖放在一旁。那法杖散发出的神秘光芒逐渐消退，教堂重新恢复了原本清冷而通风的氛围。完好如新。或许你应该花几分钟时间，感谢卢米娅这位治愈女神，以及古老的维伦，感谢他们的恩赐，嗯？
rows.raw: ' "[party.isJustPC|I|We][pc.dcb| need healing, priest. Now.|'d appreciate it if you could heal [party.isJustPC|my|our] wounds.|'d like, really appreciate some healing magic!]" "Of course, of course," Sanders smiles, tapping his staff on the ground. "Just hold still a moment. Let Velun's regrowth take hold within you, as winter giving way to spring." He closes his eyes, and a pale green glow begins to radiate from the emerald tip of the priest's staff. You feel a faint pressure and heat rolling over you from it, bathing you in the soothing glow of white magic. [party.isJustPC|The lingering pain of your wounds abates, leaving you feeling much restored.|You watch as your companion[party.oneCompanion|'s|s'] injuries fade away, restored by Sander's magic.] "There," the priest says a few moments later, opening his eyes and setting his staff aside. The warmth of its arcane glow fades, restoring the chapel to its normal airy cold. "As good as new. Perhaps you'd take a few minutes to give thanks to Lumia, the healing maiden, and ancient Velun for their grace, hmm?"'

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original: "I'd like you to bless [party.isJustPC|me|us], Brother." "Of course," the priest says with a faint smile. "Please, sit. Sit." You do so, and hand Sanders the coin he needs. He gives you a slight nod, slipping it into his robe before grasping his staff in both hands. Closing his eyes with a long exhalation, Sanders plants his staff on the ground and begins to chant: "Gods of life and purity, though you hold all the world in your embrace, I beseech you: cast your eyes upon this [party.isJustPC|traveler|party], and see the truth of their soul[party.isJustPC||s]. I ask you safeguard them against the darknesses we face: temptations of the flesh, violence against the spirit, defilement of the soul. Let their soul[party.isJustPC||s] be incandescent in your eyes!" As he speaks, the emerald head of Sanders' staff begins to glow faintly, growing in intensity with each syllable until it is a radiant fire at the prayer's end.
rows.translation: 我希望您能赐予祝福。 [party.isJustPC|我|我们]兄弟。 当然。牧师带着一丝淡淡的微笑说道。请坐，请坐。 你这样做了，就把桑德斯所需要的硬币交给了他。他微微点了点头，将硬币放进自己的长袍里，然后双手握住手中的法杖。 桑德斯长长地呼出一口气，闭上了眼睛，将法杖插在地上，开始念诵咒语：生命与纯洁之神啊，尽管你们拥抱着整个世界，但我恳求你们：请注视一下这个[party.isJustPC|旅行者|派对]去探寻他们灵魂中的真相吧[party.isJustPC||]我请求你们保护他们，使他们免受我们所面临的那些黑暗力量的侵害：肉体的诱惑、对灵魂的暴力伤害、以及灵魂的玷污。请守护他们的灵魂。[party.isJustPC||]你的眼中闪烁着炽热的光芒！ 随着他的话语响起，桑德斯法杖上的那颗翡翠头开始发出微弱的光芒，每一个音节都会让光芒变得更加强烈，直到祈祷结束时，那光芒已经变成了耀眼的火焰。

He gives you a slight nod, slipping it into his robe before grasping his staff in both hands. Closing his eyes with a long exhalation, Sanders plants his staff on the ground and begins to chant: "Gods of life and purity, though you hold all the world in your embrace, I beseech you: cast your eyes upon this [party.isJustPC|traveler|party], and see the truth of their soul[party.isJustPC||s]. I ask you safeguard them against the darknesses we face: temptations of the flesh, violence against the spirit, defilement of the soul. Let their soul[party.isJustPC||s] be incandescent in your eyes!" As he speaks, the emerald head of Sanders' staff begins to glow faintly, growing in intensity with each syllable until it is a radiant fire at the prayer's end. '

rows.original: When he finishes you feel a slight breeze blow through the church, even though the doors are closed, making the candles flicker but not gutter. "There," Sanders says quietly, taking a deep breath. "I think Velun has smiled upon you, friend. Walk in nature's embrace."
rows.translation: 当他完成动作时，你会感觉到一阵微风穿过教堂，尽管门是关着的，但这阵风还是让蜡烛的火焰闪烁起来，却没有使它们熄灭。 “好了，”桑德斯深吸一口气，轻声说道。“我想维伦已经眷顾了你，朋友。让大自然拥抱你吧。”
rows.raw: ' When he finishes you feel a slight breeze blow through the church, even though the doors are closed, making the candles flicker but not gutter. "There," Sanders says quietly, taking a deep breath. "I think Velun has smiled upon you, friend. Walk in nature's embrace."'

rows.original: When he finishes and the light goes out of his staff, a heavy chill settles over the sanctuary. Sanders looks around, chuckles, and gives you an apologetic smile. "I'm not sure you've found the eye of one of the gods, friend. Only a pure soul is likely to attract their gaze — perhaps you have something you'd like to get off your chest?"
rows.translation: 当他完成动作后，他的法杖也随之熄灭了光芒，整个圣所顿时被一股刺骨的寒意笼罩。桑德斯环顾四周，轻笑了一声，然后向你露出了一个歉意的微笑。朋友，我不确定你是否真的找到了某位神明的注视之眼。只有纯洁的心灵才有可能吸引他们的注意——或许你有什么心事想要倾诉吧？
rows.raw: "\n When he finishes and the light goes out of his staff, a heavy chill settles over the sanctuary. Sanders looks around, chuckles, and gives you an apologetic smile. \"I'm not sure you've found the eye of one of the gods, friend. Only a pure soul is likely to attract their gaze — perhaps you have something you'd like to get off your chest?\""

rows.original: [flags.SANDERS_TALK_GODS |"So can you tell me about the gods themselves?" you ask. [pc.bg acolyte scholar |You're always interested in hearing others' takes on the identities of the gods. They do change somewhat from place to place. ] Sanders smiles benevolently. "Of course, of course. There are Seven gods worshipped across Savarra, and while their names and forms may change between cultures and languages, there's undeniable consistency in their identities. For simplicity, I'll speak of them as they're described by the folk of the Frost Marches here." Sanders ushers you over to the statues that ring the chapel, starting with one depicting an exaggeratedly voluptuous woman in heavy armor and graced with a sunburst halo. "Lumia, the Golden Knight, is the queen of the Seven. She is the goddess of the sun and granter of fertility. Hers is hearth and home, pregnant women, and farmers. Those seeking children, or protection for their families, pray to the queen of sunlight. Her servants are the valkyries, elven warrior-women with wings of light that descend from on-high to shield the innocent and helpless from evil." "Of course, Velun is the patron of this temple," Sanders continues, bringing you over to the second statue: that of a heavyset older man that seems to be half human and half tree, with bark-clad limbs and growths all around his body. "He is the patron of wild things: of storm and disease, of growth and renewal, and of animals great and small. He is kind but stoic... save when evil-doers seek to disrupt the natural order, to take more from nature than they need, and especially those that would destroy forests without thought of replenishment. We have a tense relationship with the village's logging camp, but the young men there support the village's existence... I pray Velun understands that we take only what we need to thrive beside his domain. When you are lost in the wilderlands, when you starve or thirst and need its bounty, give your prayers to the forest father. His chosen folk are of course the dryads, inexorably tied to the trees as they are." The next statue is that of a fox-earned man, dressed in flowing robes and ringed by nine incredibly fluffy tails. "Keros is the trickster, the god of deception and illusion and mysteries. He's perhaps the most feared of the gods by mortal folks like you and I, but also the one that intervenes among us most. If you pray to the sly fox, he might just answer your prayers — so word them carefully, lest you get exactly what you wished for! His folk are the kitsune, and he is patron of thieves, charlatans, and gamblers." Next, the effigy of a human woman dressed in a black hood, carrying a headsman's axe. The hem of her dress rides up her leg, revealing her stepping atop a skull. "That would be Tira; she is known as the Kingmaker but is more commonly known as the Goddess of Death and Time. She is patron to kings and soldiers, the arbiter of battlefields, the chooser of souls, and the enemy of the undead. Her actions may elevate an empire but it is also her axe that brings their end. She sings and hums melodies of death yet she cherishes life as it fulfills its role in the cycle. Nothing escapes her axe forever. Her zealots and paladins alike all have a profound respect for her. Many of them wield similar weapons and become as terrifying as the tales of Tira herself, hunting for battle and trying to erase the undead that slip through her grasp." The fourth statue is of a wild-looking winged woman, radiant in her nudity save for the curves of her wings shielding breast and loins from view. A spear is held aloft in her hands, and a hawk is perched on a wrist. "Sorra, goddess of the skies, is the chainbreaker — bringer of freedom and patron of slaves and explorers. Many adventurers worship her as well, as they venture far beyond the bounds of civilization and into wild and untamed lands. Her chosen people are the harpies, though I fear the ones around Hawkethorne aren't as they once were... I wonder if Sorra has abandoned them, or if some darker force is at work.[flags.SHAR_MET | At least that young woman, Shar, has given me some hope they yet may be saved. Hers is an innocent heart indeed. ] A statue of a catboy, dressed in fine nobles' silks and wearing a fanciful hat, is the next of the Seven. He couches a citole under an arm, and in the other, plays with a mane of dark, unkempt hair. "Mallach, the god of passion and love," Sander chuckles. "You've met one of his devout already, but in short, he is the god of poetry, song, and all other forms of artistry... and his followers have proven they can advance love-making into an art. He is the patron of bards and lovers, and of course all creative folks; anyone who pursues his passions, so long as they respect the body and soul of all other folk. There's no greater anathema to Mallach than one whose passions harm others: rapists and killers especially. He is, though rarely acknowledged as such, also the god of moderation." [party.has cait |Cait presses up to you with a playful smile. "If you ever want to know about Mallach as we teach him back in his great temple in Jassira, just ask me!" ] The last of the Seven is a serpentine woman, half snake and half chesty maiden from the waist up. She's clad in dark silks around her chest and midriff and precious little else. A staff is clutched in one of her hands, and a tome in the other. "Nareva, the mysterious goddess of secrets. Her domain is over knowledge and magic, but she guards her treasures closely! One must work tirelessly to pry the secrets of the world, or indeed of our very past, from her clutches... but she adores those that commit to the quest for knowledge. Prayers to her rarely bring revelation, but perhaps, she may put you on the path to discovering what you seek for yourself; that is her way. Nareva is the patroness of magicians, and of all reptilian kind — especially salamanders and dragons." |[pc.bg acolyte scholar |You ask Sanders to refresh you on the lore of the Living Gods |You ask Sanders to explain these Living Gods of his to you ]. "But of course," he smiles. Sweeping a hand to one of the old pews nearby, he beckons you to have a seat. The two of you sit, with the priest resting both hands heavily on his towering staff. "The gods, my dear [pc.boyGirl], are all around us. Their energy suffuses everything, from the air we breathe to the eldest oaks in the Frostwood — even the stone and wood of the town here. We priests and practitioners of white magic learn to tap into that energy, channel it into the minor miracles we call our spells. Despite this omnipresence, we call them the Living Gods, because this all-encompassing presence and power is but an afterimage of them, like steam radiating from a hotspring." You glance aside at Sanders, asking him to elucidate. "The truth of the gods," he answers, leaning against his staff, "is that they're not that different from you and I. Every bit as capable of being capricious, petty, caring, and kind as a mortal... because they are like mortals. Beings of flesh and blood who walk the world among us." If that's the case, and the gods are mortal and fallible... what do they do that is deserving of worship? The old priest chuckles. "What would make anyone — anything — worthy of worship? The gods guide us, show us the way to good and wise living. They grant us the power to heal and protect, to shape the world around us into one better and brighter than any that's come before. That, to me, is worthy enough." ]
rows.translation: [flags.SANDERS_TALK_GODS |那么，你能告诉我关于这些神明本身的故事吗？”你问道。 [pc.bg acolyte scholar |你总是很感兴趣地想听听别人对于这些神祇身份的看法。这些身份在不同的地方确实会有一些差异。 ] 桑德斯慈祥地笑了笑：“当然，当然。在整个萨瓦拉地区，人们崇拜着七神。虽然这些神明的名字和形象在不同文化和语言中会有所差异，但他们的本质特征却是始终如一的。为了方便起见，我就按照这里霜冻边境地区的居民对他们的称呼来来讲吧。 桑德斯带领你来到环绕小教堂的那些雕像前，首先看到的是一座雕像，上面描绘了一位身着厚重盔甲、身材极其丰满的女性，她的头顶还环绕着一圈光芒。“卢米娅，这位黄金骑士，正是七位女王中的首位。她是太阳女神，也是繁衍与丰收的象征。她的庇护范围包括家庭、孕妇以及农民们。那些渴望拥有孩子或希望保护家人的人，都会向这位阳光女神祈祷。她的仆从是那些拥有轻型之翅膀的精灵女战士——瓦尔基里们，她们从高处降临，保护无辜与无助的人们免受邪恶的侵害。" 当然，维伦就是这座寺庙的守护神，”桑德斯继续说道，然后带你来到了第二座雕像前：那是一座体型魁梧的老人雕像，看起来他一半是人类，一半是树木，四肢覆盖着树皮，全身还长满了枝叶。他是自然界万物的守护者：无论是风暴与疾病，还是生长与更新，无论大小动物，他都予以庇护。他仁慈而坚忍……除非那些作恶之人试图破坏自然秩序，从自然界索取超出他们所需的东西，尤其是那些肆意破坏森林却毫不考虑如何进行恢复的人。我们与那个村庄的伐木营地之间的关系相当紧张，但那里的年轻人们却支持这个村庄的存在……我希望维伦能够理解，我们只是取走那些对我们在他的领地旁边生存来说必不可少的东西。当你迷失在荒野中，当你饥渴难耐、需要那些自然资源来维持生命时，那就向森林之神祈祷吧。他选择的族群当然是那些与树木紧密相连的干尼亚德族。 下一座雕像描绘的是一个狡猾的狐妖化身的人类，他身披飘逸的长袍，周围环绕着九条蓬松得惊人的尾巴。“凯罗斯是欺骗与幻术之神，也是神秘与谜团的代表。对于你我这样的凡人来说，他或许是最令人畏惧的神明，但同时也是最经常介入我们人类事务的神灵。如果你向这只狡猾的狐妖祈祷，他或许会回应你的请求——所以一定要谨慎地表达自己的心愿，否则正是如此这就是你所祈求的！他的族人是狐妖，而他则是小偷、骗子以及赌徒们的庇护者。 接下来，出现了一个身穿黑色斗篷、手持刽子手斧头的女性人像。她的裙摆高高卷起，露出她的脚正踩在一只骷髅上。那就是蒂拉；她被称为“幕后操纵者”，但更广为人知的名字是“死亡与时间的女神”。她是国王与士兵们的庇护者，战场的裁决者，灵魂的抉择者，同时也是不死生物的敌人。她的行为或许能够建立一个帝国，但也正是她的行动导致了它的覆灭。她唱着象征死亡的旋律，却同样珍视生命，因为生命在这个循环中扮演着自己的角色。没有任何东西能够永远逃过她的掌控。无论是她的狂热追随者还是忠诚的骑士们，都对她怀有深深的敬意。他们中的许多人使用类似的武器，因此变得和蒂拉的故事中描述的那些生物一样可怕。他们四处寻找战斗机会，试图消灭那些从他们手中逃脱的不死生物。 第四座雕像描绘的是一位外形野性、身披羽翼的女性。她的身体赤裸，唯有双翼的轮廓将胸部和腰部遮挡起来。她手中高举着一支长矛，而一只鹰则栖息在她的手腕上。“索拉，天空的女神，是打破枷锁的力量——自由的象征，同时也是奴隶与探险者的守护者。许多冒险者也崇拜她，因为他们会冒险穿越文明的边界，进入那些荒野未开之地。她所选中的人类是鹰身女妖，不过恐怕鹰棘镇附近的那些鹰身女妖已经不再是以前的样子了。…我在想，是不是索拉抛弃了他们，又或者是有什么更阴暗的力量在暗中作祟。[flags.SHAR_MET | 至少那个年轻女孩，莎尔，给了我一些希望，让他们或许还能被拯救。她的心灵确实纯洁无瑕。 ] 下一位“七神”是一位穿着华丽贵族丝绸、头戴奇异帽子的猫人。他一只手臂下夹着一把西托尔琴，另一只手则摆弄着自己那一头浓密而凌乱的黑色头发。“玛拉赫，激情与爱情之神啊，”桑德轻声笑道。你们已经见过他的一个虔诚信徒了。简而言之，他就是诗歌、音乐以及所有艺术形式的守护神……而他的追随者们已经证明了：他们能够将恋爱提升为一种艺术。他是吟游诗人和恋人们的庇护者，当然也是所有富有创造力的人们的守护者；只要人们追求自己的热情，并且尊重他人的身体与灵魂，那么任何人都可以成为他的追随者。对马拉克来说，没有什么比那些让他人受到伤害的人更令他憎恶了——尤其是强奸犯和杀人犯。尽管这一点很少被人承认，但他其实也是节制与平衡的神明。 [party.has cait |凯特带着一丝俏皮的微笑走到你面前：“如果你想了解关于马拉克的事情——比如我们在贾西拉的大神殿里是如何教导他的，随时都可以问我哦！ ] 七人中的最后一位是一位身形如蛇的女性，腰部以上是半蛇半少女的形态。她的上半身裹着深色的丝绸，除此之外几乎不穿其他衣物。她一只手握着一根法杖，另一只手则拿着一本典籍。娜瑞瓦，这位神秘而隐秘的女神。她的领域涵盖了知识与魔法，但她会严密守护着自己的珍宝！要想从她手中揭开世界的秘密，或是我们自身过去的真相，人们就必须付出不懈的努力。…但她非常喜爱那些致力于追求知识的人。向她祈祷很少能带来启示，但或许，她能指引你找到自己真正追求的东西；这就是她的方式。娜瑞瓦是法师们以及所有爬行动物的守护者——尤其是火蜥蜴和龙。" |[pc.bg acolyte scholar |你请求桑德斯为你讲解关于“现世神祇”这一设定的背景故事 |你要求桑德斯向你解释他所说的这些“现世神祇”究竟是什么 ]。 但当然，他微笑着，伸手示意你坐在附近的一张旧长椅上。你们俩坐下来，而那位牧师则将双手重重地放在他那高大的权杖上。诸神啊，亲爱的[pc.boyGirl]这些力量无处不在，它们渗透到我们生活的方方面面——从我们呼吸的空气，到弗罗斯特伍德最古老的橡树，甚至包括这座小镇的石块与木材。我们这些祭司和白魔法师，就是学习如何汲取这些力量，将它们引导出来，从而创造出那些我们称之为魔法的“小奇迹”。尽管这种力量无处不在，但我们仍然称它们为“现世神祇”，因为这种无处不在的存在与力量，其实只不过是它们留下的痕迹，就如同温泉中蒸腾而出的水汽罢了。 你瞥了桑德斯一眼，让他解释清楚。 众神的真相他靠在手杖上回答道，原因就在于它们与我们人类并没有太大区别。它们同样有可能表现出反复无常、小心眼、关心他人或善良等特质……因为它们本质上与我们是一样的。是就像凡人一样。那些与我们一同生活在这个世界上的血肉之躯。 如果真是这样，如果神明也是会犯错、会死亡的……那么他们究竟有什么值得人们崇拜的地方呢？ 老牧师轻声笑了起来。究竟是什么会让人——任何人都……东西 — 值得被崇拜吗？神明引导我们，指引我们走向善良与智慧的生活。他们赋予我们治愈与保护的力量，让我们能够将周围的世界塑造得比以往任何时候都要美好、更加光明。对我来说，这就已经足够值得被崇拜了。 ]
rows.raw: ' [flags.SANDERS_TALK_GODS |"So can you tell me about the gods themselves?" you ask. [pc.bg acolyte scholar |You're always interested in hearing others' takes on the identities of the gods. They do change somewhat from place to place. ] Sanders smiles benevolently. "Of course, of course. There are Seven gods worshipped across Savarra, and while their names and forms may change between cultures and languages, there's undeniable consistency in their identities. For simplicity, I'll speak of them as they're described by the folk of the Frost Marches here." Sanders ushers you over to the statues that ring the chapel, starting with one depicting an exaggeratedly voluptuous woman in heavy armor and graced with a sunburst halo. "Lumia, the Golden Knight, is the queen of the Seven. She is the goddess of the sun and granter of fertility. Hers is hearth and home, pregnant women, and farmers. Those seeking children, or protection for their families, pray to the queen of sunlight. Her servants are the valkyries, elven warrior-women with wings of light that descend from on-high to shield the innocent and helpless from evil." "Of course, Velun is the patron of this temple," Sanders continues, bringing you over to the second statue: that of a heavyset older man that seems to be half human and half tree, with bark-clad limbs and growths all around his body. "He is the patron of wild things: of storm and disease, of growth and renewal, and of animals great and small. He is kind but stoic... save when evil-doers seek to disrupt the natural order, to take more from nature than they need, and especially those that would destroy forests without thought of replenishment. We have a tense relationship with the village's logging camp, but the young men there support the village's existence... I pray Velun understands that we take only what we need to thrive beside his domain. When you are lost in the wilderlands, when you starve or thirst and need its bounty, give your prayers to the forest father. His chosen folk are of course the dryads, inexorably tied to the trees as they are." The next statue is that of a fox-earned man, dressed in flowing robes and ringed by nine incredibly fluffy tails. "Keros is the trickster, the god of deception and illusion and mysteries. He's perhaps the most feared of the gods by mortal folks like you and I, but also the one that intervenes among us most. If you pray to the sly fox, he might just answer your prayers — so word them carefully, lest you get exactly what you wished for! His folk are the kitsune, and he is patron of thieves, charlatans, and gamblers." Next, the effigy of a human woman dressed in a black hood, carrying a headsman's axe. The hem of her dress rides up her leg, revealing her stepping atop a skull. "That would be Tira; she is known as the Kingmaker but is more commonly known as the Goddess of Death and Time. She is patron to kings and soldiers, the arbiter of battlefields, the chooser of souls, and the enemy of the undead. Her actions may elevate an empire but it is also her axe that brings their end. She sings and hums melodies of death yet she cherishes life as it fulfills its role in the cycle. Nothing escapes her axe forever. Her zealots and paladins alike all have a profound respect for her. Many of them wield similar weapons and become as terrifying as the tales of Tira herself, hunting for battle and trying to erase the undead that slip through her grasp." The fourth statue is of a wild-looking winged woman, radiant in her nudity save for the curves of her wings shielding breast and loins from view. A spear is held aloft in her hands, and a hawk is perched on a wrist. "Sorra, goddess of the skies, is the chainbreaker — bringer of freedom and patron of slaves and explorers. Many adventurers worship her as well, as they venture far beyond the bounds of civilization and into wild and untamed lands. Her chosen people are the harpies, though I fear the ones around Hawkethorne aren't as they once were... I wonder if Sorra has abandoned them, or if some darker force is at work.[flags.SHAR_MET | At least that young woman, Shar, has given me some hope they yet may be saved. Hers is an innocent heart indeed. ] A statue of a catboy, dressed in fine nobles' silks and wearing a fanciful hat, is the next of the Seven. He couches a citole under an arm, and in the other, plays with a mane of dark, unkempt hair. "Mallach, the god of passion and love," Sander chuckles. "You've met one of his devout already, but in short, he is the god of poetry, song, and all other forms of artistry... and his followers have proven they can advance love-making into an art. He is the patron of bards and lovers, and of course all creative folks; anyone who pursues his passions, so long as they respect the body and soul of all other folk. There's no greater anathema to Mallach than one whose passions harm others: rapists and killers especially. He is, though rarely acknowledged as such, also the god of moderation." [party.has cait |Cait presses up to you with a playful smile. "If you ever want to know about Mallach as we teach him back in his great temple in Jassira, just ask me!" ] The last of the Seven is a serpentine woman, half snake and half chesty maiden from the waist up. She's clad in dark silks around her chest and midriff and precious little else. A staff is clutched in one of her hands, and a tome in the other. "Nareva, the mysterious goddess of secrets. Her domain is over knowledge and magic, but she guards her treasures closely! One must work tirelessly to pry the secrets of the world, or indeed of our very past, from her clutches... but she adores those that commit to the quest for knowledge. Prayers to her rarely bring revelation, but perhaps, she may put you on the path to discovering what you seek for yourself; that is her way. Nareva is the patroness of magicians, and of all reptilian kind — especially salamanders and dragons." |[pc.bg acolyte scholar |You ask Sanders to refresh you on the lore of the Living Gods |You ask Sanders to explain these Living Gods of his to you ]. "But of course," he smiles. Sweeping a hand to one of the old pews nearby, he beckons you to have a seat. The two of you sit, with the priest resting both hands heavily on his towering staff. "The gods, my dear [pc.boyGirl], are all around us. Their energy suffuses everything, from the air we breathe to the eldest oaks in the Frostwood — even the stone and wood of the town here. We priests and practitioners of white magic learn to tap into that energy, channel it into the minor miracles we call our spells. Despite this omnipresence, we call them the Living Gods, because this all-encompassing presence and power is but an afterimage of them, like steam radiating from a hotspring." You glance aside at Sanders, asking him to elucidate. "The truth of the gods," he answers, leaning against his staff, "is that they're not that different from you and I. Every bit as capable of being capricious, petty, caring, and kind as a mortal... because they are like mortals. Beings of flesh and blood who walk the world among us." If that's the case, and the gods are mortal and fallible... what do they do that is deserving of worship? The old priest chuckles. "What would make anyone — anything — worthy of worship? The gods guide us, show us the way to good and wise living. They grant us the power to heal and protect, to shape the world around us into one better and brighter than any that's come before. That, to me, is worthy enough." ]'

rows.translation: 现世神祇

rows.original: Remembering the priest's first greeting, you ask who the %"baroness" is, exactly. You wouldn't have thought a province this far out in the wilderlands would have a proper lord. "Ah, yes," Sanders chuckles, idly glancing towards the eastern hills. "Truth be told, I think many of us were equally surprised. Hawkethorne was only founded a few years ago, built near to where the settlers believed an old imperial city used to be. When they arrived, the castle on the hill east of town seemed to be just another shadowy ruin, one of many in the region. In truth, though, the castle was — and is — still occupied by the descendants of the region's original barons from, oh, two hundred years ago at least." Two hundred years? That's a long time to be isolated out here, with nothing but orc barbarians and less than friendly lupine tribes around. The priest nods. "Indeed. It must have been quite the shock to find a human alive out here after so long. But Baroness Reverra was not only alive, but quite well off from what I understand. Enough so that when the settlers talked of building the village, she gladly contributed to the cost of building from her own coffers. Indeed, she funded the construction of this temple entirely. A woman of deep faith, that one." Aside from her faith, you ask if there's anything Sanders can tell you about her. "Not all that much, truth be told," he answers. "Baroness Reverra largely keeps to herself in the castle; she takes few visitors. As far as I can tell she lives alone save for a single bodyguard, and I've never seen the fellow up close or without his helm or hood. It's quite the large castle for just the two of them, and the state of it reflects that. The place is falling apart, though she seems content to let it collapse around her. Garth and myself have both offered to round up some of the villagers to fix the place up, but Carmen has politely declined us both." Strange. "Does she just like living in a ruin?" "Perhaps she just likes her privacy more," Sanders chuckles. "After generations of solitude, I can understand not wanting dozens of strangers crawling over your home. Besides, the baroness has done more than enough for us that we ought to respect her wishes, as queer as they may be."
rows.translation: 想起那位神父最初的问候，你便询问这位“男爵夫人”到底是谁。你根本没想到，在这片荒野地区的边远省份，竟然会有一位真正的领主。 啊，是的。桑德斯轻笑着，漫不经心地望向东边的山丘。说实话，我觉得我们很多人都很惊讶。鹰棘镇这个地方是几年前才建立起来的，它建在那些移民们认为曾经有一座古老帝国城市存在的地方附近。当他们到达那里时，镇东那座山上的城堡看起来只不过是众多废墟中的一座罢了。但实际上，这座城堡至少在两百年前，就已经被这个地区最初的男爵们的后裔们占据了——而且至今仍然有人居住在那里。 两百年？在这里与世隔绝，周围只有兽人野蛮人和并不友好的狼族部落，这样的日子实在太长了。 牧师点了点头。确实如此。在这么久之后还能在这里发现一个活着的人类，想必是一件令人震惊的事情。但据我所知，雷薇拉女男爵不仅活了下来，而且生活得相当富裕。以至于当那些定居者讨论建造村庄的事情时，她非常乐意自掏腰包来承担建设费用。事实上，这座寺庙的全部建造资金都是由她提供的。真是一位信仰坚定的女性啊。 除了她的信仰之外，你还想知道桑德斯是否能告诉你关于她的其他什么信息。 说实话，也没那么多。他回答道。雷维拉女男爵在城堡里大多时间都独来独往，很少接待访客。据我所知，她除了有一名保镖外，几乎是独自生活着的，而我从未有机会近距离看到那名保镖，也从未见过他摘下头盔或兜帽的样子。对于仅仅两个人来说，这座城堡实在太大了一些，而它的现状也恰恰反映了这一点。这个地方已经破败不堪了，但她似乎并不在意让它继续倒塌下去。加斯和我都提出过要召集一些村民来修理这个地方，但卡门礼貌地拒绝了我们的帮助。 奇怪。她就是喜欢住在废墟里吗？ 也许她只是更喜欢保持自己的隐私罢了。桑德斯轻声笑了起来。经过数代人的孤独生活，我完全能够理解为什么有人不愿意让成群陌生的闯入自己的家园。更何况，那位女男爵为我们做了太多，我们理应尊重她的意愿，无论这些意愿看起来有多么奇怪。

rows.translation: 女男爵

rows.original: "When we met, you said something about having been a Flamebearer?" you ask. "What's that[pc.isBimbo|, like, all about and stuff][pc.isDK| supposed to be]?" Sanders runs a hand over the weathered head of his staff as he answers, "The Most Righteous Order of the Oriflamme. A crusader order formed by the Dawnbringer, Lumia, centuries ago to fight back the blight that swallowed Belhar and much of the world. Though the goddess has long since left our side, and the threat of wraiths and dark horrors like them has passed, the Order persists. Now we fight raiders and the lesser monsters that still threaten villages such as this, far from the protective care of a kingdom or empire." Quite the noble goal, though you've seen no white knights this far from the heartland of humanity. "What brought you out here, then?" "Retirement," the old man laughs. "I left the Order five years ago, back to the life of a mere priest now that my days as a warrior are behind me." Heading off your inevitable question, he adds, "The Order is made up entirely of trained priests and priestesses who find their calling to be a more... martial application of the faith. We leave the churches and cloisters for a while to bright the light and guidance of the gods out into the world, and to shield the faithful from those who would do them harm. When that time ends, we hang up our armor and don our robes once again." Curious, you ask what caused Sanders to want to join the Order. Why didn't he just stay a priest? Sanders gives you a faint, almost sad smile. "That.... that's a story for another time, my friend." Something tells you that you aren't getting more out of him on that front. For now, at least.
rows.translation: 我们见面时，你提到自己曾经是一名火焰使者，对吧？你说呢。那是什么？[pc.isBimbo|就是，所有这些相关的内容啦。][pc.isDK| 按理说应该是]？" 桑德斯一边回答，一边用手轻轻抚摸着自己那布满皱纹的员工们的头。圣焰最正义骑士团。这个十字军组织是由黎明使者与卢米娅在几个世纪前创立的，其初衷便是对抗那些吞噬了贝尔哈尔以及世界上许多地区的灾祸。虽然那位女神早已离开了我们的行列，那些幽灵与暗影怪物带来的威胁也早已消失，但这个骑士团依然存在。如今，我们仍在与那些袭击村庄、威胁普通民众的低级怪物作斗争——而这些地方，早已远离任何王国或帝国的保护与庇佑。 确实是个崇高的目标，不过在人类文明的中心地带之外，你恐怕还从未见过那些“白衣骑士”吧。那么，是什么让你来到这里的呢？ 退休，老人笑了。五年前，我离开了那个组织，现在重新过上了普通牧师的生活，因为我作为战士的日子已经结束了。 为了避免你们肯定会问到的问题，他补充道：这个组织完全由受过训练的男祭司和女祭司组成，他们认为将自己的信仰应用于战斗领域才是真正的使命。我们会暂时离开教堂和修道院，将神明的光芒与指引带到世间，保护信徒们免受那些伤害他们的人的侵害。当这个使命完成之后，我们就会再次穿上盔甲，恢复祭司的身份。 你好奇地问，究竟是什么让桑德斯想要加入这个组织。他为什么不继续当一名神父呢？ 桑德斯只是给了你一个淡淡的、近乎伤感的微笑。那个……这个故事改天再讲吧，我的朋友。 你有种感觉，至少在目前来说，你无法从他那里得到更多东西。

rows.original:
"Ah, Eryka," Sanders says proudly, glancing at where the ginger crusader's currently buried in her books. "I'm thankful you brought her home, [pc.name]. As is her grandfather. The village wasn't quite the same without her."
    
    Would he mind telling you a little about her?
    
    Sanders chuckles. "Well, she's right there, my [pc.boyGirl]. You could ask her yourself! But, ah, I suppose I do have a different perspective on things.[liaden.atChapel
        | It's hard to believe how much longer I've known my young apprentice than my own child. They're about the same age, too.
    ] [eryka.hasCock
        |Though I could swear something's gotten into her since you brought her home. She's been vacillating between fidgeting up a storm and spending hours meditating, and it's hard to get her to practice her blade where once it was all she wanted to do!
        |And thanks to you, she's back to her old self once again!
    ] I've been training her for near on a decade now, you know. Gods, but time does fly."
    
    That long, huh?

啊，艾瑞卡，”桑德斯自豪地说，同时瞥了一眼那位金发女战士此刻正埋头读书的地方，“我很感激你把她带回了家。[pc.name]就像她的祖父一样。没有她，这个村子就不再是一样的了。”
    
    他介意跟你讲讲她的事情吗？
    
    桑德斯笑了笑：“嗯，她就在我身边啊。[pc.boyGirl]你可以亲自去问她啊！不过，嗯，我想我对这些事情的看法确实有所不同。[liaden.atChapel
        | 真难以相信，我和我的年轻学徒相识的时间，竟然比我和自己孩子的相识时间还要长。他们的年龄也差不多。
    ] [eryka.hasCock
        |我发誓，自从你把她带回家之后，她似乎发生了什么变化。她要么坐立不安，要么花好几个小时冥想，而且现在很难让她去练习剑术了——而以前，练习剑术可是她最热衷的事情啊！
        |多亏了你，她终于恢复到了以前的状态！
    ]你知道，我已经训练她将近十年了。天啊，时间过得真快。
    
    这么久啊？
    
    他点了点头：“是的。她六岁的时候，她的母亲把她带到了这里，然后第二年就去世了。我从未认识过艾瑞卡的父亲，但她在年轻时以及中年时期，我确实见过她的母亲。真的，母女俩长得太像了：她们的性格都充满激情，无论是言行还是外貌，都显得十分热烈；显然，她们认为只有歌声或呐喊，才能打破那种沉寂。哦，自从她去世后，她的父亲就变得不再像从前那样了。那些该死的发烧症状……
    
    那么，他应该很了解艾瑞卡的家人了。
    
    “她的祖父和我曾经一起工作过一段时间。他是个……”桑德斯停顿了一下，用手捋了捋胡子，“他是个好人，但有些技能让正派的人会嗤之以鼻：开锁、跟踪之类的本事。我帮助他改过自新，过上了诚实的生活，看到他安定下来并组建家庭，我感到非常高兴。他学习了木工手艺，结婚了，有了萨拉——也就是艾瑞卡的母亲——以及他的儿子们。几年后，我们在鹰棘镇再次相遇，这纯粹是巧合；而更让我开心的是，萨拉和艾瑞卡选择来到这里定居，与艾薇丽丝夫人一起生活。当萨拉经过时，艾瑞卡显得闷闷不乐，显然她需要一些东西来为自己的生活带来一丝希望，一些值得追求的目标。因此，她的祖父把她带到了我面前，请求我开始训练她，让她成为一名织布工。我立刻就意识到，她根本没有成为一名谦逊的乡村女祭司的资质！不，她太有主见了，和她母亲一样；同时，她的身体素质也像她父亲一样强健。这样的性格和体魄，最适合成为一名圣骑士，于是她最终也成为了圣骑士。"
    
    神父自豪地望着小教堂的另一边，说道：“她是个好女孩。[pc.name]，她对我来说非常珍贵，这份感情深埋在我心中。能够让她回到我身边，我真是太高兴了。

rows.original: You glance over to where Liaden is sweeping the chapel's front porch and ask Sanders how it is that he's had a beautiful daughter all these years and never knew she even existed? Sanders laughs awkwardly and worries at the collar of his frock. "The realities of spending your life traveling, I suppose. Liaden's mother, Lyana, is a paladin of Lumia, just as I was before I became the shepherd of this village. We trained together from the days we could barely lift our lances to the day we both took our vows — to protect the innocent and defend the weak wherever the sun shone. But those self-same vows meant that we were destined to part, to each carry Lumia's torch to our own part of the world. I went north, and she went west." "Lyana was..." he sighs, leaning against the lectern and watching Liaden work. "She was my best friend. There were other women in my life after her, I suppose, but Lyana was the only one who ever captured my heart. But I never knew she had a child at all, much less mine. I suppose... I suppose it was very like her, to not wish to part me from my destiny. Perhaps she heard the stories of my exploits, of the people I was helping, and decided to withhold Liaden's existence. Or as Lia herself says, simply never had a way to tell me. I was always on the move as a young man, and as the years passed, my reports to the other paladins became less and less frequent." Would he have done things differently, if he'd known?" "Goddess take me, but if I had known that she was with child when we parted, I would have cut my way across Belhar and all the Marches to see Lyana again!" Sanders says firmly, shaking his head. "Had I heard a word of it, I would have been there for her. For both of them. And now that I know Lyana is putting down roots in Maidenbridge, you can rest assured I've sent her a stern letter... and a heartfelt request that she come and speak in person. In the meantime... it seems Liaden intends to stay in Hawkethorne.[var0| No doubt thanks, at least in part, to that charming hornet knight of yours. It seems my girl's quite taken with the lady Azyrran!] I'm truly thankful for the opportunity to make up for lost time with her while it lasts, though. Twenty years of lost time, can you believe it!" He shakes his head and smiles at Lia as she comes back in, broom over her shoulder like it's her poleaxe. "What're you two whisperin' about?" Nothing, nothing...
rows.translation: 你望向正在清扫教堂前廊的莉娅登，问桑德斯：这么多年来，他明明有个漂亮女儿，怎么会连她的存在都一无所知？ 桑德斯尴尬地笑了笑，不安地扯着法衣的领口。“这大概就是常年漂泊的代价吧。莉娅登的母亲莉安娜和我一样，曾是卢米娅的圣骑士——直到后来，我才成了这座村庄的牧者。从我们还勉强举得起长枪时起，就一直在一起训练，直到共同立下誓言的那一天：在阳光所及之处保护无辜、捍卫弱者。可也正是这份誓言注定了我们必须分别，各自把卢米娅的火炬带往世界的一方。我去了北方，她则去了西方。” “莉安娜她……”他叹息着，靠在讲经台旁，注视着忙碌的莉娅登。“她曾是我最好的朋友。后来我的生命里大概也出现过其他女人，但只有莉安娜真正俘获过我的心。可我从不知道她有个孩子，更别说那孩子还是我的。我想……我想这确实很像她的作风，不愿让我偏离自己的使命。也许她听说了我的事迹，知道我帮助过的那些人，于是决定对我隐瞒莉娅登的存在。又或许就像莉娅自己说的，她只是一直没有办法把消息告诉我。年轻时的我总在四处奔波，随着岁月流逝，我向其他圣骑士递交报告的次数也越来越少。” 如果他早些知道，会作出不同的选择吗？” “愿女神宽恕我，但如果分别时我知道她怀了孩子，我就是一路杀穿贝尔哈和整个边境地区，也要再见莉安娜一面！”桑德斯坚定地说道，同时摇了摇头。“只要我听到半点消息，就一定会陪在她身边——陪在她们母女身边。现在我知道莉安娜准备在梅登布里奇安顿下来，你大可放心：我已经给她寄去一封严肃的信……以及一份诚挚的请求，希望她能亲自过来谈谈。与此同时……莉娅登似乎打算留在鹰棘镇。[var0|这肯定至少有一部分要归功于你那位迷人的黄蜂骑士。看来我家姑娘相当迷恋阿兹兰女士！]不管怎样，只要她还留在这里，我都由衷感激能有机会弥补失去的时光。整整错过了二十年，你敢相信吗！” 他摇摇头；莉娅回来时，他看着她露出微笑。她把扫帚扛在肩上，仿佛那是自己的长柄斧。 “你们俩在嘀咕啥呢？” 没什么，没什么……

rows.original:
You ask Sanders if he has a moment to speak. In private.
    
    "[pc.name]? Is everything alright? No, hmm... [flags.LIADEN_SANDERS|Liaden, dear, mind the chapel for a bit while I speak with our friend here.|Well, what is a priest if not private counsel!]"
    
    The older man ushers you off to the small side office off the sanctuary and closes the door. It's a small, cozy little room, full of paper and candles and chests that, now that you think about it, probably contain the arms and armor of a warrior under those heavy brass locks. When Sanders quirks a brow at you, gesturing for you to speak, you tell him bluntly that you found Gweyr up on the Rift, and that she told you her story. All of it.
    
    "Ah," he nods solemnly. "Well. I'm glad you had the chance to meet. It seems you and she have some common interests these days."
    
    And he didn't think to mention these interests at any previous point?
    
    Sanders sighs. "I had thought that dark stain on our village's history was behind us. You're right, though, I have done you and Cait a disservice by holding my tongue about the matter. Still, it hardly seemed relevant. We never captured this 'master' Tollus, nor found any trace of where he might have gone or what he was trying to do beyond his temporal designs on Castle Hawkstone. Knowing what Garth, River, and I know would not have helped you much, would it?"
    
    Maybe, maybe not, but you do feel a bit lied to. 
    
    Sanders takes that to heart, wincing and putting a hand to his chest. "I am sorry, my friend. Please understand, what happened that day between Gweyr and the young villagers... bearing witness to such wanton slaughter was enough to make me set aside my paladin vows. It drove most of the settlers back then away, over time, such that the village nearly failed entirely. It wasn't until Lady Ivris came north with fifty Belharan refugees that we began to recover. We..."
    
    The old man shakes his head sadly. "And now I'm making excuses for myself like a chastised squire. Please, accept my apology, [pc.name]."
rows.translation:
你问桑德斯是否有时间谈谈。私下谈。
    
    “[pc.name]？一切都还好吗？不，嗯……[flags.LIADEN_SANDERS|莉娅丹，亲爱的，我和这位朋友谈话时，麻烦你照看一下礼拜堂。|好吧，牧师的职责不正包括私下为人排忧解难吗！]”
    
    老人领你来到圣殿旁的小办公室，关上房门。那是一间小巧舒适的屋子，到处堆着纸张、蜡烛和箱子；仔细想来，那些箱子上挂着沉重的黄铜锁，里面多半装着战士的武器与护甲。桑德斯挑眉示意你开口，于是你直截了当地告诉他，自己在裂隙上找到了格薇尔，她还向你讲述了自己的故事。全部故事。
    
    “啊，”他神情严肃地点点头。“好吧。很高兴你们有机会见面。看来，如今你和她有了一些共同目标。”
    
    而此前他从没想过提起这些目标吗？
    
    桑德斯叹了口气。“我原以为村庄历史上的那道黑暗污点已经成为过去。不过你说得对；在这件事上保持沉默，确实亏欠了你和凯特。只是，它几乎与眼下的事情毫无关系。我们从未抓住那位‘导师’托勒斯，也没找到任何线索，说明他去了哪里，或者除了暂时觊觎鹰石城堡之外还想做什么。即使你知道我、加斯和瑞弗所知道的一切，也不会得到多少帮助，对吧？”
    
    或许如此，或许不是；但你确实觉得自己受到了欺骗。
    
    桑德斯将你的话听进了心里；他痛苦地皱起脸，一只手按住胸口。“对不起，我的朋友。请你理解，那天格薇尔与年轻村民之间发生的事情……仅仅目睹那般肆意屠杀，就足以让我放弃圣骑士誓言。随着时间推移，它迫使当时的大多数定居者离开，村庄几乎彻底消亡。直到艾薇莉丝女士带着五十名贝尔哈尔难民来到北方，我们才开始恢复。我们……”
    
    老人悲伤地摇摇头。“现在，我却像个受训斥的侍从一样为自己找借口。[pc.name]，请接受我的道歉。”

rows.original:
"It's okay," you tell him, putting a hand on Sander's shoulders.
        
        The priest smiles warmly. "I thank you, [pc.name]. In the years since Gweyr's exile, Garth and I have been this village's first line of defense against a darkness that seems ever deeper as the years pass, growing closer with every winter. I am glad to have someone like you around now, someone young and capable, to take up a burden I fear neither of us was ever fit to shoulder. There was a time I was called a hero, a Warrior of White, paladin of Lumia... but Gweyr was right, in that my idealism made me too weak, too easily torn between ideal and reality. And Garth isn't much harder than I am, despite outward appearances. We've both had blood on our hands more than once over the decades, but even the best bronze bends. Gweyr was hard iron, though, strong and sturdy until she broke. I earnestly wish things could have been different, but..."
        
        But if they had, Tollus might well be ruling this barony now.
        
        Sanders nods. "I fear you're right. Still, though, if I hadn't sent Gweyr to walk the ice, she'd have taken a knife at some point soon after that day. Either in the back or while she slept... or worse, the villagers' anger would have boiled over to her children. I can't say it's 'better' this way, but... but some stories don't have happy endings. Even those about old mystical knights and bright-eyed young adventurers."
        
        [pc.dcb
            |Maybe, but you're going to make your own happy ending. You're sure of it.
            |Hopefully your story will, at least...
            |Aww, that's so sad. Poor Sanders! You can't help but leap up and give him a big ol' hug to set his mind at ease. You're gonna have a happy ending and drag him along for the ride, too!
        ]
        
        Sanders chuckles softly. "I hope so, [pc.name]. I really do. So, shall we step out?"
        
        You let him lead you back to the nave.
rows.translation:
没关系，”你把手放在桑德的肩上，对他说。
        
        神父温暖地笑了：“谢谢你。[pc.name]自从格维尔被流放以来，加斯和我一直担任着这个村庄的第一道防线，抵御着那种似乎随着岁月流逝而愈发浓厚的黑暗势力——每到冬天，这种黑暗似乎都会离我们更近一些。现在有你这样的年轻人加入我们，真是太好了。你年轻又有能力，能够承担起这个恐怕我们俩都无力承担的重担。曾经有一段时间，人们称我为英雄，称我为“白色战士”，称我为卢米亚的守护者……但格维尔说得对，正是我的理想主义让我变得过于软弱，让我在理想与现实之间难以做出抉择。而加斯，尽管外表上看似坚强，其实也并不比我强多少。这些年来，我们俩都曾不止一次地手上沾满鲜血，但即便是最坚硬的青铜也会弯曲。然而，格维尔却如同硬铁一般，坚强而坚固，直到最终断裂。我真心希望事情本可以有所不同，但是……
        
        但如果他们那么做了，现在统治这个领地的很可能就是托勒斯了。
        
        桑德斯点了点头：“恐怕你说得对。不过，如果我没有派格维尔去冰原上执行任务，她很可能在那天之后不久就被刺杀了。要么是在她背后做那种事，要么就是趁她睡觉的时候……更糟糕的是，村民们的愤怒可能会波及到她的孩子们。我不能说这种方式“更好”，但是……有些故事就是没有幸福的结局。即使是那些关于古老神秘骑士和充满活力的年轻冒险者的故事也不例外。"
        
        [pc.dcb
            |也许吧，但你会自己创造属于你的幸福结局。你对此深信不疑。
            |希望你的故事至少也能如此……
            |哎呀，真让人难过。可怜的桑德斯！你肯定会忍不住站起来，给他一个大大的拥抱，让他安心下来。你一定会得到幸福的结局，而且也会让他一起分享这份幸福哦！
        ]
        
        桑德斯轻声笑了笑：“但愿如此。[pc.name]我是真的这么想的。那么，我们出去吧？”
        
        你让他带着你回到了教堂的主厅。
rows.raw:
"
        "It's okay," you tell him, putting a hand on Sander's shoulders.
        
        The priest smiles warmly. "I thank you, [pc.name]. In the years since Gweyr's exile, Garth and I have been this village's first line of defense against a darkness that seems ever deeper as the years pass, growing closer with every winter. I am glad to have someone like you around now, someone young and capable, to take up a burden I fear neither of us was ever fit to shoulder. There was a time I was called a hero, a Warrior of White, paladin of Lumia... but Gweyr was right, in that my idealism made me too weak, too easily torn between ideal and reality. And Garth isn't much harder than I am, despite outward appearances. We've both had blood on our hands more than once over the decades, but even the best bronze bends. Gweyr was hard iron, though, strong and sturdy until she broke. I earnestly wish things could have been different, but..."
        
        But if they had, Tollus might well be ruling this barony now.
        
        Sanders nods. "I fear you're right. Still, though, if I hadn't sent Gweyr to walk the ice, she'd have taken a knife at some point soon after that day. Either in the back or while she slept... or worse, the villagers' anger would have boiled over to her children. I can't say it's 'better' this way, but... but some stories don't have happy endings. Even those about old mystical knights and bright-eyed young adventurers."
        
        [pc.dcb
            |Maybe, but you're going to make your own happy ending. You're sure of it.
            |Hopefully your story will, at least...
            |Aww, that's so sad. Poor Sanders! You can't help but leap up and give him a big ol' hug to set his mind at ease. You're gonna have a happy ending and drag him along for the ride, too!
        ]
        
        Sanders chuckles softly. "I hope so, [pc.name]. I really do. So, shall we step out?"
        
        You let him lead you back to the nave. 
        "

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original: You know Gweyr put Sanders in a tough spot, and her actions clearly traumatized him. It's okay.
rows.translation: 你知道，格维尔让桑德斯陷入了困境，她的行为显然给他带来了心理创伤。不过，这也没关系。
rows.raw: "You know Gweyr put Sanders in a tough spot, and her actions clearly traumatized him. It's okay."

rows.translation: 但是格维尔！！

rows.original: No, you aren't just accepting that without giving Sanders a piece of your mind. He tore apart Garth's family, could have sent Gweyr to her death, and for what!? "For her life!" Sanders snaps back, suddenly finding his fire again. "If she'd stayed in this village, surrounded by the parents of children she slaughtered, Gweyr would have caught a knife within a month — in the neck as she slept or in the back while she worked. Or worse, their anger would have found its way to her children, to Garret and Gwyneth! Gweyr knew it too. Knew she'd have to leave to protect them. You didn't... [pc.name], you didn't see the bodies! Gweyr isn't just a warrior, she's a butcher, tore them to pieces like a feral wolf into sheep. You can't unsee that, can't unhear the screams. I know I couldn't. I still can't! Do not lecture me on righteousness when you haven't put half a village's children into a mass grave with your own hands!" Sanders snarls, fists tightening... and then the fury breaks, and the old man slumps back against the door, breathing hard. "There was a time I was called a hero, a Warrior of White, paladin of Lumia... but Gweyr was right, in that my idealism made me too weak, too easily torn between ideal and reality. That's why I swore off Lumia's order, hung up my blades and armor. She proved I was too weak for this. That not all stories of mystic knights and dark sorcerers have happy endings. Some fairy tales are just sick mockeries." The old man turns and leaves, head hanging low. [flags.LIADEN_SANDERS |When you come out of his office, Liaden is leaning against the wall beside the door, arms crossed. "What was that ruckus all about?" she asks, glancing between you and her father. "Never seen Pa that huffy about anything." You just shake your head. Old business from the village's history, she'll have to ask her father directly. "Sheesh. Alright, alright. Just go easy on him, I didn't come all the way up here just for the old guy to have a heart attack. Okay?" Alright, alright... ]
rows.translation: 不，你不能就这样接受，而不把心里的话告诉桑德斯。他拆散了加斯的家庭，甚至可能把格薇尔送去送死——这一切究竟是为了什么！？ “为了让她活命！”桑德斯厉声反驳，突然重新燃起怒火。“如果她留在村里，被那些遭她屠杀的孩子的父母包围，不出一个月，格薇尔就会挨上一刀——要么睡梦中被割开喉咙，要么干活时从背后中刀。更糟的是，他们的怒火可能会殃及她的孩子，殃及加勒特和格温妮丝！格薇尔自己也明白。她知道，为了保护孩子，自己必须离开。你没有……[pc.name]，你没见过那些尸体！格薇尔不只是战士，她是个屠夫，像野狼扑进羊群一样把他们撕成碎片。那种景象永远无法忘记，那些尖叫也永远无法从耳中消失。我做不到。直到现在仍然做不到！你没有亲手把半个村庄的孩子埋进集体坟墓，就别来教训我何谓正义！” 桑德斯怒吼着，双拳越握越紧……随后怒火骤然破碎；老人瘫靠在门上，大口喘息。“曾经，我被人称为英雄、白之战士、卢米娅的圣骑士……但格薇尔说得没错：我的理想主义令我太过软弱，太容易被理想与现实撕裂。正因如此，我背弃了卢米娅教团，收起刀剑和护甲。她证明了我太过软弱，不适合继续走这条路。并非所有神秘骑士与黑暗术士的故事都有幸福结局。有些童话，不过是病态的嘲弄。” 老人低垂着头，转身离开。 [flags.LIADEN_SANDERS |你走出办公室时，莉娅丹正抱着双臂，靠在门旁的墙上。 “刚才那阵吵闹究竟是怎么回事？”她看看你，又看看父亲，开口问道。“从没见老爸为什么事情发过这么大的火。” 你只是摇摇头。那是村庄历史上的旧事，她得直接去问父亲。 “真是的。好吧，好吧。对他温和一点；我大老远来到这里，可不是为了看老头子心脏病发作。好吗？” 好吧，好吧…… ]
