rows.raw: " [liaden.atChapel |Stepping into the chapel, the sound of raised voices comes to you from amidst the pews in direct contrast to the usual hushed atmosphere of the chapel. Well, it's mostly one voice that's raised — Lia[liaden.isDFN|||den]'s — as she rounds on her father. "So you're just gonna keep on goin' like this, Dad? Even after it's all settled?" "Forgiveness is one thing, Liaden. But we shouldn't forget, if only to learn from those mistakes and avoid repeating them in the future. However you want to apportion blame between Gweyr and I for what happened all those years ago, you can't expect me to act as if nothing happened back then, nor that it hasn't left its mark on either of us. No, even Carmen was shaken by the entire ugly situation; if she'd left her castle rarely before, she barely showed up after that. Not even Garth offering to collect taxes for her could lure her out." "Hmph. Stubborn old man." Liaden turns her back on Sanders. "Mom painted a very different picture of you before I left Maidenbridge." "With all due respect to your mother, dear, she has not seen me in person for a little over two decades; I didn't even know of your existence until you showed up on my doorstep. A lot can and has happened since then, Liaden — it's only now that I realize the burden that our commanders in the Oriflamme bore when they passed down certain orders to those like your mother and I, when the weight of those decisions lay upon their shoulders." "Maybe you're right, Dad, but that doesn't excuse you acting like... like, I don't know, a spurned lover or somethin'. You even threw the sword away!" Sanders' face darkens with a frown. "I didn't throw it away Liaden. I — " Before he can finish the sentence, Sanders notices you waiting patiently at the back of the pews and clears his throat. "We have a visitor, Liaden. Perhaps later." "Ah. Sorry." Liaden's scowl melts into a sheepish expression once she spots your silhouette. "Sorry you had to see that, [pc.name]." While you indeed didn't intend to eavesdrop, you more or less expected something like this to happen after Gweyr returned to Hawkethorne. Such an important matter, and the two of them wouldn't have spoken about it? Please. What's this about a sword, though? You don't remember that in the account of the story you were given; Gweyr told you he was wielding a spear that night. "I was. This is a related matter, though, but it's also a long story and best not recounted when tempers are running high. Perhaps you could ask me again when you're sure you have the time to stay awhile and listen, [pc.name]. The same goes for you, Liaden — go and take a cold bath, and we'll continue this when you're more level-headed." Liaden glances between the two of you, perhaps seeking your help in resisting her father out of sheer obstinacy[liaden.isDFN |... but, much as it might be fun to shout about things, it really might just be better to cool off and talk about it later |... but it really might just be better to cool off and talk about it later |, and when none is forthcoming lets her shoulders slump ]. [party.has azyrran |[azyrran.kdb |"He's right, Lia," Azyrran pipes up from beside you. "Like it or not, your father's right. You're not going to make any headway when you're all worked up." |"Hey, don't worry about it. A bath's a good idea anyway." Azzy pats the smaller woman on the shoulder. "[azzy.liaden |Wanna get it ready, sweet thing? [liaden.isDFN |[pc.name] and I wi |I' |I' ]ll be right behind you. |Let me know if you want company. ]" |Azyrran flits up behind Lia and rubs her shoulders. "Aww, it's okay, Lia! Calming down sounds like a good idea anyway. Or," she giggles, "maybe [liaden.isDFN |the three of us |we |we ] could get worked up in a different way![azzy.liaden | | Just let me know! ]" ] |[liaden.poly |Actually, come to think of it, she might be able to use some, mmm, distraction... ] ] [var0|That last suggestion brings an almost-unwilling smile to her face. ]"Fiiine. You'd better not go missing when I come find you later, Dad." With that, she stomps off back towards the rectory, leaving a bemused Sanders staring after her. "Her mother was like that sometimes," he sighs. "I liked that, a long time ago. Now I'm not sure why. At any rate, [pc.name][party.has azyrran|, Azyrran], I'm sorry you had to see it." [party.has azyrran |[azyrran.kdb |"These things happen. I think she just needs to have her mind on something else right now," Azzy says cautiously. "[liaden.poly |Which... um, [pc.name], if you want to come with... |[azzy.liaden |I, um... I'll just be, uh, doing that. With conversation. Yeah. |I'll try to talk to her! ] ] |"I don't know," the Hive Knight murmurs, looking in the same direction. "I like it. Either way, she'll have other things on her mind soon." |"Hee hee. It's no biggie!" Azzy assures him. "[azzy.liaden |[liaden.poly |[pc.name] and ]I'll make sure she forgets aaaaaall about it. |Maybe I can give her something else to think about! ]" ] |[liaden.poly |It's fine. Briefly, your eyes flick to the door she took. So, you should probably... um... wait, does he...? |Like you said, it was expected. It'd have happened sooner or later, so you're not surprised. ] ] [liaden.poly |Sanders' eyes twinkle knowingly. "I wouldn't keep her waiting if I were you[party.has azyrran | two ]. You go ahead and let tempers... cool. After that, come see me when you're ready for a long tale." |"Be that as it may, I do owe you and my daughter the final part of this entire story, the part that she wasn't around to witness. Not all loose ends have been tied up, but at least the matter can be considered resolved, can't it? "Forgiveness is one thing, [pc.name]. You're guessing that it's a long story, then? rows.original: [party.has azyrran |When you do get to the rectory, you and Azzy find Lia in the midst of drawing her bath. She throws a hesitant grin over her shoulder as soon as she hears you. "Hey. I guess you're here to tell me I'm bein' silly over nothin' an' to just relax." |Lia's in the midst of drawing her bath when you find her — well, you and Azzy, because within moments of your departure for the rectory, you're joined by the [azyrran.kdb |blushing Hive Knight |mountainous dragoon |bubbly bimbug ] that makes up the third part of your little polycule. As soon as the paladin sees the two of you over her shoulder, she manages a hesitant grin. "Hey, [pc.name]. And hey, Azzy. Y'all are gonna tell me I've been workin' myself up over nothin', right?" ] Maybe not nothing, but getting mad about it wasn't going to help. No matter who was right, she and her dad would both get frustrated and clam up, and nothing would get solved. Besides, she's probably worked up a sweat from all that yelling... "A sweat, huh?" She chuckles. "Smooth." [azyrran.kdb |"I mean, is she wrong?" Azzy asks. She slides in closer to ostentatiously examine Lia's bare arms. "That... that is a little sweat right there." |Azzy sweeps in closer, looming over Lia with black eyes all a-glitter. "Tsk. I see a great deal of sweat on you. Cleanliness is important, my flower." |"The smoothest! That's us!" Azzy giggles. She flits over to Lia and gets really, really close, doing her absolute best impression of a minute academic examination. "Oooh! Yeah! I see li'l sweatbeads right there!" ] Mhm. You sashay over to Lia's other side, gently raising an eyebrow at the utterly minuscule amount of sweat that you can see. Better clean it off as soon as possible... "Goddess help me," she laughs. "The women I love are complete dorks." Hey. That... is true. But she missed an important word: you're her dorks. [azyrran.kdb |"That's us!" chirps Azzy. She wiggles her chitin-covered fingers into prime position to pull off Lia's breastplate at the first opportunity, then continues: "And we're going to give you a bath." |Instead of issuing a verbal protest, the war-hornet on Lia's other flank simply stands tall and imposing, one of the many things she does best. "We love you too. And we are going to give you a bath." |"That's such a silly word! Dork. Dork dork." Azzy flutters long eyelashes, then puts her hand meaningfully on Lia's breastplate. "First things first — let's continue from when Gweyr was exiled from the village, made to walk the ice as the customs of lupines demanded. While the mood of those who'd lost their families was bitter and sour in equal measure, I was the one who ultimately made the decision and that weight fell upon me." Liaden frowns. Yes, I'm no longer sure it was, either. But at this point..." Sanders shrugs and turns his palms upward. "We can have this argument again later; [pc.name] is here to listen to what happened." Liaden folds her arms and sets her lips straight in a way that leaves little doubt that she's going to be picking it up with her father later. "All right, go on." If he doesn't mind, please. "Shortly after Gweyr left, I resigned my commission with the Order of the Oriflamme. While I was already considered semi-retired — I certainly expected to see a lot less battle ministering to Hawkethorne than riding around half of Old Belhar — I felt I wasn't capable of making the choices wisely, or correctly bearing the authority that came with being a holy paladin." "I was still pretty young when the missive arrived in Dawnsword. Everyone was surprised that you'd resign your commission and take up Velun's mantle, especially Mother — and that was the last time she ever heard of you... let alone from you." "If I'd known you existed, Liaden, I swear to you I would've written regularly over those years. More than that, even. But I didn't, and at the time I was afraid of your mother coming to ask inconvenient and prickly questions. Since I only knew of just her..." He bows his head before continuing. "You were raised in Dawnsword, though, weren't you? Then you must've known of the previous grandmaster, who was forced to execute his own nephew for insubordination. A brave young officer who rode out to meet a challenge to single combat against marauding orcs and won, greatly improving morale... and did so by disobeying a direct order to hold the line. The kind of decision that you may have to make in the future, Liaden. Keep that in mind if and when you return to the Order from this peaceful backwater. "Ahem. In any case, once my resignation was taken care of, there was the matter of the sword." "You really did throw it away! But no, that would've been wrong — the weakness was mine, and I wasn't prepared to foreclose on the possibility of someone genuinely proving worthy of it someday. Unless you're mistaken, the point of this talk is to fill you in on details like this, isn't it? Lia folds her arms, blows out her breath, and nods. "I'm sorry. You're right. Okay. So, I'm a sworn sister — a very junior one, but still — of the Order of the Oriflamme, one of the organizations of Lumian paladins. [etheryn.lnhConfidence |She blushes furiously at that, realizing just how much she's spoken up; the surest way to get Ryn to come out of her shell is to mention her people. |"S-Sure!" She manages a smile. |"I'm happy to help!" She perks her ears up. ] "We never knew much about her husband. He sounds like a real hero... with an appropriate weapon." He nods. "I |You wonder how that story comes out for the frost elves. The priest shrugs expressively. "I can't say for certain, given how much of the tales of that time have passed into legend, but there's no hint of theft or malice in the Order's lore about it. Apparently it was borne by one of the first frost-elven noblewomen to marry a southerner and to convert to Lumia's worship, and when she fell in battle the blade passed to her husband — Sigebert himself. As befits such a great warrior, i ]t's made for smiting and striking and utterly purging irredeemable darkness from the land. It's meant for dispatching that which you know is beyond all hope and saving. It's absolutely a weapon for heroes, but it's also a weapon of last resort. I wasn't about to bring something like that to meet the village youth, even if Tollus had deceived them. That would've meant a commitment to a course of action that in all likelihood would've made everything worse.[silly | I wasn't about to go Anakin on those younglings, [pc.name]. I'm Obi-wan, remember? ] "By bringing that kind of overkill to a stand-off, you send a message to the other party that I didn't want sent, [pc.name]. Even until the end, I still hoped that at least some of the village youths could be brought to their senses. That's why Gweyr saw me with my lance." You suppose that that makes a certain amount of sense, but if that's the case, why did the Order just let him semi-retire to Hawkethorne with such a deadly holy relic? "It wasn't exactly by choice." Sanders smiles thinly. "One of the things for which the Dawnsword is known is that it chooses its own wielders. Not that there is a mind residing within the blade or anything, but as with some other enchanted items, there is a sort of spiritual energy inside it. No one save the purest of heart, the most righteous, the people capable of battling evil without losing their balance and falling to it themselves, are fit to wield the blade. Any who don't meet those standards simply can't make it work. "Shortly after joining the Order I did something particularly heroic which doesn't really bear mentioning now, given it's another story in and of itself. The important thing is, the grandmaster decided that a paladin with such a clearly great destiny should be given a weapon by which to bring Lumia's light directly to the world outside their fortress. I was allowed to test myself, the Dawnsword found me worthy, and so it would remain with me until age, infirmity, or choice removed it from my grasp." So they couldn't have taken it from him even if they'd wanted to — not until he left the Order itself, if then. "Quite. I think there were a few doubts even while I was still adventuring for the Order. For all the sword's power, I used it as more of a holy symbol of Lumia's authority than for the outright smiting the grandmaster clearly intended me to do. Only when I was truly left with no choice did I use the blade as a weapon. As a result, I think that a few people — not all, perhaps not even most, but a few — in the Order came to think that I was too soft." [pc.isDK |Maybe he was too soft. |Maybe. By his own words, the sword itself saw him as 'balanced', though. It's a tough call. ] "Perhaps," he sighs. "But yes, by the grandmaster's lights I might not have been fit to wield it any longer even before resigning my commission, and the last fig leaf of pretense vanished after I left the faith for Velun. I won't deny that I was tempted to head straight up to the River Ridell and toss it into the waters, let it be carried into the mountains and maybe out to sea. But no, that would've been wrong — the weakness was mine, and not any fault of the blade's or Lumia's. To those ends, I buried it in an appropriate place, where it would wait... perhaps forever. If the sword had chosen me, and if I could not consider myself worthy anymore, I had doubts about whether anybody ought to claim it, even my brothers and sisters." Another sigh, deeper and more heartfelt than the first. "In hindsight, I think I see now that arrogance combined with fatalism in my eyes. I thought I knew better than the sword whom its rightful owner ought to be, and if it could not choose rightly, then I would keep it from choosing at all." ]

rows.raw: " [liaden.atChapel |"I thought you might. It's about time I got this off my chest. Liaden! Come here — I'm about to tell [pc.name] what you want to know, too." Liaden hops down from where she's polishing some old statue or other, sets down her rag and sidles into the pews, taking a seat[party.has azyrran | next to Azzy ]. You [liaden.isDFN |sit right next to [party.has azyrran |them |her ] |[azyrran.fucked |sit right on Azzy's other side |take up position across Sanders ] |take up position across Sanders ], then motion for him to go on. "Are you finally gonna to tell me where you put the sword, Dad? I've searched the whole chapel and — " "I told you that it wasn't here, Lia, and I didn't lie." What's this about a sword, then? "First things first — let's continue from when Gweyr was exiled from the village, made to walk the ice as the customs of lupines demanded. While the mood of those who'd lost their families was bitter and sour in equal measure, I was the one who ultimately made the decision and that weight fell upon me." Liaden frowns. "I still don't believe you did the right thing, Dad." "When one has the benefit of hindsight and the fact that thanks to [pc.name], everything turned out for the best, it's easy to judge. Yes, I'm no longer sure it was, either. But at this point..." Sanders shrugs and turns his palms upward. "We can have this argument again later; [pc.name] is here to listen to what happened." Liaden folds her arms and sets her lips straight in a way that leaves little doubt that she's going to be picking it up with her father later. "All right, go on." If he doesn't mind, please. "Shortly after Gweyr left, I resigned my commission with the Order of the Oriflamme. While I was already considered semi-retired — I certainly expected to see a lot less battle ministering to Hawkethorne than riding around half of Old Belhar — I felt I wasn't capable of making the choices wisely, or correctly bearing the authority that came with being a holy paladin." "I was still pretty young when the missive arrived in Dawnsword. Everyone was surprised that you'd resign your commission and take up Velun's mantle, especially Mother — and that was the last time she ever heard of you... let alone from you." "If I'd known you existed, Liaden, I swear to you I would've written regularly over those years. More than that, even. But I didn't, and at the time I was afraid of your mother coming to ask inconvenient and prickly questions. Since I only knew of just her..." He bows his head before continuing. "You were raised in Dawnsword, though, weren't you? Then you must've known of the previous grandmaster, who was forced to execute his own nephew for insubordination. A brave young officer who rode out to meet a challenge to single combat against marauding orcs and won, greatly improving morale... and did so by disobeying a direct order to hold the line. The kind of decision that you may have to make in the future, Liaden. Keep that in mind if and when you return to the Order from this peaceful backwater. "Ahem. In any case, once my resignation was taken care of, there was the matter of the sword." "You really did throw it away! You were given a weapon by which to bring Lumia's light directly to the world, and you just got rid of it. Dad, I can't believe — " "I won't deny that I was tempted to head straight up to the River Ridell and toss it into the waters, let it be carried into the mountains and maybe out to sea. But no, that would've been wrong — the weakness was mine, and I wasn't prepared to foreclose on the possibility of someone genuinely proving worthy of it someday. To those ends, I buried it in an appropriate place, where it might wait for its rightful wielder to someday come and claim it... or, at the very least, could remain apart from the cycle of death that I felt responsible for." "Rightful owner! You couldn't have just sent it back? Who'd you think it would be waiting for?" Sanders shrugs again. "You, maybe. Or Garth. Or [pc.name][pc.swornGod lumia | — [pc.heShe] would certainly be qualified, if nothing else ]. It gets to decide, not me; I'm certainly not worthy of such." "Or a bandit," she says sourly. "Righteousness doesn't give you a map in your head to all the world's holy artifacts. If you just left it lyin' around..." Whoa, wait just a moment — up until now, the both of them have been talking over your head. While they both clearly know what they're talking about when it comes to this sword, you have absolutely no idea what they're referring to in the slightest. Unless you're mistaken, the point of this talk is to fill you in on details like this, isn't it? Lia folds her arms, blows out her breath, and nods. "I'm sorry. You're right. Okay. So, I'm a sworn sister — a very junior one, but still — of the Order of the Oriflamme, one of the organizations of Lumian paladins. So's my mom, and once upon a time, Dad was one of the Order's brothers. The Order's... well, we're no valkyries[pc.swornGod lumia | like you ], but we're there to protect the innocent, fight bandits and Wraithkin, and that kinda thing, and we've done a good enough job that we've spread pretty far from where the Order started in Yvennes. That covers an unfathomable amount of ground, though! So circling back around for a moment, he felt the need to tell you about this epilogue to the entire sordid story of Hawkethorne's history because he secretly hopes you're the worthy one destined to possess the artifact he declined. “是的。当时，我的兄弟姐妹们告诉我，我所做的只是不让那些值得拥有这把剑的人得到它，而不仅仅是那些不值得的人。我当时觉得他们是在嫉妒。但他们的想法其实是有道理的。是确实，从某种角度来看——而这种观点，随着时间的推移，我越来越认同它。最终，”他叹息道，“我是这样对待自己的……也是这样对待其他人的。我仍然认为，除非是在极其危急的情况下，否则我不会再像以前那样去参加战争了；但我不能再让其他人也感受到那种犹豫不决、不愿参战的心情了。嗯……其实，你并不一定想重新讨论那场大屠杀中发生过或没有发生的事情。这样的讨论可能会持续一整天，而对所有参与其中的人来说，那肯定不会是愉快的一天。你真正应该感激的是，桑德斯改变了主意，而且这一改变并非出于某种不便，而是因为他真心认为自己之前做错了什么。因此，他正在努力弥补自己的其中一个错误。顺便问一下，关于那把晨曦剑：它在哪里？还是在他很久以前放置它的那个地方吗？ ] 据我所知，是的；自从我把剑柄埋起来的那天起，我就再也没去检查过它，因为那样做就违背了初衷。也许在过去的二十年里，已经有人把它拿走了。即便没有，即使你能找到我当初放置它的地方，也不能保证它就会选择你。 [pc.swornGod lumia |你或许已经证明了自己有资格加入这位女士创立的、最为严谨且最为忠诚的服务组织。 |你可能已经多次拯救了鹰棘镇了。 ]但从现在开始，做出决定的应该是晨曦剑，而不是我。 “我今天之所以请你们听我讲述这个故事，是因为我认为你们应该得到这个机会；事实上，如果晨曦剑认为你们比我更值得，我会感到非常自豪。但我不会给你比我的前同伴们更多的优势。毕竟，正如我们一直所说，如果那把剑拒绝你作为它的主人，那么找到它也不会对你有什么帮助。必须进行一些考验才行。所以：我把它藏在了收获谷和海岸之间的角峰山脉里。在那么广阔的空间里，你一定能找到自己想要的东西。 不过，这其实意味着需要搜索的范围大得难以想象——从山脚地带，到地下山脉，再到那些广袤的土地超过山腹深域、风啸峰峦，甚至更南边的那些地区……鉴于角峰山脉的辽阔范围，那些地方可能距离萨坦尼有一半的路程。你可能会搜索数周，甚至数月，却什么也找不到！ “正是这个意思，没错。桑德斯对你微微一笑。“就像我说的，我本来就打算让这个东西变得无处可寻。也许现在该让这把剑自己来做出决定了，但我还是无法再进一步缩小选择范围了。话虽如此，但我相信，只要有正确的灵感，你们就一定有成功的希望。 好吧，好吧。那么，回到刚才的话题，他觉得有必要告诉你们关于鹰棘镇这段悲惨历史的这个结局，因为他在心里暗自希望，你们才是那个有资格拥有他拒绝交给别人的那件神器的人。就这样吗？ “是的。我不知道你是否是但你确实应该得到一个公平的机会。[pc.name]， [pc.isDK |无论你采取这些行动背后还有哪些其他动机，事实依然是…… ]自从你来到这个村庄，你就如同一道光芒，为这里带来了希望。就像二十年前一样，现在人们似乎又一次需要希望了，而我相信你能够帮助他们。因此，我决定向你讲述这个故事的结局。[pc.name]，我不敢保证能提供什么帮助，但如果你真的接受我的建议去寻找那把晨曦剑，一定要小心。在我藏剑的地方附近，路上充满了危险，保持谨慎是非常必要的。 你会考虑的。话虽如此，在我们所有的讨论中，还有另一件事他似乎忘了提到…… “嗯？” 关于“晨曦剑”到底长什么样子，虽然考虑到到目前为止所说的一切，你其实已经在期待他会说出类似“只有被选中的人才能认出它”这样的话了。你说的对吗？” “它看起来其实非常普通，”桑德斯干笑着回答，“这把晨曦剑只不过是一个采用精灵工艺制作的剑柄，剑身在护手分有一点损坏。如果你不了解它的来历，也没有注意到上面的卢米安铭文以及里面隐藏的那颗小宝石，你肯定会以为它只是一块等着被熔化再锻造的废铁罢了。毫无疑问，它的外表确实骗过了很多路人，让他们没有意识到它的真正价值。但在经历了长达两个半世纪的神战之后，它依然完好无损，甚至没有受到任何损伤。只要你知道该怎么做，只要晨曦剑认可你，它就会在剑刃原本的位置绽放出光芒，重新焕发生机。 但是，没错。如果你真的适合做某件事……当你遇到它的时候，你就会明白的。 [pc.isDK |哎呀，这句话也太老套了吧。所以，他是想让你大费周章地去为他寻找那些所谓的“宝藏”吗？ |哎呀，他这么做肯定会让你脸红吧。但同时，他也在期待你主动去寻找，对吧？ ] 我已经把我的故事讲完了，当然也不会强迫你做任何事。你当然应该做你认为正确的事情。” …… “好吧，我也把我想说的都说出来了。谢谢你的倾听。[pc.name]说了一堆话，让我觉得口渴了。所以，除非你们还有别的事情要告诉我，否则我就去后面喝点水了。” 当桑德斯离开长椅，消失在牧师住宅里时，你开始思考他刚才讲述的那个相当长的故事。 [pc.isDK |显然，这个老人是想逼你成为他那些旧东西的接手人。 [pc.swornGod lumia |公平地说，考虑到你目前所处的处境，这确实是一份非常适合你的机会 |而且，你不得不承认，这样的文物确实具有很大的吸引力 ]。 |高尚、正义、责任……这些概念有很多需要你去理解、去领悟。不过，无论你还会想到什么，有一件神圣的武器存在。 [pc.swornGod lumia |被赋予了你那位女神的力量 |拥有太阳的力量 ]在某个地方。也许你会证明自己值得拥有它，从而获得一件有用的物品，用来对抗那些在边境地区肆虐的恶魔。即使你没有成功得到它，这样的物品被妥善保管，不会落入那些可能会滥用它的人手中，这也是一件好事。 ]另一方面，都已经过去二十年了，即使他给了你一些线索，但目前来看，这些线索也并不能让我们取得什么进展；这件事最终可能会变成一场徒劳无功的追寻。真是让人左右为难啊。 ]
rows.raw: " [liaden.atChapel |As Sanders steps away from the pews and disappears into the rectory, Liaden rolls her eyes and turns to you. "Sorry about my dad being insufferable, [pc.name]." [party.has azyrran |[azyrran.kdb |"Well, he is right," Azyrran points out. "I remember having similar discussions with Mom before, and — well, whatever you think of his actions in the past handling the whole business with Garth's wife, the fact remains that he's not obligated to tell you anything just because you're his daughter. I suppose it's different for me given that we're all our mother's daughters back in the hive, but that doesn't make the point any less valid." |"It's not very fun, but when he's right, he's right. Sometimes there are things you just don't tell people, even if they're your daughter. Mother didn't tell us everything back in the hive, either." Azzy interlaces her fingers with Lia's and gives the smaller woman a confident grin. "You've earned the answer now, though, haven't you?" |"It's okay! Sometimes parents can be stinky." Azyrran wrinkles her nose. "Mommy didn't always tell us stuff either. But that's just how lots of people do, even with the ones they love lots and lots. Not me, though!" ] |Well, he's right. However he may have handled matters with Gweyr — and you'll be first in line with complaints — the fact remains that he's not obligated to tell her anything about this Dawnsword thing just because she's his daughter, or at least from what you've been piecing together from this conversation. ] At any rate, you think you're up on the sword's lore, more or less, but what exactly is it? What does it look like? "You — oh, of course. I just took it for granted that everyone would know, because everyone I grew up with did. It's just a sword hilt — I guess an elven sword hilt, huh? — with a bit of broken blade just past the guard, and if you didn't know better or see the gem embedded in the hilt you might imagine it was just some scrap waiting to be smelted down and reforged. But it's survived the two and a half centuries since the Godswar without so much as an additional scratch on it, and if you know what to do, if the Dawnsword likes you, it'll come to life with a ray of radiance in place of where the blade once was. I've never actually ever seen it, since Dad left with the artifact before I was born, but Mom and everyone else back home could describe it perfectly." And now she wants it? "Well, I mean..." She shrugs helplessly. "No paladin of the Dawn Maiden in her right mind would turn her nose up at the chance to be proven worthy of wielding Lumia's greatest weapon. But even if — if I'm not, I hate the idea that the thing's just sittin' out in a grotto somewhere in the mountains, not getting the respect it deserves. It [silly |belongs in a museum |ought to be back at the Oriflamme's reliquary where it belongs ], y'know? Or, even better, in the hands of someone else who'll actually use it for smiting evil. [pc.swornGod lumia |Like you! I mean, you're the literal Champion of Lumia. Come to think of it, you oughta be the one who decides what happens to it." [party.has azyrran |[azyrran.kdb |"I mean, you don't have to be a valkyrie to wield the sword, right?" Azzy points out. "Great faith, purity of heart... I mean, yeah, [pc.names] up there, but I think you could be worthy too, Lia! Who knows what a sword really wants anyway?" |"Aaah, don't count yourself out." As is her wont, the Hive Knight gives Liaden a gentle pat on the head. "It's not a sword for valkyries, it's a sword for the valiant and pure of heart, and [azzy.liaden|my Lia's|you're] as much of that as anybody. It could be you or [pc.name] just as easily." |"Don't put yourself out of the running just yet, sweetling," Azyrran says, reaching over to pat Liaden on the shoulder. "I mean, it's true that [pc.name] is hard to beat when it comes to rescuing hives in need... but you're not bad, either! Who knows what a silly sword really thinks?" ] |That's gracious of her, and you'd happily accept the blade if it chose you, but you and your sisters don't have a monopoly on Lumia's favor. After all, the weapon's been in the hands of her order for hundreds of years; a warrior like Lia could be just as worthy as any other of your goddess's servants. There's no need for her to count herself out yet. ] |Maybe it could even be you or Azzy — you both do plenty of that too. And if it's not for any of us, well, at least finding it or even not finding it would be a good bit of closure." [party.has azyrran |[azyrran.kdb |"Hey, if this is a sword for the worthy, I think you've got a shot at getting its favor! I mean, you've got faith, purity of heart, strength..." Azzy trails off into a wordless blush. "Um... yeah." |"I think you've got a shot at more than closure," Azzy hums. She pats Liaden on the head as she continues: "If it's a sword for the valiant and pure of heart, [azzy.liaden|my Lia's|you're] definitely in the running." |"Don't put yourself out of the running just yet, sweetling," Azyrran says, reaching over to pat Liaden on the shoulder. "I think you're pretty great and have a good chance!" ] |Ah, now she's talking as if it's already a foregone conclusion. Until she's gone out and actually started looking, let alone actually managing to figure out where her father hid the thing, she really shouldn't count herself out of the running just yet. ] ] "I guess. Thanks, [party.has azyrran |you guys |[pc.name] ]. No matter who it goes to — if any of us — the important thing is that it comes out of whatever hole Dad left it in." She pauses. "I... goddess, I'm sorry, I've been just kinda presumin' this whole time without askin'. Do you actually want to come along?" [party.has azyrran |[azyrran.kdb |"Of course we'd be willing to help you, Liaden. Isn't that right, [pc.name]?" |"Like you had to ask," Azzy chuckles. "Right, [pc.name]?" |Azzy lets stream a fountain of giggles. "Sure thing, cutie! We'd both love to help, right?" ] Liaden sighs. "I'm not gonna lie — I know what I have to do, but I don't know if I have the strength to do it. A pair of reliable someones at my side would help a lot." Well, [silly |by engaging with this option and the story so far, you've more or less given your implicit consent to this whole shebang, so why not. You'll presumably be getting some cool loot out of it, right? |[flags.LIAZZY_3SUM|think of this as a way for the three of you to build up your relationship a bit more! Besides|while you aren't as friendly with her as Azzy is and wouldn't want to presume], you wouldn't have asked Sanders to sit down and fill you in with a long talk if you weren't interested in this whole Dawnsword thing to begin with. So... yes. ] |Well, you wouldn't have asked Sanders to sit down and fill you in with a long talk if you weren't interested in this whole Dawnsword thing to begin with. So... yes. [pc.isDK |You'll expect that this be made worth your time, of course, but you're not against it |You'd be happy to help her ]. ] "All right. Come back and talk to me when you're ready to start hunting — while Dad's been utterly and stubbornly tight-lipped about the matter, turning the chapel upside-down once more after that last talk hasn't been completely fruitless now that I know what to look for. I've managed to piece together some clues which should narrow down our search, so we won't be wandering around the mountains for weeks with nothing more than a feeling to go on." |Rightful owner, huh? Did he have anybody particular in mind, way back when? Sanders shrugs again. "I didn't. What I thought twenty years ago doesn't matter much anymore. The point is that the sword should decide now. It could choose someone like you, maybe[pc.swornGod lumia | — given that you've been admitted into the highest echelons of the Lady of Light's service, you would certainly be qualified, if it comes to that ]. Or Garth.[party.has etheryn | Or Etheryn. ] Or anyone else, for that matter." [party.has etheryn |At the mention of her name, Ryn blushes[etheryn.highConfidence |, but her ears stay high and proud. "It's nice of you to say my name there, and I'm definitely tempted! But [pc.name] would probably do much more with it than I would. [etheryn.fucked |Although," she murmurs with a sidelong, eyelash-fluttering glance, "maybe [pc.heShe] can bring it back to the Winter City [pc.himselfHerself]! |It's been in the south for so long that maybe it belongs down here with you all. ] | in embarrassment; her drooping ears convey more about what she thinks about that idea than her words do. "That's n-not — I mean, it would be amazing, but the sword's been in the south for so long... maybe it belongs among you, with someone like [pc.name]. ] At any rate, I'd just be happy if it went to a warrior who could use it against evil, like in the past." "That's more than fair," the priest says. "I confess that if it truly did once belong to your family, I for one wouldn't mind seeing it return to a good Lumian queen of your line. But yes, you're right: it's the blade's choice, not ours, and blood doesn't always tell." ] [pc.isDK |Worthiness and righteousness aside, this sounds like a truly deadly weapon, and that's what's important. |It's a flattering idea. ] You're still kind of shocked that this chance even exists, though. If this Dawnsword was such an important relic to the Order of the Oriflamme, wouldn't they have sent someone to come and retrieve it from him once they'd realized he'd broken ranks? While the Marches may be remote, they also fall quite firmly under Lumian influence; it would have been a long but not particularly hard journey to reach him. A nod. "They did; two of them showed up a couple of months after the fact. I told them the general area where I'd buried it, and to go and retrieve the thing if they felt they were worthy. They came back with a hilt, but the wrong one. I told them that what they found wasn't the blade they were looking for, and that their failure proved as much." [pc.isDK |He was in such good standing that they just took his word for it, huh... "Oh, of course not. Their first reaction was to suspect I was lying and turn the entire chapel upside-down in search of the Dawnsword, searching with senses both divine and mundane. Confronting evil so many times can indeed turn a man jaded, to be sure, but that someone would stick to one's true faith and conviction even if it leads one to a bitter end was surprising to my brothers. That they would suspect me... well, it's not unwarranted. People are fallible, after all. The truth is often what we make of it; you heard what you wanted to hear, believed what you wanted to believe, and at the time it was disappointing to see my old brothers-in-arms fall into the same trap. "Now that I have a little distance from it, I can see that what I was doing was arrogating to myself the power to choose who would receive the Dawnsword, rather than leaving it with the sword itself, and then choosing 'no one.' Still, they weren't wrong to be suspicious, even if my choice came from a righteous arrogance rather than a nefarious one." He shrugs. "It had the same result." And there's his martyrdom rushing in again. You'd rather not get involved in that particular bit of wallowing. Instead, you ask about the Dawnsword: is it still wherever he left it? |But now that he's had some time to stew on it, he doesn't think the same way. "Yes. At the time, my brothers and sisters told me that all I was doing was keeping the blade out of the hands of the worthy, not merely the unworthy. I thought it was sour grapes. But what they were saying was true, from a certain point of view — a point of view I found myself coming closer and closer to with every passing year. In the end," he sighs, "I did this to myself... and to everybody else. I still don't think I could go to war again like I once did, save in the absolute direst of circumstances, but I can't inflict that same reluctance on everybody else any longer." It... well, you don't necessarily want to rehash everything that happened and didn't happen in the massacre. That could last a whole day, and it wouldn't be a fun day for anyone involved. What you do appreciate is that Sanders has changed his mind, and not on account of inconvenience, but because he genuinely believes he did something wrong. And as a result, he's making up for at least one of his mistakes. By the way, about the Dawnsword: where is it? Still where he left it way back when? ] "As far as I know, yes; I haven't gone to check in on it since the day I buried the hilt, as that would defeat the point. Perhaps someone's already claimed it in the two decades that've passed since then. And even if not, even if you find it exactly where I left it, there's no guarantee that it'll choose you. [pc.swornGod lumia |You may have proven yourself worthy of joining the lady's greatest and most dedicated order of service |You may have saved Hawkethorne several times over now ], but it's from here on, it's the Dawnsword that makes its decisions, not I. "I've asked you to listen to my story today because I think you ought to have a chance; indeed, I'd be proud if the Dawnsword found you more worthy than me. But I'm not going to give you too much of an advantage over my former comrades. After all, like we've been saying, finding the sword won't do you much good if it rejects you as its wielder. There needs to be some trial. So: I hid it in the Hornpeak Mountains between Harvest Valley and the coast. Somewhere in all that space, you'll find what you're looking for." That covers an unfathomable amount of ground, though! Foothills, Undermountain, the lands over the Undermountain, the Windy Peaks, and even lands further south... given how far the Hornpeaks stretch, it could be halfway to Sartanni. You could search for weeks, even months, and not turn up anything! "That's the point, yes." Sanders gives you a little smile. "Like I said, I meant for it to be impossible to find. Maybe it's past due that the sword should decide for itself, but I still can't bring myself to narrow things down any more than that. That said, I'm sure that with the right inspiration, you've got a better than fighting chance." All right, all right. So circling back around for a moment, he felt the need to tell you about this epilogue to the entire sordid story of Hawkethorne's history because he secretly hopes you're the worthy one destined to possess the artifact he declined. Is that it? "Yes. I don't know if you are, but you deserve a fair chance. [pc.name], [pc.isDK |regardless of what other motivations you may have for your actions, the fact remains that ]you've been a light within this village ever since you arrived. Like twenty years ago, it looks like the people are in need of hope again, and I believe this will help. That's why I'm filling you in on the closing chapter of this story. "[pc.name], I can't promise very much, but if you do take up my offer and go to look for the Dawnsword, do be careful. There's a great deal of danger out there on the way to where I hid the blade, and it would pay to be cautious." You'll consider it. That being said, in all this talking there's another thing he's forgotten to mention... "Yes?" What the Dawnsword looks like, although given everything up till now you're half-expecting him to say something like 'you'll recognize it if you've been chosen.' Are you right? "It's deceptively mundane," Sanders replies with a dry chuckle. "The Dawnsword's just a hilt of elven design with a bit of broken blade just past the guard, and if you didn't know better — or notice the Lumian inscriptions and the little gem hidden within it — you'd imagine it was just some scrap waiting to be smelted down and reforged; no doubt the appearance has fooled many a passer-by who didn't recognize its true value. But it's survived the two and a half centuries since the Godswar without so much as an additional scratch on it, and if you know what to do, if the Dawnsword likes you, it'll come to life with a ray of radiance in place of where the blade once was. "But yes. If you're meant for it... you'll know it when you see it." [pc.isDK |Sheesh, what a cheesy line. So, he's expecting you to make the trek and go on a treasure hunt for him? |Aww, he's going to make you blush. But at the same time, he's expecting you to make the search, isn't he? ] "I've told you my part of the story, and I'm certainly not about to force you to do anything. You must do what you feel is right, of course." ... "All right, I've said my piece. Thanks for listening, [pc.name]. All this talking has made me thirsty, so unless you have anything else for me, I'm going into the back to get a drink." As Sanders steps away from the pews and disappears into the rectory, you consider the rather lengthy story he's just told you. [pc.isDK |Clearly the old man wants to push you into being the bearer of his hand-me-down, [pc.swornGod lumia |and to be fair it would be a fitting piece for you given the deal you've taken |and you can't deny there is an appeal to an artifact like that ]. |Worthiness, righteousness, responsibility... there's a lot going on for you to get your head around. Whatever else you might think, though, there's a holy weapon [pc.swornGod lumia |imbued with your goddess's power |with the power of the sun ] out there. Maybe you will prove worthy of it and gain a valuable item to use against the demons swarming around the Marches. Even if you don't, it'll be good for such a thing to be safe and out of the hands of anybody who might try to corrupt it. ] On the other hand, it's been twenty years, and even if he's given you a tiny hint, there's still not much here to go on; it could end up being a wild goose chase. Decisions, decisions. ] "

rows.original:
As you enter Hawkethorne's square, your eyes slide from the Frost Hound to the shops, from the traders to the villagers. Everything looks safe. Everything looks secure.
    
    You suppose, now that you're the avatar of the goddess of defending hearth and home, you're going to be thinking about that [pc.isDK
        |kind of thing
        |even more than you already did
    ].
    
    And speaking of Lumia: a certain former adherent of the Dawn Maiden is on his way to see you right now. Sanders is downright beaming as he walks over, and you can see perhaps a little more purpose in his step than normal. Well, then...
    
    [pc.wingsVRN
        |With a flicker of intention, your glowing wings emerge from the ether, spread wide, then fold back to their ready position behind your back.

rows.translation: 拥抱

rows.original:
[pc.isDK
            |"You could say that," you say.
            |"Of course!" you chirp.
        ] Then you get to see the first surprised look you've seen on Sanders' face maybe ever, as you open your arms and give him a warm valkyrie embrace — one that doesn't just use your arms, but your wings, too. "[pc.isDK
            |I guess I should thank you, too, huh? For helping out along the path.
            |Thank you for everything you've done for me.
        ]"
        
        Surprise or no, he returns the hug with a genuine smile. "[pc.isDK
            |There's no need, [pc.name], but I appreciate it
            |Of course, [pc.name]
        ]. I am very proud of you. The depth of Lumia's love for you is a testament to your own nature and abilities, but if in some small way I helped you unlock them... well, I could not be happier." He squeezes you in the hug a little. "If I had a daughter, I would have been overjoyed if she were like you."
        
        "Awww..." You squeeze right back. But when you release him from the embrace, you look him in the eyes. "[pc.dcb
            |So, all that said, I know that you're not in Lumia's service anymore. We're still good, though, right?"
            |Even right down to being in Lumia's service? I know you left, and while I don't want to pry, I was a little worried about whether we'd have some friction over this."
            |It sounds like you don't have a problem with me doing sun mommy stuff, and that's a relief! I was kinda worried, since you don't do sun mommy — sun daddy? I guess? — stuff anymore."
        ]
        
        "[pc.dcb
            |We are
            |No friction at all
            |There's no need to worry
        ]," he says reassuringly. "What is between Lumia and myself is nothing bad. What caused me to leave her service... [QUEST_HIGH_GROUND.isCompleted
            |well, you know that story well enough, and it is less about her and more about my own failings
            |it's perhaps a story for another time
        ]. I would not continue to wear my robes as a brother of the Oriflamme — rather than the vestments of a priest of Velun, the god whom so many of my parishioners petition — if I did not still love and respect the Lady of Light and those who serve her. I am proud of you, and I am glad to count another valkyrie among my friends."
        
        "Another? Maybe we really should make sure that you visit once all this is over."
        
        "I'd like that." Sanders' eyes flick around the growing crowd of townsfolk. "I suspect our friends are all very glad that you've entered Lumia's service, too. There's nothing quite so reassuring as knowing that a valkyrie is nearby." Then he claps you on the shoulder. "That goes for me, as well. Hawkethorne feels just that much safer with you here. Congratulations again, [pc.name]. May you continue to walk in the Dawn Maiden's light."

            |我想自己也该谢谢你，对吧？谢谢你一路提供帮助。
            |谢谢你为我所做的一切。
        ]”
        
        尽管感到惊讶，他仍带着真诚的微笑回抱你。“[pc.isDK
            |不必如此，[pc.name]，不过我很感激
            |这是自然，[pc.name]
        ]。我为你感到无比骄傲。卢米娅对你怀有如此深厚的爱，足以证明你本身的品格与能力；不过，假如我曾以微薄之力帮助你释放这些潜能……那么，我不可能更加欣慰。”拥抱中，他又将你搂紧了一些。“如果我有女儿，而她能像你一样，我一定会欣喜若狂。”
        
        “哎呀……”你也紧紧回抱他。不过，当你松开怀抱后，又直视着他的双眼。“[pc.dcb
            |那么，话虽如此，我知道你已经不再侍奉卢米娅。不过我们之间还是没问题，对吧？
            |甚至包括同样侍奉卢米娅这件事？我知道你已经离开她；虽然我不想窥探隐私，但还是有点担心这会不会让我们之间产生摩擦。
            |听起来你不介意我做太阳妈妈的事情，真让我松了口气！我之前还有点担心，因为你已经不做太阳妈妈——或许该说太阳爸爸？——的事情了。
        ]”
        
        “[pc.dcb
            |我们当然没问题
            |完全没有任何摩擦
            |你不必担心
        ]，”他出言安慰。“我和卢米娅之间并没有什么糟糕的事情。至于是什么让我离开她的麾下……[QUEST_HIGH_GROUND.isCompleted
            |好吧，那个故事你已经足够熟悉了；它与她关系不大，更多是因为我自己的失败
            |或许该留到另一天再讲
        ]。许多教区居民向维伦神祈祷，可我依然穿着圣焰骑士团修士的长袍，而不是维伦祭司的法衣；假如我不再深爱并尊敬光明女士以及侍奉她的人，就绝不会如此。我为你感到骄傲，也很高兴能将另一位女武神视为朋友。”
        
        “另一位？也许等一切结束后，我们确实应该确保你前去拜访一次。”
        
        “我会喜欢的。”桑德斯的目光扫过日渐聚集起来的镇民。“我想，朋友们同样都很高兴你投入了卢米娅麾下。没有什么比知道附近就有一位女武神更令人安心。”随后，他拍了拍你的肩膀。“对我而言也是如此。有你在，鹰棘镇便更加安全。再次祝贺你，[pc.name]。愿你继续行走在黎明圣女的光辉之中。”

rows.original:
As you enter Hawkethorne's square, your eyes slide from the Frost Hound to the shops, from the traders to the villagers. Everything looks safe. Everything looks secure.

    You suppose, now that you're the avatar of the goddess of defending hearth and home, you're going to be thinking about that [pc.isDK
        |kind of thing
        |even more than you already did
    ].
    
    And speaking of Lumia: there's one particular Lumian on her way to see you right now. Liaden breaks into a jog as soon as she leaves the chapel doors, followed with somewhat less urgency by her father. "[pc.name]! That's you, right?"
    
    [pc.dcb
        |A smile tugs at the corner of your mouth. "Who else?"
        |You smile. "It's still me."
        |"Yipyup!" you cheer. "Still me! I think! I don't think I'm anybody else right now."
    ]
    
    "Wow." She breaks into an excited smile of her own. "Just... wow. You're amazin'. Should I... I dunno, kneel or somethin'? I've never met a lady valkyrie before."
    
    "From what I remember of the Order's protocol," Sanders says, puffing slightly, "there is no need — at least, not outside of ceremonial purposes." His eyes twinkle. "I'm sure she appreciates the gesture, though."

"[pc.dcb |Fine |I don't know |Gosh, I dunno ]," you muse. "I'm still getting used to things. [pc.dcb |It is fun to see what hugs as a valkyrie do to people, though. |I will say, though, that giving hugs as a valkyrie has been pretty fantastic so far. |Like, everything's even more warm and light and fun and friendly than before! Especially the hugs! ]" Lia murmurs, "It's like bein' held by my [liaden.poly |girl ]friend and Lumia at the same time." "There's no feeling quite like it." Sanders' eyes defocus with memory, then brighten up again, along with his smile. "Valkyries inspire by merely existing. You were already that kind of person before you joined their ranks, [pc.name]. Pardon my saying so, but seeing Lumia's light added to the light that already shines through you... feels right." Now it's your turn to thank them for the compliments. But once you've done that, you cock your head and ask Sanders, "[pc.dcb |So... I know you're not a Lumian cleric anymore. There's not going to be any friction, right? |Lumia's light... I know you used to be a Lumian cleric, and now you're not. I know things seem fine, but do you think there's anything that might cause problems between us down the track? |Um, sooo... like, is it okay if I ask about how come you switched from sun mommy stuff to tree daddy stuff? I mean, it sounds like you don't have a problem with Lumia or anything... ]" "My daughter has sworn her service to the Lady of Light, too," he points out, "and I could not be happier." His eyebrows lift with gentle amusement. "What is between me and Lumia is nothing bad; there is a reason I still wear the robes of a brother of the Oriflamme rather than ones more appropriate to[pc.isBimbo | | Velun, ] the god whom so many of my parishioners petition. There are things done and undone, thoughts and actions that need more resolution than I have given them, but no ill will toward Lumia, and certainly not toward her honest, honorable servants. No, [pc.name], I'm proud to know another valkyrie, and even prouder to name her friend." "And you know you're good with me," Lia says feelingly. Her father nods in the direction of the Frost Hound. "As with, I think, the rest of the town. Having me and Lia around is well and good, but there is something about a valkyrie that does much to allay people's fears. At any rate," he says, clapping you on the shoulder, "congratulations again, [pc.name]. May you continue to walk in the Dawn Maiden's light."

rows.original: As you make your way through the valley, a piercing cry for help fills your ears. Following the noise, you find a sheep girl on her hands and knees while a crazy horse towers over her menacingly, eyes raging with lust as his beastly member slowly stiffens. The stallion snorts triumphantly, reaching down to grab his prize when he notices [party.som|you|you and your companion|you and your companions] watching from a distance. His eyes narrow hungrily, finding you to be a much tastier treat than the sheep girl mewling at his feet. Pawing the ground with his hooves, he lets out a piercing whinny before preparing to charge.

She pulls out a small handkerchief and begins to vigorously wipe your [pc.face], scrubbing off the sweat and specks of dirt splattered across it. You stand there awkwardly while the tiny sheep girl cleans your face, a bit taken aback to do much else. Every once in a while she pauses, licking her thumb to smear something off your [pc.skinFurScales] before continuing her wiping. "There! Much better," she exclaims proudly. Uh, thanks...you guess. rows.original:
Clementine gasps at your suggestion, her eyes widening in unrestrained glee as her tail wags furiously. 

    "Really!? You wanna cuddle!?" she says, practically bouncing in her seat.
    
    You cock your eyebrow at her, surprised at this sudden change in her. She looks like a child about to be given some sweets, eyes raving and limbs bustling as she awaits your answer. 
    
    With an unavoidable smile creeping on your [pc.lipsChaste], you tell her yes, [pc.isBimbo|you would love to snuggle with her.|you would love to cuddle with her.] 
    
    "Okay okay! Let’s go to my bed!" she says happily. 
    
    Following her, Clementine leads you to her room, which is a small, cozy little place for a small, cozy little girl like Clementine. She hops on her bed, patting the sheets as she invites you to join her which you do so joyfully, scooping up Clementine in your [pc.arms] as she wraps herself around you, enveloping you in a fluffy embrace. A dopey smile is plastered over her lips, beaming at you with love and adoration.
    
    She sure likes to cuddle.
    
    "Of course! I don’t know a sheepfolk that doesn’t enjoy a good cuddle." she tells you, "And I don’t know anyone who would pass down a cuddle with a sheepfolk. We’re so warm and cuddly, it’s like snuggling with a cloud." 
    
    Chuckling you scratch behind her ears, making her coo in appreciation. She nestles herself against you, eyes closing as she loses herself to the moment. You do the same, letting your eyes rest as you relax into Clementine’s fleece. 
    
    For an hour or so, you melt against each other, basking in each other’s warmth. There’s no sound but the rise and fall of your breaths, no movement save for the soft caress you lay upon her ears. It’s a brief but highly relaxing moment from all your adventure. A well needed break from all you’ve been through.
    
    But alas, all good things must end. You eventually break off your wonderful cuddle, sitting up in the bed as you tell Clementine that you have to go. 
    
    "Aww, okay. Stay safe [pc.name]. And come back anytime you want some more cuddles!" she tells you. 
    
    You most definitely will.
rows.translation:
克莱门汀听到你的提议后，眼睛瞪得大大的，脸上洋溢着无拘无束的喜悦，尾巴也兴奋地摇个不停。 

    “真的吗！？你想拥抱我！？”她几乎是在座位上跳来跳去地说。
    
    你挑了挑眉毛，对她这种突然的变化感到有些惊讶。她看起来就像一个即将得到糖果的孩子，眼睛亮晶晶的，四肢也忙个不停，急切地等待着你的回答。 
    
    你不禁在[pc.lipsChaste]上漾起一抹无法压抑的微笑，对她说想，[pc.isBimbo|你会很想和她依偎在一起。|你会很想和她拥抱在一起。] 
    
    “好吧好吧！我们去我的床上吧！”她开心地说道。 
    
    克莱门汀带着你走进她的房间——对于像她这样一个小女孩来说，这个房间确实是一个小巧而舒适的地方。她跳上床，轻轻拍打着床单，邀请你跟她一起上去，你高兴地答应了，用你的[pc.arms]把克莱门汀抱了起来，一起躺在了床上。当她紧紧拥抱着你，用柔软的怀抱将你完全包裹起来时，她的嘴唇上挂着一抹傻傻的微笑，那目光中充满了爱意与崇拜。
    
    她真的很喜欢拥抱别人呢。
    
    “当然啦！我还不认识哪个羊人不喜欢好好拥抱一下的呢。”她对你说，“我也不知道有谁会拒绝和羊人抱一抱。我们在一起的时候感觉如此温暖、舒适，就像抱着一片云朵一样。” 
    
    你笑着在她耳后挠了挠，她开心地发出呜呜声表示感谢。她依偎在你身边，闭上眼睛，完全沉浸在这一刻之中。你也是如此，闭上双眼，放松下来，沉浸在克莱门汀的羊毛里。 
    
    大约一个小时的时间里，你们就这样紧紧相拥，共同感受着彼此带来的温暖。周围一片寂静，只有你的呼吸声此起彼伏，除了你轻轻抚摸她耳朵的动作外，没有任何其他动静。这一刻如此短暂，却让人感到无比放松，仿佛是从漫长的冒险中得到的一次难得的休息，也是对你所经历的一切的一种必要缓解。
    
    但是，可惜，所有美好的事情终究都会结束。你最终结束了那段美好的拥抱，坐起来对克莱门汀说，你必须离开了。 
    
    “哎呀，好吧。注意安全，[pc.name]。只要你想要更多的拥抱，随时都可以回来哦！”她对你说。 
    
    你肯定会的。

[rand
        |"Even though the Frost Marches are a lot poorer than most of the Heartlands, I like that there aren't a lot of aristocrats around here. I can't tell you how many nobles I've met who are so arrogant! Thinking they deserve everything in the world because they own a big castle, even though they've never worked a day in their life."
        
        "But oh my gods, the Baranian ones are the worst! This duchess, who thankfully lived an acre away from my family's farm, was a tyrant. The farmers that lived under her were bled dry for their crops to the point where some had to beg for food because they couldn't save enough. And she's not even the worst of them! I always heard tales from the city about some servant getting imprisoned or publicly humiliated for making a small mistake or accidentally offending their masters. I swear, I just don't understand how in my race of so many gentle and kind people there could be so many cruel folks at the top."
        
        "Sorry, I kinda got carried away. Anyways, I'm just happy I don't have lick anyone's boots up here. Everyone here's just getting by, and it makes us all equal in a sense. I can't stand cutting my fleece so short, it makes me feel naked," she says with a disgusted shudder.
        
        "It does get a little too cold sometimes. I wear my dresses most of the time, but sometimes I find myself shivering back home for some warmer clothes. But the chapel’s enormous in comparison. I mean there’s villages in the Heartland that don’t have churches half as nice as this one." 
        
        "Only problem I have is that it's really bleak for a chapel. Hard to pay your respects to the Seven when there’s this foreboding sense of dread. Especially the gargoyles. I feel like I’ll get nightmares if I look at them too long," she says, stroking her arm wool for comfort. "I much prefer the chapels back in Barania, they definitely had a lighter atmosphere. But I don’t know, I guess it’s just because I’m not a northerner." 
        
        "I do have to say though, Brother Sanders is one of the nicest priests I’ve met. He’s very relaxing to talk to and he never openly judges you, either. I’ve met plenty a priest and priestesses who like to scold you for your lack of prayer and how you’ll be damning yourself to a terrible afterlife when Tira comes for you."
        |"Do you find it weird that the baroness never comes out of her castle? Even the shyest nobles in the Heartland have made some effort to appear in public. But there’s some people who’ve lived here their entire lives and they’ve never even seen her! Can you believe it?" she exclaims.
        
        It is quite strange, you have to admit.
        
        "I get wanting to have some privacy, but a ruler has to be around her subjects sometimes. I mean there’s people in town who do a better job leading than she does, like Brother Sanders or Garth." she says. Her ears fall flat when she realizes she’s just said some pretty treasonous words when it comes to the baroness.

        |虽然霜冻之地比腹地的大部分地区都要贫穷，但我却很喜欢这里没有那么多贵族。我实在数不清遇到过多少傲慢无礼的贵族！他们以为只要拥有一座宏伟的城堡，就理所应当得到世界上的一切，尽管他们一生中从未做过一天正经工作。但是，我的天啊，巴拉尼亚的那些女统治者才是最糟糕的！这位公爵夫人，幸好她住得离我们家的农场有一英里远，否则的话……她真是个暴君。那些受她统治的农民们，因为她的压迫而失去了所有的收成，有些人甚至不得不去乞讨食物，因为他们根本存不下任何东西。而且她甚至还不是最糟糕的那个！我在城里经常听到这样的故事：有些仆人因为犯了一些小错误，或者不小心得罪了他们的主人，就被关进监狱或者当众受到羞辱。我实在想不通，为什么在我们这个种族中，既然有这么多温和善良的人，为什么高层却会有这么多残忍的人。抱歉，我有点太激动了。总之，我很高兴在这里没有人需要巴结别人。这里的每个人都在努力维持生计，从某种意义上来说，这让我们所有人都平等了。嗯，虽然从严格意义上讲，女男爵才是这片土地的统治者和所有者，但就贵族而言，我觉得她也没什么问题，尽管我从未见过她。"

她这话是什么意思呢？

            |呃，嗯，我想你也是住在北方吧。但我指的是像你这样永久性地居住在这里，而不是像你那样总是四处冒险。

        ]我的意思是，我并不孤单，在这里我交到了很多朋友，比如内莉娅和你。但我想，我可能已经太习惯一直看到羊人族了，所以当只有我一个人的时候，会感觉有点奇怪。也不知道，也许我只是有点想家罢了。
        |我喜欢这里这么冷，”她笑着说，脸上带着愉悦的表情。

真的吗？大多数搬到这里的人都会抱怨天气太冷。就连这里本地出生的人也一样会抱怨寒冷。

“嗯，我其实挺喜欢这种寒冷的，因为这样我的羊毛就能长得又厚又茂盛。在巴拉尼亚，甚至在一些心脏地带的地方，夏天的气温高得惊人，如果你不想被热得活活烤死，就不得不把羊毛剪得短得几乎贴在皮肤上。我实在受不了把羊毛剪得这么短，那样让我感觉自己就像赤条条的一样，”她说着，不禁厌恶地打了个寒颤。
        
        有时候天气确实会变得太冷了。我大多数时候都会穿裙子，但有时候回到家后，我还是会因为太冷而发抖，于是就会去找一些更暖和的衣服穿。而且，我在这里使用的柴火量比在巴拉尼亚的时候要多得多；不过幸好这里的柴火价格要便宜很多，否则我会很麻烦的。我为那些没有毛皮来保暖的人们感到十分难过，真无法想象他们该有多冷。
        |对于像鹰棘镇这样的小镇来说，这座小教堂确实相当令人印象深刻。说实话，当我看到第一批房屋时，我并没有抱有太大的期望——其中有一半的房子看起来几乎都快撑不住了。但相比之下，这座小教堂确实规模宏大。我的意思是，在内陆地区，有些村庄里的教堂甚至都没有这么漂亮。

我唯一觉得不满意的地方就是，这个小教堂的氛围实在太阴森了。在这种令人不寒而栗的氛围中，人们很难真正地向七神表达敬意。尤其是那些滴水嘴兽，盯着它们看太久的话，我怕会做噩梦，”她边说边抚摸着自己的手臂，试图获得些许安慰。“我其实更喜欢巴拉尼亚地区的那些小教堂，那里的氛围确实要轻松许多。不过我也说不准，也许只是因为我不是北方人吧。不过我确实得说，桑德斯修士是我遇到过的最友善的神父之一。和他交谈非常让人放松，而且他也从不会公开批评别人。我遇到过很多神父和女祭司，他们总是会因为别人不经常祈祷而责备他们，还会说如果蒂拉降临，这些人就会陷入可怕的来世。"
        |你难道不觉得奇怪吗？那位女男爵从来都不离开她的城堡……就连心脏地带那些最害羞的贵族，也至少会努力出现在公共场合吧。但有些人在这里生活了一辈子，却从来都没有见过她！你能相信吗？”她惊呼道。

“确实挺奇怪的，你得承认这一点。”

“我理解人们想要一些隐私，但一个统治者有时候还是需要出现在她的子民身边的。我的意思是，镇上有些人的领导能力比她强得多，比如桑德斯修士或者加斯。她是这么说的。当她意识到自己刚刚说了些对男爵夫人来说相当不敬的话时，她的耳朵都快耷拉下来了。

“不过，千万别告诉别人是我说的这些话！
        |你知道吗，妮莉亚以前也是一名冒险者。我自己绝对想不出来。她还告诉我，大多数哥布林都会选择成为冒险者。我不是想冒犯谁，但我觉得他们的身高应该会严重影响到他们的冒险能力吧？有些哥布林甚至只有三英尺高！如果连门把手都够不着，怎么去战斗怪物和强盗呢？我并不是故意要批评，只是真的不明白……
        |克莱门汀紧张地挠着脖子，显然有话想对你说，但又害怕说出来。

“怎么了？”

“嗯，其实是这样的……”她开始说道，同时回头看了看周围，想确认是否有人在看着她——尽管她很清楚家里根本没有人。我去了一个摊位，那里有一个半人马在负责经营。排队的人很多，所以我想他肯定是在卖食物，但是……”她的话说到这里戛然而止，脸颊顿时涨得通红。她把身体向前倾靠在桌子上，示意你把脸凑近一些。 [party.isJustPC
            |尽管她又一次确认自己的家中确实没有人。
            |这样她就可以私下里对你低语了。
        ]你翻了个白眼，但还是满足了她的要求，慢慢靠近她，这样她就可以在你耳边低声说话了。[pc.ear]有个人在和他发生性关系！”她惊呼道。

嗯，没错。这就是苏戈的主要收入来源——与他人发生性关系罢了。

“但、但是，我是说在公共场合啊！”她惊叫道，彻底放弃了保持秘密的企图。“要是小孩子看到了怎么办？这里不是有禁止公共场合猥亵行为的法律吗？[party.has cait
            |
            
            凯特听到克莱门汀的打扰，暗自窃笑：“显然，你短期内是去不了贾西拉了。
            |
        ] 
        
        苏戈的摊位被布置得相当隐蔽，路人们如果不拉开帘子，是根本看不到他在里面做什么的。这意味着克莱门汀要想看到苏戈的实际操作，就必须进入他的摊位才行。
        
        听到你的话，克莱门汀的脸又红了一阵：“我、我在那个排队的地方等了差不多半个小时！要是早知道那是半人马的……卖淫摊位，我根本就不会去排队！我本来就不是那种会干涉别人职业的人，但他就不能去妓院工作，而不是把摊位设在市场中间吗？真是太荒谬了！我可以向你保证，在巴拉尼亚，他们是绝对不会批准这种事情的！妓女被禁止参与公共活动，而且必须持有合法的执照才能从事她们的工作。”

她再次倒抽一口气，因为她突然意识到了另一个令人震惊的事实。
        
        他到底有没有执照啊！？”她惊恐地叫道，紧紧抓住自己的脖子。

说实话，看到克莱门汀这种天真的样子，真的会让人忍不住发笑，而她则会恼怒地对你撅起嘴来。
    ]

    [rand
        |"Even though the Frost Marches are a lot poorer than most of the Heartlands, I like that there aren't a lot of aristocrats around here. I can't tell you how many nobles I've met who are so arrogant! Thinking they deserve everything in the world because they own a big castle, even though they've never worked a day in their life."
        
        "But oh my gods, the Baranian ones are the worst! This duchess, who thankfully lived an acre away from my family's farm, was a tyrant. The farmers that lived under her were bled dry for their crops to the point where some had to beg for food because they couldn't save enough. And she's not even the worst of them! I always heard tales from the city about some servant getting imprisoned or publicly humiliated for making a small mistake or accidentally offending their masters. I swear, I just don't understand how in my race of so many gentle and kind people there could be so many cruel folks at the top."
        
        "Sorry, I kinda got carried away. Anyways, I'm just happy I don't have lick anyone's boots up here. Everyone here's just getting by, and it makes us all equal in a sense. Well, I guess the baroness is technically the leader and owner of the land, but as far as nobles go she's fine by me, even if I've never seen her."
        |"I feel kinda out of place here," she says a bit glumly.
        
        What does she mean?
        
        "Well, it's just that I'm the only sheepfolk in town, probably the only sheepfolk up north to be honest. [pc.ra sheepfolk
            |Er, well, I guess, you're also up north too. But I meant more like living here, you know, permanently, not like how you adventure all the time.
            |
        ] I mean, I'm not lonely, I've made plenty of friends here like Nelia and you, but I guess I just got so used to seeing sheepfolk all the time that it feels weird being the only one. I don't know, maybe I'm just homesick."
        |"I love how cold it is up here," she says with a pleasant smile.
        
        Really now? Most people who move here complain about the cold. Hell, even the people born here complain about the cold.
        
        "Well, I mostly like it because I can let my wool grow out nice and thick. Back in Barania and even some parts of the Heartland, the summers get so hot that you practically have to shear your wool to the skin if you don't want to get cooked alive. I can't stand cutting my fleece so short, it makes me feel naked," she says with a disgusted shudder.
        
        "It does get a little too cold sometimes. I wear my dresses most of the time, but sometimes I find myself shivering back home for some warmer clothes. And I've been using way more firewood than back in Barania; I'm just thankful it's so much cheaper here. I feel terrible for all the folk who don't have any fur to keep them warm, can't imagine how cold they must be all the time."
        |"The chapel’s really impressive for a town like Hawkethorne. I’ll be honest, I didn’t expect much when I saw the first homes; half of them barely looked like they could stand on their own. But the chapel’s enormous in comparison. I mean there’s villages in the Heartland that don’t have churches half as nice as this one." 
        
        "Only problem I have is that it's really bleak for a chapel. Hard to pay your respects to the Seven when there’s this foreboding sense of dread. Especially the gargoyles. I feel like I’ll get nightmares if I look at them too long," she says, stroking her arm wool for comfort. "I much prefer the chapels back in Barania, they definitely had a lighter atmosphere. But I don’t know, I guess it’s just because I’m not a northerner." 
        
        "I do have to say though, Brother Sanders is one of the nicest priests I’ve met. He’s very relaxing to talk to and he never openly judges you, either. I’ve met plenty a priest and priestesses who like to scold you for your lack of prayer and how you’ll be damning yourself to a terrible afterlife when Tira comes for you."
        |"Do you find it weird that the baroness never comes out of her castle? Even the shyest nobles in the Heartland have made some effort to appear in public. But there’s some people who’ve lived here their entire lives and they’ve never even seen her! Can you believe it?" she exclaims.
        
        It is quite strange, you have to admit.
        
        "I get wanting to have some privacy, but a ruler has to be around her subjects sometimes. I mean there’s people in town who do a better job leading than she does, like Brother Sanders or Garth." she says. Her ears fall flat when she realizes she’s just said some pretty treasonous words when it comes to the baroness.
        
        "D-don’t tell anyone I said that, though!"
        |"Did you know Nelia used to be an adventurer? I never would’ve guessed it myself. She even told me that most goblins become adventurers. Not to be offensive but I would’ve figured that their short height would seriously impair their adventuring ability. I mean some of them are as short as three feet! How do you fight monsters and bandits when you can’t even reach a door handle? I’m not trying to be mean, I’m just, I don’t get it..."
        |Clementine scratches her neck nervously, clearly wanting to tell you something but too afraid to say it.
        
        What’s up?
        
        "Umm, well it’s just that..." she starts, looking behind herself to see if anyone’s looking at her despite knowing full well there’s no else in her house. "I went to a stall and there was a centaur manning it. There was a big line so I t-thought he must be selling some food b-but..." she trails off, a red blush burning through her cheeks. She leans forward on the table, waving at you to move your face closer to hers [party.isJustPC
            |despite once again knowing that there’s no one else in her home.
            |so that she can whisper to you in private.
        ] You roll your eyes but accede to her requests, inching yourself closer so that she can whisper in your [pc.ear]. 
        
        
        "There was a man having sex with him!" she gasps.
        
        Well, yeah. That is Sugo’s main source of revenue. Fucking and getting fucked.
        
        "B-but, I-I mean in public!" she exclaims, completely throwing her attempt at secrecy out the window. "L-like what if a kid sees that? Don’t you have laws here against public indecency?"[party.has cait
            |
            
            Cait snickers at Clementine’s disturbance. "Clearly you’re not gonna be visiting Jassira any time soon."
            |
        ] 
        
        Sugo’s stall is pretty well closed off, enough that passerbys wouldn’t see his business without pulling back the drapes. Which would mean that Clementine would’ve had to have entered his stall to witness Sugo in action.
        
        Clementine’s face flushes another shade of red at your words, "W-well I stood in that l-line for almost half an hour! I wouldn’t have if I had known it was a centaur’s, s-sexstall! I’m not one to butt into people’s...p-profession, but couldn’t he work in a whorehouse instead of being right in the middle of the market? It’s just, ahh it’s just so scandalous! They would not approve of this back in Barania, I assure you! Prostitutes are forbidden from public activity and require a proper license to perform their line of work."
        
        She gasps once again, coming to another horrible realization.
        
        "Does he even have a license!?" she cries out in horror, clutching her neck wool tightly.
        
        You honestly can’t help but laugh at Clementine’s innocence, making her pout at you in annoyance.
    ]'

rows.original: "You wanna know about me?" she asks coyly though by the way her ears are wiggling and the rapid wagging of her tail, Clementine’s more than happy to have an excuse to talk about herself. "Okay I guess I should start at the beginning. I was born in Barania, the only sheepfolk nation in the world." [party.has arona| Arona interrupts Clementine with a rambunctious laugh, making the sheep girl frown in anger. "H-hold, hold on a minute," Arona begins, trying to speak between her uncontrollable laughter. "There’s a nation in the world...ruled by sheepfolk...and it’s called Barania?" "Yes." Clementine says begrudgingly. That just sets Arona off even further, making her slap her hand against the table as she howls in laughter.[party.has cait| "Knock it off, Arona! Clementine’s trying to speak!" Cait exclaims angrily.|] [arona.isDom|You pout at Arona, she may be your alpha but this is still incredibly rude. She manages to calm her laughing after a while, occasionally slipping out a chuckle or two.|You shoot a fierce glare at Arona, quickly halting her laughing before she mumbles out an apology, awkwardly clearing her throat afterwards.] Clementine folds her arms angrily, her face scrunched into a cute pout. She waits until Arona’s laughing has completely stopped before continuing.|] "I was the oldest of six siblings; my Father was uh, w-well he was a busy person. Our large family made it hard to make ends meet. We were farmers you see, but our small farm couldn’t compete with the large estates that produced more crops in a month than we could in a year. Selling our wool wasn’t an option either, in a nation of sheepfolk there’s simply an abundance of it. Most people sold theirs to textile mills but that was never enough to make a living. I moved out when I was about eighteen summers. It was...hard leaving home but it was better for everyone. Made it easier for my family to live." "I thought I would get a farm of my own and follow in my parents' footsteps but I soon realized that it simply wasn’t the life for me. Waiting weeks for crops to grow only to have them ruined by a drought or stolen by a pack of roaming gnolls convinced me to pursue other passions. Like sewing!" "Most sheepfolk know some basic level of sewing but I decided to stake my career on it. Unfortunately that led me into the familiar problem of competition." She sighs. "Once more the abundance of my people pitted me against impossible odds. Everyone and their mother fancied themselves a tailor or a seamstress; there was just no place for a little fish like me in such a big pond." "So I decided to travel around, poke around the Heartland to ply my trade. It didn’t go very well. Most of my clothes were average at best and the close proximity to Barania meant more often than not that I would be competing with other sheepfolk who were far beyond my league. I tried to get an apprenticeship a handful of times but we sheepfolk can be amazingly prideful when it comes to our wool." "You see most sheepfolk who are tailors and seamstresses only apprentice their kin, proudly flaunting their wool as a mark of their heritage. I found a number of non-sheepfolk who would teach me but most of them just saw me as a wool factory rather than a real apprentice. Anytime I complained for higher wages or a real hand at sewing they would give some backhanded excuse or just fire me and hire another sheepfolk." "That led to me coming here. I learned that the Frost Marches had an extremely small population of sheepfolk, meaning I could practice my trade without too much competition. You rescued me from that marefolk, I managed to get an apprenticeship under Nelia in exchange for supplying my wool and that’s pretty much it." Nelia doesn’t abuse her for her wool like her previous employers? "No, she’s a very kind woman. That and I’m one of the few sheepfolk in the Frost Marches. If I decided to stop supplying her it’s not like she could just grab another sheepfolk off the streets." "Ummm, what else, what else. Oh! I love to bake, as you probably know. Seeing people enjoy my baking just makes my heart melt inside. If I wasn’t a seamstress I would definitely be a baker. Only thing is I can’t stand the mess, there’s just so much to clean up afterwards." Clementine kicks her legs back and forth, thinking of what else to say. "Mmmm, that’s about it really. Sorry it’s not the most exciting story."
rows.translation: 你想了解关于我的事情吗？”她娇嗔地问道，不过从她耳朵的摆动以及尾巴快速摇动的样子来看，克莱门汀其实非常乐意找个借口来谈论自己。 “好吧，我想我应该从一开始讲起。我出生在巴拉尼亚，那是世界上唯一的羊人国度。 [party.has arona| 阿罗娜突然放声大笑，打断了克莱门汀的话，这让这位牧羊女孩愤怒地皱起了眉头。 “等、等一下，”阿罗娜边笑边试图说道，“世界上有一个国家……是由羊人统治的……它叫巴拉尼亚，对吗？” “对。”克莱门汀不情愿地回答道。 这反而让阿罗娜笑得更厉害了，她甚至拍着桌子，放声大笑起来。[party.has cait| 别闹了，阿罗娜！克莱门汀正在试图说话呢！”凯特愤怒地喊道。|] [arona.isDom|你对着阿罗娜撅起了嘴——虽然她可能是你的“主导者”，但这种行为还是太无礼了。过了一会儿，她终于止住了笑声，只是偶尔还会偷偷地笑出声来。|你狠狠地瞪了阿罗娜一眼，立刻让她停止了笑声。随后，她尴尬地低声道了歉，还不停地清了清嗓子。] 克莱门汀生气地抱起双臂，脸蛋皱成可爱的嘟嘴状。她等到阿罗娜的笑声完全停止后，才继续说道。|] 我是六个兄弟姐妹中最大的；我的父亲，嗯，他是个很忙碌的人。我们这个大家庭让我们的生活陷入了困境。我们是一家农民，但我们的小农场根本无法与那些大型农场竞争——那些大型农场在一个月内生产的农作物，就比我们一年生产的还要多。在这个以养羊人为主的国家里，出售羊毛根本不是个可行的选择——因为这里的羊毛实在太多了。大多数人都会把羊毛卖给纺织厂，但这样的收入根本不足以维持生计。大约在十八岁的时候，我离开了那里。离开家确实很艰难，但这对每个人来说都是最好的选择。这样也能让我的家人生活得更加安心。 我原本以为自己可以拥有一片属于自己的农场，继承父母的事业，但很快我就意识到，这种生活方式并不适合我。花费数周时间等待农作物生长，结果却因为干旱而颗粒无收，或者被一群游荡的豺狼偷走——这些经历让我决定去追求其他自己热爱的东西，比如缝纫！ 大多数羊人族都掌握一些基本的缝纫技巧，但我决定将自己的职业生涯押在这一点上。不幸的是，这也让我陷入了那个老问题——竞争。”她叹了口气，“又一次，我们族群人数众多，这让我陷入了几乎毫无胜算的竞争之中。几乎每个人都自认为是裁缝或缝纫匠；在这么大的‘池塘’里，像我这样的‘小鱼’根本没有任何生存空间。 于是我决定四处游历，去 Heartland 地区摆摊卖货。不过进展并不顺利。我的衣服大多只能算马马虎虎，而由于距离巴拉尼亚很近，我经常要和其他那些实力远超我的羊人竞争。我试着找过几次学徒的机会，但对我们羊人来说，羊毛可是我们极其看重的东西，因此他们在选择学徒时也会格外挑剔。 你知道，大多数从事裁缝工作的羊人族都会只收自己的族人当学徒，他们总是骄傲地展示自己的羊毛，以此作为自己传统的象征。我也遇到过一些非羊人族愿意教我手艺的人，但大多数人只把我当作一个羊毛加工工，而并非真正的学徒。每当我要求更高的工资或真正得到一些缝纫指导时，他们总会找一些托词推脱，或者直接解雇我，然后雇另一个羊人族来代替我。 这就是我来到这里的原因。我发现霜冻之地地区的羊人数量非常少，这意味着我可以在这里毫无竞争地从事我的职业。是你把我从那些马人手中救出来的，后来我得以在内莉娅的指导下当学徒，作为交换，我需要为她提供羊毛，大致就是这样的经历。 内莉娅并没有像她之前的雇主们那样，因为我要羊毛就欺负我吧？ “不，她是个非常善良的女人。而且，我也是霜冻边境为数不多的羊人之一。如果我决定不再给她供应羊毛，她也不可能随便从街上找另一个羊人来代替我。 嗯，还有什么呢？哦！我想起来了爱你知道的，就是用来烘焙的。看到人们喜欢我做的面包，我的心里真的会感到无比开心。如果我不是从事裁缝工作的，我肯定会选择成为一名面包师。不过，我实在受不了烘焙后留下的那一片狼藉，事后总有太多东西需要清理。” 克莱门汀来回晃动着双腿，思考着还能说些什么。 “嗯，其实也就这些了。抱歉，这个故事并不是特别有趣。
