rows.original: [rand |You've noticed that despite being a frostscale salamander, Darius has picked up on many Jassiran customs and is quite knowledgeable about their culture. Is that something he learned from Barney? Darius pauses a moment, formulating his reply before slowly shaking his head. "Yes and no. I... I may have been born in this part of the world, I think, but I must've been sold as a slave before I was old enough to recall anything of that. My earliest memories are of Jassira, and that was where I grew up." He was a slave? "Yes... that's right. I was fortunate in that my first owner was a kindly old woman who treated me well, perhaps because of my exotic appearance. That, however, won me no favor amongst her other slaves, who took the opportunity to show their resentment for me behind her back. Then she fell into hard times, and I was sold off to another owner who was not so kind, although I didn't know it at first... "Suffice to say that I managed to free myself from her clutches, even though it took me years to figure out what kind of person she truly was. Then I happened to meet Barnaphous, who was on his way out of Jassira at the time; we had some time together, and in the end he encouraged me to return to what I should regard as my ancestral lands, and live amongst people who looked like me." [party.has cait |"Dad never mentioned you in any of the adventures he told Calla and me about." Darius gives Cait a thin little smile. "There're many people out there who owe your father a little of this and that, a favor or two. If he were to recount all of them, I'm sure he'd never get to telling the actual tale. But yes, while I traveled with him but for only a short while, it was long enough to know that Barnaphous Zethra is a man with many friends. You're quite fortunate to have such a father, Cait." ] So, he eventually moved to Tychris? A nod. "After Barnaphous and I parted ways, I took a ship across the ocean with the money I had; there were too many bad memories in Jassira for me and I thought a fresh start elsewhere couldn't be any worse than my other options. It was quite the trip, but I did make it to Tychris... and stayed there for a handful of years until Barnaphous suddenly writes to me and asks me to come bring a whole bunch of stuff down to this little village for him. "And that's the abridged version of my history, really." |Did Darius always have an interest in the arcane? "Well, I did, but I never quite had the chance to have any formal schooling in the arts, what with my circumstances growing up. Most of it was self-taught under the auspices of my second owner; at the time, I thought she was keeping such a close eye on my progress because she cared for me. What a fool I was. I started dabbling in magic for her sake, and later... it became a matter of revenge. "Most of the practical knowledge that's being applied here in this laboratory I either picked up over the year I traveled with Barnaphous, or during my stint as a librarian in Tychris. Many people fetishise formal schooling, especially since it used to be a mark of privilege in the old Belharan Empire, but when it comes to actual learning I'd like to think I'm at least a couple steps ahead of your average hedge-wizard. When I applied for the position at the palace library, they were a bit skeptical given my lack of credentials, but I was sufficiently able to demonstrate my knowledge that I did eventually get the position. It took some persuading and it was a grunt job, but I got it and that's what mattered." That's interesting... "The Order Astrida sometimes sends agents out to gather relics for the goddess Nareva herself; I've seen their little processions through the palace when they do depart. While I'd have loved to be able to join them, I'm not exactly fit for the job, and even if I were you have to be born to the position. Still, a salamander can dream." |"As much as possible, I'd like to think of Tychris, and by extent the larger Marches as my home. While Jassira was where I grew up, it's hard to consider it as someplace where I belonged. If you'd asked me this question five, six years ago I might've given you a different answer, but as it stands I've felt more at home here in this part of the world than I've ever been." Home is where the heart is, as the saying goes, and his heart wasn't in Jassira. "It was for a while, but... things happened. Still, I like it that there's a Jassiran-style Mallachite temple here; it brings back all the good parts of that place without all the bad. That, and the fact that it's managed by Barnaphous' daughter helps a lot, heh." |"Nothing beats a good spice tea after work. The spice doesn't actually do anything for me since I'm a frostscale and all, but it's a habit I've grown used to — even slaves get a spice ration in Jassira, albeit measly, hard spice loaf of the sort that's thrown out the back of bakeries at the end of the day. Barnaphous, though, he got me into the habit, and there's something relaxing about boiling the water and steeping the spice that's relaxing and soothing for the nerves." So, he doesn't smoke or snort or eat it like the catfolk do. Darius shakes his head. "Like I just said, it's about the making of the tea and what it means to me. A placebo effect, if you will; I've always found it a good way to start a day I know will be hectic — which is every day these days. This is quite the interesting anomaly you've got here, really..." |You note that Darius is quite tall, even for a 'mander. He nods. "I grew up, but not out; while I never actually starved as a child, Barnaphous says it's unlikely I got a proper diet as a slave and it's left its mark on me. In a land of five to six-foot cat-people, that's bound to draw some stares; my second owner used to parade me around to intimidate others while she was about her business. She said... she liked her men younger than her, and taller too." ...You seem to have struck a nerve there. "You did, but it doesn't matter. Even when I returned to Tychris, I was still a good half to a whole foot taller than most other frostscales; it was a bit of a shock to find that I still couldn't stretch out in bed. I'd imagined all the other salamanders would be as tall as I was... but all their weight went to thickening their bodies instead of lengthening them. Ha! "Still, it has its uses. Barnaphous says I'm good for picking things off high places, and though he means it as a joke it's actually quite true. Some of this instrumentation can be quite fiddly for a man of his build." ]
rows.translation: [rand |你可能已经注意到，尽管达里厄斯是一只冰鳞蝾螈，但他却掌握了许多贾西兰人的习俗，对他们的文化也相当了解。这是他从巴尼那里学到的吗？ 达里厄斯停顿了一下，仔细思考后才缓缓摇了摇头。既是也不是。我想，我可能是出生在这个地区的，但在我还有记忆之前，我就被卖成了奴隶。我最早的记忆是与贾西拉有关的，我也是在那里长大的。他曾经是奴隶吗？ “是的……没错。我很幸运，我的第一个主人是一位善良的老妇人，她对待我很好，也许是因为我外貌与众不同。然而，这并没有让我得到她其他奴隶的喜爱，那些奴隶总是找机会在她背后表现对我的不满。后来她陷入了困境，而我也被卖给了另一个并不那么善良的主人，虽然起初我并不知道这一点…… “总之，我终于摆脱了她的控制，尽管花了好几年时间才弄清楚她究竟是一个怎样的人。后来，我偶然遇到了巴纳福斯，他当时正准备离开贾西拉；我们一起度过了些时光，最后他鼓励我回到我应该称之为故乡的地方，去和那些和我长相相似的人们一起生活。" [party.has cait |爸爸在给我们俩讲那些冒险故事时，从来没有提到过你。” 达里厄斯对着凯特微微一笑：“这个世界上有很多人欠你父亲的情或债，欠他一些帮忙或恩惠。如果他要把这些事都讲出来，恐怕永远也讲不完那个真正的故事。不过，虽然我和他一起旅行的时间不长，但那段时间足以让我明白：巴纳福斯·泽特拉确实是一个拥有很多朋友的人。凯特，你能有这样的父亲，真是非常幸运。 ] 所以他最终搬去了提克里斯？ 点头道：“在和巴纳福斯分道扬镳后，我带着手头的钱乘船穿越了大洋。在贾西拉，我有太多不堪回首的记忆，所以我觉得在别的地方重新开始，总不会比之前的选择更糟糕吧。这一路确实相当艰辛，但我最终还是来到了提克里斯……并在那里住了好几年。直到巴纳福斯突然写信给我，邀请我带一大堆东西来到这个小镇帮他。 其实，这就是我经历的简要概括。 |达里乌斯一直以来都对神秘学感兴趣吗？ “嗯，我确实感兴趣，但由于我成长的环境，我从未有机会接受过系统的神秘学教育。大部分知识都是我在第二任主人的指导下自学获得的；当时，我以为她之所以如此关注我的学习进展，是因为她关心我。我真是个傻瓜。起初，我是为了她才开始接触魔法的，后来……这变成了一种复仇的方式。 这个实验室里所运用的大部分实用知识，都是我在跟随巴纳福斯旅行的那一年里学到的，或者是在我担任提克里斯图书馆馆长的期间积累的。很多人过分推崇正规的教育体系，尤其是因为在古老的贝尔哈兰帝国，接受正规教育曾经是一种特权象征。但就真正的学习效果而言，我认为自己至少比那些普通的草药师要强上几步。当我申请宫廷图书馆的这个职位时，由于我缺乏相关资历，他们对此有些怀疑。但我成功地证明了自己的专业知识，最终还是得到了这个职位。虽然过程中需要一些说服工作，而且这份工作也比较琐碎，但能够得到它才是最重要的。" 那倒挺有意思的…… “阿斯特里达教团有时会派遣使者们去为娜雷瓦女神收集遗物；每当他们出发时，我都会看到他们列队穿过宫殿。虽然我很想加入他们，但我确实不适合这份工作，而且就算我适合，也必须出身于相应的家族才行。不过，梦想总归是可以有的吧。 |尽我所能，我想把提克里斯，以及更广泛的边境地区，视为自己的家园。虽然贾西拉是我成长的地方，但很难将其视为属于我的地方。如果你在五六年前问我这个问题，我可能会给出不同的答案，但如今，我觉得自己在这个世界上这个地方，比在任何其他地方都更像家。俗话说，家是心灵栖息的地方，而他的心其实并不在贾西拉。 “有那么一段时间，确实是这样……但后来发生了一些事情。不过，我还是很喜欢这里有这座具有贾西拉风格的马拉克信徒神庙；它让我想起了那个地方所有美好的回忆，却没有那些不好的东西。再加上这个项目是由巴纳福斯的女儿负责管理的，这也起到了很大的帮助作用，呵呵。 |没有什么比下班后喝一杯美味的香料茶更惬意的了。虽然作为霜鳞族的一员，这些香料其实对我并没有什么作用，但这也已经成为我养成的习惯——在贾西拉，就连奴隶也能得到一些香料，虽然数量很少，不过是那些在面包店每天结束时被扔掉的劣质香料面包而已。不过，巴纳福斯确实让我养成了这个习惯。煮水然后将这种香料泡进去，这个过程本身就有一种让人放松的效果，能够缓解神经的紧张。 所以，他并不像那些猫族族那样吸烟、吸鼻烟，也不会把这种香料吃掉。 达里厄斯摇了摇头。“就像我刚才说的，这其实与泡茶的过程以及这种行为对我而言意味着什么有关。你可以把它看作是一种心理作用吧；我一直觉得，在知道这一天会非常忙碌的时候——而如今这样的日子实在太多了——用这种方式开始一天，是个不错的方法。你这里遇到的这个异常情况确实相当有趣…… |你注意到，即使对于一个“曼德尔人”来说，大流士也相当高大。 他点了点头：“我是长大了，但并没有变高；事实上，我从来都没有真正饿极了巴纳福斯说，小时候作为一名奴隶，我很可能没有得到合理的饮食，而这无疑对我的身体产生了影响。在一个大多数人都身高有五到六英尺的国度里，这样的外貌肯定会引起别人的注意；我的第二任主人在忙自己的事情时，常常会带着我到处走，以此来吓唬别人。她说……她喜欢比自己年轻、个子更高的男人。 ……看来你说到她的心坎里去了。 “确实如此，但这也无所谓。即使当我回到提克里斯时，我的身高仍然比大多数其他霜之族成员高出半英尺到一整英尺。因此，当我发现仍然不过，这也有它的用处。巴纳福斯说我很适合去高处取东西，虽然他只是开玩笑，但实际上确实如此。对于他那样的体型来说，有些仪器确实很难使用。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |You've noticed that despite being a frostscale salamander, Darius has picked up on many Jassiran customs and is quite knowledgeable about their culture. Is that something he learned from Barney? Darius pauses a moment, formulating his reply before slowly shaking his head. "Yes and no. I... I may have been born in this part of the world, I think, but I must've been sold as a slave before I was old enough to recall anything of that. My earliest memories are of Jassira, and that was where I grew up." He was a slave? "Yes... that's right. I was fortunate in that my first owner was a kindly old woman who treated me well, perhaps because of my exotic appearance. That, however, won me no favor amongst her other slaves, who took the opportunity to show their resentment for me behind her back. Then she fell into hard times, and I was sold off to another owner who was not so kind, although I didn't know it at first... "Suffice to say that I managed to free myself from her clutches, even though it took me years to figure out what kind of person she truly was. Then I happened to meet Barnaphous, who was on his way out of Jassira at the time; we had some time together, and in the end he encouraged me to return to what I should regard as my ancestral lands, and live amongst people who looked like me." [party.has cait |"Dad never mentioned you in any of the adventures he told Calla and me about." Darius gives Cait a thin little smile. "There're many people out there who owe your father a little of this and that, a favor or two. If he were to recount all of them, I'm sure he'd never get to telling the actual tale. But yes, while I traveled with him but for only a short while, it was long enough to know that Barnaphous Zethra is a man with many friends. You're quite fortunate to have such a father, Cait." ] So, he eventually moved to Tychris? A nod. "After Barnaphous and I parted ways, I took a ship across the ocean with the money I had; there were too many bad memories in Jassira for me and I thought a fresh start elsewhere couldn't be any worse than my other options. It was quite the trip, but I did make it to Tychris... and stayed there for a handful of years until Barnaphous suddenly writes to me and asks me to come bring a whole bunch of stuff down to this little village for him. "And that's the abridged version of my history, really." |Did Darius always have an interest in the arcane? "Well, I did, but I never quite had the chance to have any formal schooling in the arts, what with my circumstances growing up. Most of it was self-taught under the auspices of my second owner; at the time, I thought she was keeping such a close eye on my progress because she cared for me. What a fool I was. I started dabbling in magic for her sake, and later... it became a matter of revenge. "Most of the practical knowledge that's being applied here in this laboratory I either picked up over the year I traveled with Barnaphous, or during my stint as a librarian in Tychris. Many people fetishise formal schooling, especially since it used to be a mark of privilege in the old Belharan Empire, but when it comes to actual learning I'd like to think I'm at least a couple steps ahead of your average hedge-wizard. When I applied for the position at the palace library, they were a bit skeptical given my lack of credentials, but I was sufficiently able to demonstrate my knowledge that I did eventually get the position. It took some persuading and it was a grunt job, but I got it and that's what mattered." That's interesting... "The Order Astrida sometimes sends agents out to gather relics for the goddess Nareva herself; I've seen their little processions through the palace when they do depart. While I'd have loved to be able to join them, I'm not exactly fit for the job, and even if I were you have to be born to the position. Still, a salamander can dream." |"As much as possible, I'd like to think of Tychris, and by extent the larger Marches as my home. While Jassira was where I grew up, it's hard to consider it as someplace where I belonged. If you'd asked me this question five, six years ago I might've given you a different answer, but as it stands I've felt more at home here in this part of the world than I've ever been." Home is where the heart is, as the saying goes, and his heart wasn't in Jassira. "It was for a while, but... things happened. Still, I like it that there's a Jassiran-style Mallachite temple here; it brings back all the good parts of that place without all the bad. That, and the fact that it's managed by Barnaphous' daughter helps a lot, heh." |"Nothing beats a good spice tea after work. The spice doesn't actually do anything for me since I'm a frostscale and all, but it's a habit I've grown used to — even slaves get a spice ration in Jassira, albeit measly, hard spice loaf of the sort that's thrown out the back of bakeries at the end of the day. Barnaphous, though, he got me into the habit, and there's something relaxing about boiling the water and steeping the spice that's relaxing and soothing for the nerves." So, he doesn't smoke or snort or eat it like the catfolk do. Darius shakes his head. "Like I just said, it's about the making of the tea and what it means to me. A placebo effect, if you will; I've always found it a good way to start a day I know will be hectic — which is every day these days. This is quite the interesting anomaly you've got here, really..." |You note that Darius is quite tall, even for a 'mander. He nods. "I grew up, but not out; while I never actually starved as a child, Barnaphous says it's unlikely I got a proper diet as a slave and it's left its mark on me. In a land of five to six-foot cat-people, that's bound to draw some stares; my second owner used to parade me around to intimidate others while she was about her business. She said... she liked her men younger than her, and taller too." ...You seem to have struck a nerve there. "You did, but it doesn't matter. Even when I returned to Tychris, I was still a good half to a whole foot taller than most other frostscales; it was a bit of a shock to find that I still couldn't stretch out in bed. I'd imagined all the other salamanders would be as tall as I was... but all their weight went to thickening their bodies instead of lengthening them. Ha! "Still, it has its uses. Barnaphous says I'm good for picking things off high places, and though he means it as a joke it's actually quite true. Some of this instrumentation can be quite fiddly for a man of his build." ] "

rows.translation: 他自己

rows.original: [rand |"I met Barnaphous shortly after I got away... I mean, I left my second and last owner. The man and his cart were stalled by the roadside with a broken wheel and I gave him a hand. Back then, I wasn't sure what I wanted to do with my life — the circumstances that led me to leave my second owner also left me rather aimless. The man set in a cup of spice tea while I replaced his wheel, and he asked me if I'd like to travel with him for a while, since I looked rather lost." Barney just up and asked him if he wanted to come with? [party.has cait |Cait nods and sighs. "That's Dad for you, alright. He's mostly a good judge of people, and impulsive too; I can completely believe him doing such a thing on the spur of the moment. There was a time back in Tronarii when he bought a share in a dust elf foundry just because he liked the cut of the owner's jib. Sure, it ended up making him even richer than he was, but... I'm getting sidetracked here." |"I'm not sure what he saw in me, if he did see anything in me. Barnaphous has always been an impulsive man in all the time I've known him — a trait that isn't always a bad thing, but nevertheless promises to keep things interesting. ] "I didn't know much of what I wanted to do, save that it ought to be different from what I did as a slave," Darius continues. "I had a little money with me when I fled, but that was already drying up; Barnaphous offering to let me travel with him was about as good a deal as any I'd have gotten, and given that he wasn't setting off any alarms in my mind it was as good a deal as any other. And as it turned out, it was the best offer I had the wherewithal to take in my life." |"Most of the year or two I traveled with Barnaphous were in and about Jassira and Tronarii, attending to his concerns. Back then, the man had developed a passing interest in metallurgy... of course, what passes for a passing interest in Barnaphous' books is an intense obsession for anyone else. "It behooved a rotund catfolk like him to have someone like me around, though. Having an seven-foot exotic 'mander at his side who knew a few parlour tricks of his own certainly dissuaded most would-be highwaymen from him and his cart. Those were rather tumultuous years for Jassira... with the Sultana changing any and every law on a whim, we tried to stay in Tronarii on business as long as possible, seeing to his business and scientific concerns. I wasn't interested in all this at first, but as I traveled with him, by and large I learned the value of intellectual curiosity." Ha! The way he is now, Darius certainly isn't the kind of man you'd have figured for being uninterested in the world about him. "Being a slave for as long as you can remember will do that to you — it's hard to appreciate the world for what it is when your basic needs aren't fully met. Barnaphous, though, regards the world with such a childlike wonder that helped me understand the simple joy of discovering something just because it's there. At first I thought him just silly and whimsical, but after two or three months on the road with him, I began to understand." |"I really owe a lot to Barnaphous — all the way down to my life, if that. I'm not sure where I might've ended up had I just ignored him and his cart by the roadside and left it at that; I was in a bad place at the time and would've likely ended up much worse off before long. I truly owe a lot to him, which is why when he wrote to me and asked me to meet him here, I dropped everything as quickly as I could and made my way to Hawkethorne." Well, Tychris isn't that far away — a four-hour carriage ride, if he ever needs to nip back to the city for any pressing business which might crop up. "Which it's unlikely to, given how I wrapped up all my loose ends before heading down here; I mostly lived in the palace library anyway, so it's not as if I have anything left behind gathering dust in my absence. But back to the point — if Barnaphous tells me to jump, I'm not going to ask him how high, because I'm going to jump as high as I can for his sake. I owe him as much." [party.has cait |"Wow, you're really devoted to Dad, aren't you?" "More than you can imagine," Darius replies, giving Cait an upnod. "Your father has friends like me on both sides of the ocean, I'd imagine — Tronarii, Jassira, half the new nations emerging from Belhar's ruinous corpse and more. He's the kind of man who makes friends easily, and it's served him well in his time. Knowing the right people can get you far." Cait hums at that. "I'd imagine so. Garth knew the right people, and look at what he managed to do with the temple in just ten days." "And it just so happened that your father was able to call on me as an assistant when he needed one, mere hours away where he made from his discovery. You're standing to inherit quite the network of contacts from your father, Caitriss — I'm sure that someone in your position will be able to put them to good use down the line." |That's some impressive loyalty that Barney's built up with him. "Tell me about it. Barnaphous is the kind of man who makes friends easily, and it's served him well in his time; he has friends like me on both sides of the ocean, I'd imagine — Tronarii, Jassira, half the new nations emerging from Belhar's ruinous corpse and more. For example, he was able to call on me as an assistant when he needed one, mere hours away from where he made his discovery... knowing the right people can get you far." ] You're not about to deny that. |How long has he known Barney? Darius scratches his chin. "Oh, huh. Five or six years, maybe seven... it certainly feels longer than that, I can tell you as much. I only traveled with him for a year or two, but we'd exchange letters from time to time. While he moved around a lot, there was this temple of Mallach he favored, and I'd send any missives there for him to pick up when he dropped by. Of course, given the fickleness of letters getting anywhere near their destination in a timely manner these days, receiving any reply from him was a rare treat, but we still did our best to keep in touch with each other. Letting him fall out of my life completely would have felt... sacreligious, in a sense. It just wouldn't be something I'd have allowed myself to live with doing. "I can't say I go way back with Barnaphous like some of the Tronariians he introduced me to did, but I'm glad to have been a part of his life for a little while." |"I didn't have any formal education in the arcane, but I guess those long nights with Barnaphous came about as close to it as I ever will have. While I learned a parlour trick or hedge-wizard's incantation during my service to my second owner, who thought my talents cute even as she leveraged them, I never quite approached it in the manner that Barnaphous taught me to. Instead of being content with knowing that things worked and using the arcane as-is, he pushed me to ask why this was the case, to dig deeper beneath the surface. "At first, he had the answers to my questions, and then as those nights wore on one after the other, he didn't. And more importantly, he didn't just teach me the answers, but also that it was okay that I didn't have the answers, and how to get into the proper frame of mind for approaching the answers. That was something exceedingly new for someone who'd just left slavery half a year ago — the idea that admitting that you didn't know might be a good thing. And it is, because if you don't admit that you don't know, you can't learn. He taught me a little of everything, because of how the way different fields of study interacted; the truly interesting things tend to crop up on the borders, and you need to be able to see the bigger picture. Specialisation, as he liked to say, is something insects do." For Barney to trust Darius with being his assistant in this endeavour simply goes to show the confidence that he has in the 'mander's skills and attitude, if nothing else. "I haven't had many teachers, it's true, but he's the best I've ever had. Under him, I didn't just learn, but I also learned how to learn, and that's a skill that's rare enough in this day and age. Under that bumbling, cheery facade of his is a pretty sharp mind, and it would've been completely and utterly wasted in one of the Sultana's tax offices or whatever a distant relative of hers would be up to. It's all I can do to hope that I can get all his stories out of him before he's too old to travel much anymore." ]
rows.translation: [rand |在我离开之后不久，我就遇到了巴纳福斯……我的意思是，我离开了我的第二位也是最后一位主人。那个男人和他的马车因为车轮坏了而停在路边，我帮了他一把。那时候，我还不确定自己未来想做什么——那些让我离开第二位主人的原因，也让我感到十分迷茫，不知道该往哪个方向前进。那男人一边喝着加了香料的茶，一边让我帮他更换轮子。他看到我看起来有些迷路，便问我是否愿意陪他一起旅行一段时间。 巴尼直接走上前去，问他是否愿意一起来。 [party.has cait |凯特点了点头，叹了口气：“这就是你爸爸，没错。他在判断人方面通常很准，但也容易冲动；我完全相信他会一时冲动做出这样的举动。在特洛纳里的时候，他就因为喜欢某个老板的言谈方式，就买下了那家尘埃精灵铸造厂的股份。当然，最终这让他变得比以前更加富有，但是……我有点跑题了。 |我不确定他在我身上看到了什么，或者说他是否真的在我身上看到了什么。在我认识巴纳福斯这段时间里，他一直都是一个行事冲动的男人——这种性格特点并不总是坏事，但确实能让事情变得有趣起来。 ] 其实我当时并不清楚自己真正想要做什么，只知道这件事一定不能和我当奴隶时做的事情一样，”达里乌斯继续说道。“逃跑的时候我带了一些钱，但那些钱很快就花光了；巴纳福斯提出让我和他一起旅行，这个提议对我来说已经算是最好的选择了。而且，由于他并没有让我感到任何不安或疑虑，这个提议确实是我当时能够接受的最佳选择。事实上，后来证明，这确实是我这一生中得到的最好的机会。 |在那一年或两年里，我大部分时间都是和巴纳福斯一起在贾西拉和特洛纳里地区四处奔波，处理他手头的事情。那时候，他对冶金学产生了一丝兴趣……当然，对巴纳福斯来说只是一丝兴趣，但对别人来说，这已经是一种近乎痴迷的爱好了。 不过，像他这样的圆胖猫族，确实需要有人像我这样的存在在身边。有一个身高七英尺、掌握着一些独特技巧的异域伙伴在身边，肯定能吓退大多数想要劫掠他和他的货车的强盗。对贾西拉来说，那些年真是充满了动荡……由于苏丹娜总是随心所欲地修改各种法律，我们尽量长时间地留在特洛纳里，帮忙处理他的生意和科研事务。起初我对这些并不感兴趣，但随着与他一同旅行的经历，我逐渐明白了求知欲的重要性。" 哈！以他现在的样子来看，达里乌斯绝对不是那种会让你认为他对周围的世界毫无兴趣的人。 “从小就被当作奴隶生活，这样的经历确实会让人产生这样的想法——当你的基本需求都无法得到满足时，就很难去真正欣赏这个世界了。然而，巴纳福斯看待这个世界的方式充满了孩童般的惊奇与好奇，这让我明白了那种仅仅因为某物存在就去发现它所带来的简单而纯粹的快乐。起初，我以为他只是个愚蠢又古怪的人，但在与他一起旅行的两三个月后，我开始逐渐理解他的想法了。" |我真的欠巴纳福斯很多——甚至可以说，我的整个人生都欠他。如果当时我无视他以及他停在路边的马车，那么我不知道自己会落得什么下场。当时我的处境很糟糕，很快情况就会变得更糟。我真的非常感激他，因此当他写信邀请我到这里见面时，我立刻放下手头的一切，赶往鹰棘镇。” 嗯，提克里斯可不是这样那个距离相当遥远——如果他有什么紧急事务需要处理，乘坐马车的话需要四个小时才能回到城市。 “不过这种情况不太可能发生，因为在我来到这里之前，我已经把所有未处理的事情都解决了；而且我大部分时间都在宫殿的图书馆里度过，所以我的东西根本不可能有什么会被遗忘在原地积灰的。但回到正题——如果巴纳福斯让我跳，我不会问他要跳多高，因为为了他，我会跳得尽可能高。我欠他这个情。 [party.has cait |哇，你真的非常疼爱爸爸，对吧？” “远超你的想象，”达里乌斯回答道，同时向凯特点了点头。“我想，你父亲在海洋的两边都有像我这样的朋友——特洛纳里、贾西拉家族，还有那些从贝尔哈尔的废墟中新兴出来的新国家里的许多人士吧。他就是那种很容易交到朋友的人，这在他的职业生涯中确实帮了他大忙。结识合适的人确实能让你取得很大的成就。 凯特听后轻声附和道：“我想也是吧。加斯认识了很多合适的人，看看他在短短十天内为那座寺庙做了多少事情。而巧合的是，当你父亲需要帮助时，他能够及时找到我作为他的助手——我当时就在几小时的路程之外，正是由于我的发现，他才能取得今天的成就。凯特，你将继承你父亲建立起的人脉网络，我相信，处于你这样的位置，一定能够好好利用这些人脉资源。" |巴尼对他表现出了令人印象深刻的忠诚。 “说说看吧。巴纳福斯这种人很容易交到朋友，而这在他的一生中确实帮了他大忙；我想，他在大洋的两边都有像我这样的朋友——特洛纳里、贾西拉，还有那些从贝尔哈尔的废墟中新兴出来的新国家里的许多人，等等。例如，他在需要助手的时候，能够立刻找到我——而我当时距离他发现那个东西的地方仅仅几小时的路程……因为你知道，结识合适的人确实能帮助你走得更远。 ] 你总不会否认这一点吧。 |他认识巴尼有多久了？ 达里乌斯挠了挠下巴，说道：“哦，大概有五六年吧，也可能有七年……不过说实话，感觉时间似乎更长一些。我虽然只和他一起旅行了一两年，但我们还是会偶尔互相写信交流的。虽然他经常四处奔波，但有一座他特别喜欢的玛拉赫神庙，我会把所有的信件都寄到那里，等他有空的时候去取。当然，考虑到如今信件能否及时送达目的地实在难以预料，因此能收到他的回信已经算是非常幸运了，但我们仍然会尽最大努力保持联系。如果让他彻底从我的生活中消失，从某种意义上来说，我会觉得那是一种违背常理、违背道德的行为。我绝对无法接受这样的事情发生。 “虽然我和巴纳福斯的关系并没有像他介绍给我的那些特罗纳里安人那样深厚，但能够有那么一段时间成为他生活中的一部分，我还是很高兴的。" |我并没有接受过任何关于神秘力量的正规教育，但我想，与巴纳福斯共度的那些漫长夜晚，已经让我尽可能接近这种境界了。在为我的第二位主人服务期间，我确实学到了一些花招或是护林巫师的咒语，我的主人虽然觉得我的这些才能很有趣，但也确实利用了它们；不过，我从未真正按照巴纳福斯教给我的方法去学习这些知识。他并不满足于让我仅仅了解这些力量的运作原理，然后原封不动地使用它们，而是不断激励我去探索、去深入理解。为什么事实确实如此，我们需要更深入地探究其中的原因。 “起初，他能够回答我提出的所有问题，但随着那些夜晚一个接一个地过去，他再也无法回答了。更重要的是，他不仅告诉了我答案，还让我明白：没有答案也没关系，以及应该如何调整自己的心态来寻找答案。对于一个半年前才刚摆脱奴隶制的人来说，这种想法确实是非常新颖的——承认自己不知道某些事情，竟然可能是一件好事。事实确实如此，因为如果你不承认自己不知道，你就无法学习。他教会了我很多东西，因为不同学科之间的相互关联；真正有趣的东西往往出现在这些学科的交界处，而你需要具备把握整体局势的能力。用他自己的话来说，专业化才是昆虫才会做的事情。" 巴尼愿意让达里乌斯担任他在这项任务中的助手，这一事实本身就充分说明了他对达里乌斯的能力与态度的信任。 “说实话，我并没有遇到过很多老师，但他确实是迄今为止遇到的最好的老师。在他指导下，我不仅学到了知识，还学会了如何学习——这种能力在当今这个时代已经变得十分难得。在他那笨拙却开朗的外表之下，其实隐藏着一颗相当敏锐的头脑，而这样的头脑，如果被用在苏丹娜的税务办公室里，或者被她某个远亲用来处理那些繁琐的事情，那简直就是浪费了。我所能做的，就是希望在他年纪太大、无法再经常旅行之前，能把他的所有故事都记录下来。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"I met Barnaphous shortly after I got away... I mean, I left my second and last owner. The man and his cart were stalled by the roadside with a broken wheel and I gave him a hand. Back then, I wasn't sure what I wanted to do with my life — the circumstances that led me to leave my second owner also left me rather aimless. The man set in a cup of spice tea while I replaced his wheel, and he asked me if I'd like to travel with him for a while, since I looked rather lost." Barney just up and asked him if he wanted to come with? [party.has cait |Cait nods and sighs. "That's Dad for you, alright. He's mostly a good judge of people, and impulsive too; I can completely believe him doing such a thing on the spur of the moment. There was a time back in Tronarii when he bought a share in a dust elf foundry just because he liked the cut of the owner's jib. Sure, it ended up making him even richer than he was, but... I'm getting sidetracked here." |"I'm not sure what he saw in me, if he did see anything in me. Barnaphous has always been an impulsive man in all the time I've known him — a trait that isn't always a bad thing, but nevertheless promises to keep things interesting. ] "I didn't know much of what I wanted to do, save that it ought to be different from what I did as a slave," Darius continues. "I had a little money with me when I fled, but that was already drying up; Barnaphous offering to let me travel with him was about as good a deal as any I'd have gotten, and given that he wasn't setting off any alarms in my mind it was as good a deal as any other. And as it turned out, it was the best offer I had the wherewithal to take in my life." |"Most of the year or two I traveled with Barnaphous were in and about Jassira and Tronarii, attending to his concerns. Back then, the man had developed a passing interest in metallurgy... of course, what passes for a passing interest in Barnaphous' books is an intense obsession for anyone else. "It behooved a rotund catfolk like him to have someone like me around, though. Having an seven-foot exotic 'mander at his side who knew a few parlour tricks of his own certainly dissuaded most would-be highwaymen from him and his cart. Those were rather tumultuous years for Jassira... with the Sultana changing any and every law on a whim, we tried to stay in Tronarii on business as long as possible, seeing to his business and scientific concerns. I wasn't interested in all this at first, but as I traveled with him, by and large I learned the value of intellectual curiosity." Ha! The way he is now, Darius certainly isn't the kind of man you'd have figured for being uninterested in the world about him. "Being a slave for as long as you can remember will do that to you — it's hard to appreciate the world for what it is when your basic needs aren't fully met. Barnaphous, though, regards the world with such a childlike wonder that helped me understand the simple joy of discovering something just because it's there. At first I thought him just silly and whimsical, but after two or three months on the road with him, I began to understand." |"I really owe a lot to Barnaphous — all the way down to my life, if that. I'm not sure where I might've ended up had I just ignored him and his cart by the roadside and left it at that; I was in a bad place at the time and would've likely ended up much worse off before long. I truly owe a lot to him, which is why when he wrote to me and asked me to meet him here, I dropped everything as quickly as I could and made my way to Hawkethorne." Well, Tychris isn't that far away — a four-hour carriage ride, if he ever needs to nip back to the city for any pressing business which might crop up. "Which it's unlikely to, given how I wrapped up all my loose ends before heading down here; I mostly lived in the palace library anyway, so it's not as if I have anything left behind gathering dust in my absence. But back to the point — if Barnaphous tells me to jump, I'm not going to ask him how high, because I'm going to jump as high as I can for his sake. I owe him as much." [party.has cait |"Wow, you're really devoted to Dad, aren't you?" "More than you can imagine," Darius replies, giving Cait an upnod. "Your father has friends like me on both sides of the ocean, I'd imagine — Tronarii, Jassira, half the new nations emerging from Belhar's ruinous corpse and more. He's the kind of man who makes friends easily, and it's served him well in his time. Knowing the right people can get you far." Cait hums at that. "I'd imagine so. Garth knew the right people, and look at what he managed to do with the temple in just ten days." "And it just so happened that your father was able to call on me as an assistant when he needed one, mere hours away where he made from his discovery. You're standing to inherit quite the network of contacts from your father, Caitriss — I'm sure that someone in your position will be able to put them to good use down the line." |That's some impressive loyalty that Barney's built up with him. "Tell me about it. Barnaphous is the kind of man who makes friends easily, and it's served him well in his time; he has friends like me on both sides of the ocean, I'd imagine — Tronarii, Jassira, half the new nations emerging from Belhar's ruinous corpse and more. For example, he was able to call on me as an assistant when he needed one, mere hours away from where he made his discovery... knowing the right people can get you far." ] You're not about to deny that. |How long has he known Barney? Darius scratches his chin. "Oh, huh. Five or six years, maybe seven... it certainly feels longer than that, I can tell you as much. I only traveled with him for a year or two, but we'd exchange letters from time to time. While he moved around a lot, there was this temple of Mallach he favored, and I'd send any missives there for him to pick up when he dropped by. Of course, given the fickleness of letters getting anywhere near their destination in a timely manner these days, receiving any reply from him was a rare treat, but we still did our best to keep in touch with each other. Letting him fall out of my life completely would have felt... sacreligious, in a sense. It just wouldn't be something I'd have allowed myself to live with doing. "I can't say I go way back with Barnaphous like some of the Tronariians he introduced me to did, but I'm glad to have been a part of his life for a little while." |"I didn't have any formal education in the arcane, but I guess those long nights with Barnaphous came about as close to it as I ever will have. While I learned a parlour trick or hedge-wizard's incantation during my service to my second owner, who thought my talents cute even as she leveraged them, I never quite approached it in the manner that Barnaphous taught me to. Instead of being content with knowing that things worked and using the arcane as-is, he pushed me to ask why this was the case, to dig deeper beneath the surface. "At first, he had the answers to my questions, and then as those nights wore on one after the other, he didn't. And more importantly, he didn't just teach me the answers, but also that it was okay that I didn't have the answers, and how to get into the proper frame of mind for approaching the answers. That was something exceedingly new for someone who'd just left slavery half a year ago — the idea that admitting that you didn't know might be a good thing. And it is, because if you don't admit that you don't know, you can't learn. He taught me a little of everything, because of how the way different fields of study interacted; the truly interesting things tend to crop up on the borders, and you need to be able to see the bigger picture. Specialisation, as he liked to say, is something insects do." For Barney to trust Darius with being his assistant in this endeavour simply goes to show the confidence that he has in the 'mander's skills and attitude, if nothing else. "I haven't had many teachers, it's true, but he's the best I've ever had. Under him, I didn't just learn, but I also learned how to learn, and that's a skill that's rare enough in this day and age. Under that bumbling, cheery facade of his is a pretty sharp mind, and it would've been completely and utterly wasted in one of the Sultana's tax offices or whatever a distant relative of hers would be up to. It's all I can do to hope that I can get all his stories out of him before he's too old to travel much anymore." ] "

rows.translation: 巴尼

rows.original: [rand |Is this makeshift laboratory they've got going up about the portal safe? Cait lives here, after all. Darius scratches his horns. "Well, 'safe' is a relative term. Nothing's completely safe when you're dealing with a portal, because of its very nature — no matter what precautions we take, there's always going to be that element of instability. You know what I mean, having experienced it personally yourself." Um... not exactly, but you think you understand what he's getting at. "It's as safe as Barnaphous and I can make it, which is enough for me to brew up some spice tea and get to the reading while within a stone's throw of it. So long as we keep the spectrometer running, we should get plenty of advance warning of any actual danger if, say, the portal decides to open spontaneously." That's not as reassuring as you'd have liked it, but you trust Barney and him to know what they're doing. "Plenty of people work with potentially lethal things all the time. It's like working with quicksilver — certainly deadly in its own right, but so long as you take the proper precautions working with it isn't as intimidating any longer. I wouldn't worry too much about it if I were you." |All this that they've got going on here is quite impressive — [pc.bg arcanist |given your background as an arcanist, you've some idea of what they're doing here, and for them to be able to produce such a sophisticated setup on a shoestring budget is beyond belief |you don't know much of what's actually going on here, it's all quite over your head. Nevertheless, you can tell that they've put in a lot of effort into this, and on a shoestring budget, too ]. How did they manage? Darius looks away and clears his throat. "Ah. Well, Barnaphous did ask me to bring me some things from Tychris when he wrote to me, so I got the components he required — mostly everyday things, to be sure." These devices look to be anything but everyday, though. "Mostly the tools needed to make the fine pieces — much of Tychris' fine craft was lost in the Godswar, but what little the frostscales still retain still puts them considerably ahead of the competition. However, by and large it is Barnaphous' ingenuity; he's a master of creating such devices out of anything at hand. I guess it comes with always being on the road — you can't quite rightfully lug about a laboratory with you, but still it goes to show how deeply he understands what he chooses to study. "The spectrometer, for example, was put together from a tin bath, a chip of emerald for the focus, several copper springs he had the blacksmith make, and a couple of fine glass tubes he asked me to bring from Tychris. It's rather ungainly, but it does the job well enough for our purposes. Then there's the matter of the spice distillery Salwah asked him to hook up..." Yeah... you remember meeting Barney in the old caravanserai and the trick with the smoke and lights he tried to pull off on you, thinking it was the centaurs come to get him. Wonder what went into that. Darius nods. "Sounds like Barnaphous, all right. Well, the exact composition would've varied depending on what he'd on hand, but I know he always uses a bit of crackle powder when he does that trick. It does very well to scare off the unlearned." |So, what exactly is it that they're doing here that requires all this arcane apparatus to be here in Cait's private quarters? Not that there's any lack of space, of course, but... [party.has cait |"It's all right, [pc.name]," Cait says from beside you. "Garth's people wanted to wall off the spot where the portal was, but I asked them not to. It... reminds me of why I'm really here, and if Calla does make it back somehow, someday, I want to be the first to greet her. That makes... a whole lot of sense. ] Darius clears his throat. "Well, the first task is to keep the portal stable on this end, prevent it from spontaneously opening and posing a danger to anyone. We're trying to figure out if we can open and close the portal at will, where it leads, and if it would be possible to, say, send someone over to the other side to retrieve Calla. If there's no hope of that, then we owe it to her to find a way to permanently close it so that no one else can befall her fate. "That being said, the portal, dormant or otherwise, still produces a considerable amount of latent energy — it's quite fitting that we're tapping the portal's magic in order to power the devices by which we're studying it. Of course, everything has to be carefully managed lest we create some sort of mishap and the Order Astrida has to be sent in. It's never good when that lot are sent out from the gates of Tychris, but on the bright side, if we do something terrible enough to warrant their attention chances are we'd be all dead, or worse." Then all the winding and cranking he does... "Calibrations, tuning, or winding up the emergency spring-loaded systems. But by and large, our ideal outcome is that we're able to discover useful information about the portal that could lead us to retrieving Calla. Of course, Barnaphous being who he is, the man also has a considerable interest in the thing for its very phenomenal nature and how it reacts to the yearly astrological alignment that the cult was using to send people through as sacrifices. We don't know for sure if there're any malevolent entities on the other side that actually received those helpless souls or if the cult's actions were merely those of insane zealots; either way, the lessons of Estelore drive home the fact that we need to be extremely careful while we're studying this matter." |Actually, you just had a thought: if Darius came from Tychris and he was working at the palace library, wouldn't they be interested in what he was doing down here? Enough, perhaps, to send some actual material aid for Barney's laboratory down here instead of having to rely on... well, cobbled-together instruments? Darius frowns. "It may not look like much, but everything Barnaphous has put together here is extremely functional. We're not idiots jockeying for the palace's patronage from dwindling coffers here, so there's no need to look nice. Anything Barnaphous didn't already have on him or couldn't source locally, I obtained from Tychris before arriving here." All right, maybe that came out wrong. What you meant was that you'd expected one of the last actual bastions of scholarly pursuits in this part of the world to take more interest in what should be a discovery of some import, to want to study it more closely. Barney and Darius may not need material aid if he's adamant about it, but certainly the attention and patronage of — The 'mander cuts you off with a dismissive wave of a hand. "They're having their own troubles now. Money, politics... the same thing that happens whenever an organisation grows large enough to be noticed. That, and something with the Lady Tethys and her daughter... either way, I mean to dutifully send letters back every fortnight, and head back in person every month to report Barnaphous' and my collated findings. To date, I haven't received anything more than perfunctory acknowledgement of our work here. "Barnaphous has always been of the mind that scientific endeavour should be the domain of independently wealthy ladies and gentlemen, labouring away quietly on their own or in small groups at best, unbeholden to anything but their own curiosity and desire to understand the underpinnings of our world. Maybe it wasn't so in the past, but given the state of things as they are now, my experiences have led me to agree with this assessment." It's... romantic, to be sure. You were just hoping that with more resources at hand, the two of them could be making speedier progress towards finding a way to retrieve Calla, or at least give Cait some closure on the matter if that isn't possible. "If we were to accept funding from official sources in Tychris, we'd be directing our research according to their agenda, not ours; our task here is to observe the truth, but unfortunately many of what scholars remain in this day and age are more interested in creating their own so-called truth, rather than reporting it. If the Order Astrida were to... no, attracting attention from that lot never ends up well. Don't worry about us, [pc.name] — we have sufficient resources for our needs. Barnaphous is a man of many means, to put it lightly." |You've noticed that Darius comes into the lab every day, rain or shine, regardless of what else is going on in the temple. That's got to take some dedication. "Someone's got to make sure the monitoring apparatus is in good working order, if nothing else. Collecting the readings... while we don't actually need someone watching them all the time, it's not like I've got anything better to do. Certainly, I'm not about to be partaking of the temple's services, despite them being all around me!" Daris looses a shaky laugh. "This is a place of passion, and if you don't mind, my passion is right here. Yes, this is my worship of Mallach, thank you very much." [party.has cait |"Are you sure?" Purring, Cait rubs up against the 'mander, curling the tip of her tail about his. "You wouldn't allow Sally and I to tempt you?" ] Seriously, though. "Barnaphous takes over in the evenings, so I'm able to have some time to myself. Frankly, though, I stay on even then — it's nice to be able to relax over spice tea and reminisce old times. As an added bonus, I'm also on hand if he suddenly needs me for something. I don't see any problems with this..." ]
rows.translation: [rand |他们正在那个传送门附近搭建的这个临时实验室，真的安全吗？毕竟，凯特就住在这里。 达里乌斯挠了挠自己的角：“嗯，‘安全’这个概念其实是相对的。当你涉及到传送门的时候，没有什么东西是绝对安全的——因为传送门的本质本身就决定了这一点。无论我们采取什么预防措施，总是会存在一定的不稳定性。你明白我的意思吧，因为我自己也有过这样的经历。” “嗯……其实不太明白，但你觉得你理解他的意思了。” “这个地方和巴纳福斯一样安全，而且我也能到达那里。对我来说，这就足够了——我可以在那里泡些香料茶，然后安心地阅读书籍。只要我们让光谱仪持续运行，那么一旦某个传送门突然开启，我们应该就能及时得到足够的预警。 虽然这并没有你想象中那么令人安心，但你也信任巴尼，相信他知道自己在做什么。 有很多人每天都在接触可能致命的物质。这就好比在处理水银一样——水银本身确实具有致命性，但只要采取适当的预防措施，处理它其实并不会那么可怕。如果我是你，就不会太为此担心。 |他们在这里所做的一切确实令人印象深刻—— [pc.bg arcanist |鉴于你作为一名奥术师的经历，你应该明白他们在这里到底在做什么。而他们能够用如此有限的预算建立起如此复杂的设施，实在令人难以置信。 |你其实并不太了解这里到底发生了什么，这一切都超出了你的理解范围。不过，你可以看出他们确实付出了很多努力，而且还是在一个极其有限的预算下完成的。 ]他们是怎么做到的呢？” 达里乌斯移开了视线，清了清嗓子说道：“啊，其实巴纳福斯在给我写信的时候，让我从提克里斯那里带一些东西过来，所以我拿来了他所需要的那些零件——当然，大部分都是些日常用品罢了。” 不过，这些设备看起来可一点都不像日常用品啊。 主要是制作这些精细部件所需的工具——在神战期间，提克里斯的大部分精湛工艺都丢失了，但霜鳞族所保留的那一点点知识，仍然使他们远远领先于竞争对手。不过，真正起到决定性作用的是巴纳福斯的创造力；他总能利用手头的一切材料制造出这样的装置。我想，这大概是因为他一直处于漂泊之中吧——毕竟你不可能真的带着一个实验室到处跑，但这一点确实体现了他对自己研究领域的深刻理解。 比如说，那个光谱仪就是他用一个锡制容器、一块祖母绿用来调节焦点、几根铜弹簧（这些都是他让铁匠制作的），还有几根精美的玻璃管（这些是他让我从提克里斯带来的）组装而成的。虽然看起来有点笨重，但对我们来说，它的功能已经足够满足了。另外，还有萨尔瓦让他帮忙搭建的香料蒸馏装置…… 是啊……你还记得在那个老旅舍里遇到巴尼吧？他当时用了烟雾和灯光来迷惑你，以为那是半人马来抓他的。真不知道他当时是怎么想的那个达里乌斯点了点头。“听起来像是巴纳福斯干的，没错。不过具体的配方会根据他手头有什么材料而有所不同，但我知道他在使用那个把戏时总会加入一些‘噼啪粉’。这种粉末在吓唬那些不懂门道的人时效果非常好。 |那么，接下来是什么呢？正是如此难道他们在这里所做的那些事情，真的需要用到所有这些复杂的设备吗？当然，凯特的私人空间里并不缺乏空间，但是…… [party.has cait |没关系，[pc.name]，”凯特在你旁边说道，‘加斯的人本来想把传送门所在的地方围起来，但我阻止了他们。因为那个地方……让我想起了自己真正来到这里的原因。如果卡拉有朝一日真的能回来，我希望成为第一个迎接她的人。 这样想的话……确实很有道理。 ] 达里乌斯清了清嗓子，说道：“首先，我们的任务是保持这个端口的稳定性，防止它自行打开从而对他人造成危险。我们正在尝试弄清楚是否能够随意控制这个端口的开闭，它通向哪里，以及是否有可能派人穿过它去把卡拉救出来。如果这些都无法实现，那么为了她，我们至少必须找到一种方法来永久关闭这个端口，这样就不会有其他人遭遇和她一样的命运了。 话虽如此，这个门户无论处于何种状态，依然会释放出大量的潜在能量——因此，我们利用这个门户所蕴含的能量来为研究它的设备提供动力，实在是再合适不过了。当然，一切都必须谨慎处理，否则就可能会引发一些麻烦，到时候阿斯特里达组织就不得不介入了。每当那些人从提克里斯的大门被派出来时，情况从来都不会好到哪里去。不过从好的方面来看，如果我们真的做出了足以引起他们注意的糟糕事情，那么很可能我们早就死了，或者遭遇更糟的后果。" 然后他所做的所有那些复杂的调整和操作…… “其实就是进行校准、调试，或者为那些紧急弹簧装置施加必要的压力。但归根结底，我们的目标就是能够获取关于这个传送门的有用信息，从而帮助我们找到卡拉。当然，以巴纳福斯的性格，他对这种事物自然也会产生浓厚的兴趣——毕竟它的性质实在非同寻常，而且它还会对每年一次的占星现象产生反应，而那个邪教正是利用这些占星现象来将人们作为祭品献祭的。我们并不确定，在另一边是否真的存在一些邪恶势力接收了那些无助的灵魂，或者那个邪教组织的所作所为仅仅是一些狂热分子的疯狂行为；无论如何，埃斯托洛尔的经历都告诉我们，在研究这个问题时，我们必须格外谨慎。" |其实，你刚刚想到了这样一个问题：如果达里乌斯来自提克里斯，而且他在皇宫图书馆工作，那么他们难道不会对他在这里做的事情感兴趣吗？或许，这种兴趣足以让他们为巴尼的实验室提供一些实质性的帮助，而不是让实验室继续依赖那些拼凑起来的仪器吧？ 达里乌斯皱起了眉头：“也许并不会看说实话，我并不是特别感兴趣，但巴纳福斯在这里准备的一切确实都非常实用。我们可不是那些为了从日益枯竭的国库中获得宫廷的支持而争斗的傻瓜，所以根本没有必要这样做。看很好。那些巴纳福斯身上没有或者在当地无法获取的物品，都是我在来到这里之前从提克里斯那里得到的。” 好吧，也许我的表达有些不清楚。你的意思应该是，你原本期望这个地区为数不多的学术研究堡垒之一，会对这样一个具有重要意义的发现表现出更大的兴趣，并愿意更深入地进行研究吧。如果巴尼和达里乌斯坚持自己的立场，他们可能并不需要物质上的帮助，但肯定需要得到更多的关注与支持…… 曼德尔挥了挥手，不屑地打断了我的话：“他们现在正忙于自己的麻烦事。金钱、政治……每当一个组织发展到足以引起人们注意的时候，就会遇到这些麻烦。另外，还有关于泰西斯女士和她女儿的事情……不管怎样，我打算每两周按时回信汇报工作进展，每个月都会亲自去汇报巴纳福斯和我收集到的所有信息。到目前为止，我们在这里的工作只得到了敷衍了事的回应而已。 巴纳福斯一直认为，科学研究应该是那些经济独立的女士和先生的事情——他们应该独自或至多以小团队的形式默默地进行研究，完全不受任何外界因素的干扰，只追求自己的好奇心以及了解这个世界运作原理的愿望。也许过去并非如此，但鉴于目前的状况，我的经历让我认同这种观点。 这确实……很浪漫。你只是希望，如果有更多的资源，他们两人能够更快地找到找回卡拉的方法；或者，如果那不可能实现的话，至少能让凯特在这个问题上得到一些释怀。 如果我们接受了提克里斯官方来源的资助，我们的研究方向就会受到他们的支配，而不是我们自己的意愿；我们在这里的任务应该是探寻真相，然而遗憾的是，如今许多学者更热衷于创造他们自己所谓的‘真相’，而不是去报道真相本身。如果“阿斯特里达秩序”招来了那群人的注意……不，任何试图吸引他们注意的行为最终都不会有好结果。你们不用担心我们。[pc.name]我们的需求所需的资源已经足够了。坦白说，巴纳福斯是个财力雄厚的人。 |你一定注意到了，无论天气如何，无论寺庙里还发生着什么，达里乌斯每天都会来到实验室。这种坚持确实需要极大的决心。 “至少，也必须有人确保那些监测设备能够正常运转。正在收集这些数据……虽然其实并不需要有人一直监督这些读数，但我也没什么其他事情可做。当然，我也不会去参加寺庙里的各种仪式，尽管这些仪式就在我身边发生！达里斯勉强挤出一丝笑意：“这里充满了激情，如果你不介意的话，我的激情就在这里。没错，这就是我对马拉克的崇拜，非常感谢你。 [party.has cait |你确定吗？”凯特发出轻柔的呼噜声，身体紧贴着那个“领导者”，尾巴的尖端还绕在了他的身上。“你不会让我们莎莉和我来诱惑你吧？ ] 说真的。 “晚上是巴纳福斯负责工作，所以我才能有属于自己的时间。不过说实话，即使在他工作的时候，我也会留在店里——边喝着香料茶边放松心情，回忆过去的时光，这种感觉真的很不错。另外，如果他突然需要我的帮助，我也在现场，所以我觉得这样没有任何问题…… ]
rows.raw: " [rand |Is this makeshift laboratory they've got going up about the portal safe? Cait lives here, after all. Darius scratches his horns. "Well, 'safe' is a relative term. Nothing's completely safe when you're dealing with a portal, because of its very nature — no matter what precautions we take, there's always going to be that element of instability. You know what I mean, having experienced it personally yourself." Um... not exactly, but you think you understand what he's getting at. "It's as safe as Barnaphous and I can make it, which is enough for me to brew up some spice tea and get to the reading while within a stone's throw of it. So long as we keep the spectrometer running, we should get plenty of advance warning of any actual danger if, say, the portal decides to open spontaneously." That's not as reassuring as you'd have liked it, but you trust Barney and him to know what they're doing. "Plenty of people work with potentially lethal things all the time. It's like working with quicksilver — certainly deadly in its own right, but so long as you take the proper precautions working with it isn't as intimidating any longer. I wouldn't worry too much about it if I were you." |All this that they've got going on here is quite impressive — [pc.bg arcanist |given your background as an arcanist, you've some idea of what they're doing here, and for them to be able to produce such a sophisticated setup on a shoestring budget is beyond belief |you don't know much of what's actually going on here, it's all quite over your head. Nevertheless, you can tell that they've put in a lot of effort into this, and on a shoestring budget, too ]. How did they manage? Darius looks away and clears his throat. "Ah. Well, Barnaphous did ask me to bring me some things from Tychris when he wrote to me, so I got the components he required — mostly everyday things, to be sure." These devices look to be anything but everyday, though. "Mostly the tools needed to make the fine pieces — much of Tychris' fine craft was lost in the Godswar, but what little the frostscales still retain still puts them considerably ahead of the competition. However, by and large it is Barnaphous' ingenuity; he's a master of creating such devices out of anything at hand. I guess it comes with always being on the road — you can't quite rightfully lug about a laboratory with you, but still it goes to show how deeply he understands what he chooses to study. "The spectrometer, for example, was put together from a tin bath, a chip of emerald for the focus, several copper springs he had the blacksmith make, and a couple of fine glass tubes he asked me to bring from Tychris. It's rather ungainly, but it does the job well enough for our purposes. Then there's the matter of the spice distillery Salwah asked him to hook up..." Yeah... you remember meeting Barney in the old caravanserai and the trick with the smoke and lights he tried to pull off on you, thinking it was the centaurs come to get him. Wonder what went into that. Darius nods. "Sounds like Barnaphous, all right. Well, the exact composition would've varied depending on what he'd on hand, but I know he always uses a bit of crackle powder when he does that trick. It does very well to scare off the unlearned." |So, what exactly is it that they're doing here that requires all this arcane apparatus to be here in Cait's private quarters? Not that there's any lack of space, of course, but... [party.has cait |"It's all right, [pc.name]," Cait says from beside you. "Garth's people wanted to wall off the spot where the portal was, but I asked them not to. It... reminds me of why I'm really here, and if Calla does make it back somehow, someday, I want to be the first to greet her. That makes... a whole lot of sense. ] Darius clears his throat. "Well, the first task is to keep the portal stable on this end, prevent it from spontaneously opening and posing a danger to anyone. We're trying to figure out if we can open and close the portal at will, where it leads, and if it would be possible to, say, send someone over to the other side to retrieve Calla. If there's no hope of that, then we owe it to her to find a way to permanently close it so that no one else can befall her fate. "That being said, the portal, dormant or otherwise, still produces a considerable amount of latent energy — it's quite fitting that we're tapping the portal's magic in order to power the devices by which we're studying it. Of course, everything has to be carefully managed lest we create some sort of mishap and the Order Astrida has to be sent in. It's never good when that lot are sent out from the gates of Tychris, but on the bright side, if we do something terrible enough to warrant their attention chances are we'd be all dead, or worse." Then all the winding and cranking he does... "Calibrations, tuning, or winding up the emergency spring-loaded systems. But by and large, our ideal outcome is that we're able to discover useful information about the portal that could lead us to retrieving Calla. Of course, Barnaphous being who he is, the man also has a considerable interest in the thing for its very phenomenal nature and how it reacts to the yearly astrological alignment that the cult was using to send people through as sacrifices. We don't know for sure if there're any malevolent entities on the other side that actually received those helpless souls or if the cult's actions were merely those of insane zealots; either way, the lessons of Estelore drive home the fact that we need to be extremely careful while we're studying this matter." |Actually, you just had a thought: if Darius came from Tychris and he was working at the palace library, wouldn't they be interested in what he was doing down here? Enough, perhaps, to send some actual material aid for Barney's laboratory down here instead of having to rely on... well, cobbled-together instruments? Darius frowns. "It may not look like much, but everything Barnaphous has put together here is extremely functional. We're not idiots jockeying for the palace's patronage from dwindling coffers here, so there's no need to look nice. Anything Barnaphous didn't already have on him or couldn't source locally, I obtained from Tychris before arriving here." All right, maybe that came out wrong. What you meant was that you'd expected one of the last actual bastions of scholarly pursuits in this part of the world to take more interest in what should be a discovery of some import, to want to study it more closely. Barney and Darius may not need material aid if he's adamant about it, but certainly the attention and patronage of — The 'mander cuts you off with a dismissive wave of a hand. "They're having their own troubles now. Money, politics... the same thing that happens whenever an organisation grows large enough to be noticed. That, and something with the Lady Tethys and her daughter... either way, I mean to dutifully send letters back every fortnight, and head back in person every month to report Barnaphous' and my collated findings. To date, I haven't received anything more than perfunctory acknowledgement of our work here. "Barnaphous has always been of the mind that scientific endeavour should be the domain of independently wealthy ladies and gentlemen, labouring away quietly on their own or in small groups at best, unbeholden to anything but their own curiosity and desire to understand the underpinnings of our world. Maybe it wasn't so in the past, but given the state of things as they are now, my experiences have led me to agree with this assessment." It's... romantic, to be sure. You were just hoping that with more resources at hand, the two of them could be making speedier progress towards finding a way to retrieve Calla, or at least give Cait some closure on the matter if that isn't possible. "If we were to accept funding from official sources in Tychris, we'd be directing our research according to their agenda, not ours; our task here is to observe the truth, but unfortunately many of what scholars remain in this day and age are more interested in creating their own so-called truth, rather than reporting it. If the Order Astrida were to... no, attracting attention from that lot never ends up well. Don't worry about us, [pc.name] — we have sufficient resources for our needs. Barnaphous is a man of many means, to put it lightly." |You've noticed that Darius comes into the lab every day, rain or shine, regardless of what else is going on in the temple. That's got to take some dedication. "Someone's got to make sure the monitoring apparatus is in good working order, if nothing else. Collecting the readings... while we don't actually need someone watching them all the time, it's not like I've got anything better to do. Certainly, I'm not about to be partaking of the temple's services, despite them being all around me!" Daris looses a shaky laugh. "This is a place of passion, and if you don't mind, my passion is right here. Yes, this is my worship of Mallach, thank you very much." [party.has cait |"Are you sure?" Purring, Cait rubs up against the 'mander, curling the tip of her tail about his. "You wouldn't allow Sally and I to tempt you?" ] Seriously, though. "Barnaphous takes over in the evenings, so I'm able to have some time to myself. Frankly, though, I stay on even then — it's nice to be able to relax over spice tea and reminisce old times. As an added bonus, I'm also on hand if he suddenly needs me for something. I don't see any problems with this..." ] "

rows.original:
[rand
        |"Quite well, actually. Like I think I've mentioned before, it really does bring back all the best parts of my life back in Jassira while hiding the worst. I have a clean living space, Salwah is a decent cook, and my days are calm and routine. From the perspective of someone who was a slave as a boy, such simple pleasures are sufficient for my needs."
        
        He doesn't partake of the temple's, uh, other activities?
        
        "You mean the poetry recital? I attend because Barnaphous does, and his company turns any event pleasant."
        
        No... 
        
        "Or perhaps you mean when River comes up to the temple to perform?"
        
        No... 
        
        "Well, I avoid the spice hall as much as I can. I'm not a catfolk, so it really doesn't do anything for me, and while spice tea is one thing all the heavy smoke and clink of spice plates isn't my style."
        
        Now you're thinking he's being obtuse on purpose.
        
        "The sacred whores and orgies aren't the point of the temple, although they do make up the lion's share of its notoriety. As far as temple activities go, though, I'm partial to being able to have a nice cold bath. By myself, of course." He chuckles. "No, [pc.name], I don't partake of the sex, and if I were to it wouldn't be on a formal basis. Salwah is already miffed enough at my continued presence in the temple, despite Caitriss making an exception for me."
        |Do the goings-on in the temple distract him from his work?
        
        "Sometimes, a whiff of smoke does creep in from the spice hall if someone leaves the door open. That's quite annoying. As for the temple's other activities... the walls are thick, and they don't carry sound that well. By design, I'd imagine."
        
        You see.
        
        Darius smiles and taps his forehead. "Yes, you see. Seriously, though — it's more a matter of one's frame of mind, than anything. Yes, I'm still young as frostscales reckon things, but the atmosphere here in this little corner of the temple is considerably different than the rest of it. I have needs, to be sure... but there are other needs, too, which I find far more fascinating than the other things going on around me. There are exceptions, as with anything, but out of sight, out of mind."
        |"Frankly, I'm quite interested in the temple's architecture. Barnaphous tells me that this used to be a pale elf ruin before Garth's people came in and fixed up the place for Cait."
        
        That's right. Before that, the demon cult had been squatting in the rubble, and even so it was surprisingly sturdy for having been abandoned so long. If the supports weren't sturdy after all those decades, they'd have to be replaced, and Garth's people wouldn't have been able to build around them.
        
        "Hm, hm. Despite the Jassiran trappings, the original splendour of the pale elves still manages to shine through in its architectural style. It's a marvelous rehabilitation of such a ruin, a fresh breath of air."
        
        Barney personally oversaw the construction work, if you remember correctly.
        
        "Ah!" Darius snaps his fingers. "That would explain it, yes. Barnaphous always had an interest in old architecture, especially of that period — he spends far too long up at Castle Hawkstone than what his pretexts cover for, really. But if he was the one directing the builders, it doesn't surprise me that the rather quaint blend of pale elf and Jassiran aesthetics was the result."
        |"There's a lot of space in this temple," Darius remarks. "It feels like it was built with the intention of accommodating many more people..."
        
        That, and it's a refurbished pale elf temple, which no doubt housed many druids in its heyday.
        
        "Yes, yes. It may be the matron's entire life's work to see it utilised to its maximum capacity, but I'm sure that given her drive and dedication, it'll eventually get done."
        
        [party.has cait
            |"I don't know about that, really," Cait says with a shake of her head. "It seems so far off..."
            
            "Now, don't undersell yourself."
            
        ]
        Hmm, you have perfect faith in Cait to get it done — for Calla and her dad, if not for her faith.
        
        "In the meantime, though, the vast, empty halls are quite fetching, especially when I have the pleasure of being alone in them. Hearing my footsteps echo... there's something to living in a restored ruin, isn't there?"
        |"I'd never have imagined that there'd be running water in such a place, but here we are. It's good for the baths, if nothing else — many of the baths in Jassiran temples have to be manually drained and filled by hand. Water is a precious commodity over there, as you'd imagine."
        
        Frankly, you found it quite surprising yourself.
        
        "For those who know the geology of the Marches, hot springs are quite commonplace — the Belharans built quite the grand resort up to the northeast, in what the locals call the Windy Peaks. No one goes there these days, what with it being overrun with harpies, but pressurised aquifers, whether heated or not, are all over the lay of the land. If the water weren't flowing on its own, I'm sure Barnaphous would have built a screw pump or something for his dear daughter's temple, but as things stand it really does save Salwah a lot of time when scrubbing the place out."
    ]
