Past the old stone bridge, better part of a day's walk from here. She sometimes helps the villagers with their more arcane problems: potions, rituals. Things little Ivris in her shop can't or won't do. Her help comes at a cost, but... it might be worth it to get a few answers, if you catch my meaning." You nod. Maybe you ought to pay that witch a visit... if you can get past the monsters in the woods. Something tells you, though, that it won't be easy."

rows.translation: 两耳之间
在肩上
古林

rows.original: "You mentioned orcs closing in from the hills, right?" Garth nods slowly, face twisting into a scowl. "I did. Raiders from the Sailgrave islands out east, judging by their banners. That means they're dangerous warriors. Good enough to face minotaurs head on and win. Usually their kind stay well south of here, beach their longboats and pillage a few coastal villages before sailing off by day's end. But these bastards, they've trekked across a mountain range to get to us. Started building fortifications in the foothills, like they mean to stay a while." That sounds... bad. "Are they a threat to the village?" "Any tribe would be. We don't have a proper guard, no soldiers except me and old man Sanders and whatever villagers we can round up into a militia. But these islanders are worse[pc.ora orc|; they're not like you heartlander orcs]. Experienced, organized, well armed. Their war camp is one rise from being in sight of the village — we can see their cookfire smoke in the daylight now. If they wanted a fight with Hawkethorne, though, they would have attacked already." Garth scowls, rapping his knuckles on the hardwood. "I'd say they're looking for something. Or someone. Doesn't mean we're safe, though. They might get low on supplies, or just get bored of breeding harpies and singing war-songs, and start to look our way. I've asked Leorah and her hunters to keep an eye on them, but even then, we're going to have to be on our guard while they're here. Nobody can sleep soundly." [pc.ora orc |"And talking to them would just be a sign of weakness, right?" you hazard. He's right, they aren't your people, but an orc's an orc all the same. You've known plenty that think that way. Garth gives you an approving nod. "That's the size of it. I'm not sending one of our men to his death... or a woman to a worse fate. Island orcs only know two ways through a challenge, and neither of them are good." |"Have you tried talking with them?" you hazard, already knowing the answer by the way Garth scowls at your question. "No. I'm not sending one of our men to his death... or a woman to a worse fate. They're brutes, and they think diplomacy is a sign of weakness." ]
rows.translation: “你说有兽人正从山麓逼近，对吧？” 加斯缓缓点头，脸庞因怒容而扭曲。“我确实说过。从他们的旗帜来看，是东边帆葬海岸群岛来的劫掠者。这意味着他们是危险的战士，强大到足以正面迎战弥诺陶洛斯并取胜。通常这类人都会待在南边很远的地方，让长船冲上沙滩，洗劫几座沿海村落，然后在日落前扬帆离去。但这群混蛋为了找到我们，居然跋涉穿越了一整条山脉。他们开始在山麓修筑防御工事，看起来打算待上一阵。” 听起来……很糟。“他们会威胁村子吗？” “任何部落都会构成威胁。我们没有正规的卫队；除了我、桑德斯老爷子，以及能召集起来组成民兵的村民，根本没有士兵。但这些岛民更加危险[pc.ora orc|；他们跟你这种腹地兽人不同]。他们经验丰富、组织严密、武装精良。战营再翻过一道坡就会出现在村子的视野里——现在白天都能看见他们炊火的烟了。不过，他们如果想跟鹰棘镇开战，早就已经动手。” 加斯皱起眉头，用指节敲击硬木。“依我看，他们是在找什么东西。或者某个人。不过这不代表我们安全。他们可能会缺少物资，也可能只是厌倦了让鹰身女妖怀孕和唱战歌，转而把目光投向我们。我已经请莱奥拉和她的猎手监视他们；即便如此，只要他们还在，我们就必须保持警惕。谁也睡不安稳。” [pc.ora orc |“而跟他们谈判只会被视为软弱，对吧？”你试探道。他说得没错；他们不是你的族人，但兽人终究是兽人。你认识许多抱持这种想法的兽人。 加斯赞许地点了点头。“就是这么回事。我不会派我们的人去送死……也不会让女人遭遇更糟的命运。岛屿兽人只知道用两种方式应对挑战，而两种都不是什么好事。” |“你试过跟他们谈谈吗？”你试探道；从加斯听到问题后皱起的眉头来看，你早已知道答案。 “没有。我不会派我们的人去送死……也不会让女人遭遇更糟的命运。他们是一群野蛮人，认为外交就是软弱的象征。” ]

rows.original: Damning claims, but if Garth's right, then something has to be done about them before they turn their sights on town. There's no way you can take on the whole camp at once, but there's got to be some way to get them to pack up and leave.
rows.translation: 这些指控相当严重，但如果加斯说得没错，就必须在他们把目光转向镇子之前采取行动。你不可能一次对付整座营地，不过一定有办法让他们收拾东西离开。
rows.raw: "Damning claims, but if Garth's right, then something has to be done about them before they turn their sights on town. There's no way you can take on the whole camp at once, but there's got to be some way to get them to pack up and leave."

rows.original: "Just keep a cool head before you sally out eastward," Garth adds, watching you warily. "The foothills are even more dangerous than the Old Forest has been lately. I'd stick to the woods until you've gotten your bearings here in the Marches. Learn to use that [pc.weapon] of yours before you go crossing blades with a war camp full of ornery islanders."
rows.translation: “在你向东出发之前，先保持冷静，”加斯补充道，警惕地看着你。“丘陵地带比近来的古林还要危险。在熟悉边境地区之前，我会先待在树林里。先学会怎么用你的[pc.weapon]，再去和一整座营地里脾气暴躁的岛民交锋。”

I'd stick to the woods until you've gotten your bearings here in the Marches. Learn to use that [pc.weapon] of yours before you go crossing blades with a war camp full of ornery islanders." '

rows.original:
"Hey!" your orc companion bellows from her table. "I can damn well hear you, grayfur!"
    
    Garth snarls at her, not deigning to respond.
rows.translation:
“嘿！”你的兽人同伴从她的桌边吼道，“我听得一清二楚，灰毛！”
    
    加斯冲她龇牙低吼，根本不屑回应。
rows.raw:
'
    "Hey!" your orc companion bellows from her table. "I can damn well hear you, grayfur!"
    
    Garth snarls at her, not deigning to respond.

    
    '

rows.original: Or, maybe, claim Hawkethorne as protected territory. Plenty of barbarian tribes will accept tribute or allegiance from settled people, if the terms are right.
rows.translation: 或者，也可以宣布鹰棘镇是受保护的领地。只要条件合适，许多野蛮人部族都会接受定居者的贡赋或效忠。
rows.raw: " Or, maybe, claim Hawkethorne as protected territory. Plenty of barbarian tribes will accept tribute or allegiance from settled people, if the terms are right."

rows.translation: 兽人部落？

rows.original:
"So the valley south of town seems nice," you prompt.

    "Should hope so," Garth chuckles, setting his mug and rag aside and setting his hands on the bar, looking you over a moment. "It's where most of the barony lives. And where we get all our food and booze. Something happens down there, and things are going to get real bad for Hawkethorne."
    
    You blink. "Expecting something?"
    
    "Know something," he sighs. "There's two tribes of beastkin live down there: the marefolk and the centaurs. Both horse-like, but very different... and they've both been peaceable for as long as I've been around. Until now. Suddenly have centaur marauders attacking farmsteads, marefolk grabbing people off the roads. Used to be the mares'd have this ritual of 'kidnapping' men once in a while, but that was all fun and games for the young men. Heh, even I let myself get taken once... it was a treat. Now though, there's violence in the air. Folk are getting scared."
    
    [pc.isDK|"So what do you want from me?"|"What can I do?"]
    
    Garth shrugs. "Don't know. It's in the opposite direction of your demon's trail, but there's a particular farm on the road down there that supplies a big chunk of the Frost Hound's food... if you could go down there and make sure everything's okay, I'd certainly appreciate it. Hell, you put the mares and centaurs in their place again, maybe the baroness would take notice..."
    
    Now that's something to think about...
rows.translation:
所以镇子南边的那个山谷看起来挺不错的，”你说道。

    “希望真是这样吧，”加斯轻笑着，把杯子和小抹布放在一边，双手撑在吧台上，打量了你一会儿。“那里住着这个领地的大多数人。这就是我们获取所有食物和酒的地方。但是那里发生了某些事情，对鹰棘镇来说，情况将会变得非常糟糕。”
    
    你眨了眨眼：“在期待什么发生吗？”
    
    “其实……”他叹了口气，“那里生活着两个兽人部落：马人族和半人马族。它们都长得像马，但却截然不同……在我存在的这段时间里，它们一直都是和平相处的。直到现在。突然间，半人马掠夺者开始袭击农庄，而马女们则开始在道路上抓走人们。以前，马女们偶尔会“绑架”一些男人，但对那些年轻男子来说，这只是些有趣的游戏罢了。呵呵，就连我也有那么一次被骗了……不过那也挺有趣的。不过现在，空气中弥漫着暴力的气息，人们都开始感到害怕了。
    
    [pc.isDK|那你到底想从我这里得到什么？|我该怎么办呢？]
    
    加斯耸了耸肩：“不知道。那个地方在你的恶魔踪迹的相反方向，但在那条路上有座农场，它为‘霜犬酒馆’提供了大部分食物……如果你能去那里确认一下一切正常，我会非常感激的。说不定，如果你把那些母马和半人马送回该去的地方，女男爵会注意到的……”
    
    这倒是个值得考虑的问题……

rows.translation: 丰收谷？

rows.original: You lean into the bar and tell Garth that you managed to find Pupperidge Farms and keep it safe from the cult — but you've noticed quite a bit of damage to surrounding farmsteads. "Oh? Good to hear the girls are safe. I knew their father... promised him I'd check in on his kiddos from time to time, but this damn leg..." Garth grunts, rapping his knuckles on his bad knee. "Sounds like the centaurs and marefolk are having at it, though. Had some farmers come into town seeking refuge; others just leaving the valley altogether. Can't afford to let that chaos keep going on. We rely on the valley for almost all our food." Yeah, losing the town's main food supply would be... bad. "What can I do?" Garth sighs. "From what I hear, the centaurs are the aggressors. Marefolk are all up in arms over it. Maybe check in with their leader, or else go beat some sense into the centaur chieftain. Tall Dan or something, I think he was called. They've got a camp in the far west side of the valley, but the bridge has been taken up. You'll have to ford the river and it's probably a lot more dangerous down there than in the parts of the valley closer to town. Marefolk village and centaur camp have a straight shot at each other, so the fighting's likely been vicious. Keep your guard up." Right. Always do.
rows.translation: 你靠在吧台上，告诉加斯，你终于找到了帕珀里奇农场，并且成功保护它免受那个邪教的侵害——不过你也注意到，周围的农场都受到了相当严重的破坏。 “哦？听说姑娘们都安全无恙，真是太好了。我知道他们的父亲……答应过我会偶尔去看看他的孩子们，但这条该死的腿……”加思哼了一声，用指关节敲了敲自己受伤的膝盖。“不过，听起来半人马和马人族之间正在发生冲突。有些农民来到镇上寻求庇护；而另一些人则干脆离开了这个山谷。我们无法承受这种混乱继续下去。我们几乎所有的食物都依赖这个山谷。” “没错，如果失去了这个城镇的主要食物来源，那后果会很严重……我该怎么办呢？” 加思叹了口气：“据我所知，先动手的是半人马。马人族对此都义愤填膺。或许你可以去和他们的首领谈谈，或者去把那个半人马首领揍醒。我记得他叫高个丹之类的名字。他们在山谷最西边扎了营，不过那座桥已经被拆掉了。你只能涉水过河，而且那边很可能比山谷里靠近城镇的地方危险得多。马人族村庄和半人马营地正对着彼此，所以打起来多半很惨烈。保持警惕。” 没错。永远都要保持警惕。

rows.translation: 丰收谷

rows.original: "The forest beyond the river seems... different," you tell the old wolf. "And unnaturally cold." He nods, staring into the bottom of a mug for a moment before responding. "Yeah. Been a long time since anybody from Hawkethorne's been that far north, but the stories say that there used to be a kingdom of snow elves up there. I know there's an old fortress on the road, seen that with my own eyes, but never had a reason to cross the bridge. Like you said, when you get to the river, it starts getting cold." So nothing he can tell you about the region? "Not much. Sorry, kid. A few villagers have gone just past the river in search of that old witch, call her Lady Evergreen — I think Cait was looking forward to seeing her, too. Her hut, or whatever she lives in, shouldn't be more than an hour's walk from the old wayfort. Doesn't mean getting there will be easy, though." You raise an eyebrow. "If things were as bad in the forest as you say they were, and your demon fled further north... she'll have had more time to prepare for you. And I doubt the elves will be happy to see you wandering through their lands either." [party.has etheryn|Well, hopefully Etheryn's presence will ameliorate the issue...]
rows.translation: “河对岸的森林似乎……不太一样。”你告诉老狼。“而且冷得不自然。” 他点点头，盯着杯底看了片刻才回答。“是啊。已经很久没有鹰棘镇的人去到那么北边了，不过传说那里曾经有一个雪精灵王国。我知道路上有一座古老堡垒，亲眼见过，却从来没有理由过桥。就像你说的，走到河边，天气就开始变得寒冷。” 所以，他没什么关于那个地区的情报能告诉你？ “不多。抱歉，孩子。有几个村民曾渡过河，去找那个被称为常青女士的老巫婆——我想凯特也很期待见到她。她的小屋，或者她住的随便什么地方，离旧驿堡应该不到一小时路程。不过，这并不代表前往那里会很轻松。” 你挑起眉毛。 “如果森林里的情况真像你说的那么糟，而那个恶魔又逃向了更北方……那她就有了更多时间为你作准备。我也不觉得那些精灵会乐意见到你在他们的领地上到处游荡。” [party.has etheryn|嗯，希望伊瑟琳在场能缓和这个问题……]
rows.raw: ' "The forest beyond the river seems... different," you tell the old wolf. "And unnaturally cold." He nods, staring into the bottom of a mug for a moment before responding. "Yeah. Been a long time since anybody from Hawkethorne's been that far north, but the stories say that there used to be a kingdom of snow elves up there. I know there's an old fortress on the road, seen that with my own eyes, but never had a reason to cross the bridge. Like you said, when you get to the river, it starts getting cold." So nothing he can tell you about the region? "Not much. Sorry, kid. A few villagers have gone just past the river in search of that old witch, call her Lady Evergreen — I think Cait was looking forward to seeing her, too. Her hut, or whatever she lives in, shouldn't be more than an hour's walk from the old wayfort. Doesn't mean getting there will be easy, though." You raise an eyebrow. "If things were as bad in the forest as you say they were, and your demon fled further north... she'll have had more time to prepare for you. And I doubt the elves will be happy to see you wandering through their lands either." [party.has etheryn|Well, hopefully Etheryn's presence will ameliorate the issue...]'

rows.original:
Leaning up against the counter, you tell the old bar-wolf that if you're going to be making the Frost Hound a base of operation, you're going to need a way to store more gear than just what you can shove under your bed.

    "Understandable," Garth says, topping off a mug and sliding it down to [party.has brint|Brint|a waiting customer]. "You're gonna want to find chests. Great for organizing your kit, keeping it secure. I've got one I can part with, but that's it. Only good carpenter in town is Leorah, and she's got better things to do than make chests now that we've got so many threats looming. Probably putting most of her time into bow-making."
    
    So what are you supposed to do?
    
    "Find more?" Garth laughs. "There's plenty of ruins around that probably still have a chest or two lying around, or something usable as one. Just go exploring. In the meantime, like I said, I've got one I can give you at friends' rates, say fifty hawks?"

    那么，你该怎么做呢？

rows.translation: 观察者

rows.original:
If he has a moment, please?
    
    Garth sets down the mug he's polishing on the counter with a clink and thud, his ears folding back. "I'm not sure I like the look on your face, [pc.name]. This isn't going to be good, even if it's not your fault."
    
    Can you speak in private?
    
    "I figured as much. Gwyneth, watch the bar for me while I figure out what's up with [pc.name]!"
    
    As Gwyn shuffles out of the nursery to take her father's place at the tap, Garth waves you [party.hasCompanions
        |away from [party.compNames] and 
    ]over into the little yard behind the Frost Hound. Slamming the door shut behind the both of you, he folds his arms and eyes you up and down.
    
    "There, now you can tell me the bad news, whatever it is."
    
    It's not really bad news. You've found his wife. Gweyr's living up in the Glacial Rift, hunting Tollus and his cult; she's been on their tail for years now.
    
    "I know."
    
    He knew?
    
    "I know she isn't dead. Old man Sanders knows she isn't dead. River knows she isn't dead. That makes the three of us. I... every season or so, I sneak out of town to meet her just outside of the gates, sneak out when Gwyn and Garret are in bed and aren't watching. There's... there's a signal."
    
    You shake your head. And he, no all three of them, just... kept it from everyone? Gwyn and Garret?
    
    "When it comes to Gwyn, she doesn't care. And when it comes to Garret... if I told my idiot son that his mother was still alive, he'd drop everything to go and find her up in the glacier. Do you seriously think he'd last a moment up there?"
    
    ...No.
    
    "If you spoke with my wife, [pc.name], then you know that she's not going to come back, not until she can clear her name and live with herself, even if almost everyone who condemned her that day is now gone. She trusted me to raise the pups — "
    
    And that was worth depriving them of their mother? Things might've turned out differently if she were around — 
    
    "That's not you, that's the anger talking there, [pc.name]. You think it's bad, us keeping it from the kids? How the fuck do you think I feel, having to slink out in the dark to meet my wife? Do you think I haven't begged her to come home and live with us, live here in Hawkethorne while hunting those freaks from here? I..." Garth balls his fists. "Shit, don't you get it, [pc.name]? Sometimes there are no good choices and you have to take the one that's open to you because it's the only way forward. What would you have done in my place? Wrestled my wife to the ground and forced her to stay with us?"
    
    He could've at least told you and Cait about what happened sixteen years ago, when Tollus first arrived and tried to annex the fledgeling village. Might've saved you some trouble. Might've saved the lives of some people down in Harvest Valley or elsewhere. But even though everyone else in that ugly matter's moved on since then, the three of them still kept their mouths shut.
    
    Garth's gaze turns from angry to pleading. "We agreed that it was for the best, [pc.name]. Do you think we've done nothing in the intervening years?"
    
    And does the baroness know?
    
    "She does."
    
    So that makes four of them, not three.
    
    "And what are you going to do now?"
    
    You're going to go back up, you're going to help Gweyr finish cleaning up this ugly mess, and you're going to bring her back down to her family and see if she can't untangle this knot as well. And while you can understand why Garth, Sanders and River kept all of this from you, why so much as speaking of her is taboo in the whole village, you don't have to like it in the least and frankly, you find it all disgusting. And when she finally comes home... the both of them owe their two children an apology, and an explanation.
    
    Garth looks askance at you, as if wanting to challenge you for moralising at him... but he knows you're right, too. Wordlessly, he turns and stomps back into the bar, displacing Gwyn and setting back to the mugs with renewed fervor.
    
    "Did you do something to Daddy?"
    
    You look at Gwyn and sigh. The two of you just discussed some ugly truths, that's all. No one was coming out of that exchange happy, but... it's for the best that you said those words.
rows.translation:
如果他有空的话，麻烦了？

加思把正在擦拭的杯子重重地放在柜台上，耳朵都快贴到后脑勺上了。“我不太喜欢你现在的表情[pc.name]这样下去肯定不会有什么好结果的，即使这不是你的错。”

你能私下谈谈吗？

“我早料到了。格温妮丝，你帮我照看一下吧，我得弄清楚到底发生了什么。[pc.name]当格温从婴儿房走出来，取代她父亲的位置去接水时，加思向你招手。 [party.hasCompanions
        |远离[party.compNames]以及 
    ]走进寒霜猎犬后面的小院子，他把门关上后，双臂交叉抱在胸前，上下打量着你。

“好了，现在你可以告诉我那个坏消息了，不管是什么。”

其实这并不是什么坏消息。你找到他的妻子了。格维尔现在正在冰川裂谷一带活动，一直在追捕托勒斯和他的邪教组织；这些年来，她一直都在追踪他们的行踪。

“我知道。”

他知道？

“我知道她并没有死。桑德斯老头也知道她并没有死。瑞弗知道她并没有死。这样，我们就变成了三个人。我……每隔一个季节左右，我就会偷偷离开小镇，在城门外面与她会面。总是在格温和加雷特入睡、不会注意我的时候偷偷出门。因为……存在着某种信号。你摇了摇头。那么，是他，还是他们三个人，都选择对所有人隐瞒这件事？格温和加雷特也知道吗？

“至于格温，她根本不在乎。而加雷特……如果我告诉我那个愚蠢的儿子，他的母亲还活着，他会立刻放下手头的一切，去冰川里寻找她。你真觉得他在那里能坚持一会儿吗？”

……不。

“如果你能和我妻子谈谈的话[pc.name]，那么你就知道，她不会再回来了，直到她洗清自己的罪名，能够堂堂正正地生活下去为止。尽管那天那些指责她的人，现在都已经不在了。她信任我把那些小狗抚养长大——

那么，为了这个理由，就剥夺它们母亲的爱，真的值得吗？如果她还在身边，事情可能会发展成另一种样子吧——

“那不是你，那是愤怒在说话罢了。[pc.name]你认为我们瞒着孩子们这件事很糟糕吗？你知道我当时是怀着怎样的心情，在暗影中偷偷溜出去见我妻子吗？我求她回家和我们一起生活，陪我一起在鹰棘镇生活，一起猎杀那些怪物……我……”加思握紧了拳头，“该死，你到底懂不懂我的感受？[pc.name]有时候，根本没有好的选择，你只能接受眼前那个选项，因为那是唯一的出路。如果你处在我的位置，你会怎么做？会强行把我的妻子按在地上，逼她留在我们身边吗？他至少应该告诉你和凯特关于十六年前发生的事情——当时托勒斯首次到来，试图吞并那个刚刚建立起来的村庄。这样做或许可以避免你们遇到一些麻烦，或许还能挽救哈维斯特山谷或其他地方的一些人的生命。但尽管自那以后，与那件丑事有关的其他人都已经选择了遗忘，这三个人却依然选择保持沉默。

加斯的目光从愤怒转为恳求：“我们当初是同意这样做的，因为我们认为这是最好的选择[pc.name]你难道认为在这些年里我们什么都没做吗？”

那么那位女男爵知道这件事吗？

“她知道。”

所以现在一共有四个人知道了，而不是三个人。

“那你现在打算怎么做呢？”

你得回去，帮助格维尔把这一团糟的局面收拾好，然后把她送回她的家人身边，看看她是否也能帮助解开这个复杂的难题。虽然你可以理解为什么加思、桑德斯和瑞弗会对你隐瞒这一切，为什么在整个村庄里，哪怕只是提到她的名字也被视为禁忌，但你完全不必喜欢这种做法，坦白说，你觉得这一切都非常令人作呕。当她终于回到家时……他们两个人都欠自己的孩子一个道歉，以及一个解释。

加思用怀疑的目光看着你，似乎想指责你对他进行道德说教……但他也知道你是对的。他一言不发地转身，重重地走回酒吧，把格温挤到一边，然后又满怀热情地开始摆弄那些杯子。

“你是不是对爸爸做了什么？”

你看着格温，叹了口气。你们俩刚刚只是讨论了一些令人不快的真相，而已。没有人会从那次谈话中感到满意，但是……你说出那些话，反而是件好事。

rows.translation: 下一步
观察者

rows.original: [rand |Garth coughs not so discreetly and turns to look at you out of the corner of his eye. "For what it's worth and everything that's happened, for all that you've done not just for the town but personally for my family as well... thank you. I'm sorry for not telling you and Cait what I knew of 'Master' Tollus just after she brought you back home in the blizzard." While everything worked out in the end, he's got a lot of thinking and repenting to do in his time. Garth sighs, sets down the mug he's polishing, and holds his head in his hands. "Look, I'm not trying to make excuses for myself, but we'd thought the matter was largely done and dusted, that our shame had been buried, that we'd long since gone on with our lives. And while people did disappear from time to time, that was nothing strange in this wild and dangerous part of the world — less so than the heartlands, perhaps, but treacherous in their own right. Sure, part of it was me not wanting to believe that Tollus was still lurking in the Marches, that my wife hadn't chased him off to seek greener pastures... but when Cait came into my bar that night asking for help, the last thing I was expecting was for Tollus to have returned after all this time." "Look, once more, I'm sorry for withholding the truth from the two of you. To my shame, my first thought in all of this was to cover it up, to stop the miserable, dark past of this village from coming to light, and if you hadn't gone up there with Cait I'd have done it myself to keep the matter under wraps; not that I'd likely have made it out alive given my bad knee, but..." While you're thankful for the free accommodations you've been having in the Hound all this while, he owes you big time. This is the sort of debt that can't be repaid with money — not just to you, but far more importantly, to his kids. They're the ones who've been truly harmed by all this cowardice. Garth hangs his head. "Yes. You're right. But... thanks for all you've done for my family so far, despite how I treated you at the outset, and thanks for bringing my wife home." |So, how's Gweyr taking to settling back in the Hound? You'd imagine that his wife would've a lot to say about how he's done up the place in her years of absence. Garth answers the jibe with a noncommittal half-shrug. "Oh, she agrees with some of the things I've done with the place, and disagrees with others. Thankfully, there're enough of the former that she's willing to forgive me for the latter, like how we we've always been since we were an item." Ah, nothing like a happily married couple that's stuck together for years upon years. "She says maybe it was for the best that she left for a bit — without her around to do the heavy lifting in my stead, I'd to bulk up a bit and stop being such a scrawny guy. I'm pretty sure she was joking, but..." Well, given her description of him when he was younger, Garth has indeed put on a whole bunch of bulk since then. But it's good to at least see that Gweyr is getting back some of her old dry humor — she was downright morose after everyone returned from confronting Tollus beneath the waves. She's spoken to no one about what the lureling no doubt showed her in an attempt to strike at her psyche, but you were able to see how it affected her despite her efforts to keep a stiff upper lip. you take it she's been keeping herself busy ever since her return? Garth nods and sighs. "I've got enough hands these days to cook, serve and clean, so she spends a good chunk of her time at Gwyn's, trying to work away at our daughter. When she's not there, she's taken an interest in managing the town militia with Sanders and me. I suppose if anyone's capable of whipping a bunch of ex-farmhands fresh up from Harvest Valley into something that's worth half a damn, it'll be her. "Me, I'm just glad my wife's home. She's a woman who looks and feels like she knows what she's doing, and that's pretty damned invaluable in times like this. People want to believe in someone like that, and another one can't hurt. Old man Sanders and I may be good, but we can only be stretched so thinly. Yeah, she's having no problems settling in nicely, all right — really does feel like someone paved the way for her to do just that." |"The way Gweyr just manages to have our boy eating out of her hand... it makes me wonder what might have happened if she hadn't left to walk the ice, if Garret would've been less of a wastrel these past years just sitting around, drinking and snapping at me every chance he got. I feed the pup, I raise the pup, I teach him everything I know, and his answer to that is to be closer with his mother whom he's only just had the chance to know." "Look, I'm not jealous or anything, the boy has a style that he inherited from his mother, so it makes sense. But at the same time... I find it a little sad." Yeah, you find it a little sad too as to why Garth simply can't understand why his son might be just a little bit resentful that he was lied to about his mother for most of his childhood. At least he had some idea that Gweyr might've been alive out there somewhere, as opposed to his sister who went so far as to believe their mother ran out on them and was dead. That Garret gives him the time of day after the truth's been revealed just goes to show how far he's come — not necessarily because of his mother, but on his own — to realize that while he may certainly disagree with what his father did to him, he at least understands why Garth did it. That's more than that Garret you met at first locked up in an animal cage or the Garret drinking his brains out on at his father's taps would've done. Even if everything's right and his mother is but a blank slate for Garret, that's better than the alternative. Garth instinctively looks like he's going to argue, then slumps his shoulders and shakes his head. "I guess I deserve it, huh?" Deserve's got nothing to do with it. He did raise his son to the best of his ability... but if Garret is anything like his mother, then the sting of that kind of betrayal hurts a lot. Maybe the best thing Garth can do is to give it time, let his son find himself a little while longer now that he's got a new influence in his life. If nothing else, Garth still has Gwyn around, and she really does love her daddy unconditionally. A sigh. "My only remaining worries in this world are that I'll never live to see the day my son ceases to be an idiot and my daughter gets married off." |How's his relationship with his wife working out now that they're finally back together after all these years? You can understand if he doesn't want to answer, given that it's a pretty personal question, but you're really just hoping that everything's going to work out fine for everyone involved and that the ending of this little tale that's stretched decades is at least content, even if it can't be outright happy. "It's... fine. I'm glad to have my wife back, it's nice to have someone sleeping beside you again after all this time, and we've had a lot of catching up to do. It's kind of like when we were first in love all over again, only now our joints ache more and we're not as vigorous as we used to be." Garth clears his throat uncertainly. "It's taken all this while, but I think we're heading back once more towards the life that the both of us envisioned for ourselves when we made the decision to leave the Crossed Swords and head back up north to the land of our birth. We could have hung on for a while — a mercenary company is no place to raise a pup, but it can be done as my father-in-law proved — but here and now, I have this feeling that I'm making the same kind of weighty decision as my wife and I did back then, to get when the going's good." If it makes him happier, and gives him closure to this whole story. "Closure, yeah, that's what it is. Closure. I guess that's what it is when there isn't that little weight at the back of my mind wondering when it is that I'll ever have to tell the kids about their mother, or what to do if anyone ever found out... to be honest, best it was you rather than one of the town gossips. And now that everyone knows at least some part of the story thanks to Tollus poking his head around down in the valley... I'm actually surprised that the consequences wasn't as terrible as I'd imagined them to be. People like my wife, and I haven't been hounded out of town either, so..." Like what you experienced so far down beneath the water, maybe the worst nightmares are those one creates for oneself. There's an argument to be made that he's punished himself enough for his misdeeds, but only the gods can judge him on that now. |"My wife's wasted no time in making herself useful. Fat much of a retirement this is for her, ha." Well, she did say that it was going to be her last adventure, not her death. A woman like her isn't going to twiddle her thumbs, idle around, and wait to die peaceably in her sleep. Garth snorts. "Well, she's certainly living up to the position of unofficial alderman's wife, if nothing else. Gweyr hasn't been back in Hawkethorne that long and she's already installed herself in our daughter's nursery, slid into an unofficial position with the local militia, and even gone around to bother Ogrish. The woman's always been good at dealing with people and leaving me to balance the books, so I'm not really surprised. People like her." There's something to be said for that — Gweyr is very forthright and direct. People whom she hasn't strangled within minutes of meeting her are pretty much safe in the knowledge that she doesn't mind having them around, and that kind of honesty is refreshing in this day and age. "It's starting to feel a bit like we're back in the Crossed Swords again... with her barking orders and people following her just because she seems to know what she's doing and has every right to be giving them. Wouldn't work with someone like Sanders or you, but most folks are rattled enough of late to want to have someone to follow, and somehow the word's spread like wildfire that she's my wife, having come home from some kind of amazing adventure to retire in her glory days. "It's not too different from the life we might've had if we'd stayed on as mercenaries instead of opting for moving on, I guess. Staying on, fighting until our bodies gave out... and if we didn't get ourselves killed, hang on around the edges and offer our advice and experience to the young folks. Yeah... if we'd stayed on with the Crossed Swords, this is about what we'd have been doing, and we'd be looking to retire about now. Guess the more things change, the more they stay the same, don't they?" ]
rows.translation: [rand |加思咳嗽了一声，动作并不隐蔽，然后用眼角余光看向你。“不管这有什么意义，也不管发生了什么，更不管你为这个小镇做了多少事，更不用说你也为我的家人付出了很多……谢谢你。很抱歉，在凯特把你从暴风雪中带回家后，我没有立刻把我知道的关于‘托勒斯大师’的事情告诉你们。 虽然最终一切都得到了解决，但在那段时间里，他确实有很多事情需要思考和反思。 加思叹了口气，放下了正在擦拭的杯子，双手抱头说道：“听着，我并不是想为自己找借口，但我们原本以为这件事已经彻底解决了，我们的耻辱也被埋葬在了过去，我们早就应该继续过自己的生活了。虽然偶尔会有人失踪，但在这个荒凉而危险的地区，这并不算什么奇怪的事——或许比起内陆地区来说，这种情况还要少见一些，但这里本身就充满了危险。当然，部分原因也是因为我不愿意相信托勒斯仍然潜伏在边境地区，也不愿意相信我的妻子没有离开他去寻找更好的生活。…但那天晚上当凯特来到我的酒吧寻求帮助时，我完全没料到托勒斯在经历了这么久之后竟然会回来。 听着，我再次为没有向你们俩坦白真相而感到抱歉。令我羞愧的是，在这件事上，我的第一个念头就是掩盖事实，不让这个村庄那段悲惨而黑暗的过去被公之于众。如果你们没有和凯特一起上山，我也会亲自去这么做，把这件事保密下去；不过，以我那受伤的膝盖，恐怕我也活不下来吧…… 虽然你很感激这些天来Hound为你提供的免费住宿，但他确实欠你一个人情债。这种债是无法用金钱来偿还的——不仅仅是对你而言，更重要的是，对他的孩子们来说更是如此。正是这些孩子的利益受到了他这种怯懦行为的真正伤害。 加思低下了头。“是的，你说得对。但是……感谢你一直以来为我的家人所做的一切，尽管我一开始对你的态度并不好，也感谢你把我的妻子带回了家。 |那么，格维尔在“猎犬号”上重新安顿下来后，感觉怎么样呢？你可能会觉得，在他离开的这些年里，他的妻子肯定有很多话要说，关于他是怎么布置这个地方的。 加思对这种调侃只是淡淡地耸了耸肩，没有给出明确的回答。“哦，有些我做的改动她表示认同，有些则不赞成。不过幸好，认同我的做法比较多，所以她也就愿意原谅我那些不让她满意的地方了。毕竟，我们从一开始就是这样的关系嘛。 啊，没有什么比一对幸福地结婚多年、一直在一起生活的夫妻更让人羡慕的了。 “她说，也许她暂时离开一段时间其实是件好事——如果没有她来替我承担那些繁重的工作，我就得努力锻炼身体，不再这么瘦弱了。我挺确定她是在开玩笑的，但是…… 嗯，根据她对加思年轻时的描述，他确实从那以后变壮了很多。不过至少可以看到，格薇尔又恢复了一些她那老式的冷幽默了——在大家从海底与托勒斯的战斗中回来后，她之前可是显得非常沮丧的。她没有跟任何人谈论过那个诱饵究竟向她展示了什么，那个诱饵无疑是试图打击她的心理。不过，尽管她努力保持镇定，你还是能看出那件事对她产生了多大的影响。那么，你认为她从回来之后就一直在忙于各种事情来转移注意力吗？ 加思点了点头，叹了口气说道：“这些天我有足够的人手来做饭、端菜和打扫卫生，所以她大部分时间都在格温家，努力教导我们的女儿。当她不在那里的时候，就会和我还有桑德斯一起负责管理镇上的民兵组织。我想，如果有人能够把一群刚从丰收谷来的前农场工人训练成有一定战斗力的队伍，那肯定就是她了。 对我来说，能让我妻子待在家里就足够了。她是个看起来很可靠、也确实知道自己在做什么的女性，在这种时候，这样的存在简直是无价之宝。人们总是愿意相信这样的人，而这样的人也不会带来任何伤害。老桑德斯和我或许还算不错，但我们的能力也有限啊。没错，她适应新环境的过程确实很顺利——真的感觉有人为她铺平了道路，让她能够顺利地融入新环境。 |格维尔居然能让我们的孩子完全听她的话……这让我不禁思考，如果她没有去冰原上行走，如果加雷特这些年来没有整天无所事事、酗酒闹事，还一有机会就对我发脾气，那么会发生什么呢？是我喂养了这个孩子，是我把他抚养长大，是我把我所知道的一切都教给了他，然而他的回报却是选择与刚刚才认识的母亲走得更近。 听着，我并不是嫉妒什么，那个男孩有他从母亲那里继承来的那种风格，所以这也情有可原。但同时……我总觉得这有点让人难过。” 是啊，你也会觉得有点难过，因为加斯就是不明白，为什么他的儿子会对自己在童年时期大部分时间都被隐瞒关于母亲的真相而感到一丝怨恨。至少他明白，格维尔可能还活着，而他的姐姐则认为他们的母亲抛弃了他们，已经去世了。在真相大白之后，加雷特仍然愿意与他交谈，这恰恰说明了他已经取得了多大的进步——这并非因为他的母亲，而是他自己的努力。他虽然可能不同意父亲对自己的所作所为，但至少他理解了加思为什么会那样做。这可比你最初遇到的那个被关在动物笼子里的加雷特，或者那个整天喝着父亲提供的酒喝得烂醉如泥的加雷特要好多了。即使一切都顺利，他的母亲对加雷特来说也只是一张白纸，但这样的结果总比其他情况要好。 加思本能地想要争辩几句，但最终只是耸了耸肩，摇了摇头说道：“我想，这是我应得的吧？” 但实际上，这根本与他应不应得无关。他确实已经尽自己最大的努力来抚养儿子了。但是，如果加雷特真的和他母亲一样，那么这种背叛带来的伤害将会非常深刻。或许加思能做的最好的事情就是给时间一些时间，让他的儿子在生命中有了新的影响之后，有更多的时间去找到属于自己的道路。至少，加思还有格温在身边，而她确实是无条件地爱着她的父亲。 一声叹息。“在这个世界上，我唯一剩下的担忧就是，我可能永远无法看到我的儿子不再犯傻，也看不到我的女儿结婚的那一天。 |经过这么多年的分离，他们终于重新在一起了，那么他和他妻子的关系现在怎么样呢？考虑到这是一个相当私人的问题，如果他不愿意回答，也是可以理解的。但你真心希望所有相关的人都能过得幸福美满，希望这个持续了数十年的故事能够有一个令人满意的结局，哪怕不能做到完全幸福也好。 没关系……我很高兴我的妻子能回到我身边，经过这么长时间，终于又有一个人在身边陪伴我睡觉了，我们也有很多事情需要补上。这有点像我们重新坠入爱河的时候，只不过现在我们的关节变得更加疼痛了，也不像以前那么精力充沛了。加思不确定地清了清嗓子，说道：“虽然花费了这么长的时间，但我认为我们终于又要重新走向当初决定离开十字剑组织，回到北方故乡时，我们两人共同憧憬的那种生活了。我们本可以再坚持一段时间——毕竟，雇佣兵公司并不是养育孩子的理想环境，但正如我岳父所证明的那样，这也是可行的。然而此刻，我有一种感觉，自己正在做出与我和妻子当年一样的重要决定：在形势有利的时候果断行动。" 如果这能让他更开心，能让这个故事有一个圆满的结局的话…… “圆满的结局，没错，就是这个意思。圆满的结局。我想，当我的心里不再一直惦记着什么时候该告诉孩子们他们的母亲去哪里了，或者如果有人发现了该怎么办的时候，我想这就叫做圆满的结局吧。说实话，你来做这件事反而比镇上的那些爱传闲话的人要好得多。现在由于托勒斯在山谷里打探消息，大家都至少了解到了事情的部分真相……其实让我感到惊讶的是，后果并没有我想象中那么糟糕。人们喜欢我的妻子，我也没有被赶出镇子，所以…… 就像你在水下所经历的那些事情一样，也许最可怕的噩梦其实是那些自己臆造出来的。有人认为，他已经为自己的过错受到了足够的惩罚，但现在只有神明才能对他的行为做出评判。 |我妻子可没浪费时间，立刻就开始帮忙干活了。对她来说，这算什么退休生活啊，哈哈。” 不过，她确实说过这会是她最后一次做这些事了。冒险不是她的死亡，而是别的什么。像她这样的女人，绝不会无所事事、闲逛度日，然后安详地死在睡梦中。 加思哼了一声：“嗯，至少她确实配得上‘非正式副市长夫人’这个头衔。格维尔回到鹰棘镇才不久，就已经在我们女儿的 nursery安顿下来，还在当地民兵组织中获得了一个非正式的地位，甚至还去打扰了奥格瑞什。这个女人向来擅长与人打交道，因此让我来负责处理各种账务工作，我对此也并不感到意外。像她这样的人很受欢迎。 这话确实有道理——格维尔做人非常直率坦诚。那些在和她见面后几分钟内没有遭到她“威胁”或“压制”的人，基本上可以放心地待在她身边，因为她们显然不介意别人靠近自己。在这种时代，这种坦诚的态度确实令人感到耳目一新。 现在感觉有点像我们又回到了‘交叉之剑’的时代……她总是发号施令，其他人也因为觉得她确实知道自己在做什么，而且完全有资格发号施令，所以才会听从她的安排。这种作风在桑德斯或者你这样的人身上是行不通的，但最近大多数人都处于一种迷茫、不安的状态，所以他们很希望有个人能够带领他们。不知怎么的，消息就像野火一样迅速传开了——大家都认为她是我的妻子，她经历了一场惊心动魄的冒险后回到了家中，现在正是她辉煌人生的最后阶段。 我想，这和如果我们没有选择离开，而是继续当雇佣兵的话，所过的生活并没有太大区别。继续战斗，直到身体再也支撑不住……如果没能战死的话，就留在这个行业里，为年轻人提供自己的建议和经验。没错……如果我们当初还留在‘十字剑团’，现在大概也会是这样的生活，而且也应该快要退休了吧。也许，事情变化得越多，有些东西反而会保持不变，不是吗？ ]
rows.raw: " [rand |Garth coughs not so discreetly and turns to look at you out of the corner of his eye. "For what it's worth and everything that's happened, for all that you've done not just for the town but personally for my family as well... thank you. I'm sorry for not telling you and Cait what I knew of 'Master' Tollus just after she brought you back home in the blizzard." While everything worked out in the end, he's got a lot of thinking and repenting to do in his time. Garth sighs, sets down the mug he's polishing, and holds his head in his hands. "Look, I'm not trying to make excuses for myself, but we'd thought the matter was largely done and dusted, that our shame had been buried, that we'd long since gone on with our lives. And while people did disappear from time to time, that was nothing strange in this wild and dangerous part of the world — less so than the heartlands, perhaps, but treacherous in their own right. Sure, part of it was me not wanting to believe that Tollus was still lurking in the Marches, that my wife hadn't chased him off to seek greener pastures... but when Cait came into my bar that night asking for help, the last thing I was expecting was for Tollus to have returned after all this time." "Look, once more, I'm sorry for withholding the truth from the two of you. To my shame, my first thought in all of this was to cover it up, to stop the miserable, dark past of this village from coming to light, and if you hadn't gone up there with Cait I'd have done it myself to keep the matter under wraps; not that I'd likely have made it out alive given my bad knee, but..." While you're thankful for the free accommodations you've been having in the Hound all this while, he owes you big time. This is the sort of debt that can't be repaid with money — not just to you, but far more importantly, to his kids. They're the ones who've been truly harmed by all this cowardice. Garth hangs his head. "Yes. You're right. But... thanks for all you've done for my family so far, despite how I treated you at the outset, and thanks for bringing my wife home." |So, how's Gweyr taking to settling back in the Hound? You'd imagine that his wife would've a lot to say about how he's done up the place in her years of absence. Garth answers the jibe with a noncommittal half-shrug. "Oh, she agrees with some of the things I've done with the place, and disagrees with others. Thankfully, there're enough of the former that she's willing to forgive me for the latter, like how we we've always been since we were an item." Ah, nothing like a happily married couple that's stuck together for years upon years. "She says maybe it was for the best that she left for a bit — without her around to do the heavy lifting in my stead, I'd to bulk up a bit and stop being such a scrawny guy. I'm pretty sure she was joking, but..." Well, given her description of him when he was younger, Garth has indeed put on a whole bunch of bulk since then. But it's good to at least see that Gweyr is getting back some of her old dry humor — she was downright morose after everyone returned from confronting Tollus beneath the waves. She's spoken to no one about what the lureling no doubt showed her in an attempt to strike at her psyche, but you were able to see how it affected her despite her efforts to keep a stiff upper lip. you take it she's been keeping herself busy ever since her return? Garth nods and sighs. "I've got enough hands these days to cook, serve and clean, so she spends a good chunk of her time at Gwyn's, trying to work away at our daughter. When she's not there, she's taken an interest in managing the town militia with Sanders and me. I suppose if anyone's capable of whipping a bunch of ex-farmhands fresh up from Harvest Valley into something that's worth half a damn, it'll be her. "Me, I'm just glad my wife's home. She's a woman who looks and feels like she knows what she's doing, and that's pretty damned invaluable in times like this. People want to believe in someone like that, and another one can't hurt. Old man Sanders and I may be good, but we can only be stretched so thinly. Yeah, she's having no problems settling in nicely, all right — really does feel like someone paved the way for her to do just that." |"The way Gweyr just manages to have our boy eating out of her hand... it makes me wonder what might have happened if she hadn't left to walk the ice, if Garret would've been less of a wastrel these past years just sitting around, drinking and snapping at me every chance he got. I feed the pup, I raise the pup, I teach him everything I know, and his answer to that is to be closer with his mother whom he's only just had the chance to know." "Look, I'm not jealous or anything, the boy has a style that he inherited from his mother, so it makes sense. But at the same time... I find it a little sad." Yeah, you find it a little sad too as to why Garth simply can't understand why his son might be just a little bit resentful that he was lied to about his mother for most of his childhood. At least he had some idea that Gweyr might've been alive out there somewhere, as opposed to his sister who went so far as to believe their mother ran out on them and was dead. That Garret gives him the time of day after the truth's been revealed just goes to show how far he's come — not necessarily because of his mother, but on his own — to realize that while he may certainly disagree with what his father did to him, he at least understands why Garth did it. That's more than that Garret you met at first locked up in an animal cage or the Garret drinking his brains out on at his father's taps would've done. Even if everything's right and his mother is but a blank slate for Garret, that's better than the alternative. Garth instinctively looks like he's going to argue, then slumps his shoulders and shakes his head. "I guess I deserve it, huh?" Deserve's got nothing to do with it. He did raise his son to the best of his ability... but if Garret is anything like his mother, then the sting of that kind of betrayal hurts a lot. Maybe the best thing Garth can do is to give it time, let his son find himself a little while longer now that he's got a new influence in his life. If nothing else, Garth still has Gwyn around, and she really does love her daddy unconditionally. A sigh. "My only remaining worries in this world are that I'll never live to see the day my son ceases to be an idiot and my daughter gets married off." |How's his relationship with his wife working out now that they're finally back together after all these years? You can understand if he doesn't want to answer, given that it's a pretty personal question, but you're really just hoping that everything's going to work out fine for everyone involved and that the ending of this little tale that's stretched decades is at least content, even if it can't be outright happy. "It's... fine. I'm glad to have my wife back, it's nice to have someone sleeping beside you again after all this time, and we've had a lot of catching up to do. It's kind of like when we were first in love all over again, only now our joints ache more and we're not as vigorous as we used to be." Garth clears his throat uncertainly. "It's taken all this while, but I think we're heading back once more towards the life that the both of us envisioned for ourselves when we made the decision to leave the Crossed Swords and head back up north to the land of our birth. We could have hung on for a while — a mercenary company is no place to raise a pup, but it can be done as my father-in-law proved — but here and now, I have this feeling that I'm making the same kind of weighty decision as my wife and I did back then, to get when the going's good." If it makes him happier, and gives him closure to this whole story. "Closure, yeah, that's what it is. Closure. I guess that's what it is when there isn't that little weight at the back of my mind wondering when it is that I'll ever have to tell the kids about their mother, or what to do if anyone ever found out... to be honest, best it was you rather than one of the town gossips. And now that everyone knows at least some part of the story thanks to Tollus poking his head around down in the valley... I'm actually surprised that the consequences wasn't as terrible as I'd imagined them to be. People like my wife, and I haven't been hounded out of town either, so..." Like what you experienced so far down beneath the water, maybe the worst nightmares are those one creates for oneself. There's an argument to be made that he's punished himself enough for his misdeeds, but only the gods can judge him on that now. |"My wife's wasted no time in making herself useful. Fat much of a retirement this is for her, ha." Well, she did say that it was going to be her last adventure, not her death. A woman like her isn't going to twiddle her thumbs, idle around, and wait to die peaceably in her sleep. Garth snorts. "Well, she's certainly living up to the position of unofficial alderman's wife, if nothing else. Gweyr hasn't been back in Hawkethorne that long and she's already installed herself in our daughter's nursery, slid into an unofficial position with the local militia, and even gone around to bother Ogrish. The woman's always been good at dealing with people and leaving me to balance the books, so I'm not really surprised. People like her." There's something to be said for that — Gweyr is very forthright and direct. People whom she hasn't strangled within minutes of meeting her are pretty much safe in the knowledge that she doesn't mind having them around, and that kind of honesty is refreshing in this day and age. "It's starting to feel a bit like we're back in the Crossed Swords again... with her barking orders and people following her just because she seems to know what she's doing and has every right to be giving them. Wouldn't work with someone like Sanders or you, but most folks are rattled enough of late to want to have someone to follow, and somehow the word's spread like wildfire that she's my wife, having come home from some kind of amazing adventure to retire in her glory days. "It's not too different from the life we might've had if we'd stayed on as mercenaries instead of opting for moving on, I guess. Staying on, fighting until our bodies gave out... and if we didn't get ourselves killed, hang on around the edges and offer our advice and experience to the young folks. Yeah... if we'd stayed on with the Crossed Swords, this is about what we'd have been doing, and we'd be looking to retire about now. Guess the more things change, the more they stay the same, don't they?" ]"

rows.translation: 格维尔

rows.original: "You must have learned a thing or two while you were an adventurer, right?" you ask, leaning half across the bar. Garth eyes you suspiciously, still polishing his glasses. "
rows.translation: 在当冒险者的这段时间里，你肯定学到了不少东西吧？你这么问，身体半倚在吧台上。加斯怀疑地盯着你，一边继续擦拭着他的眼镜。"
rows.raw: '\n "You must have learned a thing or two while you were an adventurer, right?" you ask, leaning half across the bar. Garth eyes you suspiciously, still polishing his glasses. "'

rows.original: " Garth looks you up and down, sighs, and sets the cleaned glass aside. "That right? Yeah, I used to be a pretty decent swordsman back in the day. Not the best, mind, or I'd be walking without a cane. Still... yeah, I reckon I could teach you a thing or two, kiddo. Question is: are you ready to learn? Fighting's more than just brawn and meat: it's as much courage, quick-thinking, and strategy as anything. I can teach you to swing a blade, but not how to think. That... you have to bring yourself." You nod, saying that you're willing to put in your part. "Good. Now throw in some coin, and we're in business."
rows.translation: " 加斯上下打量了你一番，叹了口气，然后将清洗干净的玻璃杯放在了一边。是吗？嗯，过去我确实是个还算不错的剑客。当然，也不是最顶尖的，否则现在我就不需要拄拐杖了。不过……嗯，我想我确实可以教你一些东西，孩子。问题在于：你准备好学习了吗？战斗不仅仅是靠力量和体力，还需要勇气、机智和策略。我可以教你如何使用剑，但无法教你如何思考。这个……得靠你自己去领悟。 你点了点头，表示愿意尽自己的一份力。 好的。现在投些钱进来，我们就开始正式运作了。
rows.raw: "" Garth looks you up and down, sighs, and sets the cleaned glass aside. "That right? Yeah, I used to be a pretty decent swordsman back in the day. Not the best, mind, or I'd be walking without a cane. Still... yeah, I reckon I could teach you a thing or two, kiddo. Question is: are you ready to learn? Fighting's more than just brawn and meat: it's as much courage, quick-thinking, and strategy as anything. I can teach you to swing a blade, but not how to think. That... you have to bring yourself." You nod, saying that you're willing to put in your part. "Good. Now throw in some coin, and we're in business.""

rows.original: I need to get better. I think you're the guy that can make that happen.
rows.translation: 我需要变得更好。我觉得你就是那个能够帮助我实现这一目标的人。
rows.raw: "I need to get better. I think you're the guy that can make that happen."

rows.original: Any way I could convince you to share some wisdom? Something tells me I'm going to need it.
rows.translation: 有没有什么办法能说服你分享一些智慧呢？我有种预感，我以后肯定会需要这些智慧的。
rows.raw: "Any way I could convince you to share some wisdom? Something tells me I'm going to need it."

rows.original: Could you, like, teach me how to be a big tough fighter like you? Pretty please? I'd be so toootally grateful!
rows.translation: 你能教我怎么变成像你一样厉害的战士吗？真的求你啦！我会非常感激的！
rows.raw: "Could you, like, teach me how to be a big tough fighter like you? Pretty please? I'd be so toootally grateful!"

rows.original: Staring down the burly wolf-man, you say that you'd like to train with him again. There's still plenty you can learn from him. "That right?" Garth chuckles. "Well, you're an able enough pupil. A far sight better than half the hunters who come here thinking they're the next dragonslayer. Alright. Pitch in a little coin, and I'll show you what I know."
rows.translation: 你凝视着那个魁梧的狼人，说道自己很想再与他一起训练。你还有很多东西可以从他那里学到。 是吗？加斯轻声笑了起来。嗯，你确实是个相当有能力的学徒。比那些自以为能成为下一个屠龙者的猎人要好多了。好吧，投一枚硬币进来，我就告诉你我所知道的东西。
rows.raw: " Staring down the burly wolf-man, you say that you'd like to train with him again. There's still plenty you can learn from him. "That right?" Garth chuckles. "Well, you're an able enough pupil. A far sight better than half the hunters who come here thinking they're the next dragonslayer. Alright. Pitch in a little coin, and I'll show you what I know.""

rows.translation: 属性

rows.original: You're still level 1! You haven't even assigned any attribute points yet.
rows.translation: 你还是1级呢！甚至还没有分配任何属性点数呢。
rows.raw: "You're still level 1! You haven't even assigned any attribute points yet."

rows.translation: 属性

rows.original: Re-assign the Attribute points you gained from levelling up. You can't re-assign the points you started with at Level 1, nor any temporary points. Costs 300 Electrum Coins and a day of training time.
rows.translation: 你可以重新分配因升级而获得的属性点数。不过，你无法重新分配在1级时初始拥有的那些点数，也无法重新分配任何临时获得的点数。进行这项操作需要花费300枚琥珀金币，并且还需要消耗一天的训练时间。
rows.raw: "Re-assign the Attribute points you gained from levelling up. You can't re-assign the points you started with at Level 1, nor any temporary points. Costs 300 Electrum Coins and a day of training time."

rows.original: You don't have the 300 EC required to retrain.
rows.translation: 你没有重新训练所需的300枚琥珀金币。
rows.raw: "You don't have the 300 EC required to retrain."

rows.translation: 学习技能

rows.original: Train any Warrior or Thief power that you are high enough level to use. Costs 100 Electrum Coins per level of the power, and will take up the rest of your day.
rows.translation: 当你等级足够高时，可以学习任何战士或盗贼职业相关的技能。学习每项技能需要消耗100枚琥珀金币，而且学习过程会占用你一整天的时间。
rows.raw: "Train any Warrior or Thief power that you are high enough level to use. Costs 100 Electrum Coins per level of the power, and will take up the rest of your day."

rows.translation: 学习技能

rows.original: There are no powers Garth can teach you right now.
rows.translation: 目前，加斯并没有任何能力可以教给你。
rows.raw: "There are no powers Garth can teach you right now."

rows.translation: 更换职业

rows.original: Change your class to Warrior or Thief, martial classes focused on stalwart defense and devastating strikes, respectively. Switching classes does not transfer or unlock new Talents, though it will give you the perks of your new class up to your current level. You would be well-advised to have the coin to buy additional talents afterwards. Switching classes costs 3,000 Electrum Coins, and will take one full week of time.
rows.translation: 将你的职业改为战士或盗贼吧。战士职业注重坚实的防御，而盗贼职业则擅长造成毁灭性的攻击。职业转换并不会转移或解锁新的天赋，但会让你立即获得新职业在当前等级下所能提供的优势。建议你在转换职业后尽快准备足够的金币来购买额外的天赋。职业转换需要花费3,000枚琥珀金币，并且整个过程需要整整一周的时间。
rows.raw: "Change your class to Warrior or Thief, martial classes focused on stalwart defense and devastating strikes, respectively. Switching classes does not transfer or unlock new Talents, though it will give you the perks of your new class up to your current level. You would be well-advised to have the coin to buy additional talents afterwards. Switching classes costs 3,000 Electrum Coins, and will take one full week of time."

rows.original: You don't have the required 3,000 EC.
rows.translation: 你没有所需的3,000枚琥珀金币。
返回

rows.original: "Alright then," Garth says, picking up his cane from behind the bar. "Gwyn and I keep enough room clear in our yard for practice. Come with me, and we'll get started." You eagerly follow the old wolf out of the Frost Hound, keeping apace with him the short distance to the small cottage he and his daughter share. Gwyn's sitting on the porch when you arrive, nursing one of her pups as the others crawl happily about her, exploring the world outside with wide, awe-filled eyes. With a faint blush, she buttons her blouse as you arrive and, exchanging a few words with her father, ushers her brood inside. She returns with a pair of practice blades, dull but nearly as weighty as a real sword you soon come to find out. The rest of the day is spent in hard, sweaty combat practice. Not with Garth
rows.translation: 那好吧。加斯从吧台后面拿起了他的手杖，说道。格温和我在院子里留出了足够的空间用来练习。跟我来吧，我们马上就可以开始。 你急切地跟随那只老狼走出了寒霜猎犬，沿着短短的路程跟随着它，来到了它和女儿共同居住的小屋。当你到达时，格温正坐在门廊上，正在喂养她的一只幼崽，而其他的小崽们则开心地在她身边爬来爬去，用那双充满惊奇与好奇的眼睛探索着外面的世界。当你到达时，她脸上带着一丝红晕，系好了上衣的纽扣。与父亲简短交谈了几句后，她便带着孩子们进了屋。不久后，她拿回来两把练习用刀——虽然刀刃很钝，但重量却几乎与真正的剑相当，这一点你很快就会发现。 剩下的时间都被用来进行艰苦而充满汗水的战斗训练。不过，这些训练并不是和加斯一起进行的。
rows.raw: ' "Alright then," Garth says, picking up his cane from behind the bar. "Gwyn and I keep enough room clear in our yard for practice. Come with me, and we'll get started." You eagerly follow the old wolf out of the Frost Hound, keeping apace with him the short distance to the small cottage he and his daughter share. Gwyn's sitting on the porch when you arrive, nursing one of her pups as the others crawl happily about her, exploring the world outside with wide, awe-filled eyes. With a faint blush, she buttons her blouse as you arrive and, exchanging a few words with her father, ushers her brood inside. She returns with a pair of practice blades, dull but nearly as weighty as a real sword you soon come to find out. The rest of the day is spent in hard, sweaty combat practice. Not with Garth'

rows.original: , but with Gwyn. The wolfess has clearly learned from the best, as she proves herself to be a fearsome blademaster in the first minutes of your training. But she's as much a student as you are, it seems: Garth is never far, instructing you both on stance and form, pointing out weaknesses and vulnerabilities to either exploit or shield. By the time you're done for the evening, you're bruised and exhausted... but stronger for it. You can feel it in your bones.
rows.translation: 但是和格温一起训练的话就不同了。这位女狼显然向最优秀的人学习了，因为在你们训练的最初几分钟里，她就证明了自己是一位令人畏惧的剑术大师。不过，她似乎和你一样，也是一名学生：加斯始终在旁边，指导你们调整姿势和动作，指出你们各自的弱点，以便你们能够利用这些弱点或避开它们。当训练结束时，你们已经浑身是伤、精疲力竭……但同时也变得更强了。这种变化，你们能真切地感受到。
rows.raw: ", but with Gwyn. The wolfess has clearly learned from the best, as she proves herself to be a fearsome blademaster in the first minutes of your training. But she's as much a student as you are, it seems: Garth is never far, instructing you both on stance and form, pointing out weaknesses and vulnerabilities to either exploit or shield. By the time you're done for the evening, you're bruised and exhausted... but stronger for it. You can feel it in your bones.\n    \n    "

rows.original:
, you're rewarded with a home-cooked meal courtesy of Gwyneth. Though winded from practice, she's still a perfect model of a hostess, all but waiting on you hand and foot. Without a blade in hand, she suddenly seems much meeker, almost girlish where hours prior there had been a fierce maiden of war. 
    
    You and Garth share drinks afterwards as his daughter puts the children to bed, a congratulatory round before you head back to the Frost Hound for much needed slumber.
rows.translation:
练习结束后，格温妮丝为你准备了一顿家常菜作为奖励。虽然她因为练习而有些疲惫，但她依然展现出了主妇应有的风范，几乎是在寸步不离地照顾你。当她没有手持任何工具时，她显得格外温顺，几乎有点像个小女孩；而就在几个小时之前，她还是一个充满斗志的勇士呢。
    
    之后，在加斯的女儿哄孩子们睡觉的时候，你们一起喝了些酒，互相道贺一番，然后你便回到了霜犬酒馆号，准备好好休息一番了。
rows.raw: ", you're rewarded with a home-cooked meal courtesy of Gwyneth. Though winded from practice, she's still a perfect model of a hostess, all but waiting on you hand and foot. Without a blade in hand, she suddenly seems much meeker, almost girlish where hours prior there had been a fierce maiden of war. \n    \n    You and Garth share drinks afterwards as his daughter puts the children to bed, a congratulatory round before you head back to the Frost Hound for much needed slumber. "

rows.translation: 正如你所预料的那样
那个夜晚

rows.original: You've got much more training ahead...
rows.translation: 你还有很长的学习之路要走……

rows.original: You'll be putting these lessons to use soon enough.
rows.translation: 你很快就会用到这些知识了。
rows.raw: "You'll be putting these lessons to use soon enough."

rows.translation: 下一步
观察者

rows.original: [gweyr.returned |As you step into the Frost Hound, you can't help but notice the lack of patrons today. [dayNight |Sure, it's daytime, but drink isn't the only thing Garth serves in his tavern |It's most uncharacteristic, considering that the tavern is supposed to be the heart of Hawkethorne ]. Maybe it's got something to do with the decidedly chillier atmosphere that pervades the common room... it's as if someone left the doors open for a good half-day. Then you notice the considerably imposing shape of Gweyr standing by the door with her arms folded, with Garth backing her up a little ways away from the bar. The two of them share a glance as you enter, and then the old wolfess clears her throat and steps forward. "[pc.name], there you are; I've been expecting you for a while now. I think we need to talk for a moment." Gweyr gestures at the nearest empty table, and the expression on her face and the ways her fists are clenched suggests that she's not taking no for an answer. You turn your gaze to Garth, who merely sets down the tankard he's cleaning and leans forward on the bartop to give you a nod. All right, then. You pull out a stool and take your place at the table[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames] settling down beside you ]. What's the matter? Gweyr shows you her teeth. "It's about my daughter." ...Uh-oh. "See, while I may have been estranged from my baby girl for much of her life and she may think ill of me, I still love her as much as the day she was born; ever since I've come back, I've seen it as my duty to try and make up for all the years that I failed to be with her, regardless of how much she may resent me. "Now then, my husband's told me that this has happened before when I was away, and it hasn't escaped either of us that our daughter's belly is starting to round out again with yet another litter of puppies. Now, she's a big girl and can make some of her decisions for herself, even if she's still living under my roof; it would be awful of me and an insult to Garth's raising of her to come back after twenty years and start telling her how to live her life after I've been gone so long. That being said, I am her mother, and it's only natural for me to [silly |do a concern |be concerned ] about her getting herself knocked up again; for example, I made sure to shut up those loose tongues that were going around saying it was her father or brother who'd done the deed. Yes, I shut them up in a very personal manner, if you get where I'm coming from. Do you?" You do. Yes, you do. "Good, good. The first fool that took advantage of my daughter, Garth and Garret ran him out of town, and I may or may not have taken a personal interest in the matter once he was out of sight from the village gates. Now, I'm sure someone whom I trusted to have my back when my life was on the line wouldn't do such a thing to a poor puppy like my daughter, good-natured girl that she is." If you did, you wouldn't have give money to her little nursery, would you? Garth sighs as he speaks up from the bar. "It would've been nice if you could've asked either my wife or I first — Gweyr here dragged me out all the way to meet her father and beg him for permission mere weeks before his head got stoved in by a war-hammer — but young people will be young people. The both of us were young once, too, and I'll admit there are worse people I could think of to father my little girl's pups. If nothing else, you helped Cait when no one else would, and have done me and mine more services than I'd ever expected.[var1| That, and you've been making sure your get's well-paid for materially at least.]" Well, he has been letting you stay in his rooms for free ever since that night. Gweyr sighs and takes the reins of the conversation once more. "We're not unreasonable people, [pc.name] — my husband's kindness is but natural given that you're not just our best chance, but you've been going around solving peoples' problems ever since you arrived in town, or so I hear. But regardless of what you've done for us, don't you go around upsetting our daughter like the last suitor did, or —" Oh yes, you've heard this one before. Don't you go making her cry, or she'll come to get you, right? Traditionally, the role would have fallen to Garth, but you understand she's more suited to being the hands-on one in the family. "Oh no, I won't come to get you. Someone else more terrible than me will. Her idiot brother, to be precise." You chance a look at Garret, sprawled out at a nearby table with his arms outstretched and his head between his elbows. Yeeeah... you have your doubts about how terrifying Gweyr's idiot son is. Indeed, somehow, the mention of Garret fails to evoke the deep-seated terror she was going for. "Don't underestimate him. Sometimes, my son being an idiot has its uses — he takes after me where it counts, and unlike me he doesn't have the wisdom to know when to stop. He can't be bargained with. He can't be reasoned with. He doesn't feel pity, or remorse, or fear. And he absolutely will not stop, ever, until you're dragged back in here by the scruff of your neck to pay your dues to my little girl. You get me?" [pc.isDK |You shrug |If that's the way she's going to put it ]. Is there anything else she'd be so helpful as to let you know? "That's all. Just... take good care of Gwyneth; I wasn't around for her when she needed me most, so I'll be damned if I let myself be delinquent now. Now, Garth and I were in a similar place where you are now, so I'm not going to drag the both of you to Sanders and demand you marry her right there and then. That being said... please don't abuse the kindness in her soul, because people like her are extremely rare in this day and age when only the hard tend to survive." All right, then. You'll be going. "Right. Now then, get. We'll speak more about this when this whole shitshow is over and things have a chance at settling down. Before then, there's not much point in talking about it." With that, Gweyr thumbs over her shoulder, dismissing you. ]也许这与公共休息室里弥漫着的那种明显更为阴冷的气氛有关……就好像有人把门敞开了大半天的时间。然后你注意到，格维尔双臂交叉站在门边，那巍然的身影显得格外醒目；而加斯则站在离吧台稍远的地方，站在她的旁边。当你走进去时，他们两人相互对视了一眼，随后那位老女狼清了清嗓子，向前走了过来。[pc.name]，就是你，我等了你好一会儿了。我觉得我们有必要谈一谈。”格维尔指向旁边那张空桌子，她脸上的表情以及紧握的拳头都表明，她不会接受拒绝。你将目光转向加思，只见他放下正在擦拭的酒壶，向前倾身在吧台上点了点头。 现在，我丈夫告诉我，这种事情在我不在家的时候确实发生过。我们俩都注意到了，我们女儿的肚子又开始变圆了，看来又要生一窝小狗了。不过，她现在已经是个大姑娘了，可以自己做一些决定了，虽然她仍然住在我的家里。如果在我离开这么久之后才回来，就开始对她的生活指手画脚，那不仅对我不公平，也是对加思这些年来对她所付出的养育之心的侮辱。话虽如此，我是她的母亲，对我来说，这样做是很自然的。 [silly |表示关心或担忧 |感到担忧 ]关于她再次怀孕的事情；比如，我坚决让那些散布谣言的人闭嘴，他们当时一直在说是她的父亲或兄弟干的。没错，我用了非常直接的方式让他们闭嘴，你应该能理解我的意思。你是这样做的，对吧？” “是的，你确实这么做了。” rows.raw: " [gweyr.returned |As you step into the Frost Hound, you can't help but notice the lack of patrons today. [dayNight |Sure, it's daytime, but drink isn't the only thing Garth serves in his tavern |It's most uncharacteristic, considering that the tavern is supposed to be the heart of Hawkethorne ]. Maybe it's got something to do with the decidedly chillier atmosphere that pervades the common room... it's as if someone left the doors open for a good half-day. Then you notice the considerably imposing shape of Gweyr standing by the door with her arms folded, with Garth backing her up a little ways away from the bar. The two of them share a glance as you enter, and then the old wolfess clears her throat and steps forward. "[pc.name], there you are; I've been expecting you for a while now. I think we need to talk for a moment." Gweyr gestures at the nearest empty table, and the expression on her face and the ways her fists are clenched suggests that she's not taking no for an answer. You turn your gaze to Garth, who merely sets down the tankard he's cleaning and leans forward on the bartop to give you a nod. All right, then. You pull out a stool and take your place at the table[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames] settling down beside you ]. What's the matter? Gweyr shows you her teeth. "It's about my daughter." ...Uh-oh. "See, while I may have been estranged from my baby girl for much of her life and she may think ill of me, I still love her as much as the day she was born; ever since I've come back, I've seen it as my duty to try and make up for all the years that I failed to be with her, regardless of how much she may resent me. "Now then, my husband's told me that this has happened before when I was away, and it hasn't escaped either of us that our daughter's belly is starting to round out again with yet another litter of puppies. Now, she's a big girl and can make some of her decisions for herself, even if she's still living under my roof; it would be awful of me and an insult to Garth's raising of her to come back after twenty years and start telling her how to live her life after I've been gone so long. That being said, I am her mother, and it's only natural for me to [silly |do a concern |be concerned ] about her getting herself knocked up again; for example, I made sure to shut up those loose tongues that were going around saying it was her father or brother who'd done the deed. Yes, I shut them up in a very personal manner, if you get where I'm coming from. Do you?" You do. Yes, you do. "Good, good. The first fool that took advantage of my daughter, Garth and Garret ran him out of town, and I may or may not have taken a personal interest in the matter once he was out of sight from the village gates. Now, I'm sure someone whom I trusted to have my back when my life was on the line wouldn't do such a thing to a poor puppy like my daughter, good-natured girl that she is." If you did, you wouldn't have give money to her little nursery, would you? Garth sighs as he speaks up from the bar. "It would've been nice if you could've asked either my wife or I first — Gweyr here dragged me out all the way to meet her father and beg him for permission mere weeks before his head got stoved in by a war-hammer — but young people will be young people. The both of us were young once, too, and I'll admit there are worse people I could think of to father my little girl's pups. If nothing else, you helped Cait when no one else would, and have done me and mine more services than I'd ever expected.[var1| That, and you've been making sure your get's well-paid for materially at least.]" Well, he has been letting you stay in his rooms for free ever since that night. Gweyr sighs and takes the reins of the conversation once more. "We're not unreasonable people, [pc.name] — my husband's kindness is but natural given that you're not just our best chance, but you've been going around solving peoples' problems ever since you arrived in town, or so I hear. But regardless of what you've done for us, don't you go around upsetting our daughter like the last suitor did, or —" Oh yes, you've heard this one before. Don't you go making her cry, or she'll come to get you, right? Traditionally, the role would have fallen to Garth, but you understand she's more suited to being the hands-on one in the family. "Oh no, I won't come to get you. Someone else more terrible than me will. Her idiot brother, to be precise." You chance a look at Garret, sprawled out at a nearby table with his arms outstretched and his head between his elbows. Yeeeah... you have your doubts about how terrifying Gweyr's idiot son is. Indeed, somehow, the mention of Garret fails to evoke the deep-seated terror she was going for. "Don't underestimate him. Sometimes, my son being an idiot has its uses — he takes after me where it counts, and unlike me he doesn't have the wisdom to know when to stop. He can't be bargained with. He can't be reasoned with. He doesn't feel pity, or remorse, or fear. And he absolutely will not stop, ever, until you're dragged back in here by the scruff of your neck to pay your dues to my little girl. You get me?" [pc.isDK |You shrug |If that's the way she's going to put it ]. Is there anything else she'd be so helpful as to let you know? "That's all. Just... take good care of Gwyneth; I wasn't around for her when she needed me most, so I'll be damned if I let myself be delinquent now. Now, Garth and I were in a similar place where you are now, so I'm not going to drag the both of you to Sanders and demand you marry her right there and then. That being said... please don't abuse the kindness in her soul, because people like her are extremely rare in this day and age when only the hard tend to survive." All right, then. You'll be going. "Right. Now then, get. We'll speak more about this when this whole shitshow is over and things have a chance at settling down. Before then, there's not much point in talking about it." With that, Gweyr thumbs over her shoulder, dismissing you. You throw a glance at Garth, but he just picks up his tankard back up and continues polishing as if nothing had ever happened. |As you step into the Frost Hound, you can't help but notice the lack of patrons today. rows.original: "Hey, [pc.name]," Garth calls nodding you over. "Figured I'd mention something to you that might be useful, now that you're venturing out all day. There's an old building by the eastern gates. I used to use it as a gymnasium when I was a bit younger and handier with a sword. Nothing like the stuff you'd find in Khor'minos and the inside's probably covered in a three inch layer of dust by now, but if you were looking to put on a little muscle it might be helpful."[pc.toneRange 85| "Not that you need it," he adds, looking you over.|] "Thanks, Garth," you say, nodding gratefully. "I'll take a look when I'm not busy." "Aye," he says, picking up a mug. [var0|"Might have Garret take a look about fixing it up a bit."|"When my idiot son gets back around I'll have him take a look at fixing it up a bit."]
rows.translation: 嘿，[pc.name]，加斯叫你过去，”他说着点了点头。“既然你一整天都要外出活动，我觉得有件事可能会对你有帮助。有一栋旧建筑从东门进入我小时候还经常用它来锻炼身体，那时候我使用剑的技术也还算不错。虽然它肯定比不上科尔米诺斯那些先进的训练设施，而且里面的设备现在可能已经积了三英寸厚的灰尘，但如果你想增强体力的话，它还是有点用的。[pc.toneRange 85| 其实你并不需要它，”他边说边打量着你。|] 谢谢，加思，”你感激地点了点头说道，“有空的时候我会看看的。” “嗯，”他一边说，一边拿起了一个杯子。 [var0|或许可以让加雷特去看看，把这个问题解决一下。|等我那个笨儿子回来后，让他去看看能不能把这个问题解决一下。]

There's an old building by the eastern gates. I used to use it as a gymnasium when I was a bit younger and handier with a sword. Nothing like the stuff you'd find in Khor'minos and the inside's probably covered in a three inch layer of dust by now, but if you were looking to put on a little muscle it might be helpful."[pc.toneRange 85| "Not that you need it," he adds, looking you over.|] "Thanks, Garth," you say, nodding gratefully. "I'll take a look when I'm not busy." "Aye," he says, picking up a mug. [var0|"Might have Garret take a look about fixing it up a bit."|"When my idiot son gets back around I'll have him take a look at fixing it up a bit."]'

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original:
Garth pauses mid-mug-wash, frowning. "Look, [pc.name]. Sure I've... had my run-ins with orcs before, but I already told the poor girl. I think I'd remember a giant pink-haired orcish woman if she managed to squeeze an heir out of me, sorry."
    
    "Some 'run-ins'?" 
    
    "A-hem. Yes, well... look, orcs raid a lot. Sometimes a bunch of dumb young pups get their blood up and, well... spoils of war?"
    
    Uh huh... you can't really tell when a lupine man's blushing, but you're pretty sure he's about to clock you around the head if you go asking for details.
rows.translation:
加斯在洗杯子的时候停了下来，皱起了眉头。“听着，[pc.name]当然，我以前确实和兽人有过一些冲突，不过我已经告诉那个可怜的女孩了。如果那个兽人女性真的设法让我生下继承人，我想我应该会记得她的吧，实在不好意思。”
    
    “‘一些冲突’？”
    
    “嗯，是的……你看，兽人经常会发动袭击。有时候，一些愚蠢的年轻兽人就会冲动起来，然后……就会出现战利品之类的情况。”
    
    嗯……你其实很难分辨一个狼族男性什么时候在脸红，但如果你去追问细节的话，那你就可以肯定他接下来会揍你的头了。

rows.original:
Garth scratches his ear. "Am I hearing you right? You want to what?"
    
    "Set up a temple to Mallach up on the ruins of the old temple up the mount," Cait replies matter-of-factly.
    
    Garth looks between you and Cait, then sighs and draws out mugs of mead for the [party.manyCompanions
        |three
        |both
    ] of you. "Alright. Let's have a sit by the bar and I'll hear what you've to say."
    
    And he does. Cait gives him more or less the same explanation that she did when she was discussing the topic with you and Salwah, and he listens, expression unchanging. Eventually, your mugs run dry, and he scratches his chin thoughtfully as he takes them back behind the bar and gives you a refill.
    
    "Tollus and his goons weren't the first to get their panties in a twist over that place, you know. Sure, they were the most dire, but even when they weren't menacing the ruins, every couple of years some gaggle of vagrants or coven of witches goes up that way. Used to be, the wife'd chase 'em out if the baroness didn't. Having you there'd be a sight better than any of the other options, I 'spose."
    
    "That, and maybe, just maybe, Calla will be able to find her way back. If she does... I want it to be into friendly arms."
    
    "Hmm. One thing, though. Pale elves were the first ones there — the ruins are those of one of their temples."
    
    Cait frowns. "Is that... a problem? I don't think Etheryn's going to mind."
    
    "Well, not on my part — you've done enough good around the town that I'd be happy to have you both settle down here, and we have plenty of catfolk around who would appreciate a place for their own faith. I don't see old man Sanders having a problem, either — he's no hardliner. Man might serve Velun today, but he used to be with Lumia and his little chapel pays service to all of the Seven. Don't think the town would complain; if someone's going to be up there, I'd rather it be you than that last band of thugs.
    
    "What I'm more worried about is if the place is safe for you and the folks who come to visit. Like I said, there's always been something weird about that hill that draws in crazies and killers both. That's been good a reason as any for us to leave it abandoned... but if you want to settle down there, you'd best check it out first. Being a woman of the cloth, I'm sure you shouldn't have any problems with that."
    
    Cait glances at you, then turns back to Garth. "I'll go take a closer look. We didn't really get to do a thorough examination the first time [pc.name] and I made the climb. My father's a magician of some repute — I'm sure he'll be able to help."
    
    "You do that, Cait. Tell me when you're done and I'll see about getting the townsfolk together to put up your little house of worship. We'll get it done in days."
    
    Your pink kitten beams at that, then tips back her head and polishes off her drink. A fresh spring in her step, Cait grabs you by the hand and tugs excitedly. "C'mon, [pc.name]! Let's go get dad, then get up there and do a bit of surveying!"
    
    Enthusiastic, isn't she? Even the usually dour Garth manages a smile and nod at the two of you as your pink kitten all but drags you out, bouncing along as the two of you emerge onto the street.
rows.translation:
加思挠了挠耳朵：“我听清楚了吗？你想要做什么？”

“在山上的那座旧寺庙的废墟上为马拉克建立一座新的寺庙吧，”凯特理所当然地回答道。

加思看了看你和凯特，然后叹了口气，去拿了几杯蜂蜜酒来[party.manyCompanions
        |三
        |两者都
    ]好吧，我们去吧台边坐一会儿，我听听你有什么要说的。”

他照做了。凯特向他解释的内容，基本上和她当初与你以及萨尔瓦讨论这个话题时说的一样，而他只是静静地听着，面无表情。最终，你们的杯子都喝空了，他若有所思地挠了挠下巴，然后把杯子拿回吧台去续杯，再拿回来递给你们。
    
    你知道，托勒斯和他的那些手下并不是第一批为那个地方大动肝火的。当然，他们的威胁最为严重，但即便他们没有去威胁那些废墟，每隔几年也总会有一群流浪者或一群女巫前往那里。过去，如果女男爵不亲自把他们赶走，她的妻子也会这么做。有你在那里，我想，情况肯定会比其他任何选择都要好得多。
    
    那样的话，或许，只是或许，卡拉能够找到回去的路。如果她真的做到了……我希望她能回到充满关爱的怀抱中。”

“嗯，不过有一点需要注意。那些废墟其实是苍白精灵们的寺庙遗址，他们是最早来到那里的人。”

凯特皱起了眉头：“这会……成为问题吗？我觉得伊瑟琳应该不会介意的。
    
    嗯，我没什么意见——你们在镇上做了很多好事，如果你们俩能在这里安顿下来，我会非常高兴的。而且我们这里有很多猫族，他们也很需要一个能够信仰自己宗教的地方。我觉得桑德斯老人也不会有意见的，他可不是个固执的人。虽然他现在效忠于维伦，但以前他可是属于卢米亚的，他的小教堂也为所有七大神明服务。我想镇上的居民也不会有意见的；如果非得有人去那里侍奉神明，我宁愿是你们，也不愿是那群暴徒。
    
    我更担心的是，那个地方是否对你和那些前来参观的人来说是安全的。就像我之前说的，那座山总是有些奇怪的地方，总是吸引一些疯子和杀手。这也正是我们把它废弃的原因……但如果你想在那里定居的话，最好先去考察一下。作为一名女性，我相信你应该不会遇到什么问题。
    
    凯特瞥了你一眼，然后又转过头去看着加思：“我去仔细看看吧。第一次我们并没有进行彻底的检查。[pc.name]然后我就开始爬了。我父亲可是颇有名气的魔术师——我相信他一定能帮上忙的。”

“你就这么办吧，凯特。等你弄好了，告诉我一声，我会召集镇上的居民一起来帮你搭建那个小礼拜堂的。我们几天内就能把事情办妥的。”

听到这里，你那只粉红色的小猫咪开心地笑了起来，然后仰起头喝完了杯中的饮料。凯特脚步轻快地走到你身边，兴奋地拉着你的手说：“来吧，我们走吧！[pc.name]我们去找爸爸吧，然后上去好好勘察一下环境！”
她真是太热情了，不是吗？就连平时总是阴沉沉的加斯，看到你们两个的样子，也忍不住露出了微笑，点了点头。而你的粉色小猫更是使劲地拉着你，一路上蹦蹦跳跳，直到你们俩来到街上。
