rows.translation: 家人

rows.original: Garret raises an eyebrow and sniffs the air. "What's it to you?" It's a mystery floating about town. Garth won't tell you anything about it, Gwyn thinks that she abandoned them but doesn't know anything else, and everyone else in Hawkethorne has their own opinion about where she disappeared to. Maybe he can shed some light on the matter? Garret considers you for a few seconds, then reaches up and scratches his head. "Yeah... about that, truth be told, I don't think I have the whole story about what happened to my mom. I was already up and asking about her the moment I could walk and talk, and it's taken me a lifetime to piece together what I already have. It's like everyone in town who's old enough to have remembered her has had a spell put on them to keep them quiet. Old man Sanders was kind enough to let a few things slip, and I've gleaned some more over the years from the more venerable folk in town, but there're still gaps here and there about her." Huh. So even he doesn't know. "Not everything. Seriously, if you weren't such a good friend to me, I'd have told you to bugger off. Asking about someone else's mum is kinda sorta a private thing, you know." [pc.isDK |Sometimes the hard questions need to be asked, no matter how painful they are. He should know as much. Garret just snorts at that and takes a swig from his tankard. |You're going to beg his pardon for prying, but you're going to pry all the same unless he's going to violently object to such. Garret looks you up and down. "I... don't know about that. Just keep talking for now, and I'll stop you if you start going too far, okay?" That sounds fair, yes. "Good, good." ] So, down to the meat of the matter, then. He might not have the whole picture, but what does he know, then? Upon hearing that, Garret shoots a glance at his father working away behind the bar. Satisfied that Garth appears to be suitably distracted, he leans in close to you and lowers his voice conspiratorially. "She was exiled from Hawkethorne. To be absolutely clear, that means kicked out and told not to come back on pain of death. We're not really big on hangings here, unlike some other places, but exile ranks just below that. The Long Walk, it's called in some of the ancient lupine languages — traditionally, the guilty is given a strip of jerky and a sharp stick, then thrown out onto the snow and ice, never to come back. Every ten years or so someone comes across the frozen body of a long walker, preserved in ice for centuries. It was really popular back in ancient times — execution without actually needing to get one's hands bloody." Wow. "It happened when Gwyn and I were somewhere between four or five years old, from what I've been able to glean from old man Sanders. Up till then, she'd been running the Frost Hound with my old man, trying to get used to serving drinks and making beds after the life the both of them had led up till that point. It wasn't easy, but she was determined to make it work, wanting to die in her bed rather than in a puddle of her own blood. Having children — it tends to change people, although not always for the better. "And then something happened, though. My old man won't talk about it, Sanders says it was a hard choice, and when I ask anyone else they tell me she had to choose the lesser of two evils, and that I shouldn't dig any further. It was a stupid choice she had to make, one of those huge tangled knots, and she tried to unravel it by hand instead of getting a sharp edge and chopping through the whole thing altogether. "Even if she did choose the lesser of two evils, it was enough that the town reluctantly but unanimously chose to send her on the Long Walk. Sanders tells me that if she'd done the alternative, they'd have no choice but to hang her or else make a mockery of law and lore alike." Garret pauses a moment to catch his breath. "She left the next morning at first light. Took the sharp stick and jerky, and the last anyone ever saw of her was that she was heading south towards Harvest Valley, on the road towards Tychris. My old man, he stayed behind to raise Gwyn and me, and that's that." And he's neither seen nor heard nothing of her since? "No. No one has, and even if they had they wouldn't tell me. Gwyn sure as hell doesn't know — the only reason they're less tight-lipped with me is that I apparently look less like my old man and take after her a lot more." Garret stops to think a moment with his brow furrowed, drinks a little more deeply from his tankard than is strictly necessary. "I don't really have any concrete memories of her save for her face. An old brick. The smell of blood, without any danger in it. Her hands on my head, for some reason. The streets, filled with snow. And... that's about it. I might care more about her fate than Gwyn does, but still not enough to hope that she'll ever come back. Life goes on." So it does. "And that's all I know about my mom," Garret grunts. "You're welcome to dig and pry all you want — maybe people will be a little more loose-lipped around you. I don't really care one way or the other any more. So, want to talk about something else?" He's lying, he's painfully and obviously lying, but to press right now would be bad for the both of you.
rows.translation: 加雷特挑了挑眉毛，然后闻了闻空气中的气味。这关你什么事？ 镇上流传着一个谜团。加斯拒绝透露任何相关信息，格温认为自己是抛弃了他们，但也一无所知，而鹰棘镇的其他人也都对她的去向有着各自的猜测。也许他能为这个谜团提供一些线索吧？ 加雷特思考了几秒钟，然后抬起手挠了挠头。嗯……关于这件事，说实话，我觉得自己并不完全了解我妈妈到底发生了什么。从我能够走路、会说话的那一刻起，我就开始四处打听她的下落。而花费了我整整一生的时间，我才终于拼凑出了那些我所知道的信息。好像镇上所有还记得她的人，都被施了某种魔法，让他们保持沉默。桑德斯老人好心地透露了一些信息，这些年来，我又从镇上那些年长的人那里了解到了一些新的细节，但关于她的故事，仍然存在一些空白之处。" 哈，原来连他也不知道。 不是所有事情都该说出来。说真的，如果你不是我这么好的朋友，我早就让你滚蛋了。询问别人的妈妈这种事情，其实属于比较私密的范围，你懂的吧。 [pc.isDK |有时候，有些棘手的问题必须被提出来，无论它们会带来多大的痛苦。他应该了解这一点。 加雷特只是哼了一声，然后大口喝下了杯中的酒。 |你可能会因为自己的冒昧而请求他的原谅，但除非他强烈反对，否则你还是会继续追问下去的。 加雷特上下打量了你一番。我……不太清楚这个问题。先继续聊吧，如果你说得太过了，我会阻止你的，好吗？ 听起来挺公平的，没错。 很好，很好。 ] 那么，让我们直接进入主题吧。他可能并不了解全部情况，但他究竟知道些什么？ 听到这个回答，加雷特瞥了一眼正在吧台后面工作的父亲。看到加斯似乎已经被转移了注意力，他便凑近你，压低声音，神秘兮兮地说道。 她被逐出了鹰棘镇。明确地说，那就是被赶了出去，而且还被告知如果再回来就会被处死。和我们其他一些地方不同，这里其实并不喜欢用绞刑这种方式处死人，但流放这种惩罚也差不多相当于绞刑了。在某些古老的狼族语言中，这种刑罚被称为“长途跋涉”。传统上，罪犯会被给予一条干肉和一根锋利的棍子，然后被扔到冰雪之中，从此再也不会回来。每隔十年左右，就会有人发现那些在冰层中保存了几个世纪的“长途跋涉”者的尸体。在古代，这种做法其实非常流行——人们无需亲自动手就能完成处决。 哇哦。 这件事发生在我和格温四五岁的时候，这是从桑德斯老人那里了解到的。在此之前，她一直和我父亲一起经营着‘霜犬酒馆’酒馆，努力适应为顾客提供酒水和服务、整理床铺等工作——毕竟他们之前的生活方式与这些完全不同。这并不容易，但她决心要成功，因为她宁愿在自己的床上死去，也不愿死在自家血泊中。生孩子确实会改变一个人，不过这种变化并不总是向好的方向发展。 然后某个东西不过，这件事确实发生了。我父亲拒绝谈论这件事，桑德斯说那是一个艰难的决定；而当我向其他人询问时，他们也都告诉我，她当时只能在两个坏选择中选择一个相对较小的坏处，让我不要再深究下去。那确实是一个愚蠢的决定，一个复杂得难以解决的难题，而她试图用手去解开这个结，而不是用锋利的工具直接把整个问题彻底解决掉。 即使她确实选择了两害相权之轻者，但小镇上的居民们还是不情愿地、却也一致地决定让她去参加那场漫长的远征。桑德斯告诉我，如果她选择了另一种做法，他们就只能选择将她处死，否则就会让法律和传统都沦为笑柄。加雷特停顿了片刻，喘了口气。第二天清晨天刚亮，她就离开了。她带着那根结实的棍子，踏上了旅途，而最后有人见到她的时候，她正朝着南边走去，朝着丰收谷，朝着提克里斯的方向前进。我的父亲则留了下来，抚养我和格温，事情就是这么简单。 从那以后，他就再也没有见过她，也没有听说过她的任何消息，对吧？ 不，没有人知道。就算有人知道，他们也不会告诉我。格温肯定也不知道——他们之所以对我不那么保密，大概是因为我看起来不太像我父亲，反而更像她。加雷特皱着眉头停了下来，思考了一会儿，然后比实际需要的程度更用力地喝了几口酒。关于她，我其实并没有什么具体的记忆，只记得她的脸——一张普通的脸，带着一丝血腥味，但并没有丝毫危险的气息。还有她的手，不知为何放在我的头上……还有那些被积雪覆盖的街道……大概就这些了。比起格温，我或许更关心她的命运，但也不至于希望她能回来。生活总要继续下去的。 确实如此。 关于我妈妈，我就只知道这些了。加雷特哼了一声。你们尽管去调查、去追问吧——也许人们会在你们面前说得更坦诚一些。其实我已经不再在意这些了。那么，想聊点别的吗？ 他在撒谎，很明显，他的谎言非常明显且令人痛苦，但现在逼问他反而会对你们双方都不利。
rows.raw: " Garret raises an eyebrow and sniffs the air. "What's it to you?" It's a mystery floating about town. Garth won't tell you anything about it, Gwyn thinks that she abandoned them but doesn't know anything else, and everyone else in Hawkethorne has their own opinion about where she disappeared to. Maybe he can shed some light on the matter? Garret considers you for a few seconds, then reaches up and scratches his head. "Yeah... about that, truth be told, I don't think I have the whole story about what happened to my mom. I was already up and asking about her the moment I could walk and talk, and it's taken me a lifetime to piece together what I already have. It's like everyone in town who's old enough to have remembered her has had a spell put on them to keep them quiet. Old man Sanders was kind enough to let a few things slip, and I've gleaned some more over the years from the more venerable folk in town, but there're still gaps here and there about her." Huh. So even he doesn't know. "Not everything. Seriously, if you weren't such a good friend to me, I'd have told you to bugger off. Asking about someone else's mum is kinda sorta a private thing, you know." [pc.isDK |Sometimes the hard questions need to be asked, no matter how painful they are. He should know as much. Garret just snorts at that and takes a swig from his tankard. |You're going to beg his pardon for prying, but you're going to pry all the same unless he's going to violently object to such. Garret looks you up and down. "I... don't know about that. Just keep talking for now, and I'll stop you if you start going too far, okay?" That sounds fair, yes. "Good, good." ] So, down to the meat of the matter, then. He might not have the whole picture, but what does he know, then? Upon hearing that, Garret shoots a glance at his father working away behind the bar. Satisfied that Garth appears to be suitably distracted, he leans in close to you and lowers his voice conspiratorially. "She was exiled from Hawkethorne. To be absolutely clear, that means kicked out and told not to come back on pain of death. We're not really big on hangings here, unlike some other places, but exile ranks just below that. The Long Walk, it's called in some of the ancient lupine languages — traditionally, the guilty is given a strip of jerky and a sharp stick, then thrown out onto the snow and ice, never to come back. Every ten years or so someone comes across the frozen body of a long walker, preserved in ice for centuries. It was really popular back in ancient times — execution without actually needing to get one's hands bloody." Wow. "It happened when Gwyn and I were somewhere between four or five years old, from what I've been able to glean from old man Sanders. Up till then, she'd been running the Frost Hound with my old man, trying to get used to serving drinks and making beds after the life the both of them had led up till that point. It wasn't easy, but she was determined to make it work, wanting to die in her bed rather than in a puddle of her own blood. Having children — it tends to change people, although not always for the better. "And then something happened, though. My old man won't talk about it, Sanders says it was a hard choice, and when I ask anyone else they tell me she had to choose the lesser of two evils, and that I shouldn't dig any further. It was a stupid choice she had to make, one of those huge tangled knots, and she tried to unravel it by hand instead of getting a sharp edge and chopping through the whole thing altogether. "Even if she did choose the lesser of two evils, it was enough that the town reluctantly but unanimously chose to send her on the Long Walk. Sanders tells me that if she'd done the alternative, they'd have no choice but to hang her or else make a mockery of law and lore alike." Garret pauses a moment to catch his breath. "She left the next morning at first light. Took the sharp stick and jerky, and the last anyone ever saw of her was that she was heading south towards Harvest Valley, on the road towards Tychris. My old man, he stayed behind to raise Gwyn and me, and that's that." And he's neither seen nor heard nothing of her since? "No. No one has, and even if they had they wouldn't tell me. Gwyn sure as hell doesn't know — the only reason they're less tight-lipped with me is that I apparently look less like my old man and take after her a lot more." Garret stops to think a moment with his brow furrowed, drinks a little more deeply from his tankard than is strictly necessary. "I don't really have any concrete memories of her save for her face. An old brick. The smell of blood, without any danger in it. Her hands on my head, for some reason. The streets, filled with snow. And... that's about it. I might care more about her fate than Gwyn does, but still not enough to hope that she'll ever come back. Life goes on." So it does. "And that's all I know about my mom," Garret grunts. "You're welcome to dig and pry all you want — maybe people will be a little more loose-lipped around you. I don't really care one way or the other any more. So, want to talk about something else?" He's lying, he's painfully and obviously lying, but to press right now would be bad for the both of you."

rows.translation: 母亲

rows.original: [rand |"My mom's hard on me, but I expected her to be," Garret says before taking a swig from his tankard. "I knew exactly what I was getting myself into when I agreed to come up with you to bring her home." Did he, now? "Well, admittedly not exactly, but I did have a pretty good idea, and I got every bit of it good and hard. Mom drives me to the point where I'm exhausted every day, but it's a good kind of exhausted, unlike what the old man used to put me through. That just left me tired and miserable." "Of course, I know it's mostly in the head, like how a pup sent out to shovel snow gets tired pretty quickly, but that same pup can play out in the cold for the whole day without a problem. I'm not meaning to disparage my old man when I'm saying all this, but the fact of the matter is that my Mom clicks with me better than he does. She just gets what I'm thinking, you understand? When I'm in bed at night thinking about it, it's really all about your proper attitude to things; the two really aren't that different, which makes sense given that they were in the same mercenary company together. If it'd been Mom putting me through all this, I think I would've applied myself a lot better when I was a pup." Does he regret his mother being exiled, then? "Eeeeh. She bought us time to have a future in the first place, so while it would've been nice for her to have been with me growing up I know it needed to be done. If it'd been between her and the old man, having my old man go would mean Gwyn would've suffered. Better me than her — I'm better suited to take that kind of pressure than she is. Mom and I are making up for lost time and I've got you to thank for it, so there's no need for you to worry." |"Thanks for bringing Mom home. I mean it." Now then, while the opportunity did come up because of you, he was ultimately the one who was needed to give Gweyr that push she needed to come around to the reality that her job wasn't done and that her family needed her. Garret grins. "Let's say we did it together, then. But yeah... now that Mom's home, I feel like something that's been missing in my life has finally slid back in place. I don't blame my old man for doing his best in raising me and I'm not knocking him or anything for saying this, no matter how mad I might get at him every now and then, but Mom just gets me in a way the old man just doesn't. I like to think it had something to do with what she told me all those years ago when she left..." Any luck remembering exactly what she said? "No. And you know what? Maybe it's better that way. Like the whole strongest man in the world thing..." he takes a swig from his tankard and taps his forehead. "It's all in the head, you know?" No, you don't. "Well, that's all right, so long as Mom and I know what I'm talking about. But once more... thanks for bringing Mom home. I didn't know how much the old man and I needed her until she came back, and now that she is, I feel like she's been here forever. Like part of Mom stayed behind in the place that she built, yeah?" He gestures about him at the Hound. "Shit, I'm getting all sappy and romantic. Anyways, thanks again." |"Ever since Mom came back, I feel like I have a goal in life now. Well, I guess I had that before, given that my old man wanted me to run the Hound once he passed, now that my silly puppy of a sister has her own thing going. But this is a goal that I can actually feel excited about, can look forward to." Being part of a mercenary company? "It's more than that. It's something that my grandfather started up, something that she ran for a while... I want to hear what other people have to say about her that aren't, well, you know." He waves his tankard about. "There's the excitement, and then the feeling that finally there's someplace in the world that was made for me." Look, it's good to be enthusiastic about Gweyr's arrangements to get him ahead in life, but he ought to make sure that his expectations are going to be realistic and he's not going to be getting in over his head. "Why does everyone keep on telling me that? I know full well I'm being sent off to the Belharan Heartland. Given that it was where the worst brunt of the Godswar was fought two hundred years ago, that's undoubtedly the most dangerous place in the world to date. And you know what the most dangerous place in the world desperately needs? Its strongest man, that's what. Any mercenary company's that survives working those fields, they've got to be as tough as nails and surely ask no less of their recruits." "It's funny how everyone else is just assuming I'm excited about this because I don't know the dangers involved. Well, I'm excited because I do know full well the dangers involved. I get that the old man wanted Gwyn and I to have a better life than he did, and that may work for my silly little puppy of a sister... but it's not for me. Mom understands that, and that's why everything has just clicked since then. She didn't fear death when she was my age... and I'm not going to, either. Be aware of it, be mindful of the possibility, be respectful of those others who've come before you and fallen to it... but not fear it." |"The old man looks more at peace now that Mom's home. I wouldn't put it on him to be happy in front of me, but at least he doesn't look like he's got a weight on his shoulders all the time." Really? Well, Garth might be a bit gruff and taciturn at times, but otherwise he's been pretty okay with you. "Yeah well, you're not his family, nor do you have to live with him." Garret sighs and takes a swig from his tankard. "No, he hasn't stopped being hard on me, but I think the weight of what he's done — what he was doing behind the backs of me and my little puppy sister — is finally lifted. I know that when I get to be his age, I don't want that kind of millstone hanging about my neck and dragging me down everywhere I go." He doesn't sound angry at the fact that Garth kept the fact that his mother was alive from him all these years, that he was seeing Gweyr outside the town every few months or so...? Garret thinks a moment, then rubs his brow. "I suppose there might be cause for that, but what would be the point, really? I mean, seriously, [pc.name], what would be achieved by getting mad at the old man? I get where he was coming from, I disagreed with him, I gave him a yelling-to. That's about it. "Besides, the strongest man in the world's too busy being who he is to hold grudges like that. I've got other things to work towards to and don't have the energy to waste staying mad at him. Just going to keep in mind to never be that much of a coward and move on from there." Hmm... "Look, [pc.name]. The old man wasn't always right, but I guess he tried to do right by me and my silly little puppy of a sister. That he wasn't perfect in doing so was reprehensible, but still human after that manner of speaking. I've come to terms with the fact that this is the ending he probably deserves for the rest of his life, and that's just fine. Mom'll take care of him, there's no need for me to be mad." |"It's a little strange how people just got used to seeing Mom around the place. I get it, the Hound is where out-of-towners come, and almost everyone who'd any reason to hold a grudge against her left long ago. Still, having everyone just accept that the old man had a wife way back, and for some strange reason she's back and around the place — no one's so much as batted an eye or asked an inconvenient question." You don't mind having Gweyr around, but then again you're in a unique position in which to appreciate all of this. But given all the good that Garth's done for Hawkethorne up to this day, you can see why people would be trusting enough of him to not ask any questions about a long-lost wife who's recently returned. Folks are smart enough to know it would be awkward. "Yeah, that's the thing. I wouldn't make the questions inconvenient, but they'd be asked nevertheless. Like, back when Gwyn was pregnant for the first time, so many tongues were wagging about how either the old man or I must've been the one to do it. He's what passes for the local alderman, and so you can't help but expect that people talk about him. But now that Mom's back, I haven't heard any of the talk that I'd have expected to accompany it. Weird, huh?" Now that he puts it that way... you do suppose it does bear consideration. "I know, right? I tried to ask Mom about it, and all she'd say was that she'd had a lifetime of learning how to stay unnoticed no matter where she went, if it came to that, and it was something I'd eventually pick up if I didn't get myself killed first. Sounds like a lot of fun, to be honest." ]
rows.translation: [rand |我妈妈对我很严格，但我早就预料到会这样，”加雷特一边说，一边大口喝着他的酒杯。“当我同意帮你把她带回家时，我就清楚自己会面临什么。” 他真的这么认为吗？ “嗯，老实说，我当时并没有完全想清楚。正是如此不过我确实有一个相当不错的主意，而且我也竭尽全力去实现它。妈妈每天开车送我，让我累得精疲力尽，但这种疲惫是好事，和那个老头以前让我经历的那些痛苦完全不同。那种经历只会让我感到疲惫和痛苦。当然，我知道这很大程度上只是心理作用——就像那些被派去铲雪的小狗很快就会感到疲惫，但同样的小狗却可以在寒冷的天气里玩上一整天而毫无问题。我说这些并不是要贬低我的父亲，但事实就是，我妈妈和我之间的默契比他和我的要好得多。她只是获得我的意思是，你明白我的意思吧？每晚躺在床上思考这个问题时，我真正想说的是，关键在于你对这些事情的态度；其实这两者并没有太大的区别，这也合情合理，毕竟他们曾经同属一家雇佣兵公司。如果这些都是妈妈让我经历的，我想在我还小的时候，我一定会更加努力地学习。” 那么，他是否后悔自己的母亲被流放了呢？ “嗯……她当初为我们争取到了未来的机会，所以虽然她能在我成长过程中陪伴在我身边会很好，但我知道那样做是必要的。如果这件事是在她和那个老人之间发生，让我的父亲离开的话，格温肯定会受到伤害。让我来承受这种压力总比让她受苦要好——我比她更适合面对这样的处境。我和妈妈正在弥补过去失去的时间，而这一切都要归功于你，所以你完全没有必要担心。" |谢谢你把妈妈带回家，我是真心这么说的。” 那么，既然有了这个机会确实这一切都是因为你，最终还是他起到了关键作用，他让格维尔终于意识到自己的工作还没有完成，她的家人也需要她。 加雷特笑了：“那么，就当是我们一起做到的吧。不过，现在妈妈回来了，我感觉生活中那些曾经缺失的东西终于又回到了应有的位置。我并不责怪我的父亲，他确实已经尽了最大的努力来抚养我。虽然我偶尔会生他的气，但说这些话并不是为了指责他什么。只是，妈妈……她真的很重要。得到在某种程度上，我和那个老人是不同的。我觉得这可能与多年前她离开时对我说过的话有关…… 你还记得她当时具体说了什么吗？ “不，想不起来了。你知道吗？也许那样反而更好。就像“世界上最强的人”这种说法……”他喝了一口大酒杯里的酒，然后敲了敲自己的额头，“其实这一切都只是心理作用罢了，你懂的吧？” 不，你并不懂。 “不过没关系，只要我和妈妈明白自己在说什么就行了。但是，还是要再次感谢你把妈妈带回了家。在妈妈回来之前，我根本不知道我和那位老人是多么需要她；而现在她回来了，我感觉她仿佛一直都在我们身边。就好像妈妈的某一部分，永远留在了她曾经生活过的那个地方，对吧？他指了指身边的那条猎犬，说道：“该死，我怎么突然变得这么多愁善感、浪漫起来了呢。总之，还是再次感谢你吧。 |自从妈妈回来之后，我觉得自己的人生终于有了目标。其实，之前我也应该有这样的目标吧——毕竟我爸爸希望他去世后我能接手‘猎犬俱乐部’的管理工作，而我那个傻乎乎的妹妹也有了自己的人生规划。但这一次，我真的对这个目标感到兴奋，也真心期待它的实现。 加入一支雇佣兵队伍？ “其实远不止如此。这是我祖父创立的事业，后来她也曾经负责管理它一段时间……我想听听其他人对她的评价，那些不是你所说的那种评价。”他挥了挥手中的酒杯，“那种兴奋感，还有那种终于找到属于自己的归宿的感受…… 你看，为帮助格维尔在生活中取得成功而热心为他安排各种机会固然很好，但他也必须确保自己的期望是现实的，以免让自己陷入过度努力的困境。 为什么大家都一直这么告诉我？我非常清楚，我被派往的是贝尔哈兰心脏地带。毕竟两百年前，神战的最惨烈战斗就是在那里发生的，所以那里无疑是目前世界上最危险的地方。你知道这个世界上最危险的地方最迫切需要什么吗？它需要最坚强的人，就是这样的。任何能够在那些恶劣环境中生存下来的雇佣兵组织，他们的成员肯定都坚如磐石，而对于新招募的人，他们也会提出同样的要求。" 有趣的是，其他人都以为我之所以对此感到兴奋，只是因为我还不知道其中隐藏的危险。其实，我之所以兴奋，是因为我确实非常清楚其中的危险。我明白那位老人希望我和格温能够过上比他更美好的生活，这对我那个天真无邪的妹妹来说或许适用……但对我来说并不合适。妈妈明白这一点，正因为如此，从那以后一切才变得顺理成章。她在我这个年纪时并不害怕死亡……而我也不会害怕。要意识到这种可能性，要尊重那些在你们之前就已经面对死亡的人……但不要害怕它。 |现在妈妈回来了，那位老人看起来安详多了。我真不希望他再经历那些开心就在我面前，不过至少他看起来不会总是肩负着沉重的负担。” 真的吗？嗯，虽然加斯有时候会显得有点粗鲁和沉默寡言，但除此之外，他对你的态度还算不错。 是啊，你又不是他的家人，也没必要和他住在一起。”加雷特叹了口气，喝了一大口酒。“虽然他依然对我很严厉，但我觉得他那些背着我以及我妹妹做的事情所带来的压力，终于消散了。我知道，等到我到了他那个年纪，我可不想让这样的负担一直压在我的脖子上，让我无论走到哪里都感到沉重。” 他听起来并没有因为加斯这些年来一直瞒着他母亲还活着，也没有因为加斯每隔几个月就会去镇外见格维尔而感到生气…… 加雷特思考了一会儿，然后揉了揉额头：“我想加斯这么做可能有他的原因，但究竟意义何在呢？说真的[pc.name]，对那个老人发火又能有什么好处呢？我理解他的立场，但我并不认同他的观点，所以我只是对他大声吼了一声而已，也就仅此而已。 “再说，世界上最强的人根本没时间去记恨这种小事。我还有其他更重要的事情要去做，没有精力浪费在对他生气上。我只会记住，以后不要再那么懦弱，继续向前看就是了。” 嗯…… “听着[pc.name]那位老人并不总是正确的，但我想他确实是尽力照顾我和我那个傻乎乎的妹妹的。虽然他在这些事情上做得并不完美，但这也只能说明他是个人而已。我已经接受了这样一个事实：对于他余下的生命来说，这样的结局或许正是他应得的，而这也完全没问题。妈妈会照顾他的，我完全没有必要生气。 |人们竟然已经习惯了看到妈妈在这个地方出现，这确实有点奇怪。我明白，这里本来就是外来者会聚集的地方，而且那些本来有理由对她怀有怨恨的人，早就离开了。不过，大家都就这么接受了这个事实：那个老人很久以前确实有过妻子，而出于某种奇怪的原因，她又回到了这里——竟然没有人对此表示怀疑，也没有人提出任何尴尬的问题。你并不介意让格维尔留在身边，毕竟你处于一个能够理解这一切的特殊位置。但考虑到加思至今为鹰棘镇所做的所有好事，人们自然会足够信任他，而不会对这位刚刚归来的失踪已久的妻子产生任何疑虑。大家都很聪明，知道那样做会显得很尴尬。 “没错，问题就在这里。我本来也不会提出那些问题的。不方便不过，人们还是会问起这些事情。就像当初格温第一次怀孕的时候，有很多人都在猜测，到底是那位老人还是我做了那件事。他在这里算是当地的权威人物，所以人们谈论他也是情有可原的。但是现在妈妈回来了，我却一点也没有听到那些我原本以为会随之而来的议论。真是奇怪，对吧？” 现在他这么一说……确实值得考虑一下。 “我懂的，对吧？我试着向妈妈询问这件事，但她只是说，她这一生都在学习如何无论走到哪里都能不被人注意到。如果真到了那种地步，她说我最终也会学会这个本领的——前提是别先被杀掉。说实话，听起来真的很有趣。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"My mom's hard on me, but I expected her to be," Garret says before taking a swig from his tankard. "I knew exactly what I was getting myself into when I agreed to come up with you to bring her home." Did he, now? "Well, admittedly not exactly, but I did have a pretty good idea, and I got every bit of it good and hard. Mom drives me to the point where I'm exhausted every day, but it's a good kind of exhausted, unlike what the old man used to put me through. That just left me tired and miserable." "Of course, I know it's mostly in the head, like how a pup sent out to shovel snow gets tired pretty quickly, but that same pup can play out in the cold for the whole day without a problem. I'm not meaning to disparage my old man when I'm saying all this, but the fact of the matter is that my Mom clicks with me better than he does. She just gets what I'm thinking, you understand? When I'm in bed at night thinking about it, it's really all about your proper attitude to things; the two really aren't that different, which makes sense given that they were in the same mercenary company together. If it'd been Mom putting me through all this, I think I would've applied myself a lot better when I was a pup." Does he regret his mother being exiled, then? "Eeeeh. She bought us time to have a future in the first place, so while it would've been nice for her to have been with me growing up I know it needed to be done. If it'd been between her and the old man, having my old man go would mean Gwyn would've suffered. Better me than her — I'm better suited to take that kind of pressure than she is. Mom and I are making up for lost time and I've got you to thank for it, so there's no need for you to worry." |"Thanks for bringing Mom home. I mean it." Now then, while the opportunity did come up because of you, he was ultimately the one who was needed to give Gweyr that push she needed to come around to the reality that her job wasn't done and that her family needed her. Garret grins. "Let's say we did it together, then. But yeah... now that Mom's home, I feel like something that's been missing in my life has finally slid back in place. I don't blame my old man for doing his best in raising me and I'm not knocking him or anything for saying this, no matter how mad I might get at him every now and then, but Mom just gets me in a way the old man just doesn't. I like to think it had something to do with what she told me all those years ago when she left..." Any luck remembering exactly what she said? "No. And you know what? Maybe it's better that way. Like the whole strongest man in the world thing..." he takes a swig from his tankard and taps his forehead. "It's all in the head, you know?" No, you don't. "Well, that's all right, so long as Mom and I know what I'm talking about. But once more... thanks for bringing Mom home. I didn't know how much the old man and I needed her until she came back, and now that she is, I feel like she's been here forever. Like part of Mom stayed behind in the place that she built, yeah?" He gestures about him at the Hound. "Shit, I'm getting all sappy and romantic. Anyways, thanks again." |"Ever since Mom came back, I feel like I have a goal in life now. Well, I guess I had that before, given that my old man wanted me to run the Hound once he passed, now that my silly puppy of a sister has her own thing going. But this is a goal that I can actually feel excited about, can look forward to." Being part of a mercenary company? "It's more than that. It's something that my grandfather started up, something that she ran for a while... I want to hear what other people have to say about her that aren't, well, you know." He waves his tankard about. "There's the excitement, and then the feeling that finally there's someplace in the world that was made for me." Look, it's good to be enthusiastic about Gweyr's arrangements to get him ahead in life, but he ought to make sure that his expectations are going to be realistic and he's not going to be getting in over his head. "Why does everyone keep on telling me that? I know full well I'm being sent off to the Belharan Heartland. Given that it was where the worst brunt of the Godswar was fought two hundred years ago, that's undoubtedly the most dangerous place in the world to date. And you know what the most dangerous place in the world desperately needs? Its strongest man, that's what. Any mercenary company's that survives working those fields, they've got to be as tough as nails and surely ask no less of their recruits." "It's funny how everyone else is just assuming I'm excited about this because I don't know the dangers involved. Well, I'm excited because I do know full well the dangers involved. I get that the old man wanted Gwyn and I to have a better life than he did, and that may work for my silly little puppy of a sister... but it's not for me. Mom understands that, and that's why everything has just clicked since then. She didn't fear death when she was my age... and I'm not going to, either. Be aware of it, be mindful of the possibility, be respectful of those others who've come before you and fallen to it... but not fear it." |"The old man looks more at peace now that Mom's home. I wouldn't put it on him to be happy in front of me, but at least he doesn't look like he's got a weight on his shoulders all the time." Really? Well, Garth might be a bit gruff and taciturn at times, but otherwise he's been pretty okay with you. "Yeah well, you're not his family, nor do you have to live with him." Garret sighs and takes a swig from his tankard. "No, he hasn't stopped being hard on me, but I think the weight of what he's done — what he was doing behind the backs of me and my little puppy sister — is finally lifted. I know that when I get to be his age, I don't want that kind of millstone hanging about my neck and dragging me down everywhere I go." He doesn't sound angry at the fact that Garth kept the fact that his mother was alive from him all these years, that he was seeing Gweyr outside the town every few months or so...? Garret thinks a moment, then rubs his brow. "I suppose there might be cause for that, but what would be the point, really? I mean, seriously, [pc.name], what would be achieved by getting mad at the old man? I get where he was coming from, I disagreed with him, I gave him a yelling-to. That's about it. "Besides, the strongest man in the world's too busy being who he is to hold grudges like that. I've got other things to work towards to and don't have the energy to waste staying mad at him. Just going to keep in mind to never be that much of a coward and move on from there." Hmm... "Look, [pc.name]. The old man wasn't always right, but I guess he tried to do right by me and my silly little puppy of a sister. That he wasn't perfect in doing so was reprehensible, but still human after that manner of speaking. I've come to terms with the fact that this is the ending he probably deserves for the rest of his life, and that's just fine. Mom'll take care of him, there's no need for me to be mad." |"It's a little strange how people just got used to seeing Mom around the place. I get it, the Hound is where out-of-towners come, and almost everyone who'd any reason to hold a grudge against her left long ago. Still, having everyone just accept that the old man had a wife way back, and for some strange reason she's back and around the place — no one's so much as batted an eye or asked an inconvenient question." You don't mind having Gweyr around, but then again you're in a unique position in which to appreciate all of this. But given all the good that Garth's done for Hawkethorne up to this day, you can see why people would be trusting enough of him to not ask any questions about a long-lost wife who's recently returned. Folks are smart enough to know it would be awkward. "Yeah, that's the thing. I wouldn't make the questions inconvenient, but they'd be asked nevertheless. Like, back when Gwyn was pregnant for the first time, so many tongues were wagging about how either the old man or I must've been the one to do it. He's what passes for the local alderman, and so you can't help but expect that people talk about him. But now that Mom's back, I haven't heard any of the talk that I'd have expected to accompany it. Weird, huh?" Now that he puts it that way... you do suppose it does bear consideration. "I know, right? I tried to ask Mom about it, and all she'd say was that she'd had a lifetime of learning how to stay unnoticed no matter where she went, if it came to that, and it was something I'd eventually pick up if I didn't get myself killed first. Sounds like a lot of fun, to be honest." ]"

rows.translation: 格维尔

rows.original: "It's not so much 'wanting to go out and see the world'," Garret grumbles, showing you his teeth. "That sort of stupid shit's for idiot farmboys who think that it's all going to be fun and games. Those idiots wind up dead, too, more often than not." You settle in and brace yourself for the tirade you know's coming. "Do you know what it's like living in the shadow of an old man like mine? Everyone treats you like you're a smaller, broken version of him. As if you were..." Garret stops and thinks for a moment, searching for the right word, and rolling over the syllables when he does find it. "Defective, that's the word. That's what they were thinking. No one ever said it out loud, of course, but I could see it behind their eyes, their gazes. 'How good is he compared to Garth?' 'Not good enough.' The only other person who didn't treat me that way was Gwyn. I got sick of it, started to spend as much time as I could out in the woods." Maybe he's just insecure, but you're not going to tell him that to his face. That'd just make things worse. "Going back and forth, being known as 'Garth's son'; I think the only local who wasn't family to call me by name was old man Sanders. Anyone else, it's 'Garth's son.' Neighbour looks over the fence while I'm butchering a hog, 'hey, Garth's son, how's your old man?' 'Oh look, it's Garth's pup. You want a pound of flour?' 'You've got a good set of chopping arms there. Almost as good as your father's.' Everywhere, every time. "I know they don't mean anything by it, but being constantly measured up against my old man gets tiring after a while. Like I mentioned before, I'm just a defective version of him in peoples' eyes. Not as smart. Not as strong. Without the fine attention to detail. Doesn't pour drinks fast enough. Just a lazy little brat, not as hardworking as his father. And they wonder why I head out to the woods once I've finished the tasks my old man's set me for the day." Garret takes another swig of alcohol and wipes his mouth with the back of his hand. He looks you up and down a few times, studying your expression, then shrugs. "That's why I'm saying I'm the strongest man in the world. It's not just something I'm aiming for — you know how they say if you repeat a lie long enough, you start believing it? And then when you start believing it, wearing that mask for long enough, you can work towards being the mask? Going out —" Garret hiccups, his breath smelling heavily of alcohol — "Excuse me, going out and being more than just a mercenary like my old man was —" So, what exactly is he trying to prove here? Garret answers without hesitation. "That I don't have to live in my old man's shadow forever." You turn your gaze towards Garth at the bar. The old wolf is busily wiping away at one of his many mugs with a cloth, definitely and most pointedly not looking in your direction. "Oh, of course he doesn't like it. He built the Frost Hound so that I wouldn't have to do what he did for a living and could have a good, easy life as a tavernkeeper." Garret smiles bitterly and points to himself. "Do I look like the kind of person who settles for that in his youth? Ha ha, of course not. I understand, perhaps even respect my old man's sentiments, but I've already had a lifetime's worth of 'Garth's pup.' Fifty more years of such really doesn't appeal to me, for some strange reason." He'll have to put in a lot of work to surpass his father, then. "Don't think I don't know that. Why do you think I'm such a tryhard? Was doing just that when you had to step in and save me from Westbank." He shakes his head and heaves a sigh. "I hate to admit it when he's right, but I have to admit it all the same. Come on, [pc.name], let's find something cheerier to talk about than this."
rows.translation: 与其说是因为‘想要出去看看这个世界’，不如说是别的原因。加雷特嘟囔着，露出了他的牙齿。那种愚蠢的行为，只会让那些以为一切都会很有趣、很轻松的乡巴佬送命。而那些傻瓜，最终死去的概率往往很高。 你坐下来，做好心理准备，迎接那场你早已预料到的长篇大论。 你知道生活在像我这样的老人的阴影之下是什么感觉吗？每个人都会把你当作他的缩小版、残缺的复制品来看待。就好像你……加雷特停了下来，思考了片刻，试图找到合适的词语，当终于想出这个词时，他仔细地斟酌着每一个音节。有缺陷，就是这个意思。他们都是这么想的。当然，没人会把这种想法说出来，但我能从他们的目光中看出来。‘他和加斯相比，到底有多强？’‘还不够强。’唯一没有这样看待我的人，就是格温。我受够了这种态度，于是开始尽可能多地待在森林里。 也许他只是缺乏安全感，但你不会当面跟他说这一点。那样只会让事情变得更糟。 人们总是这么称呼我，叫‘加斯的儿子’；我想，唯一一个不会用我的名字来称呼我的本地人，就是桑德斯老人了。其他人，都会叫我‘加斯的儿子’。比如，当我正在宰猪的时候，邻居会隔着篱笆对我说：‘嘿，加斯的儿子，你父亲最近怎么样？’或者‘哦，看，那是加斯的儿子吧。需要一磅面粉吗？’还有‘你的砍刀使得真熟练啊，几乎和你父亲一样好。’无论在哪里，每次都是这样。 我知道他们这么说并没有什么恶意，但总是被拿来和我的父亲作比较，确实会让人感到疲惫。就像我之前说的，在别人眼里，我只不过是他有缺陷的版本——不够聪明，不够强壮，也没有他那种细致入微的态度，倒酒的速度也不够快，就是个懒惰的小鬼，不如他父亲那么勤奋。所以，当我完成了父亲当天安排给我的任务后，他们才会好奇我为什么要去树林里。 加雷特又喝了一口酒，然后用手掌背擦了擦嘴。他上下打量了你几眼，仔细观察你的表情，然后耸了耸肩。 这就是为什么我说自己是世界上最强的人。这不仅仅是我追求的目标——你知道人们常说，如果一个谎言被反复重复足够长的时间，人们就会开始相信它。而当你真正开始相信这个谎言，长时间戴着这个面具生活时，你就有可能真的变成那个面具所代表的那个人。走出去——加勒不停地打嗝，他的呼吸中弥漫着浓重的酒精气味—— 打扰一下，我想走出一条不同于我父亲那样仅仅只是个雇佣兵的道路…… 那么，他究竟想证明什么呢？ 加雷特毫不犹豫地回答道。我不想永远活在父亲的阴影之下。 你的目光转向酒吧里的加斯。那只老狼正忙着用布擦拭他那些杯子中的一个，动作十分专注，也显得格外明显。不是正朝你的方向看去。 哦，他当然不喜欢这样。他制造出霜犬酒馆，就是为了让我不必像他那样以打猎为生，而是能够过上安稳、轻松的酒馆老板生活。加雷特苦涩地笑了笑，然后指了指自己。我看起来像那种在年轻时会满足于那种生活的人吗？哈哈，当然不是。我理解，甚至可能尊重我父亲的感受，但我已经过了足够长的一生，一直被称为‘加斯的小狗’。再过五十年，这样的情况还会继续真的出于某种奇怪的原因，我并不觉得它有吸引力。 那么，他必须付出大量的努力才能超越他的父亲。 别以为我不知道。你以为我为什么非要这么拼命呢？当初你在西岸银行救我的时候，我也在做同样的事。他摇了摇头，叹了口气。虽然很不愿意承认，但当他说得对的时候，我还是不得不承认。拜托，[pc.name]，让我们找些更开心的事情来聊吧，而不是这个。

rows.original: "Heh. You want me to introduce you to them?" Getting to know more of the locals is always good, yes. But you're just saying this because he seems to stick with his folks all the time. Family is important, yes, but so is the rest of Hawkethorne. "How about I introduce you to some folks from out of town?" That would work just as well, you suppose. He has someone in mind, you suppose? "Yeah, I know a lady by the name of Anna, lives out in Harvest Valley. She's got a sister — half-lupine by the name of Morwen; they run a farm like most people who live out there. That's why it's called Harvest Valley, after all. Good people, salt of the earth and all that. Haven't actually been around to visit them since the blizzard and all this craziness started... and ever since I got back from Westbank, my old man's been keeping me on a really tight leash. Haven't had the chance to go down and check on them." That gives you an idea. Why don't you go down and make sure they're okay? Garret eyes you. "You mean it?" [pc.dcb|Well, of course. Would you ever just run your mouth off to him like that without meaning it?|Yeah, you do. It's part of your job, after all.|Well, like, duh. There're plenty of fun things to be had on farms. Why would you not want to go and miss out on everything?] "Yeah, yeah." Garret scratches the back of his head sheepishly. "I didn't mean to say it like I distrust you or anything, but I've known Anna and Morwen for years now. Wouldn't want you going out to have a look-see, then forgetting all about it until the next time you showed up here. Frankly speaking, I've been in a half-mind for a while now to just sneak out of town and check in on them, even if it meant I'd catch hell from my old man..." He really cares quite a lot about those two, doesn't he? Garret huffs. "Anna helped out my old man and me when I was younger. We owe a lot to her, and she us. To say that I give a shit about the lady and her land is a pretty big understatement." You get as much. Next time you're in Harvest Valley, you'll drop by their farmstead and tell them Garret said hi. "Thanks. Let me tell you how to get there." The directions Garret gives you are clear and concise — which shouldn't be a surprise given the circumstances, even if he is a meathead. A few minutes later, you feel confident in following those landmarks to Anna's farmstead down in Harvest Valley. "And that's that. Thanks again. Anything else you need me for?"
rows.translation: 呵呵，你是想让我帮你介绍他们吗？ 多了解一些当地人确实总是有益的，没错。但你这么说只是因为那个人似乎总是和家人待在一起。家庭确实很重要，但鹰棘镇的其他方面也同样重要。 我给你介绍一些来自外地的人怎么样？ 我想，那样做也应该效果不错吧。他心里肯定有某个人选，对吧？ 是啊，我认识一位名叫安娜的女士，她住在收获谷。她还有一个妹妹，名叫莫文，有一半狼的血统；她们和那里的大多数人一样，经营着农场。毕竟，那个地方才被称为收获谷嘛。她们都是很好的人，真正意义上的善良之辈。自从暴风雪和那些混乱的事情发生之后，我就再也没机会去拜访她们了……而且自从我从西岸回来后，我父亲就一直严格限制我的行动，所以我也没有机会再去看看她们。 这样你应该能明白了吧。为什么不下去看看他们是否没事呢？ 加雷特注视着你。你是认真的吗？ [pc.dcb|嗯，当然不会。你难道会无缘无故地那样对他喋喋不休吗？|是的，这是你的工作职责之一。毕竟，这是你工作内容的一部分。|嗯，就是，这还用说吗？在农场里有很多有趣的事情可以去做。你为什么不是想错过所有这些机会吗？] 是啊，是啊。加雷特尴尬地挠了挠后脑勺。我这么说并不是因为不信任你，其实我和安娜、莫琳已经认识很多年了。我只是觉得，你如果去看看他们，之后可能会把这件事忘得一干二净，直到下次再见到他们的时候才想起来。说实话，我也有段时间一直在考虑偷偷离开小镇去看看他们，哪怕因此会惹恼我的父亲…… 他真的非常关心那两个人，不是吗？ 加雷特哼了一声。在我年轻的时候，安娜帮助过我和我的父亲。我们欠她很多，她也同样欠我们很多。如果说我对这位女士和她的土地毫不在意，那简直是一种轻描淡写的说法。 你想要多少就拿多少吧。下次你去收获谷的时候，顺便去他们的农场看看，告诉他们加雷特向他们问好了。 谢谢。让我来告诉您怎么去那里吧。 加雷特给你的指示非常清晰简洁——考虑到当时的情况，这一点也不足为奇，尽管他是一个笨蛋。几分钟后，你便有信心沿着那些地标找到位于丰收谷的安娜的农场了。 就这样吧。再次感谢。还有其他需要我帮忙的事情吗？

rows.original: [garret.fucked |"Why?" Garret flashes you one of his trademark winning grins — which, alas, is not very much so. Top marks for effort, though. "Do you like it that much?" You don't know about that, but now that he's mentioned it, you can't help but imagine yourself leaning into Garret, running your fingers down the stiff white fur that sprouts from its ragged edges, feeling for the broad, powerful chest beneath — "Hey, if you want to do that kind of thing, go do it where people can't see you. As much fun as it is to have other people drool over me, I'd rather not have it done in public — especially when my old man's watching. He knows a thing or two about how attractive scars can be when they're in the right places." Oh, you're sure he does. But go on — how did Garret come by this thing at so young an age, anyway? |"Huh." Now that his attention has been drawn to it, Garret self-consciously fingers the ragged end of his scar through his collar. "Guess there's no hiding this thing, is there?" It kind of sticks out where his collar meets his shoulder, yes. And even if his shirt covered it completely, there's the fact that you've already seen him in the nude once. "Yeah..." Garret waves a hand in the air that's neither here nor there. "I'd rather not talk about that. Kinda embarrassing." You can see why, especially when it's someone like him. If he doesn't want to discuss that, then why not how he got that scar? ] "Yeah, it's a long story." Garret sets down his mug and scratches his chin. "Handful of years back there now — think I must've been no more than twelve summers when it happened. It was back down at Anna's estate in Harvest Valley — did I ever tell you about her?" [flags.GARRET_FROSTHOUND_FRIENDS_TALK |Yeah, he did. "Right. |No, not really. "Then remind me to tell you about her and her sister sometime.] In any case, I was down in the fields that day, messing with the cowgirls. Morwen and I were playing prey while my old man and Anna were discussing what was the best price for a sackful of hops. Have you ever been in a really tall grassland? The wheat was almost up to my shoulders, so it was kind of like that; even at the edge of the fields, it was pretty hard to see very far — which made it perfect for playing in. "Don't know when the thing snuck up on me, but when I turned, it was there. Some horrible furry clawed thing, no doubt out of the mountains. How it'd wandered into Harvest Valley and right smack in Anna's fields, I'm not sure, but there it was. "Morwen might have screamed, I don't know. It all gets a little hazy from there. I know I ran and grabbed the nearest thing at hand — a plowshare left standing by the fence — and headed straight for it." He did what? He said he was only twelve! Garret shrugs. "I don't know how to describe it. It felt right, like I was made to do this, you know? I don't think I was thinking, wasn't time for that. Either way, I brought the blade down on its face, and cut it open. That only pissed the thing off, and it took a swipe at me; I parried the blow with the plowshare's handle, but didn't have the strength to stand up against it. The blade buckled in and caught me on the chest just like this." As if for emphasis, Garret traces a fingertip along the line of his scar. You see. "It didn't hurt, not right then; just made me angrier. Morwen definitely screamed then, and Anna and my old man came running. They yelled at me to get away, but I wasn't having any of that. It wasn't as if the blade had sunk that deep, so I pulled it out of me and gave the monster another swipe. Caught it between the eyes that time and brained it. Felt really, really good." "That's also when I heard my old man compare me to my mom for the first time." What happened next? "I..." You can see Garret working to dredge up the memories. "Could have been Anna, could have been my old man, someone came up and took the plowshare out of my hands while the other dragged me back to the homestead. Morwen got me a leather bit to bite down on, and sewed up the gash as best as she could, along with some stinking poultice. I know, the wound could've gotten infected, I could've died. But I didn't. She says it was pretty bad, that she could see my ribs in places, but I'm not quite sure I believe that. It sure didn't feel like it, at any rate." Aaand... Garret shrugs. "And that's all. If you go down to Anna's, ask her to show you the cloak she made out of the creature's pelt. We've asked most people what it might be, but even the centaurs have no idea. Pretty warm, though. "So, anything else you want to talk about?"
rows.translation: [garret.fucked |为什么？加雷特露出了他那标志性的、看似能赢得胜利的微笑——不过，说实话，其实并没有那么令人信服。不过，他的这份努力还是值得肯定的。你真的这么喜欢它吗？ 你可能之前并不知道这件事，但既然他提到了，你就不由得会想象自己靠在加雷特的身上，用手指轻轻抚摸着他那从破烂边缘延伸出来的坚硬白色毛发，同时感受着他身后那宽厚而强健的胸膛 嘿，如果你想这么做的话那个这种事情，还是去别人看不到的地方做吧。虽然让别人对我垂涎三尺也挺有趣的，但我还是不愿意在公共场合发生这种事——尤其是当我爸爸在看的时候。他很清楚，如果疤痕长在合适的位置，也会显得很有魅力。 哦，你确定他是这么做的。但继续说吧——毕竟，加雷特在这么年轻的时候是怎么得到这个东西的？ |嗯。现在他的注意力已经被吸引了过来，加雷特下意识地用手指穿过领口，触碰着自己疤痕那参差不齐的边缘。看来这件事已经藏不住了，不是吗？ 确实，他的衣领与肩膀相接的地方有点显眼。而且，即使他的衬衫完全遮住了那个部位，你毕竟已经见过他裸体的样子了。 是啊……加雷特随意地挥了挥手，那动作显得既不在这里，也不在那里。我宁愿不谈这个，有点尴尬。 你就能明白为什么了，尤其是当对方是像他这样的人。如果他不愿意谈论那个话题，那么为什么不聊聊他是怎么留下那道伤疤的呢？ ] 嗯，这是个漫长的故事。加雷特放下杯子，挠了挠下巴。那是很多年前的事了——我想当时我应该还不到十二岁。事情发生的时候，我们正在丰收谷的安娜庄园里——我之前有没有跟你说过她的事？ [flags.GARRET_FROSTHOUND_FRIENDS_TALK |是的，他这么做了。 好的。 |不，其实并不是这样。 到时候再提醒我告诉你关于她和她妹妹的事情吧。]总之，那天我正在田野里和那些女牛仔们一起玩耍。我和莫文在扮演猎物和捕猎者的角色，而我的父亲和安娜则在讨论一袋啤酒花能卖个好价钱。你有没有去过那种长满高草的草原？那里的麦苗几乎有我的肩膀那么高了，环境就是那样的；即使在田野的边缘，也很难看得很远——这样的环境简直太适合玩耍了。 我不知道那东西是什么时候悄悄出现在我面前的，但当我转过身时，它就已经在那里了。那是一种长着可怕爪子的毛茸茸生物，毫无疑问是来自山里的。我也不知道它是怎么跑到丰收谷，然后正好出现在安娜的田地里的，但事实就是，它就在那里。 莫文可能发出了尖叫，我也不确定了。从那之后，一切就变得有些模糊不清了。我只记得自己跑过去，抓起了手边最方便用的东西——一把放在篱笆旁的犁头——然后直接朝着那个方向冲了出去。 他做到了。什么他说他才十二岁而已！” 加雷特耸了耸肩。我实在不知道该如何描述这种感觉。就是觉得这样做很对，仿佛我生来就是为了做这件事的。当时我根本没时间去思考，也没那个心思。总之，我挥动刀刃砍向它的脸，把它划开了。但这反而让它更加愤怒，它朝我扑了过来；我用犁把挡住了那一击，但却没有足够的力气来抵抗它。刀刃弯曲了，就这样刺中了我的胸口。 仿佛是为了强调这一点，加雷特用指尖轻轻触摸着自己疤痕的轮廓。 “你看到了吧。 当时并没有感到疼痛，只是让我更加愤怒而已。莫尔文肯定当时尖叫了起来，安娜和我的父亲也跑了过来。他们冲我大喊，让我离开，但我根本不听他们的。毕竟那把刀并没有真正刺中我那个太深了，所以我使出了全力，再次朝那只怪物挥击。这次正好击中了它的双眼，把它击晕了。那种感觉真的非常棒。 就在那个时候，我第一次听到我父亲将我和我的母亲相提并论。 接下来发生了什么？ 我……你可以看到加雷特正在努力回忆那些往事。本来可能是安娜，也可能是我的父亲，总之有个人突然出现，从我手中夺走了那把犁头，而另一个人则把我拖回了家园。莫文给我找来一块皮革让我咬住，然后尽她所能地缝合了我的伤口，还敷上了些难闻的药膏。我知道，那个伤口很可能会感染，我甚至可能会因此丧命。但事实并没有发生。她说我的伤势相当严重，有时候甚至能看到我的肋骨，不过我不太确定是否该相信她的话……反正，伤口确实很疼。感受不管怎样，我还是挺喜欢的。 然后…… 加雷特耸了耸肩。就这些了。如果你去安娜那里，让她给你看看她用那个生物的皮毛制作的斗篷吧。我们问过很多人，但就连半人马们也不清楚那到底是什么材料制成的。不过，这件斗篷确实很保暖。 那么，还有其他你想讨论的事情吗？

Garret wastes no time in clapping his hands, a loud, thunderous echo that draws the attention — and in Garth's case, ire — of everyone in the common room. The locals are clearly used to this spectacle, the more rowdy ones immediately crowding around the two of you and forming a half-circle of spectators. "Garret." Garth comes up to your table, his voice betraying not anger, but weary resignation. "Another one of your competitions?" "Come on, old man. It's not like you didn't get up to worse in your youth. Besides, there's nothing left for me to do today but to get smashed." Garth folds his arms. "Which is rather why I'd have you learn from my mistakes instead of having to suffer them yourself." "Dunno how much of a mistake this is. Not as if I'm asking you to turn on the tap for free. Besides —" he gestures at the crowd with a sweep of his arm — "You want to miss out on all this business?" Garth looks at the crowd, some of them calling out for drinks of their own while others make bets on the likely victor of your little competition. Slowly, the old wolf shakes his head and sighs. "Fine, fine. At least I know you won't ruin the floor. I just set down new sawdust today." "That's the spirit, old man!" Mumbling to himself, Garth retreats back into the crowd, returning with a tray bearing several large tankards, each one foaming at the lip. He slams it on the wooden tabletop, steps back, and folds his arms with a scowl on his face. "Don't rush yourselves, pups. We've got all night to do this. You need more, just call out — if you're not too drunk to speak in the first place." Garret looks down at the spread of mead before him. He looks at you. He looks down at the mead again. "Well then, this is making me thirsty. You want to get started?" By all means!'

rows.translation: 立即开始

rows.original: Whoa. That last drink might have been more than you could handle — but you're not going to be admitting that to Garret's face, not when you were the one to challenge him. Garret is still his usual boisterous self, drunk not so much on the copious quantities of mead he's imbibed, but on the mood of the crowd. Gods, even you can feel it, the infectious atmosphere that pervades the entirety of the Frost Hound's common room. The only person completely unmoved by it is Garth, who looks decidedly sour as he comes up with the next round of drinks. You say something to him, you don't quite remember what, and are about to throw down the wondrous joy-juice down your throat when everything goes black. "Hey, wake up." Garret's voice. ...Wha? You come to face-down in a puddle of spilt mead, coughing and spluttering as Garret fishes you out of the mess you've made. Staring at him through bleary eyes, you manage to mumble out a few words that're neither here nor there, a little confused about the situation. "You lost, but the old man's agreed to let you pay up tomorrow when you're sober. And besides, you gave me a decent run for my money." Garret grins. "I'm not completely heartless, after all; come on, let's get you back and have you sleep things off." That... that sounds great. Even through your drunken haze, you're vaguely aware of the now-dissipating crowd, Garth's death stare on the back of your neck, and Garret's arm as it hooks itself under yours and starts dragging you away from the table. He's not entirely steady himself, but at least he's in much better shape than you are — enough for him to lug you up the stairs and towards your room, at any rate. Ugh, you think you might puke. "That's what you get for challenging the strongest man in all of Savarra. Seriously, though, don't do that — I don't mind cleaning up yet another mess, but my old man might just kill you for it." Urp. Fine. [silly|Somehow, though, the thought of Garth murdering you by stoving your head in with a tankard seems amazingly amusing at this time, and you can't help but giggle all the way down the hallway. ]It seems like an eternity, but eventually the two of you reach the door to your room, and Garret hauls you in over the threshold. "No need to thank me," you hear him say, his voice strangely distant — or maybe it's just your fogged-up hearing. "Got to show good graces to the defeated, after all." You'll — you'll beat him next time... "Yeah, yeah. Don't mind the free drinks myself. I'm pretty buzzed, to be honest..." [var0| Buzzed or not, he hauled you up here in one piece, and you've got to thank him for that. "Yeah, that's called 'putting on a strong front.' Come on, let's get you into bed and tuck you in —" You're not exactly sure what happens in the next few seconds — probably all that drink — but when consciousness returns with dizziness in tow, you're down on your back, staring up at the ceiling. Garret's in your bed, splayed out lengthwise and face-down in the mattress, and by degrees he pushes himself off and tries to get back on his feet, without much success. "Gods damn it." He grunts, trying again, then slumps back down in defeat. It would've been hilarious if your mind weren't so fogged — and if he didn't just give you a big doggy slobber on your cheek. "Hey, you don't taste half bad today," Garret says, and hiccups. "[garret.fucked|I've always wondered how you've tasted, and now that I know... damn it, you're making me want to eat you up here.|You're making me hungry for a late-night snack here.]" Pressed against him as you are, you can feel the distinct throbbing of Garret's doggy dick through his tented pants, strong and steady with powerful virility; it's not as if you're any stranger to such, considering you've seen him naked in a cage. Added to the fact that he's drunkenly pawing at your [pc.top], there's little doubt as to what he intends to do. If you'd rather not have events play out, this would be the time to protest — or alternatively accept, or perhaps even encourage, his clumsy advances. If you don't act now, soon both of you will be too far gone to have any real control over your actions. What now? | All of a sudden, his support vanishes, and you fall straight down into the sweet, waiting embrace of the bed. Odd — you don't remember it being this soft, but that's for the better, right? "Sleep tight. My old man will settle the bill with you in the morning." A click of the door, and he's gone. You're reeking, disheveled and look like several kinds of wreckage, but that can be solved in the morning. In the morning... ]
rows.translation: 哇哦，最后一杯酒可能确实超出了你的承受能力……但你绝对不会当着加雷特的面承认这一点，毕竟是你主动向他发起挑战的。加雷特还是像往常一样吵闹活泼，他醉的并不是因为喝了太多蜂蜜酒，而是因为现场的气氛……天啊，真是这样。你能感受到那种弥漫在整个“寒霜猎犬”公共区域里的感染力极强的氛围。 唯一完全不受这种氛围影响的人是加斯，当他去准备下一轮酒水时，脸上明显带着不悦的表情。你跟他说了些什么，具体说了什么你已经不太记得了，就在你准备把那种美妙的酒水咽下去的那一刻，一切都陷入了黑暗。 嘿，醒醒。加雷特的声音。 …… “什么？” 你脸朝下陷在洒了一地的蜂蜜酒里，不停地咳嗽着、呛着，而加雷特则把你从这一团糟中拉了出来。你用模糊的双眼盯着他，勉强挤出几句语无伦次的话，完全搞不清楚发生了什么。 你输了，但那位老人同意让你明天清醒后把钱还上。而且，你确实让我玩得挺尽兴的。加雷特咧嘴笑了。我不是。完全地毕竟，你太无情了；来吧，我们带你回去，让你好好睡一觉，把那些烦心事都忘掉吧。 那……那听起来真不错。即使在你醉酒的状态下，你仍然隐约意识到了周围逐渐散去的人群，加斯那凝视着你的目光，还有加雷特的手臂搭在你的胳膊上，开始拉你离开桌子。他的动作虽然不太稳，但至少他的身体状况比你好多了——至少他有能力把你拖上楼梯，带到你的房间去。 呃，你觉得自己可能会吐出来。 这就是你挑战萨瓦拉最强之人所要付出的代价。说真的，千万别这么做——我并不介意再收拾一次烂摊子，但我的老爹可能会因此杀了你。 呃，好吧。 [silly|然而，此刻一想到加斯会用一个大酒杯把你的头砸烂来杀死你，这个想法反而显得非常有趣，你忍不住一路笑着走下了走廊。 ]仿佛过了漫长的时间，但最终你们俩还是走到了房间的门口，而加雷特将你拉进了房间。 不用谢我。你听到他说话，他的声音听起来异常遥远——或许只是你的听力出现了问题。毕竟，还是应该对失败者表现出宽容和善意。 下次你一定能打败他…… 是啊，是啊。那些免费饮料就当我自己请的吧。说实话，我现在已经有点微醺了…… [var0| 不管有没有发出嗡嗡声，他终究还是把你安全地带到了这里，因此你真的应该感谢他。 没错，这就是所谓的‘装出一副坚强的样子’。来吧，我们帮你上床睡觉，再把你盖好被子…… 接下来几秒钟里发生了什么，你其实并不太清楚——大概是因为喝了太多酒吧——但当意识逐渐恢复时，你发现自己仰面躺在床上，头晕目眩。加雷特躺在你的床垫上，身体呈俯卧姿势，他试图挣扎着坐起来，但却屡次失败。 该死的。他哼了一声，又尝试了一次，最终还是失望地坐了回去。要不是你头脑昏沉得厉害，要不是他还把口水抹在了你的脸上，这一幕简直会让人捧腹大笑。 嘿，你今天的味道还挺不错的嘛。加雷特说着，然后打起了嗝。“[garret.fucked|我一直很好奇你的味道究竟如何，现在知道了……该死，你真的让我想要把你吃掉。|这真让我想吃点深夜零食了。]” 当你紧贴着他的时候，你能清楚地感受到加雷特那坚硬而有力的阴茎在紧绷的裤子里不停地跳动，那股充满阳刚之气的节奏十分明显。考虑到你曾经见过他赤裸着的样子，这种感觉对你来说并不陌生。更何况，他现在还醉醺醺地不停地抓弄你[pc.top]毫无疑问，他打算做什么。 如果你不想让某些事情发生，现在就是抗议的时候——或者，你也可以选择接受，甚至鼓励他那些笨拙的举动。如果你现在不采取行动，很快你们俩就会陷入无法控制自己行为的境地。 现在该怎么办呢？ | 突然间，支撑你的力量消失了，你整个人直接坠入了那张柔软的床铺中。奇怪的是——你并不记得床铺原来这么柔软，不过这样反而更好，对吧？ 睡吧，早上我老爸会帮你把账结清的。 门一关，他就走了。你身上臭烘烘的，衣衫不整，看起来简直像一堆破烂，但这些问题明天早上就能解决。 明天早上…… ]

rows.translation: 接纳他吧

rows.original: Aah, you could do with a big fluffy lunk in bed with you.
rows.translation: 啊，你真该在床上有个柔软蓬松的大家伙陪着你。
rows.raw: "Aah, you could do with a big fluffy lunk in bed with you."

rows.translation: 推开

rows.original: No! Not now! Summoning up what strength you have left after that ill-fated drinking competition, you plant both palms on Garret's broad chest and attempt to shove him away. It's a feeble, uncoordinated effort and by rights shouldn't have worked at all, but to your surprise Garret draws back and stops fumbling at you. He doesn't look angry, frustrated, or even upset... hurt would more accurately describe the look on his face. Still, it's only there for a moment, a flicker of weakness before his ego swells to fill in the vacated space. "Guess you aren't sober enough to appreciate my amazing awesomeness," he says, grinning and giving your [pc.hair] a friendly tousle. Yes, he's definitely slurring his words a lot more now — that, or your hearing is going. "Actually, I'm kinda proud of you. It takes a lot to say no to the strongest man in all of Savarra." You'd have told him to [pc.isDK |fuck off |get real ], but Garret has pushed himself off the mattress with a sudden surge of strength and is wobbling out the doorway. Once or twice he stumbles, almost enough to send him sprawling to the floor once more, but he manages to keep it together until he's effectively out of view. [garret.fucked|| Ugh. Did... did Garret really want you, or was that just the mead talking? Well, now you'll never know. Or you might, if you could get him that buzzed again... ]
rows.translation: 不行！现在不行！在你那场倒霉的饮酒比赛后，你拼尽最后的力气，将双手按在加勒宽阔的胸膛上，试图把他推开。这个动作显得软弱无力、毫无协调性，按常理来说根本不应该有效果，但令你惊讶的是，加勒竟然后退了几步，不再对你动手动脚。他看起来既没有生气，也没有沮丧，甚至没有任何不悦的表情…… 受伤这个描述才更准确地刻画了他脸上的表情。 然而，这种脆弱感仅仅持续了一瞬间，就在他的自尊心重新占据上风之前，那种脆弱瞬间便消失了。 看来你还不够清醒，根本无法体会到我的非凡之处。他笑着说，友善地揉乱了你的[pc.hair]。没错，他现在确实说话含糊不清了很多——要么就是你的听力在下降。其实，我挺为你感到骄傲的。能够拒绝整个萨瓦拉地区最强壮的男人，这需要很大的勇气。 你本想叫他[pc.isDK |滚开 |认真点吧。 ]但是加雷特突然使出全部力气，从床垫上爬了起来，摇摇晃晃地走出了门口。他有那么一两次差点绊倒，差点再次摔倒在地，但他最终还是稳住了身体，直到完全消失在视线之外。 [garret.fucked|| 唉……加雷特真的是喜欢你吗，还是只是酒的作用而已？现在你永远也不会知道了。不过，如果你能让他再次产生那种感觉的话，也许就能知道答案了…… ]

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original: This isn't the time for that, you just want to sleep! Push Garret away.
rows.translation: 现在不是谈这个的时候，你只是想睡觉而已！把加雷特推开。
rows.raw: "This isn't the time for that, you just want to sleep! Push Garret away."

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original: "Another round!" Garret bellows, not even bothering to look down at the huge pile of empty tankards laid out on the table before the two of you. "We can do this all night, friend!" The crowd is getting quite excited now; the game's gotten pretty deep now, yet neither player is showing any sign of giving up. Garret flashes you a grin, gives you a thumbs-up, and reaches for the next tankard in line. "Guess that's how things roll when you challenge the strongest man in all of Savarra!" Mm-hm. Together, the two of you pick up you tankards and drain them, Garret doing so with his usual gusto. Perfectly calm, he slaps the now-empty tankard on the table and wipes his mouth with the back of his hand. "Feeling like giving up yet? Because I can —" Garret's smile broadens; he loosens his grip on his tankard. Still staring straight at you, he falls forward face-down straight into the mound of empties — there's no buckling, no swaying, no bending, just from upright to horizontal in one big and beautiful geometrically perfect arc. Then he begins to snore. Victory, it would appear, is yours. Behind you, the bookies are already collecting on their bets as to the winner of the drinking competition; you can only hope you didn't disappoint. At length, Garth comes over and begins the laborious process of clearing up the bodies stricken on the battlefield. "Guess you won," he says, but there's no joy in his voice. "I'll be putting the cost of tonight's frivolities on my idiot son's bill." Those were the terms of the challenge, yes. Looking back at Garret, he's sleeping like a baby, head turned to the side, mouth open, and a small trickle of drool oozing out from between his open jaws. The stench of alcohol rises from him, a veritable miasma — or maybe it's coming from you, it's hard to tell. After all, you've drunk just as much as Garret has. "Need a hand?" Garth's voice. "You don't look too good. I can get Gwyn to take you back to your room, if need be." No, no, you'll be fine. Besides, shouldn't he see to Garret first? Garth shrugs and finishes the precarious balancing act of piling up the last of the empties on his tray. "This isn't the first time this has happened, and he'll serve as a warning to the other patrons not to overindulge. Besides, I think he's happier like this." Hmm, he does have a point. Right, you'll be going to sleep this off, then. "Night. Don't fall down the stairs. I hope this was worth it for you." You'd have said something, but your tongue doesn't seem to want to cooperate. Neither, it seems, do your legs when it comes to climbing up the stairs to your room. But make it you do, and you barely have time to toss your things aside and slam the door shut before collapsing into bed and blacking out.
rows.translation: 再来一轮！加雷特大声吼叫着，甚至都没有费心去看你们两人面前桌子上那堆空酒壶。我们可以整晚都做这个，朋友！ 现在人群变得相当兴奋了；游戏已经进行到了相当深入的阶段，然而两位玩家都没有表现出任何放弃的迹象。加雷特向你露出了微笑，竖起了大拇指，然后伸手去拿队列中的下一杯酒。看来，当你挑战萨瓦拉最强大的男人时，事情就是会这样发展的吧！ 嗯，你们两个一起把那些酒杯拿过来，把酒喝光吧。加雷特还是像往常一样干得热火朝天。他表现得非常镇定，把已经空了的酒杯重重地放在桌上，然后用手背擦了擦嘴。 是不是想放弃了？但我还可以继续—— 加雷特的笑容变得更加灿烂，他松开了紧握着的大酒杯。依然直视着你的眼睛，他整个人向前倾倒，面朝下坠入了那一堆空酒瓶之中——没有丝毫的摇晃、弯曲，只是从直立状态笔直地倒下，形成一个完美而规整的几何弧线。 然后他开始打呼噜了。 看来，胜利属于你。在你身后，那些下注的人已经在收回他们关于谁会赢得这场饮酒比赛的赌注了；你只能希望自己没有让他们失望吧。最终，加斯走了过来，开始着手清理战场上那些倒下的战士们的遗体。这个过程相当繁琐。 看来你赢了。他说着，但语气中却没有任何喜悦之情。今晚这些无聊的开销，就让我记在我那个蠢儿子的账上吧。 没错，这些就是挑战的规则。回头看看加雷特，他正像婴儿一样熟睡着，头偏向一侧，嘴巴张开，有少量口水从他的牙缝中渗出来。他身上散发着浓重的酒精气味，简直像是一股瘴气——或许这种气味其实来自你很难说。毕竟，你喝的酒量和加雷特一样多。 需要帮忙吗？加斯的声音。你看起来状态不太好。如果有需要，我可以让格温带你回房间。 不，不，你不会有事的。而且，他不应该先去照顾加雷特吗？ 加斯耸了耸肩，继续小心翼翼地把剩下的空容器堆放到托盘上。这种事情已经不是第一次发生了，他的遭遇应该能给其他顾客一个警告，让他们不要过度消费。另外，我觉得他现在这样反而更开心。 嗯，他说的确实有道理。对了，那你现在就去睡一觉，睡一觉就会好的。 晚安。小心别从楼梯上摔下来。希望这一切对你来说是值得的。 你本想说些什么，但舌头似乎不愿意配合你。同样，当你试图爬上楼梯回到房间时，双腿也不听使唤。不过，只要你坚持完成了这些动作，你就几乎没有时间把东西扔到一边、关上门，然后立刻倒在地上昏睡过去。
rows.raw: " "Another round!" Garret bellows, not even bothering to look down at the huge pile of empty tankards laid out on the table before the two of you. "We can do this all night, friend!" The crowd is getting quite excited now; the game's gotten pretty deep now, yet neither player is showing any sign of giving up. Garret flashes you a grin, gives you a thumbs-up, and reaches for the next tankard in line. "Guess that's how things roll when you challenge the strongest man in all of Savarra!" Mm-hm. Together, the two of you pick up you tankards and drain them, Garret doing so with his usual gusto. Perfectly calm, he slaps the now-empty tankard on the table and wipes his mouth with the back of his hand. "Feeling like giving up yet? Because I can —" Garret's smile broadens; he loosens his grip on his tankard. Still staring straight at you, he falls forward face-down straight into the mound of empties — there's no buckling, no swaying, no bending, just from upright to horizontal in one big and beautiful geometrically perfect arc. Then he begins to snore. Victory, it would appear, is yours. Behind you, the bookies are already collecting on their bets as to the winner of the drinking competition; you can only hope you didn't disappoint. At length, Garth comes over and begins the laborious process of clearing up the bodies stricken on the battlefield. "Guess you won," he says, but there's no joy in his voice. "I'll be putting the cost of tonight's frivolities on my idiot son's bill." Those were the terms of the challenge, yes. Looking back at Garret, he's sleeping like a baby, head turned to the side, mouth open, and a small trickle of drool oozing out from between his open jaws. The stench of alcohol rises from him, a veritable miasma — or maybe it's coming from you, it's hard to tell. After all, you've drunk just as much as Garret has. "Need a hand?" Garth's voice. "You don't look too good. I can get Gwyn to take you back to your room, if need be." No, no, you'll be fine. Besides, shouldn't he see to Garret first? Garth shrugs and finishes the precarious balancing act of piling up the last of the empties on his tray. "This isn't the first time this has happened, and he'll serve as a warning to the other patrons not to overindulge. Besides, I think he's happier like this." Hmm, he does have a point. Right, you'll be going to sleep this off, then. "Night. Don't fall down the stairs. I hope this was worth it for you." You'd have said something, but your tongue doesn't seem to want to cooperate. Neither, it seems, do your legs when it comes to climbing up the stairs to your room. But make it you do, and you barely have time to toss your things aside and slam the door shut before collapsing into bed and blacking out."

rows.original:
You head over to the bench and lie down atop it, picking up some heavy rocks and shuffling your back into the surface until you're comfortable. Using your [pc.feet] to push yourself into the backboard, you grunt and begin raising the weights into the air above your [pc.chest].

    You halt some time later, sweating lightly and breathing harder as you let the rocks fall back to the floor. That was a good workout — your muscles are pumped and your heart is beating hard in your chest. You feel tighter and more toned already!

你走到长凳旁躺下，拿起几块沉重的石头，调整背部在凳面上的位置，直到躺得舒服。你用[pc.feet]蹬住靠板稳住身体，低吼一声，将重物举到[pc.chest]上方。

    一段时间后，你停下动作，微微出汗，呼吸也变得急促，任由石块落回地面。这次锻炼效果不错——你的肌肉充血膨胀，心脏也在胸腔里有力地跳动。你已经感觉身体更加紧实、线条更加鲜明了！

rows.original: You step inside the rack and under the bar, adjusting the height of it until it sits easily across your shoulders, and hook some sand-filled buckets over it. It's covered in rust but holds strong as you begin to lower it, squatting down before rising back up. This isn't so bad. You repeat a few sets before moving on to other exercises, raising the bar above your head until you can't possibly do any more then resting, placing the bar at the bottom of the rack before pulling it upwards. By the time you're done you're breathing hard and slick with sweat, heart beating in your chest. Now that was a workout, and you can see it paying off already with the pump emphasizing your newly gained tone and musculature. Time to get some water.

奔跑吧

rows.original:
You start off around the track, jogging at a light pace. It's pleasant out here with the wind gently blowing in your face, and you've spent half an hour in the field before you even realize it. Slowing to a halt, you get your breathing down to a measured rate and do some post-run stretching. You feel great, and it looks like you've shed some weight.

        Either way, it was a job well done. Feeling accomplished, you straighten up and look around.

你从跑道周围开始，以轻松的速度慢跑起来。微风轻拂着脸庞，这种感觉真是太惬意了。不知不觉中，你已经在这片场地里跑了半个小时。你慢慢停下来，调整呼吸，然后做了一些跑后的拉伸运动。你感觉棒极了，似乎还瘦了一些。

        无论如何，这次锻炼的效果确实不错。感到很有成就感，你挺直身子，环顾四周。

[brint.isBrienne
                |You pop back up and give Brienne a kiss on the nose. "All done."
                
                She giggles. "Thanks, I think. Am I cleaner now? Hard to say."
                
                You smile. "Let's wash off a bit and get back to it."
                
                You head back into the gym renewed and refreshed.
                |You give Brint a quick kiss on the cheek. "All done.[brint.isDaddy
                    | Thanks, daddy.
                ]"
                
                He chuckles. "Am I supposed to think I'm cleaner now?"
                
                You grin at him. "Lemme wash you off a bit before we get back to it."
                
                You head back into the gym renewed and refreshed.
            ]

rows.original: As you enter the Frost Hound's back yard, you're greeted by the sight of Gweyr standing out in the open, sniffing the air with her muzzle raised. The old wolfess' careful demeanor and measured movements make it clear what she's about: a lone wolf on the hunt, much like how you remember her from your time together in the rift. For what exactly, though, is in the question... Who's the unlucky bastard? At the sound of your voice, Gweyr stops, realizes how she must look — what would be perfectly natural out on the snow and ice is pretty out of place in the back yard with the chickens. Straightening up and clearing her throat, she eyes you and acts as if nothing had ever happened. "Didn't expect to see you [dayNight |around today, [pc.name]. Thought you'd left on another adventure or somesuch." Well, you did, and now you've returned from your little outing |out this late, [pc.name]. My daughter's closed up for the day, so you wouldn't be heading on out to the nursery, would you?" Maybe you were hoping to see Gwyn, maybe you were hoping to see her ]. Back to the point, though, who's the unlucky bastard? "I'm looking for my son. His scent's all about the place, but I just can't find him. I try to follow him to where I think it's the strongest where he should be, and he's not there." Gweyr rubs her temples. "I know Garth likes to say that he takes after me, but he's just as bad as his father in this regard. Slippery little fish, and he doesn't even know it. At least, he's got no reason to be hiding from his mom." [garret.atFH |Huh. Is she sure? You just passed through the Frost Hound's taproom, and Garret was there drinking his father's stock, same as always whenever he gets a break. Gweyr frowns. "Are you sure? I just checked the place and his usual table, even asked Garth if he'd seen the pup." You saw him on the way in, so... |Huh. You think you saw him while you were coming in from the square to the Frost Hound — he was in between one of the many odd jobs Garth keeps him busy with these days. Gweyr frowns. "Are you sure? I just checked the square and asked River if he'd seen the pup." You saw him on the way in, so... ] "The boy's even more talented than I thought if he's somehow managed to hide in plain sight, and from me at that." A scowl, and then Gweyr expression brightens, her ears perking up. "On that other hand, that means this is going to be all the more necessary." What is? "Oh, you'll find out soon enough. As his friend, I'm sure you'll be mighty interested in what I've got in store for him. Mind coming with me? Having one of his friends about might make it easier on him." Judging by the toothy grin Gweyr's got on her muzzle and the way she's rubbing her palms together, you can only guess that it isn't anything good. Well, scratch that — it's probably good for Garret, given that it's coming from his mother, but is certainly going to fit neatly into the category of tough love. All right, then, you'll see what all of this is about. "Good, good. Now, where did you see my dear idiot son last?" You have no idea how Gweyr managed to miss Garret when he's just sitting at his table — or maybe it's only that the latter was hoping to remain invisible to his mother, but not to you. Whatever the case, it's an absolutely trivial matter to point out the so-called strongest man in Savarra to Gweyr, who squints at her son as he downs another half-tankard of rye beer with the clear intent of washing it down with the other half soon enough. "Why didn't his father or I notice him before? It seems so obvious when you point it out and it matches up with what my nose was telling me, but... hmph. I guess I should've trusted my nose over my eyes. Thanks, [pc.name]." Oh no, the pleasure's all yours, if only for the privilege of seeing the fireworks go off. But Gweyr's already sweeping past you and straight into the common room, people unconsciously moving out of her way like a school of fish parting about a boulder mid-stream. Garret splutters when he sees his mother making a beeline for him — this is something he's clearly not expecting — and barely has enough time to set his tankard down before Gweyr lays a thick hand on his shoulder, thumb and forefinger poised to pick him up by the scruff of his neck if need be. "There you are," Gweyr says, a note of finality in her voice as she gives her son's shoulder a squeeze. "I've been looking for you for a bit now — the strongest man in all of Savarra wouldn't be hiding from or afraid of his dear old mother, would he?" "No, of course not." Nonchalantly, Garret takes another swig from his tankard and looks up at his mother. If he was knowingly hiding from his mother, that's a pretty good save he's making there, acting all cool and unfazed while she leans her weight on him. "Something the matter, Mom? Just enjoying a drink before everything gets all hectic again." "It's going to be hectic, all right. I've spent a little while catching up with your father about your situation, and I do agree with you on a handful of matters. You've been spending your entire life resenting being called 'Garth's pup' and touting yourself as the strongest man in the world... so strong that your dear old mother might not be able to handle you by yourself, especially since you grew up without me around to mind you. That's my fault, and I'm going to be making good on it." "How so, Mom?" Gweyr reaches into her clothes and pulls out a small, rolled up note. "I got a reply yesterday from the Crossed Swords. They're still on campaign down south in the heartlands, but once they're done they'll be coming up here to pick you up and take you off to be schooled, for lack of a better word; it's the least they can do for their old leader, if nothing else. Your father's taught you what he knows and I plan to do the same before you leave, but the world's changed since our day and there's no better way to learn and be tested than by experience. Assuming you come back alive, pup, you'll be more than ready to settle down and take the Frost Hound off our cold, dead bodies." "Gods, Mom. Don't put it like that. So, uh, just to get this right. You'll be throwing me in with the Crossed Swords, then?" "For as long as you like. I don't expect Old Belhar to have gotten any safer over the last twenty years, if the two hundred before that are any indicator. It's a dangerous place — you may very well die, and your father and I were lucky to live long enough to be able to make the decision to retire. Your grandfather didn't." "And what does the old man think of all of this?" "I'm right here, pup," Garth growls over from the bar. "You could just ask me to my face, you know. Anyway, your mother's right — I've done all I could to settle you down, but if you're so determined to get out of this village and see the world at the very least you'll be in good hands. Many of the people I know that helped me build much of Hawkethorne as it stands today, I met while crossing Old Belhar with your mother. While you've already gotten the chance to know many of them over the years, there's no harm in making some contacts of your own if you're going to inherit the Frost Hound someday." Garret grins, then rises from his seat and hugs Gweyr fiercely, enough to elicit a grunt from the old wolfess. "Thanks, Mom. You too, old man." "Don't be too happy," Garth grunts as he turns back to polishing the mugs. "It's not going to be an easy life. Death won't necessarily come in glorious battle — more are killed from drinking bad water, shivering in a half-dugout hole while the rain pours down around you. The Crossed Swords may have done well for themselves since your mother and I left the company, but they're still the kind of mercenary company you hire to get jobs done, as opposed to prancing around and putting on a show for your clients. It'll be a harder, more disciplined life than what I've been able to give to you these last twenty years." "Nothing the strongest man in the world won't be able to handle. So, when are they coming, Mom?" Gweyr shrugs. "As soon as their contract is over and they can make their way up here. Could be weeks, could be months[silly |; for plot convenience, they'll take just long enough to arrive in the epilogue when this game is finally done ]. Don't think too much about it or get too excited, pup." "Even so, that's still something to look forward to, another reason to get out of bed every morning." In all his excitement, Garret seems to notice you for the first time, and giving you the same smile that he graced his mother with, squeezes you with his brawny arms in yet another hug. "Thanks, [pc.name]. This wouldn't have happened if you hadn't convinced me to try and bring Mom home." He doesn't need to mention it. While you did indeed help Gweyr deal with her unfinished business and close the book on that chapter of her life, allowing to set up the circumstances to allow her to return home after all these years, he was the one who ultimately convinced her to do it. "Doesn't change a word of what I said, [pc.name]. Thanks again." He turns to Gweyr. "So, Mom, anything I should do until your old friends come to pick me up?" "I don't expect your life to change much until then, pup. There's still a lot of drudge work to be done in between the fun bits, especially when you're just a fresh face, so I'm not going to pull you off the manual labor your father's having you do. That being said, I'll stand in for him every now and then, try and get you prepared for the kind of life you'll be having on the road. It's very different from what you've had so far, but that much should be obvious. "But... yes. Just go, pup, go when the time comes. If you're anything like me when I was your age, you're wasting your life sitting around in your father's tavern. Either you come back having worked it all out of your system and ready to settle down, or you don't come back at all because there's no body to bring back. Down in the heartlands, it's not just other people you'll be up against, but things as well." "Nothing the strongest man in the world won't be able to handle, then." Sighing happily, Garret sits back down at his table and starts polishing off the other half of his tankard. You can't tell if he was just kidding about the strongest man in the world thing yet again... but that's the point, isn't it? "Don't worry, Mom, old man. I'll be sure to come back to you before the both of you die." "Look at how excited he is," Garth says with a sigh, shaking his head. "I'm just waiting for the reality of the matter to sink in..." Gweyr just grins. "Don't know about that. Growing up with my father was fun. Hard, but fun. Our pup will be cursing the captains and commander half the time... and he'll be having the time of his life with the other half. Or have you forgotten all the fun we had together on campaign?" "I mostly remember your dad telling me to balance the books he didn't want to bother with himself. Man never checked my work... I guess he was choosing to trust me inasmuch as he was giving me a chance." "Mhm." Turning back to her Garret, Gweyr claps her son on the shoulder. "Drink up, pup. Tomorrow, I'll start seeing in earnest what you're made of."
rows.translation: 当你走进寒霜猎犬的后院时，首先映入眼帘的是格维尔——她站在开阔地中，高高扬起鼻子嗅着空气。这只老母狼那谨慎的神态和从容的动作清楚地表明了她此刻正在做什么：就像你们在裂隙中共同度过的那些日子里你所记得的那样，她正在独自狩猎。不过，问题究竟出在什么地方呢…… 那个倒霉的家伙是谁呢？ 听到你的声音，格维尔停下了动作，意识到自己现在这个样子一定很滑稽——在冰雪覆盖的环境中这种装扮还算自然，但放在有鸡的后院里，就显得格格不入了。她挺直身子，清了清嗓子，然后看着你，表现得好像什么事情都没有发生过一样。 “真没想到会在这里见到你。 [dayNight |大约在今天，[pc.name]我还以为你又去参加什么冒险活动了呢。” “嗯，确实去了，不过现在我已经从那次小旅行中回来了。 |都这么晚了[pc.name]我女儿今天没去托儿所，所以你也不会去那里吧？” 也许你本来是想见格温的，也许你就是想见她。 ]不过，还是回到正题吧，那个倒霉的家伙到底是谁呢？ “我在找我的儿子。他的气味到处都能闻到，但我就是找不到他。我试图跟着他的气味去他应该在的地方，可他根本不在那里。”格维尔揉着太阳穴说道，“我知道加思总爱说他和我长得像，但在这方面，他和他父亲一样糟糕。那个滑不溜溜的小家伙，他自己却完全不知道。至少，他没有任何理由要躲躲藏藏地不见妈妈吧。 [garret.atFH 不，当然没有。”加雷特若无其事地又喝了一口酒，然后抬头看着自己的母亲。如果他真的是在故意躲着母亲的话，那他的表现确实相当出色——在母亲依靠他的时候，他依然表现得冷静而淡然。“妈妈，有什么事吗？只是想在一切变得忙碌之前先喝点酒放松一下罢了。
