格维尔从她的衣服里拿出一张卷起来的小纸条：“昨天我收到了‘十字剑团’的回复。他们现在还在南方的腹地执行任务，等任务结束后，他们会来接你，然后送你去接受教育——虽然用‘教育’这个词可能不太准确，但至少这是他们能为他们的老领袖做的最起码的事了。你父亲把他所知道的一切都传授给了你，我也打算在你离开之前做同样的事。但是，自我们那个时代以来，世界已经发生了变化，而没有什么比亲身经历更能让人真正学习和成长了。只要你能活着回来，孩子，你就会准备好承担起责任，把“霜犬酒馆”从我们这些冰冷、无用的躯体上夺走。" 天啊，妈妈，别这么说。那么，嗯，让我把意思弄清楚吧。也就是说，你打算把我安排到‘十字剑组织’里去吗？” “你想待多久就待多久吧。如果过去两百年的情况能说明什么的话，那我敢肯定，在过去的二十年里，老贝尔哈尔并没有变得安全任何一点。那是个危险的地方——你很可能会丧命，而我和你父亲能够活到现在，能够决定退休，其实已经算是很幸运了。你的祖父就没有这么幸运。 那这个老人对这一切是怎么看的呢？” “我就在这儿，小家伙，”加斯从酒吧那边吼道，“你大可以直接问我啊。总之，你妈妈说得对——我已经尽力让你安定下来生活了，但如果你一心想要离开这个村庄去看看外面的世界，那么你至少会遇到可靠的人来帮助你。我认识的那些帮助我打造了如今这个鹰棘镇的人，很多都是我在和你的母亲一起穿越旧贝尔哈时遇到的。这些年来，你已经有机会认识了他们中的许多人，但如果你将来真的要继承霜犬酒馆的话，主动去建立一些联系也是没有坏处的。" 加雷特咧嘴一笑，然后从座位上站起来，紧紧地拥抱了格维尔，这一拥抱力度之大，以至于让那位老女狼发出了哼声。“谢谢你，妈妈。你也一样，老家伙。” “别太高兴了，”加思边说边转过身去，继续擦拭那些杯子。这不会是一段轻松的生活。死亡并不一定发生在辉煌的战斗中——更多的人是因为喝了不干净的水而死去，或者是在大雨倾盆的时候，蜷缩在半挖好的坑洞里瑟瑟发抖而丧命。自从你母亲和我离开那家佣兵公司后，‘交叉之剑’可能确实取得了一些成就，但他们依然属于那种你只需要雇佣他们来完成任务罢了，而不是让他们在客户面前招摇过市、炫耀武力之类的佣兵组织。这将是一种更加艰难、更加需要自律的生活方式，比我过去二十年所能给予你的要复杂得多。 世界上最强的人肯定能够解决任何问题。那么，他们什么时候会来呢，妈妈？” 格维尔耸了耸肩：“等他们的合同结束，能够来到这里的时候吧。可能要等几周，也可能要等几个月。[silly |为了剧情发展的需要，它们所需要的时间正好足以让游戏在最终结束时进入尾声阶段。 ]别想得太复杂，也别太兴奋，小家伙。” “不过，这确实是一件值得期待的事情，也是每天早上起床的另一个理由。”加雷特满心兴奋地似乎这才第一次注意到你，他露出了和对待他母亲时一样的微笑，然后用他那结实的双臂再次紧紧抱住了你。“谢谢。[pc.name]如果你没有说服我去尝试把妈妈带回家，这一切就不会发生。” 他其实没有必要提这个。虽然你确实帮助格维尔处理了她未了的事务，让她的那段人生画上了句号，也为她多年后能够回家创造了条件，但最终还是他说服了她去这么做。 “但这丝毫不会改变我所说的话[pc.name]再次感谢。”他转向格韦尔说道，“那么，妈妈，在你的老朋友们来接我之前，我还需要做些什么吗？” “在那之前，我觉得你的生活应该不会有什么大的变化，孩子。在那些有趣的事情之外，还有很多繁琐的工作需要完成，尤其是当你还是个新人的时候。所以，我不会让你停止你父亲让你做的那些体力活的。话虽如此，我偶尔会代替他，尽力帮助你们为将来在旅途中的生活做好准备。那种生活方式与你们目前的生活经历截然不同，这一点应该很明显吧。 但是……好吧。去吧，孩子，等到时候再出发。如果你和我在你这个年纪时一样，那么你只是把时间浪费在你父亲的酒馆里而已。要么你回来时已经解决了所有问题，准备安定下来生活；要么你就根本不会回来，因为根本没有什么人等着你回来。在那些内陆地区，你面临的对手不仅仅是其他人，还有各种物品那么，世界上没有任何事情是世界上最强壮的人无法处理的了。”加雷特开心地叹了口气，重新坐回桌旁，开始喝完剩下的酒杯里的酒。现在还无法判断他这次所说的“世界上最强壮的人”到底是不是又在开玩笑。但关键就在于这里，不是吗？”“别担心，妈妈，老头。我一定会在你们俩去世之前回到你们身边。” “看看他有多兴奋，”加思叹息着说道，同时摇了摇头，“我只是还在努力接受这个事实罢了。格维尔只是笑了笑：“这个我就不知道了。和父亲一起长大确实很有趣，虽然过程很艰难，但确实很开心。我们的孩子有一半时间会诅咒那些船长和指挥官……而另外一半时间，他一定会玩得非常开心。还是说，你已经忘记了我们一起完成那些任务时所经历的所有快乐时光了？” “我主要记得的是你爸爸让我帮他核对那些账目，他根本不想亲自去处理这些事情。他从来都没有检查过我的工作……我想，他是在信任我，才会给我这个机会吧。嗯。”格韦尔转过身，拍了拍儿子的肩膀：“喝完吧，小家伙。明天，我就真正看看你到底有什么本事。
rows.raw: " As you enter the Frost Hound's back yard, you're greeted by the sight of Gweyr standing out in the open, sniffing the air with her muzzle raised. The old wolfess' careful demeanor and measured movements make it clear what she's about: a lone wolf on the hunt, much like how you remember her from your time together in the rift. For what exactly, though, is in the question... Who's the unlucky bastard? At the sound of your voice, Gweyr stops, realizes how she must look — what would be perfectly natural out on the snow and ice is pretty out of place in the back yard with the chickens. Straightening up and clearing her throat, she eyes you and acts as if nothing had ever happened. "Didn't expect to see you [dayNight |around today, [pc.name]. Thought you'd left on another adventure or somesuch." Well, you did, and now you've returned from your little outing |out this late, [pc.name]. My daughter's closed up for the day, so you wouldn't be heading on out to the nursery, would you?" Maybe you were hoping to see Gwyn, maybe you were hoping to see her ]. Back to the point, though, who's the unlucky bastard? "I'm looking for my son. His scent's all about the place, but I just can't find him. I try to follow him to where I think it's the strongest where he should be, and he's not there." Gweyr rubs her temples. "I know Garth likes to say that he takes after me, but he's just as bad as his father in this regard. Slippery little fish, and he doesn't even know it. At least, he's got no reason to be hiding from his mom." [garret.atFH |Huh. Is she sure? You just passed through the Frost Hound's taproom, and Garret was there drinking his father's stock, same as always whenever he gets a break. Gweyr frowns. "Are you sure? I just checked the place and his usual table, even asked Garth if he'd seen the pup." You saw him on the way in, so... |Huh. You think you saw him while you were coming in from the square to the Frost Hound — he was in between one of the many odd jobs Garth keeps him busy with these days. Gweyr frowns. "Are you sure? I just checked the square and asked River if he'd seen the pup." You saw him on the way in, so... ] "The boy's even more talented than I thought if he's somehow managed to hide in plain sight, and from me at that." A scowl, and then Gweyr expression brightens, her ears perking up. "On that other hand, that means this is going to be all the more necessary." What is? "Oh, you'll find out soon enough. As his friend, I'm sure you'll be mighty interested in what I've got in store for him. Mind coming with me? Having one of his friends about might make it easier on him." Judging by the toothy grin Gweyr's got on her muzzle and the way she's rubbing her palms together, you can only guess that it isn't anything good. Well, scratch that — it's probably good for Garret, given that it's coming from his mother, but is certainly going to fit neatly into the category of tough love. All right, then, you'll see what all of this is about. "Good, good. Now, where did you see my dear idiot son last?" You have no idea how Gweyr managed to miss Garret when he's just sitting at his table — or maybe it's only that the latter was hoping to remain invisible to his mother, but not to you. Whatever the case, it's an absolutely trivial matter to point out the so-called strongest man in Savarra to Gweyr, who squints at her son as he downs another half-tankard of rye beer with the clear intent of washing it down with the other half soon enough. "Why didn't his father or I notice him before? It seems so obvious when you point it out and it matches up with what my nose was telling me, but... hmph. I guess I should've trusted my nose over my eyes. Thanks, [pc.name]." Oh no, the pleasure's all yours, if only for the privilege of seeing the fireworks go off. But Gweyr's already sweeping past you and straight into the common room, people unconsciously moving out of her way like a school of fish parting about a boulder mid-stream. Garret splutters when he sees his mother making a beeline for him — this is something he's clearly not expecting — and barely has enough time to set his tankard down before Gweyr lays a thick hand on his shoulder, thumb and forefinger poised to pick him up by the scruff of his neck if need be. "There you are," Gweyr says, a note of finality in her voice as she gives her son's shoulder a squeeze. "I've been looking for you for a bit now — the strongest man in all of Savarra wouldn't be hiding from or afraid of his dear old mother, would he?" "No, of course not." Nonchalantly, Garret takes another swig from his tankard and looks up at his mother. If he was knowingly hiding from his mother, that's a pretty good save he's making there, acting all cool and unfazed while she leans her weight on him. "Something the matter, Mom? Just enjoying a drink before everything gets all hectic again." "It's going to be hectic, all right. I've spent a little while catching up with your father about your situation, and I do agree with you on a handful of matters. You've been spending your entire life resenting being called 'Garth's pup' and touting yourself as the strongest man in the world... so strong that your dear old mother might not be able to handle you by yourself, especially since you grew up without me around to mind you. That's my fault, and I'm going to be making good on it." "How so, Mom?" Gweyr reaches into her clothes and pulls out a small, rolled up note. "I got a reply yesterday from the Crossed Swords. They're still on campaign down south in the heartlands, but once they're done they'll be coming up here to pick you up and take you off to be schooled, for lack of a better word; it's the least they can do for their old leader, if nothing else. Your father's taught you what he knows and I plan to do the same before you leave, but the world's changed since our day and there's no better way to learn and be tested than by experience. Assuming you come back alive, pup, you'll be more than ready to settle down and take the Frost Hound off our cold, dead bodies." "Gods, Mom. Don't put it like that. So, uh, just to get this right. You'll be throwing me in with the Crossed Swords, then?" "For as long as you like. I don't expect Old Belhar to have gotten any safer over the last twenty years, if the two hundred before that are any indicator. It's a dangerous place — you may very well die, and your father and I were lucky to live long enough to be able to make the decision to retire. Your grandfather didn't." "And what does the old man think of all of this?" "I'm right here, pup," Garth growls over from the bar. "You could just ask me to my face, you know. Anyway, your mother's right — I've done all I could to settle you down, but if you're so determined to get out of this village and see the world at the very least you'll be in good hands. Many of the people I know that helped me build much of Hawkethorne as it stands today, I met while crossing Old Belhar with your mother. While you've already gotten the chance to know many of them over the years, there's no harm in making some contacts of your own if you're going to inherit the Frost Hound someday." Garret grins, then rises from his seat and hugs Gweyr fiercely, enough to elicit a grunt from the old wolfess. "Thanks, Mom. You too, old man." "Don't be too happy," Garth grunts as he turns back to polishing the mugs. "It's not going to be an easy life. Death won't necessarily come in glorious battle — more are killed from drinking bad water, shivering in a half-dugout hole while the rain pours down around you. The Crossed Swords may have done well for themselves since your mother and I left the company, but they're still the kind of mercenary company you hire to get jobs done, as opposed to prancing around and putting on a show for your clients. It'll be a harder, more disciplined life than what I've been able to give to you these last twenty years." "Nothing the strongest man in the world won't be able to handle. So, when are they coming, Mom?" Gweyr shrugs. "As soon as their contract is over and they can make their way up here. Could be weeks, could be months[silly |; for plot convenience, they'll take just long enough to arrive in the epilogue when this game is finally done ]. Don't think too much about it or get too excited, pup." "Even so, that's still something to look forward to, another reason to get out of bed every morning." In all his excitement, Garret seems to notice you for the first time, and giving you the same smile that he graced his mother with, squeezes you with his brawny arms in yet another hug. "Thanks, [pc.name]. This wouldn't have happened if you hadn't convinced me to try and bring Mom home." He doesn't need to mention it. While you did indeed help Gweyr deal with her unfinished business and close the book on that chapter of her life, allowing to set up the circumstances to allow her to return home after all these years, he was the one who ultimately convinced her to do it. "Doesn't change a word of what I said, [pc.name]. Thanks again." He turns to Gweyr. "So, Mom, anything I should do until your old friends come to pick me up?" "I don't expect your life to change much until then, pup. There's still a lot of drudge work to be done in between the fun bits, especially when you're just a fresh face, so I'm not going to pull you off the manual labor your father's having you do. That being said, I'll stand in for him every now and then, try and get you prepared for the kind of life you'll be having on the road. It's very different from what you've had so far, but that much should be obvious. "But... yes. Just go, pup, go when the time comes. If you're anything like me when I was your age, you're wasting your life sitting around in your father's tavern. Either you come back having worked it all out of your system and ready to settle down, or you don't come back at all because there's no body to bring back. Down in the heartlands, it's not just other people you'll be up against, but things as well." "Nothing the strongest man in the world won't be able to handle, then." Sighing happily, Garret sits back down at his table and starts polishing off the other half of his tankard. You can't tell if he was just kidding about the strongest man in the world thing yet again... but that's the point, isn't it? "Don't worry, Mom, old man. I'll be sure to come back to you before the both of you die." "Look at how excited he is," Garth says with a sigh, shaking his head. "I'm just waiting for the reality of the matter to sink in..." Gweyr just grins. "Don't know about that. Growing up with my father was fun. Hard, but fun. Our pup will be cursing the captains and commander half the time... and he'll be having the time of his life with the other half. Or have you forgotten all the fun we had together on campaign?" "I mostly remember your dad telling me to balance the books he didn't want to bother with himself. Man never checked my work... I guess he was choosing to trust me inasmuch as he was giving me a chance." "Mhm." Turning back to her Garret, Gweyr claps her son on the shoulder. "Drink up, pup. Tomorrow, I'll start seeing in earnest what you're made of." "

rows.original: [flags.GWEYR_NURSERY_MET |[rand |As you draw close, you find mother and daughter having a brief discussion about the nursery's logistics, or at least that's the way Gweyr puts it from the few snippets of actual conversation you manage to catch. It's more the tone of what's being said that tells you more: short, clipped words delivered in a flat, emotionless tone by both women. After a moment or two of this, the two part ways, each one very assiduously not looking at the other — until you greet Gweyr and the old wolfess softens a little. Getting along with her daughter's still a challenge, huh? "We're working through it. At least we can get through a conversation without tearing each others' throats out, which is more than what I can say. I don't ever see her fully forgiving me, and she's got a right to do so, but this isn't so bad either. If I'd been in my daughter's shoes... well, I'd be dead already." Good thing it wasn't Garret that held the grudge against her, then. "Sure, sure. So, is there something you needed of me, or are you just here to make small talk?" |Approaching Gweyr, you find the old wolfess in a chair in a corner of the nursery, folding clothes with a deft hand. One stack is her daughter's usual outfit, at least a dozen copies in the pile; the other just so happens to be Gweyr's own clothes. Like it or not, it's undeniable that the daughter inherited her mother's penchant for uniforms. "Nothing to see here," Gweyr says, rolling her eyes even as a small smile forms on her muzzle. "Just noting that my daughter can't run away from what's in her blood, no matter how many times she denies me." And of the penchant for being everybody's mom... "No doubt from my husband's side of the family. Now then, is there something you need of me? It'll keep my mind occupied while me hands work." |It takes a little bit of searching to find Gweyr — you eventually find her playing with the nursery children, the wolfess surprisingly spry despite her age. It's not surprising given the active life she's led up to this point, but despite her size the kids aren't intimidated by her any. Maybe they just haven't learned to be afraid of her yet. Seeing you approach, though, Gweyr lazily extricates herself from the pile of little bodies and shakes herself off to a chorus of "aww"s. Showing the kids her teeth and giving them a wave, she pads towards you and gives you a nod. "Well, if it isn't [pc.name]." Working with the kids? She's surprisingly good at it, even if she doesn't have a smile that isn't menacing. "Ah well, you know, Gwyn and Garret were young once, so I've had practice. That, and it's really not that different from dealing with selkies, only you have to make the kid gloves extra thick, so to speak. I may be good at bloody death and murder, but it's not the only things I've ever attempted in my life. After all, I tried my hand at barmaiding once and wasn't too bad at it, if I may say. "Anyway, what's up?" |Looking for Gweyr eventually leads you to the nursery kitchens, where Gweyr is putting on a big pot of something that smells vaguely of seafood on to simmer. The old wolfess stirs it a couple of times, looks satisfied, then turns to you. "Don't look at me like that, this stuff is for the kids." You suspect one of the reasons Gwyn is so curvaceous is that she can't help but sneak tastes of anything and everything she cooks for the nursery's residents. A shrug. "My father taught me some basic self-control. That, and this stuff is puppy food — it's the stuff I'd feed Gwyn and Garret just after they were weaned. Yes, there's no doubt about it, especially after the look she gives you as you approach, softening only when she realizes you're not a threat. A bit high-strung, eh? "Old habits die hard," is the dry answer you get. "While I didn't quite expect to ever be able to come home, I'm glad I did. I thought I'd die with nothing and no one around save for the empty howling of the chill wind, and here I am, being proven wrong by the day. I used to be apprehensive of growing old, but now... I wouldn't mind going on for a handful more years just to be able to see how things turn out because of people like me, Sanders and my husband. Being able to watch over these kids while they play brings me back years to when Gwyn and Garret were born." And now Gwyn's a mother in her own right. "Yes." Gweyr looks thoughtful and melancholy for a moment, then sighs and pushes herself out of the chair. "Ah, it's too early in the day to get all upset. Can we change the topic, [pc.name]?" ] |Carefully, you stand a little way away from Gweyr and wait for her to be done with her current task — which just so happens to be tending to a large pot of what smells like fish gruel. Moments slip by, the old wolfess' ears twitching, until she finally grunts and turns to you. "There, I can let this simmer for a couple of hours. Is there anything you wanted of me, [pc.name]?" You just wanted to check in with her, see how she's fitting back into Hawkethorne; it would be downright irresponsible to convince her to come home and just foist her onto a family that's been estranged from her. After twenty years of exile as a hermit — "Well, I wasn't that much of a hermit," Gweyr snaps. "The jotuns, the selkies, the siorcs, even the avanai — they all count as people, and were sad to see me go even if they understood why I was doing it." Very well, after twenty years of exile from Hawkethorne, then, it's changed to the point where it's a new place for her. So... how's she doing? You see she's making herself useful in her daughter's nursery. "It's not a bad idea," Gweyr says after considering her words. "If Carmen saw fit to fund its day-to-day running with money from one of her trusts — her castle never had any gold in its vaults like the fool Tollus believed — it's got to be worth something. It's not the path I would've chosen had I been in my daughter's shoes, but given that I was missing for so much of Gwyn's life I don't really have the right to criticize her on the decisions she's made in my absence. It's honest work and earns respect from the townsfolk, and that's good enough." That, and being in the nursery all day lets her be close to her daughter. "Yes." A sigh. "Things could always be better, but for now we have an armistice for the sake of her father's sanity. We're tolerating each others' presence, and that's frankly further than I thought we'd be getting along given how she first reacted when I arrived home. From there on out... well, I've just got to keep on chipping away at it. If I can hound Tollus for twenty years across forests, mountains and the ice, I can fix things with my daughter before my dying day." Those're fighting words she's saying, and you can only wish her the best of luck for the days ahead. [var0 |"Oh, by the by. There's something I've been meaning to talk to you about." That would be? "While I was getting acquainted with the nursery, some of the other women Gwyneth's employed were quick to show off my daughter's darling pups that she'd produced when I was away. There was the first litter by that ne'er-do-well who took to his heels upon receiving the news, of course. Eight at one go — I don't know where that came from, but it certainly wasn't from anyone on my side of the family. And both my son and daughter." Ah. She doesn't seem surprised. Gweyr sighs. "Moving in the circles I used to in my youth, it wasn't odd to find people who'd altered their bodies with alchemy to play all sorts of tricks, receive all kinds of pleasure, experiment with themselves. Some of them were contracted clients, others marks the former wanted taken out along with their holdings. So no, being well-traveled has its benefits. That, and there are peoples who are that way by virtue of their race." Well, she's a grandma now. And frankly, given the things that could've happened to her kids while she was away from them, they could've gotten themselves into much worse shenanigans — if this could be considered to be anything but positive to begin with. Gweyr sighs. "My daughter was a grown woman — if barely, and in body — when you put those puppies into her; it's not as if they weren't going to be well-cared for given the baroness's generous funding for the nursery, either. And given that I was completely absent from her life to the point that unlike Garret, she doesn't even remember my face from when she was a child, I really don't have a leg to stand on to criticize you in any way. Garth's an old softy at heart, and she didn't just inherit that aspect of him, she turned it up to eleven to boot. If Gwyn doesn't have anyone to take care of her, that dangerously submissive streak in her is going to have my daughter presenting herself to anyone who'd care. "And Garret? Garret's really determined to follow in my footsteps, isn't he? Both the pup and his sister were happy accidents... the problem is that he isn't the leader of a mercenary company like I was, and he doesn't have the means to leave with you and set up a nice little tavern in a village you'd heard was being founded and could make a new start in. Or at least, I take it that's what the both of you presumably aren't about to do — knowing the both of you and how full of surprises you are, I'm not discounting the possibility. I don't know what you see in him, but then again I didn't get what Garth saw in me back in the day, either. And I'll be frank in that this is partly my fault — Garth may have taught him how to fight, but as I said before, my husband's an old softy at heart and completely unsuited to raising a pup like him. Things might've been different if I were around to guide him while he was growing up, but that ship's long since sailed." So, what's her point? "You're asking me? I don't know where I'm going with this. Maybe I'm just afraid that my grandkids are going to suffer from the same thing that my kids did, but it's not the exact same case, is it? Even now, I'm still learning about how my husband, Sanders and River conspired to keep mum about me regardless of how much Garret pressed the matter. Maybe this is, in some small part, the chance to atone for what I did in my youth. That being said, I'm going to see what I can do about my pups before I die, make up for all the lost time that they should've spent with me." |"Oh, by the by. |当你靠近时，你看到母女俩正在简短地讨论托儿所的一些安排事宜，至少从你设法听到的那些零星对话片段来看，格维尔是这么描述的。其实，更能说明问题的是她们的说话语气——两位女性都用简洁、生硬的话语，以一种毫无情绪色彩的方式表达着自己的意思。过了一两分钟，两人便分道扬镳了，每个人都刻意避免看向对方——直到你向格维尔打招呼，那位老母狼的神情才稍微缓和了一些。 和女儿相处起来，果然还是挺有挑战性的，嗯？ 我们正在努力解决这个问题。至少我们现在能够进行对话，而不会互相争吵，这已经比我预期的要好多了。我从来没见过她完全原谅我，她也有权利这样做，不过目前的情况也还不算太糟。如果我处在我女儿的位置上……嗯，我早就死了。” 幸好怀恨在心的不是加勒特。 “当然，当然。那么，你是有什么事情需要我帮忙的，还是只是想来闲聊几句而已？" |当你接近格维尔时，你看到那位老女狼坐在育儿室的一个角落里的椅子上，熟练地折叠着衣物。其中一叠是她女儿平时穿的服装，那堆里至少有十几件；而另一叠，恰好是格维尔自己的衣服。无论你喜不喜欢，事实不可否认：这个女儿继承了她母亲对制服的喜爱。 “这里没什么好看的，”格维尔说着，翻了个白眼，但嘴角却浮现出一丝微笑，“只是想说，我的女儿永远无法摆脱她与生俱来的这种特质，无论她怎么否认我这么说。还有那种总想扮演大家妈妈的角色…… “这肯定是我丈夫那边的家族遗传。那么，你现在有什么需要我帮忙的吗？这样我一边干活一边也能打发时间。" |要找到格维尔需要稍微费些功夫——最终你会看到她正在和那些幼儿园的孩子们一起玩耍，这位年纪不小的女狼竟然行动得如此敏捷。考虑到她一直以来都过着活跃的生活，这一点也不足为奇；不过尽管她体型庞大，那些孩子们却丝毫不觉得害怕。也许他们只是还没有学会害怕她吧。 不过，当你走过来时，格维尔懒洋洋地从那一堆小身体中爬出来，抖了抖身子，引来了孩子们一阵“哇哦”的叫声。她向孩子们露出牙齿，挥了挥手，然后慢慢走向你，点了点头。 嗯，如果不是这样的话[pc.name]和孩子们一起工作？她做得出奇地好，尽管她的笑容总让人觉得有些威胁性。 “嗯，你知道的，格温和加雷特也曾经年轻过，所以我也有经验嘛。没错，其实这与处理水精灵的事情并没有太大区别，只不过相对来说，你需要更加谨慎、更加小心翼翼才行。虽然我可能擅长杀戮和暴力行为，但这并不是我这一生中唯一尝试过的事情。毕竟，我曾经尝试过玩“巴尔马iding”这个游戏，说实话，我还挺擅长的。 “不管怎样，最近怎么样？ |最终，你找到了格维尔，发现她正在厨房里煮着一锅散发着淡淡海鲜气息的汤。这位年迈的雌狼不时地搅拌着汤，看起来很满意，然后才转向你。别那样看着我，这些东西都是给孩子们吃的。” 你怀疑，格温之所以会有如此诱人的身材，原因之一就是她总是忍不住会偷偷尝一尝自己为幼儿园的孩子们准备的各种食物。 耸了耸肩：“我父亲教会了我一些基本的自我控制能力。还有，这些食物其实就像小狗的零食——就是我在格温和加勒特断奶后会给它们吃的东西。鱼和其他海鲜对身体很有好处；我真的很希望能从海边获取更多这样的食物，但这里能买到的都只是河里的鱼。不过，这个味道确实很好闻……” “那是海豹脂肪的味道。好吧，[pc.name] — 你来这里并不是为了和我讨论婴儿食品的细节吧。是不是有什么事情需要我帮忙的？ |寻找格维尔的任务让你在育儿室的某个角落找到了那位年迈的女狼人。她坐在一把旧摇椅上，从那个位置观察着孩子们玩耍。她看起来很放松，但你注意到她肌肉中始终存在着那种微妙的紧张感，这种紧张说明她随时准备从椅子上跳起来采取行动。是的，毫无疑问，尤其是当你靠近她时，她看你的眼神——只有当她意识到你不会构成威胁时，那种眼神才会变得柔和一些。 有点紧张吧？ “老习惯难改”，这就是你得到的冷淡回答。虽然我从未想过自己有朝一日能够回家，但能够回到这里，我真的很高兴。我原本以为自己会孤独地死去，周围只有寒冷的风在呼啸，但事实证明我是错的。过去，我总是害怕变老，但现在………我并不介意再活上几年，就为了能够看到因为像我、桑德斯以及我丈夫这样的人，事情会发展成什么样子。看着这些孩子们玩耍，会让我回想起格温和加勒特出生的那些日子。现在，格温也已经成为了母亲。 “是啊。”格维尔沉思了一会儿，脸上浮现出忧郁的神情，然后叹了口气，从椅子上站了起来。“啊，现在这个时候烦恼还太早了。我们能换个话题吗？[pc.name]？" ] |你小心翼翼地站在距离格维尔稍远的地方，等待她完成手头的任务——而她此刻正在照料一大锅散发着鱼粥气味的汤。时间一点点流逝，那位老狼妇的耳朵不时抽动着，终于，她发出一声低哼，转向了你。 “好了，这个汤再炖上几个小时就可以了。你还需要我帮忙什么吗？[pc.name]你只是想看看她的近况，了解她是如何重新适应鹰棘镇生活的；如果劝她回家，却把她强行交给一个与她疏远的家庭，那简直是不负责任的行为。在过了二十年隐居生活之后—— 嗯，我其实并不是什么隐士，”格维尔说道，“那些乔顿人、海豹精、西奥克人，甚至阿瓦奈人——他们都是人，看到我离开他们肯定也很难过，尽管他们理解我为什么这么做。” 那么，经过二十年的流放生活，鹰棘镇已经变得如此不同，对她来说，这里已经完全变成了一个陌生的地方。那么……她现在过得怎么样呢？你知道的，她在女儿的托儿所里尽自己的一份力。 这个主意不错，”格维尔在仔细考虑了她的话之后说道，“如果卡门愿意用她旗下的某个信托基金来资助这个项目的日常运作——她的城堡里从来就没有像那个愚蠢的托勒斯所认为的那样有大量的黄金储藏——那么这个项目肯定有一定的价值。如果我是我女儿，我可能不会选择这条路，但考虑到我在格温的成长过程中缺席了这么长时间，我真的没有资格在她在我不在的时候所做的决定上批评她。她的工作是认真努力的，也赢得了镇上人们的尊重，这就足够了。" 是啊。”她叹了口气，“情况本来可以更好的，但为了她父亲的 sake，我们现在暂时达成了妥协。我们都在容忍对方的存在，说实话，考虑到她刚见到我回家时的反应，我觉得我们能相处得这么好已经超出我的预期了。从那以后……嗯，我只需要坚持不懈地继续努力下去。只要我能追着托勒斯在森林、山脉和冰原上追上二十年，我就一定能在有生之前提前解决我和女儿之间的问题。 她说的那些话简直就是在挑衅别人，对于她未来的日子，你只能祝她一切顺利了。 [var0 |哦，对了，有件事我一直想跟你说。” “什么事呢？” rows.raw: " [flags.GWEYR_NURSERY_MET |[rand |As you draw close, you find mother and daughter having a brief discussion about the nursery's logistics, or at least that's the way Gweyr puts it from the few snippets of actual conversation you manage to catch. It's more the tone of what's being said that tells you more: short, clipped words delivered in a flat, emotionless tone by both women. After a moment or two of this, the two part ways, each one very assiduously not looking at the other — until you greet Gweyr and the old wolfess softens a little. Getting along with her daughter's still a challenge, huh? "We're working through it. At least we can get through a conversation without tearing each others' throats out, which is more than what I can say. I don't ever see her fully forgiving me, and she's got a right to do so, but this isn't so bad either. If I'd been in my daughter's shoes... well, I'd be dead already." Good thing it wasn't Garret that held the grudge against her, then. "Sure, sure. So, is there something you needed of me, or are you just here to make small talk?" |Approaching Gweyr, you find the old wolfess in a chair in a corner of the nursery, folding clothes with a deft hand. One stack is her daughter's usual outfit, at least a dozen copies in the pile; the other just so happens to be Gweyr's own clothes. Like it or not, it's undeniable that the daughter inherited her mother's penchant for uniforms. "Nothing to see here," Gweyr says, rolling her eyes even as a small smile forms on her muzzle. "Just noting that my daughter can't run away from what's in her blood, no matter how many times she denies me." And of the penchant for being everybody's mom... "No doubt from my husband's side of the family. Now then, is there something you need of me? It'll keep my mind occupied while me hands work." |It takes a little bit of searching to find Gweyr — you eventually find her playing with the nursery children, the wolfess surprisingly spry despite her age. It's not surprising given the active life she's led up to this point, but despite her size the kids aren't intimidated by her any. Maybe they just haven't learned to be afraid of her yet. Seeing you approach, though, Gweyr lazily extricates herself from the pile of little bodies and shakes herself off to a chorus of "aww"s. Showing the kids her teeth and giving them a wave, she pads towards you and gives you a nod. "Well, if it isn't [pc.name]." Working with the kids? She's surprisingly good at it, even if she doesn't have a smile that isn't menacing. "Ah well, you know, Gwyn and Garret were young once, so I've had practice. That, and it's really not that different from dealing with selkies, only you have to make the kid gloves extra thick, so to speak. I may be good at bloody death and murder, but it's not the only things I've ever attempted in my life. After all, I tried my hand at barmaiding once and wasn't too bad at it, if I may say. "Anyway, what's up?" |Looking for Gweyr eventually leads you to the nursery kitchens, where Gweyr is putting on a big pot of something that smells vaguely of seafood on to simmer. The old wolfess stirs it a couple of times, looks satisfied, then turns to you. "Don't look at me like that, this stuff is for the kids." You suspect one of the reasons Gwyn is so curvaceous is that she can't help but sneak tastes of anything and everything she cooks for the nursery's residents. A shrug. "My father taught me some basic self-control. That, and this stuff is puppy food — it's the stuff I'd feed Gwyn and Garret just after they were weaned. Fish and other seafood's good for you; I'd love to get more from the coast but all they have here is stuff from the river." It smells really good, though... "That's the seal fat speaking. All right, [pc.name] — you didn't come here to talk the details of baby food with me. Is there something I can help you with?" |Looking for Gweyr has you tracking down the old wolfess in a corner of the nursery, watching the kids play from her vantage point in an old rocking chair. She may appear relaxed, but you note the slight, ever-present tension in her muscles that signals her readiness to leap out of the chair at a moment's notice. Yes, there's no doubt about it, especially after the look she gives you as you approach, softening only when she realizes you're not a threat. A bit high-strung, eh? "Old habits die hard," is the dry answer you get. "While I didn't quite expect to ever be able to come home, I'm glad I did. I thought I'd die with nothing and no one around save for the empty howling of the chill wind, and here I am, being proven wrong by the day. I used to be apprehensive of growing old, but now... I wouldn't mind going on for a handful more years just to be able to see how things turn out because of people like me, Sanders and my husband. Being able to watch over these kids while they play brings me back years to when Gwyn and Garret were born." And now Gwyn's a mother in her own right. "Yes." Gweyr looks thoughtful and melancholy for a moment, then sighs and pushes herself out of the chair. "Ah, it's too early in the day to get all upset. Can we change the topic, [pc.name]?" ] |Carefully, you stand a little way away from Gweyr and wait for her to be done with her current task — which just so happens to be tending to a large pot of what smells like fish gruel. Moments slip by, the old wolfess' ears twitching, until she finally grunts and turns to you. "There, I can let this simmer for a couple of hours. Is there anything you wanted of me, [pc.name]?" You just wanted to check in with her, see how she's fitting back into Hawkethorne; it would be downright irresponsible to convince her to come home and just foist her onto a family that's been estranged from her. After twenty years of exile as a hermit — "Well, I wasn't that much of a hermit," Gweyr snaps. "The jotuns, the selkies, the siorcs, even the avanai — they all count as people, and were sad to see me go even if they understood why I was doing it." Very well, after twenty years of exile from Hawkethorne, then, it's changed to the point where it's a new place for her. So... how's she doing? You see she's making herself useful in her daughter's nursery. "It's not a bad idea," Gweyr says after considering her words. "If Carmen saw fit to fund its day-to-day running with money from one of her trusts — her castle never had any gold in its vaults like the fool Tollus believed — it's got to be worth something. It's not the path I would've chosen had I been in my daughter's shoes, but given that I was missing for so much of Gwyn's life I don't really have the right to criticize her on the decisions she's made in my absence. It's honest work and earns respect from the townsfolk, and that's good enough." That, and being in the nursery all day lets her be close to her daughter. "Yes." A sigh. "Things could always be better, but for now we have an armistice for the sake of her father's sanity. We're tolerating each others' presence, and that's frankly further than I thought we'd be getting along given how she first reacted when I arrived home. From there on out... well, I've just got to keep on chipping away at it. If I can hound Tollus for twenty years across forests, mountains and the ice, I can fix things with my daughter before my dying day." Maybe this is, in some small part, the chance to atone for what I did in my youth. "There's the nursery to handle such matters and I'm not exactly sure if I can or want to stop the both of you fucking each other, so do as you please, I suppose. That being said, I'm going to see what I can do about my son before I die, make up for all the lost time that he should've spent with me." |"Oh, by the by. There's something I've been meaning to talk to you about." That would be? "While I was getting acquainted with the nursery, some of the other women Gwyneth's employed were quick to show off my daughter's darling pups that she'd produced when I was away. There was the first litter by that ne'er-do-well who took to his heels upon receiving the news, of course. Eight at one go — I don't know where that came from, but it certainly wasn't from anyone on my side of the family. Even if my great-great-grandmother was supposedly wraith-touched and her children by the Jarl came out of the womb unusually large and hearty in all respects, she was about quality, not quantity. Eight, indeed..." You have the feeling that there's more she wants to say... "Quite. Ever so quick to call me 'grandma Gweyr', they showed me to another batch of my grandchildren. From you." Ah. Gweyr sighs. "My daughter was a grown woman — if barely, and in body — when you put those puppies into her; it's not as if they weren't going to be well-cared for given the baroness's generous funding for the nursery, either. And given that I was completely absent from her life to the point that unlike Garret, she doesn't even remember my face from when she was a child, I really don't have a leg to stand on to criticize you in any way. Garth's an old softy at heart, and she didn't just inherit that aspect of him, she turned it up to eleven to boot. If Gwyn doesn't have anyone to take care of her, that dangerously submissive streak in her is going to have my daughter presenting herself to anyone who'd care. "I don't know where I'm going with this. Maybe I'm just afraid that my grandkids are going to suffer from the same thing that my kids did, but it's not the exact same case, is it? Even now, I'm still learning about how my husband, Sanders and River conspired to keep mum about me. Even if you're not around as much as Gwyn would like you to be... which means that Grandma Gweyr has to be, I suppose. Maybe this is, in some small part, the chance to atone for what I did in my youth. "Gwyn seems happy and there doesn't appear to be any real harm done, so... just continue being good to her, that's all I ask of you. If this is what my little girl wants to do with her life, being a mother to everyone... even if I feel like part of why she did this was to spite me and everything she'd heard about me, I can't deny the results." |"Don't wish luck on me, you'll need all of it you can get. Tollus is still out there, and though we struck a blow against him and his plans he's still got his crazies cooking up no good gods know where. You say you've kicked his ass twice now, but that's no reason to get overconfident. You're not the only one learning from your mistakes, you know." ] Either way, you're glad she's settled into town and started to make herself known and useful. "I couldn't stand it if I were just to spend the rest of my days just sitting around and doing nothing, that rots the body and brain alike. Use them or lose them, as my father was fond of saying. I'd heard about how the village had grown from Garth and of course had the chance to see it once or twice from afar, but being able to live here is pretty nice. Garth and Sanders have built a nice thing here, if only I were around all this while. Now that I'm to make up for lost time... if you need an old bitch, [pc.name], I'll be around here most days." ] "

rows.original: Gweyr smiles at the question. "Waste not, want not. Even with my son helping, there was only so much I could bring back with me... a woman like me who's used to traveling at a moment's notice does so light, after all. No, given all the favors that the other peoples of the rift have done me over the years, most of what I had, I gave to them. It's just me, my spear and the clothes on my back — I don't need more than that to be comfortable." [party.has arona |"Now that's an attitude I can get behind," Arona says from beside you. "Carrying lots of stuff around just means that folks like my girls can take it off you." ] So she gave it all away, then. "Most importantly, to friends. Just a little extra inducement to remember my son when I brought him to meet them, make sure that his name and face are associated with good things happening, rather than bad. Well, there's something I have for you, too. Give me a moment." Ooh. Standing up, Gweyr stretches and pads out of the nursery towards the family cabin, returning shortly after with a wooden case big enough to fit in both hands. Despite the heavily scuffed exterior, you can tell from what varnish remains that it's well-made and presumably was once pretty grand. "Here, this is for you. A small gesture of my appreciation for not just helping me with Tollus, but also for bringing my family back together. You managed to do what I couldn't despite nipping at Tollus's heels for twenty years — without you, I wouldn't be able to enjoy my dotage." Ah, to call it a dotage is quite self-depreciating. She's still got her wits about her, and is working every day towards something rather than waiting on her bed for a straw death, isn't she? A huff. "Either way, take this with you. I'd have given it to Garret, but the pup needs to learn how to shoulder a proper burden. Don't be fooled by how big it is — it's one of the things Garth and I found in our youth digging around under the earth, what with it being bigger on the inside than it is on the outside. Given the old saying that packs full of loot are often low on supplies, this should help you with that." Begging her pardon, but as small as it is, that's relative to the size of a trunk. It's still not portable enough for you to be lugging it around on your adventures and still be able to move freely. "That's why it's just a saying. Anyway, it's yours now. Just about the right size to serve as a footlocker by your bed or fit in a saddlebag, I'd say. If your adventuring life is anything like what mine was like, you'll be accumulating all kinds of junk that you aren't using but don't want to throw away, either — Garth was such a pack rat in his youth what with him coming from a poor background that it took me years to break him of the bad habit. This should help with that." You nod. The case is light, but bulky; you're sure you'll be able to find somewhere to put it, be it in your room at the Hound, at the Wayfort, or elsewhere. Your storage capacity has increased by ten items. "That's the last of my old possessions," Gweyr says with a sigh. "Now, is there anything else I can do for you?"
rows.translation: 格维尔听到这个问题笑了笑：“不浪费，就不会缺少。即使有我儿子的帮忙，我也能带回来的东西也是有限的……毕竟，像我这样习惯随时准备出发的人，需要的东西本来就很少。不，这些年来，裂隙中的其他民族给了我很多帮助，所以我把大部分东西都给了他们。现在，就只剩下我、我的长矛以及身上的衣服——这些对我来说就已经足够了。 [party.has arona |这种态度我完全支持，”阿罗娜在你身旁说道，“背着那么多东西，其实就是让像我女儿们这样的人来帮你把东西拿下来罢了。 ] 所以，她把一切都告诉了他们。 “最重要的是，要告诉朋友们。这样当我带儿子去见他们时，就能再给他们一些额外的理由，让他们记住我的儿子，确保他们的名字和面孔能与美好的事情联系在一起，而不是坏事。嗯，我也有些东西要给你们。稍等一下。 哦。 格维尔站起身来，伸了伸懒腰，然后从婴儿房走向家庭小屋，不久后便回来了，手里拿着一个木箱，这个木箱大到足以容纳他的双手。尽管箱子的外表已经磨损严重，但从残留的清漆痕迹可以看出，这个箱子制作得相当精良，想必曾经非常漂亮。 给，这是给你的。这是我对你表示感谢的小礼物——不仅因为你在帮助我对付托勒斯这件事上发挥了重要作用，更因为你让我的家庭重新团聚。二十年来，我一直努力追踪托勒斯的踪迹，但却始终无法完成这个任务；如果没有你，我如今也无法安享晚年。 啊，说她老糊涂未免太自贬了。她头脑依然清醒，每天都在为某件事努力，而不是躺在床上等死，不是吗？ “哼，无论如何，把这个带上吧。我本来想把它交给加雷特，但这只小狗需要学会如何承担真正的责任。别被它的外表所迷惑——其实这是加斯和我年轻时在地下挖掘时发现的物品之一，它的内部结构比外部要大很多。俗话说，装满战利品的背包往往物资匮乏，这个建议应该能帮到你解决这个问题。 请原谅我的直言，但尽管它体积很小，相对于树干的大小来说已经算是很小的了。不过，它仍然不够便携，你无法在冒险途中带着它四处移动，同时还能保持自由行动。 “正因为如此，它才只是一种说法而已。总之，现在这个东西是你的了。我觉得它的大小正好可以放在床边当储物箱使用，或者放进马鞍包里。如果你的冒险生活和我当年的经历相似的话，你会积累各种各样既不用又不想扔掉的杂物——加斯年轻时家境贫寒，因此养成了收集东西的习惯，我花了好几年才让他改掉这个坏习惯。这应该能帮上忙。 你点了点头。这个箱子虽然重量不大，但体积却挺大的；你相信自己一定能找到地方放置它，无论是放在“猎犬”旅馆的房间里，还是“荒废驿堡”旅馆里，或者其他任何地方。 你的存储容量增加了十件物品。 那些都是我过去拥有的东西了，”格维尔叹息道，“现在，还有什么我可以为您做的吗？

rows.original: [rand |"Before you ask, I'm fully aware of the bastards that my husband's gone and fathered in my absence." She has? Gweyr seems quite blaise and nonchalant about the entire matter for someone who's stuck to her husband through twenty years of cold, lonely nights. "It's... well, all about the context. I understand the orc thing wasn't really his fault given that he did it under duress, and as for the other one... well, that love potion he stupidly drank was meant for me in a bid to try and convince me to come home with him one of those years. That he ended up feeling guilty about it and was bamboozled into downing the thing himself... well, I prefer that he felt guilty about the idea of drugging me rather than not feeling guilty about it, to be sure. "That's not to say I'm letting Garth off the hook, gods no. But it's not to the degree where I need to make a fuss of it in public — he's the village's unofficial alderman, which means there're already enough tongues wagging about him." You take it that Garth's paying the price for his, uh, infidelity, for lack of a better word to put it... Gweyr smiles, or more correctly, shows you her teeth. "Every day, and he likes it." |"I'm fairly proud of what Garth's been able to do with Hawkethorne in my absence. After I was sent to walk the ice and most people left, he became the de facto village alderman simply by virtue of being one of the few people who remained until Mistress Ivris came around with a new bunch of settlers." You've to admit that Hawkethorne is a cut above most other local settlements, even if they did build on the infrastructure of the old town ruins. Paved streets, for one... you remember the tale Gweyr recounted to you of Hawkethorne twenty years past, and the village's grown a lot since then. "I didn't marry Garth for nothing, you know. Say what you want of my husband, but the man gets shit done. He can get together the best men and materials to throw up something big and impressive in ten days — for example, the Frost Hound itself was built within two weeks, from top to bottom and all adjoining buildings. That's something even the Prince of Tychris wouldn't be able to do." No? "No. He'd have to sit through committees, sign papers, hear people debate whether that trash was a good use of public funds, deal with bagmen skimming cash off the top — for all that he's supposed to be the most powerful man in the Marches, the Prince of Tychris wouldn't be able to build the Hound in two weeks. But my husband can work sorceries like promising workmen to come and deliveries to be shipped with no downpayment but a promise, and it gets done with all funds properly appropriated, no one trying to steal from the pot, and the books balanced. "Things just work when he's around; there's a reason why my father put him in charge of the company's logistics and why I wound up marrying him, that's all I'm saying. I wouldn't trust him to lead, but that's not what he's good at anyway." |"It's strange to be sleeping next to Garth in bed again," Gweyr muses. "Not in a bad way, mind you, but I expected to die cold and alone when my task was done or I got too old to pursue it. Sure, he'd sneak out of town every season to meet me at the edges of the Old Forest, but that's different; I'd forgotten what it was like to have a warm body next to you." Twenty years is a long time to be alone, that's for sure. "It's not something you should forget, but I did anyway and it makes me feel a little guilty. Say what you like, but Garth's more or less managed to keep himself together and faithful to me during that time as well, even if there've been a few mistakes on his part. But it's a good show despite me not being there to breathe down his neck every day, and I feel like I should show my respect to him for pulling it off." |You know, given Gweyr's description of Garth twenty years ago and how he looks now, he's filled out a lot since then. It's hard to believe that he used to be something approaching lithe in his youth. Gweyr laughs at that. "You should've seen him when he first showed up in our camp and asked my father if he could sign up with the Crossed Swords — he was spindly and underfed to the point where you wouldn't have believed he could draw a bowstring and heft a shortsword. Times were lean in the villages where he'd come from, as he told my father. If it'd been up to the younger me, I wouldn't have thought twice about asking him to move on, but my father had different ideas." And what does the older Gweyr think of him? "Hey, I still consider myself married to him, so..." |"We made a good team back in the day, still do. Whether it was on the campaign trail, deep under the earth or striking the ground that this very tavern stands on, he covered for me, and I for him. I guess that's part of why I didn't mind keeping him around... it's not very romantic to openly say that one of the reasons you married your husband was so that he could balance your books for you, but one doesn't get the privilege of sappy romance amidst the cold and wind." Hah. Their proposal must've been a sight to see — what did Garth do, present her with a bunch of rocks? "To be clear, he didn't present me with anything, and if he'd done anything like that I'd have smacked him upside the head for wasting the pay I'd doled out to him on trivialities. The kind of life we led... if you give a shit about someone, you tell him or her as much, and if that someone feels the same way about you he or she says so. The fact that I'd two of his pups inside of me suggested that I gave a damn about him, and he said the same of me, so that was that. Oh, the rest of the company was always looking for an excuse to carouse and get up to all kinds of stupid shit, but as far as the two of us were concerned that was that. We had better things to spend our money on, like getting in on a bunch of settlers we'd heard were heading up north." The founders of Hawkethorne, you take it. Gweyr nods. "Riordan, we'd met before on campaign, his order had hired us from time to time. Garth did the numbers and figured that if we left the company and followed them up north, we could have a go of having a more stable life for the sake of our children. Harder in some ways as settlers and pioneers, but more stable. It felt like the right thing to do to commemorate our impromptu marriage. No priest of any of the Seven, no vows, no ceremonies or gifts, we just recognized each other as such and that was that, then put together our things over the next week and left with Sanders after I'd appointed my second-in-command as my successor." ]
rows.translation: [rand |在你问之前，我早就知道我丈夫在我不在的时候和哪些女人生了孩子。” 她知道吗？对于一个陪伴丈夫度过了二十年漫长而孤独的夜晚的人来说，格维尔对这件事表现得竟然如此淡然、如此不在意。 嗯……其实一切都取决于具体的背景。我知道他当时是在胁迫下才做出那种行为的，所以那些兽人相关的事情真的不是他的错；至于另一件事……那个他愚蠢地喝下的爱情魔药，其实是别人为了说服我当年跟他一起回家而准备的。结果他反而因此感到内疚，还被哄骗着亲自把那东西喝下了……嗯，想到要给我下药时他会感到内疚，总比丝毫不内疚来得好，这一点是肯定的。 “但这并不意味着我要放过加斯，天哪，绝对不是这样。不过也不至于需要在大庭广众之下大吵大闹——他毕竟是村里的非正式议员，这意味着关于他的闲言碎语已经够多了。” 你认为是加斯在为自己那些……呃，不忠的行为付出代价吧，实在找不到更好的词来形容了…… 格维尔笑了，或者更准确地说，是露出了牙齿。“每天都是这样，而且他乐在其中。 |在我不在的时候，加思能够带领鹰棘镇取得这样的成绩，我真的感到非常自豪。当我被派去执行任务，大多数人都离开了，而他却因为是少数几个留下来的人之一，自然而然地成为了这个村庄的实际领导者——直到艾薇莉丝女士带着新一批移民来到这里。 你不得不承认，鹰棘镇确实比大多数其他当地定居点都要先进，即使它们都是建立在旧城镇废墟的基础之上。比如说，那些铺好的街道……你还记得二十年前格维尔给你讲的关于鹰棘镇的故事吧？从那以后，这个村庄已经发展了很多。 你知道，我嫁给加斯可不是白费的。你们可以随便评价我的丈夫，但他的能力确实不容置疑。他能够召集最优秀的人才和最优质的材料，在十天内完成一些规模庞大、令人印象深刻的项目——比如说，那座‘霜犬酒馆’城堡就是从上到下、包括所有附属建筑，都在两周内建成的。就连提克里斯王子也做不到这一点。 不。” “不。他得参加各种委员会会议，签署各种文件，听人们争论那些资金是否被合理使用了，还得处理那些从中贪污私利的中间人——尽管按理说他是边境地区最有权势的人，是提克里斯王子，但他还是无法在两周内完成那项工程。不过我丈夫却能施展魔法，比如让可靠的工人前来工作，让货物在不需要任何预付款的情况下就能被运送过来，只需要一个承诺而已。事情就办成了。只要所有的资金都得到了妥善的使用，没有人试图从中牟取私利，而且各项账目也都相符的话， “事情就会变得很简单。工作每当他出现在我身边时，我就会想到：我父亲之所以让他负责公司的物流工作，而我最终又嫁给了他，其中肯定有原因。我就是想说，我根本不会信任他带领但那本来也不是他的强项。 |再次和加思一起躺在床上睡觉，感觉真是有些奇怪，”格维尔沉思道，“当然，这种感觉并不糟糕。但我原本以为，等到我的任务完成，或者我年纪太大再也无法继续执行这些任务时，我就会孤独地冻死在某个地方。当然，他每个季节都会偷偷离开小镇，到古林的边缘来与我见面，但那和现在的情况不一样……我已经忘记了自己身边有这样一个温暖的身体是什么感觉了。二十年的时间，独自度过，那确实是一段很长的时光。 这件事你不应该忘记，但我还是忘记了，现在想想，会让我感到有些内疚。不管别人怎么说，但在那段时间里，加思基本上还是能够控制自己的行为，并且对我保持着忠诚，尽管他也犯过一些错误。尽管我没有每天都在他身边督促他，但这个节目依然非常成功。我觉得自己应该为他取得的成就表示敬意。 |你知道，根据格维尔二十年前对加斯的描述，以及他现在的样子来看，从那以后他的体格确实变壮了很多。很难相信他年轻时曾经那么瘦削。 格维尔听到这里笑了起来。你真该看看他刚来到我们营地的时候，他问我的父亲是否可以加入‘十字剑团’——那时他瘦骨嶙峋，营养不良到让人根本无法相信他竟然能够拉弓、挥舞短剑。他告诉我父亲，他来自的那些村庄里，日子过得非常艰难。如果是由当年的我来做决定，我一定会毫不犹豫地劝他离开那里，但我父亲的想法却不同。那么，年长的格维尔对他又有什么看法呢？ 嘿，我仍然认为自己和他是夫妻，所以…… |过去我们是一支非常出色的团队，现在依然如此。无论是在竞选活动中，还是在地下深处，又或者是在建造这座酒馆的过程中，他总是为我保驾护航，我也同样为他出力。我想，这大概就是为什么我不介意让他继续留在我身边吧。…虽然直截了当地说，结婚的原因之一就是为了让丈夫帮你整理账目，这听起来并不怎么浪漫，但在寒冷的风中，人们确实很难享受到那种浪漫的氛围。 哈，他们的提议肯定很有意思吧——加斯到底做了什么，难道是拿了一堆石头给她看吗？ “说清楚吧，他根本什么都没给我，要是他真那么做了，我肯定会打他的头，浪费我的工资太不应该了。我会。在我身上，他倾注了很多关爱。我们那样的生活方式……如果你真的在乎某个人，你就会把这种感情直接告诉他/她；而如果对方也有同样的感受，他/她也会告诉你。事实上，我怀上了他的两个孩子，这说明我在乎他，而他也是这么认为的，所以事情就是这样。哦，公司里的其他人都总是找各种借口去玩乐、干些愚蠢的事情，但对我们两个人来说，根本不在乎这些。我们有更重要的事情要花钱去做，比如加入那些据说正往北方迁徙的定居者队伍。鹰棘镇的创始人们，你们应该明白这一点。” 格维尔点了点头：“里奥丹，我们在之前的战役中曾经见过面，他的部队偶尔会雇佣我们。加思算过账，他认为如果我们离开这家公司，跟随他们前往北方，为了我们的孩子们，我们或许能够过上更加稳定的生活。在某些方面，作为定居者和开拓者，我们的生活更加艰辛，但也更加稳定。我们认为，这样做才是对这段即兴婚姻的最好纪念。没有七大宗教中的任何一位神父，没有誓言，没有仪式，也没有礼物，我们只是彼此承认了这一事实，就这样而已。之后，在我指定我的副手作为我的继任者之后，我们在接下来的一周里收拾好了行李，然后和桑德斯一起离开了。" ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"Before you ask, I'm fully aware of the bastards that my husband's gone and fathered in my absence." She has? Gweyr seems quite blaise and nonchalant about the entire matter for someone who's stuck to her husband through twenty years of cold, lonely nights. "It's... well, all about the context. I understand the orc thing wasn't really his fault given that he did it under duress, and as for the other one... well, that love potion he stupidly drank was meant for me in a bid to try and convince me to come home with him one of those years. That he ended up feeling guilty about it and was bamboozled into downing the thing himself... well, I prefer that he felt guilty about the idea of drugging me rather than not feeling guilty about it, to be sure. "That's not to say I'm letting Garth off the hook, gods no. But it's not to the degree where I need to make a fuss of it in public — he's the village's unofficial alderman, which means there're already enough tongues wagging about him." You take it that Garth's paying the price for his, uh, infidelity, for lack of a better word to put it... Gweyr smiles, or more correctly, shows you her teeth. "Every day, and he likes it." |"I'm fairly proud of what Garth's been able to do with Hawkethorne in my absence. After I was sent to walk the ice and most people left, he became the de facto village alderman simply by virtue of being one of the few people who remained until Mistress Ivris came around with a new bunch of settlers." You've to admit that Hawkethorne is a cut above most other local settlements, even if they did build on the infrastructure of the old town ruins. Paved streets, for one... you remember the tale Gweyr recounted to you of Hawkethorne twenty years past, and the village's grown a lot since then. "I didn't marry Garth for nothing, you know. Say what you want of my husband, but the man gets shit done. He can get together the best men and materials to throw up something big and impressive in ten days — for example, the Frost Hound itself was built within two weeks, from top to bottom and all adjoining buildings. That's something even the Prince of Tychris wouldn't be able to do." No? "No. He'd have to sit through committees, sign papers, hear people debate whether that trash was a good use of public funds, deal with bagmen skimming cash off the top — for all that he's supposed to be the most powerful man in the Marches, the Prince of Tychris wouldn't be able to build the Hound in two weeks. But my husband can work sorceries like promising workmen to come and deliveries to be shipped with no downpayment but a promise, and it gets done with all funds properly appropriated, no one trying to steal from the pot, and the books balanced. "Things just work when he's around; there's a reason why my father put him in charge of the company's logistics and why I wound up marrying him, that's all I'm saying. I wouldn't trust him to lead, but that's not what he's good at anyway." |"It's strange to be sleeping next to Garth in bed again," Gweyr muses. "Not in a bad way, mind you, but I expected to die cold and alone when my task was done or I got too old to pursue it. Sure, he'd sneak out of town every season to meet me at the edges of the Old Forest, but that's different; I'd forgotten what it was like to have a warm body next to you." Twenty years is a long time to be alone, that's for sure. "It's not something you should forget, but I did anyway and it makes me feel a little guilty. Say what you like, but Garth's more or less managed to keep himself together and faithful to me during that time as well, even if there've been a few mistakes on his part. But it's a good show despite me not being there to breathe down his neck every day, and I feel like I should show my respect to him for pulling it off." |You know, given Gweyr's description of Garth twenty years ago and how he looks now, he's filled out a lot since then. It's hard to believe that he used to be something approaching lithe in his youth. Gweyr laughs at that. "You should've seen him when he first showed up in our camp and asked my father if he could sign up with the Crossed Swords — he was spindly and underfed to the point where you wouldn't have believed he could draw a bowstring and heft a shortsword. Times were lean in the villages where he'd come from, as he told my father. If it'd been up to the younger me, I wouldn't have thought twice about asking him to move on, but my father had different ideas." And what does the older Gweyr think of him? "Hey, I still consider myself married to him, so..." |"We made a good team back in the day, still do. Whether it was on the campaign trail, deep under the earth or striking the ground that this very tavern stands on, he covered for me, and I for him. I guess that's part of why I didn't mind keeping him around... it's not very romantic to openly say that one of the reasons you married your husband was so that he could balance your books for you, but one doesn't get the privilege of sappy romance amidst the cold and wind." Hah. Their proposal must've been a sight to see — what did Garth do, present her with a bunch of rocks? "To be clear, he didn't present me with anything, and if he'd done anything like that I'd have smacked him upside the head for wasting the pay I'd doled out to him on trivialities. The kind of life we led... if you give a shit about someone, you tell him or her as much, and if that someone feels the same way about you he or she says so. The fact that I'd two of his pups inside of me suggested that I gave a damn about him, and he said the same of me, so that was that. Oh, the rest of the company was always looking for an excuse to carouse and get up to all kinds of stupid shit, but as far as the two of us were concerned that was that. We had better things to spend our money on, like getting in on a bunch of settlers we'd heard were heading up north." The founders of Hawkethorne, you take it. Gweyr nods. "Riordan, we'd met before on campaign, his order had hired us from time to time. Garth did the numbers and figured that if we left the company and followed them up north, we could have a go of having a more stable life for the sake of our children. Harder in some ways as settlers and pioneers, but more stable. It felt like the right thing to do to commemorate our impromptu marriage. No priest of any of the Seven, no vows, no ceremonies or gifts, we just recognized each other as such and that was that, then put together our things over the next week and left with Sanders after I'd appointed my second-in-command as my successor." ] "

rows.original:
[rand
        |Gweyr thinks a moment. "Green. Lush. Plenty of grassland and rolling downs, and in order to go anywhere you've to take barges down the rivers."
        
        There aren't any roads?
        
        "Not safe ones, at the very least. That, and the barges can carry more easier — those rivers are slow and massive, [pc.name]. It's possible to pole a barge upriver with a crew, or have animals draw your barge, even if it's slow going. But the roads... well the main reasons that people don't use the roads is that the dangers lurking in the countryside aside, the roads continually change. Those low hills with their greenery — it all looks like it'd make for great cultivable farmland, but they're all filled with death.
        
        "Outside of the relatively safe spots where cities and villages have sprung up, the earth keeps moving, and it's been that way for as long as anyone can remember, the last two hundred years at least. Hills forcing their way up from underground, sinkholes and crevasses suddenly appearing in the ground to swallow anything and anyone above — it's as if something great and terrible's sleeping under the Heartlands, and it shifts in its slumber every now and then."
        
        You see.
        
        "That, and the wraith-touched creatures are what's mostly preventing people from resettling the frankly excellent land, but no one has any reasonable solution to the former, and the latter just keep coming — often out of the rents in the earth. That's why people use the rivers to get around, they're safer than trying to trek cross-country."
        |"I was born on the move — unlike Garth and me, my mother didn't want to quit being a mercenary when I was born, so I grew up in my father's company, always moving from place to place in the Heartlands. You could argue that it was no place for a pup, but then the entire land was dangerous... being within a wall of palings didn't mean nothing if a wraith-touched beast decided to fuck with the people within.
        
        "Plenty of work for mercenaries. It wasn't considered overkill to hire an entire company to deal with one or two beasts — the nastiest, meanest monsters crawl out from under the earth there, and one person or even a handful of plucky adventurers weren't going to be able to bring to bear the kind of force needed to take them down. It's why there aren't any isolated farmsteads in that place; you're alone, you may as well be meat. And if there weren't any monsters from beneath the earth to fight, there were always more monsters hiding behind their walls, willing to pay to have one company or the other snipe at their rivals. A hundred little warlords, some bigger than others, all of them jockeying for the right to name themselves Belhar's rightful successor state."
        
        Sounds like a dangerous place to live. Why would anyone stay there?
        
        "Because, my [pc.mf
            |boy
            |girl
        ], the Heartlands are the richest, most abundant lands on the continent even after being blasted to smithereens from the Godswar. There's good eating, there's good drinking... not much call for shaft and seam mining when the earth turns itself so much, but people pan the rivers and dig pits into the ground. You hear of the glorious cities of the old empire, towers that stretched up to touch the sky... and all of them were swallowed up by the earth. Sometimes, when you get a quake, a bunch of half-buried ruins will show up and treasure hunters flock to the place shortly after once word gets out. Bringing their wealth with them and bringing wealth back after risking their lives for it... only to realize there's nothing for sale to spend it on.
        
        "Growing up like that made me tough by necessity — especially after my mother got her throat torn open by a set of claws — but while I realized that I wouldn't be who I am today without it, I also didn't want my children to be rootless like I was. It's why Garth and I left to settle Hawkethorne when I discovered I was pregnant; it'd be a hard but stable life, and the original plan was for us to send them for a tour or two with the Crossed Swords when they were old enough. Then... well, I've already told you."
        |"The heartlands... they're a place dotted with a hundred different warlords, all squabbling with each other. Any two-bit would-be monarch with a shred of power, be it muscle, magic, or whatever is setting up shop, claiming one of the safe havens amongst the rivers and downs and declaring themselves the true successor to the old empire. I don't know, maybe some of them might even have legit claims, but most of those the Crossed Swords contacted with were simply glorified robbers who'd decided to settle down and be stationary instead of roving up and down the rivers."
        
        So the place is in constant political turmoil, huh?
        
        A nod. "Well, father just called it the churn, and it made work for us. One petty ruler comes up and hires us to sack his or her rival, and when one of them inevitably tries to double-cross us and we don't get paid, we sack and loot the asshole too. Don't get me wrong, we never allowed ourselves to be contracted out to someone who obviously couldn't pay us. Still, when you get big fish in a small pond, people get ideas like they can hire mercenaries of reasonable repute and not give them their due."
        
        With how dangerous the Heartlands are, it's a wonder how any of them get the wealth to hire mercenaries on the regular... 
        
        "The land on which the old empire sat upon was the richest, lushest land on the continent, said to be blessed by the gods themselves. It still is — if nothing else, so many of our clients were well-dressed and fat, and the people living there weren't starving. The harvest was amazingly bountiful, if you didn't mind having to send out folks with spears and shields to defend those bringing it in before it all rotted in the fields. 
        
        "To think that all this was just a fraction of the bounty the old empire must've been producing in its heyday... if you're one of the people who had the luck to be born within the heavy walls of one of the more powerful warlords and had no reason to leave at all whatsoever, it wasn't a bad life. Can't say the same for poor bastards like us."
        |"The rivers, the barges, the waters... they're what keeps the Heartlands going. Hiring a barge or two to bring the company from job to job wasn't cheap, but at least there were no shortage of captains willing to make the trip. Having armed men on your craft makes it a lot less likely to be waylaid by river pirates, after all. Not enough for any of them to offer my father or I a discount... but our presence was appreciated all the same."
        
        Why exactly were the rivers safe? If the earth moved that often, wouldn't one of the distrophisms eventually strike at a river's course? Or the wraith-touched beasts, either — why wouldn't they attack people on the water?
        
        Gweyr shrugs. "Fuck if I know. There were one or two attacks by beasts on barges during my time, but the rivers were far safer than trying to cross the grasslands and downs were. Best theory I heard was that it wasn't that the rivers prevented the quakes and such, but that the quakes eventually rerouted all the rivers to flow along places where they didn't happen. Same thing with the beasts: if they appear from the cracks, crevices and whatnot, then the places where the earth doesn't move are naturally going to be safer. Either way, you want to get anything or anyone anywhere, you're taking a barge... which makes the barge captains pretty important people."
        
        Important that mercenaries would be hired to take out a rival or two?
        
        "Oh for gods' sakes, no. Not that there isn't any lack of backstabbing amongst that lot as there is amongst any other group of nobs, but they know how important they are to the Heartlands and wouldn't wage open war. Sabotage, intimidation, fraud, yes... but killing them and burning or stealing their fleets of barges? That's asking for trouble right there, and well above our pay grade. Even the petty warlords tend to leave the river barges alone — all they have to do is collectively embargo you and you're soon starving. Then again, someone might be willing to cheat on the rest of them, for a hefty fee...
        
        "Neither Father nor I liked the bastards. The most we ever spoke to them was to secure the safe passage of our people up or downriver, and we preferred it that way."
        |Common legend is that the Heartland is full of ruins with unimaginable treasures lying beneath the earth — how much truth is there to those tales?
        
        Gweyr mulls over her answer before giving it to you. "Some. You can't go around digging in someone's field and expect to unearth a chest full of riches, but it's fairly common for someone to find a few shards of old pottery or an ancient coin every now and then. The local folktales have it that the imperial heartland was the most densely-populated place in the world at the time, [pc.name]. City folk lived in homes that were stacked upon each other ten, fifteen high like rats in cages, while every crossroads had a waystation doing brisk business offering rest to the weary. Suffice to say that there were a lot of people, and all of that got swallowed up by the earth. The wraith-touched beasts that come out from under the ground — the locals say that they're ancient imperial citizens, warped by the same forces that cause the land to shift and unleashed upon their descendants."
        
        "Different warlords responded differently to the ruins which the quakes unearthed. Some of them would send their own people, some of them were afraid of them and would let the inevitable flock of treasure hunters deal with it. Others hired expendables like us to clear out the place, grab any loot and make sure there weren't any dangers lurking about that needed taking care of. Naturally, we were handsomely paid, usually a flat fee with a cut of anything found."
        
        Going into those places must've been perilous.
        
        "There weren't traps or anything — more often than not, those were mostly the remnants of homes, civic buildings, even a half-buried bridge once. You wouldn't set a snare in the middle of your own kitchen, would you? No, the most common killers were the mundane: suffocation from bad air from the places having buried too long was the biggest one. Unstable buildings falling on people. The dark making people unhinged and freak out. But those don't make for good stories, so all you hear are the tales of twisted beasts from the deep."
        
        "And as for treasure... well, the things we found were scattered so loosely and so commonly that they must've been trash, but trash to the people of old Belhar is treasure to the likes of us. There were other things we found too, things that must've gotten swallowed up more recently. The remains of people. Half a farmstead. Garth and I found a whole barge once in a half-submerged cavern, complete with its rotted crew and cargo, gods know how they got there. You won't be finding gold and jewels, but the odds and ends you do pick up might be saleable to wizards interested in digging up the past, or warlords seeking to bolster their claim to the throne of old Belhar in any way they can."
        
        So no lost vaults overflowing with gems and ancient electrum hawks, no buried wizards' towers, no lost pleasure palaces waiting to be plundered?
        
        "I don't doubt that if the people of old Belhar were as fuck-all rich as they were, some of those must've existed — after all, it's said that the entire catfolk population of the region is descended from pleasure-slaves brought in to fill the brothels and boudoirs. But as to the holes and crevices that Garth, I and the rest of the company went spelunking in... no, no fabulous riches beyond compare."
        |About the manifold quakes that shake the heartlands... what are the theories she's heard about them? As to why they happen, that is.
        
        Gweyr shrugs. "Your guess is as good as mine."
        
        You know that, but you want to hear some of the folklore that she came into contact with while down south. [pc.bgMulti scholar arcanist
            |While folk tales may be just that with all that entails, your time as a scholar at the academy impressed upon you that sometimes they're grown from a seed of truth... or at the very least reveal something of the local culture and people. 
            |While folk tales may be just that with all that entails, your time as an arcanist taught you that sometimes folk tales can harbor a grain of truth that can be a starting point for investigation. 
        ]Just a passing interest, really, since you're not planning to head down south with Kasyrra running around, but still. What can she tell you?
        
        "Well, hmm. The biggest one I heard was that there's one of the greatest wraiths from the Godswar still locked inside the earth. For one reason or another, the gods weren't able to destroy it like the others, so they settled for chaining it deep beneath the spot where it made its throne and putting their blessing upon the land so it couldn't seep out over time. It's a neat explanation for how the Heartlands can still be so rich and fertile after everything that's happened to it, but so completely and utterly fucked once you dig any deeper than twelve feet beneath the ground."
        
        That makes sense. Any others that she's heard?
        
        "Well, the second biggest one is more or less the same as the first, only with a corrupted dragon instead, so I won't go into detail on that. There's also one where people say that it's the magics that the mages of Estelore released, the power of the portals that destabilized the weave of the world... and the other one that the religious hierarchies preferred, being that the sins and iniquity of the people of old Belhar coalesced and manifested into a tangible force from their sheer depth and degree, a curse that lures people in with its beautiful and lush exterior, only for them to find death once there."
        
        Hmm.
        
        "The only thing all the folktales I heard agree on is that prior to the Godswar, the imperial heartland was as stable and peaceful as could be — the worst that would happen was a bit of minor flooding from the rivers during a particularly heavy rain from the coast. But quakes, massive wildfires, destructive storms and the like — no, none of that. Whatever's twisting the land right now, it's a consequence of that black spot on our history."
    ]
rows.translation:
[rand
        |格维尔思考了一会儿，然后说道：“绿色的、茂盛的草原，一望无际的草地和连绵起伏的丘陵……要想去任何地方，都得乘着驳船沿着河流前进。”

“那么根本没有道路吗？”

“至少没有安全的道路。而且，驳船运输起来更加方便——那些河流水流缓慢，河道也很宽阔。[pc.name]可以雇佣船员用篙将驳船划向上游，或者让动物来拉驳船，尽管这样行驶速度会比较慢。但是道路……嗯，人们不选择使用道路的主要原因是，除了乡间潜伏的各种危险之外，道路本身也在不断发生变化。那些长满绿植的低矮小山，看起来全都非常适合耕种，但实际上，它们全都布满了死亡。

“在那些城市和村庄得以建立、相对安全的地区之外，大地一直在不断移动，至少在过去的两百年里，一直都是这样。山丘从地下缓缓隆起，地面突然出现天坑和裂缝，将一切经过之物吞噬殆尽——仿佛在中心地带之下，沉睡着某种既伟大又可怕的存在，而它偶尔会在这沉睡中翻动身躯。你看，

“正是这些被怨灵影响的生物，以及那些受到怨灵影响而变异的生物，才阻碍了人们重新定居在这片其实非常肥沃的土地上。对于前者，目前还没有任何可行的解决办法；而对于后者，它们却一直在不断出现——往往是从地底中钻出来的。这就是为什么人们会选择利用河流来出行，因为这样比徒步穿越山区要安全得多。
        |我是在漂泊中出生的——与加斯不同，我出生时母亲并不想放弃她那佣兵的生活，因此我在父亲的团队中长大，一直在中央地带四处迁徙。有人可能会说这样的环境不适合一只幼犬成长，但事实上，整个地区都充满了危险…… 即使被围在栅栏之中，如果有什么被怨灵影响的野兽决定来骚扰里面的人，那这一切也毫无意义。

“对于雇佣兵来说，这可是大量的工作。为了对付一两只野兽而雇佣一整支雇佣兵队伍，根本不算过分——因为那里会出现一些极其凶恶、残忍的怪物，单靠一个人，甚至是一小群勇敢的冒险者，根本无法凝聚起足够的力量来消灭它们。这就是为什么那个地方没有任何与世隔绝的农庄的原因——如果你独自一人待在那里，那你简直就跟肉一样，很容易成为别人的猎物。而且，即使没有地底出来的怪物需要对抗，也总会有更多的怪物隐藏在墙后，它们愿意花钱让某一方去狙击它们的竞争对手。一百个小军阀，有些势力比其他的大一些，他们都在争抢那个能够自称是贝尔哈尔合法继承者的头衔。

听起来那地方简直太危险了，怎么会有人愿意住在那里呢？
        
        因为，我的[pc.mf
            |男孩
            |女孩
        ]即使在神战中被炸得片瓦不留，心土之地依然是这片大陆上最富饶、物产最丰富的地区。这里有美味的佳肴，有醇香的酒饮……当地的地壳活动如此频繁，人们几乎不需要进行采矿作业，只需在河流中淘洗矿物，或在地面上挖坑取材即可。你一定听说过那个古老帝国的辉煌城市，那些高耸入云的塔楼……而如今，它们全都被大地吞没了。有时候，当地震发生时，一些半埋在土里的废墟就会暴露出来，而一旦消息传开，寻宝者们就会立刻蜂拥而至。他们带着自己的财富来到这里，又冒着生命危险去赚取更多的财富……却最终发现，根本没有什么东西可以用来花费这些钱。

“这样的成长环境迫使我变得坚强——尤其是在我的母亲被一把爪子划开了喉咙之后——但我虽然明白没有这些经历，我就不会成为今天的自己，但我也不希望我的孩子们像我一样没有根基、没有依靠。这就是为什么当我发现自己怀孕后，我和加思决定搬到鹰棘镇去生活的原因——那里的生活虽然艰苦，但却安定。原本的计划是等孩子们长大一些后，让我们带着他们和“十字剑团”一起去旅行几次。那么……嗯，我已经告诉过你了。
        |那些内陆地区……到处都是成百上千个军阀，他们互相争斗不休。任何有点势力的人，无论是依靠武力、魔法，还是其他手段，都会在那里建立据点，宣称自己是那个古老帝国的真正继承者，并将那些地势险要、安全的地区据为己有。我也不确定，也许其中有些人确实有合理的诉求，但Crossed Swords接触过的那些人，大多数其实都只是些改过自新的强盗——他们决定安定下来，不再在河流沿岸四处游荡了。"
        
        所以这个地方一直处于政治动荡之中，是吧？

他点了点头：“嗯，我们父亲把这种状况叫做‘政治动荡’，而这种动荡反而为我们带来了生意。有些小统治者会雇我们去赶走他们的竞争对手，而当其中某一方试图背叛我们、导致我们拿不到报酬时，我们就会把那个混蛋也赶走并抢走他们的财产。别误会，我们从来不会同意把工作交给那些显然没有能力支付我们报酬的人。不过，当一个小池塘里突然出现了“大鱼”时，人们就会产生这样的念头：可以雇佣一些声誉不错的“雇佣兵”，而不用支付他们应得的报酬。"
        
        考虑到腹地的环境如此危险，他们究竟是如何获得足够的财富来定期雇佣雇佣兵的…… 

“据说，那个古老帝国曾经统治的土地是这片大陆上最富饶、最肥沃的土地，甚至被认为是受到神明庇佑的地方。现在依然如此——至少从很多客户的外表来看，他们都衣着光鲜，体态丰腴；而那些生活在那里的人们也并没有挨饿。收成确实非常丰富，只不过为了防止粮食在田里腐烂，我们不得不派出手持长矛和盾牌的人去保护那些负责运送粮食的人。 
        
        想想看，这一切只不过是那个古老帝国在鼎盛时期所拥有的财富的一小部分而已……如果你有幸出生在某个强大军阀的领地内，根本没有任何理由离开那里，那么这样的生活其实也挺不错的。但我们这些可怜的家伙，就另当别论了。
        |那些河流、那些驳船、那些水域……正是它们维持着心脏之地的运转。雇用一两条驳船来运送公司所需的物资，费用确实不低，但至少有足够的船长愿意承担这项任务。毕竟，如果在船上配备武装人员，就能大大降低遭到河盗劫掠的风险。虽然他们的数量还不足以让我们父亲或我得到任何折扣……但我们的存在还是受到了他们的欢迎。
        
        那些河流究竟为何能够保持安全呢？如果地球如此频繁地发生地质变动，难道就不会有某种灾变最终影响到河流的走向吗？那些被怨灵影响的野兽也同样如此——它们为什么不会攻击在水上活动的人类呢？
        
        格维尔耸了耸肩：“我哪知道啊。在我那段时间里，确实有一两次野兽袭击了运货船，但河流比穿越草原和丘陵地带要安全得多。我听过的最合理的解释是：并不是河流阻止了地震之类的灾害，而是地震最终改变了河流的流向，使它们改道流经那些不会发生地震的地方。对于那些怪物来说也是如此：如果它们是从裂缝、缝隙之类的地方出现的，那么那些地面没有发生移动的区域自然就会更安全一些。无论如何，如果你想在任何地方获取任何东西或遇到任何人，你都得乘坐驳船才能到达那里。因此，这些驳船船长们其实都是相当重要的人物。
        
        雇佣佣兵来对付一两个竞争对手，这真的有必要吗？

“哦，看在上帝的份上，不必。虽然那些人当中也像其他贵族群体一样充满了背信弃义的行为，但他们知道自己对腹地的重要性，因此不会发动公开的战争。破坏、恐吓、欺诈，这些手段当然可以使用……但直接杀害他们，还烧毁或抢走他们的驳船队？那可真是自找麻烦，而且完全超出了我们的能力范围。就连那些小军阀们通常也不会去招惹这些河上的驳船——他们只需要联合起来对某一方实施贸易禁运，对方很快就会陷入饥荒。不过，也有人可能会为了一笔丰厚的报酬，而在其他人面前作弊……
        
        我和父亲都不喜欢那些混蛋。我们与他们交谈，也只是为了确保我们族人能够安全地沿河而上或而下，我们更希望保持这种状态。
        |人们普遍传说，中心地带遍布废墟，地下埋藏着难以想象的宝藏——这些传说有多少真实性呢？

格维尔在回答你之前，仔细思考了一下自己的话。“有些是真的。你不能随便在别人的田地里挖来挖去，就指望能挖出一箱财宝来，但偶尔也有人会发现一些古老的陶器碎片或一枚古代硬币。当地的民间传说称，在那个时候，帝国的腹地是世界上人口最密集的地区。[pc.name]城市里的人们居住在层层叠叠的房屋中，这些房屋有的有十层高，有的有十五层高，就像笼子里的老鼠一样。而每一个十字路口都有一家客栈，生意十分兴隆，为疲惫的人们提供休息的地方。可以说，那里的人口非常多，而所有这些人都被大地吞没了。那些从地下钻出来的怪物——当地人说，它们其实是古代帝国的子民，由于那些导致大地变形的力量而发生了变异，然后这些变异的怪物就被释放出来，危害后代的生存。
        
        不同的军阀对地震揭露出来的那些遗迹采取了不同的应对措施。有些会派出自己的手下去处理，有些则害怕那些遗迹会带来危险，便任由那些蜂拥而至的寻宝者去处理它们。还有的则雇佣像我们这样的临时工，让我们去清理那些地方，抢走能抢到的财物，并确保那里没有需要处理的危险隐患。当然，我们得到的报酬也是相当丰厚的——通常是一笔固定的费用，再加上所找到财物的其中一部分作为提成。
        
        进入那些地方肯定非常危险。

“那里并没有陷阱之类的东西——通常情况下，那些地方大多是一些房屋的残骸、公共建筑，甚至还有曾经有一座半埋在土里的桥。你总不会在自己的厨房里设置陷阱吧？不，最常见的致死原因其实是那些看似平常的因素：在那些尸体被埋葬太久的地方，恶劣的空气会导致人们窒息，这是最主要的致死原因之一。不稳固的建筑物会倒塌压在人们身上，暗影也会让人失去理智、陷入恐慌。但这些事情并不适合被编成有趣的故事，所以人们听到的，往往只是关于深海中那些恐怖怪物的传说罢了。"
        
        至于那些财宝……嗯，我们找到的那些东西分散得太过零乱，也太过普通，所以它们应该只是垃圾罢了。但对古老的贝尔哈尔人来说，这些垃圾对我们来说却就是财宝。我们还找到了其他一些东西，那些应该是最近才被丢弃的。人类的遗骸……半个农庄……加斯和我在一个半淹没的洞穴里发现了一整艘驳船，船上还有腐烂的船员和货物，天知道它们是怎么到那里去的。你不会在这里找到黄金或珠宝，但那些你捡到的零星物品，或许能卖给那些对探索过去感兴趣的巫师，或者那些想尽一切办法来巩固自己对古老贝尔哈尔王位宣称权的军阀们。"
        
        那么，就不存在那些充满宝石和古代电金鹰的失落宝库，不存在被埋藏的巫师塔，也不存在那些等待被洗劫的失落享乐宫殿了吗？

“我毫不怀疑，如果古代贝尔哈尔的人们真的有那么富有的话，那么其中一些东西肯定存在——毕竟，有传言称，这个地区的所有猫族都是从被带到这里来充实妓院和闺房的享乐奴隶后代。但是至于加思、我以及其他同事们去探索过的那些洞穴和裂缝……不，里面并没有什么无与伦比的巨额财富。
        |关于那些震撼大陆腹地的频繁地震……她听说过哪些关于它们的理论呢？也就是关于这些地震为何会发生的理论。

格维尔耸了耸肩：“你猜的和我一样，也没什么把握。”

你心里其实明白这一点，但还是想听听她在南方期间听到的那些民间传说吧。 [pc.bgMulti scholar arcanist
            |虽然民间故事可能仅仅只是故事而已，但你在学院里作为学者的经历让你认识到，有时候这些故事其实源自某些真实的事件……或者至少能够反映当地的文化和人们的生活。 
            |虽然民间故事通常只是普通的传说而已，但你作为秘术师的经历让你明白，有时候这些故事中确实蕴含着一丝真相，而这些真相可以成为进一步调查的起点。 
        ]其实只是随便问问而已，毕竟你也不打算带着卡希拉去南方旅行，不过还是想了解一下……她能告诉你些什么呢？

“嗯，我听说的最大一个传闻是，有一只来自‘神战’时期的最强大的怨灵还被困在地下呢。由于种种原因，众神无法像摧毁其他东西那样消灭它，于是他们决定将它封印在它建立王座的深处，并为这片土地施加祝福，以防止它的力量随着时间的流逝而渗漏出来。这个解释确实很合理，能够说明为什么在经历了种种变故之后，腹地地区依然能够保持如此富饶和肥沃的地貌；但一旦你深入地下十二英尺以下，就会发现那里其实已经彻底被破坏、变得一片荒芜了。
        
        有道理。她还听说过其他什么说法吗？

“嗯，第二种说法和第一种差不多，只不过其中出现的是一条被腐蚀的龙，所以我就不详细介绍了。还有一种说法是，真正导致世界结构失衡的，其实是埃斯托洛尔的法师们释放出的魔法，以及那些传送门所蕴含的力量。还有另一种观点，为那些宗教权威们所青睐：他们认为，古代贝尔哈尔人民的罪孽与邪恶汇聚在一起，从它们深邃的本质中产生出一种有形的力量——一种诅咒。这种诅咒以美丽而诱人的外表吸引人们，但一旦人们落入其中，便会面临死亡。"
        
        嗯。

“我听过的所有民间故事都有一个共同点：在神战之前，帝国的核心地区是极其稳定和和平的——最糟糕的情况也不过是在沿海地区遭遇特大暴雨时，河流会引发一些小规模的洪水。但是地震、大规模的野火、破坏性强的风暴之类的灾害，根本不可能发生。目前那些正在改变这片土地状况的现象，都是我们历史上那个暗影事件的后果。
    ]
