"
    [rand
        |Gweyr thinks a moment. "Green. Lush. Plenty of grassland and rolling downs, and in order to go anywhere you've to take barges down the rivers."
        
        There aren't any roads?
        
        "Not safe ones, at the very least. That, and the barges can carry more easier — those rivers are slow and massive, [pc.name]. It's possible to pole a barge upriver with a crew, or have animals draw your barge, even if it's slow going. But the roads... well the main reasons that people don't use the roads is that the dangers lurking in the countryside aside, the roads continually change. Those low hills with their greenery — it all looks like it'd make for great cultivable farmland, but they're all filled with death.
        
        "Outside of the relatively safe spots where cities and villages have sprung up, the earth keeps moving, and it's been that way for as long as anyone can remember, the last two hundred years at least. Hills forcing their way up from underground, sinkholes and crevasses suddenly appearing in the ground to swallow anything and anyone above — it's as if something great and terrible's sleeping under the Heartlands, and it shifts in its slumber every now and then."
        
        You see.
        
        "That, and the wraith-touched creatures are what's mostly preventing people from resettling the frankly excellent land, but no one has any reasonable solution to the former, and the latter just keep coming — often out of the rents in the earth. That's why people use the rivers to get around, they're safer than trying to trek cross-country."
        |"I was born on the move — unlike Garth and me, my mother didn't want to quit being a mercenary when I was born, so I grew up in my father's company, always moving from place to place in the Heartlands. You could argue that it was no place for a pup, but then the entire land was dangerous... being within a wall of palings didn't mean nothing if a wraith-touched beast decided to fuck with the people within.
        
        "Plenty of work for mercenaries. It wasn't considered overkill to hire an entire company to deal with one or two beasts — the nastiest, meanest monsters crawl out from under the earth there, and one person or even a handful of plucky adventurers weren't going to be able to bring to bear the kind of force needed to take them down. It's why there aren't any isolated farmsteads in that place; you're alone, you may as well be meat. And if there weren't any monsters from beneath the earth to fight, there were always more monsters hiding behind their walls, willing to pay to have one company or the other snipe at their rivals. A hundred little warlords, some bigger than others, all of them jockeying for the right to name themselves Belhar's rightful successor state."
        
        Sounds like a dangerous place to live. Why would anyone stay there?
        
        "Because, my [pc.mf
            |boy
            |girl
        ], the Heartlands are the richest, most abundant lands on the continent even after being blasted to smithereens from the Godswar. There's good eating, there's good drinking... not much call for shaft and seam mining when the earth turns itself so much, but people pan the rivers and dig pits into the ground. You hear of the glorious cities of the old empire, towers that stretched up to touch the sky... and all of them were swallowed up by the earth. Sometimes, when you get a quake, a bunch of half-buried ruins will show up and treasure hunters flock to the place shortly after once word gets out. Bringing their wealth with them and bringing wealth back after risking their lives for it... only to realize there's nothing for sale to spend it on.
        
        "Growing up like that made me tough by necessity — especially after my mother got her throat torn open by a set of claws — but while I realized that I wouldn't be who I am today without it, I also didn't want my children to be rootless like I was. It's why Garth and I left to settle Hawkethorne when I discovered I was pregnant; it'd be a hard but stable life, and the original plan was for us to send them for a tour or two with the Crossed Swords when they were old enough. Then... well, I've already told you."
        |"The heartlands... they're a place dotted with a hundred different warlords, all squabbling with each other. Any two-bit would-be monarch with a shred of power, be it muscle, magic, or whatever is setting up shop, claiming one of the safe havens amongst the rivers and downs and declaring themselves the true successor to the old empire. I don't know, maybe some of them might even have legit claims, but most of those the Crossed Swords contacted with were simply glorified robbers who'd decided to settle down and be stationary instead of roving up and down the rivers."
        
        So the place is in constant political turmoil, huh?
        
        A nod. "Well, father just called it the churn, and it made work for us. One petty ruler comes up and hires us to sack his or her rival, and when one of them inevitably tries to double-cross us and we don't get paid, we sack and loot the asshole too. Don't get me wrong, we never allowed ourselves to be contracted out to someone who obviously couldn't pay us. Still, when you get big fish in a small pond, people get ideas like they can hire mercenaries of reasonable repute and not give them their due."
        
        With how dangerous the Heartlands are, it's a wonder how any of them get the wealth to hire mercenaries on the regular... 
        
        "The land on which the old empire sat upon was the richest, lushest land on the continent, said to be blessed by the gods themselves. It still is — if nothing else, so many of our clients were well-dressed and fat, and the people living there weren't starving. The harvest was amazingly bountiful, if you didn't mind having to send out folks with spears and shields to defend those bringing it in before it all rotted in the fields. 
        
        "To think that all this was just a fraction of the bounty the old empire must've been producing in its heyday... if you're one of the people who had the luck to be born within the heavy walls of one of the more powerful warlords and had no reason to leave at all whatsoever, it wasn't a bad life. Can't say the same for poor bastards like us."
        |"The rivers, the barges, the waters... they're what keeps the Heartlands going. Hiring a barge or two to bring the company from job to job wasn't cheap, but at least there were no shortage of captains willing to make the trip. Having armed men on your craft makes it a lot less likely to be waylaid by river pirates, after all. Not enough for any of them to offer my father or I a discount... but our presence was appreciated all the same."
        
        Why exactly were the rivers safe? If the earth moved that often, wouldn't one of the distrophisms eventually strike at a river's course? Or the wraith-touched beasts, either — why wouldn't they attack people on the water?
        
        Gweyr shrugs. "Fuck if I know. There were one or two attacks by beasts on barges during my time, but the rivers were far safer than trying to cross the grasslands and downs were. Best theory I heard was that it wasn't that the rivers prevented the quakes and such, but that the quakes eventually rerouted all the rivers to flow along places where they didn't happen. Same thing with the beasts: if they appear from the cracks, crevices and whatnot, then the places where the earth doesn't move are naturally going to be safer. Either way, you want to get anything or anyone anywhere, you're taking a barge... which makes the barge captains pretty important people."
        
        Important that mercenaries would be hired to take out a rival or two?
        
        "Oh for gods' sakes, no. Not that there isn't any lack of backstabbing amongst that lot as there is amongst any other group of nobs, but they know how important they are to the Heartlands and wouldn't wage open war. Sabotage, intimidation, fraud, yes... but killing them and burning or stealing their fleets of barges? That's asking for trouble right there, and well above our pay grade. Even the petty warlords tend to leave the river barges alone — all they have to do is collectively embargo you and you're soon starving. Then again, someone might be willing to cheat on the rest of them, for a hefty fee...
        
        "Neither Father nor I liked the bastards. The most we ever spoke to them was to secure the safe passage of our people up or downriver, and we preferred it that way."
        |Common legend is that the Heartland is full of ruins with unimaginable treasures lying beneath the earth — how much truth is there to those tales?
        
        Gweyr mulls over her answer before giving it to you. "Some. You can't go around digging in someone's field and expect to unearth a chest full of riches, but it's fairly common for someone to find a few shards of old pottery or an ancient coin every now and then. The local folktales have it that the imperial heartland was the most densely-populated place in the world at the time, [pc.name]. City folk lived in homes that were stacked upon each other ten, fifteen high like rats in cages, while every crossroads had a waystation doing brisk business offering rest to the weary. Suffice to say that there were a lot of people, and all of that got swallowed up by the earth. The wraith-touched beasts that come out from under the ground — the locals say that they're ancient imperial citizens, warped by the same forces that cause the land to shift and unleashed upon their descendants."
        
        "Different warlords responded differently to the ruins which the quakes unearthed. Some of them would send their own people, some of them were afraid of them and would let the inevitable flock of treasure hunters deal with it. Others hired expendables like us to clear out the place, grab any loot and make sure there weren't any dangers lurking about that needed taking care of. Naturally, we were handsomely paid, usually a flat fee with a cut of anything found."
        
        Going into those places must've been perilous.
        
        "There weren't traps or anything — more often than not, those were mostly the remnants of homes, civic buildings, even a half-buried bridge once. You wouldn't set a snare in the middle of your own kitchen, would you? No, the most common killers were the mundane: suffocation from bad air from the places having buried too long was the biggest one. Unstable buildings falling on people. The dark making people unhinged and freak out. But those don't make for good stories, so all you hear are the tales of twisted beasts from the deep."
        
        "And as for treasure... well, the things we found were scattered so loosely and so commonly that they must've been trash, but trash to the people of old Belhar is treasure to the likes of us. There were other things we found too, things that must've gotten swallowed up more recently. The remains of people. Half a farmstead. Garth and I found a whole barge once in a half-submerged cavern, complete with its rotted crew and cargo, gods know how they got there. You won't be finding gold and jewels, but the odds and ends you do pick up might be saleable to wizards interested in digging up the past, or warlords seeking to bolster their claim to the throne of old Belhar in any way they can."
        
        So no lost vaults overflowing with gems and ancient electrum hawks, no buried wizards' towers, no lost pleasure palaces waiting to be plundered?
        
        "I don't doubt that if the people of old Belhar were as fuck-all rich as they were, some of those must've existed — after all, it's said that the entire catfolk population of the region is descended from pleasure-slaves brought in to fill the brothels and boudoirs. But as to the holes and crevices that Garth, I and the rest of the company went spelunking in... no, no fabulous riches beyond compare."
        |About the manifold quakes that shake the heartlands... what are the theories she's heard about them? As to why they happen, that is.
        
        Gweyr shrugs. "Your guess is as good as mine."
        
        You know that, but you want to hear some of the folklore that she came into contact with while down south. [pc.bgMulti scholar arcanist
            |While folk tales may be just that with all that entails, your time as a scholar at the academy impressed upon you that sometimes they're grown from a seed of truth... or at the very least reveal something of the local culture and people. 
            |While folk tales may be just that with all that entails, your time as an arcanist taught you that sometimes folk tales can harbor a grain of truth that can be a starting point for investigation. 
        ]Just a passing interest, really, since you're not planning to head down south with Kasyrra running around, but still. What can she tell you?
        
        "Well, hmm. The biggest one I heard was that there's one of the greatest wraiths from the Godswar still locked inside the earth. For one reason or another, the gods weren't able to destroy it like the others, so they settled for chaining it deep beneath the spot where it made its throne and putting their blessing upon the land so it couldn't seep out over time. It's a neat explanation for how the Heartlands can still be so rich and fertile after everything that's happened to it, but so completely and utterly fucked once you dig any deeper than twelve feet beneath the ground."
        
        That makes sense. Any others that she's heard?
        
        "Well, the second biggest one is more or less the same as the first, only with a corrupted dragon instead, so I won't go into detail on that. There's also one where people say that it's the magics that the mages of Estelore released, the power of the portals that destabilized the weave of the world... and the other one that the religious hierarchies preferred, being that the sins and iniquity of the people of old Belhar coalesced and manifested into a tangible force from their sheer depth and degree, a curse that lures people in with its beautiful and lush exterior, only for them to find death once there."
        
        Hmm.
        
        "The only thing all the folktales I heard agree on is that prior to the Godswar, the imperial heartland was as stable and peaceful as could be — the worst that would happen was a bit of minor flooding from the rivers during a particularly heavy rain from the coast. But quakes, massive wildfires, destructive storms and the like — no, none of that. Whatever's twisting the land right now, it's a consequence of that black spot on our history."
    ]

rows.original: [rand |Gweyr sighs. "It's hard, isn't it? At least Garret has faint memories of me... Gwyneth has absolutely no recollection of what I looked like, or anything that I ever did for her, and grew up with an image of me pieced together from hearsay and figments of her own imagination. To be fair, how she sees me is actually better than how I actually am... but that's not a high bar to surmount." There, there. "It just feels like she's smushed together everything she hates into the world and put that into the place what I should be, then proceeded to burn it. An effigy of sorts, like the orcs sometimes do in the south." Well, if she keeps on doing what she's doing and proving to her that the mother she has in reality isn't the mother she's built up in her mind, one day she'll be forced to accept that the latter isn't real. A short, bitter, barking laugh. "Oh, would that be the case. The girl feels that something's true, so that's what it is. Knowingly or otherwise, she's built her entire identity and person in opposition to the caricature she's cooked up — I'm not blaming her for it, I might even have done the same if I thought my mother abandoned us at a young age. No, what I got instead was Father coming in and letting a girl of seven summers know that her mother had her throat slit by the claws of a misshapen monster from under the earth." ...Does the know the truth of what happened that night? "Garth's tried to explain it to her... but she won't listen, not even from Daddy dearest. Like I said, the poor girl's built who she is in opposition to everything she thinks I am, and it'll take an act of the gods to move her from it. Still, it's not going to stop me from trying." |"Gwyneth was such a big pup when she was just born," Gweyr reminisces with a sigh. "I remember holding her and her brother in my arms, and thinking of her 'yes, this is a child who is strong enough to take after me.' Not that I was completely wrong, of course, but given that she's so much like her father now... no, she's not like her father, she's taken his traits and doubled, tripled them in intensity. When I left to walk the ice, she wasn't that different from her brother, and now... can you imagine her holding a weapon?" Gwyn has the body for it, but her mind... "At least her father has a bit of backbone in him where it counts, but the girl's completely, dangerously and disturbingly submissive. I could teach her to draw a bow, she's got the strength for it, but she wouldn't just lose the nerve to fight assuming she had any to begin with; she'd get down on all fours and present herself for the taking if that's what was demanded of her. Blunt, yes, but that's what it is. "I'm not saying that it's bad or anything — I'm here in the very place my girl's built, after all, and she's won almost as much respect from the townsfolk as her father has. It's just that the younger me holding her in my arms would never have imagined she would turn out this way, and the older me wonders if anything would have been different if I'd been around to mind her growing up instead of just leaving her to her father." Well, there isn't much point to pursuing what-ifs at this juncture. The bigger question is what to do going forward. "Oh, do allow an old woman a bit of melancholy every now and then. I wasn't looking for answers or solutions, I was looking for someone to talk to." A dry chuckle. "I'm fully aware that reminiscing about the past in such a fashion isn't going to do much practical good... but I want to do it anyway." |"I really don't know where my daughter gets her figure from," Gweyr says with a dry chuckle. "All of the women in my line were stout, to say the least, except for my great-grandmother, or that's what my father told me — a white witch who married into the line. And even so, she was supposed to be just so-so, instead of absolutely lush like Gwyneth is." Maybe it's from her father's side of the family? "Hmm... I don't know. When I asked Garth about his folks, he told me they were pretty thin. Of course, that might've just been because those were lean years and everyone was scraping by on the edge of starvation. Might've been if they were fed well, they would've been plumper... Garth himself didn't, at any rate." You have to admit that Gwyn's motherly figure — even before she got pregnant for the first time, according to local rumor — does lend itself to her profession of choice, and it's even become moreso ever since then. It's hard to say which came first, the girl or the job, but the two have fed each other to the point where it really doesn't matter any more. "It's like her body reshaped itself to be the exact opposite of what I thought she'd grow up to be, like she knew what I was hoping for the future and willed herself to grow in the exact opposite direction. A body designed to not just survive the strains of being pregnant and giving birth, but take pleasure in doing so over and over again..." Gweyr draws a deep breath and looks a little shell-shocked and despondent. "Oh, my girl, my sweet little pup. What have I done to you by not being there when you needed your mother, that you've decided to be everyone's?" All right, now she's taking too much blame upon herself. There's no way she can prove that Gwyn's current state would have changed any from what it is now if she hadn't gone out to confront Tollus that night, nor can she change anything about it. "..." |She's probably heard the rumors floating about town, yes? "I have. It's just how the way things are — people will believe anything about a figure that's remotely public. Given that my husband's worked his way up into being the de facto village alderman over the last twenty years, I'd be surprised if there weren't unkind things said about him and his behind his back. The same thing goes for our daughter, too — now that she's the nursery matron and funded by the baroness's trusts no less, she's someone out and about town. It was the same way with my father, too... that and the Crossed Swords were all supposed to be a bunch of murderous rapists or what have you. It's just the price you pay for being a big fish, be it in a small pond or the open sea." Ah. "Besides, Garth knows full well that if he tried to fuck our daughter, let alone get her pregnant, I'd clobber the shit out of him seven ways, one each for every one of the gods he'd have to explain himself to when I was done with him. The man's had his temptations and slip-ups, as we've all, but by and large he's remained loyal to me in the twenty years I wasn't around and I can respect that." She sighs. "Yes, the girl has an obsession with her father that anyone should frankly find disturbing, but I'm not surprised that it turned out that way when he was the only one to care for a tender and reclusive pup for all these years. I'd be able to sniff out any funny business in no time at all, and he knows that — not that I'm suggesting that it's only the fear of me that keeps his hands off Gwyneth, of course. "Really, it's just cruel. The poor girl, she believes I'm back just to steal her father away from her. It's been a little while now and she seems to have realized that maybe that's not exactly the case given all the work I've been doing, but I can't fault her for being mistrustful given that she's been the only woman in her father's daily life for a long while now. Frankly speaking, I might've done the same thing in her shoes, if my mother whom I never knew just reappeared in my family one day. I just hope that I can try and fix all this before my dying day..." |"The girl takes mostly after her father, but I can see a bit of me here and there, especially when she doesn't have her guard up," Gweyr says with a sad chuckle. "For example, her penchant for wearing the exact same thing every day, down to the gloves, and having more than a dozen identical outfits. You never see her change her clothes in any meaningful manner, do you?" No, you don't think you've ever seen her in anything but that getup. Be it working at the nursery, manning the Hound's kitchen or minding the taps and common room while Garth is otherwise occupied, Gwyn's always been in that blouse and apron from the very moment you first set into the Frost Hound, and you've never seen her wear anything else. "Maybe it's more than just what's in her blood," Gweyr adds. "Maybe she wants stability in a world that she knows is cold and hard beyond these four walls. But that penchant for uniforms... yes, that's my girl, no doubt about it. I was barely old enough when my father had me fitted for my first gambeson with the company's insignia on the front... "I lost my own mother at a fairly young age, too. Didn't end up with a bleeding scar on my heart like my poor, poor girl did. Maybe it's because I still remember something of her before she got herself killed, maybe it's because there were still plenty of other people in the company to glom on to, as opposed to all the people who must've hated the girl and pinned the guilt of my actions on her after I was sent to walk the ice. But most of all, I believe the biggest reason my poor pup and I turned out so differently was that my father never kept from me what'd happened to my mother." ... "He just came back one day and told me a wraith-touched monster had torn her throat out. I was young, and even so I'd had one or two other members of the company die before then. He never pulled any punches, and even though I wept at the sight of what was left of my mother after they retrieved the pieces they could find, I think it was ultimately better than it would've been by deceiving me like my husband did to my poor girl. I don't blame him for it — trying to explain to Gwyn why she didn't have a mother and what happened to her wasn't something I would've relished, and Garth isn't as cold as my father was, but even so. He mightn't have had the stomach for it, but working with Sanders and River to cover the whole thing up and keep it from the girl... well, you can see what she's like now." ]
rows.translation: [rand |格维尔叹了口气：“这确实很难，不是吗？至少加雷特还对我有些模糊的记忆……而格温妮丝却完全不记得我长什么样子，也不记得我曾经为她做过什么。她成长过程中所了解的关于我的信息，全都来自于别人的传闻和她自己的想象。公平地说，她对我的看法其实比我真实的自我要好……不过，这个标准其实并不高，很容易就能达到。 别难过，别难过。 她似乎把所有她讨厌的东西都集中到我的身上，然后把它们强加到我应该成为的样子上，之后又把这一切都“烧毁”了。某种意义上的替身，就像南方的一些兽人有时会做的那样。” 嗯，如果她继续这样下去，不断向自己证明：现实中的母亲并不是她心中想象中的那个母亲，那么总有一天，她将不得不接受这个事实——那个想象中的母亲其实并不存在。 一阵短促而刺耳的笑声。“哦，如果是那样的话……那个女孩感觉起来……事实就是如此。无论她是否有意，她将自己的整个身份与人格构建成了与她所臆造出的那种刻板形象完全相反的样子——我并不是在责怪她，如果我认为自己的母亲在年幼时抛弃了我们，我可能也会做出同样的选择。不，相反，发生的是父亲走进来，告诉一个七岁的小女孩：她的母亲被地下那些畸形的怪物用爪子割开了喉咙。 ……她知道那天晚上究竟发生了什么吗？ 加思试图向她解释……但她就是不听，哪怕是来自她最亲爱的爸爸的话也不行。就像我说的，那个可怜的女孩已经形成了与她所认为的我的一切相反的观念，要想让她改变这种想法，恐怕只有神明才能做到了。不过，这并不会阻止我尝试。 |格温妮丝刚出生的时候，真的是个非常可爱的小家伙，”格维尔叹息着回忆道，“我记得当时把她和她的弟弟抱在怀里，心想：‘没错，这个孩子有足够的潜力来继承我的事业。’当然，我当时并没有完全错，不过现在看，她实在太像她父亲了。不，她并不像她的父亲，她继承了父亲的那些特质，而且将这些特质的强度提升了一倍、甚至三倍。当我去冰面上行走时，她和她的哥哥并没有太大区别，但现在……你能想象她手持武器的样子吗？ 格温拥有适合这样的身体的条件，但她的心理状态…… “至少她的父亲在关键时刻还有一定的骨气，但这个女孩却表现得极其顺从，这种顺从甚至让人感到危险和不安。我完全可以教她如何使用弓箭，她也有足够的力气来做到这一点，但只要有人要求她战斗，她不仅会立刻失去勇气，甚至会直接趴在地上，任由别人摆布。直白，没错，但事实就是如此。 “我并不是说这糟糕或者任何其他事情——毕竟，我现在正站在我女儿成长过的这片土地上，而她在镇上获得的尊重，几乎和她父亲一样多。只是，年轻时的我，抱着她的时候，从未想象过她会变成这样；而年长的我，则在想，如果我在她成长过程中一直陪伴在她身边，而不是把她交给她父亲，会不会有什么不同呢？嗯，在这个节骨眼上，再去纠结那些‘如果……会怎样’的问题也没什么意义。更重要的是，接下来该怎么做。 “哦，请允许一位老妇拟像尔沉浸在忧郁之中吧。我并不是在寻找答案或解决办法，我只是需要一个人可以倾诉而已。干笑了一声，”我说，“我非常清楚，以这样的方式回忆过去并不会带来什么实际的好处……但我就是想这么做。 |我真的不明白我女儿是怎么拥有那样的身材的，”格维尔干笑着说，“我们家族里的女性，至少可以说，都是比较丰满的，只有我的曾祖母除外——至少我父亲是这么告诉我的。她是一个白女巫，后来嫁入了我们家族。不过即便如此，她的身材也只算一般而已，远没有格温妮丝那么丰满。 也许这和她父亲那一方的家族有关吧？ “嗯……我也不确定。当我问加思关于他父母的情况时，他告诉我他们身材比较瘦削。当然，那也可能只是因为在那些连年饥荒的年代，大家都在勉强维持生计。如果他们能得到足够的食物，或许会变得胖一些……不过加思本人，无论如何，也并不胖。 你不得不承认，根据当地的传闻，即使在第一次怀孕之前，格温那种母性化的性格特点就已经很适合她选择的这份职业了，而自从那以后，这种特点变得更加明显了。很难说到底是这个女孩先有了这样的性格，还是这份职业让她逐渐形成了这样的性格，但这两者相互促进，现在已经分不清谁先出现了。 她的身体似乎发生了某种变化，变得完全与我原本想象中的她未来的样子相反。就好像她知道我对她未来的期望，于是刻意让自己朝着完全相反的方向发展。她的身体不仅能够承受怀孕和分娩带来的种种压力，而且还能从中获得快乐，甚至愿意一次又一次地经历这些过程。格维尔深深地吸了一口气，看起来既震惊又沮丧。‘哦，我的宝贝女儿，我亲爱的小姑娘……在你需要妈妈的时候，我没有在你身边，我究竟做了什么，让你决定要成为所有人的妈妈呢？" 好吧，现在她把自己承担了太多的责任。她根本无法证明，如果那晚没有去与托勒斯对峙，格温现在的状况会不会有什么不同，她也无法改变任何已经发生的事情。 “…… |她应该已经听说了那些在镇上流传的谣言吧？ “我听说了。事实就是这样的——对于那些稍微有点公众知名度的人来说，人们什么都会相信。考虑到我丈夫在过去的二十年里逐渐成为了这个村庄的实际上的领导者，如果没有人相信这些谣言，我反倒会感到奇怪。不是人们在他背后说了一些刻薄的话。我们的女儿也是如此——现在她成为了托儿所的负责人，而且还是由男爵夫人的信托基金提供资金支持的，因此她经常在城里活动。我父亲当年也是这样……还有那些“十字剑组织”的成员，也被人们认为是一群杀人犯之类的坏人。其实，无论是在小池塘里，还是在广阔的海洋中，成为“大鱼”就必须承受这样的代价。 再说，加斯心里很清楚，如果他敢碰我们的女儿，更别想让她怀孕，我一定会把他打得半死不活。到时候他还得向那些他需要向他们解释事情的神明们解释自己的行为，每个神明都会让他挨一顿痛打。这个人也像我们所有人一样，经历过诱惑和犯错，但在我离开的这二十年里，他总体上还是对我保持着忠诚，对此我表示尊重。”她叹了口气，“没错，那个女孩对她的父亲有着一种让人感到不安的执着，但考虑到这些年来只有她的父亲关心这个温柔而孤僻的孩子，这样的结果也不足为奇了。我绝对能在第一时间察觉到任何可疑的行为，而他心里也明白这一点——当然，我并不是说他之所以不敢对格温妮丝动手，只是因为害怕我。 真的，这太残忍了。那个可怜的女孩，她以为我回来只是为了把她父亲从她身边夺走。不过现在过了段时间，她似乎也开始意识到，也许并不是这样的正是如此考虑到我一直以来所做的所有努力，她不信任我也是情有可原的——毕竟很长一段时间以来，她都是她父亲生活中唯一的女性。坦白说，如果我的母亲有一天突然重新出现在我的家庭中，换作是我，可能也会做出同样的反应。我只希望自己能在有生之前提前解决这一切…… |这个女孩在很多方面都随她父亲，但有时候我也能在她身上看到自己的影子，尤其是在她没有防备的时候，”格维尔带着一丝伤感的笑声说道，“比如，她总是每天都穿一模一样的衣服，连手套都一样，而且她有十几套完全一样的服装。你从来没见过她真正地更换过衣服，对吧？ 不，你绝对不认为自己见过她穿过其他衣服。无论是在托儿所工作，还是在猎犬餐厅帮忙，又或者是当加思有其他事情要忙时负责照看水龙头和公共休息室，从你第一次来到霜犬酒馆镇的那一刻起，格温就总是穿着那件衬衫和围裙，你从来没见过她穿过别的衣服。 也许这不仅仅是因为她的血液中流淌着这样的基因，”格维尔接着说道，“也许她只是想要在这个她深知充满寒冷与残酷的世界中找到一丝稳定感。但对她来说，制服就是象征稳定与归属的东西……没错，这完全就是我的女儿。我還很小的时候，父亲就已经为我定制了第一件印有公司标志的护甲…… 我也在很小的时候就失去了自己的母亲。不过，我的心里并没有留下像那个可怜的女孩那样的伤痕。也许是因为我仍然记得她被害之前的样子，也许是因为在我被派去执行那些任务的时候，公司里还有很多人可以依靠，而不是所有人都在恨那个女孩，都将我那些行为的过错归咎于她。但最重要的是，我认为我和我那可怜的小狗之所以会有如此不同的结局，最大的原因就是我的父亲从未向我隐瞒过关于我母亲的事情。 有一天他突然回来，告诉我有一个被怨灵附身的怪物割断了她的喉咙。那时我还很年轻，不过在此之前，公司里已经有了一两个人去世了。他从不隐瞒任何事情，即使当我看到他们把能找到的母亲残骸收拢起来时，我哭得撕心裂肺，但我认为，这样的真相终究比像我丈夫那样欺骗我，要好得多。我并不责怪他——试图向格温解释她为什么没有母亲，以及她母亲究竟发生了什么，这种事情我本身也不愿意去做。加斯虽然不像我父亲那样冷酷无情，但即便如此，他可能也没有勇气去面对这些。所以，他选择与桑德斯和瑞弗合作，掩盖这一切，不让那个女孩知道真相。嗯，你现在应该能看到她是什么样的人了吧。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |Gweyr sighs. "It's hard, isn't it? At least Garret has faint memories of me... Gwyneth has absolutely no recollection of what I looked like, or anything that I ever did for her, and grew up with an image of me pieced together from hearsay and figments of her own imagination. To be fair, how she sees me is actually better than how I actually am... but that's not a high bar to surmount." There, there. "It just feels like she's smushed together everything she hates into the world and put that into the place what I should be, then proceeded to burn it. An effigy of sorts, like the orcs sometimes do in the south." Well, if she keeps on doing what she's doing and proving to her that the mother she has in reality isn't the mother she's built up in her mind, one day she'll be forced to accept that the latter isn't real. A short, bitter, barking laugh. "Oh, would that be the case. The girl feels that something's true, so that's what it is. Knowingly or otherwise, she's built her entire identity and person in opposition to the caricature she's cooked up — I'm not blaming her for it, I might even have done the same if I thought my mother abandoned us at a young age. No, what I got instead was Father coming in and letting a girl of seven summers know that her mother had her throat slit by the claws of a misshapen monster from under the earth." ...Does the know the truth of what happened that night? "Garth's tried to explain it to her... but she won't listen, not even from Daddy dearest. Like I said, the poor girl's built who she is in opposition to everything she thinks I am, and it'll take an act of the gods to move her from it. Still, it's not going to stop me from trying." |"Gwyneth was such a big pup when she was just born," Gweyr reminisces with a sigh. "I remember holding her and her brother in my arms, and thinking of her 'yes, this is a child who is strong enough to take after me.' Not that I was completely wrong, of course, but given that she's so much like her father now... no, she's not like her father, she's taken his traits and doubled, tripled them in intensity. When I left to walk the ice, she wasn't that different from her brother, and now... can you imagine her holding a weapon?" Gwyn has the body for it, but her mind... "At least her father has a bit of backbone in him where it counts, but the girl's completely, dangerously and disturbingly submissive. I could teach her to draw a bow, she's got the strength for it, but she wouldn't just lose the nerve to fight assuming she had any to begin with; she'd get down on all fours and present herself for the taking if that's what was demanded of her. Blunt, yes, but that's what it is. "I'm not saying that it's bad or anything — I'm here in the very place my girl's built, after all, and she's won almost as much respect from the townsfolk as her father has. It's just that the younger me holding her in my arms would never have imagined she would turn out this way, and the older me wonders if anything would have been different if I'd been around to mind her growing up instead of just leaving her to her father." Well, there isn't much point to pursuing what-ifs at this juncture. The bigger question is what to do going forward. "Oh, do allow an old woman a bit of melancholy every now and then. I wasn't looking for answers or solutions, I was looking for someone to talk to." A dry chuckle. "I'm fully aware that reminiscing about the past in such a fashion isn't going to do much practical good... but I want to do it anyway." |"I really don't know where my daughter gets her figure from," Gweyr says with a dry chuckle. "All of the women in my line were stout, to say the least, except for my great-grandmother, or that's what my father told me — a white witch who married into the line. And even so, she was supposed to be just so-so, instead of absolutely lush like Gwyneth is." Maybe it's from her father's side of the family? "Hmm... I don't know. When I asked Garth about his folks, he told me they were pretty thin. Of course, that might've just been because those were lean years and everyone was scraping by on the edge of starvation. Might've been if they were fed well, they would've been plumper... Garth himself didn't, at any rate." You have to admit that Gwyn's motherly figure — even before she got pregnant for the first time, according to local rumor — does lend itself to her profession of choice, and it's even become moreso ever since then. It's hard to say which came first, the girl or the job, but the two have fed each other to the point where it really doesn't matter any more. "It's like her body reshaped itself to be the exact opposite of what I thought she'd grow up to be, like she knew what I was hoping for the future and willed herself to grow in the exact opposite direction. A body designed to not just survive the strains of being pregnant and giving birth, but take pleasure in doing so over and over again..." Gweyr draws a deep breath and looks a little shell-shocked and despondent. "Oh, my girl, my sweet little pup. What have I done to you by not being there when you needed your mother, that you've decided to be everyone's?" All right, now she's taking too much blame upon herself. There's no way she can prove that Gwyn's current state would have changed any from what it is now if she hadn't gone out to confront Tollus that night, nor can she change anything about it. "..." |She's probably heard the rumors floating about town, yes? "I have. It's just how the way things are — people will believe anything about a figure that's remotely public. Given that my husband's worked his way up into being the de facto village alderman over the last twenty years, I'd be surprised if there weren't unkind things said about him and his behind his back. The same thing goes for our daughter, too — now that she's the nursery matron and funded by the baroness's trusts no less, she's someone out and about town. It was the same way with my father, too... that and the Crossed Swords were all supposed to be a bunch of murderous rapists or what have you. It's just the price you pay for being a big fish, be it in a small pond or the open sea." Ah. "Besides, Garth knows full well that if he tried to fuck our daughter, let alone get her pregnant, I'd clobber the shit out of him seven ways, one each for every one of the gods he'd have to explain himself to when I was done with him. The man's had his temptations and slip-ups, as we've all, but by and large he's remained loyal to me in the twenty years I wasn't around and I can respect that." She sighs. "Yes, the girl has an obsession with her father that anyone should frankly find disturbing, but I'm not surprised that it turned out that way when he was the only one to care for a tender and reclusive pup for all these years. I'd be able to sniff out any funny business in no time at all, and he knows that — not that I'm suggesting that it's only the fear of me that keeps his hands off Gwyneth, of course. "Really, it's just cruel. The poor girl, she believes I'm back just to steal her father away from her. It's been a little while now and she seems to have realized that maybe that's not exactly the case given all the work I've been doing, but I can't fault her for being mistrustful given that she's been the only woman in her father's daily life for a long while now. Frankly speaking, I might've done the same thing in her shoes, if my mother whom I never knew just reappeared in my family one day. I just hope that I can try and fix all this before my dying day..." |"The girl takes mostly after her father, but I can see a bit of me here and there, especially when she doesn't have her guard up," Gweyr says with a sad chuckle. "For example, her penchant for wearing the exact same thing every day, down to the gloves, and having more than a dozen identical outfits. You never see her change her clothes in any meaningful manner, do you?" No, you don't think you've ever seen her in anything but that getup. Be it working at the nursery, manning the Hound's kitchen or minding the taps and common room while Garth is otherwise occupied, Gwyn's always been in that blouse and apron from the very moment you first set into the Frost Hound, and you've never seen her wear anything else. "Maybe it's more than just what's in her blood," Gweyr adds. "Maybe she wants stability in a world that she knows is cold and hard beyond these four walls. But that penchant for uniforms... yes, that's my girl, no doubt about it. I was barely old enough when my father had me fitted for my first gambeson with the company's insignia on the front... "I lost my own mother at a fairly young age, too. Didn't end up with a bleeding scar on my heart like my poor, poor girl did. Maybe it's because I still remember something of her before she got herself killed, maybe it's because there were still plenty of other people in the company to glom on to, as opposed to all the people who must've hated the girl and pinned the guilt of my actions on her after I was sent to walk the ice. But most of all, I believe the biggest reason my poor pup and I turned out so differently was that my father never kept from me what'd happened to my mother." ... "He just came back one day and told me a wraith-touched monster had torn her throat out. I was young, and even so I'd had one or two other members of the company die before then. He never pulled any punches, and even though I wept at the sight of what was left of my mother after they retrieved the pieces they could find, I think it was ultimately better than it would've been by deceiving me like my husband did to my poor girl. I don't blame him for it — trying to explain to Gwyn why she didn't have a mother and what happened to her wasn't something I would've relished, and Garth isn't as cold as my father was, but even so. He mightn't have had the stomach for it, but working with Sanders and River to cover the whole thing up and keep it from the girl... well, you can see what she's like now." ] "

rows.original: [rand |"I know Garth tried his best to raise our son as well as he could, but at the end of the day he just fundamentally doesn't understand the pup. My husband grew up hungry all the time, and so much of his early life was spent looking for a warm roof to sleep under and a full belly, to the point that he told my father outright that it was his motivation for signing up with the Crossed Swords. Everything he's done has been to give Garret a stable, if hardworking existence, which is what he'd have wanted in the pup's place." "But that's not Garret wants, and sending him out to work off his energy on odd jobs isn't getting to the root of the problem; seeing our son build his life just to oppose his father makes me sad when I mostly have fond memories of my own. I saw someone call him 'Garth's pup' the other day, and smelled how much it really hurt him..." You think you remember him saying something along the lines of choosing to pick up wrestling because it was something that Garth wasn't doing, that if he chose to pick up the sword like his father did he'd always be playing second fiddle. But given how he was when you first found him in Westbank, locked up in a cage, and how he is now, you imagine he's had an epiphany or two along the way. As he was, you wouldn't have brought him all the way out to the rift to meet her, because he'd just have been an embarrassment. "The boy needs adversity, and he hasn't had any real trouble in his life since his father did his best to keep him from it. So, he keeps on acting out, hoping to be able to find the trouble he so craves; there's no call for heroes in a time of peace and plenty, after all. Well then, thanks for watching out for my son and doing my job for me. I don't know why I didn't just try to visit him on any of the times I came down to meet Garth, maybe ask him to take him out of town to meet me or even sneak in to see him myself... maybe I was just a coward and didn't want to have to explain myself or deal with the inevitable that would happen." "But if Garret's anything like me when I was younger, trying to keep him rooted by force isn't going to do Garth or the pup any good; he's not content to sit down in one place and do the same job like my daughter is, not until he's gotten it all out of his system. Would I have been there for him... well, it's something I'm going to fix, now that I'm finally home. I've had a long talk with his father about how to handle the pup, and since Garth did his best and didn't do as well as he'd hoped, it's my turn to see what I can do for my idiot son." |So, no doubt she's heard her son going about touting himself as the strongest man in Savarra... Gweyr just grins. What does she think of that? "It's bullshit. Garth knows it's bullshit, everyone who knows him knows it's bullshit, Sanders knows it's bullshit, and of course, I know it's bullshit because this old woman here could pin him down with her arms behind her back without so much as breaking a sweat. And yet, [pc.name], sometimes what you need to bullshit to cultivate the proper attitude to be able to get where you need to go." Such as being an insufferable ass? "Annoying from time to time, yes. Completely insufferable? Well, when you put it in perspective, maybe not so much. The pup himself knows it's bullshit, I'm sure of that, but when you want to be a certain kind of person you have to start acting and thinking that way. Fake it until you make it, like the old quartermaster used to say. He'll never realistically be the strongest man in the world, but it's an ideal worth chasing, and ideals aren't necessarily worthless just because you might not be able to see a path that gets you from here to there. And who knows? He might just be able to make it someday." Yes, but somehow you don't quite think he's going about it the right way... "See, that's a matter for my son to hash out by himself. You started with the very idea of this whole 'strongest man in the world' thing being silly in and of itself, and now you're saying he's not going about it the right way, which may very well be true but at least it's not ridiculous on its face. So long as Garret knows in the back of his mind that he's just bullshitting himself in a bid to push himself onward, I'm fine with it. You've got to work with different people differently, isn't that the case?" You're still not quite convinced of this whole thing... on the other hand. Gweyr's survived a lot in her time that would've broken many other people. The old wolfess just shows you her teeth at your hesitation. "Sure, maybe it's because he's my son, or maybe it's because I'm the kind of bitch who likes this sort of thing, but swagger isn't necessarily a bad thing. Just saying, hmm? It's a bit too fantastic for many peoples' tastes, something out of a fairy tale or legend... but I've had enough of those in my day. You want to be larger than life, you've got to think and act like someone who's larger than life, even if you aren't." |"I went and tested my son the other day, since he was doing his whole 'strongest man in the world' schtick again." ...Tested him? Gweyr flicks a ear in your direction. "You know, dear. Beat him to within an inch of his life. Age and experience trump youth and foolhardiness every time, so on and so forth. Went at him with nothing but my fists, since that's his forte." Oh... "Hey, I liked him. The pup didn't stay down, instead got back right up and came swinging at me again like the strongest man in all of Savarra should. It's not all about dishing them out, it's about how you take them and whether you've it in you to crawl to your feet and face down your opponent again." The old wolfess sighs wistfully. "Would I had been there to raise him right when he was younger... not that I'm implying my husband did a bad job, just not one suited for the boy. They fought some, but he always held back, and I think Garret sensed that on an instinctual level and resented it. "In the end, I'm prouder of my son than I'd have been if he'd managed to thrash the stuffing out of me without taking a hit, because now I know that the pup can come back up from being bloodied a bit. He's done really well despite having what I'd consider a sheltered life, and I'm not saying that just because I'm his mother." You don't know about that, Garret's got the kind of countenance that only a mother could love. "And considering the bruises and cuts he'll be wearing for a bit, a face that only I could smile at. Oh, don't look at me like that, he'll be fine. I think I beat every part of him into submission but his pride, and that's what counts. He's still calling himself the strongest man in the world, but given how the pup looks right now I'm sure it's taken on a different meaning. Ha!" |The medallion Garret had, that thing he showed her when the two of you were convincing Gweyr to come home... Sighing, the old wolfess props up her chin with her knuckles and gets a faraway look in her eyes. "It was the emblem of the Crossed Swords, you know. A very simple insignia that people could remember easily. All of us had it emblazoned on our gambesons... Father said that it was part of our family's history, that we were supposed to have been descended from some bigwig or the other. Didn't know. Didn't care. Well, I did care, but only in what it meant to my father and his men." Garret hasn't let it go to his head, though. You remember... he still calls himself a tavernkeeper's son, no more, no less. "It's a way of thinking that I can get behind, wanting to make your own glory and not resting on the laurels of your folks... and at the same time respecting those things they did. It's what my father taught me at any rate, and that my boy has eventually worked his way to this point with your help is something I have to thank you deeply for." You? Oh, heh. It's not like you actively set out to reform Garret or club any kind of sense into that thick skull of his, but you'll take the compliment if she's handing it out. Truth be told, Garret had to have to want this decision at the end of the day — leading a horse to water, making it drink and all. He'd have to had wanted the epiphany to begin with, so credit where's credit's due. "He'll get the chance to make a name for himself all right, I'll make sure of that. Perhaps it's just me wanting to make good on all the years that I lost out on the ice that I should've spent with him, but I want to see him in a good place before I die. That, or in a grave, because nothing else will satisfy him; I should know, because I was there myself." And she believes Garret will settle down once he's had his fill of adventure? "Happened to me. Came out of the blue, really... but it still happened to me, and while I wouldn't have even entertained the thought mere days ago suddenly the notion of settling down with Garth didn't seem so bad after all. You can change your perspective on people and events pretty quickly." |So, has Garret managed to recall her last words to him before she left to walk the ice? "No, he hasn't, and to be fair I don't think I'll tell him unless he asks me straight up, which I don't think he will." Oh? "Like his sister, he's grown up with not so much me, but an image of me that he's created in his mind. That valorization of his dear old mother's been one of the things that's been keeping that fire inside of him burning, made him behave in his really quite silly but quite endearing ways, given all the stories I've been flooded with about my dear son ever since I returned to town." ... Endearing? She considers Garret's behavior endearing? "There's a lot of me in him, you know. He just needs the proper environment to be in so that it can be put to proper use — you wouldn't blame a fish for being quite useless out of water, would you? Same thing applies here in that my son just needs the kind of environment I had growing up, and I know exactly where that can be found. In the meantime, I'm going to do what I can with him." "Unlike his sister, my poor pup doesn't think of his mother as someone who abandoned the family — I remember feeling his eyes on my back as Sanders hounded me out of Hawkethorne all those years ago. He just saw his mother thrash the daylights out of people who were holding the village hostage, and then go riding off into the sunset victorious. How much of what he remembers I don't know, but I do know from the way he acts around me that anything that he does recall is good. What more could an old woman ask for, really, and why would I break an illusion like this unless he wants me to? If it'll keep him going, let him believe that I dispensed some great and terrible wisdom in those last moments we shared together. No harm in it, right?" ]
rows.translation: [rand |我知道加斯已经尽了最大努力来抚养我们的儿子，但他从根本上来说并不了解这只小狗的习性。我丈夫在成长过程中一直处于饥饿的状态，他的早年生活大部分时间都在为寻找一个可以遮风挡雨的地方和足够的食物而奔波，甚至他曾直接告诉我的父亲，这就是他加入‘十字剑组织’的原因。他所做的一切，都是为了让加雷特拥有一个稳定而勤奋的生活——这正是他如果处在加雷特的位置上也会希望拥有的生活。 但这并不是加雷特想要的，让他去做一些零工来发泄精力，并不能从根本上解决这个问题；看到我们的儿子为了与父亲对抗而建立自己的人生，让我感到很难过，因为我对自己的父亲有着许多美好的回忆。前几天，我看到有人称他为‘加思的小狗’，我能感受到这对他来说有多伤人…… 你记得他说过类似这样的话：选择学习摔跤，是因为加斯并没有选择这个方向；如果他像他的父亲一样选择学习剑术，那么他就会永远处于次要的位置。但考虑到你最初在西岸银行发现他的时候，他还被关在笼子里，而现在的他已经发生了很大的变化，你可以想象，在这段时间里他一定经历了一些重要的领悟。如果还是以前的他，你根本不会带他来到裂隙这里去见她，因为他只会带来尴尬。 这个男孩需要面对逆境，因为自从他父亲竭力保护他免受任何困难之后，他的生活中就再没有真正遇到过任何麻烦。因此，他总是故意惹是生非，希望能够找到自己如此渴望的那些困难；毕竟，在和平与富足的时代，根本不需要英雄。那么，谢谢你们一直照顾我的儿子，也替我完成了这份责任。我不知道为什么，在每次来见加思的时候，我都没有试着去看看他，或许应该请他带儿子去外地见我，或者我自己偷偷地去看看他。也许我只是一个懦夫，不想为自己辩解，也不想面对那些不可避免会发生的事情。 但如果加雷特和我年轻时一样，强行让他待在一个地方做同样的事情，对加思或那只小狗都没有好处。他不会像我女儿那样，满足于坐在一个地方重复同样的工作，直到他把内心所有的想法和能量都释放出来为止。如果我当时能在他身边……嗯，现在我终于回家了，这件事我一定会去弥补的。我和他父亲认真地谈过如何照顾那只小狗，既然加思已经尽力了，但结果并没有达到他的期望，那么现在就轮到我来为我的这个傻儿子做点什么了。" |所以，毫无疑问，她肯定听到自己的儿子到处吹嘘自己是萨瓦拉最强壮的人…… 格维尔只是笑了笑。 她对此会怎么想呢？ “那完全是胡说八道。加斯知道那是胡说，所有认识他的人都知道那是胡说，桑德斯也知道那是胡说，当然，我也知道那是胡说——因为这位老妇人就算双臂背后交叉，也能轻松把他按倒在地，而自己却连一滴汗都不会流。[pc.name]，有时候，你就需要说些废话，培养出正确的态度，这样才能达到你想要的目标。” 比如，成为一个让人难以忍受的混蛋？ “偶尔让人感到烦躁，是的。但真的让人无法忍受吗？嗯，当你把事情放在更客观的角度来看时，也许也就不是那么回事了。那只小狗自己肯定知道那都是胡说八道，我对此很确定。但是，当你想要成为某种类型的人时，你就必须开始按照那种方式去行动和思考。就像那位老军需官曾经说的那样：假装到真的成为那样的人为止。他或许永远无法成为世界上最强大的人，但这个目标依然值得追求。毕竟，理想并不一定因为我们看不到实现它的途径就变得毫无价值。谁知道呢？也许有一天，他真的能够做到。 嗯，不过你总觉得他的做法不太对劲……” “你知道，这件事应该由我儿子自己来决定。你从一开始就认为‘世界上最强壮的人’这个概念本身就很荒谬，现在又说他的做法不对，这也许确实是真的，但至少这个想法本身并不荒唐。只要加雷特在内心深处明白，自己只是在自说自话，以此来激励自己继续前进，我就没意见。对待不同的人，确实需要采取不同的方式，不是吗？ 另一方面，你似乎仍然对这件事不太相信……不过，格维尔在她的生活中经历了很多事情，这些事情足以让很多人崩溃。 这只老母狼之所以会在你犹豫不决的时候露出獠牙，正是因为这样。当然，也许是因为他是我的儿子，又或许是因为我就是那种喜欢这类事情的人，但趾高气扬并不一定是件坏事。只是说说而已，嗯？对很多人来说，这种行为未免太夸张了，简直就像出自童话或传说中的情节一样。…但我这辈子已经受够了这类事情。如果你想成为非凡的人物，你就必须以非凡的方式去思考和行动，即使你本身并不是那样的人。 |前几天我带我儿子去做了检查，因为他又开始故作‘世界上最强壮的人’的样子了。已测试完毕。他？ 格维尔朝你的方向甩了甩耳朵，说道：“你知道的，亲爱的。一定要把他打得命都快没了吧。年龄和经验永远比年轻和鲁莽更重要，诸如此类。我就只用拳头跟他打，因为那正是他的强项。 哦…… “嘿，我真的很喜欢它。那只小狗并没有倒下，而是立刻站了起来，再次朝我冲了过来，表现得就像萨瓦拉最强大的勇士一样。关键不在于你能否给予对手打击，而在于你如何承受这些打击，以及你是否有勇气再次站起来，面对你的对手。那位年迈的母狼叹息道：“要是我能在他年幼的时候就在他身边抚养他该多好……并不是说我的丈夫没有尽到责任，只是他的方式并不适合这个孩子。他们之间确实发生过一些争执，但我的丈夫总是忍让着，而我想加雷特在直觉上察觉到了这一点，因此对他产生了怨恨。 说到底，比起我的儿子能不费一枪一弹就把我打得落花流水，我现在反而更为他感到骄傲。因为现在我知道，这个孩子即使受了些伤，也能重新站起来。尽管他过着在我看来相当安逸的生活，但他依然取得了如此出色的成绩。而我这么说，并不是因为我是他的母亲。 你可能不知道，加雷特有着那种只有母亲才会喜欢的面容。 “而且考虑到他身上那些淤青和伤口，也只有我才会对他露出微笑。哦，别用那种眼神看我，他不会有事的。我想我已经把他所有的反抗都压服了，除了他的自尊心——而这才是最重要的。他仍然自称是世界上最强壮的男人，但看看现在这只小狗的样子，我想他的这个说法已经有了不同的含义了。哈！ |加雷特拥有的那枚奖章，就是你们俩当时劝说格维尔回家时他给她看的那个东西…… 老狼女叹了口气，用指关节托着下巴，目光变得恍惚起来。你知道，那可是十字剑家族的标志。一个非常简单、容易让人记住的徽章。我们每个人的护腿上都印有这个标志……父亲说，这是我们家族历史的一部分，说明我们应该是某个显赫人物的后裔。不知道。也不在乎。嗯，我确实在意，但只在意这对我父亲和他的伙伴们意味着什么。” 不过，加雷特并没有因此而骄傲自满。你记得吗……他仍然自称是一个酒馆老板的儿子，仅此而已。 “这种追求自我荣耀、不愿依赖父母成就的思维方式，我完全能够理解。同时，也要尊重他们所做过的事情。至少这是我父亲教给我的。而我的儿子能够在你们的帮助下走到今天这一步，我真的非常感谢你们。 你？哦，呵呵。你又不是主动去试图改变加雷特，也不是想把什么道理强行灌进他那厚实的脑袋里，但既然别人夸你，你当然也会欣然接受。说实话，归根结底，加雷特自己必须愿意做出这个决定——就像把马牵到水边，让它自己喝水一样。他最初就必须有这样的觉悟，所以该表扬谁就表扬谁吧。 他一定会有机会为自己赢得名声的，我会确保这一点的。也许这只是因为我想要弥补那些在冰场上错失的岁月，那些本该与他一起度过的时光；但我希望在有生之年看到他处于一个好的境地。否则，他只能入土为安，因为没有其他方式能让他满足；这一点我深有体会，因为我自己也曾经历过那些时刻。 她认为，当加雷特体验够了冒险生活之后，就会安定下来吗？ “这种事就发生在我身上。真的，完全出乎意料……但事实就是如此。虽然几天前我根本不会考虑这种可能性，但突然间，我觉得和加思安定下来生活也不是坏事。人们对人和事的看法其实是会很快改变的。 |那么，加雷特是否已经记起了她离开去在冰面上行走之前对他说过的最后一句话呢？ “没有，他还没有记起来。说实话，我觉得除非他直接问我，否则我不会告诉他的——而我认为他应该不会这么做的。哦？” “就像他的姐姐一样，他也是在并没有真正接触过我的情况下长大的，而是在他的脑海中构建出了关于我的形象。他对自己亲爱的母亲的这种崇拜，正是让他在内心保持着那份热情的原因之一；也正是这种情感，让他做出了那些虽然看起来很傻，但却非常可爱的行为。自从我回到小镇后，我收到了太多关于我亲爱的儿子的消息。" ……可爱？她竟然认为加雷特的行为很可爱？ “你知道，他身上有很多我的影子。他只需要一个合适的环境，就能将这些优点充分发挥出来——你不会责怪一条鱼在水中无法生存吧？同样的道理也适用于他，我的儿子只需要一个与我成长过程中所拥有的相同的环境，而我知道这样的环境在哪里。在此之前，我会尽我所能来帮助他。 与他的姐姐不同，我那可怜的小狗并不认为它的母亲是那个抛弃了家庭的人。我还记得，多年前当桑德斯把我赶出鹰棘镇的时候，我能感觉到它的目光一直跟随着我。在它的眼中，它的母亲只是狠狠地惩罚了那些劫持了村庄里人们的人，然后胜利地骑马远去了。我不知道它真正记住了多少事情，但我确实从他在我身边的表现来看，我可以知道，他记得的一切都是美好的。对于一个老妇人来说，还能有什么更多的要求呢？而且，除非他是希望我打破这种幻想，否则我为什么要这么做呢？如果这能让他继续坚持下去，那就让他相信，在我们共度的最后那些时刻，我确实传授给了他一些伟大而深刻的智慧吧。这样做并没有什么坏处，对吧？ ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"I know Garth tried his best to raise our son as well as he could, but at the end of the day he just fundamentally doesn't understand the pup. My husband grew up hungry all the time, and so much of his early life was spent looking for a warm roof to sleep under and a full belly, to the point that he told my father outright that it was his motivation for signing up with the Crossed Swords. Everything he's done has been to give Garret a stable, if hardworking existence, which is what he'd have wanted in the pup's place." "But that's not Garret wants, and sending him out to work off his energy on odd jobs isn't getting to the root of the problem; seeing our son build his life just to oppose his father makes me sad when I mostly have fond memories of my own. I saw someone call him 'Garth's pup' the other day, and smelled how much it really hurt him..." You think you remember him saying something along the lines of choosing to pick up wrestling because it was something that Garth wasn't doing, that if he chose to pick up the sword like his father did he'd always be playing second fiddle. But given how he was when you first found him in Westbank, locked up in a cage, and how he is now, you imagine he's had an epiphany or two along the way. As he was, you wouldn't have brought him all the way out to the rift to meet her, because he'd just have been an embarrassment. "The boy needs adversity, and he hasn't had any real trouble in his life since his father did his best to keep him from it. So, he keeps on acting out, hoping to be able to find the trouble he so craves; there's no call for heroes in a time of peace and plenty, after all. Well then, thanks for watching out for my son and doing my job for me. I don't know why I didn't just try to visit him on any of the times I came down to meet Garth, maybe ask him to take him out of town to meet me or even sneak in to see him myself... maybe I was just a coward and didn't want to have to explain myself or deal with the inevitable that would happen." "But if Garret's anything like me when I was younger, trying to keep him rooted by force isn't going to do Garth or the pup any good; he's not content to sit down in one place and do the same job like my daughter is, not until he's gotten it all out of his system. Would I have been there for him... well, it's something I'm going to fix, now that I'm finally home. I've had a long talk with his father about how to handle the pup, and since Garth did his best and didn't do as well as he'd hoped, it's my turn to see what I can do for my idiot son." |So, no doubt she's heard her son going about touting himself as the strongest man in Savarra... Gweyr just grins. What does she think of that? "It's bullshit. Garth knows it's bullshit, everyone who knows him knows it's bullshit, Sanders knows it's bullshit, and of course, I know it's bullshit because this old woman here could pin him down with her arms behind her back without so much as breaking a sweat. And yet, [pc.name], sometimes what you need to bullshit to cultivate the proper attitude to be able to get where you need to go." Such as being an insufferable ass? "Annoying from time to time, yes. Completely insufferable? Well, when you put it in perspective, maybe not so much. The pup himself knows it's bullshit, I'm sure of that, but when you want to be a certain kind of person you have to start acting and thinking that way. Fake it until you make it, like the old quartermaster used to say. He'll never realistically be the strongest man in the world, but it's an ideal worth chasing, and ideals aren't necessarily worthless just because you might not be able to see a path that gets you from here to there. And who knows? He might just be able to make it someday." Yes, but somehow you don't quite think he's going about it the right way... "See, that's a matter for my son to hash out by himself. You started with the very idea of this whole 'strongest man in the world' thing being silly in and of itself, and now you're saying he's not going about it the right way, which may very well be true but at least it's not ridiculous on its face. So long as Garret knows in the back of his mind that he's just bullshitting himself in a bid to push himself onward, I'm fine with it. You've got to work with different people differently, isn't that the case?" You're still not quite convinced of this whole thing... on the other hand. Gweyr's survived a lot in her time that would've broken many other people. The old wolfess just shows you her teeth at your hesitation. "Sure, maybe it's because he's my son, or maybe it's because I'm the kind of bitch who likes this sort of thing, but swagger isn't necessarily a bad thing. Just saying, hmm? It's a bit too fantastic for many peoples' tastes, something out of a fairy tale or legend... but I've had enough of those in my day. You want to be larger than life, you've got to think and act like someone who's larger than life, even if you aren't." |"I went and tested my son the other day, since he was doing his whole 'strongest man in the world' schtick again." ...Tested him? Gweyr flicks a ear in your direction. "You know, dear. Beat him to within an inch of his life. Age and experience trump youth and foolhardiness every time, so on and so forth. Went at him with nothing but my fists, since that's his forte." Oh... "Hey, I liked him. The pup didn't stay down, instead got back right up and came swinging at me again like the strongest man in all of Savarra should. It's not all about dishing them out, it's about how you take them and whether you've it in you to crawl to your feet and face down your opponent again." The old wolfess sighs wistfully. "Would I had been there to raise him right when he was younger... not that I'm implying my husband did a bad job, just not one suited for the boy. They fought some, but he always held back, and I think Garret sensed that on an instinctual level and resented it. "In the end, I'm prouder of my son than I'd have been if he'd managed to thrash the stuffing out of me without taking a hit, because now I know that the pup can come back up from being bloodied a bit. He's done really well despite having what I'd consider a sheltered life, and I'm not saying that just because I'm his mother." You don't know about that, Garret's got the kind of countenance that only a mother could love. "And considering the bruises and cuts he'll be wearing for a bit, a face that only I could smile at. Oh, don't look at me like that, he'll be fine. I think I beat every part of him into submission but his pride, and that's what counts. He's still calling himself the strongest man in the world, but given how the pup looks right now I'm sure it's taken on a different meaning. Ha!" |The medallion Garret had, that thing he showed her when the two of you were convincing Gweyr to come home... Sighing, the old wolfess props up her chin with her knuckles and gets a faraway look in her eyes. "It was the emblem of the Crossed Swords, you know. A very simple insignia that people could remember easily. All of us had it emblazoned on our gambesons... Father said that it was part of our family's history, that we were supposed to have been descended from some bigwig or the other. Didn't know. Didn't care. Well, I did care, but only in what it meant to my father and his men." Garret hasn't let it go to his head, though. You remember... he still calls himself a tavernkeeper's son, no more, no less. "It's a way of thinking that I can get behind, wanting to make your own glory and not resting on the laurels of your folks... and at the same time respecting those things they did. It's what my father taught me at any rate, and that my boy has eventually worked his way to this point with your help is something I have to thank you deeply for." You? Oh, heh. It's not like you actively set out to reform Garret or club any kind of sense into that thick skull of his, but you'll take the compliment if she's handing it out. Truth be told, Garret had to have to want this decision at the end of the day — leading a horse to water, making it drink and all. He'd have to had wanted the epiphany to begin with, so credit where's credit's due. "He'll get the chance to make a name for himself all right, I'll make sure of that. Perhaps it's just me wanting to make good on all the years that I lost out on the ice that I should've spent with him, but I want to see him in a good place before I die. That, or in a grave, because nothing else will satisfy him; I should know, because I was there myself." And she believes Garret will settle down once he's had his fill of adventure? "Happened to me. Came out of the blue, really... but it still happened to me, and while I wouldn't have even entertained the thought mere days ago suddenly the notion of settling down with Garth didn't seem so bad after all. You can change your perspective on people and events pretty quickly." |So, has Garret managed to recall her last words to him before she left to walk the ice? "No, he hasn't, and to be fair I don't think I'll tell him unless he asks me straight up, which I don't think he will." Oh? "Like his sister, he's grown up with not so much me, but an image of me that he's created in his mind. That valorization of his dear old mother's been one of the things that's been keeping that fire inside of him burning, made him behave in his really quite silly but quite endearing ways, given all the stories I've been flooded with about my dear son ever since I returned to town." ... Endearing? She considers Garret's behavior endearing? "There's a lot of me in him, you know. He just needs the proper environment to be in so that it can be put to proper use — you wouldn't blame a fish for being quite useless out of water, would you? Same thing applies here in that my son just needs the kind of environment I had growing up, and I know exactly where that can be found. In the meantime, I'm going to do what I can with him." "Unlike his sister, my poor pup doesn't think of his mother as someone who abandoned the family — I remember feeling his eyes on my back as Sanders hounded me out of Hawkethorne all those years ago. He just saw his mother thrash the daylights out of people who were holding the village hostage, and then go riding off into the sunset victorious. How much of what he remembers I don't know, but I do know from the way he acts around me that anything that he does recall is good. What more could an old woman ask for, really, and why would I break an illusion like this unless he wants me to? If it'll keep him going, let him believe that I dispensed some great and terrible wisdom in those last moments we shared together. No harm in it, right?" ] "

rows.translation: 加雷特

rows.original: [rand |"Tollus lured the first kids of his little cult with the claim that there were vaults full of gold beneath the baroness's castle that she wasn't sharing to help the settlers," Gweyr says with a snort. "That story was... plausible, to say the least. That castle is large enough, and the stretch of mountain it sits upon strong enough, for there to have be some extensive vaults beneath if that's what she wanted. However, given the trust and stipend that's been awarded to my daughter for upkeep of this place, there was never any gold to begin with. "I've seen it several times back when I was in the Crossed Swords — people finding relics and getting rich, then proceeding to drink it all away in a couple years because they never think of putting that money to work. Say what you want of Tollus, but he knew how to speak to people when he'd the mind to. The village kids of twenty years ago were a bit smarter and more daring than most — you had to have guts to try and be a pioneer — but the idea that the baroness would just sit on a pile of wealth and not do anything with it was plausible to them because that's what they'd have done in her place." It's possible that the baroness has vaults beneath her castle, though? "More than possible, actually likely if it follows Belharan architecture from the period; I've dug through enough ruins to know that old Belhar likes their standardization and organization. Still, I've never actually asked the baroness if I could take a look. What would the point have been, anyway? She keeps her money in banks and places like Tychris... smart woman to make her money work for her. If there's anything in her vaults that isn't just dust and cobwebs, I don't want or need to know what it is." |"Hawkethorne was built upon the ruins of the village that stood here more then two hundred years ago. According to the baroness, the wraiths swept through the village and did a number on it, then flowed about the castle and went on their merry way up north towards the elves. The survivors who'd taken shelter in the castle were too disheartened to go on and left for Tychris, seeking the safety of numbers; what buildings weren't already wrecked from the passage of the wraiths' armies eventually fell into disrepair over the years." You've noticed that both Sanders' chapel and the statue in the town square are obviously from the Hawkethorne of old, what with their architecture being incongruous with the rest of how the village is built. What of the other buildings? The Frost Hound? "Ah... well, the Hound's foundations were placed on some particularly solid ground, but no, we didn't incorporate any of the ruins into it — I was very particular about that. Garth and I were supposed to build it with our own sweat, and no one else's. There's a certain pride in that and I think it struck a balance, being able to build upon ground that someone else had doubtlessly prepared, yet going through the effort to make something of your own so you don't forego the work you put into it. "Still, it's a reason why the village is so haphazard as it is. Many of the settlers who came with our bunch chose to try and fix up the ruined homes and make them livable — after Sanders had gone through each and every one of them for ghosts, curses and that kind of thing. The buildings that came up after used those first fixer-uppers as points from which they got their bearings, and so the place was a bit of a mess even twenty years ago. Now that I've had a chance to walk around town for a bit, everything being more prosperous hasn't changed that in the slightest — everything's still a mess, just a richer mess. Not that there's anything wrong with that, it shows that the village's got life and grown with its people, rather than being ordered top-down in grids like the old imperial cities were." |Sanders hasn't given her any more trouble, has he? Or the other way around, for that matter? You could sense how close it came to blows when she first arrived back in town, and hope the situation hasn't gone downhill any. Gweyr looks a little sheepish at the question. "We-ll. That's a touchy subject." Isn't going to stop you from asking it. For obvious reasons, you'd really not let things get to another head just because no one wants to sit down and talk. "Well, I'm not going to say that he's outright forgiven me for what I did, and the same goes for me to him. That being said, letting buried demons be just that is something we can live with for the sake of the village. [var0|Riordan's got a daughter, and I've got kids to look out for|Riordane considers the kids of the village the children he never had, and I've got me own pups to look out for]. If nothing else, we can at least agree that we shouldn't let our bloody business taint their lives any more than it already has." A detente, then? "That. I'm not going to be heading into the chapel any time to confess all my sins... and after hearing the anguish he went through after what happened, going so far as to renounce Lumia and take up the mantle of Velun, I feel a little bad for him. Just a little. The man's clearly suffered and anguished over his decisions, sending me off to walk the ice included, and so I can forgive him. Just a little. And sure, he may have never outright lied to my son about me... but he never told the whole truth either. "Long story short, you don't have to worry, [pc.name]. So long as he doesn't start any trouble, I'm not going to cause any on my end, and I'm sure he feels the same way about me as well. The future of Hawkethorne is important — at least the both of us can agree on that. People like you[var0|, Liaden] and my pups are just that. The sooner the ugliness of the past can be consigned to tales to be heard and learned from instead of lived, the better." |"The other day, I went and took my first proper look at the militia Garth and Sanders whipped up in my absence." And what's her verdict? "An undisciplined rabble, but you really can't expect that much more from people who have lives to run and mett at most maybe for a half-day every other week to go through some basic drills with those two. They're not any actual fighting force... but you don't need much more than that in order to protect a village this size. Maybe if Hawkethorne grows to the point where professional men-at-arms would be needed, I'd be more upset, but as things stand I won't be living to see that day. Maybe in Garret's or Gwyn's, if they're lucky and hardworking." Well, she could help hurry that day along. She's got lots of practice in this whole soldiering thing, doesn't she? Gweyr arches an eyebrow at you. "I'd like to remind you that the village has a militia — these are people who have lives, [pc.name]. It'd be about as useful as putting me in a dress and trying to pass me off as a princess — they don't have the inclination or time for the kind of regimen I'd want to put them through, assuming that I held any kind of authority in their eyes to begin with. And to be frank, I think I like it this way. Everyone knows each other and where everyone else lives, and that's a pretty good deterrent against someone getting too big for his breeches. No point spending time and effort on a lost cause, is there? That's for my pups to handle, if it ever comes to that." |"Hawkethorne's changed so much since I left to walk the ice," Gweyr says with a small, reminiscing sigh. "If not for the Hound, the chapel and the statue in the middle of town, I wouldn't be able to tell that it was the same place Garth and I settled." It's like leaving your kids and returning years later to see them all grown up without you, isn't it? The old wolfess winces. "About there, yes. There're so many more people here now, and everything's so much richer, for lack of a better word..." Well, it wasn't always like this even when you first arrived in town. Tollus's shenanigans have driven many of the folk from Harvest Valley into town seeking refuge, and fewer people are heading out into the woods with all the recent trouble. You're sure that once things settle down, the people holed up within the walls will return back to their old homes. "That's the hope. That's the hope. And it doesn't make it any easier — in fact, it just makes it worse. Profiting off other people's genuine misfortune here, that doesn't sit well with me." Idealistic words coming from a woman who used to be a mercenary. Gweyr shows you her teeth. "You don't know how my father or I ran the Crossed Swords, so please don't make any assumptions here. That, and twenty years out on the ice gives a woman plenty of time to reflect on her life." |How old is River, anyway? Does she know? Gweyr shrugs. "Little guy looked as he did when we first met him on the train of settlers going back up north. Hasn't visibly aged a day since. Have you ever seen an old catfolk? It's like they stay the same for decades upon decades, looking relatively young... and then a bit past middle age they just fold in upon themselves into shrivelled-up felines. So, no. I'm just waiting for the day I walk out to the square to give him his milk, and instead of the little guy I know I'll find a raisin in his place." ... Gweyr laughs, seeing your expression. "[pc.ra catfolk |Hit a little too close to home there, did I? Ah, that's the price catfolk pay for being so good-looking for so much of their lives |Well, maybe that's a bit of an overstatement, but that's the price catfolk pay for being so pretty for so much of their lives ]. Live in a way that has you aging gracefully, friend. Don't wind up like me here, all decrypt and feeling the wind in your bones every time the weather turns ever so slightly gray." River is a king of living in the moment — sure, he remembers so much, but is willing to let all of it go and live day to day. To be fair, it's only because he's got people around him who're willing to shoulder that burden for him. One way or the other, it's hard to imagine Hawkethorne without him sitting on the bench by the statue; he's all but a fixture of the town square at this point. He'll be missed when it's eventually time for him to go. ]
rows.translation: [rand |托卢斯用这样一个借口诱骗了他那个小教派里的那些孩子：他说女男爵的城堡下面有装满黄金的地下金库，而她为了帮助那些新来定居的人，拒绝与他人分享这些财富。”格维尔冷笑道，“至少，这个故事听起来……还挺可信的。那座城堡规模足够大，它所处的山脉也足够坚固，因此如果她真有这样的需求，完全可以在地下建造规模庞大的地窖。然而，考虑到我女儿为维护这个地方而获得的信任与资助，其实从一开始就根本没有足够的黄金来建造这些地窖。 我在‘十字剑’组织的时候就见过很多次这种情况——人们找到了那些珍宝，一下子变得富有了，但几年后却把所有的钱都花光了，因为他们根本不知道该如何把钱用来投资或赚钱。你们可以随便评价托勒斯，但至少他知道该如何跟人们沟通，当他愿意这么做的时候。二十年前的那些乡村孩子，比大多数人都更聪明、更敢于冒险——要想成为先驱，就必须有勇气。但对他们来说，这位女男爵只会坐拥巨额财富而无所作为，这种想法也是可以理解的，因为如果他们处在她的位置上，也会这么做。" 那位女男爵的城堡下面很可能有地下储藏室，对吧？ “其实很有可能，如果这种建筑风格符合那个时期的贝尔哈兰建筑风格的话；我曾经考察过太多废墟，因此知道，古代的贝尔哈兰人非常注重建筑的标准化和布局规范。不过，我其实从未真正问过那位女男爵是否可以看看她的藏宝处。反正问了也没什么用吧？她的钱都存放在银行和像提克里斯这样的地方……真是个聪明的女人，懂得让自己的钱为自己工作。如果她的藏宝室里真有什么除了灰尘和蜘蛛网之外的东西，我既不想也不需要知道那是什么。" |鹰棘镇城堡是建在两百多年前曾坐落于此的村庄的废墟之上。据那位女男爵所说，那些幽灵曾肆虐那个村庄，造成了严重的破坏，随后它们又绕着城堡流动，继续向北方方向奔去，前往精灵们的领地。那些躲在城堡里的幸存者们已经心灰意冷，不再愿意继续留在那里，于是便前往了提克里斯，寻求人群带来的安全感；而那些在幽灵军队的侵袭下已经损毁的建筑物，也随着时间的流逝逐渐荒废了。" 你一定注意到了，桑德斯的礼拜堂以及镇广场上的那座雕像，它们的建筑风格明显属于古老的鹰棘镇时期，与村庄其他部分的建筑风格完全不协调。那么其他建筑呢？比如“霜犬酒馆”那座建筑？ 啊……嗯，‘猎犬’的基础确实是建立在一些非常稳固的基础之上的，但是并没有使用任何废墟材料——我在这一点上非常坚持。本来应该由加斯和我用自己的汗水来建造它，而不是依靠别人的努力。这样做其实有一种特别的自豪感，而且我认为这样也能达到一种平衡：虽然我们是建立在前人已经准备好的基础上，但还是要自己付出努力去完成它，这样才能确保自己不会忽视自己所付出的辛勤劳动。 不过，这也正是这个村庄如今如此杂乱无章的原因。那些和我们一起来到这里的定居者中，有很多人选择尝试修复那些被毁坏的房屋，让它们变得适合居住——在桑德斯检查过每一栋房屋，确保其中没有鬼魂、诅咒之类的东西之后，他们才这么做的。后来建起来的那些建筑，都是以那些最初被翻修过的房屋作为参照点来建造的，因此，即使在二十年前，这个地方也依然是一片混乱。现在，我有机会在镇上走走看看，虽然一切都变得更加繁荣了，但这种情况丝毫没有改变——一切依然很混乱，只不过是变得更加混乱罢了。这并没有什么不妥，恰恰说明这个村庄是有活力的，它是随着人们的居住而发展起来的，而不是像那些古老的帝国城市那样，由上而下按照网格规划来建设的。 |桑德斯应该没有再给她带来什么麻烦吧？或者反过来，也是同样的情况？当她第一次回到镇上时，你能感觉到局势有多么紧张，希望现在的情况没有进一步恶化。 格维尔听到这个问题后显得有些尴尬：“呃，这个……有点敏感吧。” 但这并不妨碍你继续提问。显然，你不会因为没人愿意坐下来讨论这个问题，就任由事情继续恶化吧？交谈嗯，我不能说他已经完全原谅了我所做的一切，而我对他也是如此。不过，为了村庄的利益，我们还是可以选择让那些埋藏在心底的怨恨继续存在吧。 [var0|里奥丹有个女儿，而我还有自己的孩子需要照顾。|里奥丹把村里的孩子们当作自己从未拥有过的孩子来照顾，而我也有自己的小狗需要照料呢。]至少我们可以达成这样一个共识：我们不能再让我们的生意进一步扰乱他们的生活了。” 那么，算是暂时停战吧？ “没错。我也不会每次都去教堂忏悔我的所有罪过。……在听了他所经历的那些痛苦之后——他甚至放弃了卢米娅，转而承担起了维伦的责任——我对他感到有些同情。只是一点点而已。很明显，他为自己所做的决定而痛苦、挣扎，包括让我去冰原上行走这件事，因此我能够原谅他。就那么一点点而已。当然，他可能从未对我的儿子说过关于我的任何谎言……但他也从未告诉过全部真相。 “长话短说，你不必担心[pc.name]只要他不惹麻烦，我也不会主动招惹他，我相信他对我也是同样的态度。鹰棘镇的未来非常重要——至少这一点我们俩是认同的。像你这样的人[var0|李亚登]我的孩子们也是如此。过去那些丑陋的事情，如果能尽早被当作故事来听、来学习，而不是真正去经历它们，那就再好不过了。 |前几天，我终于有机会仔细看看加思和桑德斯在我不在的时候召集起来的那支民兵组织了。” 那么，她的评价是什么呢？ “那只是一群缺乏纪律的乌合之众罢了。不过，对于那些平时要忙于自己的生活，而且最多也只是每隔一周才能花半天的时间和这两个人一起进行一些基础训练的人来说，你也不能指望他们能做得更好吧。他们其实并不算是一支真正的战斗力量……但对于保护这样一个规模的村庄来说，这样的力量已经足够了。或许等到鹰棘镇的发展规模到了需要雇佣专业武装人员的地步，我才会更加担忧，但就目前的情况来看，我恐怕活不到那一天。也许可以在加雷特或格温的家里，如果他们运气好且足够努力的话。” 嗯，她可以帮助加快那天的进程吧。她在这方面可是有很多经验的，不是吗？ 格韦尔挑了挑眉毛看着你。我想提醒大家，这个村庄有一个民兵组织 — 这些都是有着自己生活的普通人。[pc.name]这简直就像给我穿上一条裙子，试图把我伪装成公主一样——前提是他们在我眼中真的具备任何权威，否则他们根本不会有兴趣，也不会有时间去遵循我想要他们遵守的那些规定。说实话，我觉得这样挺好的。大家彼此都认识，也知道彼此住在哪里，这样就能有效防止有人变得过于傲慢或嚣张。把时间和精力浪费在毫无希望的事情上，实在没有意义，不是吗？如果真到了那一步，那就交给我那些小伙伴来处理吧。 |自从我离开去冰原上漂泊之后，鹰棘镇变了很多，”格韦尔轻叹着，语气中充满了回忆。“要不是有那条猎犬、那座小教堂以及镇中心的那座雕像，我根本无法认出这里就是加斯和我曾经定居的地方。” “这就好比离开自己的孩子，多年后再回来时，发现他们已经都在没有你的陪伴下长大了，不是吗？” 那位年迈的母狼苦涩地点了点头：“差不多吧。现在这里的人口多了很多，一切都变得不一样了更富有嗯，说实话，情况并不总是这样的……当初你刚来到这个小镇的时候，情况也并非如此。托卢斯的那些恶作剧让许多来自丰收谷的人们不得不来到小镇寻求庇护，而最近发生的这些麻烦事也让越来越少的人愿意再去森林里了。你确信，一旦局势稳定下来，那些躲在城墙内的人们就会回到他们原来的家中。 “这就是我们的希望。确实如此。但这也并没有让事情变得更容易——事实上，情况反而更糟了。在这里利用别人的真正不幸来牟取利益，这种行为让我感到非常不舒服。” 这些理想主义的话语，出自一个曾经当过雇佣兵的女性之口。 格维尔露出了锋利的牙齿：“你根本不了解我的父亲和我是如何管理‘交叉之剑’组织的，所以请不要随便妄加猜测。再加上在冰上度过了二十年，这样的经历让一个女人有足够的时间去反思自己的人生。 |瑞弗到底多大了？她知道吗？ 格维尔耸了耸肩：“那个小家伙，我们第一次在前往北方的移民列车上遇到他的时候，就是那个样子。从那以后，他一点都没有变老。你见过老年的猫族吗？它们似乎几十年都不会发生变化，看起来依然很年轻……但一旦过了中年，它们就会逐渐萎缩，变成干瘪的猫一样。所以，不，我只是在等待那么一天——当我走到广场去给它喂奶时，却发现代替那只我熟悉的小家伙的，竟然是一颗葡萄干。…… 看到你的表情，格维尔笑了起来。[pc.ra catfolk |这话未免有点伤人吧？啊，对于猫族来说，拥有如此出众的外貌，这大概就是他们必须付出的代价吧…… |嗯，也许这么说有点夸张了，但猫族正是因为他们一生中大部分时间都拥有如此美丽的容貌，才不得不付出这样的代价。 ]朋友，要以一种能让自己优雅老去的方式生活吧。可别像我这样，到最后一切都变得毫无意义，每当天气稍微变阴沉一点，就觉得浑身都不对劲。 瑞弗才是真正懂得活在当下的人——当然，他记得很多事情，但他愿意放下这一切，一天天地过好每一天。公平地说，这一切之所以能够成真，正是因为他身边有那些愿意为他分担这份责任的人。无论如何，很难想象如果没有他坐在雕像旁的长椅上，鹰棘镇会是什么样子——在如今这个阶段，他几乎已经成为了镇广场上不可或缺的一部分了。当他最终离开的时候，人们一定会想念他的。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"Tollus lured the first kids of his little cult with the claim that there were vaults full of gold beneath the baroness's castle that she wasn't sharing to help the settlers," Gweyr says with a snort. "That story was... plausible, to say the least. That castle is large enough, and the stretch of mountain it sits upon strong enough, for there to have be some extensive vaults beneath if that's what she wanted. However, given the trust and stipend that's been awarded to my daughter for upkeep of this place, there was never any gold to begin with. "I've seen it several times back when I was in the Crossed Swords — people finding relics and getting rich, then proceeding to drink it all away in a couple years because they never think of putting that money to work. Say what you want of Tollus, but he knew how to speak to people when he'd the mind to. The village kids of twenty years ago were a bit smarter and more daring than most — you had to have guts to try and be a pioneer — but the idea that the baroness would just sit on a pile of wealth and not do anything with it was plausible to them because that's what they'd have done in her place." It's possible that the baroness has vaults beneath her castle, though? "More than possible, actually likely if it follows Belharan architecture from the period; I've dug through enough ruins to know that old Belhar likes their standardization and organization. Still, I've never actually asked the baroness if I could take a look. What would the point have been, anyway? She keeps her money in banks and places like Tychris... smart woman to make her money work for her. If there's anything in her vaults that isn't just dust and cobwebs, I don't want or need to know what it is." |"Hawkethorne was built upon the ruins of the village that stood here more then two hundred years ago. According to the baroness, the wraiths swept through the village and did a number on it, then flowed about the castle and went on their merry way up north towards the elves.
