The survivors who'd taken shelter in the castle were too disheartened to go on and left for Tychris, seeking the safety of numbers; what buildings weren't already wrecked from the passage of the wraiths' armies eventually fell into disrepair over the years." You've noticed that both Sanders' chapel and the statue in the town square are obviously from the Hawkethorne of old, what with their architecture being incongruous with the rest of how the village is built. What of the other buildings? The Frost Hound? "Ah... well, the Hound's foundations were placed on some particularly solid ground, but no, we didn't incorporate any of the ruins into it — I was very particular about that. Garth and I were supposed to build it with our own sweat, and no one else's. There's a certain pride in that and I think it struck a balance, being able to build upon ground that someone else had doubtlessly prepared, yet going through the effort to make something of your own so you don't forego the work you put into it. "Still, it's a reason why the village is so haphazard as it is. Many of the settlers who came with our bunch chose to try and fix up the ruined homes and make them livable — after Sanders had gone through each and every one of them for ghosts, curses and that kind of thing. The buildings that came up after used those first fixer-uppers as points from which they got their bearings, and so the place was a bit of a mess even twenty years ago. Now that I've had a chance to walk around town for a bit, everything being more prosperous hasn't changed that in the slightest — everything's still a mess, just a richer mess. Not that there's anything wrong with that, it shows that the village's got life and grown with its people, rather than being ordered top-down in grids like the old imperial cities were." |Sanders hasn't given her any more trouble, has he? Or the other way around, for that matter? You could sense how close it came to blows when she first arrived back in town, and hope the situation hasn't gone downhill any. Gweyr looks a little sheepish at the question. "We-ll. That's a touchy subject." Isn't going to stop you from asking it. For obvious reasons, you'd really not let things get to another head just because no one wants to sit down and talk. "Well, I'm not going to say that he's outright forgiven me for what I did, and the same goes for me to him. That being said, letting buried demons be just that is something we can live with for the sake of the village. [var0|Riordan's got a daughter, and I've got kids to look out for|Riordane considers the kids of the village the children he never had, and I've got me own pups to look out for]. If nothing else, we can at least agree that we shouldn't let our bloody business taint their lives any more than it already has." A detente, then? "That. I'm not going to be heading into the chapel any time to confess all my sins... and after hearing the anguish he went through after what happened, going so far as to renounce Lumia and take up the mantle of Velun, I feel a little bad for him. Just a little. The man's clearly suffered and anguished over his decisions, sending me off to walk the ice included, and so I can forgive him. Just a little. And sure, he may have never outright lied to my son about me... but he never told the whole truth either. "Long story short, you don't have to worry, [pc.name]. So long as he doesn't start any trouble, I'm not going to cause any on my end, and I'm sure he feels the same way about me as well. The future of Hawkethorne is important — at least the both of us can agree on that. People like you[var0|, Liaden] and my pups are just that. The sooner the ugliness of the past can be consigned to tales to be heard and learned from instead of lived, the better." |"The other day, I went and took my first proper look at the militia Garth and Sanders whipped up in my absence." And what's her verdict? "An undisciplined rabble, but you really can't expect that much more from people who have lives to run and mett at most maybe for a half-day every other week to go through some basic drills with those two. They're not any actual fighting force... but you don't need much more than that in order to protect a village this size. Maybe if Hawkethorne grows to the point where professional men-at-arms would be needed, I'd be more upset, but as things stand I won't be living to see that day. Maybe in Garret's or Gwyn's, if they're lucky and hardworking." Well, she could help hurry that day along. She's got lots of practice in this whole soldiering thing, doesn't she? Gweyr arches an eyebrow at you. "I'd like to remind you that the village has a militia — these are people who have lives, [pc.name]. It'd be about as useful as putting me in a dress and trying to pass me off as a princess — they don't have the inclination or time for the kind of regimen I'd want to put them through, assuming that I held any kind of authority in their eyes to begin with. And to be frank, I think I like it this way. Everyone knows each other and where everyone else lives, and that's a pretty good deterrent against someone getting too big for his breeches. No point spending time and effort on a lost cause, is there? That's for my pups to handle, if it ever comes to that." |"Hawkethorne's changed so much since I left to walk the ice," Gweyr says with a small, reminiscing sigh. "If not for the Hound, the chapel and the statue in the middle of town, I wouldn't be able to tell that it was the same place Garth and I settled." It's like leaving your kids and returning years later to see them all grown up without you, isn't it? The old wolfess winces. "About there, yes. There're so many more people here now, and everything's so much richer, for lack of a better word..." Well, it wasn't always like this even when you first arrived in town. Tollus's shenanigans have driven many of the folk from Harvest Valley into town seeking refuge, and fewer people are heading out into the woods with all the recent trouble. You're sure that once things settle down, the people holed up within the walls will return back to their old homes. "That's the hope. That's the hope. And it doesn't make it any easier — in fact, it just makes it worse. Profiting off other people's genuine misfortune here, that doesn't sit well with me." Idealistic words coming from a woman who used to be a mercenary. Gweyr shows you her teeth. "You don't know how my father or I ran the Crossed Swords, so please don't make any assumptions here. That, and twenty years out on the ice gives a woman plenty of time to reflect on her life." |How old is River, anyway? Does she know? Gweyr shrugs. "Little guy looked as he did when we first met him on the train of settlers going back up north. Hasn't visibly aged a day since. Have you ever seen an old catfolk? It's like they stay the same for decades upon decades, looking relatively young... and then a bit past middle age they just fold in upon themselves into shrivelled-up felines. So, no. I'm just waiting for the day I walk out to the square to give him his milk, and instead of the little guy I know I'll find a raisin in his place." ... Gweyr laughs, seeing your expression. "[pc.ra catfolk |Hit a little too close to home there, did I? Ah, that's the price catfolk pay for being so good-looking for so much of their lives |Well, maybe that's a bit of an overstatement, but that's the price catfolk pay for being so pretty for so much of their lives ]. Live in a way that has you aging gracefully, friend. Don't wind up like me here, all decrypt and feeling the wind in your bones every time the weather turns ever so slightly gray." River is a king of living in the moment — sure, he remembers so much, but is willing to let all of it go and live day to day. To be fair, it's only because he's got people around him who're willing to shoulder that burden for him. One way or the other, it's hard to imagine Hawkethorne without him sitting on the bench by the statue; he's all but a fixture of the town square at this point. He'll be missed when it's eventually time for him to go. ] "

rows.translation: 鹰棘镇

rows.original: [flags.GWEYR_TALK_CULT |[rand |"Be careful. Tollus and his inner circle of henchmen have gotten extremely dangerous in such a short period of time — they've managed to accrue more power in a mere handful of months than they did over the twenty years I hounded them, no doubt thanks to the demoness they managed to bring through. Even their minions are nothing to sneeze at any more — even untrained and undisciplined, those that we faced in that sunken castle would've been a match for any one of the Crossed Swords, maybe two. These aren't village kids that Tollus had to sway any more." Well, you're improving really damn quickly, too. "Good. Then keep pace with him, and keep on kicking his ass. Tollus isn't stupid — he knows that power you buy, beg, borrow or steal from something or someone else isn't yours, and he'll be looking to wean himself off that demoness' teat as soon as he can. Everything you have, you've built up yourself from scratch some way or another, and that's one of the biggest edges that you hold over him. Go and get him, tiger." You will. There's always the annoying fact that he keeps on getting away, though... "Don't get cocky, don't get overconfident — that's what killed so many of my men back in the heartlands. And as for him getting away all the time... are you really that surprised? Even I know well enough that a hole with only one exit is known as a trap; someone like Tollus is going to have multiple ways of fucking off when things go badly for him. "I think that if you really do want to pin him down, you'll have to do some prep and cut off his avenues of retreat before you go about calling him out. There was no reasonable way we could do that down under the sea, but if he's really by the coastland then you'll have better chances at being able to reconnoitre the area and see if you can't cut off his escape beforehand. Worms like Tollus don't have the grace to die on their own — not with him being untouched by time's fire as it is. No, someone's got to pin him down and drive a stake through that ugly heart of his, and it may as well be you." It would be nice to deal with the bastard once and for all. And this time, you'll go for the head, not the gut. Gweyr rubs her temples. "It ought to have been fatal — if not from the wound itself, then from Leold spilling his guts into his blood and the whole bloody infection thing. Wasn't counting on him being so valuable to Tollus. Like I said, [pc.name] — overconfidence. Don't make the same mistake I did." |"Remember, head east past the mountains and to the coast. Given the direction they were last seen heading, that's where Tollus and his flunkies are most likely to have ended up. There's no shortage of old ruins for them to start digging up, so I expect that you won't have any trouble finding them once you manage to get there. "And be careful. I'll wager that the cult isn't the only thing that you'll need to be mindful of — the place was cursed before the Belharans ever arrived, and whatever they were doing down by the water has only made it ever more so. It's not as bad as the heartlands, but it's still damnably blasted, and only the gods know what has happened to the people who used to live there, suffice to say that they probably aren't people any more. "You're the best chance we have at this point, kid. Keep a good head on your shoulders, and try to come back home in one piece." |"I don't know if it might even be a possibility, but given the things we found deep under the sea, it's a safe bet that Tollus is planning to double-cross his demonic mistress," Gweyr says thoughtfully. "If you could somehow manage to warn her of his impending treachery in a way that doesn't arouse her suspicion, you might be able to turn the two of them against each other, buy us some more time for us to act. It's a gamble, but at this point I'm not sure whether Tollus or the demoness he purportedly serves is a bigger threat." You'll think about it. The potential is there... although you're not sure how Kasyrra might react to such an accusation, regardless of evidence. [kas.romantic|And let's face it: while you privately know that you'd have her ear anytime, getting her to take Tollus as a credible threat is going to be an uphill task.] "It's a long shot, there's no doubt about it. But if the opportunity does come up, I think it's worth the try. We're already so limited in our options to turn this thing around that I do sometimes wonder if half the things we're doing are just to stave off that feeling of dread... but that's not something I'm going to devote too much thought to." |"From all the things my Dad told me, I'd advise you to have a plan to get wet when you arrive at the coast. The place was already low-lying to begin with and experienced rather drastic tidal changes, but whatever happened to the place during the Godswar only made that even worse. I'd wager a whole chunk of the ruins are underwater at high tide, and you can only get in at low, since we don't have Imora's help any more. "There's also a lot of mud and silt, which makes the ground unstable... don't wind up getting yourself caught in soft ground in your haste to not get swept out to sea when the tide comes in. Of course, I'd wager that none of the locals are bothered in the least by any of this." |One thing that you've noticed about Tollus and his cult is that despite the devices and machines that Kasyrra was able to build, such as the one you saw in the Winter City, the cult itself hasn't been deploying any of them. That implies that either Kasyrra didn't want to teach them, or that they weren't willing to learn. Or maybe it's something else altogether, but you just found it odd that Kas didn't disseminate that knowledge amongst her own people. Maybe she was just boasting back then... Gweyr shrugs. "It's clear that Tollus has no love for his mistress, yes, but the members of his cult are clearly enthralled with the demoness herself. Then again, being sex-addled, scatter-brained maniacs doesn't lend itself well to actually learning anything serious — I'd say that only Tollus's inner circle still have their brains about them. "I honestly don't know. Maybe she doesn't trust them, maybe they don't want to learn, maybe the demoness' creations are so far beyond us that we have no chance of comprehending them because we wouldn't even know where to begin, even with instruction. Without any concrete evidence of motivation, I can only speculate. Still, it's only to our advantage — imagine if every single two-bit goon of Tollus's cult had that kind of knowledge at their fingertips and the wherewithal to use it. The odds stacked against us would be far worse than they already are." ] |Gweyr mulls over your question for a moment. "Given everything we've learned so far, as well as what I've been able to gather from my husband and the other townsfolk about Tollus's activities down south in the valley, he's clearly working towards some huge ultimate goal or the other. The centaurs may have been a burden that was passed down to him by the demoness he serves that he turned to his own purposes, but his actions in the rift were completely on his own initiative as far as I can tell. While I don't have any idea of what a man like him might ultimately want aside from the obvious accrual of power for its own sake, I know that he wants it really badly and thus it's imperative that we stop him from getting it." Has she any leads? Any follow-up information that she might've gained from the other residents of the rift when she was saying her goodbyes? "The jotuns did tell me that the cultists packed up their things and left in an orderly fashion — it wasn't a rout or even a retreat, it was a disengagement. It was too clean and neat, as if they'd been planning it for a good while now, and had always known that their presence within the rift was always meant to be temporary. There were a few stragglers who might've been a skeleton crew or simply left behind and the jotuns dealt with them easily, but it's still worrying. The people of the rift don't really care what goes on in the world that's outside of their little backyard, but we do. "The last anyone saw any sizable group of them, they were spotted by the selkies flying off over the mountains and towards the southeast. That would place them directly on the eastern coast." [party.has arona |"That was where Argoth was going to put down our longships at first," Arona grunts. "Problem was, we couldn't find a proper way over the mountains from the beaches there, so we had to circle around a bit to get where we wanted to go." ] The eastern coast... sounds like a stretch, and a pretty long one at that. Gweyr nods. "The coast runs along the entire edge of the mountains, and it's where the Marches end and Sailgraves begin. If Tollus managed to make his way there with his cult in tow, you'll need to go east from the foothills and somehow make your way over the peaks. That could be a problem." You already have some idea of how that might be the case, but you'd like her perspective on it nonetheless. "There are two ways to head east — under the mountains, or over them. Garth informs me that the minotaurs are barring entry to their domain, which makes that a problem because the eastern gates of Khor'minos open out into the tunnels that lead into the coastlands. The other way is to try and scale the mountains... which is all but impossible because the harpy matron makes her roost there. Her ugliest, meanest daughters are nothing like the scatterbrained sluts who infest the foothills, so don't take them lightly. If you try to climb, they will pull you off and dash you upon the rocks below, if you try to fly over — well, it's the same thing. "That does raise the question of why the harpies haven't actually pulled his fliers out of the sky, which leads me to suspect he used that magic ship of his to transport anyone and anything he cared for along the coast." There aren't any passes through the eastern mountains, then. "No. There may have used to be, but if there ever were the harpies have blocked them off long ago; they don't like people wandering about in the ruins they've claimed as their own. That's all the harpies ever do... squat in the remains better people have left behind and pride themselves on it as if they were the ones to build them in the first place. They damn well didn't dig those baths to begin with, that's for sure." That's very interesting, but Tollus and the coastlands... let's say you found a way across the mountains. Is there anything she knows that might help you start narrowing down the search for him and his cult? Gweyr thinks a moment. "I've never been there before myself, but my father used to tell me that the Belharans made their biggest settlement in the Marches down by the coast. The ocean brought in warm air from the south, and that suited their sensibilities... that, and the confluence of mountain and sea so close together created a sort of effect on the place. The local lupine tribes used to stay away from the coast, saying it was cursed, and thus the Belharans had no opposition when they established a beachhead in the place in order to study this phenomenon. According to Dad, they brought in a huge number of artifacts and people to the handful of scholarly settlements that lay along the coast. If I were Tollus, I'd be digging in those for the remaining pieces of whatever puzzle he's trying to solve." All right. Make it down to the coast, kick Tollus's ass again, call it a day. "Good luck. While this old dog doesn't have any more adventures left in her, I'm here if you need any advice on the situation. That's our job now: cover the rear, share what we know, and give ourselves up if necessary so you kids can live. While I still have things to live for... they're all related to you kids these days. If it comes down to it, I've lived a long life and have no regrets; only the gods are left to judge me now." ]
rows.translation: [flags.GWEYR_TALK_CULT |[rand |小心。在这么短的时间内，托勒斯和他的核心手下已经变得极其危险了——他们在短短几个月内获得的权力，比我花了二十年时间追捕他们所获得的还要多，这无疑要归功于他们设法招致的那位女恶魔。就连他们的手下也不再是可以小觑的存在了——尽管这些家伙没有受过训练，也没有纪律性，但在那座沉没的城堡里与我们交手的那些人，至少可以与“十字剑团”的任何一名成员抗衡，甚至可能对付两名成员。这些已经不再是托勒斯需要用手段去收买或控制的乡下孩子了。嗯，你的进步速度也快得惊人啊。” “很好。那就继续保持这个势头，继续把他打得落花流水吧。托勒斯并不傻——他很清楚，你无论是通过购买、乞讨、借钱还是其他方式获得的那些力量，其实都你的他会尽快摆脱那个女人的控制。你所拥有的一切，都是你自己通过努力一点一点积累起来的，而这正是你比他更具优势的地方之一。去把他抓回来，老虎。” “你一定能做到的。不过，总是有那么个恼人的问题……他就是总能够逃脱。” “别太自大，别过于自信——正是这种态度让我在内陆失去了太多战士。至于他总能逃脱……你真的觉得这很意外吗？就连我都知道，只有一个出口的洞其实就是个陷阱；像托勒斯这样的人，一旦遇到麻烦，肯定会有很多办法逃掉。 我认为，如果你真的想让他无法逃脱，就必须做好充分的准备，切断他所有的退路。在……之前你就去把他找出来吧。在海底，我们根本不可能采取那种行动；但如果他真的在海岸附近，那你就有更大的机会侦察那个区域，看看是否能在他逃跑之前阻止他。像托勒斯这样的家伙，根本不会自己选择死亡——尤其是他这种仿佛被时间遗忘的存在。不，必须有人把他制服，然后用一根木桩刺穿他那丑陋的心脏，而这个人，很可能是你。会这次终于有机会彻底解决那个混蛋了。而且这次，一定要击中要害，而不是他的内脏。 格维尔揉了揉太阳穴：“这本该致命的——就算不是因为那道伤口，也会因为利奥尔德的内脏出血以及那该死的感染而丧命。我本来没指望他对托勒斯来说会如此重要。就像我之前说的[pc.name] — 过于自信。千万不要重蹈我的覆辙。 |记住，向东穿过山脉，然后前往海岸。根据他们最后一次被看到的行进方向，托勒斯和他的手下很可能已经去了那里。那里有大量的古老遗迹可供他们挖掘，所以我相信你们一旦到达那里，应该不会遇到任何找他们的困难。 还有，一定要小心。我敢打赌，你们需要留意的不仅仅是那个邪教组织——在贝尔哈兰人到来之前，这个地方就已经被诅咒了，而他们在水边进行的那些活动，只会让这种诅咒变得更加严重。虽然这里没有腹地那么糟糕，但环境依然糟糕至极。只有神明才知道那些曾经居住在这里的人们发生了什么，可以肯定的是，他们很可能已经不在人世了。人们目前来说，你是我们最好的希望了，孩子。一定要保持冷静，努力平安回家。 |我不知道这是否真的有可能，但根据我们在海底发现的那些线索，可以肯定的是，托勒斯正在密谋背叛他的恶魔女主人，”格维尔若有所思地说道，“如果你能想办法以一种不会引起她怀疑的方式，警告她他即将背叛她，或许就能让他们彼此对立，从而为我们争取更多行动的时间。这确实是个冒险的决定，但现阶段我并不确定，托勒斯本身，还是他所谓的所侍奉的那个女恶魔，哪个才是更大的威胁。 你可以仔细考虑一下。这个可能性确实是存在的……不过，无论证据如何，你也不确定卡希拉会对这样的指控做出怎样的反应。 [kas.romantic|说实话：虽然你心里清楚，随时都可以和她沟通，但要让她真正将托勒斯视为一个值得重视的威胁，其实是一件相当困难的事情。] 这个机会的成功几率很低，这一点毫无疑问。但如果真的有机会出现，我认为尝试一下还是值得的。目前我们在扭转这一局面时可以选择的手段实在太有限了，有时候我甚至会怀疑，我们所做的那些事情，有一半其实只是为了缓解那种恐惧感而已……不过，这个问题我并不打算花太多时间去思考。 |根据我爸爸告诉我的那些情况，我建议你们在到达海岸后，最好事先做好会被淋湿的准备。那个地方本来就地势低洼，而且潮汐变化也非常剧烈；而在“神战”期间，那个地方肯定发生了更严重的变化，情况因此变得更加糟糕了。我敢打赌，在涨潮的时候，那些废墟的很大一部分都会被水淹没，而只有在退潮的时候才能进入那些地方，因为我们现在再也没有伊莫拉的帮助了。 “而且那里还有很多淤泥和泥沙，这使得地面变得非常不稳定。…在潮水涌来时，为了不被冲到海里，你千万不要急功近利，以免陷入松软的地面中。当然，我敢打赌，这里的当地人根本不会因为这些事情而感到困扰。 |你可能已经注意到，关于托勒斯和他的教派，尽管卡希拉制造出了各种设备和机器——比如你在冬城看到的那些——但这个教派本身却从未使用过这些技术。这说明，要么是卡希拉并不愿意将这些知识传授给他们，要么就是他们本身不愿意学习。当然，也有可能是其他原因……不过你确实觉得奇怪：为什么卡希拉不把这些知识传播给自己的族人呢？也许当时她只是在炫耀罢了…… 格维尔耸了耸肩：“很明显，托勒斯对他的情妇并没有丝毫感情，但他的那些追随者显然被这位女恶魔迷住了。不过，这些沉溺于性欲、头脑混乱的疯子们，根本不可能认真学习任何东西——我认为，只有托勒斯的亲信们才还算清醒些。 说实话，我也不清楚。也许她不信任他们，也许他们根本不想学习，又或许那些恶魔女创造的东西远远超出了我们的理解范围，我们根本无从下手，即使有人指导我们也无济于事。由于没有任何关于其动机的确凿证据，我只能进行推测。不过，这对我们来说反而有利——试想，如果托勒斯教派的每一个卑鄙小人都掌握了这样的知识，并且有能力加以运用，那会是什么后果呢？对我们来说，这些不利因素会比现在更加严重。 ] |格维尔仔细思考了你提出的问题。“根据我们目前所了解到的所有信息，以及我从我丈夫和其他镇民那里获得的关于托勒斯在山谷南部活动的消息，可以明显看出，他正在为某个重大的终极目标而努力。那些半人马或许只是他侍奉的那位女恶魔传给他的负担，而他将其为己所用；但就我所知，他在裂隙中的行动完全出自他的主动意愿。虽然我并不清楚像他这样的人最终究竟想要什么——除了追求权力本身之外——但我知道，他非常渴望得到权力，因此我们必须阻止他得逞。" 她有什么线索吗？在道别时，她是否从裂隙中的其他居民那里得到了什么进一步的消息？ “那些巨灵确实告诉我，那些邪教徒是有条不紊地收拾好东西离开了——那并不是一场溃逃，甚至也不算是一种撤退，只是他们主动选择了离开而已。一切都太整洁、太井然有序了，仿佛他们早就为此做了充分的准备，而且一直都清楚自己存在于这个裂隙中的时间只是暂时的。虽然还有少数人可能只是残余力量，或者只是被遗忘了，但那些巨魔们轻松就解决了他们，这仍然让人感到担忧。裂隙中的居民们其实并不关心他们那小范围领域之外世界上发生的事情，但我们却很在意。 最后一次有人看到他们中有相当数量的人时，是看到那些海豹精飞越山脉，朝着东南方向飞去了。那么，他们应该就在东海岸附近。 [party.has arona |阿戈斯原本打算把我们的长船停放在那里，”阿罗娜低声说道，“但问题在于，我们找不到一条合适的路线能够从那些海滩穿过山脉，所以不得不绕道一番才能到达目的地。 ] 东部海岸……听起来是一段相当长的路线。 格维尔点了点头：“这条海岸线沿着山脉的整个边缘延伸，正是边境地区与航海者领地的分界线。如果托勒斯带着他的教派成功抵达了那里，你们就需要从山脚向东行进，然后想办法翻越那些山脉。这可能会遇到不少麻烦。 你大概已经猜到可能会是这种情况，但还是想听听她的看法。 “有两条路线可以通往东方——要么从山下穿过，要么翻越山脉。加斯告诉我，弥诺陶洛斯正在封锁通往他们领地的道路，这就成了一个问题，因为科尔米诺斯的东门通向那些通往海岸地区的隧道。另一种方法是试图翻越那些山脉……但这几乎是不可能的，因为那个凶恶的女头目就栖息在那里。她那些最丑陋、最恶毒的女儿们，与那些出没在山脚下的那些愚蠢、放荡的女子们完全不同，所以千万不要小看她们。如果你试图攀爬，它们会把你拉下来，然后把你摔在下面的岩石上；如果你试图飞过去——嗯，结果也是一样的。 这就引出了一个问题：为什么那些女妖们并没有把他的传单从天空中抓下来呢？这让我怀疑，他一定是用那艘魔法飞船，把那些他珍视的人或物运到了沿海地区。” 那么，东部山脉应该没有任何通道可以穿过吧。 不。也许以前确实有，但如果真有的话，那些女妖早就把它们封锁起来了；她们可不喜欢有人在他们占据的废墟里闲逛。女妖们所做的就是这些……占据别人留下的遗迹，还洋洋自得地以为这些遗迹是她们自己建造的。可以肯定的是，那些浴场根本不是她们挖出来的。 这确实很有趣，但是托勒斯和那些沿海地区……假设你找到了穿越山脉的方法，她是否知道些什么可以帮助你缩小寻找他和他的教派的范围呢？ 格维尔思考了一会儿。我自己从未去过那里，但我父亲曾经告诉我，贝尔哈兰人在沿海的边境地区建立了他们最大的定居点。海洋从南方带来了温暖的空气，这种气候很适合他们的生存习惯。此外，山脉与海洋如此接近地交汇在一起，也在这一地区产生了一种特殊的自然现象。当地的狼族部落过去总是避开这片海岸，认为它被诅咒了；因此，当贝拉人决定在这里建立据点来研究这一现象时，并没有遭到任何反对。据爸爸说，他们把大量的文物和人们带到了那些分布在海岸线上的少数学术定居点里。如果我是托勒斯，我一定会仔细研究这些文物，试图找出他正在试图解开的那个谜题中缺失的线索。" 好吧，一路赶到海岸边，再把托勒斯打得落花流水，然后就结束这一天吧。 “祝你好运。虽然我这老狗已经没有更多的冒险可以经历了，但如果你需要关于当前情况的建议，我随时都在。这就是我们现在的使命：掩护后方，分享我们所知道的一切，必要时甚至要牺牲自己，只为了让你们这些孩子能够活下去。虽然我还有很多理由继续活下去……但这些理由如今都与你们这些孩子息息相关。归根结底，我这一生已经走得很长了，也没有任何遗憾；现在，只有神明才能评判我。" ]
rows.raw: " [flags.GWEYR_TALK_CULT |[rand |"Be careful. Tollus and his inner circle of henchmen have gotten extremely dangerous in such a short period of time — they've managed to accrue more power in a mere handful of months than they did over the twenty years I hounded them, no doubt thanks to the demoness they managed to bring through. Even their minions are nothing to sneeze at any more — even untrained and undisciplined, those that we faced in that sunken castle would've been a match for any one of the Crossed Swords, maybe two. These aren't village kids that Tollus had to sway any more." Well, you're improving really damn quickly, too. "Good. Then keep pace with him, and keep on kicking his ass. Tollus isn't stupid — he knows that power you buy, beg, borrow or steal from something or someone else isn't yours, and he'll be looking to wean himself off that demoness' teat as soon as he can. Everything you have, you've built up yourself from scratch some way or another, and that's one of the biggest edges that you hold over him. Go and get him, tiger." You will. There's always the annoying fact that he keeps on getting away, though... "Don't get cocky, don't get overconfident — that's what killed so many of my men back in the heartlands. And as for him getting away all the time... are you really that surprised? Even I know well enough that a hole with only one exit is known as a trap; someone like Tollus is going to have multiple ways of fucking off when things go badly for him. "I think that if you really do want to pin him down, you'll have to do some prep and cut off his avenues of retreat before you go about calling him out. There was no reasonable way we could do that down under the sea, but if he's really by the coastland then you'll have better chances at being able to reconnoitre the area and see if you can't cut off his escape beforehand. Worms like Tollus don't have the grace to die on their own — not with him being untouched by time's fire as it is. No, someone's got to pin him down and drive a stake through that ugly heart of his, and it may as well be you." It would be nice to deal with the bastard once and for all. And this time, you'll go for the head, not the gut. Gweyr rubs her temples. "It ought to have been fatal — if not from the wound itself, then from Leold spilling his guts into his blood and the whole bloody infection thing. Wasn't counting on him being so valuable to Tollus. Like I said, [pc.name] — overconfidence. Don't make the same mistake I did." |"Remember, head east past the mountains and to the coast. Given the direction they were last seen heading, that's where Tollus and his flunkies are most likely to have ended up. There's no shortage of old ruins for them to start digging up, so I expect that you won't have any trouble finding them once you manage to get there. "And be careful. I'll wager that the cult isn't the only thing that you'll need to be mindful of — the place was cursed before the Belharans ever arrived, and whatever they were doing down by the water has only made it ever more so. It's not as bad as the heartlands, but it's still damnably blasted, and only the gods know what has happened to the people who used to live there, suffice to say that they probably aren't people any more. "You're the best chance we have at this point, kid. Keep a good head on your shoulders, and try to come back home in one piece." |"I don't know if it might even be a possibility, but given the things we found deep under the sea, it's a safe bet that Tollus is planning to double-cross his demonic mistress," Gweyr says thoughtfully. "If you could somehow manage to warn her of his impending treachery in a way that doesn't arouse her suspicion, you might be able to turn the two of them against each other, buy us some more time for us to act. It's a gamble, but at this point I'm not sure whether Tollus or the demoness he purportedly serves is a bigger threat." You'll think about it. The potential is there... although you're not sure how Kasyrra might react to such an accusation, regardless of evidence. [kas.romantic|And let's face it: while you privately know that you'd have her ear anytime, getting her to take Tollus as a credible threat is going to be an uphill task.] "It's a long shot, there's no doubt about it. But if the opportunity does come up, I think it's worth the try. We're already so limited in our options to turn this thing around that I do sometimes wonder if half the things we're doing are just to stave off that feeling of dread... but that's not something I'm going to devote too much thought to." |"From all the things my Dad told me, I'd advise you to have a plan to get wet when you arrive at the coast. The place was already low-lying to begin with and experienced rather drastic tidal changes, but whatever happened to the place during the Godswar only made that even worse. I'd wager a whole chunk of the ruins are underwater at high tide, and you can only get in at low, since we don't have Imora's help any more. "There's also a lot of mud and silt, which makes the ground unstable... don't wind up getting yourself caught in soft ground in your haste to not get swept out to sea when the tide comes in. Of course, I'd wager that none of the locals are bothered in the least by any of this." |One thing that you've noticed about Tollus and his cult is that despite the devices and machines that Kasyrra was able to build, such as the one you saw in the Winter City, the cult itself hasn't been deploying any of them. That implies that either Kasyrra didn't want to teach them, or that they weren't willing to learn. Or maybe it's something else altogether, but you just found it odd that Kas didn't disseminate that knowledge amongst her own people. Maybe she was just boasting back then... Gweyr shrugs. "It's clear that Tollus has no love for his mistress, yes, but the members of his cult are clearly enthralled with the demoness herself. Then again, being sex-addled, scatter-brained maniacs doesn't lend itself well to actually learning anything serious — I'd say that only Tollus's inner circle still have their brains about them. "I honestly don't know. Maybe she doesn't trust them, maybe they don't want to learn, maybe the demoness' creations are so far beyond us that we have no chance of comprehending them because we wouldn't even know where to begin, even with instruction. Without any concrete evidence of motivation, I can only speculate. Still, it's only to our advantage — imagine if every single two-bit goon of Tollus's cult had that kind of knowledge at their fingertips and the wherewithal to use it. The odds stacked against us would be far worse than they already are." ] |Gweyr mulls over your question for a moment. "Given everything we've learned so far, as well as what I've been able to gather from my husband and the other townsfolk about Tollus's activities down south in the valley, he's clearly working towards some huge ultimate goal or the other. The centaurs may have been a burden that was passed down to him by the demoness he serves that he turned to his own purposes, but his actions in the rift were completely on his own initiative as far as I can tell. While I don't have any idea of what a man like him might ultimately want aside from the obvious accrual of power for its own sake, I know that he wants it really badly and thus it's imperative that we stop him from getting it." Has she any leads? Any follow-up information that she might've gained from the other residents of the rift when she was saying her goodbyes? "The jotuns did tell me that the cultists packed up their things and left in an orderly fashion — it wasn't a rout or even a retreat, it was a disengagement. It was too clean and neat, as if they'd been planning it for a good while now, and had always known that their presence within the rift was always meant to be temporary. There were a few stragglers who might've been a skeleton crew or simply left behind and the jotuns dealt with them easily, but it's still worrying. The people of the rift don't really care what goes on in the world that's outside of their little backyard, but we do. "The last anyone saw any sizable group of them, they were spotted by the selkies flying off over the mountains and towards the southeast. That would place them directly on the eastern coast." [party.has arona |"That was where Argoth was going to put down our longships at first," Arona grunts. "Problem was, we couldn't find a proper way over the mountains from the beaches there, so we had to circle around a bit to get where we wanted to go." ] The eastern coast... sounds like a stretch, and a pretty long one at that. Gweyr nods. "The coast runs along the entire edge of the mountains, and it's where the Marches end and Sailgraves begin. If Tollus managed to make his way there with his cult in tow, you'll need to go east from the foothills and somehow make your way over the peaks. That could be a problem." You already have some idea of how that might be the case, but you'd like her perspective on it nonetheless. "There are two ways to head east — under the mountains, or over them. Garth informs me that the minotaurs are barring entry to their domain, which makes that a problem because the eastern gates of Khor'minos open out into the tunnels that lead into the coastlands. The other way is to try and scale the mountains... which is all but impossible because the harpy matron makes her roost there. Her ugliest, meanest daughters are nothing like the scatterbrained sluts who infest the foothills, so don't take them lightly. If you try to climb, they will pull you off and dash you upon the rocks below, if you try to fly over — well, it's the same thing. "That does raise the question of why the harpies haven't actually pulled his fliers out of the sky, which leads me to suspect he used that magic ship of his to transport anyone and anything he cared for along the coast." There aren't any passes through the eastern mountains, then. "No. There may have used to be, but if there ever were the harpies have blocked them off long ago; they don't like people wandering about in the ruins they've claimed as their own. That's all the harpies ever do... squat in the remains better people have left behind and pride themselves on it as if they were the ones to build them in the first place. They damn well didn't dig those baths to begin with, that's for sure." That's very interesting, but Tollus and the coastlands... let's say you found a way across the mountains. Is there anything she knows that might help you start narrowing down the search for him and his cult? Gweyr thinks a moment. "I've never been there before myself, but my father used to tell me that the Belharans made their biggest settlement in the Marches down by the coast. The ocean brought in warm air from the south, and that suited their sensibilities... that, and the confluence of mountain and sea so close together created a sort of effect on the place. The local lupine tribes used to stay away from the coast, saying it was cursed, and thus the Belharans had no opposition when they established a beachhead in the place in order to study this phenomenon. According to Dad, they brought in a huge number of artifacts and people to the handful of scholarly settlements that lay along the coast. If I were Tollus, I'd be digging in those for the remaining pieces of whatever puzzle he's trying to solve." All right. Make it down to the coast, kick Tollus's ass again, call it a day. "Good luck. While this old dog doesn't have any more adventures left in her, I'm here if you need any advice on the situation. That's our job now: cover the rear, share what we know, and give ourselves up if necessary so you kids can live. While I still have things to live for... they're all related to you kids these days. If it comes down to it, I've lived a long life and have no regrets; only the gods are left to judge me now." ] "

rows.original: Leaving the Frost Hound through the back door instead of the front, you find yourself in the tavern's back yard. Garth's cabin sits in one corner of the plot, and there's the chicken coop, and there... well, you never. That little log cabin wasn't there the last time you looked — how long ago was that, anyway? — but now it is, a small, homey thing that you figure must be Gwyn's nursery. That's pretty quick when it comes to construction, to be honest, but Garth is a pillar of the community and presumably got together the best people for his daughter's pet project. To be fully honest, you're not exactly sure about this — despite the speed with which the nursery has been thrown together, if the baroness can only invest this much into the future generations of Hawkethorne... ...Well, maybe it isn't right to pre-judge the situation; there might be something here that you're missing, after all. Large, wooden-slatted windows with nets drawn over them let plenty of light into the interior, but there's no reason to pussyfoot about the matter. Striding up to the door, you turn the handle and push your way in. Huh. The cabin isn't as spartan as what its exterior suggested, but there's still something or the other about the place that's a little lacking. However, saying that to Gwyn's face seems a bit tactless, especially considering how enthusiastic the wolfess is as she bounds towards you, her hefty chest bouncing up and down ever so slightly as she bobs a curtsy. "You came," she says, a little out of breath. "I was getting worried." Well, she's glad to see you, looks like. What was she getting worried about, if you might ask? Gwyn waves off your question perhaps a little too quickly. "Oh, nothing." Her gaze spins around left and right, as if she were looking for something. Eventually, though, the wolfess' eyes land back on yours, and a small smile plays upon her muzzle. "Come to see the place, [pc.name]?" Yes, you wanted to see what it was like, considering Cait was gushing all over it. Look, you're going to try and be tactful about the matter, but... the nursery is a bit more cramped than you expected it to be. "I know. I would've petitioned for more funding, but the baroness was rather explicit in her letter that while she would keep me from going under, expanding the place was going to be up to me. She could pay for much more, but long story short, I wouldn't learn anything if it was all dropped in my lap. We don't have much, it is true, but the children are cared for, and they're warm and comfortable. I also have a little help from a few of the other mothers in the village who've volunteered to put in their time, so it isn't too much of a burden." You see. She nods. "Like I told you before, donations are always welcome. I won't charge you since the baroness's fund is paying for everything, but extra money would always be appreciated. If you're concerned for the children's living conditions, then here's your chance to help give them a hand." All right. [pc.isChamp|You didn't want to lay into her like that, but... "No, no, it's quite all right. I do understand — in fact, I'm a little glad that you're showing such concern." Is it just your imagination, or is Gwyn blushing a little? Probably just your imagination, but it's adorable all the same.|She didn't have to be such a bitch about it, but you'll let it slide for now.] "Now, if you need me, I'll be around, but I've got some things to do otherwise. Like they say, a woman's work is never done." No one's work is ever done up here, to be honest. Gwyn giggles. "I suppose that's true up here in Hawkethorne; Daddy works harder than everyone else. Still, my point stands — so long as you don't disturb the children, you're welcome to visit any time." Any time. One final nod from Gwyn, a swish of her skirts, and she's off, leaving you to ponder your next move.
rows.translation: 如果从后门而不是前门离开霜犬酒馆，你就会来到酒馆的后院。加斯的小屋坐落在那块地的一角，那里还有鸡舍那里……嗯，你从来都不会注意到这些细节。上次你来的时候，那小木屋还根本不存在——到底那是多久以前的事了呢？——但现在它确实在那里了，一座小巧而温馨的小屋，你应该猜到那一定是格温的玩乐场所吧。说实话，建造速度也确实快得惊人，不过加斯确实是社区的栋梁，想必也为女儿的这个特别项目挑选了最优秀的人才。 说实话，你其实并不确定这些事情——尽管这个托儿所是如此迅速地建立起来的，但如果女男爵只能投入有限的资源的话这个 ……嗯，也许现在就对这种情况下结论还为时过早；毕竟，可能还有一些你尚未注意到的细节。那些装有纱窗的大型木制百叶窗让充足的光线照进室内，但在这个问题上，我们没有必要再犹豫不决了。你大步走到门前，转动门把手，推门走了进去。 嗯，这个小屋并不像它的外观所显示的那样简陋，但这个地方还是有些地方显得有点欠缺。然而，当着格温的面这么说似乎有点不得体，尤其是考虑到那只母狼正满怀热情地向你奔来，它那厚实的胸脯在鞠躬时微微上下晃动。 你来了。她边说边有点气喘吁吁。我开始担心起来了。 嗯，看起来她见到你很高兴。如果你想问的话，她之前到底在担心些什么呢？ 格温似乎有点太快地回答了你的问题。哦，没什么。她的目光左右扫视，仿佛在寻找着什么。然而最终，那只母狼的目光又落回到了你的身上，她的嘴角浮现出一丝微笑。来看看这个地方吧，[pc.name]？" 是的，你本来就想看看实际情况到底是怎样的，毕竟凯特对那里赞不绝口。听着，你得尽量委婉地处理这件事，但是……婴儿房确实比你想象中要拥挤一些。 我知道。我本应该申请更多的资金，但女男爵在信中说得非常清楚：虽然她会确保我的事业不会失败，但是否继续扩大规模，最终还是要由我来决定。她完全有能力提供更多的资金，但长话短说，如果所有东西都直接摆到我面前，我根本学不到任何东西。的确，我们拥有的并不多，但孩子们都得到了照顾，他们生活得温暖而舒适。此外，村里还有一些其他母亲自愿抽出时间来帮助我，所以也并没有那么困难。太根本算不上什么负担。 你瞧。 她点了点头。正如我之前所说，我们始终欢迎大家的捐赠。由于女男爵的基金已经承担了所有费用，所以我不会向您收取任何费用，不过如果有额外的捐款，我们将不胜感激。如果您关心这些孩子的生活状况，那么现在就是您伸出援手帮助他们的机会。 好的。 [pc.isChamp|你本来并不想那样对她发火的，但是…… 不，不，完全没有关系。我完全理解——事实上，我反而很高兴你这么关心我。这只是你的想象而已，还是格温真的有点脸红了？大概只是你的想象吧，但这样想的话，还挺可爱的呢。|她本不必这么刻薄，但这次你就先忍了吧。] 现在，如果你需要我，我会在身边，不过我还有其他事情要处理。就像人们说的，女人的活儿永远做不完。 说实话，这里根本没人能把工作真正完成。 格温轻声笑了起来。我想在鹰棘镇这里确实是这样；爸爸比其他人都更加努力工作。不过，我的意思还是不变的——只要你不打扰孩子们，随时都可以来拜访。 随时都可以。 格温最后点了点头，轻轻摆动了一下裙摆，然后便离开了，留下你独自思考下一步该怎么做。

rows.translation: 下一步
观察者

rows.original: [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 12 |As you come striding into the nursery, you're bowled over by Gwyn and her [var0|big pregnant belly|boundless enthusiasm]. The nursery matron gives you a smile and lick on the face before helping you upright and pulling you into a hug. She's a good girl, all right — a big, good girl. What's the occasion? "Oh! I just wanted to thank you for contributing so much to the nursery! I don't know where you got all that money — even Daddy didn't make as much during his days as a mercenary — but it's really appreciated!" You're just doing your part to help the town. "Well, you could turn that attention elsewhere, if you like. I'm not going to say no to more funding, but I've already run out of ideas on how to make things better. The place is pretty much already as good as it will ever be, so if you hear someone else somewhere needs the stuff, just go ahead and give it to them! They'll need it more than we do now!" That's why you love Gwyn; she has such a generous heart. All right, then... you'll keep that in mind. |You enter the Nursery and can tell right away that the upgrade is finished. [ dayNight |Gwyn looks red-faced and flustered — casting you quick glances between keeping to herself in one corner of the room — but not angry. You'd actually guess she seems ecstatic, tossing you a small flirtatious wave of her fingertips. With the upgrade complete, you can probably select another once you've gathered the funds. |Gwyn isn't here but you can see a note hanging on the doorway nearby. Taking it down and scanning over it, you can't help but think of how it almost smells like arousal. "Sorry I missed you [pc.name], but hell if I didn't look at that door hoping you'd walk in so I could thank you! Swing by in the morning, alright? I've got some thanks to show you[gwyn.fucked|[pc.hasCock| and I hope you have a bone for me]]... oh and if you want, we can talk about putting more money toward the next upgrades — the kids will owe you more than you can imagine." ] ]
rows.translation: [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 12 |你大步走进托儿所，便被格温连同她的[var0|硕大的孕肚|无限的热情]撞得站不稳。托儿所的女主管微笑着舔了舔你的脸，扶你站好，再将你拥入怀中。她确实是个好姑娘——一个大个子好姑娘。这是有什么喜事？ “哦！我只是想感谢你为托儿所做出了这么多的贡献！我不知道你是怎么筹集到那么多钱的——就连爸爸在当雇佣兵的时候也没赚到这么多钱——但我真的非常感激！” 你只是在尽自己的一份力来帮助这个小镇而已。 “嗯，如果你愿意的话，可以把注意力转移到其他地方去。我当然不会拒绝更多的资金支持，但关于如何让事情变得更好，我已经想不出任何办法了。这个地方已经差不多达到它所能达到的最佳状态了，所以，如果你听到有人在其他地方需要这些东西，那就尽管把它们送给他们吧！他们现在比我们更需要这些东西！” 这就是你喜欢格温的原因，她的心真是太宽广了。好吧，那么……你一定要记住这一点。 |你一走进托儿所，就能立刻察觉到升级已经完成。 [ dayNight |格温的脸颊涨得通红，显得有些慌乱——她不时偷偷地瞥你一眼，却始终独自待在房间的一个角落里——但并没有生气。事实上，你甚至会觉得她看起来非常兴奋，她还用指尖朝你俏皮地挥了挥手。既然这次升级已经完成，等你筹集到足够的资金后，应该就可以选择另一次升级了。 |格温不在这里，但你可以看到附近门口处挂着一张便条。拿下来仔细阅读后，你不禁会觉得，这张便条似乎散发着一种令人兴奋的气息…… “抱歉，我错过了你[pc.name]，但我真的特别希望你能走进那扇门，这样我就能当面感谢你啦！明天早上过来吧，好吗？我有话要跟你说，真的非常感谢你。[gwyn.fucked|[pc.hasCock| 我还希望你能为我准备一根骨头]]……哦，如果你愿意的话，我们可以商量再投入一些资金用于接下来的升级——孩子们以后会欠你的债多得让你想象都想不到。” ] ]

I've got some thanks to show you[gwyn.fucked|[pc.hasCock| and I hope you have a bone for me]]... oh and if you want, we can talk about putting more money toward the next upgrades — the kids will owe you more than you can imagine." ] ]"

rows.original:
Gwyn's nursery is a small, cozy cabin situated behind the Frost Hound, right next to Garth's abode and the chicken coop. Built from treated logs stacked up on each other, cut planks for the roof, and tar to seal up the cracks and keep out the wind, it's not a very glamorous structure. The initial grant from the baroness has clearly gone more towards utility rather than decoration, but Gwyn's done her best to brighten the interior a little with colorful wall tapestries and curtains over the windows.

        Still, space is at a premium. Most of the cribs are cocoon-like bundles of white cloth and stretchy rope, hanging from the rafters in neat rows and bobbing about gently. Easily detachable when the extra room is needed, these hammocks do appear a little dangerous, but Gwyn knows what she's doing when it comes to childcare. There's also a large furry rug spread out over one corner of the wooden floorboards, a bit of empty space for the children to play on. In one corner by the grated hearth lies a large box stuffed with straw — an incubator that, unsurprisingly, bears a striking resemblance to a little nest.
        
        [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 1|A door in the far wall reveals a newer addition to the nursery: a well-equipped kitchen[flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 2| and fully stocked pantry], close enough so that Gwyn doesn't have to cross over to the Frost Hound to cook the childrens' meals.]
        
        The entire place is kept warm by a fire in a large hearth, securely grated so the children can't get too close to the heat. All in all, while the nursery isn't as well-built as the Frost Hound, at least it's serviceable in its simplicity. Gwyn looks happy enough with the place, at the very least, and so do the kids in her care. 
        
        [flags.NURSERY_CONSTRUCTION_TS|One side of the nursery has been cordoned off, though, and you can see a trio of burly lupines hammering, smearing and sawing away, filling the air with the faint scent of pine tar and sawdust. You can only imagine what's being built here, since Gwyn's not telling, but she's in a particularly good mood today. It's a little more effort to keep the little ones corralled and away from the construction, but there's little doubt it'll all pay off when it's over.]
        
        Gwyn herself has a small room in the back of the nursery, separated from the main building by a simple door and curtain drawn over the doorway to shield it from view. Like the rest of the nursery, it's not very large, barely enough to hold a bed and chest of drawers, but it serves its purpose.
rows.translation:
格温的婴儿房是一间小巧而舒适的小屋，位于霜犬酒馆的背后，紧挨着加斯的住所和鸡舍。这小屋是用经过处理的原木堆叠而成的，屋顶的木板也是手工切割的，而裂缝则用焦油密封起来，以阻挡寒风侵入——总之，这并不是什么外观华丽的结构。女男爵最初提供的资金显然更多被用于实用设施的搭建，而非装饰，但格温还是尽了自己最大的努力，通过使用色彩鲜艳的墙挂毯和窗帘来为室内环境增添一些亮色。

        不过，空间仍然非常有限。这些吊床大多是由白色布料和有弹性的绳子编织而成的、形似茧状的包裹，它们整齐地悬挂在房梁上，轻轻摇摆着。当需要更多空间时，这些吊床可以很容易地拆卸下来。虽然看起来有点危险，但格温在照顾孩子方面可是很有经验的。在木地板的某个角落，还铺着一块柔软的毛茸茸的地毯，为孩子们留出了足够的活动空间。而在靠近炉子的那个角落，放着一个装满稻草的大箱子——这个“孵化器”看起来简直就像一个小鸟的巢穴，这一点也不奇怪。
        
        [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 1|远处的墙上一扇门打开了，里面是婴儿房新添置的设施：一个设备齐全的厨房。[flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 2| 以及储备充足的食品储藏室]这个距离已经足够近了，因此格温不必穿过霜犬酒馆的区域去为孩子们准备饭菜。]
        
        整个房间都靠一个大型壁炉里的火焰来保持温暖，壁炉的边缘被处理得非常安全，这样孩子们就不会太靠近火焰而受到伤害。总的来说，虽然这个育儿室的结构没有“寒霜猎犬”那么坚固，但它的简单设计已经足够实用了。至少，格温对这个地方很满意，她照顾的孩子们也同样开心。 
        
        [flags.NURSERY_CONSTRUCTION_TS|不过，育儿室的一边已经被围了起来，你可以看到三个体格魁梧的人正在敲打、涂抹和锯切，空气中弥漫着淡淡的松焦油和木屑的气息。由于格温没有透露具体在建造什么，你只能猜测他们在这里正在做什么，不过她今天的心情似乎格外好。要把那些小孩子们哄住，让他们远离施工区域，确实需要费些功夫，但毫无疑问，等这一切完工后，肯定会有值得的回报。]
        
        格温自己在婴儿房的后面有一个小房间，这个房间通过一扇简单的门与主楼隔开，门口还拉上了帘子，以防止被人看到。和婴儿房的其它部分一样，这个房间也不是很大，勉强只能放下一张床和一个五斗柜，但它的作用已经足够了。

rows.original: Thanks to the continued donations of everyone — you included, of course — the nursery's grown quite a bit, more than doubling in size after its first major expansion. No longer thrown together from rough logs, the smooth, cut planks that form the walls and floor have been caulked together with strong resin, the windows actual glass instead of just holes in the walls with heavy curtains drawn over them. Outside by the chicken coop, someone's sunk a wellshaft deep into earth, seeking to supply the seemingly endless need for fresh water that the nursery has. Despite the additional space, there's only one hearth still needed thanks to the better insulation afforded by the double-spaced walls, casting a flickering light over the nursery's interior from its position of honor at the nursery's heart. Grates still prevent the little ones from wandering too close to the roaring flames, and a number of lanterns on the walls and ceiling afford warm, amber light in the evenings. The incubator is still there, even if the majority of Hawkethorne's residents don't need to use it that much. Space is still at a premium — as the nursery has grown, so has the number of Gwyn's clients. The youngest are still contained within the hanging cribs that you've gotten to know so well, but at least there's now a little more room to walk between them, and the adjoining empty space is now wide enough for the children to run around in a little. [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 6|Gwyn's also fenced off a portion of the place with colorful rope to end up with a makeshift playpen of sorts, complete with a toy chest or two and an assortment of stuffed toys that she appears to have sewn together herself. All of them look extremely durable. ]The growing number of children has led to Gwyn marshalling a few of the younger lupine women in town into her service, the additional helpers providing the extra pairs of hands that she needs to keep things running smoothly. [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 5|A bookcase mounted on the wall catches your eye — a small children's library. While it's true that most people on the frontier can't read, the children love to be read to, and Gwyn's almost always more than willing to accommodate requests for such. ]With all the improvements, the nursery is starting to look more like a place for actual habitation instead of a barnyard pen; the tapestries are coming along nicely, and various crude but quaint arts and crafts produced by the children have been put up on the walls. Yes siree, the place is truly looking domestic — much like Gwyn herself. [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 7|With all the extra money coming in from donations, Gwyn's even managed to get in a few middling paintings up on the walls, as well as mobiles hanging from the ceiling — knowing her, she's probably all for exposing her charges to art and beauty as soon as possible. ]The soft words and laughter of children fill the air, and it's certainly very calming in its own right. Beyond these walls lies the cold, unforgiving harshness of the Frost Marches, but here the warmth of Gwyn's bosom reigns supreme. Although the nursery's come a long way since its humble beginnings, you get the feeling that there's still plenty of space for it to expand into. [flags.NURSERY_CONSTRUCTION_TS|As if mirroring your thoughts, the trio of lupines pounding away at whatever it is they're building step up their pace to practically a frenzy, working away with determined furor.] Last but not least, Gwyn's room in the back of the nursery has been renovated as well — while a bit larger, it's still tiny compared to the rest of the place. But at least there's place for one to stand around in, and she's managed to fit in a table and chairs, as well as a wardrobe. Large, curtained windows on two of the walls let in plenty of light, and windowsill planters hold a number of sweet-smelling herbs in the form of small white flowers — decorative and useful.
rows.translation: 多亏了大家持续的捐赠——当然也包括你——这个托儿所已经发展得相当大了，在经过第一次大规模扩建后，其规模甚至增加了一倍以上。现在，构成墙壁和地板的木板已经不再是粗糙的原木拼接而成，而是经过精心切割、表面光滑的木板，这些木板用坚固的树脂粘合在一起；窗户也不再是墙上的洞洞，而是真正的玻璃窗，上面还挂着厚重的窗帘。在鸡舍的外面，有人把一口井挖得很深，目的是为了满足苗圃对淡水看似无穷无尽的需求。 尽管空间变大了，但由于双层墙壁提供了更好的隔热效果，实际上仍然只需要一个壁炉。这个壁炉位于婴儿房的中心位置，因此它的光芒会照亮整个婴儿房的内部空间。栅栏依然防止孩子们过于靠近熊熊燃烧的火焰，而墙壁和天花板上挂着的许多灯笼在夜晚会散发出温暖的金色光芒。尽管鹰棘镇的大多数居民并不经常需要使用它，但那个孵化器依然在那里。 空间仍然非常紧张——随着托儿所规模的扩大，格温的客户数量也在增加。最年幼的孩子们仍然被安置在那些你们已经非常熟悉的悬挂式婴儿床里，但至少现在在这些婴儿床之间的活动空间稍微大了一些，而且旁边的空地也足够让孩子们在里面自由活动了。 [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 6|格温还用彩色绳子把场地的一部分围了起来，这样就形成了一个临时的游乐区，里面还有一个或两个玩具箱，以及各种各样看起来都是她亲手缝制的毛绒玩具。所有这些玩具看起来都非常结实耐用。 ]随着儿童数量的增加，格温不得不召集镇上一些较年轻的雌性狼族来为她工作。这些额外的帮手部为她提供了所需的人力，使各项事务能够顺利进行。 [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 5|墙上摆放的一个书架吸引了你的注意——那是一个为孩子们准备的的小图书馆。虽然边境地区的大多数人都不识字，但孩子们都非常喜欢别人给他们读书听，而格温也几乎总是很乐意满足他们的这个请求。 ]经过所有的这些改进，这个育儿室看起来真的越来越像一个适合居住的地方了，而不再是一个像牲口棚那样的地方；那些挂毯也做得非常不错，孩子们制作的各种虽然粗糙但充满趣味的手工艺品也被挂在了墙上。没错，这个地方确实变得很有家的感觉了——简直就像格温本人一样。 [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 7|由于捐赠带来的额外收入，格温甚至设法在墙上挂了几幅还算不错的画作，还在天花板上悬挂了一些装饰品——以她的性格，她肯定希望尽快让她的学生们接触到艺术与美。 ]孩子们轻柔的话语和笑声充满了空气，这种氛围本身就让人感到十分宁静。在这堵墙之外，是寒冷而严酷的霜冻之地，但在这里，格温的温暖怀抱却占据了主导地位。 尽管这个托儿所已经从它最初的简陋状态发展到了今天这个地步，但你仍然能感觉到，它还有很大的发展空间。 [flags.NURSERY_CONSTRUCTION_TS|仿佛在回应你的想法，那三只正在努力建造着某物的狼犬突然加快了速度，几乎陷入了疯狂的状态，它们以极其坚定的热情继续着它们的工作。] 最后但同样重要的是，位于婴儿房后面的格温的房间也经过了翻新——虽然面积比之前稍大了一些，但与房子的其他部分相比，仍然显得很小。不过至少有足够的空间让人在里面活动，她还设法把一张桌子和几把椅子，以及一个衣柜都安置了进去。房间两面墙上装有较大的带窗帘的窗户，这些窗户能让充足的光线照进来；窗台上的花盆里种着一些散发着芳香的小白花，为房间增添了不少装饰效果。以及很有用。

rows.original:
Gwyn's nursery has certainly come a long way from its humble beginnings as a log cabin in the Frost Hound's backyard. A towering two stories tall, it counts itself amongst the more stately buildings in Hawkethorne — although it still doesn't quite match up to the Frost Hound or Chapel of Velun, it nevertheless stands in its own right as one of the town's landmarks. The old wood building has been replaced with one of solid brick, with plenty of insulation to keep the interior warm against the Frost Marches' chill. The well still sits by the chicken coop, [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 10|although there's no further need for buckets and ropes any more, not with the hand-cranked pump that's been installed.|buckets and rope lying by its side.] Despite all this, the box incubator still sits by the hearth, a reminder of the place's humble beginnings.

        The place itself is doing quite the booming business. Some things never change — Gwyn seems very fond of the hanging cribs herself — but the rest of the interior is completely changed. Various corners of the main building have been marked off with colorful posts for the older children — a free play area floored with furry rugs, a dining hall by the kitchens for mealtimes, [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 12|a small section with various child-friendly musical instruments, ]so on and so forth. [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 11|There's even what might amount to an impromptu school for the very young, staffed by some of the local villagers with a few hours to spare. There doesn't seem to be much in the way of reading, writing and such except for the few youngsters who're interested in such — unsurprising, considering how most of the local populace can't really read — but schooling appears to be more verbal and dedicated to the practical ways of life and survival up here in the Frost Marches. ]Infants themselves have a room of their own, away from the hustle and bustle of the main building, and mesh lamps hang safely out of reach, casting a warm light on the entire scene.
        
        The entire nursery is bright and colorful, painted in warm colors to contrast with the cold, unforgiving world beyond its walls. Various bits of arts and crafts, glued-together toys and the like hang up on the walls, garishly cheerful in the way only a mother could love. At the head of it all is a crudely-drawn — well, for a value of drawn, it honestly looks more like a collection of scribbles — portrait of Gwyn herself, surrounded by red and pink hearts. There aren't any words here, but none are needed to convey what's being said here. Standing in the nursery, for a moment at least, one can gain respite from a world infected by corruption.
        
        [flags.NURSERY_CONSTRUCTION_TS|Through all this, a rather familiar trio of lupines continue work on a roped-off area of wall, hammering and pounding away at whatever Gwyn's next project happens to be. Some of the youngsters wander up to them out of curiosity, but at least have better sense than to actually bother the men while they're at work.]
        
        Gwyn's room in the back of the nursery is finally, just perhaps, something worthy of someone bearing the title of nursery matron. She's clearly got a thing for natural light, huge glass windows adorning the walls, complete with heavy drapes. In one corner, a large, comfortable-looking bed, in the other, a chest of drawers and heavy wardrobe. An ornate rocking chair carved in the traditional lupine style sits by the fireplace, and upon the mantle lie a few knick-knacks of obviously sentimental value, as well as where she puts her... um, tools of the trade when she's not using them. At least they're kept out of sight in an ornate wooden box, lest one of the children accidentally wander in. Flowering herbs for use in cooking adorn the windowsill planters, their little white blossoms swaying in the breeze.
        
        Ah, it definitely gives you a sense of satisfaction to see how far the nursery's gone — and in no small part thanks to your efforts.
rows.translation:
格温的育儿室已经发生了巨大的变化，它从最初只是弗罗斯特·霍恩后院的一间小木屋发展成了如今这座两层楼高的宏伟建筑。在鹰棘镇镇上，它无疑属于较为庄严的建筑物之一——虽然还远远比不上弗罗斯特·霍恩或维伦礼拜堂的规模，但它本身也已经成为了这座小镇的标志性建筑之一。那座古老的木结构建筑已经被一座用实心砖建造的新建筑所取代，新建筑配备了充足的保温材料，从而能够在严寒的霜冻季节里保持室内温暖。那口井依然位于鸡舍旁边。 [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 10|既然已经安装了手摇泵，那么就不再需要桶和绳子了。|桶和绳子就放在它旁边。]尽管发生了这一切，那个木质孵化箱依然摆放在壁炉旁，时刻提醒人们这个地方曾经是多么的简陋。

        而这个地方本身如今已经发展得非常兴旺。有些东西始终没有改变——比如格温似乎仍然非常喜欢那些悬挂式的婴儿床——但其余的内部装饰都已经彻底改变了。主楼的各个区域都用彩色标志进行了划分，为年龄较大的孩子们提供了专门的活动空间：一个铺着柔软地毯的自由玩耍区，以及一个位于厨房附近的用餐区。 [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 12|一个摆放着各种适合儿童使用的乐器的小区域 ]等等诸如此类的事情。 [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 11|在这里，甚至还存在一种为年幼的孩子提供的临时教育形式，这些教育的师资由一些有空闲时间的当地村民担任。除了那些对阅读、写作感兴趣的少数孩子外，似乎并没有太多与这些知识相关的教学活动——考虑到大多数当地人其实并不识字，这也并不奇怪。不过，在这片冰霜之地，教育更多侧重于传授实际的生活技能和生存方法。 ]婴儿们也有自己独立的房间，远离主楼的喧嚣与忙碌。那些网状灯悬挂在他们够不到的地方，散发出温暖的光芒，照亮了整个空间。
        
        整个婴儿室都充满了明亮而鲜艳的色彩，这些温暖的色调与房间墙壁之外那寒冷、无情的世界形成了鲜明的对比。各式各样的手工艺品、粘在一起制成的玩具等等都被挂在墙上，那些色彩鲜艳、充满欢乐的装饰，只有母亲才会喜欢这样的布置。在所有这些装饰物的最显眼位置，挂着一幅粗略绘制的——嗯，严格来说，那更像是一堆乱涂乱画的痕迹——格温的肖像，周围还环绕着红色和粉色的心形图案。这里没有任何文字，但它们也并非必不可少，因为所要表达的意思已然不言而喻。至少站在这个育儿室里片刻，人们就能暂时逃离这个被腐败侵蚀的世界，获得片刻的宁静。
        
        [flags.NURSERY_CONSTRUCTION_TS|在这一切过程中，那三个熟悉的身影仍在被围起来的墙段区域里忙碌着，他们不断地用锤子敲打，忙着完成格温接下来的项目。一些年轻人出于好奇走了过来，但至少他们还算有分寸，没有在那些人工作的时候去打扰他们。]
        
        位于育儿室后面的格温的房间，终于——或许可以说——真正配得上“育儿室主管”这个头衔了。她显然非常重视自然光，房间的墙壁上装着巨大的玻璃窗，同时还配备了厚重的窗帘。在一个角落里，有一张看起来非常舒适的大床；而在另一个角落，则放着一个五斗柜和一件厚重的衣柜。壁炉旁摆放着一把采用传统风格雕刻而成的华丽摇椅，壁炉架上还放着一些显然具有纪念意义的小物件——这些都是她平时喜欢放置的东西。嗯，这些都是她平时不用的工作工具。至少它们被放在一个精美的木盒里，放在人们看不见的地方，这样就不会有孩子不小心碰到它们了。窗台上的花盆里种着一些可用于烹饪的香草植物，它们那小小的白色花朵在微风中轻轻摇曳。
        
        啊，看到幼儿园的发展取得了如此大的成就，确实会让人感到非常满足——而这在很大程度上要归功于你们的努力。
rows.raw:
"
        Gwyn's nursery has certainly come a long way from its humble beginnings as a log cabin in the Frost Hound's backyard. A towering two stories tall, it counts itself amongst the more stately buildings in Hawkethorne — although it still doesn't quite match up to the Frost Hound or Chapel of Velun, it nevertheless stands in its own right as one of the town's landmarks. The old wood building has been replaced with one of solid brick, with plenty of insulation to keep the interior warm against the Frost Marches' chill. The well still sits by the chicken coop, [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 10|although there's no further need for buckets and ropes any more, not with the hand-cranked pump that's been installed.|buckets and rope lying by its side.] Despite all this, the box incubator still sits by the hearth, a reminder of the place's humble beginnings.

        The place itself is doing quite the booming business. Some things never change — Gwyn seems very fond of the hanging cribs herself — but the rest of the interior is completely changed. Various corners of the main building have been marked off with colorful posts for the older children — a free play area floored with furry rugs, a dining hall by the kitchens for mealtimes, [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 12|a small section with various child-friendly musical instruments, ]so on and so forth. [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 11|There's even what might amount to an impromptu school for the very young, staffed by some of the local villagers with a few hours to spare. There doesn't seem to be much in the way of reading, writing and such except for the few youngsters who're interested in such — unsurprising, considering how most of the local populace can't really read — but schooling appears to be more verbal and dedicated to the practical ways of life and survival up here in the Frost Marches. ]Infants themselves have a room of their own, away from the hustle and bustle of the main building, and mesh lamps hang safely out of reach, casting a warm light on the entire scene.
        
        The entire nursery is bright and colorful, painted in warm colors to contrast with the cold, unforgiving world beyond its walls. Various bits of arts and crafts, glued-together toys and the like hang up on the walls, garishly cheerful in the way only a mother could love. At the head of it all is a crudely-drawn — well, for a value of drawn, it honestly looks more like a collection of scribbles — portrait of Gwyn herself, surrounded by red and pink hearts. There aren't any words here, but none are needed to convey what's being said here. Standing in the nursery, for a moment at least, one can gain respite from a world infected by corruption.
        
        [flags.NURSERY_CONSTRUCTION_TS|Through all this, a rather familiar trio of lupines continue work on a roped-off area of wall, hammering and pounding away at whatever Gwyn's next project happens to be. Some of the youngsters wander up to them out of curiosity, but at least have better sense than to actually bother the men while they're at work.]
        
        Gwyn's room in the back of the nursery is finally, just perhaps, something worthy of someone bearing the title of nursery matron. She's clearly got a thing for natural light, huge glass windows adorning the walls, complete with heavy drapes. In one corner, a large, comfortable-looking bed, in the other, a chest of drawers and heavy wardrobe. An ornate rocking chair carved in the traditional lupine style sits by the fireplace, and upon the mantle lie a few knick-knacks of obviously sentimental value, as well as where she puts her... um, tools of the trade when she's not using them. At least they're kept out of sight in an ornate wooden box, lest one of the children accidentally wander in. Flowering herbs for use in cooking adorn the windowsill planters, their little white blossoms swaying in the breeze.
        
        Ah, it definitely gives you a sense of satisfaction to see how far the nursery's gone — and in no small part thanks to your efforts.
        "

You just wanted to see her for a bit, have a chat, maybe get a few matters out of the way. Are you interrupting her? "Oh, of course not. Nothing that can't be picked up again later on, anyway." Her tail's wagging so fast behind her, it's a blur. "Come on, then, let's go talk in my room. The children are out and about, after all." ]

对话

rows.translation: 和格温聊一会儿吧。
轻拍她

rows.original: Gwyn's the kind of girl who likes pats over kisses.
rows.translation: 格温就是那种更喜欢轻拍而不是亲吻的女孩。
rows.raw: "Gwyn's the kind of girl who likes pats over kisses."

rows.translation: 玩得开心！

rows.original: Have a little fun with the nursery matron.
rows.translation: 和托儿所的保育员一起玩得开心一点吧。
rows.raw: "Have a little fun with the nursery matron."

rows.original: You need something to stuff the nursery matron with.
rows.translation: 你需要一些东西来把托儿所的那位保育员填满。
rows.raw: "You need something to stuff the nursery matron with."

rows.translation: 捐款支持

rows.original: The nursery already has all possible upgrades. Congratulations.
rows.translation: 托儿所已经拥有所有可能的升级项目了。恭喜你。
rows.raw: "The nursery already has all possible upgrades. Congratulations."

rows.translation: 捐款支持

rows.original: Make a contribution towards the nursery's upkeep and improvement.
rows.translation: 为托儿所的维护和改善贡献一份力量吧。
rows.raw: "Make a contribution towards the nursery's upkeep and improvement."

rows.original: You might as well wait for construction to be complete before you donate more.
rows.translation: 你不妨等到施工全部完成后再进行进一步的捐赠。
rows.raw: "You might as well wait for construction to be complete before you donate more."

rows.translation: 检查

rows.original: Gwyn is an experienced midwife, maybe she can tell you something about your current condition?
rows.translation: 格温是一位经验丰富的助产士，或许她能告诉你一些关于你目前状况的信息吧？
rows.raw: "Gwyn is an experienced midwife, maybe she can tell you something about your current condition?"

rows.translation: 索尔维格的父亲

rows.original: Ask Gwyn if she knows anything about Solveig's would-be father.
rows.translation: 问问格温，她是否知道关于索尔维格那位潜在父亲的一些信息。
rows.raw: "Ask Gwyn if she knows anything about Solveig's would-be father."

rows.translation: 婴儿床

rows.original: If there's anyone in Hawkethorne that knows anything about proper natal care, it'd be Gwyneth.
rows.translation: 在鹰棘镇，如果有人真正了解如何正确照顾新生儿，那一定是格温妮丝。
rows.raw: "If there's anyone in Hawkethorne that knows anything about proper natal care, it'd be Gwyneth."

rows.translation: 离开

rows.original: "Oh, and by the by, with that last bit, I think we've gathered enough for us to start work on the next thing I have in mind for the nursery." Pray, if she doesn't mind you asking — what does she have in mind? "Now, that's supposed to be a secret. It shouldn't be too hard to guess at, though, or long in coming — I'll have a word with Daddy, and he'll speak to some people he knows. I suppose that's another great thing about Daddy — he knows all sorts of people, and only the best of their kind." Whoa, whoa, is she talking about renovating the nursery, or is she on a daddy-worship spiel? Gwyn smiles. "Can't I do both? Seriously, though, you've my thanks for putting that last drop into the bucket. It's true that others have donated generously as well, but there's always that special something about being the one to hit the mark, isn't there? "Either way, expect to see some changes around here soon!"
rows.translation: “哦，顺便说一下，加上最后那一笔，我想我们已经募集到足够的资金，可以开始着手我接下来为托儿所准备的下一项计划了。” 请问，如果她不介意你发问的话——她心里到底在盘算什么？ “这个本该是个秘密。不过，应该也不会太难猜到，也不会太久就会有结果——我会去跟爸爸说一声，他会去联系他认识的一些人。我想，这也是爸爸的另一个过人之处——他认识各种各样的人，而且都是同行里最优秀的。” 哇哦，哇哦，她是在说要翻修托儿所，还是在吹捧她爸爸呢？ 格温笑了。“难道我不能两者兼顾吗？说真的，我要谢谢你往桶里添了最后一滴水。确实，其他人也都很慷慨地捐了款，但成为那个凑齐目标的人，总有一种特别的感觉，不是吗？” “无论如何，这里很快就会有些变化，你就等着看吧！”

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original: You take a moment to consider what you're about to do and take stock of Gwyn's words on the matter. While donating isn't strictly necessary to keep the nursery running — the fund the baroness set up pays for that — any additions to the place's facilities will have to come out of her pocket, and your contributions will help her in that regard. Of course, donating to the nursery means that you will have that much less spending money, so going overboard with your charity is probably going to mean you running short of funds yourself. So, do you [silly|feel charitable, punk? Do you?|donate?]
rows.translation: 你花了一点时间思考自己即将要做的事情，并仔细回想了一下格温关于这件事的话。虽然捐款并不是维持这个托儿所运转的必要条件——男爵夫人设立的基金已经足以支付相关费用——但任何对托儿所设施的改进都需要她自掏腰包，而你的捐款将在这方面为她提供帮助。 当然，向托儿所捐款也就意味着你能花的钱会少那么多，所以捐款过于慷慨，很可能导致你自己资金短缺。 那么，你打算怎么做呢？ [silly|发发善心吧，小子？你愿意吗？|捐赠吗？]

While donating isn't strictly necessary to keep the nursery running — the fund the baroness set up pays for that — any additions to the place's facilities will have to come out of her pocket, and your contributions will help her in that regard. Of course, donating to the nursery means that you will have that much less spending money, so going overboard with your charity is probably going to mean you running short of funds yourself. So, do you [silly|feel charitable, punk? Do you?|donate?]"

rows.translation: 100枚琥珀金币

rows.original: Digging about in your coin pouch, you grab a fistful of electrum and empty it into Gwyn's cupped hands. The nursery matron gives you a warm, kindly smile, and quickly makes the money disappear into her apron. "Your donation's very much appreciated, [pc.name]. I'll personally make sure this is put to good use. I am accountable for the nursery's finances, after all." Oh, you're just doing your part, especially since she's been so kind to care for the town's children. People strive in their own ways to make the world a better place for the next generation.
rows.translation: 你在钱袋里翻找了一番，抓出一把电银，然后将其倒入格温那双合拢的手中。这位育儿室的负责人向你露出了温暖而亲切的微笑，随后迅速将那些钱收进了她的围裙里。 非常感谢您的捐赠，[pc.name]我会亲自确保这些资源得到妥善利用。我一定会做到这一点。是毕竟，他负责管理托儿所的财务事务。 哦，你只是在尽自己的一份力而已，尤其是考虑到她一直以来都那么热心地照顾镇上的孩子们。每个人都在以自己的方式努力，为下一代创造一个更美好的世界。

rows.original: Donate 100 EC to the nursery's building fund.
rows.translation: 向托儿所的建设基金捐赠100枚琥珀金币。
rows.raw: "Donate 100 EC to the nursery's building fund."

rows.translation: 1,000枚琥珀金币

rows.original: Taking out your coin pouch, you empty a portion of its contents out onto Gwyn's apron. Gwyn looks a little surprised for a moment, but quickly composes herself and rises to give you a little curtsy before moving to collect the proffered sum. "Well! Thank you, [pc.name]. That's indeed quite the sum you've got there." Aw, shucks. You've the means, after all; this is but a small token of your appreciation for all that she's done for everyone. She's holding down the fort here in Hawkethorne, and since you can get the money, it's the least you can do for her.
rows.translation: 你掏出钱袋，将其中的一部分钱倒在了格温的围裙上。格温看起来有那么一瞬间有些惊讶，但很快便恢复了镇定，站起身来向你微微行礼，然后走过来接过你递给她的钱。 嗯！谢谢你们，[pc.name]确实，你拥有的这笔资金数量相当可观。 哎呀，真不好意思。毕竟你有能力这么做；这只不过是表达你对她为所有人所做的一切的感激之情的一种方式而已。她在鹰棘镇这里承担着许多责任，而既然你有钱，这至少是你能为她做的最起码的事情了。

She's holding down the fort here in Hawkethorne, and since you can get the money, it's the least you can do for her."

rows.original: Donate 1,000 EC to the nursery's building fund. How generous!
rows.translation: 向托儿所的建设基金捐赠1,000枚琥珀金币，真是太慷慨了！
rows.raw: "Donate 1,000 EC to the nursery's building fund. How generous!"

rows.translation: 10,000 琥珀金币

rows.original: Gwyn's eyes widen appreciably as you heft your bulging coin pouch — to be honest, it's more of a coin sack at this point — and pour out a hefty proportion of its contents onto the ground. The wolfess makes a few hesitant noises, then swallows hard and points at the pile of shiny metal on the floor. "A-are you sure? That's a lot of money... I'm not sure I can accept this." Oh no, on the other hand she should completely and totally accept this. You may be out there fixing the world, but she's the one making sure there're people suited to living in it. What's a world without people, after all? It takes all sorts to make it, so on and so forth. Yes, Gwyn's doing the world an invaluable service, and as such she should have no compunctions whatsoever about accepting this small mound of money. "Well... um..." Gwyn opens and closes her mouth a few times as if about to say something, then thinks better of it and turns her attention to the coins on the floor. "I suppose I'll have to make a few trips to and from the safe. Mind waiting for me?" Oh, of course. Some minutes later, the heap of coins is gone, and a slightly winded Gwyn pokes her head back into the room. "That's that done with, at any rate. Um... thank you." So it is.
rows.translation: 当你拎起那个鼓鼓的钱袋——说实话，现在它更像是个钱袋子——并将其中很大一部分倒在地上时，格温的眼睛明显睁大了。这只女狼发出几声犹豫的轻响，然后用力咽了口唾沫，指了指地板上那堆闪闪发光的金属。 “你确定吗？那可是一大笔钱……我不太确定自己能否接受。” 哦不，另一方面，她完全应该收下这笔钱。你或许在外头修补这个世界，但真正确保这世上有人适合在其中生活的，是她。毕竟，没有人的世界还叫什么世界？世界本就需要形形色色的人才能组成，如此等等。没错，格温为这个世界做着无价的贡献，所以她完全不必对收下这一小堆钱有任何顾虑。 “嗯……那个……”格温张了张嘴，似乎想说些什么，但最终还是改变了主意，将注意力转向地上的那些硬币。“我想我得往保险箱那儿来回跑几趟。你能等我一下吗？” 哦，当然。几分钟后，那一堆硬币不见了，而气喘吁吁的格温又把头探进了房间。 “不管怎么说，那件事总算是办完了。嗯……谢谢你。” 确实如此。

rows.raw: "Donate 10,000 EC to the nursery's building fund. How magnanimous!"

rows.translation: 返回

rows.original: You give Gwyn a good look-over from head to toe. The first thing that jumps out at you is how warm and homey the lupine girl is — although she's still young, perhaps no more than nineteen, the hard work that comes with living up in the Frost Marches has started to wear down on her youthful beauty and replace it with the harder-edged loveliness that comes as a maiden becomes a young mother. Being Garth's daughter, she's inherited his coloration, and as such a thick dark black overcoat of rougher, coarser hairs covers a dirty white undercoat of softer, fluffier fur. Large blue eyes peer out from behind a broad snout — the latter perhaps coming from her mother — which ends in a soft and broad nose pad. A pair of perky, triangular ears jut through her thick fur and hair, the latter which cumulates in a ruff or mane of sorts that seals the gap between clothing and skin at her neckline. Noticing your gaze roaming over her, Gwyn gives you a small smile. "Why, I believe you're eyeing me, [pc.name]." [pc.isDK|So you are, you reply with a small grin of your own and an arched eyebrow. What's it to her, huh?|Yes, you are, you're not going to deny that.] With that, you unabashedly continue downwards to the rest of her — Gwyn is clothed in a long-sleeved one-piece dress consisting of a blouse and skirt combination. It's sewn together from a mixture of wool and cotton dyed a simple rustic brown, all the better for hiding the spills and stains which are part and parcel of running the nursery. Even the apron she wears over her dress isn't enough to fully protect her from such mishaps, and you notice that she's also wearing a pair of gloves, no doubt to deal with such. The skirts of Gwyn's dress extend all the way down to her calves, done in traditional lupine fashion, and you have to admit they look rather comely as they swish while she walks. Beneath that, a pair of thickly furred boots so common to the cold north protects her feet, more or less completing her attire. Practical but charming at the same time — it's very... her, for lack of a better word to describe it. You have to ask, though. Every time you've seen her, she's always wearing the same thing. Does she... um... Gwyn giggles. "Of course not! It's just that this color really hides the stains and spills that don't wash out. Don't be silly!" Um, okay. "Daddy was a little creeped out when I first got to sew together my own clothing; he said Mommy was always big on uniforms, whatever that means, and that I must've gotten it from her. But that was more than seven years ago now, and he's kind of gotten used to it." Well, time to move on. [gwyn.fucked |Taking a step closer to Gwyn, you sink your fingers into her thick fur and scratch her on the head, taking care to apply a little extra attention to the back of her ears. Seized with a life of its own, Gwyn's tail begins wagging back and forth furiously, and you whisper to her that she's a good doggy and would appreciate it very much if she'd lose her clothes so that you can inspect her better. Gwyn bites her lip, but you give her another ear-scratch and she melts into a puddle of acquiescence. Slowly, she reaches around and undoes the strings holding her apron up, followed by her top and skirts. Each item of clothing is carefully folded and set aside on the bed, Gwyn herself avoiding meeting your eyes throughout the whole process. It's adorable that no matter how many times you've actually done it, how slutty she's feeling at the moment, or the lewdness of the things you've done together, Gwyn is always just a bit self-conscious about showing herself naked, even to you. At last, the wolfess stands in front of you with nothing but her nursing bra, panties and her gloves on. While that has a certain appeal to it of its very own, you did mention that you wanted all of it off, yes? "Mmh. I want you to do it." Oh, well. If you want something done right, you've got to do it yourself. rows.original: If she's got a little time, perhaps she'd like to take a break and have a small talk? It's been a while since the two of you got the chance to hold a proper conversation. Gwyn looks a little unsure at first — no doubt considering her manifold duties — then eventually relents and nods. "Oh, why not. You're always all over the place, [pc.name]; so it's always a special treat when you do drop by. Daddy always used to say that absence makes the heart grow fonder and that familiarity breeds contempt." [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 1 |That said, Gwyn leads you out of her room, through the main hall, and into the kitchens. There's not much going on at this time of day, and the place is empty save for the both of you as she guides you to a kitchen table against the wall and pulls out chairs for the both of you. "Make yourself comfortable," Gwyn says. "There's always some warm tea on, and I'll bring out the cookie jar." The wolfess is good to her word. Before long, two steaming cups of dark brown tea sit before you on the table, the cookies have been served, and the door comfortably latched shut so that the both of you can speak in private. You take one of the cookies, dip it into the mug, and take a bite. Ah, the small pleasures of life. "So," Gwyn says, "what's on your mind?" |Having said her piece, Gwyn pulls up a chair for you and invites you to take a seat. There's a tin of biscuits on one of the side tables, and she moves over to retrieve a kettle of tea from over the small fireplace in the corner before smoothing out her bedsheets and plopping down on her bed. "Not the best in hospitality," she admits, "but it'll have to do until I can scrape together some money to expand the place a little. Anyway, is there something you wanted to discuss?" ]
rows.translation: 如果她有空的话，或许愿意休息一下，聊聊天吧？你们俩已经有一段时间没有机会好好聊一聊了。 起初，格温显得有些犹豫——无疑是在考虑自己繁重的职责——但最终还是同意了，点了点头。“哦，为什么不呢。你总是到处奔波，[pc.name]；所以当你真的顺路来看我时，对我来说总是一件特别开心的事。爸爸以前总说，别离让感情更深，而熟稔则生轻慢。” [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 1 |话虽如此，格温还是带你走出了她的房间，穿过主厅，来到了厨房。这个时候厨房里没什么人，除了你们两个人之外，整个地方都空无一人。她把你引到靠墙的一张厨房桌子旁，然后为你们俩拉出了椅子。 “请随意休息吧，”格温说道。“家里总是备着一些热茶，我会把饼干罐拿出来。” 这位女狼确实言出必行。不久之后，两杯热气腾腾的深棕色茶就被端到了你的面前，饼干也准备好了，门也被轻轻关上，这样你们就可以私下交谈了。你拿了一块饼干，蘸了蘸茶，然后咬了一口。啊，这些生活中的小乐趣啊。 “那么，”格温说道，“你在想什么？” |说完这些，格温拉来一把椅子，请你坐下。旁边的桌子上放着一罐饼干，她走到角落里的小壁炉旁取来一壶茶，然后整理好床单，坐在床上。 “招待方面算不上出色，”她承认道，“不过，在我凑够钱把这地方稍微扩建一下之前，就只能这样凑合了。总之，你有什么想聊的吗？” ]
