rows.original: [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 1 3 4 8 10 12 |[rand|"It's great that we finally scraped together the money to get a proper kitchen built and kitted out. Having a proper kitchen about really makes me feel all warm and good inside," Gwyn says with a wistful sigh. Because she sneaks extra bites of her own cooking? The wolfess fluffs up a little, clearly flustered. "Maybe a bit, to see how it tastes... I wouldn't serve up to someone anything that I wouldn't eat myself." She certainly looks like it. "Hmph!" Gwyn turns up her muzzle and sniffs until you give her a few scratches between her ears. "Well, it's good food. My cooking may not be the fanciest, but it sticks to your bones and that's really what matters up here. Keeps the cold out." |"It's great to finally be able to see some progress on the nursery. Not that we weren't making any before, but people do ask where their donations are going, and it's nice to have something to show people when they start asking inconvenient questions." Do those come often? The inconvenient questions, that is. "Sometimes." Gwyn leans forward and rubs her forehead with her knuckles. "I think it comes from the misconception that the baroness's fund is paying for everything, which isn't the case. Daddy helps me to prepare the accounts of our expenses for the month, and that's exactly how much I get. Any leftover gets rolled into the principal." Um, okay... "Sorry for unloading on you like this," Gwyn says, giving you a small smile. "I'm not sure why I'm spilling all this on you, anyway. Daddy would just see it as a problem to be solved, and Garret is even worse." |"Want a pie sometime? Now that I've the space to keep them out of the children's reach until mealtimes, I'm feeling comfortable with baking a few — you should drop by sometime, and I'll give you a slice or two." She likes pies, does she? Gwyn nods so vigorously that her head's practically a blur. "Eating them is good, but making them is even better. There's something that's very peaceful about rolling out the crust and preparing the filling, then seeing and feeling all that gooey stuff fill the pie up... it makes me so hungry." You can certainly get behind Gwyn's love of pies — in fact, the way she's describing things, you think you'd really enjoy eating her pies. They must be so delicious — what's her favorite filling? "Cream." Gwyn gets an odd, faraway look in her eyes and licks her muzzle, although you don't think the wolfess realizes it herself. "I love cream pies. Especially making them." If she likes them so much, you'd be more than willing to help her make a few cream pies the next time you drop by. Perhaps you could share them; food's always better when it's shared with someone else, isn't it? "Yes, indeed. I'd love that, [pc.name]." ] |[rand|So, how's the nursery holding up? "I think we're looking at putting in some extra floor space — maybe a complete renovation from top to bottom, pulling down a wall or two and seriously expanding the place. With how many children are coming in during the day, I think it's seriously warranted." Whoa, that sounds like a lot of work. Gwyn nods. "It is. I'll try to keep the nursery open anyway, but I'll have to send the children out to play a lot while the construction's going on. Wouldn't want any one of the little ones to suffer an accident. At least the builders Daddy knows are really fast about their work." But when it's done, the payoff in terms of extra room will have been worth it. "Exactly. Which is why I'm hoping that everyone — you included, of course — can get together and make that last little push towards getting the money we need." |How's the nursery's financials holding together? "Decently. I try and be frugal where possible — while the baroness's endowment is generous, I know it's not infinite. Daddy raised me to be able to handle my money." Oh? A small, quizzical smile appears on Gwyn's muzzle. "The Frost Hound wasn't always as prosperous as it is today, [pc.name]. Definitely not when I was a girl. Garret and I went without a few things ourselves so that Daddy could keep the place afloat; not that we had any reason to complain, because Daddy was going without twice that much himself. We complained anyway." Ah, to be seven again and be the center of your little world. Gwyn nods sagely and her smile grows wider, but she says nothing more. |Gwyn shrugs at your question. "Same as always, I suppose. I've managed to corral together enough of the local ladies and worked out proper schedule. Now someone's always responsible for something. Not everyone likes it — they say it reminds them of how my mother did things — but it works." And she doesn't have to be so overworked, does she? A giggle. "Now, when I fall asleep in the clean laundry, it's because I want to, and not because I'm absolutely dog-tired." Dog-tired... that's one way of putting it. And just lying down in a huge pile of clean laundry sounds like one of those things which happens to be really appealing in theory but not so great when you actually get around to doing it. "Aww, don't be a wet blanket. Having a good roll around in the washing is one of the small pleasures of life, like a good cream pie or a warm fire and someone to snuggle against." Behind her, Gwyn's tail starts wagging furiously. "Little things you can be thankful for so the daily grind doesn't wear you down." ] |[rand|You have to wonder — just what are Gwyn's plans for the nursery going forward? "Oh, I've got plenty of things I want to do with the place, help keep the children happy while they're here for the day," Gwyn replies. "Now that I've dealt with getting the basics together, it's time to see if I can't add a few bells and whistles." What sort of things does she have in mind? Gwyn grins, then sticks out her tongue at you. "That's for me to know and for you to find out. Don't worry, any money you give will be going towards a good cause. Have you ever known me to splurge on trivialities?" No, but you'd still like to know nevertheless. "Well, all I'll say is that we're going to be focusing on quality as opposed to quantity. I want to create a pleasant environment that's conducive to the children's learning, playing and working." |"I've got together a few of the townspeople and seen if we can't put the children to some simple jobs." Whatever does she mean? "Exactly what I meant. [pc.name], you may be absent most of the time, so your children are a special case, but most of the little ones here only come to the nursery sporadically, you know. They've chores and work their parents set for them on their own time." Well yes, this is a frontier town, after all. But how does this tie in with... well, whatever she said? "Then let me finish, please. What I'm getting together is an effort to teach the children the value of a good work ethic, build some character, and hopefully test their aptitude for a variety of jobs in the process." Hmm, might be interesting, but you probably aren't too interested in the details. "Suit yourself." |"What do you think of what I've done with the place? The world outside is so dreary and gray all the time — I've tried to liven things up a little by painting the walls with warm colors, and the children are being dears at making little crafts to put up." There's plenty of color to be had, that's for sure. It's very vibrant — reminds you of late spring, to be honest. "That's what I was going for, yes." Gwyn sighs happily. "We've certainly come a long way since the one-room cabin that the nursery started out as, haven't we? It's like... hm, well, my own little paradise, and I've got to thank you for putting in this much money, even if you aren't able to give very much of your time." Oh, no worries. You're happy to help out however you can. "There's always more that can be done, but for now at least there's not as much of a pressing need for donations any more. The difference between needs and wants, as Daddy would say." Well, you hope she won't stop working as hard as she did on her first day on the job. Gwyn laughs and wags her tail. "Don't you worry about that." |So, what's Gwyn looking at next when it comes to making this place bigger and better? Is she going to put in a second floor to the nursery? Gwyn looks thoughtful a moment and rubs her chin. "You know, that's not such a bad idea — it's something that I'd indeed like to eventually do someday. But not immediately." You nod. After all, bigger isn't always better — and you can see that costing a lot of money. "Oh, of course. But it's always good to have a goal to work towards in life. Like having lots and lots of puppies." |"I won't deny it — it's nice to have people know who you are. Even if it's just 'the lady who runs the nursery', it's a bit of local fame for being useful to other people." A small smile spreads out on Gwyn's muzzle, and she sighs happily. "You know, when I'm going out to market and people are pointing at me and saying 'that's her' — in a good way, of course. It makes me feel all warm and fuzzy inside." Like they do with Garth? "Yep! Just between you and me, while I really love Daddy and all, it was kind of tiring having everyone know me just as his girl. I know people didn't mean it, but it always felt to me that Garret and I were always in his shadow." Well, that's just one of the hazards of growing up with a local hero for a parent. "Mm. I know I shouldn't complain — there are far worse circumstances to grow up in — but all things strive, don't they? Well, at least I'm 'the nursery lady' now, and Garret's still daddy's boy." Better not press him too hard — who knows what lengths her brother might go to in order to prove himself. Gwyn laughs at that. "Oh, don't worry, [pc.name]. Garret might be a hothead, but he's not stupid. He's going to show off a bit at most — I'm not going to lose any sleep over him biting off more than he can chew." ] |[rand|"You know how we have a well out back?" Yes, you've seen it. It's got to be pretty deep to get to a clean water table, isn't it? "Kinda sorta. Most people in Hawkethorne pay to have their trash dumped in the pit couple miles out of town, but that isn't the point. The point is that some weeks back, there was this catfolk passing through town, looked like he was from the heartlands — anyway, what he was trying to convince Daddy to buy was this contraption. You fix it to a pipe, turn the crank, and then it sucks up water from whatever well you like, so long as it's not more than a hundred feet deep." That sounds like quite the feat of engineering — and too good to be true. "Yep. Daddy was about to tell him to get out of the Frost Hound, but the guy and River had a talk, and River thinks the guy's not kidding." Now that's interesting. Gwyn nods. "That's how Daddy works. He may not know you, but he chooses his friends carefully. If you're a friend of his friend, then you're all right with him. Anyways, Daddy was quite interested in the screw pump, as it was called, since it could serve both the Frost Hound and the nursery, but we don't have that kind of spending money at the moment." You can imagine that such a piece of work would involve some money again, yes... "So long as you're wise about it, it's hard to have too much money on you," Gwyn replies with a grin. |"I've got to thank you for putting in so much money towards making my dream a success, [pc.name]," Gwyn tells you. "Sure, you may not be the only one who donated, but you're definitely one of my biggest contributors." Hey, you've access to the kind of money that most people in Hawkethorne can only dream of. Going out into the wilderness and doing crazy stuff is dangerous, but it also brings with it its rewards. Besides, it's always nice to see another two-storey building in town. "Yes, but thank you nevertheless. It's very heart-warming to know that the main figures in and about Hawkethorne understand the importance of investing in the next generation." ] |[rand|"It's been going very well, thank you." Gwyn replies with a dip of her head. "To be honest, I'm starting to run out of ideas as to how we can improve the nursery." Which means she hasn't actually run out of ideas yet, has she? "Of course not. We've got the space, we've got the environment — all I really want to do now is to try and bring out the children's talents. Sure, there aren't that many people who would be gifted in, say, music, but it would be a shame to not try and discover what each and every one of them is best at. Even if it's something completely mundane like fishing or weaving." She seems rather empathic on this point. Does she have a personal stake in this? Gwyn sighs. "Daddy was a soldier in his time, and although I never really knew her, I hear that Mommy was, too. Garret, he took more after the both of them than I did, but what everyone in town did was to simply assume that since I was Daddy's daughter, what I wanted to do was to take up arms like he did. "Daddy wanted to teach me and I learned anyway, even if I wasn't so keen about it. Part of me wanted desperately to please Daddy, and the other part grudgingly admitted that it was better to have the skill and not use it, rather than not have the skill and need it. Well, you can see how that turned out." Ah. "Daddy says that my figure takes after Mommy's, but the way I'm putting that to use is quite different, I'd say." The wolfess pats her wide hips for emphasis. "And not only am I not having any regrets, but I couldn't be happier doing what I do, other people aside." |The nursery is pretty big now, isn't it? "And getting a little popular, if I dare say so myself," Gwyn adds. "We're not quite full yet, but we're certainly getting there. Folks who want a day to themselves just leave their kids with us in the morning and pick them up in the evening." Must be plenty of those around. "Everyone needs a small break every now and then, even the likes of me. Sure, my work may never be done, but that doesn't mean I can't enjoy a nice cup of tea." Which is why she's sitting down with you and chatting instead of actually working, eh? Gwyn giggles. "Exactly." |"You may not have noticed it, but we're using some of the donation money to spruce up some of the older places. Just because the kitchen was the first things to be built doesn't mean we look to improving it — we just put in another oven not too long ago, and some extra shelves for the pantry." It's good that she's looking back and not neglecting what's already been built. Does the nursery take much upkeep? Gwyn laughs, her heavy bosom shaking under her dress with the sheer force of her yipping laughter. "Oh, [pc.name], you would not imagine how quickly things get worn down when you've to clean them two or three times a day. But yes, quite a bit goes towards upkeep. While the baroness's fund's grown somewhat, I don't want to dip into the principal at all, and scrimp a little on the earnings." Which means asking for more donations? "No, no, [pc.name], I'm not asking you for money. We've already got plenty of stuff. Just... do as you've always been doing, and we'll get along fine." ] |[rand|"We're holding up just fine, thank you very much. More than fine, in fact — I'm forced to admit that there isn't anything that I can think of adding to the nursery that I could reasonably get, or that would be in character for Hawkethorne. I think this place is as big as it needs to be for a village this size." Hey, it's changed a lot. You still remember how the small, dingy place this used to be... and come to think of it, she's changed a lot, too. "I'm not going to deny that," Gwyn replies with a giggle. "The change's been for the better, after all." So, what does she intend now? Keep on keeping on, as the saying goes? A happy nod. "I'm not going to need any more money to pay for improvements to the nursery, but it certainly would be nice to have to help defray the daily expenses. You can imagine that keeping this place in shape is quite the task." It is, in its own right, a hero's task. Her own work is as important as her mother's was — probably even more. Taking life is easy — helping to shape lives into useful, well-lived ones is much harder. Gwyn says nothing and keeps a remarkably straight face as she sips her tea, but the furious wagging of the wolfess' tail betrays her emotions. |"I really couldn't be happier. The nursery is everything I've dreamed of — and then a little more. I've got so many people to thank for helping to make it come true — amongst them being the baroness, for giving me the seed money to get it started, and you, of course, for... well, all you've done." Hey, she had a plan, had a clear route to get from point A to B, and stuck to it. Now it's paid off, she has every right to savor the fruits of her labors. Gwyn makes a happy noise in the back of her throat. "Yes, but it's not as if I did it alone. It makes me happy that almost everyone in Hawkethorne has come together to make this a success." It just goes to show what even a small community can do when enough people get drawn together to a common cause, doesn't it? "Yes, yes, it does." ] |[rand|"It's a bit of trouble having to run back into the Frost Hound to do the cooking," Gwyn admits. "One of the first things I want to spend money on here is to get a proper kitchen up and running so Daddy and I don't get in each other's way." That does sound reasonable, yes. You can't help but feel a little underwhelmed that the baroness wouldn't even give Gwyn a kitchen to get started with, but you suppose she's supposed to work her way out of the very bottom. Builds character and all that. "It's to push me to work harder, I guess." Gwyn gathers up her tail in her hands and tries to look cheerful, but you can't help but notice her usually perky ears laid flat against her head. Well, you'll be behind her one hundred and one percent, okay? "That's very much appreciated, thank you." |"What do I think of the place? Well, maybe I could ask you the same question — what do you think of the place?" It's... a bit small. But it has character, and more importantly, potential. Gwyn cocks an ear at you. "That's very... um, nice. What sort of character would you say the nursery has, in that case?" Her sort of character. Gwyn's character is so large it spills out of her and all over the place like a mug running over. It's rather pleasant, to be honest. "Flatterer." You only aim to please. |Gwyn considers the question for a few seconds, sighs, and rubs her face. "I suppose I wish there was a little more room around here. Not that I haven't tried to make the most of what I've got, but you can water down soup only so much before it becomes just water." That's one way of putting things. Is there any way you can help? "Daddy knows people who do good work — they did put this place together, after all — but they don't work for free." Ah. Gwyn smiles. "Not that I'm asking you for money or anything, [pc.name], but... well, gods. I am asking you for money. And not just you, pretty much everyone in Hawkethorne. I've asked Sanders to see if he can't pass around some kind of collection plate for people who go to the chapel." Well, you'll see what you can do when you have a bit of spare money on hand. ] ]
rows.translation: [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 1 3 4 8 10 12 |[rand|我们终于凑够了钱，建了一个设备齐全的厨房，这真是太好了。拥有一个像样的厨房，真的让我感到无比温暖和满足。格温叹息着说道。 “就因为她会偷偷多吃自己做的食物吗？” 那只母狼微微耸了耸毛，显然有些慌乱。也许会尝一点，看看味道如何……我绝对不会把我自己都不会吃的东西端给别人。 她当然可以。看起来喜欢。 哼！格温会抬起鼻子嗅来嗅去，直到你轻轻挠她的耳朵几下。嗯，这食物确实不错。我的烹饪手法可能不算最精致，但食物能让人暖和起来，这才是最重要的。能抵御寒冷，这才是真正的美味。 |终于能看到托儿所的建设取得了一些进展，这真是太好了。其实我们之前也在不断努力，但人们确实会询问他们的捐款用在了哪里，现在能够有一些具体的成果展示出来，确实让人感到欣慰。展示当人们开始问一些棘手的问题时。 这种尴尬的问题，是不是经常会出现呢？ 有时候。格温向前倾了倾身子，用指关节揉了揉自己的额头。我认为，这种误解源于人们认为是女男爵的基金在为这些费用买单。一切事实并非如此。爸爸会帮我整理我们这个月的开销明细，而我的收入恰恰就是这些数字。如果还有剩余，就会被计入本金中。 嗯，好吧…… 很抱歉这样把情绪发泄在你身上。格温微笑着说道。其实我也不明白为什么要把这些事情都告诉你。爸爸只会把它们看作是需要解决的问题，而加雷特的情况就更糟了。 |有空想尝尝我做的派吗？现在我有足够的空间把它们放在孩子们够不到的地方，等到吃饭时间再拿出来，所以我很有心情烤几份。你什么时候有空来一趟吧，我会给你切一两片尝尝的。 她喜欢派，对吧？ 格温用力地点了点头，以至于她的头都快看不清了。吃它们固然很好，但自己动手制作就更好了。当把面皮擀开、准备好馅料，然后看着那些黏稠的馅料慢慢填满整个派饼……这种感觉真的非常让人平静、安心，真的让我感到非常满足。饥饿。" 你完全能够理解格温对派饼的喜爱——事实上，从她描述这些派饼的方式来看，你真的会想要尝一尝她做的派饼。那些派饼一定非常美味吧？她最喜欢的馅料是什么呢？ 奶油。格温的眼神中浮现出一种奇怪的、恍惚的神情，她舔了舔自己的嘴部，不过你不会认为这只母狼自己意识到了这一点。我喜欢奶油派，尤其是制作它们的过程。 如果她这么喜欢它们，下次你再去的时候，肯定很乐意帮她做一些奶油派。或许你们可以一起分享；食物与他人分享后，总是会变得更加美味，不是吗？ 是的，当然。我非常愿意这样做。[pc.name]。" ] |[rand|那么，托儿所的情况怎么样呢？ 我认为我们需要增加一些空间——或许需要进行一次彻底的翻新，拆掉一两面墙，从而真正扩大这个地方的面积。考虑到白天会有那么多孩子来这里，我觉得这是非常必要的。 哇，听起来真是件很繁琐的工作啊。 格温点了点头。是的。我会尽量让儿童房保持开放状态，但在施工期间，我不得不让孩子们到外面去玩。我可不想让任何一个小孩子发生意外。至少，爸爸认识的那些建筑工人工作速度确实很快。 但当这一切完成之后，所获得的额外空间所带来的好处绝对值得这个努力。 正是这样。因此，我希望所有人——当然也包括你——能够齐心协力，共同努力，争取到我们所需要的资金。 |幼儿园的财务状况目前怎么样？ 还算不错。我会尽量节省开支——虽然女男爵给的钱很丰厚，但我知道这笔钱并不是无穷无尽的。爸爸教导我，要懂得如何合理管理自己的钱财。 哦？ 格温的嘴角浮现出一丝疑惑而略带笑意的表情。冰寒霜猎犬并非一直以来都像现在这样繁荣昌盛。[pc.name]当我还是个女孩的时候，绝对不会这样。加雷特和我自己也会舍弃一些东西，这样爸爸才能维持家庭的生计；其实我们并没有理由抱怨，因为爸爸自己也在牺牲更多的东西。不过，我们还是抱怨了。 啊，如果能再次回到七岁，成为自己小世界的中心该多好。 格温若有所思地点了点头，她的笑容变得更加灿烂，但除此之外，她没有再说什么。 |格温对你提出的问题耸了耸肩。我想，还是一如既往吧。我终于召集到了足够的当地女性，制定了合理的安排。现在总是有人负责具体的事务。并不是所有人都喜欢这种方式——他们说这让他们想起了我母亲以前的做事方式——但这种方法确实有效。 她也没必要工作得这么拼命，对吧？ 一阵轻笑。现在，当我躺在干净的衣服上入睡时，是因为我想要这样做，而不是因为我已经累得筋疲力尽。 累坏了……也可以这么说吧。而躺在那一大堆干净的衣物旁边，听起来在理论上确实是一件很诱人的事情，但实际上去做的时候，却并没有那么美好。 哎呀，别扫大家的兴吧。在洗衣机里尽情翻滚玩耍，其实是生活中那些小小的乐趣之一，就比如品尝美味的奶油派，或是享受温暖的炉火，还有可以依偎在一起的人。在她身后，格温的尾巴开始疯狂地摇动起来。一些值得你心怀感激的小事，这样日常的琐事就不会让你感到疲惫不堪。 ] |[rand|你不禁会想——格温对于这个育儿室未来究竟有什么计划呢？ 哦，我有很多计划想要在这个地方实施，比如在孩子们在这里度过一天期间，帮助他们保持开心。格温回答道。现在我已经把基础工作都做好了，是时候看看能否再添加一些额外的功能了。 她到底在想些什么呢？ 格温咧嘴一笑，然后朝你吐了吐舌头。这只有我和你才知道。别担心，你给的任何钱都会用于公益事业。你难道见过我在琐事上浪费钱吗？ 不，但你还是想知道的。 嗯，我只想说，我们会更加注重质量而非数量。我想要营造一个让孩子们能够愉快地学习、玩耍和学习的良好环境。 |我召集了一些镇上的居民，看看是否能让孩子们做一些简单的活计。 她到底是什么意思？ 正是我想要表达的意思。[pc.name]，你可能大部分时间都不在，所以你的孩子是个特例，但这里的大多数小孩子其实都是偶尔才会来幼儿园的。你知道的，他们都有自己的家务活，也要在父母安排的时间里完成这些任务。 嗯，毕竟这确实是一个边疆小镇。但这一切与她刚才说的那些话，究竟有什么关联呢？ 那么，请允许我把话讲完。我的目的是教导孩子们良好的职业道德的重要性，帮助他们培养一些品格，并且希望通过这个过程来测试他们是否适合从事各种不同的工作。 嗯，可能会挺有意思的，但你们可能对具体细节并不太感兴趣吧。 随你便吧。 |你觉得我对这个地方所做的这些改动怎么样？外面的世界总是那么阴沉灰暗——我试着用温暖的色彩来装饰墙壁，让这里看起来更生动一些，而孩子们也都很乖，还制作了一些小装饰品来点缀这里。 确实，这里有丰富的色彩，非常鲜艳——说实话，让人联想到晚春的季节。 没错，我正是想要达到这样的效果。格温开心地叹了口气。从最初那个只有一个房间的小木屋开始，我们确实已经走了很长一段路，不是吗？这里简直就像……嗯，我的一个小天堂。我必须感谢你投入了这么多资金，尽管你并没有投入太多时间。 哦，别担心。你愿意尽自己所能提供帮助，这就已经很好了。 总是还有更多事情可以去做，但至少目前来说，已经没有那么迫切地需要捐款了。用爸爸的话来说，这就是‘需求’与‘欲望’之间的区别。 嗯，但愿她不会像入职第一天那样继续拼命工作了。 格温笑着，摇着尾巴。你难道不担心吗？那个。" |那么，接下来格温打算如何让这个地方变得更大、更好呢？她是不是打算在婴儿房上加建一层楼呢？ 格温若有所思地沉吟了一会儿，然后揉了揉下巴。你知道，这个主意其实并不坏——我确实希望有朝一日能去做这件事。不过现在还不是时候。 你点了点头。毕竟，越大并不一定越好——而且你可以看到，这确实需要花费大量的资金。 哦，当然。不过，在生活中设定一个奋斗目标总是好事。就像想要拥有很多很多小狗一样。 |我不得不承认，让别人知道你是谁，这种感觉确实很好。哪怕别人只是称你为‘那个负责照看托儿所的女士’，但能够为别人提供帮助，这也算是一种在当地获得的小名声吧。格温的嘴角浮现出一丝微笑，她开心地叹了口气。你知道吗，每当我去参加市场活动，人们指着我说‘那就是她’——当然，都是以赞美的方式。这种感觉真的让我心里暖暖的，非常愉快。 就像他们对加斯所做的那样吗？ 没错！就咱们俩之间说吧，虽然我真的很喜欢爸爸，但是让大家都把我看作他的女儿，其实还挺让人疲惫的。我知道大家并没有恶意，但在我看来，加雷特和我似乎总是处于他的阴影之下。 嗯，这就是那些父母是当地英雄的孩子在成长过程中会遇到的种种麻烦之一吧。 嗯，我知道自己不该抱怨——毕竟还有比这更糟糕的成长环境——但万物都是在不断变化的，对吧？至少现在我成了‘保姆’，而加雷特依然还是他爸爸的宝贝儿子。 最好别逼他太紧——谁知道她哥哥会为了证明自己而做出什么事情来呢。 格温听到这话笑了起来。哦，别担心，[pc.name]加雷特虽然有时候会冲动行事，但他其实并不是这样的。愚蠢的他顶多也就是想炫耀一下而已——他要是想做力所不能及的事情，我也不会为此失眠的。 ] |[rand|你知道我们后院有个大院子吧？ 没错，你肯定也注意到了。要找到一片清澈的地下水源，水源肯定得位于相当深的地方，对吧？ 算是吧。在鹰棘镇，大多数人都愿意花钱把垃圾送到几英里外镇外的垃圾坑里处理，但重点不在于这个。重点是，几周前有只猫族路过这个小镇，看起来像是来自内陆地区——总之，他试图说服镇长购买这个装置。只要把这个装置安装在管道上，然后转动曲柄，它就能从任何深度不超过一百英尺的井里抽取水来。 这听起来确实是一项了不起的工程壮举——好得让人难以置信。 没错。爸爸本来打算让他离开那辆‘霜犬酒馆’，但那人和瑞弗聊了之后，瑞弗觉得他是认真的。 现在那个真有意思。” 格温点了点头。爸爸就是这样的。他可能不认识你，但他会选择自己的朋友。如果你是他朋友的朋友，那么他就会接受你。总之，爸爸对那种被称为‘螺旋泵’的设备很感兴趣，因为它既可以用来满足‘霜犬酒馆’的需求，也可以用在苗圃里，不过我们现在确实没有那么多钱来购买它。 你可以想象，这样的项目当然也需要投入一些资金，没错…… 只要你明智地使用这笔钱，拥有太多的钱其实也没什么坏处。格温笑着回答道。 |我必须感谢你为实现我的梦想投入了如此多的资金，真的非常感谢你。[pc.name]，”格温会告诉你的。当然，可能不止你一个人进行了捐赠，但你绝对是我最重要的捐赠者之一。 嘿，你拥有的财富是鹰棘镇大多数人都只能梦寐以求的。走进荒野去做那些冒险的事情确实很危险，但同时也会有相应的回报。而且，每当镇上又多出一座两层楼的建筑时，总是让人感到很高兴的。 是的，但还是要感谢你。知道鹰棘镇的那些重要人物都明白投资下一代人才的重要性，这真的让人感到温暖。 ] |[rand|进展得非常顺利，谢谢。格温轻轻点了点头作为回应。说实话，我实在想不出还有什么办法可以改进这个托儿所了。 这意味着她还没有。其实她还没想出新的点子吧？ 当然不是。我们既有场地，也有相应的环境——我现在真正想做的，就是努力发掘孩子们的天赋。当然，并不是每个人都在音乐等方面有天赋，但如果不尝试去发现每个人最擅长的领域，那就太可惜了。哪怕是像钓鱼或者编织这样看似平凡的活动，也同样值得去探索。 在这一点上，她似乎表现得相当有同理心。她本人是否也与此事有关呢？ 格温叹了口气。我爸爸在他那个年代是一名军人，虽然我并不真正了解妈妈的情况，但我听说妈妈也是。加雷特，他更像他们两个人，而不是像我。不过镇上的所有人都认为，既然我是我爸爸的女儿，那我肯定也会像他一样拿起武器去打仗。 爸爸想教我，而我最终还是学会了，尽管我一开始并不是很感兴趣。我内心有一部分非常渴望让爸爸开心，而另一部分则不情愿地承认：拥有这项技能却不用它，总比没有这项技能却需要它要好。嗯，你们应该能理解我的意思吧那个结果证明是这样。 啊。 爸爸说我的身材是随妈妈来的，不过我的体型呈现方式有点不同那个我认为，使用方法其实是完全不同的。那只母狼拍了拍自己宽大的臀部，以强调这一动作。我不仅没有任何后悔，而且除了别人之外，我对自己现在所做的事情感到无比开心。 |现在这个育儿室已经变得相当大了，不是吗？ 可以说，我也因此有了一点名气。格温补充道。我们还没有完全满员，但已经快到那个程度了。那些想要自己单独一天的时间的人，可以在早上把孩子交给我们，晚上再来接走。 这种东西肯定有很多吧。 每个人偶尔都需要休息一下，就连我这样的也不例外。当然，我的工作可能永远都做不完，但这并不意味着我就不能享受一杯美味的茶。 这就是为什么她现在坐在你旁边聊天，而不是真正去工作的原因，对吧？ 格温轻声笑了起来。正是如此。 |你可能没有注意到，但我们确实用了一部分捐赠资金来改善一些老旧的区域。虽然厨房是最早建好的设施，但我们依然一直在努力对其进行改进——不久前我们又添置了一台新烤箱，还为食品储藏室加装了一些新的架子。 她能够回顾过去，并且没有忽视已经取得的成果，这真是太好了。那个育儿室需要花费很多精力去维护吗？ 格温笑了起来，她那厚实的胸脯随着她爽朗的笑声而剧烈地晃动。哦，[pc.name]，你会的不是想象一下，如果每天都需要清洗这些东西两三次，它们会多快被磨损掉。确实，维护这些物品需要花费不少精力。虽然女男爵的基金有所增加，但我根本不想动用本金，因此只能尽量节省一些收入来用于维护了。 这意味着需要更多的捐款吗？ 不，不，[pc.name]，我不是在向你要钱。我们已经有很多东西了。只是……请你像以前一样去做，我们就不会有问题了。 ] |[rand|我们目前的情况非常好，非常感谢。事实上，甚至可以说非常好——我不得不承认，对于鹰棘镇这个村庄来说，我想不出还有什么可以添加到这个托儿所里，而且这些东西也是我们能够合理获得的，或者与鹰棘镇的风格相符的。我认为，对于这样一个规模的村庄来说，这个托儿所已经足够大了。 嘿，这里变化可真大啊。你还记得这个地方以前是多么破旧、昏暗吗……仔细想想，真是让人感慨万千。她是也发生了很多变化。 我并不想否认这一点。格温笑着回答道。毕竟，这种改变是朝着更好的方向发展的。 那么，她现在究竟有什么打算呢？就像俗话说的那样，继续前进吧？ 非常赞同。我不会去的。需要没有更多的钱来用于托儿所的改造了，但当然，如果有可能的话，还是应该这么做的。不错不得不帮忙承担这些日常开销。你可以想象，维持这个地方的正常运转确实是一项相当艰巨的任务。 这本身就是一项英雄该做的事。她所做的工作与她母亲的工作一样重要——甚至可能更为重要。夺走生命很容易，但帮助人们将生命塑造成有意义、充实的人生，却要困难得多。 格温一言不发，只是面无表情地喝着茶，但那只母狼剧烈摇动的尾巴却暴露了她的情绪。 |我真的再开心不过了。这个托儿所正是我梦寐以求的——甚至还要更好。有很多人帮助我实现了这个梦想，其中当然包括女男爵，她给了我启动这项事业所需的资金；当然，也离不开你，因为……嗯，你为这一切所做的贡献实在太多了。 嘿，她有一个计划，明确地知道如何从A点到达B点，而且她也坚决按照这个计划行事。现在，她的努力终于得到了回报，她完全有权利享受自己辛勤工作的成果。 格温在喉咙深处发出了一声开心的声音。是的，但这并不是我一个人完成的。让我感到高兴的是，鹰棘镇的几乎所有人都齐心协力，共同让这件事取得了成功。 这恰恰说明了，当足够多的人为了共同的目标团结起来时，即使是一个小团体也能做出令人瞩目的成就，不是吗？ 是的，确实如此。 ] |[rand|不得不跑回寒霜猎犬那里去做饭，确实有点麻烦。格温承认了。在这里，我首先想花钱做的事情就是打造一个功能齐全的厨房，这样我和爸爸就不会互相打扰了。 确实，这听起来挺合理的。不过，女男爵甚至都不给格温提供一个厨房让她开始着手做事，这确实会让人感到有些失望。不过，你也可以理解，她总得从最基础的地方开始做起吧，这样才能逐渐成长起来，对吧？这也算是塑造人物性格的一种方式嘛。 我想，这是为了激励我更加努力工作吧。格温双手把尾巴夹在身下，努力装出一副开心的样子，但你还是能注意到，她平时总是竖得高高的耳朵此刻却平贴在脑袋上。 好吧，你绝对会完全支持她的，对吧？ 非常感谢，真的谢谢您。 |我对这个地方有什么看法呢？嗯，也许我可以反过来问你同样的问题——你认为这个地方怎么样？你还记得那个地方吗？ 它……有点小。但它有特色，更重要的是，它有潜力。 格温侧耳倾听着你的话。那真是……嗯，很不错。那么，你认为这个育婴室适合培养什么样的性格呢？ 她的这种性格特点。格温的性格如此鲜明，简直仿佛要从她体内溢出来，四处流淌，就像一个杯子里的液体溢了出来一样。说实话，这种性格还挺让人喜欢的。 马屁精。 你的唯一目标就是取悦他人。 |格温思考了这个问题几秒钟，然后叹了口气，揉了揉脸。我想，要是这里的空间能再大一些该多好。其实我也一直在尽力利用现有的空间，但汤再稀释也是有限度的，超过这个限度就只剩下水而已了。 这么说也有道理。你有没有办法能帮上忙呢？ 爸爸认识一些做事很认真的人——毕竟正是他们把这个地方建了起来——但他们不会无偿工作。 啊。 格温笑了。并不是说我在向你要钱或什么别的东西，[pc.name]，但是……天啊，我真的无语了。是他们在向大家借钱。不只是你，几乎鹰棘镇的每个人都在被他们借钱。我已经让桑德斯去看看，是否可以为大家准备一个募捐盘，让那些去教堂的人能够捐款。 嗯，等你手头有了一些闲钱，你就会知道自己能做些什么了。 ] ]
rows.raw: " [flags.NURSERY_UPGRADES 1 3 4 8 10 12 |[rand|"It's great that we finally scraped together the money to get a proper kitchen built and kitted out. Having a proper kitchen about really makes me feel all warm and good inside," Gwyn says with a wistful sigh. Because she sneaks extra bites of her own cooking? The wolfess fluffs up a little, clearly flustered. "Maybe a bit, to see how it tastes... I wouldn't serve up to someone anything that I wouldn't eat myself." She certainly looks like it. "Hmph!" Gwyn turns up her muzzle and sniffs until you give her a few scratches between her ears. "Well, it's good food. My cooking may not be the fanciest, but it sticks to your bones and that's really what matters up here. Keeps the cold out." |"It's great to finally be able to see some progress on the nursery. Not that we weren't making any before, but people do ask where their donations are going, and it's nice to have something to show people when they start asking inconvenient questions." Do those come often? The inconvenient questions, that is. "Sometimes." Gwyn leans forward and rubs her forehead with her knuckles. "I think it comes from the misconception that the baroness's fund is paying for everything, which isn't the case. Daddy helps me to prepare the accounts of our expenses for the month, and that's exactly how much I get. Any leftover gets rolled into the principal." Um, okay... "Sorry for unloading on you like this," Gwyn says, giving you a small smile. "I'm not sure why I'm spilling all this on you, anyway. Daddy would just see it as a problem to be solved, and Garret is even worse." |"Want a pie sometime? Now that I've the space to keep them out of the children's reach until mealtimes, I'm feeling comfortable with baking a few — you should drop by sometime, and I'll give you a slice or two." She likes pies, does she? Gwyn nods so vigorously that her head's practically a blur. "Eating them is good, but making them is even better. There's something that's very peaceful about rolling out the crust and preparing the filling, then seeing and feeling all that gooey stuff fill the pie up... it makes me so hungry." You can certainly get behind Gwyn's love of pies — in fact, the way she's describing things, you think you'd really enjoy eating her pies. They must be so delicious — what's her favorite filling? "Cream." Gwyn gets an odd, faraway look in her eyes and licks her muzzle, although you don't think the wolfess realizes it herself. "I love cream pies. Especially making them." If she likes them so much, you'd be more than willing to help her make a few cream pies the next time you drop by. Perhaps you could share them; food's always better when it's shared with someone else, isn't it? "Yes, indeed. I'd love that, [pc.name]." ] |[rand|So, how's the nursery holding up? "I think we're looking at putting in some extra floor space — maybe a complete renovation from top to bottom, pulling down a wall or two and seriously expanding the place. With how many children are coming in during the day, I think it's seriously warranted." Whoa, that sounds like a lot of work. Gwyn nods. "It is. I'll try to keep the nursery open anyway, but I'll have to send the children out to play a lot while the construction's going on. Wouldn't want any one of the little ones to suffer an accident. At least the builders Daddy knows are really fast about their work." But when it's done, the payoff in terms of extra room will have been worth it. "Exactly. Which is why I'm hoping that everyone — you included, of course — can get together and make that last little push towards getting the money we need." |How's the nursery's financials holding together? "Decently. I try and be frugal where possible — while the baroness's endowment is generous, I know it's not infinite. Daddy raised me to be able to handle my money." Oh? A small, quizzical smile appears on Gwyn's muzzle. "The Frost Hound wasn't always as prosperous as it is today, [pc.name]. Definitely not when I was a girl. Garret and I went without a few things ourselves so that Daddy could keep the place afloat; not that we had any reason to complain, because Daddy was going without twice that much himself. We complained anyway." Ah, to be seven again and be the center of your little world. Gwyn nods sagely and her smile grows wider, but she says nothing more. |Gwyn shrugs at your question. "Same as always, I suppose. I've managed to corral together enough of the local ladies and worked out proper schedule. Now someone's always responsible for something. Not everyone likes it — they say it reminds them of how my mother did things — but it works." And she doesn't have to be so overworked, does she? A giggle. "Now, when I fall asleep in the clean laundry, it's because I want to, and not because I'm absolutely dog-tired." Dog-tired... that's one way of putting it. And just lying down in a huge pile of clean laundry sounds like one of those things which happens to be really appealing in theory but not so great when you actually get around to doing it. "Aww, don't be a wet blanket. Having a good roll around in the washing is one of the small pleasures of life, like a good cream pie or a warm fire and someone to snuggle against." Behind her, Gwyn's tail starts wagging furiously. "Little things you can be thankful for so the daily grind doesn't wear you down." ] |[rand|You have to wonder — just what are Gwyn's plans for the nursery going forward? "Oh, I've got plenty of things I want to do with the place, help keep the children happy while they're here for the day," Gwyn replies. "Now that I've dealt with getting the basics together, it's time to see if I can't add a few bells and whistles." What sort of things does she have in mind? Gwyn grins, then sticks out her tongue at you. "That's for me to know and for you to find out. Don't worry, any money you give will be going towards a good cause. Have you ever known me to splurge on trivialities?" No, but you'd still like to know nevertheless. "Well, all I'll say is that we're going to be focusing on quality as opposed to quantity. I want to create a pleasant environment that's conducive to the children's learning, playing and working." |"I've got together a few of the townspeople and seen if we can't put the children to some simple jobs." Whatever does she mean? "Exactly what I meant. [pc.name], you may be absent most of the time, so your children are a special case, but most of the little ones here only come to the nursery sporadically, you know. They've chores and work their parents set for them on their own time." Well yes, this is a frontier town, after all. But how does this tie in with... well, whatever she said? "Then let me finish, please. What I'm getting together is an effort to teach the children the value of a good work ethic, build some character, and hopefully test their aptitude for a variety of jobs in the process." Hmm, might be interesting, but you probably aren't too interested in the details. "Suit yourself." |"What do you think of what I've done with the place? The world outside is so dreary and gray all the time — I've tried to liven things up a little by painting the walls with warm colors, and the children are being dears at making little crafts to put up." There's plenty of color to be had, that's for sure. It's very vibrant — reminds you of late spring, to be honest. "That's what I was going for, yes." Gwyn sighs happily. "We've certainly come a long way since the one-room cabin that the nursery started out as, haven't we? It's like... hm, well, my own little paradise, and I've got to thank you for putting in this much money, even if you aren't able to give very much of your time." Oh, no worries. You're happy to help out however you can. "There's always more that can be done, but for now at least there's not as much of a pressing need for donations any more. The difference between needs and wants, as Daddy would say." Well, you hope she won't stop working as hard as she did on her first day on the job. Gwyn laughs and wags her tail. "Don't you worry about that." |So, what's Gwyn looking at next when it comes to making this place bigger and better? Is she going to put in a second floor to the nursery? Gwyn looks thoughtful a moment and rubs her chin. "You know, that's not such a bad idea — it's something that I'd indeed like to eventually do someday. But not immediately." You nod. After all, bigger isn't always better — and you can see that costing a lot of money. "Oh, of course. But it's always good to have a goal to work towards in life. Like having lots and lots of puppies." |"I won't deny it — it's nice to have people know who you are. Even if it's just 'the lady who runs the nursery', it's a bit of local fame for being useful to other people." A small smile spreads out on Gwyn's muzzle, and she sighs happily. "You know, when I'm going out to market and people are pointing at me and saying 'that's her' — in a good way, of course. It makes me feel all warm and fuzzy inside." Like they do with Garth? "Yep! Just between you and me, while I really love Daddy and all, it was kind of tiring having everyone know me just as his girl. I know people didn't mean it, but it always felt to me that Garret and I were always in his shadow." Well, that's just one of the hazards of growing up with a local hero for a parent. "Mm. I know I shouldn't complain — there are far worse circumstances to grow up in — but all things strive, don't they? Well, at least I'm 'the nursery lady' now, and Garret's still daddy's boy." Better not press him too hard — who knows what lengths her brother might go to in order to prove himself. Gwyn laughs at that. "Oh, don't worry, [pc.name]. Garret might be a hothead, but he's not stupid. He's going to show off a bit at most — I'm not going to lose any sleep over him biting off more than he can chew." ] |[rand|"You know how we have a well out back?" Yes, you've seen it. It's got to be pretty deep to get to a clean water table, isn't it? "Kinda sorta. Most people in Hawkethorne pay to have their trash dumped in the pit couple miles out of town, but that isn't the point. The point is that some weeks back, there was this catfolk passing through town, looked like he was from the heartlands — anyway, what he was trying to convince Daddy to buy was this contraption. You fix it to a pipe, turn the crank, and then it sucks up water from whatever well you like, so long as it's not more than a hundred feet deep." That sounds like quite the feat of engineering — and too good to be true. "Yep. Daddy was about to tell him to get out of the Frost Hound, but the guy and River had a talk, and River thinks the guy's not kidding." Now that's interesting. Gwyn nods. "That's how Daddy works. He may not know you, but he chooses his friends carefully. If you're a friend of his friend, then you're all right with him. Anyways, Daddy was quite interested in the screw pump, as it was called, since it could serve both the Frost Hound and the nursery, but we don't have that kind of spending money at the moment." You can imagine that such a piece of work would involve some money again, yes... "So long as you're wise about it, it's hard to have too much money on you," Gwyn replies with a grin. |"I've got to thank you for putting in so much money towards making my dream a success, [pc.name]," Gwyn tells you. "Sure, you may not be the only one who donated, but you're definitely one of my biggest contributors." Hey, you've access to the kind of money that most people in Hawkethorne can only dream of. Going out into the wilderness and doing crazy stuff is dangerous, but it also brings with it its rewards. Besides, it's always nice to see another two-storey building in town. "Yes, but thank you nevertheless. It's very heart-warming to know that the main figures in and about Hawkethorne understand the importance of investing in the next generation." ] |[rand|"It's been going very well, thank you." Gwyn replies with a dip of her head. "To be honest, I'm starting to run out of ideas as to how we can improve the nursery." Which means she hasn't actually run out of ideas yet, has she? "Of course not. We've got the space, we've got the environment — all I really want to do now is to try and bring out the children's talents. Sure, there aren't that many people who would be gifted in, say, music, but it would be a shame to not try and discover what each and every one of them is best at. Even if it's something completely mundane like fishing or weaving." She seems rather empathic on this point. Does she have a personal stake in this? Gwyn sighs. "Daddy was a soldier in his time, and although I never really knew her, I hear that Mommy was, too. Garret, he took more after the both of them than I did, but what everyone in town did was to simply assume that since I was Daddy's daughter, what I wanted to do was to take up arms like he did. "Daddy wanted to teach me and I learned anyway, even if I wasn't so keen about it. Part of me wanted desperately to please Daddy, and the other part grudgingly admitted that it was better to have the skill and not use it, rather than not have the skill and need it. Well, you can see how that turned out." Ah. "Daddy says that my figure takes after Mommy's, but the way I'm putting that to use is quite different, I'd say." The wolfess pats her wide hips for emphasis. "And not only am I not having any regrets, but I couldn't be happier doing what I do, other people aside." |The nursery is pretty big now, isn't it? "And getting a little popular, if I dare say so myself," Gwyn adds. "We're not quite full yet, but we're certainly getting there. Folks who want a day to themselves just leave their kids with us in the morning and pick them up in the evening." Must be plenty of those around. "Everyone needs a small break every now and then, even the likes of me. Sure, my work may never be done, but that doesn't mean I can't enjoy a nice cup of tea." Which is why she's sitting down with you and chatting instead of actually working, eh? Gwyn giggles. "Exactly." |"You may not have noticed it, but we're using some of the donation money to spruce up some of the older places. Just because the kitchen was the first things to be built doesn't mean we look to improving it — we just put in another oven not too long ago, and some extra shelves for the pantry." It's good that she's looking back and not neglecting what's already been built. Does the nursery take much upkeep? Gwyn laughs, her heavy bosom shaking under her dress with the sheer force of her yipping laughter. "Oh, [pc.name], you would not imagine how quickly things get worn down when you've to clean them two or three times a day. But yes, quite a bit goes towards upkeep. While the baroness's fund's grown somewhat, I don't want to dip into the principal at all, and scrimp a little on the earnings." Which means asking for more donations? "No, no, [pc.name], I'm not asking you for money. We've already got plenty of stuff. Just... do as you've always been doing, and we'll get along fine." ] |[rand|"We're holding up just fine, thank you very much. More than fine, in fact — I'm forced to admit that there isn't anything that I can think of adding to the nursery that I could reasonably get, or that would be in character for Hawkethorne. I think this place is as big as it needs to be for a village this size." Hey, it's changed a lot. You still remember how the small, dingy place this used to be... and come to think of it, she's changed a lot, too. "I'm not going to deny that," Gwyn replies with a giggle. "The change's been for the better, after all." So, what does she intend now? Keep on keeping on, as the saying goes? A happy nod. "I'm not going to need any more money to pay for improvements to the nursery, but it certainly would be nice to have to help defray the daily expenses. You can imagine that keeping this place in shape is quite the task." It is, in its own right, a hero's task. Her own work is as important as her mother's was — probably even more. Taking life is easy — helping to shape lives into useful, well-lived ones is much harder. Gwyn says nothing and keeps a remarkably straight face as she sips her tea, but the furious wagging of the wolfess' tail betrays her emotions. |"I really couldn't be happier. The nursery is everything I've dreamed of — and then a little more. I've got so many people to thank for helping to make it come true — amongst them being the baroness, for giving me the seed money to get it started, and you, of course, for... well, all you've done." Hey, she had a plan, had a clear route to get from point A to B, and stuck to it. Now it's paid off, she has every right to savor the fruits of her labors. Gwyn makes a happy noise in the back of her throat. "Yes, but it's not as if I did it alone. It makes me happy that almost everyone in Hawkethorne has come together to make this a success." It just goes to show what even a small community can do when enough people get drawn together to a common cause, doesn't it? "Yes, yes, it does." ] |[rand|"It's a bit of trouble having to run back into the Frost Hound to do the cooking," Gwyn admits. "One of the first things I want to spend money on here is to get a proper kitchen up and running so Daddy and I don't get in each other's way." That does sound reasonable, yes. You can't help but feel a little underwhelmed that the baroness wouldn't even give Gwyn a kitchen to get started with, but you suppose she's supposed to work her way out of the very bottom. Builds character and all that. "It's to push me to work harder, I guess." Gwyn gathers up her tail in her hands and tries to look cheerful, but you can't help but notice her usually perky ears laid flat against her head. Well, you'll be behind her one hundred and one percent, okay? "That's very much appreciated, thank you." |"What do I think of the place? Well, maybe I could ask you the same question — what do you think of the place?" It's... a bit small. But it has character, and more importantly, potential. Gwyn cocks an ear at you. "That's very... um, nice. What sort of character would you say the nursery has, in that case?" Her sort of character. Gwyn's character is so large it spills out of her and all over the place like a mug running over. It's rather pleasant, to be honest. "Flatterer." You only aim to please. |Gwyn considers the question for a few seconds, sighs, and rubs her face. "I suppose I wish there was a little more room around here. Not that I haven't tried to make the most of what I've got, but you can water down soup only so much before it becomes just water." That's one way of putting things. Is there any way you can help? "Daddy knows people who do good work — they did put this place together, after all — but they don't work for free." Ah. Gwyn smiles. "Not that I'm asking you for money or anything, [pc.name], but... well, gods. I am asking you for money. And not just you, pretty much everyone in Hawkethorne. I've asked Sanders to see if he can't pass around some kind of collection plate for people who go to the chapel." Well, you'll see what you can do when you have a bit of spare money on hand. ] ] "

rows.original: At the suggestion, Gwyn holds her smile and inclines her head ever so slightly, the wolfess' pointy ears twitching with the movement. "If that's what you want! I certainly don't mind talking about me, I can tell you that — in fact, I'm my favorite subject! Who doesn't like talking about themselves, after all?" Um... you might be able to come up with a few examples, but probably not off the top of your head. "So long as you don't go prying when I'm clear that I don't want to speak of something, we'll all be fine here." Gwyn's smile widens enough to show her teeth. "Now, shall we begin?"
rows.translation: 闻言，格温保持着微笑，微微颔首，那女狼尖尖的耳朵也随着动作轻轻抖动。“如果这就是你想要的！我当然不介意谈论自己，跟你说，事实上，我自己就是我最喜欢的话题！毕竟，谁会不喜欢谈论自己呢？” 嗯……你或许能够想出一些例子，但多半没法立刻就想出来。 “只要在我明确表示不想谈论某件事的时候，你不去追问，我们在这里就会相处得很好。”格温的笑容变得如此灿烂，以至于牙齿都露了出来。“那么，我们现在开始吧？”

rows.original: [gwyn.bellyRange 0 0.8 1.3 1.8 2.4 |[rand|Gwyn smiles, reaches down to the gentle swell of her belly, and gives it an almost absent-minded caress. "Some may think that big bellies are great, and they are, but I really do enjoy every single moment of carrying my puppies." Even the moments when her back aches like a host of wraiths and she has to go to the washroom every ten minutes? Gwyn laughs softly and gives you a big smile. "Nothing's ever perfect, [pc.name]. However, I'm given to understand that such things weigh less heavily on me than they do other women — it seems like I was practically born to this. Some people are good at cooking, others are good at fishing — I'm the one who had the good fortune to be good at making puppies. "But even so, yes, I do take those less-than-perfect moments in stride. You've got to accept the good with the bad, after all." |At your question, Gwyn grins and looks down at her small baby bump. "Better than you'd expect, even for me. I have a good feeling about this particular litter." Oh? "Of course, I can't tell for sure, but given how big I'm getting so early I think this is going to be a large litter." The wolfess licks her lips, and you can practically feel the lusty anticipation oozing off her. Pregnancy hormones are one thing, but pregnancy hormones acting on Gwyn is a whole other kettle of fish. "I suppose time will tell, won't it?" Well, you're hoping it's a large litter, because you sure want to know how utterly and thoroughly you knocked her up. "We'll see. We'll see." |"Even so early on, I keep getting hungry all the time when I have puppies growing in me; it's hard not to sneak a bite or two when I'm cooking for the children. It's gotten such that I always cook a bit more than I know I'll need." Huh. While you can understand that she's eating for more than just herself, won't she start putting on weight like this? Gwyn shrugs. "I'm not exactly chiseled like my mother reputedly was, but I haven't put on so much as a pound of baby fat, either. It's odd, I know, but it seems that everything that I eat is either used to keep me going, or turned into puppy without any excess." Hah. When she puts it that way... you guess she's a self-confessed machine for turning delicious treats into puppies, and a brutally efficient one at that. "Hah." Still, she reluctantly drags herself back to reality and shakes her head slowly. "Um... where were we? Oh, right. You shake your head and smile. That's one way of putting it, you guess — and it's not too far from the truth.. "Hee hee, isn't it? But what truly makes it great, though, is knowing that you've chosen a worthy and decent mate to father your pups. The bastard who knocked me up with my first litter — well, I was dumb plus I was also in heat, so I spread my legs without knowing what I was doing. You, on the other hand..." Oh, so you're just worthy and decent? You thought you might rank a wee bit higher than that, doesn't she think? Gwyn sticks her tongue out at you to match your grin, and settles back in her chair with her hands clasped over the swell of her increasingly overstuffed womb. "I'd have said I don't just spread my legs for anyone, but that excuse isn't available to me any more, is it? All right then, if you're fishing for praise, you can have it. [pc.name], you are a pretty damn good mate to have knocked me up this thoroughly." That's more like it. Although isn't that a contradiction when it comes to the father of her first litter, considering how many puppies were in that one? "Oh, hush, you. If you keep on like this, you're not getting any from me." Oh, she doesn't have to worry about that — all you have to do is cuddle and caress her puppy pack plenty, and she'll be in the mood for anything Gwyn grumbles and mutters some, but doesn't deny that fact. ] |[rand|Whoa, Gwyn's starting to get really big now. Still, the sheer size of that thing must count for something — even if it weighed nothing, her belly must still get in the way, right? A cheery whistle. "I gave up trying to see my toes a long time ago, [pc.name]. Now even putting on my socks in the morning is a problem." If that's the case, you can't even begin to imagine how she ever picks up anything that's on the ground. "The children are often more than happy enough to do it for me," Gwyn replies with a laugh. "Oh, it's a bit of this and that, to be honest," Gwyn says as she waves a hand in the air dismissively before sipping her tea. Well, if that's the worst complaint that Gwyn can think up, she's a truly blessed mother. "People do tell me that I have that glow, and I suppose my fur does get a lot glossier and smoother when I'm carrying puppies in me. Must say that I'm truly blessed in all things maternal, aren't I?" It's hard to make a case otherwise... ] |[rand|Ye gods, Gwyn's as big as a house — and a three-storey mansion at that. "I will admit... I'm being weighed down a little, although it's nothing I can't handle. But that's your fault for knocking me up, isn't it?" Well, it wouldn't be so extreme if her womb wasn't an overeager puppy factory, but then again you know that she wouldn't have it any other way. "It's very sweet of you to be concerned — as it is for everyone else, really — but my body knows enough to not bite off more than it can chew, thank you very much. This isn't the first time I've done this; I'm not about to up and explode or something." To be fair, she does look fit to pop any moment, and the way she's stuffing her face with tea and cookies isn't helping the situation any. A giggle. "Oh, I'll be popping soon, all right — just not in the way you mean. Maybe you'll be around for the big occasion?" You might be, or maybe you might not be. After all, you're often away from Hawkethorne, and while she'll probably be having that litter of puppies soon, no one can tell the exact moment. It'll be, as they say, hit and miss. "We'll see, then. We'll see." |"I suppose I should be saying this, even if I haven't gotten around to it: thank you." Oh? Whatever for? You can imagine several dozen different things that Gwyn might conceivably thank you for, but what's the issue at hand? "Hey, don't look a gift horse in the mouth. When someone else's praising you, the least you can do is accept the praise gratefully." Either way, what's the big event? "You made me this way, of course!" Gwyn sighs and pats the stretched skin of her monstrously swollen breasts and belly. "It's been a crazy few months, but it's the good kind of crazy, and I've enjoyed every moment of it." She does have a leg up by having the kind of constitution which lends itself to being massively gravid and full and puppies. "Oh, it's not been completely perfect, but at any moment I do feel that the good outweighs the bad by quite a bit. So... thank you." It's been your pleasure. Gwyn nods and laughs. "Give me a week or two after I've popped these puppies, and I'll be more than happy to do it all over again." Sigh. If it were anyone but Gwyn saying that, you'd be sure she was joking. Since it is Gwyn, though... |Smiling, Gwyn sets down her tea and sighs wistfully. "You know what I would really like right now, [pc.name]?" No, you don't, although the way she's saying it does have you intrigued. "What I'd really like is for someone to walk over to the pantry, get out the butter — the good chamomile butter, thank you — and rub it all over me. Especially on my tummy, yes, but generally all over will do just fine. Yes, indeed — the day's not been going too well since this morning, and I'm feeling like I could use a little buttering up. A lot of buttering up, given how much of me there is." Does she want that someone to lick it all off, too? "That would be nice, but not strictly necessary." Well, not right now. You were under the impression that you were suppose to grease ovens before you put in the batter to bake, and not during the baking. Ovens do get really hot while the buns are rising all snug and warm inside it — you'd rather not risk getting burned, yes? "See, this is the exact sort of thing I've had to put up with all day — wiseasses making cracks at me, thinking they're funny. It's got to be that, because I'm sure I can't be any more obvious." ] ]

rows.original: [rand|So, is there something that Gwyn really likes to eat? A small smile. "Why? Thinking of getting me something?" Maybe, maybe. A small gift is usually appropriate to show one's appreciation for another, after all. Although one can hardly give meaningful gifts when one isn't sure about the other's likes, yes? Gwyn lets out a small bark of laughter, which quickly fades into a giggle. "You know, if I were anyone else, I'd probably have said something on the lines of 'if you were close enough to give me a gift, you'd know what I like.' Daddy certainly would. But I'm nice that way." So, then... anything she'd like to stuff her face-mouth with? "Truth be told, I'm not too picky an eater. Comes with being brought up on a steady diet of the Frost Hound's leftovers. Although..." Yes? "I do really love cream pies, they're so thick and filling and I can bake them by myself in my oven. They taste so much better home-made, then I can make them just how I like them — extra big, with lots of cream and a dense crust. Goodness, I'm already getting hungry just thinking about it." Well, if that's what she's interested in, perhaps a gift of your time would be much more in line. You could definitely help her make some cream pies someday, if she doesn't mind. "Hmm... yes, I'd like that." |"I'd like to say that I'm on pretty good terms with most of the caravaners who bother coming up to the frontier these days," Gwyn tells you after a little thought. "I guess it comes naturally with seeing them all the time, I suppose." She sees them a lot? The market isn't cutting it for her? A shake of Gwyn's furry head. "Not with the amounts I've to buy to keep the nursery running; it's much easier to make my purchases wholesale at this point rather than deal with the streets and stalls. I get a better price for buying in bulk, they don't have to worry about not being able to offload the last of their goods, and everyone wins." Mm. "The roads are definitely more dangerous of late, but life goes on. If you need a bit of gossip from down on south, though, feel free to ask away. No guarantees as to whether it'll be true, of course." |"I try and nip down to the chapel once a week to get some quiet time." Somehow, you don't find that surprising. Even during night, you get the suspicion that the nursery isn't exactly peaceful. Gwyn nods. "That, and of course I try not to fall behind in my obligations to the Living Gods. I'll fully admit that I've never been the very religious sort save for what's needed to get along — but Sanders is a very nice man to talk to, and he's naturally very aware and appreciative of the work I'm doing here, as I am of his." ]
rows.translation: [rand|那么，有没有什么食物是格温特别喜欢吃的呢？ 她微微一笑。“为什么？是打算给我买些什么吗？” 也许吧，也许吧。毕竟，送一份小礼物通常是表达感激之情的恰当方式。不过，当一个人不确定对方喜欢什么的时候，也确实很难送出有意义的礼物，对吧？ 格温轻声笑了起来，那笑声很快便变成了窃笑。“你知道，如果换成别人，我大概会说‘你要是跟我亲近到能送我礼物，你早就知道我喜欢什么了’之类的话。爸爸肯定会这么说。不过我这人就是这么好。” 那么……她还有什么想塞进嘴里的东西吗？ “说实话，我对食物并不算挑剔。这是从小吃霜犬酒馆的剩饭养成的。不过……” 嗯？ “我真的很喜欢奶油派，它们又厚实又管饱，而且我可以在自己的烤箱里亲手做。自制的奶油派味道好得多，而且我想怎么做就怎么做——做得特别大，放很多奶油，再配上紧实的外皮。天哪，光是想想我就开始觉得饿了。” 嗯，如果她真的对那个感兴趣，那么送她一些你的时间或许会更合适。如果她不介意的话，你完全可以哪天帮她做几个奶油派。 “嗯……好呀，我很乐意。” |“我得说，如今还愿意跑到边境来的那些商队成员，大多跟我关系都挺不错，”格温思索片刻后告诉你。“我想，大概是总跟他们见面，自然就熟络了吧。” 她经常见到他们吗？市场环境对她来说已经不够理想了吗？ 格温摇了摇她那毛茸茸的脑袋。“以我为了维持托儿所运转所需的采购量来说，市场可满足不了；现在整批进货比应付街头摊位方便多了——批量购买能拿到更好的价格，他们也不必担心最后那点货砸在手里，大家都得益。” 嗯。 “最近道路确实更危险了，但日子还得过。不过，如果你想听听从南方传来的闲话，尽管来问我。当然，内容是否属实我可不敢保证。” |“我尽量每周去一趟小教堂，图个清静。” 不知为何，你并不觉得意外。哪怕是在夜里，你也怀疑那个托儿所并不怎么安宁。 格温点了点头。“除了那个，我当然也尽量不落下对现世神祇们应尽的义务。我完全承认，除了应付场面所需的那点之外，我从来都不是什么虔诚的人——但桑德斯是个很值得一聊的人，他自然很清楚我在这里做的事并心怀感激，我对他做的事也一样。” ]
rows.raw: " [rand|So, is there something that Gwyn really likes to eat? A small smile. "Why? Thinking of getting me something?" Maybe, maybe. A small gift is usually appropriate to show one's appreciation for another, after all. Although one can hardly give meaningful gifts when one isn't sure about the other's likes, yes? Gwyn lets out a small bark of laughter, which quickly fades into a giggle. "You know, if I were anyone else, I'd probably have said something on the lines of 'if you were close enough to give me a gift, you'd know what I like.' Daddy certainly would. But I'm nice that way." So, then... anything she'd like to stuff her face-mouth with? "Truth be told, I'm not too picky an eater. Comes with being brought up on a steady diet of the Frost Hound's leftovers. Although..." rows.translation: 家人

rows.original: [var0 |[rand|"Daddy's been pestering me to get more sword practice in." Again? Gwyn shifts her eyes. "Yep, again." Well, you've had some iteration of this conversation with her in the past, so there's really no point going through it again. If she's going to continue like this just to please Garth... "I suppose. Not that I really like fighting that much, even if I'm good at it, but if I had to, you know what I'd have liked to be?" What? "A shieldmaiden like out of one of the old stories. One of those great stout lupines with their spears and painted shields, servants to the old pack jarls, not some kind of gritty sellsword that Daddy and Mommy used to be." Gwyn's large blue eyes shine for a moment, and the wolfess heaves a large sigh. "He laughed, patted my head and said the time for shieldmaidens and their glory had long passed, but if I wanted to learn the spear and shield in addition to my existing lessons, he'd teach me." That sounds... tactless, to put it one way. "Daddy's not one for sugar-coating the truth. That was his way of caring, not that I understood it at the time. I get that he's just looking out for me and doesn't want me to backslide now that I have a job outside the Frost Hound, but old habits are hard to break." |"Garret's been teasing me about being a big puppy again." You don't know if that's something worthy of being teased over... Gwyn pouts. "It just gets to me. I'm eighteen, I'm a mother, and the baroness herself named me to head the nursery she's paying for. I'm not a puppy anymore. It's not as if he's that much older than I am anyway — Daddy tells me that he was the first out of Mommy's belly by a few minutes, that's all." Well, it shouldn't get to her. It's natural for children to feel ashamed of being overly childish, since their job is to grow up. By the same token, there's nothing wrong with adults being a little bit childish when the situation allows for it. It's important to not lose that sense of youth and wonder — that's how people turn into cynical old grouts. "Hmp." Besides, it's adorable that she can be so puppy-like at times, and it's probably one of the reasons she's so good with puppies herself. Being a big, lovable, huggable puppy isn't all bad; she should cherish it. Gwyn presses her ears flat against her head, but her tail starts wagging frenziedly. Talk about conflicting signals. "Well, if you say so..." |"Daddy's been getting more business at the Frost Hound lately." Oh? You'd have imagined that there would be less business with all the troubles since... well, since then. She knows what you mean. Gwyn shakes her head mopily. "No. If anything, the troubles are attracting more people up to Hawkethorne, people who're too bored and with nothing better to do with their lives than to seek out danger for its own sake. How do you think Daddy gets the money to put you up for free?" Huh, you never really thought about it... but now that Gwyn's mentioned it, it does make sense. "I haven't actually looked at the books yet, but you've brought in — and continue to bring in — more money than Daddy spends on your room and board, so there's that." Well, glad you could help[pc.isChamp|, although you're not so sure that making money off the probable misfortune of others is the best way to go about it]. Gwyn shrugs. "It's not as if we can stop them from coming up here, and so long as they do, we might as well lighten their purses. That's what Daddy says, and I have to agree." |Does Gwyn ever miss her mother? She looks at you oddly, then gives a contemptuous sniff, her muzzle high in the air. "No. I can't miss what I never saw, what I never had." Isn't that a rather cold way of putting it? The wolfess looks annoyed at that, and snaps at the air. "Oh, please. I'm sure she had very good reasons for doing what she did, so I'm going to give her the benefit of the doubt for that. However, by all accounts, I'm not going to miss not having her around. Just looking at how Daddy and Garret fight sometimes is enough to raise one's hackles — can you imagine how Mommy would have been like? "If you can't, I can. 'Why aren't you more like Garret, Gwyn?' 'Garret's got a much better attitude than you do, girl.' 'Some days, I can't quite believe you came out from the same womb together.' I love Daddy and I know he loves me back, but that doesn't mean that we don't have... our off days, days when someone's just feeling grumpy or bitter or something. But her? I don't need another person belittling the perfectly useful work I'm doing with my life." All right, all right. You get the idea. On her part, Gwyn bites her lip, takes a deep breath, and stops panting. "The fact that I can play Daddy some helps, something which I don't think I'd be able to do with Mommy if she were around. Even if she turned up at the door tomorrow, I'm not sure I'd want to call myself a daughter of hers." Harsh. "Harsh, but it's the truth." [pc.isDK|And what's the truth? That she gets just a bit jealous when she considers another woman being in front of her in line for her daddy's love? Gwyn says nothing and quickly sips her tea to hide her face, but the ever-so-brief dark expression of sheer envy and resentment on her face tells you all you need to know. |] |"Garret wanted a bit of rough and tumble a couple of days ago, but I turned him down.[gwyn.bellyRange 0.4| It's not that I'm seriously encumbered by this tummy of mine, but more that] I'm not for these things any more." Rough and tumble, huh. Sounds like a bit of a scrap. "That it was. We did it a lot when we were but puppies — fists, teeth and feet — it was more fun in those days, and a great way for us to work out our problems behind the woodpile. Daddy certainly knew what was going on — it's obvious, now that I look back on it — but he didn't say anything at all." Who tended to win those little bouts? Gwyn smiles and shrugs. "There was no telling for sure. That's what made it fun. One day I'd send Garret off howling, and the next he'd have me by the throat. Games are always the most fun when you go in knowing you have a fair chance, but don't have a good grip on the outcome. Rough and tumble time provided that. "Too old now to go about getting into scraps with my brother, especially since we're much stronger these days. Doesn't stop him from asking every now and then, though." |"I worry about Garret sometimes. He's been beating himself up over his ineptitude ever since you'd to step him and haul him out of the pickle he'd dumped himself in. It was kinda amusing at first, but it's dragged on for long enough that it isn't funny any more." Well, what does she suggest be done? "I don't know, which is why I'm worrying. Knowing my idiot brother, he might very well decide to go out there once again to try and prove himself or something, live up to Daddy's name. Difference between Daddy and him is that Daddy had the whole of Mommy's mercenary company backing him up, and Garret's got just his own two hands. "It wasn't very safe out there to begin with, be it in Harvest Valley or the Old Forest, and things have only gotten worse since... since the storm. Maybe since you were the one who got him out of that fix, he might be willing to listen to you — more than he would to his baby sister." You'll see what you can do about that. "Thank you, [pc.name]. I know it may not seem it when I talk about him, but Garret's my big brother, after all. I can sniff out every inch of his hide, and I'm pretty sure he respects you a whole lot for getting him home safely, even if he won't 'fess up and say it out loud." ] |"I... well, there's not much to really say at the moment. Garret's still been missing since the snowstorm the day you came into town, and Daddy's been worried sick over him since then. I suppose if anyone's skilled at surviving out in the Old Forest it'd be Garret, but he's been gone for so long that things aren't looking good." Both she and Garth look quite blase about it, if she doesn't mind you saying. "Well, what did you expect? We can't let the fact that Big Brother's missing stop our lives. So long as there isn't a body, there's still hope, but we're not going to sit around doing nothing." You'll let her know if you come across any hearsay of her brother, then. Gwyn waves you off. "If you want to do that, then please speak to Daddy about it. I... I don't want to get my hopes up for nothing after so long." ]
rows.translation: [var0 |[rand|爸爸一直催着我多练习剑术。 又来？ 格温移开了视线。没错，又是这样。 嗯，你过去已经和她多次讨论过这个问题了，所以再重复讨论也没有意义。如果她只是为了取悦加斯而继续这样下去的话…… 我想是的。虽然我确实挺擅长打架的，但说实话，我并不是真的那么喜欢打架。不过如果非得这么做的话，你知道我希望能扮演什么角色吗？ 什么？ 一个仿佛出自古老故事中的女盾兵。那种身强力壮、手持长矛、身披彩绘盾牌的勇士，是那些古老部落首领的忠诚仆从，而不是那种父母曾经雇佣的普通雇佣兵。格温那双大大的蓝眼睛闪烁了一下，这只母狼发出了一声长长的叹息。他笑了笑，拍了拍我的头，说“守护女战士们以及她们的荣耀，早已成为过去的事情了。不过，如果我想在现有的课程之外再学习长矛与盾牌的运用，他愿意教我。 这么说吧，那听起来确实有点不得体。 爸爸从来不会用甜言蜜语来掩盖事实。那其实是他的表达方式，只是当时我并不理解。现在我明白了，他只是关心我，不希望我在离开霜犬酒馆之后再走回原来的道路，但老习惯确实很难改掉。 |加雷特一直取笑我，说我又变成了一只小狗。 你根本不知道这件事是否值得被拿来开玩笑…… 格温撅起了嘴。这真的让我很难过。我才18岁，还是个母亲，而那位女男爵亲自指名让我来做这件事我去管理那个她出资建立的托儿所吧。我已经不是小狗了，而且他其实也并没有比我大多少——爸爸告诉我，他只是比我在妈妈肚子里多出来几分钟而已，就是这么简单。 嗯，这件事不应该影响到她。孩子们会因为自己表现得过于幼稚而感到羞愧，这是很正常的，因为他们的使命就是成长。同样地，当情况允许时，成年人偶尔表现得有点幼稚也并没有什么错。重要的是，不要失去那种青春活力与好奇心——否则人们就会变成那些愤世嫉俗的老人。 哼。 另外，她有时候会表现得那么像一只小狗，这种行为实在太可爱了，这也可能是她自己这么喜欢小狗的原因之一。成为一名可爱、让人想拥抱的小狗，其实也没什么不好的；她应该珍惜这种感觉。 格温把耳朵贴在脑袋上，但她的尾巴却开始疯狂地摇动起来。真是矛盾的行为啊嗯，如果你这么说的话…… |最近，爸爸在‘寒霜猎犬’那里的业务量越来越大。 哦？你可能会认为，自从发生了那些麻烦事之后，生意会变得冷清起来吧……嗯，就是从那时候开始。然后她明白你的意思。 格温沮丧地摇了摇头。不。事实上，这些麻烦反而吸引了更多人来到鹰棘镇——那些生活无聊、找不到更有意义的事情可做，因此才刻意去追求危险的人。你猜爸爸是怎么弄到钱来免费供你读书的？ 哈，你之前其实从未认真思考过这个问题……不过现在既然格温提到了，那确实有道理。 其实我还没仔细看过那些账本，但你们赚的钱——而且赚的钱一直都在增加——已经超过了爸爸为你们支付的生活费和住宿费，这一点是事实。 嗯，很高兴你能提供帮助。[pc.isChamp|虽然你并不确定，通过利用他人的不幸来赚钱真的是最好的方式。]格温耸了耸肩。我们总不可能阻止他们来到这里，既然他们来了，我们还不如让他们多花点钱。爸爸是这么说的，我也觉得有道理。 |格温会想念她的母亲吗？ 她用一种奇怪的眼神看着你，然后轻蔑地哼了一声，鼻子高高翘在空气中。不。我无法错过那些我从未见过、从未拥有过的东西。 这种说法未免太冷酷了吧？ 狼女听后显得很不高兴，她对着空气“哼”了一声，说道：“哦，拜托了。我相信她这么做肯定有她的原因，所以我决定暂时相信她。不过，说实话，没有她在身边我反而会觉得自在些。只要看看爸爸和加勒有时候打架的样子，就足以让人感到烦躁了——你们能想象妈妈会是什么样子吗？ 如果你做不到，那我来做。‘为什么你不能像加雷特那样呢，格温？’‘加雷特的态度可比你好多了，姑娘。’‘有时候，我简直不敢相信你们其实是同一个母亲生的。’我爱爸爸，也知道他也爱我，但这并不意味着我们就没有……情绪不好的时候，有时候就是会觉得烦躁或者郁闷之类的。但是她呢？我可不需要再有人来贬低我正在为生活所做的这些有意义的事情。 好吧，好吧。你明白我的意思了吧。格温咬了咬嘴唇，深吸一口气，然后停止了喘息。 能够扮演‘父亲’这个角色，确实让我感到有些安慰。我觉得，如果妈妈还在身边，我恐怕就无法这样做。即使她明天就出现在我家门口，我也不确定自己是否还会愿意称自己为她的女儿。 太苛刻了。 残酷，但这就是事实。 [pc.isDK|那么，真相是什么呢？难道就是当她看到另一个女人站在自己前面，争夺她爸爸的爱时，她会感到一丝嫉妒吗？ 格温什么也没说，只是迅速喝了一口茶，试图掩饰自己的情绪，但她脸上那一瞬间的嫉妒与怨恨之情，已经说明了一切。 |] |几天前，加雷特想要闹点动静，但我拒绝了他的请求。[gwyn.bellyRange 0.4| 其实并不是说我的肚子真的给我带来了太多麻烦，而是……]我再也不喜欢这类事情了。 打打闹闹的，哈。听起来像是一场小冲突啊。 确实是这样。当我们还是小狗的时候，我们经常这样玩——用拳头、牙齿和足部互相攻击，那些日子真的很有趣，也是我们解决矛盾的好办法。爸爸肯定知道发生了什么——现在回想起来，这一点很明显——但他什么也没说。 谁通常会在那些小比赛中获胜呢？ 格温微笑着耸了耸肩。谁也说不准结果会怎样。正是这种不确定性才让游戏变得有趣。有时候我会把加雷特打得哭哭啼啼，而第二天他就会反过来掐住我的脖子。当你知道自己有公平的机会，却又无法预知最终结果时，游戏才会真正变得有趣。而这种充满不确定性和激烈对抗的体验，正是游戏带来的乐趣所在。 现在年纪大了，再也不会和弟弟打架了，尤其是我们现在都强多了。不过，他还是会偶尔问起这件事来。 |有时候我真的很担心加雷特。自从你出手把他从自己造成的困境中解救出来之后，他就一直因为自己的无能而自责不已。一开始这还挺有意思的，但现在已经持续太久了，一点都不好笑了。 那么，她建议应该采取什么措施呢？ 我不知道，所以才担心。以我那个傻弟弟的性格，他很可能会再次出去尝试证明自己，想不辜负爸爸的名声。不过爸爸和他不一样，爸爸有妈妈领导的佣兵团队支持他，而加雷特只有自己的一双手。 从一开始，无论是收获谷还是古林，外面的环境都不太安全，而自从那场风暴之后，情况更是变得糟糕了……也许因为是你把他从困境中解救出来的，所以他更愿意听你的意见——比听他妹妹的意见更愿意。 你会看到自己能为此做些什么的。 谢谢，[pc.name]我知道，当我谈论他的时候，这可能不会显得很明显，但毕竟加雷特是我的哥哥。我非常了解他的性格，我敢肯定，因为你帮他安全地回到了家，他非常感激你，尽管他可能不会公开承认这一点。 ] |我……嗯，目前实在没什么好说的。自从你来到这个小镇的那天发生暴风雪之后，加勒就一直失踪了，从那以后爸爸就一直非常担心他。我想，如果有人擅长在古林里生存的话，那肯定就是加勒，但他已经失踪太久了，情况看起来不太妙。 如果她不介意的话，她和加斯对这件事似乎都显得相当淡然。 嗯，你还能期待什么呢？我们总不能因为大哥失踪了就停止自己的生活。只要没有找到尸体，就还有希望，但我们不会坐以待毙的。 那么，如果你听到任何关于她哥哥的传闻，一定要告诉她。 格温向你挥了挥手，示意你离开。如果你想这么做的话，那就请跟爸爸商量一下。我……毕竟等了这么久，可不想白白抱有希望。 ]
rows.raw: " [var0 |[rand|"Daddy's been pestering me to get more sword practice in." Again? Gwyn shifts her eyes. "Yep, again." Well, you've had some iteration of this conversation with her in the past, so there's really no point going through it again. If she's going to continue like this just to please Garth... "I suppose. Not that I really like fighting that much, even if I'm good at it, but if I had to, you know what I'd have liked to be?" What? "A shieldmaiden like out of one of the old stories. One of those great stout lupines with their spears and painted shields, servants to the old pack jarls, not some kind of gritty sellsword that Daddy and Mommy used to be." Gwyn's large blue eyes shine for a moment, and the wolfess heaves a large sigh. "He laughed, patted my head and said the time for shieldmaidens and their glory had long passed, but if I wanted to learn the spear and shield in addition to my existing lessons, he'd teach me." That sounds... tactless, to put it one way. "Daddy's not one for sugar-coating the truth. That was his way of caring, not that I understood it at the time. I get that he's just looking out for me and doesn't want me to backslide now that I have a job outside the Frost Hound, but old habits are hard to break." |"Garret's been teasing me about being a big puppy again." You don't know if that's something worthy of being teased over... Gwyn pouts. "It just gets to me. I'm eighteen, I'm a mother, and the baroness herself named me to head the nursery she's paying for. I'm not a puppy anymore. It's not as if he's that much older than I am anyway — Daddy tells me that he was the first out of Mommy's belly by a few minutes, that's all." Well, it shouldn't get to her. It's natural for children to feel ashamed of being overly childish, since their job is to grow up. By the same token, there's nothing wrong with adults being a little bit childish when the situation allows for it. It's important to not lose that sense of youth and wonder — that's how people turn into cynical old grouts. "Hmp." Besides, it's adorable that she can be so puppy-like at times, and it's probably one of the reasons she's so good with puppies herself. Being a big, lovable, huggable puppy isn't all bad; she should cherish it. Gwyn presses her ears flat against her head, but her tail starts wagging frenziedly. Talk about conflicting signals. "Well, if you say so..." |"Daddy's been getting more business at the Frost Hound lately." Oh? You'd have imagined that there would be less business with all the troubles since... well, since then. She knows what you mean. Gwyn shakes her head mopily. "No. If anything, the troubles are attracting more people up to Hawkethorne, people who're too bored and with nothing better to do with their lives than to seek out danger for its own sake. How do you think Daddy gets the money to put you up for free?" Huh, you never really thought about it... but now that Gwyn's mentioned it, it does make sense. "I haven't actually looked at the books yet, but you've brought in — and continue to bring in — more money than Daddy spends on your room and board, so there's that." Well, glad you could help[pc.isChamp|, although you're not so sure that making money off the probable misfortune of others is the best way to go about it]. Gwyn shrugs. "It's not as if we can stop them from coming up here, and so long as they do, we might as well lighten their purses. That's what Daddy says, and I have to agree." |Does Gwyn ever miss her mother? She looks at you oddly, then gives a contemptuous sniff, her muzzle high in the air. "No. I can't miss what I never saw, what I never had." Isn't that a rather cold way of putting it? The wolfess looks annoyed at that, and snaps at the air. "Oh, please. I'm sure she had very good reasons for doing what she did, so I'm going to give her the benefit of the doubt for that. However, by all accounts, I'm not going to miss not having her around. Just looking at how Daddy and Garret fight sometimes is enough to raise one's hackles — can you imagine how Mommy would have been like? "If you can't, I can. 'Why aren't you more like Garret, Gwyn?' 'Garret's got a much better attitude than you do, girl.' 'Some days, I can't quite believe you came out from the same womb together.' I love Daddy and I know he loves me back, but that doesn't mean that we don't have... our off days, days when someone's just feeling grumpy or bitter or something. But her? I don't need another person belittling the perfectly useful work I'm doing with my life." All right, all right. You get the idea. On her part, Gwyn bites her lip, takes a deep breath, and stops panting. "The fact that I can play Daddy some helps, something which I don't think I'd be able to do with Mommy if she were around. Even if she turned up at the door tomorrow, I'm not sure I'd want to call myself a daughter of hers." Harsh. "Harsh, but it's the truth." [pc.isDK|And what's the truth? That she gets just a bit jealous when she considers another woman being in front of her in line for her daddy's love? Gwyn says nothing and quickly sips her tea to hide her face, but the ever-so-brief dark expression of sheer envy and resentment on her face tells you all you need to know. |] |"Garret wanted a bit of rough and tumble a couple of days ago, but I turned him down.[gwyn.bellyRange 0.4| It's not that I'm seriously encumbered by this tummy of mine, but more that] I'm not for these things any more." Rough and tumble, huh. Sounds like a bit of a scrap. "That it was. We did it a lot when we were but puppies — fists, teeth and feet — it was more fun in those days, and a great way for us to work out our problems behind the woodpile. Daddy certainly knew what was going on — it's obvious, now that I look back on it — but he didn't say anything at all." Who tended to win those little bouts? Gwyn smiles and shrugs. "There was no telling for sure. That's what made it fun. One day I'd send Garret off howling, and the next he'd have me by the throat. Games are always the most fun when you go in knowing you have a fair chance, but don't have a good grip on the outcome. Rough and tumble time provided that. "Too old now to go about getting into scraps with my brother, especially since we're much stronger these days. Doesn't stop him from asking every now and then, though." |"I worry about Garret sometimes. He's been beating himself up over his ineptitude ever since you'd to step him and haul him out of the pickle he'd dumped himself in. It was kinda amusing at first, but it's dragged on for long enough that it isn't funny any more." Well, what does she suggest be done? "I don't know, which is why I'm worrying. Knowing my idiot brother, he might very well decide to go out there once again to try and prove himself or something, live up to Daddy's name. Difference between Daddy and him is that Daddy had the whole of Mommy's mercenary company backing him up, and Garret's got just his own two hands. "It wasn't very safe out there to begin with, be it in Harvest Valley or the Old Forest, and things have only gotten worse since... since the storm. Maybe since you were the one who got him out of that fix, he might be willing to listen to you — more than he would to his baby sister." You'll see what you can do about that. "Thank you, [pc.name]. I know it may not seem it when I talk about him, but Garret's my big brother, after all. I can sniff out every inch of his hide, and I'm pretty sure he respects you a whole lot for getting him home safely, even if he won't 'fess up and say it out loud." ] |"I... well, there's not much to really say at the moment. Garret's still been missing since the snowstorm the day you came into town, and Daddy's been worried sick over him since then. I suppose if anyone's skilled at surviving out in the Old Forest it'd be Garret, but he's been gone for so long that things aren't looking good." Both she and Garth look quite blase about it, if she doesn't mind you saying. "Well, what did you expect? We can't let the fact that Big Brother's missing stop our lives. So long as there isn't a body, there's still hope, but we're not going to sit around doing nothing." You'll let her know if you come across any hearsay of her brother, then. Gwyn waves you off. "If you want to do that, then please speak to Daddy about it. I... I don't want to get my hopes up for nothing after so long." ] "
