I was worried she wouldn't be used to leaving the comforts of the temple for some rural locale, but Caitriss really came through with trying to one-up some of the grandest Jassiran temples around. "I don't exactly know what'll happen to us after enough years have gone by, but at least I have hope that it'll be good. We've gotten off on the right foot so far, and that means a lot in the long run." ] "

rows.translation: 他的妹妹

rows.original: [rand |"Ah, right. Mr. Zethra was always traveling all over not just Jassira, but the world — when he visited our temple, he sometimes had Cait and Calla in tow. I don't think the twins were actually allowed to leave the temple until they came of age, their parents being who they were and all, but Mr. Zethra managed to get them out anyway and take them around Jassira with him on short trips. I guess they figured it was all right if it was their dad doing it and he was just taking them from temple to temple. "I still remember it — Amina was playing the harp on stage when Cait and Calla were dragged into the place by Mr. Zethra, who just wanted to rest his feet for a while. Calla was quiet, but Cait hit it off with Amina immediately; the moment the number was over, she went up and started gushing about how great the music was. At the time, I thought she was just another adoring fan about to get in my sister's way and was about to remove her, but Amina told me to hold, that she wanted to listen to what this girl had to say." You [pc.isChamp |smile |snort ]. Yeah, Cait does tend to have that effect on people — comes with being so bubbly, cheerful and above all, earnest. With an attitude like that, you guess it only made sense that they would hit it off quite well. "Many people want to get close to the singers and dancers, always with ulterior motives — hoping a bit of that fame rubs off on them, if nothing else. Caitriss... didn't have that. Oh, that didn't stop me from keeping an eye on her, but she came and visited again, and again, and again over the years, sometimes as often as once a month or once every two months. Long enough for the girls to catch up, but not so long that the novelty of her and her sister's presence would wear off, for them to outstay their welcome by the ocean. "Eventually, I had to figure that Cait really didn't mean my sister any ill, that her offer of friendship to my sister was as genuine as these things get. And though she could only come by as often as her father would bring her, Amina nevertheless looked forward to each and every one of her visits." |Did Imad and his sister know Calla? "You don't know her, huh." Not personally. Cait always likes to talk about her sister, but the most you saw of Calla was for a few moments before she was brought into that portal that night. Imad and Amina must've known her though, right? "Mostly as Cait's sister. The girl was taciturn and unassuming — not so much because she was a quiet, mousy thing or anything of the likes, but you always got the feeling that she was giving you the cold shoulder. I stopped paying attention to her as soon as I was sure that sour attitude of hers wasn't going to spoil things for Amina." ...Huh. Given what Cait's told you of her sister and from various mentions, you figured a younger Calla would've been more than happy to go on a trip with her family... "Well, it was from one temple to another. It probably wasn't much of a change from one to the other, and the city beyond the temple enclosure wasn't a place for young girls who weren't familiar with the place to go wandering off into. Even she understood as much, if the expression on her face whenever she looked at her dad told me anything; I still remember it after all these years. Maybe I was wrong, but the way she would look at Mr. Zethra made me feel like she was spoiled rotten, which just made me want to have even less to do with her." You look over your shoulder, half-expecting to find Cait [party.has cait |about to protest her sister being badmouthed, but your pink kitten's instead wandered off to a nearby low table where several catfolk have engaged her in what by all appearances is quite the banal conversation |having been listening in on your conversation all this while, but contrary to all expectations she's not there ]. You breathe a small sigh of relief, then turn back to Imad for him to finish the rest of his tale. "Since you asked me honestly, I'll give you an honest answer, [pc.name]. Calla always struck me as the kind of kitten who insisted on rebelling for its own sake, and not because there was any kind of cause to champion; she insisted on being contrary for its own sake, and it showed. Amina and I, we understand that while some of the problems in our lives came from the temple, its hierarchy and the way things were done, we also got a lot of good out of it. Calla's stance on the whole thing was far more reactionary, and from where I stand, a lot more petulant. She didn't like Amina because she danced and sang for the temple as a girl... I could tell. I'm not going to say I'm unperturbed by the fact that she's gone, but that's mostly because Cait cares about her and that's it." |"Oh yes, I know Mr. Zethra. Every relative of the reigning sultan or sultana, no matter how distant, gets quite the royal treatment when they step into any temple — the ties between the religious and secular authorities go back generations, to the point where one could unironically call them one big happy family," Imad says with a smile that could easily have been a grimace. "Whenever Mr. Zethra visited, we were always told to be quiet and respectful — kind of hard to do when he's the kind of jolly fat guy he's always been, even when he was younger." It's hard to imagine Barney being young, but with enough effort... "It helps if you're young at heart all the time, and Mr. Zethra never seemed to lose that childish curiosity that dominated his personality all the while. I guess it helped that he was low enough on the ladder that no one really cared about him, and his position was more make-work than anything, an excuse for him to travel and indulge his curiosities at the sultanate's expense. A small price to pay for keeping the outer family at bay and from greater ambitions, I suppose." It's hard to imagine Barney with greater ambitions and ulterior motives, but you can understand the sentiment. He's certainly an edge case when it comes to these things[pc.bg noblescion |, a fact that you personally know all too well ]. "He'd do little magic shows for the children when he was around. Only they weren't magic — well, mostly so. He was always careful to explain that it was a lot of alchemy, smoke and mirrors instead of what people usually think of when magic is mentioned, but the end result was the same anyway. Either way, he was so much more fun than most of the visitors we usually got, and no one would say no to him, so we usually would have half the day off to indulge his flights of fancy when dealing with the temple children. "It feels a little strange, to be thinking back to those days, and now I'm here in his daughter's temple keeping the crowds in check. I guess in a way, Amina and I are paying him back for what he did for us." |"Given that our temple was in a port city, sometimes Mr. Zethra would come and drop off Cait and Calla here for a while, and then he'd go overseas to do... whatever it is he does when he's not on official business, I'm not sure. If he was supposed to be gone a couple weeks or so, he'd return and collect the sisters before heading on home, otherwise, our temple would send someone to bring them back to their mother." Was that allowed? "Well, by all rights it wasn't, but a reasonable donation to the temple's coffers always got the relevant people to bend the rules and look the other way for a spell. It wasn't as if letting the Zethra twins stay with us a bit was going against some iron creed, and the main reason that they were watched so closely was that their father was a big shot, after all. If something happened to the sisters on a stay that he himself wanted the rules bent for, then the Temple wasn't going to be liable for them. "Me... well, Calla was always cold to me, but Cait was always looking out for Amina and keeping her away from trouble; it happened a good number of times over the years. Even though I'm Amina's older brother, I can't always be there to fish her out of trouble, and I really appreciated Cait being around. It's the memories of Caitriss being the more sensible one and always taking care of my sister that led me to conclude that maybe coming all the way here to this corner of the world would be worth leaving the relative comfort and safety of our temple for, would be worth making the trip over the ocean." Would Amina have obeyed if he'd said no? You don't think so, but... "It'd be reasonable to think that way, but if I hadn't been sure that any temple that Caitriss ran would be a better one for her mind and soul than the one we lived in? Yes. She'd have cried, she'd have protested, but at the end of the day she'd have seen reason. That's how it's always worked out between Amina and me since we were kids. And knowing that Caitriss is there to be the voice of reason when I'm not around gives me that peace of mind that lets me do my job all the better." |Was Barney always such a jolly person back in the day? Imad smiles at that. "Oh yes, every bit the character — and caricature — that he loves to be. He was even fatter in those days, too, when his body could afford to shovel all kinds of rich food into his face. But I liked him, not just for his magic snows, not just for Cait and Calla who'd come in tow, but also because the temple staff would get off our backs when he arrived. Amina loved listening to his stories, too, but I personally didn't care very much for those. Still, he was a fun character to be around." And the whole most major of the minor pregidistitators schtick... "Still running it ten-odd years ago, yes. It's a shame he's getting up there in years — for all the energy that his spirit has, I can tell that his body's starting to have trouble keeping up. Salwah's been cooking him more sensible meals when he deigns to eat at the temple — more nourishment and less nonsense. The day he leaves us... I don't say this of many people, really, but I'll feel his loss." ]
rows.translation: [rand |“啊，对了。泽特拉先生总是四处旅行，不仅在贾西拉，还在世界各地——他来我们神庙的时候，有时会带着凯特和卡拉一起来。我觉得，鉴于他们父母的身份，这对双胞胎在成年之前其实是不被允许离开神庙的；可泽特拉先生还是想办法把她们带了出去，带着她们在贾西拉一带做了几次短途旅行。我猜她们觉得，既然是自己的父亲这么做，那就没什么问题——反正他只是把她们从一座神庙带到另一座神庙而已。” “我至今还记得那一幕——当凯特和卡拉被泽特拉先生拽进那个地方的时候，阿米娜还在舞台上弹奏竖琴，而他只是想歇歇脚罢了。卡拉很安静，但凯特立刻就和阿米娜聊得火热；一曲刚结束，她就走上前，开始滔滔不绝地称赞那音乐有多棒。当时我以为她不过是又一个狂热的粉丝，只会妨碍我妹妹，正打算把她赶走，可阿米娜让我等等——她说她想听听这个女孩有什么要说的。” 你[pc.isChamp |微笑 |哼了一声 ]。是啊，凯特确实常常对别人产生这种影响——毕竟她那么活泼、开朗，最重要的是，那么认真。带着这样的性子，你会觉得她们相处得那么投机也是理所当然的。 “很多人都想接近那些歌手和舞者，总是怀着不可告人的目的——哪怕只是盼着能沾上一点她们的名气也好。凯特丽丝……并没有那种心思。哦，这倒也没能让我不再留意她。这些年来，她一次又一次地来拜访，有时甚至一个月来一次，或者每两个月来一次。这时间够长，足以让女孩们叙叙旧，却又不会长到让她和她妹妹的出现失去新鲜感，不会长到让她们在海边待得惹人厌烦。” “最终，我不得不承认，凯特对我妹妹确实没有半点恶意，她向我妹妹表达的友谊已经真诚到不能再真诚了。虽然她只能趁她父亲带她来的时候才能过来，但阿米娜依然期待着她的每一次到访。” |伊马德和他妹妹认识卡拉吗？ “你并不认识她，对吧。” 算不上亲自认识。凯特总是喜欢谈起她的妹妹，但那晚你看到卡拉的时间，也只是在她被带进那道传送门之前的短短片刻而已。不过伊马德和阿米娜肯定认识她吧？ “主要是作为凯特的妹妹。那姑娘沉默寡言、不事张扬——倒不是因为她是个安静、胆怯的小东西之类，而是你总觉得她在冷淡地对待你。等我确信她那种乖戾的态度不会坏了阿米娜的事之后，我就不再留意她了。” ……嗯。考虑到凯特跟你讲过的关于她妹妹的事，以及你听来的各种说法，你本来以为年轻些的卡拉应该会很乐意和家人一起出门旅行…… “嗯，那也不过是从一座神庙到另一座神庙而已。两处之间大概也没什么分别，而神庙围墙外的那座城市，也不是不熟悉那里的小姑娘该独自乱逛的地方。这一点连她自己都明白——如果她看父亲时的表情能说明什么的话；过了这么多年，我至今还记得。也许是我错了，但她看泽特拉先生的那种眼神，让我觉得她被宠坏到了骨子里，这只会让我更不想和她有任何牵扯。” 你回头张望，半心以为会看到凯特[party.has cait |正要抗议有人诋毁她妹妹，结果你的粉色小猫却跑到了附近的一张矮桌旁，几只猫族正拉着她聊着一些看样子相当无聊的话题 |其实一直都在旁听你们的谈话，但出乎所有意料，她并不在那里 ]。你轻轻松了口气，然后又转回伊马德，让他把剩下的故事讲完。 “既然你诚实地问我，那我就给你一个诚实的回答，[pc.name]。卡拉给我的印象，一直是那种为了反抗而反抗的小猫，并不是因为有什么值得捍卫的主张；她执意要事事唱反调，而且表现得很明显。阿米娜和我都明白，我们生活里的有些问题确实来自神庙、来自它的等级制度和行事方式，但我们也从中得到了很多好处。卡拉对这一切的立场要反动得多，在我看来也任性得多。她不喜欢阿米娜，只因为阿米娜年少时曾为神庙唱歌跳舞……我看得出来。我不会说她的离世对我毫无触动，但那主要是因为凯特在乎她，仅此而已。” |“哦，是的，我认识泽特拉先生。现任苏丹或苏丹娜的每一位亲属，无论关系多疏远，只要踏进任何一座神庙，都会受到极高的礼遇——宗教与世俗当权者之间的纽带已经延续了好几代人，到了人们完全可以毫不讽刺地称他们为一个快乐的大家庭的地步，”伊马德说着，脸上那个笑容怎么看都像是苦笑。“每次泽特拉先生来访，我们都被告知要安静、要毕恭毕敬——可他一直是那种快活的胖家伙，哪怕年轻时候也一样，这可实在有点难为人。” 很难想象巴尼年轻时的样子，不过只要足够努力…… “如果你一直保持一颗年轻的心，那就有帮助了，而泽特拉先生似乎从未丢掉那种主宰着他整个性子的孩子气好奇心。我想这也有赖于他的地位够低，根本没人真正在意他，他那个职位更多是给他找点事做，只是个借口，让他能花苏丹国的钱到处旅行、满足自己的好奇心。要我说，用这点代价把外姓家族挡在外面、不让他们生出更大的野心，倒也划算。” 很难想象巴尼会有什么更大的野心或不可告人的目的，但你能理解这份心情。在这类事情上，他确实是个特例[pc.bg noblescion |，这一点你本人再清楚不过了 ]。 “他在的时候，会给孩子们变些小戏法。只不过那并不是魔法——嗯，大体上不是。他总是小心地解释说，那其实是炼金术、障眼法和烟雾罢了，并不是人们提到魔法时通常想到的那些东西，但最终效果反正都一样。不管怎么说，他比我们平常接待的大多数访客都有趣得多，而且没人会拒绝他，所以应付神庙里的孩子时，我们常常能放半天假，由着他尽情发挥那些奇思妙想。” “回想起那些日子，感觉有点奇怪；而如今我竟然在他女儿的神庙里，维持着人群的秩序。我想，从某种意义上说，阿米娜和我是在报答他为我们做过的一切。” |“由于我们的神庙在一座港口城市，有时泽特拉先生会把凯特和卡拉送到我们这里待一阵子，然后他就出海去办……他公务之外做的那些事吧，我也不太清楚。如果他估计要走两周左右，就会回来接上姐妹俩再回家；不然的话，我们神庙就会派人把她们送回她们母亲那里。” 那样做是被允许的吗？ “嗯，按理说是不允许的，但给神庙的金库捐一笔合情合理的款项，总能让管事的那些人破个例、睁一只眼闭一只眼一阵子。让泽特拉家这对双胞胎在我们这儿住上一阵，又不是在违背什么铁律；而她们之所以被看得那么紧，说到底还是因为她们的父亲是个大人物。如果姐妹俩在他本人要求破例的这次寄住期间出了什么事，那神庙也不必为她们负责。” “我……嗯，卡拉对我一直很冷淡，但凯特总是照顾着阿米娜，让她远离麻烦；这些年来这种事发生过很多次。虽然我是阿米娜的哥哥，但我不可能总在她身边把她从麻烦里捞出来，所以我真的很感激有凯特在。正是这些关于凯特丽丝更为明事理、总是照顾我妹妹的记忆，让我得出这样的结论：也许，一路来到世界的这个角落，值得离开我们神庙里那份相对的舒适与安稳，值得漂洋过海走这一趟。” 如果他当时拒绝了，阿米娜还会听他的话吗？你觉得不会，但是…… “那样想也合情合理，但要不是我确信，只要是凯特丽丝经营的神庙，对她的心智与灵魂来说都会胜过我们原先居住的那一座，我还会这么选吗？会的。她会哭，会抗议，但到最后她还是会明白道理的。从小到大，阿米娜和我之间一直都是这样解决的。而知道我不在的时候有凯特丽丝在那里充当理智的声音，这份安心让我能把自己的职责做得更好。” |当年的巴尼一直都是这么个快活的人吗？ 伊马德听到这话笑了。“哦，是的，他完全就是他自己喜欢扮演的那个角色——也是那副夸张的漫画形象。当年他还更胖些，那时候他的身体还经得起把各种肥甘厚味往嘴里塞。可我喜欢他，不只是因为他那些魔法雪景，也不只是因为跟着他来的凯特和卡拉，还因为他一到，神庙的管事们就不会再来烦我们了。阿米娜也爱听他讲故事，不过我本人对那些故事并不怎么感兴趣。但他终归是个有趣的家伙。” 还有那套“次等预言师里最了不起的一位”的把戏…… “十多年前他还在玩那一套，没错。可惜他年岁渐长，这实在令人惋惜——他的精神无论多有活力，我也看得出他的身体开始跟不上了。只要他肯赏脸在神庙里吃饭，萨尔瓦就一直给他做些更合宜的饭菜——更有营养，少些胡闹。等到他离开我们那天……我很少对人这么说，但我真的会想念他。” ]

Every relative of the reigning sultan or sultana, no matter how distant, gets quite the royal treatment when they step into any temple — the ties between the religious and secular authorities go back generations, to the point where one could unironically call them one big happy family," Imad says with a smile that could easily have been a grimace. "Whenever Mr. Zethra visited, we were always told to be quiet and respectful — kind of hard to do when he's the kind of jolly fat guy he's always been, even when he was younger." It's hard to imagine Barney being young, but with enough effort... "It helps if you're young at heart all the time, and Mr. Zethra never seemed to lose that childish curiosity that dominated his personality all the while. I guess it helped that he was low enough on the ladder that no one really cared about him, and his position was more make-work than anything, an excuse for him to travel and indulge his curiosities at the sultanate's expense. A small price to pay for keeping the outer family at bay and from greater ambitions, I suppose." It's hard to imagine Barney with greater ambitions and ulterior motives, but you can understand the sentiment. He's certainly an edge case when it comes to these things[pc.bg noblescion |, a fact that you personally know all too well ]. "He'd do little magic shows for the children when he was around. Only they weren't magic — well, mostly so. He was always careful to explain that it was a lot of alchemy, smoke and mirrors instead of what people usually think of when magic is mentioned, but the end result was the same anyway. Either way, he was so much more fun than most of the visitors we usually got, and no one would say no to him, so we usually would have half the day off to indulge his flights of fancy when dealing with the temple children. "It feels a little strange, to be thinking back to those days, and now I'm here in his daughter's temple keeping the crowds in check. I guess in a way, Amina and I are paying him back for what he did for us." |"Given that our temple was in a port city, sometimes Mr. Zethra would come and drop off Cait and Calla here for a while, and then he'd go overseas to do... whatever it is he does when he's not on official business, I'm not sure. If he was supposed to be gone a couple weeks or so, he'd return and collect the sisters before heading on home, otherwise, our temple would send someone to bring them back to their mother." Was that allowed? "Well, by all rights it wasn't, but a reasonable donation to the temple's coffers always got the relevant people to bend the rules and look the other way for a spell. It wasn't as if letting the Zethra twins stay with us a bit was going against some iron creed, and the main reason that they were watched so closely was that their father was a big shot, after all. If something happened to the sisters on a stay that he himself wanted the rules bent for, then the Temple wasn't going to be liable for them. "Me... well, Calla was always cold to me, but Cait was always looking out for Amina and keeping her away from trouble; it happened a good number of times over the years. Even though I'm Amina's older brother, I can't always be there to fish her out of trouble, and I really appreciated Cait being around. It's the memories of Caitriss being the more sensible one and always taking care of my sister that led me to conclude that maybe coming all the way here to this corner of the world would be worth leaving the relative comfort and safety of our temple for, would be worth making the trip over the ocean." Would Amina have obeyed if he'd said no? You don't think so, but... "It'd be reasonable to think that way, but if I hadn't been sure that any temple that Caitriss ran would be a better one for her mind and soul than the one we lived in? Yes. She'd have cried, she'd have protested, but at the end of the day she'd have seen reason. That's how it's always worked out between Amina and me since we were kids. And knowing that Caitriss is there to be the voice of reason when I'm not around gives me that peace of mind that lets me do my job all the better." |Was Barney always such a jolly person back in the day? Imad smiles at that. "Oh yes, every bit the character — and caricature — that he loves to be. He was even fatter in those days, too, when his body could afford to shovel all kinds of rich food into his face. But I liked him, not just for his magic snows, not just for Cait and Calla who'd come in tow, but also because the temple staff would get off our backs when he arrived. Amina loved listening to his stories, too, but I personally didn't care very much for those. Still, he was a fun character to be around." And the whole most major of the minor pregidistitators schtick... "Still running it ten-odd years ago, yes. It's a shame he's getting up there in years — for all the energy that his spirit has, I can tell that his body's starting to have trouble keeping up. Salwah's been cooking him more sensible meals when he deigns to eat at the temple — more nourishment and less nonsense. The day he leaves us... I don't say this of many people, really, but I'll feel his loss." ] "

rows.original:
[rand
        |"Our temple was in one of the biggest port cities by the coast," Imad muses. "There were always people coming and going, not just from within Jassira but also from foreign lands. Strange people, strange clothes, strange mannerisms, strange ideas — it was a house, but neither my sister nor I could ever really think of it as home. There was simply no sense of familiarity, that a home should have. People would come into the temple and try to pay for services with foreign currency that weren't hawks, and would get gently but firmly refused; this happened at least twice a week despite the proclamation clearly written by the entrance in Belharan. Maybe they couldn't read."
        
        ...Literacy is a skill that one takes for granted. [pc.bg acolyte scholar noblescion arcanist
            |Given your background, you had the chance to learn, but that can't be said for most people
            |Given your humble background, having learned to read and write was nothing short fo a small miracle, and you're glad you got the chance to do so. This whole quest would be a lot more troublesome without being literate
        ].
        
        "It was also the biggest slave market in the country," Imad adds with a rueful grin. "The unfortunate would be driven in from the insides of Jassira to the coast, where they would be sold to foreigners for the highest bidder; no one at those markets were seeking to buy for personal use, they were all wholesalers dealing in flesh. Well, mostly to foreigners — ships lined the docks every day, waiting for their cargo to be driven up on deck. That's how catfolk were spread all over the world, you know."
        
        The way he's speaking of it as if it was a fact of life... 
        
        "It was. You couldn't pass by the waterfront without hearing the markets about their business. The poor souls for sale were mostly Tronariians taken in skirmishes, or people who couldn't pay their debts. Debts, I might add, to anubian moneylenders. They'd spit at my feet, Amina's feet when we went out of the temple on business, ignoring the fact that it was another catfolk holding their bindings, but that's life for you.
        
        "If you were a certain kind of person, I guess it might've been a nice place, a vibrant place, a city that never slept. Amina absolutely loathed the place, and didn't want to step out of the temple compound unless she absolutely had to. Me, I couldn't be worked up about it all the way she was, but even so I always made sure to wash out my mouth every time I walked the streets."
        |"It was an okay place to live, I guess, an okay place to grow up in; there were worse places where Amina and I could have grown up. For all of Jassira's shortcomings, it was less touched by the Godswar than other places, and I'm thankful for that. Amina may have complained about our temple upbringing, but it gave us things that most people didn't have the fortune to acquire like an education."
        
        And the sultana?
        
        "No one really thinks about the sultana, they're more interested in the tax collector who shakes them down in her name. Even throughout the reign of the so-called mad sultana who kept on changing the laws every other day, most of the officials just ignored her edicts and kept on as they'd been doing for the last century or two. That's just the reality of things — inasmuch as someone in an oasis village cares about her, she's just a face on a coin.
        
        "Sure, there's trouble. Sure, there're shortcomings. But everywhere has these problems, and it's up to you to pick which ones you're more comfortable with tackling. Amina couldn't handle the pressures of the big city, and is happier here, that's not to say that Hawkethorne, the Marches or even this temple don't have their own little problems."
        
        You give Imad a weak grin. Don't you know it.
        
        "I can't speak for Amina, but for most of my life I've more or less felt rootless. Like... like a breath of desert wind, blown from place to place. Anubians are supposed to be a tight-knit racial community in Jassira, but we never had the opportunity to be a part of that. Here, at least, I don't have that feeling, which is maybe the most important change I've felt in my whole life, and I like it." He thumbs over his shoulder at Amina on the stage. "And judging by how beautifully she plays these days, I believe my sister agrees, even if she won't say it to your face."
        |"To be honest, I only know very much about a little corner of Jassira. There's a whole stretch of the country I'd once hoped to at least pass through as a merc — oases, dunes, cliffsides, the grand river valley that flows through the mudflats and deltas before rushing out to the sea — but fact is, before Amina and I left for the Marches, we'd never even set foot beyond the city, and most of the time we didn't leave the temple compound. It was interesting listening to petitioners talk about their travels as they cleaned off the sand from their shoes, but unlike Amina, I was always aware of how actually dangerous the world out there was, and how sheltered our lives in the temple were. It's part of why I eventually decided that I'd to accompany her on the trip all the way to this corner of the world; there was no way she was going to make it alone."
        
        Of course, there wasn't any way he was going to tell her that to her face, was there?
        
        Imad smiles wryly. "Actually I did. Amina was huffy for a bit, then admitted that I was right. But there's a lot to Jassira that even the people who live there don't really know anything about save for stories, and I'd say that's true for most people who live anywhere. From the temple we lived in, Jassira was the smell of the ocean and rotting fish on the docks, the constant lights of the streets even at night, the cry of the slave auctions at dawn. It was the seedy alleys which were actually safer than the main thoroughfares, the wholesale markets, the smell of spice bread fresh out of the oven in the morning from the bakery next to the temple. 
        
        "I guess if you want to hear about that part of Jassira, you're more than welcome to ask, but I don't really know very much about what comes to mind when most people think of the nation — endless dunes under the scorching sun coupled with the gold-plated minarets of the palaces and all. But if you want to ask about the various flavors of spice beer that were made by the breweries around where I lived, I can tell you all about them."
        |"First-time visitors would always double-take a little when they saw Amina and me around. There's nothing against anubians serving Mallach — everyone knows that it happens to sate people with certain tastes, it's just something that you hear about that happens far away and not something you ever expect to encounter in person. Do you get what I'm saying?"
        
        Kind of the way how you always thought demons were a safely distant thing until they were up in your face.
        
        "I guess. Temple and sultanate are one big happy family at this point, have been for generations, which means it's mostly catfolk. But you can see it when they look at you — it's not revulsion, not anything to say what you're doing is wrong, it's just... well, surprise. 'Why are you here? Aren't you supposed to be overseeing to spice caves, or arguing someone's case in court, or running a mercantile exchange?'
        
        "Of course, they changed their minds pretty quick, especially if they wound up with my cock inside of them. But point being that in Jassira, who you are creates expectations on what you're supposed to do with yourself. That isn't necessarily a bad thing — most people either go along to get along, or don't have the ability to plan for themselves and just go and do things according to what society tells them to. It's a good thing to have a plan that most people can follow. Of course, for the people who can't do that for some reason or the other, or want to do something different..."
        
        As far as you can tell, he and Amina came out ahead.
        
        "Despite our slow start, we were lucky and also able to take the initiative when opportunity presented itself — for example, leaving our home temple and coming up here. But I'm not going to pretend that everyone is brave enough, smart enough, strong enough or lucky enough to do what we did. And for that, having a life set out before you can be comforting; too many choices can be paralyzing. And for those who can do it... we did it anyway. It's a different way of doing things than up here, but that's only to be expected, given that the people in the Marches are different and different people need different ways of doing things." 
        |What's the thing he misses most about Jassira?
        
        "Being able to have a nice drink of spice coffee at the bakery just outside the temple every morning."
        
        ...That's it?
        
        "Yes."
        
        What about... uh, the culture? The music? The history? The people? The way of life? The things that make Jassira what it is?
        
        Imad shrugs. "Is that what foreigners think that's what makes the jewel of the desert shine?"
        
        More than, you don't know, some kind of beverage you've never heard of?
        
        "I don't know, [pc.name] — despite having been raised in the temple and trained to carry out duties within, I'm a fairly simple man. And one of the best things to happen every day was to walk out to the bakery that was next to the temple, sit down, and have a nice cup of thick spice coffee on top of the breakfast served in the temple refectory. I'd make the cup stretch for half an hour, maybe the full hour, make small talk with the people passing by.
        
        "All of them were familiar faces, yet they never knew my name, and I didn't know theirs. That was okay, we'd make small talk about parts of our lives that we'd never get to experience from the other side. I don't know about art or history, or if my way of life was very special; familiarity breeds contempt and all that. But I guess you're right in that I did know the people I'd mingle with while having my spice coffee."
        
        If he wants to, he can go down to the Frost Hound for a drink... 
        
        Imad shakes his head. "No, that's different. The atmosphere's different, what can and can't be talked about is different, the people are different. And most importantly, I don't belong there. Everyone's friendly, but I can tell it's not somewhere I belong. And besides, coffee doesn't exist here. Trust me, I asked Mr. Zethra. Soil's too cold, air's too crisp; the seeds won't sprout. Maybe someday I'll get my hands on some... but not today. And even so, it won't be the same."
    ]
rows.translation:
[rand
        |我们的寺庙位于海岸边最大的港口城市之一，”伊马德沉思道，“那里总是人来人往，不仅有来自贾西拉国内的人，还有来自外国的人。那些人穿着奇怪的衣服，有着奇怪的举止和想法……那确实是一个家，但我和我的妹妹却从来都无法真正将其视为自己的家。这里完全缺乏那种家应该具有的亲切感。人们会走进这座寺庙，试图用非鹰币的外币来支付各种费用，但总会被温和而坚定地拒绝；尽管贝尔哈兰的入口处清楚地写着相关说明，这种情况每周至少会发生两次。也许他们不识字。”

……识字是一项人们往往认为理所当然的能力。 [pc.bg acolyte scholar noblescion arcanist
            |以你的背景来说，你确实有机会学习，但大多数人可就没有这样的机会了。
            |考虑到你出身卑微，能够学会读写简直就是个小小的奇迹，你也很庆幸自己有机会获得这样的机会。如果没有识字能力，整个任务将会困难许多。
        ]那里也是全国最大的奴隶市场，”伊马德带着一丝懊悔的笑容补充道，“那些不幸的人会被从贾西拉的内陆地区驱赶到海岸边，在那里他们会被卖给出价最高的外国人；那些市场上没有人是出于个人需求购买奴隶的，他们都是从事奴隶交易的批发商。嗯，主要是运往国外的。每天都有船只停靠在码头，等待将货物运上船舱。就是这样，猫族族才遍布了世界各地的，你知道的。
        
        他谈论这件事的方式，就好像这是生活中理所当然的事情一样……

“确实如此。只要你走过海滨地区，就肯定会听到那些商贩们谈论自己的生意。那些被拍卖的可怜人，大多是在小冲突中被俘的特罗纳里人，或者是那些无力偿还债务的人。而这些债务，往往是欠给阿努比亚放债者的。每当我们出于公务从神庙出来时，那些放债者会朝我们的足部吐口水——其实真正束缚他们的，其实是另一个猫族种族，但这就是你们的生活啊。
        
        如果你是某种类型的人，我想这个地方可能会变得很美好——一个充满活力、永远不会沉睡的城市。但阿米娜却极其厌恶这个地方，除非万不得已，否则她根本不愿意走出寺庙的范围。至于我，虽然没有她那么强烈的情绪，但每次走在街上时，我都会确保自己漱口干净。
        |我觉得那是个不错的居住之地，也是个适合成长的地方；比起其他一些地方，阿米娜和我能在那里长大已经算是幸运的了。尽管贾西拉有很多不足之处，但这个地方受‘神战’的影响相对较小，为此我感到庆幸。阿米娜可能会抱怨我们在寺庙中长大的经历，但这种成长方式确实让我们获得了大多数人都没有的机会，比如接受教育。
        
        那么苏丹娜呢？

“其实没人真正关心苏丹娜，人们更感兴趣的是那些以她的名义向他们征税的人。即使在那个所谓的‘疯狂苏丹娜’统治期间，她每天都在改变法律，但大多数官员仍然对她颁布的法令置若罔闻，继续照旧行事，就像过去一两个世纪一样。这就是现实——对于一个绿洲村庄里的普通人来说，苏丹娜只不过是硬币上的一张面孔而已。
        
        当然，存在一些问题，也有一些不足之处。但任何地方都会遇到这样的问题，关键在于你要选择那些你更愿意去解决的问题。阿米娜无法承受大城市的压力，所以在这里她过得更开心；但这并不意味着鹰棘镇、边境地区，甚至这座寺庙没有它们自己面临的小问题。
        
        你向伊马德露出一个勉强的微笑。你难道不明白吗？

“我无法代表阿米娜来说话，但在我的大部分人生中，我一直感觉自己没有根，就像一阵沙漠之风，被吹到了这个地方，又吹到了那个地方。在贾西拉，阿努比人本应是一个紧密团结的种族群体，但我们从来就没有机会成为其中的一员。至少在这里，我没有那种感觉，而这或许是我这辈子所经历的最重要的变化，我真的很喜欢这样。”他侧头朝舞台上的阿米娜指了指，“而且从她这些天的演奏水平来看，我相信我的妹妹也同意这一点，尽管她不会当面这么说。"
        |说实话，我对贾西拉这个国家的了解其实非常有限。这片土地上有很多地方，我曾经希望能以雇佣兵的身份至少走一走——那些绿洲、沙丘、悬崖峭壁，还有那条蜿蜒流经沼泽地与三角洲、最终汇入大海的宏伟河流……但事实上，在我和阿米娜离开前往边境地区之前，我们甚至从未踏出过城市的范围，而大部分时间，我们也只是待在神庙的范围内而已。听那些请愿者们一边清理鞋子上的沙子，一边讲述他们的经历，确实挺有意思的。但与阿米娜不同，我一直都很清楚外面的世界其实有多危险，也明白我们在寺庙里的生活是多么安逸。这也是我最终决定陪她一起踏上这段旅程，前往这个世界的角落的原因之一——她绝对不可能独自完成这段旅程。
        
        当然，他不可能当面告诉她这些，对吧？

伊马德苦笑着说道：“其实我告诉她了。阿米娜一开始很生气，但后来还是承认我是对的。不过关于贾西拉，就连住在那里的人也有很多事情并不了解，只能通过一些故事来了解这些情况；我想，对于大多数生活在任何地方的人来说，都是这样的吧。从我们居住的寺庙里，能闻到海风的气息，以及码头上传来的鱼腐烂的味道；夜晚街道上依然亮着灯光，黎明时分还能听到奴隶拍卖的叫卖声。那些破败的小巷其实比主干道更加安全，还有批发市场，以及早晨寺庙旁边面包店里飘出来的新鲜香料面包的香气。 
        
        如果你想了解关于贾西拉的那些方面，随时都可以问我，不过说实话，对于大多数人提到这个国家时所想到的那些景象——炙热阳光下的无边沙丘、宫殿里那些镀金的宣礼塔等等——我其实了解得并不多。不过，如果你想了解我居住地区那些啤酒厂生产的各种香料啤酒，那我完全可以告诉你所有相关信息。
        |初次来到这里的人，看到阿米娜和我在一起时，总会忍不住多看几眼。阿努比亚人为马拉克服务，并没有什么不妥——大家都知道，这种事情确实会发生，而且它能满足某些人的特殊口味。只不过，这种事通常发生在遥远的地方，人们根本不会想到自己会亲眼见到。你明白我的意思吗？
        
        就像你总是以为恶魔是那些遥远而安全的存在，直到它们突然出现在你面前。

“我想也是。在这个时候，神庙和苏丹国已经是一个和谐共处的大家庭了，这种状况已经持续了好几代人，也就是说，那里的居民大多都是猫族。但是当你看到他们看着你的时候，你能感受到那种神情——那并不是厌恶，也不是在指责你的行为有什么不对，只是……嗯，感到惊讶而已。“你为什么会在这里？你不是应该在监管香料矿穴，或者在法庭上为某人辩护，或者经营一家商行吗？'
        
        当然，他们很快就会改变主意，尤其是当我的阴茎进入他们的身体之后。但关键在于，在贾西拉，你的身份会决定人们对你应该如何处理自己的行为抱有怎样的期望。这并不一定是坏事——大多数人要么为了与他人相处而顺应这些期望，要么根本没有能力为自己做出规划，只能按照社会的要求来行事。有一个大多数人都能遵循的计划，当然是件好事。当然，对于那些由于某些原因无法遵循这个计划，或者想要尝试一些不同做法的人来说……
        
        从目前的情况来看，他和阿米娜取得了成功。

“尽管我们起步较慢，但运气也不错，而且在机会出现时也能够抓住主动权——比如，离开我们的家庭寺庙，来到这里。但我并不认为每个人都有足够的勇气、智慧、力量或运气去做出我们所做的事情。因此，当一个人的人生目标已经明确时，这会带来一种安慰感；因为过多的选择反而会让人陷入迷茫，甚至失去行动的能力。而对于那些有能力做到这一点的人……我们还是选择了去做。这里的做事方式与那里不同，但这也在意料之中，因为边境地区的人们与众不同，不同的人自然需要不同的做事方式。" 
        |他最怀念贾西拉的哪一点呢？

“就是每天早上都能在寺庙外面的面包店里喝上一杯美味的香料咖啡。”

……就只有这个吗？

“是的。
        
        那么……呃，文化呢？音乐呢？历史呢？人们呢？生活方式呢？那些让贾西拉成为独一无二的地方的因素呢？

伊马德耸了耸肩：“外国人就是这么认为的吗？他们觉得正是这些因素让这片沙漠中的宝石焕发出光彩吗？难道是某种你从未听说过的饮料吗？

“我不知道[pc.name] — 尽管我在寺庙中长大，也接受了履行寺内职责的训练，但我其实是个非常简单的人。每天最让我开心的事情，就是走到寺庙旁边的面包店，坐下来，一边享用寺庙食堂提供的早餐，一边喝上一杯香浓的香料咖啡。我会慢慢地品尝这杯咖啡，也许会花上半个小时，甚至整整一个小时，同时还会和路过的人闲聊几句。
        
        他们都是我熟悉的面孔，但却从来不知道我的名字，我也不知道他们的名字。这也没关系，我们会聊一些关于自己生活中那些对方永远无法体验到的经历。我不知道艺术或历史是什么，也不清楚我的生活方式是否有什么特别之处；毕竟，熟悉往往会让人产生轻视之情。不过，你说得对，我在喝香料咖啡的时候，确实认识那些与我一起聊天的人。
        
        如果他愿意的话，可以去“寒冰猎犬”酒吧喝一杯……

伊马德摇了摇头：“不行，那不一样。那里的氛围不同，可以谈论的事情也不同，那里的人也不同。最重要的是，我并不属于那里。虽然大家都很友善，但我能感觉到，那并不是属于我的地方。而且，这里根本没有咖啡。相信我，我可是问过泽斯拉先生的。这里的土壤太冷，空气太干燥，种子根本无法发芽。也许有一天我会得到一些……但不是今天。即便如此，那也不会是同样的感觉了。
    ]
rows.raw:
"
    [rand
        |"Our temple was in one of the biggest port cities by the coast," Imad muses. "There were always people coming and going, not just from within Jassira but also from foreign lands. Strange people, strange clothes, strange mannerisms, strange ideas — it was a house, but neither my sister nor I could ever really think of it as home. There was simply no sense of familiarity, that a home should have. People would come into the temple and try to pay for services with foreign currency that weren't hawks, and would get gently but firmly refused; this happened at least twice a week despite the proclamation clearly written by the entrance in Belharan. Maybe they couldn't read."
        
        ...Literacy is a skill that one takes for granted. [pc.bg acolyte scholar noblescion arcanist
            |Given your background, you had the chance to learn, but that can't be said for most people
            |Given your humble background, having learned to read and write was nothing short fo a small miracle, and you're glad you got the chance to do so. This whole quest would be a lot more troublesome without being literate
        ].
        
        "It was also the biggest slave market in the country," Imad adds with a rueful grin. "The unfortunate would be driven in from the insides of Jassira to the coast, where they would be sold to foreigners for the highest bidder; no one at those markets were seeking to buy for personal use, they were all wholesalers dealing in flesh. Well, mostly to foreigners — ships lined the docks every day, waiting for their cargo to be driven up on deck. That's how catfolk were spread all over the world, you know."
        
        The way he's speaking of it as if it was a fact of life... 
        
        "It was. You couldn't pass by the waterfront without hearing the markets about their business. The poor souls for sale were mostly Tronariians taken in skirmishes, or people who couldn't pay their debts. Debts, I might add, to anubian moneylenders. They'd spit at my feet, Amina's feet when we went out of the temple on business, ignoring the fact that it was another catfolk holding their bindings, but that's life for you.
        
        "If you were a certain kind of person, I guess it might've been a nice place, a vibrant place, a city that never slept. Amina absolutely loathed the place, and didn't want to step out of the temple compound unless she absolutely had to. Me, I couldn't be worked up about it all the way she was, but even so I always made sure to wash out my mouth every time I walked the streets."
        |"It was an okay place to live, I guess, an okay place to grow up in; there were worse places where Amina and I could have grown up. For all of Jassira's shortcomings, it was less touched by the Godswar than other places, and I'm thankful for that. Amina may have complained about our temple upbringing, but it gave us things that most people didn't have the fortune to acquire like an education."
        
        And the sultana?
        
        "No one really thinks about the sultana, they're more interested in the tax collector who shakes them down in her name. Even throughout the reign of the so-called mad sultana who kept on changing the laws every other day, most of the officials just ignored her edicts and kept on as they'd been doing for the last century or two. That's just the reality of things — inasmuch as someone in an oasis village cares about her, she's just a face on a coin.
        
        "Sure, there's trouble. Sure, there're shortcomings. But everywhere has these problems, and it's up to you to pick which ones you're more comfortable with tackling. Amina couldn't handle the pressures of the big city, and is happier here, that's not to say that Hawkethorne, the Marches or even this temple don't have their own little problems."
        
        You give Imad a weak grin. Don't you know it.
        
        "I can't speak for Amina, but for most of my life I've more or less felt rootless. Like... like a breath of desert wind, blown from place to place. Anubians are supposed to be a tight-knit racial community in Jassira, but we never had the opportunity to be a part of that. Here, at least, I don't have that feeling, which is maybe the most important change I've felt in my whole life, and I like it." He thumbs over his shoulder at Amina on the stage. "And judging by how beautifully she plays these days, I believe my sister agrees, even if she won't say it to your face."
        |"To be honest, I only know very much about a little corner of Jassira. There's a whole stretch of the country I'd once hoped to at least pass through as a merc — oases, dunes, cliffsides, the grand river valley that flows through the mudflats and deltas before rushing out to the sea — but fact is, before Amina and I left for the Marches, we'd never even set foot beyond the city, and most of the time we didn't leave the temple compound. It was interesting listening to petitioners talk about their travels as they cleaned off the sand from their shoes, but unlike Amina, I was always aware of how actually dangerous the world out there was, and how sheltered our lives in the temple were. It's part of why I eventually decided that I'd to accompany her on the trip all the way to this corner of the world; there was no way she was going to make it alone."
        
        Of course, there wasn't any way he was going to tell her that to her face, was there?
        
        Imad smiles wryly. "Actually I did. Amina was huffy for a bit, then admitted that I was right. But there's a lot to Jassira that even the people who live there don't really know anything about save for stories, and I'd say that's true for most people who live anywhere. From the temple we lived in, Jassira was the smell of the ocean and rotting fish on the docks, the constant lights of the streets even at night, the cry of the slave auctions at dawn. It was the seedy alleys which were actually safer than the main thoroughfares, the wholesale markets, the smell of spice bread fresh out of the oven in the morning from the bakery next to the temple. 
        
        "I guess if you want to hear about that part of Jassira, you're more than welcome to ask, but I don't really know very much about what comes to mind when most people think of the nation — endless dunes under the scorching sun coupled with the gold-plated minarets of the palaces and all. But if you want to ask about the various flavors of spice beer that were made by the breweries around where I lived, I can tell you all about them."
        |"First-time visitors would always double-take a little when they saw Amina and me around. There's nothing against anubians serving Mallach — everyone knows that it happens to sate people with certain tastes, it's just something that you hear about that happens far away and not something you ever expect to encounter in person. Do you get what I'm saying?"
        
        Kind of the way how you always thought demons were a safely distant thing until they were up in your face.
        
        "I guess. Temple and sultanate are one big happy family at this point, have been for generations, which means it's mostly catfolk. But you can see it when they look at you — it's not revulsion, not anything to say what you're doing is wrong, it's just... well, surprise. 'Why are you here? Aren't you supposed to be overseeing to spice caves, or arguing someone's case in court, or running a mercantile exchange?'
        
        "Of course, they changed their minds pretty quick, especially if they wound up with my cock inside of them. But point being that in Jassira, who you are creates expectations on what you're supposed to do with yourself. That isn't necessarily a bad thing — most people either go along to get along, or don't have the ability to plan for themselves and just go and do things according to what society tells them to. It's a good thing to have a plan that most people can follow. Of course, for the people who can't do that for some reason or the other, or want to do something different..."
        
        As far as you can tell, he and Amina came out ahead.
        
        "Despite our slow start, we were lucky and also able to take the initiative when opportunity presented itself — for example, leaving our home temple and coming up here. But I'm not going to pretend that everyone is brave enough, smart enough, strong enough or lucky enough to do what we did. And for that, having a life set out before you can be comforting; too many choices can be paralyzing. And for those who can do it... we did it anyway. It's a different way of doing things than up here, but that's only to be expected, given that the people in the Marches are different and different people need different ways of doing things." 
        |What's the thing he misses most about Jassira?
        
        "Being able to have a nice drink of spice coffee at the bakery just outside the temple every morning."
        
        ...That's it?
        
        "Yes."
        
        What about... uh, the culture? The music? The history? The people? The way of life? The things that make Jassira what it is?
        
        Imad shrugs. "Is that what foreigners think that's what makes the jewel of the desert shine?"
        
        More than, you don't know, some kind of beverage you've never heard of?
        
        "I don't know, [pc.name] — despite having been raised in the temple and trained to carry out duties within, I'm a fairly simple man. And one of the best things to happen every day was to walk out to the bakery that was next to the temple, sit down, and have a nice cup of thick spice coffee on top of the breakfast served in the temple refectory. I'd make the cup stretch for half an hour, maybe the full hour, make small talk with the people passing by.
        
        "All of them were familiar faces, yet they never knew my name, and I didn't know theirs. That was okay, we'd make small talk about parts of our lives that we'd never get to experience from the other side. I don't know about art or history, or if my way of life was very special; familiarity breeds contempt and all that. But I guess you're right in that I did know the people I'd mingle with while having my spice coffee."
        
        If he wants to, he can go down to the Frost Hound for a drink... 
        
        Imad shakes his head. "No, that's different. The atmosphere's different, what can and can't be talked about is different, the people are different. And most importantly, I don't belong there. Everyone's friendly, but I can tell it's not somewhere I belong. And besides, coffee doesn't exist here. Trust me, I asked Mr. Zethra. Soil's too cold, air's too crisp; the seeds won't sprout. Maybe someday I'll get my hands on some... but not today. And even so, it won't be the same."
    ]
    "

rows.original: "Where'd you hear that?" Imad grunts, his voice suddenly lowering and turning gruff. "From Salwah? From my little sister? Mallach's balls, I guess it doesn't matter." Well, does he? "I... do. Not that I've enjoyed it all the time, but it's a holy duty, and duty means doing things that we may not personally like. But to give you an answer, yes, that's right. It's not my main job here at the temple, but I do stud for those who want a pup put into them. If you want it, there're terms you have to abide by." Similar to those Sally has, you expect. "Similar, but not the same. Studding is less glamorous than surrogacy in the temple hierarchy. I'm not sure why, but I was never one for temple doctrine. But... yes, allow me to explain. "First off, the price. Being less glamorous than surrogacy still leaves room for a lot of fanfare; having a heir sired by holy seed is still meant to be an ostentatious service that people buy to flaunt their wealth. Although some choose to have said heir raised by the temple, unlike the case of surrogacy, it's not required. In the case that you don't want the pup raised in the temple, that'll be around two thousand hawks." Two thousand hawks, huh. "It's the price Mistress Salwah informed me I should be charging should someone raise any interest in the matter. She does control the temple finances, after all." All right, what's next? "Like I said, in the case you don't want your pups raised in the temple, that's perfectly fine and you won't have to pay fifteen thousand hawks for the privilege. I understand you have an arrangement with the matron of the nursery down in the village, so that's presumably where you'll be putting them when they're born. And lastly, there's the matter of... well, pups. Mistress' Salwah's brand ensures that any child she conceives turns out to be a kitten, my brand ensures that they come out as anibian pups." That was frankly expected, what with the portal shenanigans you've been subject to. "Pardon?" Never mind. So that's it? Two thousand hawks, you get to keep the pups? A terse nod. "That's it. Now that I've explained it to you, there's no reason for you to not know. Ask again when you're ready, and we can begin."
rows.translation: “你从哪儿听来的？”伊马德咕哝道，声音突然压低，变得粗哑起来。“从萨尔瓦那儿？还是我妹妹那儿？马拉克的蛋蛋，算了，我想这也无关紧要。” 不过，真的无关紧要吗？ “我……确实会去。倒不是说我每次都乐在其中，但这是一项神圣的职责，而职责就意味着要做那些我们个人也许并不喜欢的事。不过，给你个明确的答复：没错，是这样。配种并不是我在这座神殿里的主要工作，但我确实会为那些想被种上幼崽的人配种。如果你要，就得遵守一些条件。” 和莎莉的那些差不多，你想。 “差不多，但并不一样。在神殿的等级体系里，配种没有代孕那么风光。我也说不清为什么，只是我从来就不吃神殿教义那一套。不过……是的，让我解释一下。” “首先是价钱。虽然不如代孕风光，可讲究的排场依然不少；让神圣的种子为你生下一位继承人，仍被当作一种用来炫耀财富的铺张服务。虽然也有人选择把这位继承人交给神殿抚养，但与代孕不同，这并不是必须的。如果你不打算让幼崽在神殿里长大，那大约要两千枚鹰币。” 两千枚鹰币，是吗。 “这是萨尔瓦女士交代我该收的价，万一有人对这事有兴趣。毕竟，神殿的财务确实由她掌管。” 好吧，接下来呢？ “就像我说的，如果你不希望自己的幼崽在神殿里长大，那完全没问题，你也不必为这个便利支付一万五千枚鹰币。我知道你和村里托儿所的负责人有约定，所以等它们出生以后，你大概会把它们送到那儿去。最后，还有那个问题……嗯，就是幼崽。萨尔瓦女士的烙印能确保她怀上的孩子生下来是猫崽，而我的烙印则能确保它们生出来是阿努比亚幼崽。” 老实说，考虑到你经历过的那些传送门闹剧，这也在意料之中。 “什么？” 没什么。那就这样？两千枚鹰币，幼崽归你？ 他简短地点了点头。“就这样。既然我已经解释清楚了，你也没有理由不知道。等你准备好了再来问，我们就可以开始了。”

        |Imad nods as you voice your desire, and clears his throat. "You know what the donation required is. It doesn't feel like anything's about to happen right now, so I'm willing to be with you, but the temple needs to run and we're on a shoestring budget as things stand. You have the money?"
        |Imad raises an eyebrow at you, folding his arms across his tanned barrel chest to frame the brand tattooed prominently across it; there's little doubt in your mind that this is a motion he's carefully practised time and again for maximum effect, and it shows plainly. "Oh?"
        
        [pc.dcb
            |He can totally go and oh himself, and drop the innocent schtick. It's not like he denies servicing the temple's patrons on the side, either before he arrived here or after.
            
            "No need to get your panties in a twist about it, I was just teasing you," Imad grunts, holding out his hands palms forward
            |What's up with the sudden surprise? It's not like he's ever hidden the fact that he's always been more than a simple bouncer; this is a temple of Mallach, after all.
            
            "I was just teasing, trying to get a rise out of you," Imad replies, grinning
            |Aww, why does he look like that? Wasn't he always, like, totally open about being up for some fun sex?
            
            "Gods, with how eager you are, you'd never make a Mallachite. You'd just give away the goods for free," Imad says with a grin
        ]. "But sure. Things look pretty peaceful around here, so I don't see why I can't head on to the back with you for a bit. If you want to buy my time for a little while, it'll cost you a donation to the temple's coffers."
        
        How much?
        
        "Twenty-five electrum for a romp is the price Salwah's set for me. Fifty electrum, and I'm yours for the next couple of hours — unless, of course, someone starts a fight or something equally stupid. You'll get a refund if that happens, of course, or we can pick up where we left off..."
        
        Twenty-five electrum, huh?
        
        "Twenty-five electrum. I'm a fairly easygoing person, so I'm down for a plethora of things; if you want to fuck or get fucked by a hunky piece of anubian meat, then that's the donation you need to make to the temple. Well? Will you pay?"[party.has cait
            | He glances over at Cait, who's detached herself from you and is talking to one of the girls working the lounge. "It is for the matron and her temple, after all."
        ] 
    ]

        |当你表明自己的愿望时，伊马德点了点头，清了清嗓子。“你知道需要多少捐赠。眼下看起来不像会出什么事，所以我愿意陪你，但神殿得运转，而我们现在手头紧得很。钱带了吗？”
        |伊马德朝你扬起一边眉毛，双臂交叉抱在晒成古铜色的桶状胸膛前，恰好框住那道醒目地纹在胸口的烙印。你毫不怀疑，这个动作是他为了达到最佳效果而反复练过的，而效果一目了然。“哦？”
        
        [pc.dcb
            |他尽管去『哦』他自己好了，别再装那副无辜的样子。他从不否认自己私下也招待神殿的顾客，无论是来这里之前还是之后。
            
            “没必要为这事气得跳脚，我只是逗你玩，”伊马德咕哝道，双手掌心朝前摊开
            |这突如其来的惊讶是怎么回事？他从没掩饰过自己远不只是一个普通保镖；毕竟这里是马拉克的神殿。
            
            “我只是在逗你，想激你一下，”伊马德咧嘴笑着回答
            |哎呀，他为什么是那副表情？他不是一向都很坦率地说自己乐意来点有趣的性爱吗？
            
            “天啊，瞧你这急不可耐的样子，你永远也当不成马拉克信徒。你只会把货白送出去，”伊马德笑着说
        ]。 “不过当然可以。这里看起来挺太平的，所以我看不出有什么理由不能陪你去后面待一会儿。如果你想买我一段时间，就得向神殿的库房捐一笔钱。”
        
        多少钱？
        
        “打一炮二十五枚琥珀金币，这是萨尔瓦给我定的价。五十枚琥珀金币，接下来几个小时我就归你了——当然，除非有人打架或者干出别的同样蠢的事。要是那样，你当然会拿到退款，或者我们可以接着刚才的地方继续……”
        
        二十五枚琥珀金币，是吗？
        
        “二十五枚琥珀金币。我这个人相当随和，很多花样都愿意试；如果你想操一个，或者被一个魁梧的阿努比亚汉子操，那这就是你该向神殿捐的数目。怎么样？你付吗？”[party.has cait

        ]

"I am a monk," he states plainly, "of the Spring Order of Macah."

        A monk? Like the kind you'd see at a temple?
        
        "Ah, somewhat," he answers, "we follow a strict code of honor like your men of the cloth might, but we answer a different calling than they." He starts to smile as he explains. "We aim to make the world a better place through personal discipline, and with that comes training our bodies and minds to both become resilient to outside influence." 
        
        He gestures to the training dummy. "We learn to defend ourselves as part of this, as it is important to keep ourselves safe on our pilgrimages."
        
        You're assuming that's why he's here.
        
        "Of course," he says, "I'm a fusata, if you couldn't tell, and I am far from my home in Macah."
        
        He stands with a proud smile, hands now on his hips.
        
        "But I am just where I belong now!"
        
        Maybe you could ask him about his pilgrimage.

rows.original:
"I'm not sure," he says with an odd bit of confidence. "The purpose of a Spring Order monk's pilgrimage isn't to reach a specific place though. Rather, it is to find somewhere in need of help, and to make a difference, a better world, wherever your path leads you."

            [pc.isDK|Sounds like an aimless journey|Sounds like a noble goal].
            
            "So many would say," he explains, "I find myself stopped in this place. It's honestly not so different from Macah, high and cold. But I feel as though something is wrong here, something that I can help with, my path."
            
            You tell the monk that you yourself are on a quest in this part of the world.
            
            "Maybe we can help each other then," he says with a genuine smile.
            
            Who knows, maybe you'll need a monk on your side in the future... or maybe he'll need you.

rows.original:
"Wanna try using the rack, June?" you say, jabbing your head at it. "It looks complicated but I promise it'll help you get bigger."

        "Uuhh-" June says, glancing between you and the rack before stepping closer to you. "If you want to show me how to use it..."
        
        "Great, let's go then," you say, smiling at him. "Don't worry, you'll be fine."
        
        You teach him how to safely lift the bar over his head though you have to give him some help to do so, gently lowering it down to his shoulders as he huffs and pushes it back up. After that, you get him into a proper squatting stance with his legs spread and back straight, guiding him down until he achieves a deep enough depth and standing back up. This one he actually seems quite good at; his legs might not be muscular, but he's doing a good job of it.
        
        By the time he's done his fur is soaked with sweat and he's panting hard, leaning on the bar for support as you grin.
        
        "That wasn't so bad, was it?" you say, patting him on the back. You can feel how tightly his muscles are wound right now — he really put everything into that. "Good work, June."
        
        "Th- thanks," he puffs, slowly leaning back and moaning. "Okay... I'm going to sit down for a while then go home. Slowly."
        
        "Try not to fall when you walk," you say, nudging him. "See you soon, June."
        
        "Yeah!" he says, wagging his furry tail. "Talk to you later, [pc.name]."
        
        He exits the gym a little gingerly, somewhat humbled but educated by the experience.

"Want a form check on your workouts, June?" you offer.
    
        "Sure!" he chirps, getting under the bar and straightening his back. "Hup-"
        
        June dips downwards and stands back up in a smooth motion, prompting you to nod approvingly. It's not like he's doing it with much weight but that can come later, when he's a bit bigger and more used to it all.         By the time the two of you finish you're both sweaty and breathing hard, though admittedly June is more tired than you are. You spend some time chatting to him before stepping away, leaving him to spread his wings on his own a bit. He doesn't need you hovering over him.

You nod at the bench. "Wanna try the bench some, June? Some variation in your workout is nice."

        He hesitates. "I don't know, it seems a little more complicated and I- I don't want to look silly."
        
        [pc.dcb|"Nonsense," you say, dismissing his concerns with a wave of your wrist. "Get on the bench and I'll show you."|"You'll be fine," you assure him, motioning him over to the bench. "Trust me, I'll help you. It's easy."|"Aw, nah!" you say, bouncing. "You'll be perfectly fine, Junebug! Trust me, I'll be there every step of the way for you!"]
        
        "Weeellll... okay," he says, getting to his feet. "If you promise to show me how..."
        
        You get him to lie down on the bench and patiently talk him through positioning, how to plant his feet in the ground and thrust his back into the bench for extra leverage. To his own surprise he starts lifting the rocks you give him with ease, steadily raising them into the air until you stop him.
        
        "See? It's not so bad," you say, smiling.
        
        "That was easy!" he half-laughs, giddy with success. "I should have done this sooner."
        
        "Don't get too excited just yet, June," you tell him. "Still another four sets to go."
        
        He's definitely worn out by the time you're done with teaching him, but he's happy with what he's done. Turning to you, June smiles gratefully.
        
        "Thanks, [pc.name]. That wasn't so bad, really," he says, sitting down on the bench. "I'm gonna rest then head home. U-uh, if you want to work out together again... I'd be really happy."
        
        "Sure," you say, nodding. The lupine's tail begins to wag through his shorts immediately, brushing across the bench. "We'll get you trained in no time, June. Next time we'll do the bench again, okay?"
        
        He's still a little timid about it all but you're at least getting him to use the 'real weights', like he wanted. You watch him go with a touch of satisfaction before turning back to the equipment.

"This place really is remarkable," Kas says, placing her hands on the temple altar. With night fallen in earnest, you're the only two people in the sanctuary. In a moment, Kasyrra's disguise has melted away, wings unfurling from her back and bones readjusting to her greater, more majestic height. The dagger at her hip becomes her greataxe, caught in hand as her clothes tear free of her more voluptuous figure. The demoness smiles at you, tail curling around your leg. "In my world, there was once a goddess of fertility, but she encouraged loving couplings only for the purposes of breeding. This Mallach god's servants practically yell from the rooftops to take birth control and fornicate as passionately as possible with as many people as will have you. No wonder it's been so easy to conquer in this land. He's all but paved the road for me — had I known a bit more about your pantheon when I set out, I'd have just masqueraded as a Mallachite missionary. Perhaps I ought to borrow little Cait's visage for a bit. Hmm, but I came here for a reason."
    
    Cracking the butt of her axe upon the marble floor, Kas speaks forcefully to the icon of Mallach above you: "Prince of pleasure and lord of lust, I invoke you! Hear me-"
    
    "Not so loud!" a voice behind you shushes. "You'll wake the poor priestesses, silly girl."
    
    You and Kas both whirl around to find a bottom-heavy, raven-haired catboy reclining on the cushions near the stage, wrapped in nothing but sheerest silk around his waist and shoulders. Mallach looks every bit the image of his idols in the temple, small and supple and resting a golden lute across his lap. 
    
    "I hear you, girl," the deity continues, dancing his fingers silently across the strings. "You're not so pathetic as to be beneath the notice of gods, especially when you're so brazen as to invade holy ground once again. Really, the arrogance of it!"
    
    "Silence, godling," Kas snaps, grip tightening around her axe — just for a moment, before she forces herself to relax. "Need I provide a pillow for you to quiet yourself in while I speak my piece?"
    
    Mallach laughs shrilly. "Amazing! I've never seen someone so eager to be smited before. I ought to go fetch Nareva so she can record this for posterity. But do go on, I'm dying of curiosity: why is the so-called demon desecrating yet another of my temples?"
    
    "I come in peace, fool. Indeed, I come bearing an offering for you." Kas rolls her wrist, producing a small sack from the aether and tossing it at Mallach's feet. "What I have taken from you, returned."
    
    The temples' patron gives Kasyrra a suspicious look and spins a finger in the air. The leather strap holding the bag unties itself, and with another gesture, its contents begin to float out. One by one, tiny pink crystals drift up from the ground, forming a little halo around Mallach's brow — perhaps thirty in total. They're the same soulstones as you saw Alissa produce back at the Winter City. Each one makes the god's expression soften, all but marvelling at the gifts.
    
    "What is the meaning of — oh. Ah, I see. The souls of the temple staff you stole away from Khor'minos. What a wicked witch you are, disguising such a daring challenge as an offering. You know full well that I can't refuse, can I?"
    
    "You wouldn't be much of a god if you did," Kas grins. "I will send the demons I made from that lethicite back to your care presently. The question is... can you restore their souls, godling? Are you truly so powerful?"
    
    Mallach looks between you and Kasyrra, the amusement now gone from his face. "Tell me, [pc.title], have you realized what she wants from you yet? Why your demon lover hasn't just ripped that pretty soul out of your chest — or do you truly think a hollow monster like her cares for you?"
    
    A wing wraps around your shoulders. "I care!" Kas snarls, "Marae knows it takes all the restraint I have... but if you're a god of passions, surely you can see the truth of it!"
    
    "Oh, passions, yes, you have more to spare than most. Every time you look at [pc.himHer] I can see your aura burning. But that's not love, is it? You're not even capable of it. Lust, of course, even protectiveness as if [pc.heShe] were your very own property. But you treat [pc.himHer] like a doting puppy, following you around from place to place hoping for scraps at the table of your body. You wouldn't know love if it struck you as surely as one of Sorra's thunderbolts." 
    
    Kas winces as if slapped. 
    
    "So again, I ask you, [pc.name] — you know by now that your soul is unique, steeped in strength from beyond our world. And it's growing ever more powerful, day by day. You know she craves it. Needs it. But for what?"

    卡丝将她的斧头猛力砸在大理石地面上，然后充满力量地对头顶上那尊玛拉赫的神像说道：“愉悦之君，欲望之主，我召唤你！请听我说——”
    
    “别这么大声！”你身后有人轻声提醒道，“你会把那些可怜的女祭司们吵醒的，傻姑娘。
    
    你和卡希一起转过身，发现一个身材矮小、头发呈乌黑的猫人正靠在舞台附近的垫子上休息，他的腰间和肩上只缠着最薄的丝绸。马拉克看起来简直就是寺庙里那些偶像们的翻版——身材娇小灵活，膝上还放着一把金色的琉特琴。 
    
    我明白你的意思，姑娘，”那位神明继续说道，手指轻轻地在琴弦上滑动。“你倒也不至于卑微到连神明都不会注意你，尤其是当你还敢如此大胆地再次闯入圣地的时候。真是厚颜无耻啊！
    
    闭嘴，小神棍，”卡丝厉声说道，手中紧握着斧头——不过只是片刻而已，随后她强迫自己放松下来。“难道我还需要给你准备一个枕头，让你在我说话的时候安静一会儿吗？”
    
    马拉克发出尖锐的笑声：“太不可思议了！我从来没见过有人这么渴望被惩罚。我应该去把娜瑞瓦叫过来，让她把这一幕记录下来，留作后世传颂。不过你继续说吧，我真的太好奇了：这个所谓的恶魔为什么要再次毁坏我的神庙呢？
    
    我是带着和平而来的，傻瓜。事实上，我带来了礼物送给你们。”卡丝转动手腕，从虚空中取出一个小袋子，扔到了马拉克的脚边。“我之前从你那里拿走的东西，现在都还回来了。”
    
    那位神庙的赞助者用怀疑的目光看着卡希拉，然后在空中转了转手指。固定包子的皮带突然松开了，随着另一个动作，包里的物品开始缓缓飘出来。一颗颗小小的粉色水晶从地面升起，围绕着马拉克的额头形成了一个小光环——大概总共有三十颗吧。这些就是你之前在冬城看到艾莉莎制作过的那些灵魂石。每一块都能让神明的表情变得柔和，他们对这些礼物无不感到惊叹。
    
    原来如此——哦，我明白了。你从科尔米诺斯那里偷走的那些神庙工作人员的灵魂，原来如此。你真是个邪恶的女巫，把这么大胆的挑战伪装成一份‘礼物’。你明明知道我不可能拒绝，对吧？”
    
    “如果你真的拒绝了，那你也就算不上什么神明了。”卡希咧嘴笑道，“我马上就会把那些用莱蒂锡特石制造出来的恶魔交还给你。问题在于……你真的有能力恢复他们的灵魂吗，小神明？你真的有那么强大的力量吗？
    
    马拉克将目光在你和卡希拉之间来回移动，他脸上的笑容已经消失了。“告诉我[pc.title]你难道还没明白她真正想要什么吗？为什么你的那个恶魔般的爱人没有直接把你那颗美丽的灵魂从胸腔里扯出来——还是说，你真以为像她这样的空洞怪物会真正关心你？”
    
    一只翅膀搭在了你的肩上。“我在乎！”卡丝咆哮道，“玛莱知道，我是在竭力克制自己……但如果你真的是情感之神，难道你看不出真相吗？”
    
    “哦，情感啊……没错，你确实比大多数人拥有更多的情感。每次你看着[pc.himHer]我能感受到你身上的那种冲动与渴望。但那并不是爱，对吧？你根本不具备爱的能力。有的只是欲望，甚至还有一些保护欲[pc.heShe]那些本应属于你的东西，你却对它们不加珍惜。[pc.himHer]就像一只充满爱意的小狗一样，到处跟着你，希望能从你身上得到一些残羹剩饭。如果爱情像索拉的雷霆一样突然降临到你身上，你可能也根本意识不到它的存在。”
    
    卡希顿时感到一阵刺痛，仿佛被扇了一耳光。
    
    “所以，我再次问你[pc.name] — 你现在应该已经明白，你的灵魂是独一无二的，它蕴含着来自我们世界之外的力量，而且这种力量正在一天天变得更强。你知道，她渴望这种力量，也需要它……但究竟是为了什么呢？

            |pink cat
        ]

rows.original:
Sanders frowns. "That poor girl's been through a lot. I could mend her bruised flesh, but her mind is still tightly-locked."
    
    Locked? Is she unconscious?
    
    "No, but her mouth stays shut and she struggles to move. I tried to talk her out of her torpor, but she only gave me a name: Kira."
    
    [party.has cait
        |"Kira? Is that her name?" Cait asks.
        |Kira? Maybe it's her name?
    ]
    
    "That's what I think, yes. [silly
        |River brought a plushie and asked her to show us where the centaur marauders touched her
        |River and I have managed to get her to wordlessly describe some of what happened to her
    ]. She had it rough, very rough. She also mimicked arcane gestures one of the corrupted individuals made."
    
    Some kind of magic?
    
    Sanders nods. "A very aggressive form of black magic. When I was a young paladin, I battled a couple of powerful sorcerers that used it. Facing a psychic fighter is a jarring experience, so I can't imagine how it was to be under its spell for extended periods of time. Some people stay scarred for life after this kind of incursion into their mind."
    
    Is there anything you can do to help her?
    
    "She is trapped in a prison of her own mind. In my experience, she can either open up all of a sudden or stay silent forever. It's usually not a good idea to pressure her, especially if the control charm isn't properly removed. There's not much we can do, and what little we can do can ruin what little sanity she still has and demolish her trust in us."
    
    [party.has cait
        |Cait steps closer. "We'll do anything."
        |He can count on you.
    ]
    
    Sanders produces a small parchment. "Take this, it's the recipe for [silly
        |Claritea
        |the potion of clarity
    ], a very strong remedy. You'll need fox berries, milk tea, and frostleaf to brew it. Once you have everything, bring them to Ivris. She'll do the heavy lifting for us."
    
    Why doesn't he brew it himself? 
    
    "I'm not an alchemist and potions aren't my forte. We need a professional in this case, and she's the best I know. In the meantime, I'll talk to Kira about our plan. Seeing you all of a sudden with a weird concoction might awaken bad memories. If she goes into a state of shock, all your efforts will be for naught."
    
    You recover the list and thank Sanders. [party.has cait
        |Your kitty companion sighs. She's doing a lot to help the mage that destroyed her father's wards and put him in danger.
        
        "She's a victim in this story. You've seen what she coughed up when we defeated her, how roughly they tugged her around, and how sticky her clothes were. I-If I didn't reach the Hound back then, maybe I would be in her place."
        
        Sanders places a hand on her shoulder and smiles. "Don't torment yourself, young lady. Tollus and the cult are the ones responsible for her predicament, not you. I'm sure she'll thank you for freeing her from the marauders."
        
        Cait withstands the priest's soulful eyes for a handful of seconds. "Yes, you are right. Come [pc.name]. We've got a magic potion to brew."
    ]
    
    "May the Seven light your path," Sanders says. "I'll be praying for your safe return and for Kira's quick recovery."

    ]她的生活非常艰难，真的非常艰难。她甚至还模仿了那些已腐化者所做的神秘手势。”

    桑德斯点了点头：“是一种非常凶猛的黑魔法。当我还是个年轻的圣骑士的时候，我就与一些使用这种魔法的强大巫师交过手。面对这样的心灵战士，确实是一种令人不快的体验，因此我无法想象长期处于它的控制之下会是什么感受。有些人在这种精神入侵之后，会留下终生的心理创伤。”
    
    你有什么办法可以帮助她吗？
    
    “她被困在自己构筑的心理牢笼之中。以我的经验来看，她要么会突然敞开心扉，要么就会永远保持沉默。通常来说，对她施加压力并不是一个好主意，尤其是当那种控制她的力量还没有被彻底消除的时候。我们能做的并不多，而那些为数不多的尝试，反而可能会毁掉她仅存的那一点点理智，也会彻底摧毁她对我们的信任。”
    
    [party.has cait
        |凯特走了过来，说道：“我们愿意做任何事情。”
        |他可以信赖你。
    ]
    
    桑德斯拿出一张小羊皮纸：“拿着这个，这是[silly
        |清灵茶
        |清醒药剂
    ]的配方，一种非常有效的药剂。你需要用到狐莓、奶茶和霜叶来制作它。一旦准备齐全这些材料，就把它们带到艾薇莉丝那里。她会帮我们完成剩下的工作。”
    
    为什么他不自己来制作呢？ 
    
    “我不是炼金术士，制作药剂也不是我的强项。在这种情况下，我们需要一位专业人士，而她是我认识的最合适的人选。与此同时，我会和基拉讨论我们的计划。如果她突然看到你拿着一份奇怪的药剂，可能会唤起一些不好的回忆。如果她因此陷入惊恐状态，那么你们所有的努力都将白费。”
    
    你找回了那份清单，然后感谢了桑德斯。 [party.has cait
        |你的小猫伙伴叹了口气。她正在尽自己最大的努力去帮助那位毁掉了她父亲的保护结界、使她的父亲陷入危险的法师。
        
        “在这个故事里，她也是受害者。你们看到了我们打败她时她咳出来的东西，看到了他们把她拽来拽去时有多粗暴，也看到了她的衣服有多黏。我、如果当时我没有来到寒霜猎犬，也许现在落到这般境地的就会是我了。”
        
        桑德斯把手放在她的肩上，微笑着说道：“别自责了，年轻姑娘。真正导致她陷入这种困境的，是托勒斯以及那个邪教组织，而不是你。我相信她一定会感谢你将她从那些掠夺者手中解救出来的。”
        
        凯特与那位神父那充满深情的目光对视了几秒钟，然后说道：“是的，你说得对。来吧，[pc.name]。我们还有一种魔法药剂要熬制呢。”
    ]
    
    “愿七神照亮你的道路，”桑德斯说道，“我会为你的平安归来以及基拉的早日康复祈祷。”
rows.raw:
"
    Sanders frowns. "That poor girl's been through a lot. I could mend her bruised flesh, but her mind is still tightly-locked."
    
    Locked? Is she unconscious?
    
    "No, but her mouth stays shut and she struggles to move. I tried to talk her out of her torpor, but she only gave me a name: Kira."
    
    [party.has cait
        |"Kira? Is that her name?" Cait asks.
        |Kira? Maybe it's her name?
    ]
    
    "That's what I think, yes. [silly
        |River brought a plushie and asked her to show us where the centaur marauders touched her
        |River and I have managed to get her to wordlessly describe some of what happened to her
    ]. She had it rough, very rough. She also mimicked arcane gestures one of the corrupted individuals made."
    
    Some kind of magic?
    
    Sanders nods. "A very aggressive form of black magic. When I was a young paladin, I battled a couple of powerful sorcerers that used it. Facing a psychic fighter is a jarring experience, so I can't imagine how it was to be under its spell for extended periods of time. Some people stay scarred for life after this kind of incursion into their mind."
    
    Is there anything you can do to help her?
    
    "She is trapped in a prison of her own mind. In my experience, she can either open up all of a sudden or stay silent forever. It's usually not a good idea to pressure her, especially if the control charm isn't properly removed. There's not much we can do, and what little we can do can ruin what little sanity she still has and demolish her trust in us."
    
    [party.has cait
        |Cait steps closer. "We'll do anything."
        |He can count on you.
    ]
    
    Sanders produces a small parchment. "Take this, it's the recipe for [silly
        |Claritea
        |the potion of clarity
    ], a very strong remedy. You'll need fox berries, milk tea, and frostleaf to brew it. Once you have everything, bring them to Ivris. She'll do the heavy lifting for us."
    
    Why doesn't he brew it himself? 
    
    "I'm not an alchemist and potions aren't my forte. We need a professional in this case, and she's the best I know. In the meantime, I'll talk to Kira about our plan. Seeing you all of a sudden with a weird concoction might awaken bad memories. If she goes into a state of shock, all your efforts will be for naught."
    
    You recover the list and thank Sanders. [party.has cait
        |Your kitty companion sighs. She's doing a lot to help the mage that destroyed her father's wards and put him in danger.
        
        "She's a victim in this story. You've seen what she coughed up when we defeated her, how roughly they tugged her around, and how sticky her clothes were. I-If I didn't reach the Hound back then, maybe I would be in her place."
        
        Sanders places a hand on her shoulder and smiles. "Don't torment yourself, young lady. Tollus and the cult are the ones responsible for her predicament, not you. I'm sure she'll thank you for freeing her from the marauders."
        
        Cait withstands the priest's soulful eyes for a handful of seconds. "Yes, you are right. Come [pc.name]. We've got a magic potion to brew."
    ]
    
    "May the Seven light your path," Sanders says. "I'll be praying for your safe return and for Kira's quick recovery."
    
    "

rows.original:
[party.has cait
        |"Hello Ivris. We have the ingredients for the [silly
            |Claritea
            |potion of clarity
        ]. Sanders said you could brew it for us?" Cait asks.
        |"We brought the ingredients for the [silly
            |Claritea
            |potion of clarity
        ]. Can you brew it for me?" you ask.
    ]
    
    The wyld elf nods. "That was quick. Please, place the ingredients on the table next to my cauldron. I'll take it from here."
    
    She turns around and goes to the back room, certainly to fetch the other ingredients. In the meantime, you place the milk tea, frostleaf, and fox berries near the empty pot. A strong fire already blazes under the cast iron cauldron. Either Ivris knew you were coming or she planned another concoction before your arrival.
    
    A minute later, she comes back with her arms full. She casually hops around the shop. It's a miracle she doesn't bump into anything or drop something on the way. You wouldn't believe she's blind if it weren't for her pink blindfold. She places jars filled with dried herbs and jam-like paste around her workspace, but what catches your attention is the big, ripe melon that she drops on a wooden plank.
    
    "Can you please slice and mash the wild melon into pulp? It's very important for the recipe."
    
    [party.has cait
        |"No problem," Cait says. "That's the least we can do to help you."
    ]
    
    [pc.dcb
        |Reluctantly, you
        |Wordlessly, you
        |Yip yup! You're gonna squish this melon dry. You
    ] take a sharp knife and start cutting the juicy fruit[party.som
        |
        | with [companion1.name]'s help
        | with [companion1.name] and [companion2.name]'s help
    ].
    
    Ivris pours the milk tea and frostleaf first. She stirs the simmering content a little before adding some red jelly and honey. The soup slowly takes a pink color while she slices dried herbs. She then squeezes the fox berries' juice into a small vial and mixes everything together.
    
    "We are reaching the critical part, [pc.name]," she says before handing you the vial. "The potion will soon become deep red. When it does, put this into the pot. I would happily do it, but as you can see, I'm a little colorblind," she teases.
    
    You barely have the time to take the glass container before the liquid darkens. You spill the crimson droplets into the cauldron then stir. In the blink of an eye, the bubbling concoction takes a bubblegum color. 
    
    "It turned pink. Is this fine?"
    
    Ivris huffs the air deeply. Her concerned frown slowly turns into a smile. "Smells like success! We just need to add the last ingredient and let it simmer for a couple of minutes."
    
    [party.has cait
        |"It's the first time I hear someone using wild melon in a healing potion. Is it some kind of catalyst?"
        |Good. What makes melon so important in this recipe?
    ]
    
    Ivris gives [party.has cait
        |Cait
        |you
    ] her most impish smile. "It's for the taste, silly!"
    
    She adds the thinly-sliced melon into the pot then firmly stirs it. While she takes care of that, you help her clean the workplace with a wet sponge and soap from Khor'minos. [pc.isBimbo
        |Gosh, the bubbles it makes are so pretty
        |It makes lots of bubbles, but leaves her knives and planks pristine clean
    ]. The wyld elf apothecary leaves the potion simmer and goes back behind the counter to fetch a leather gourd and a glass pipette. She pulls the cauldron out of the fire then fills the gourd with the thic[silly
        |c
        |k
    ], pinkish liquor. Once they are all filled to the brim, she hands it to you.
    
    "And voila! Be careful. Side effects include sweating, itching, an intense feeling of dehydration, and mild hallucinations. Don't drive a cart, ride a horse, or drink alcohol after ingesting it. Clean any spills with water as soon as possible."
    
    "Thank you Ivris," you say.
    
    "Oh! One more thing. Keep a bucket and a mop around. Some people have a very... visceral reaction to this treatment. The rest is up to you — and to her."
rows.translation:
[party.has cait
        |“你好，艾薇莉丝。我们带来了制作[silly
            |清灵茶
            |清醒药剂
        ]的材料。桑德斯说你能替我们调制？”凯特问道。
        |“我们带来了制作[silly
            |清灵茶
            |清醒药剂
        ]的材料。你能替我调制吗？”你问道。
    ]
    
    野精灵点点头。“动作真快。请把材料放在我坩埚旁边的桌上吧，接下来交给我。”
    
    她转身走进后屋，显然是去拿其余材料。趁这段时间，你把奶茶、霜叶和狐莓放到空锅旁边。铸铁坩埚下已经燃着熊熊烈火。要么艾薇莉丝早知道你会来，要么她在你抵达之前便打算调制别的药剂。
    
    一分钟后，她抱着满怀东西回来了。她若无其事地在店里轻快穿行，途中居然没撞到任何东西，也没有失手掉落什么，简直堪称奇迹。若不是她戴着粉色眼罩，你根本不会相信她看不见。她将装满干燥草药和果酱状膏体的罐子摆在工作台四周，但真正吸引你注意的，是她放到木板上的那颗硕大成熟的甜瓜。
    
    “能麻烦你把野生甜瓜切开，再捣成果泥吗？这对配方非常重要。”
    
    [party.has cait
        |“没问题，”凯特说道。“这是我们最起码能帮上的忙。”
    ]
    
    [pc.dcb
        |你不太情愿地
        |你一言不发地
        |好耶！你要把这颗甜瓜榨得一滴不剩。你
    ]拿起一把锋利的刀，开始切割多汁的果实[party.som
        |
        |，[companion1.name]也来帮忙
        |，[companion1.name]和[companion2.name]也来帮忙
    ]。
    
    艾薇莉丝先倒入奶茶和霜叶。她稍稍搅动正在煨煮的液体，随后加入一些红色果冻和蜂蜜。她切着干燥草药，锅里的汤汁则慢慢染上粉色。接着，她把狐莓汁挤进一只小瓶，将所有材料混合在一起。
    
    “我们快到关键步骤了，[pc.name]。”她说着，把小瓶递给你。“药剂很快会变成深红色。等颜色一变，就把这个倒进锅里。我很乐意亲自动手，不过你也看得出来，我多少有点分不清颜色。”她打趣道。
    
    你才刚接过玻璃容器，液体便已经暗了下来。你将猩红色液滴倒入坩埚，然后开始搅拌。眨眼之间，冒泡的混合物便变成了泡泡糖般的粉色。 
    
    “它变成粉红色了。这样没问题吗？”
    
    艾薇莉丝深深嗅了嗅空气。她担忧的皱眉逐渐化作笑容。“闻起来成功了！只要加入最后一种材料，再煨上几分钟就好。”
    
    [party.has cait
        |“我还是第一次听说有人会在治疗药剂里使用野生甜瓜。它是某种催化剂吗？”
        |很好。甜瓜为什么在这份配方里如此重要？
    ]
    
    艾薇莉丝朝[party.has cait
        |凯特
        |你
    ]露出最顽皮的笑容。“当然是为了味道啦，笨蛋！”
    
    她把切成薄片的甜瓜加入锅中，用力搅拌起来。她忙着照料药剂时，你则用湿海绵和来自科尔米诺斯的肥皂帮她清理工作台。[pc.isBimbo
        |天啊，冒出来的泡泡真漂亮
        |它会产生许多泡泡，却把她的刀具和木板洗得一尘不染
    ]。野精灵药剂师让药剂继续煨煮，自己回到柜台后面取来一只皮葫芦和一根玻璃滴管。她把坩埚移出火焰，然后用浓[silly
        |得
        |稠
    ]的粉红色药液装满葫芦。全部装到满满当当之后，她便把葫芦递给了你。
    
    “大功告成！小心一点。副作用包括出汗、瘙痒、强烈脱水感，以及轻微幻觉。服用后不要驾车、骑马或饮酒。如有药液洒出，请尽快用水清洗。”
    
    “谢谢你，艾薇莉丝。”你说道。
    
    “哦！还有一件事。记得在附近准备一只水桶和一把拖把。有些人对这种治疗的反应会非常……激烈。剩下的就要看你——还有她自己了。”
