rows.raw: ' Arona pauses her shouting and berating for a moment, watching Lyric cry and cower in front of her[lyric.isTall |. Even after [lyric.hisHer] transformation into a tall dragon, taller than even the towering Arona, [lyric.heShe]'s still the little kobold you knew when you first found [lyric.himHer] ]. But, despite her loud castigations, she doesn't look at Lyric judgmentally or unfavorably. Again, her expression is hard to read. "Tell me something," she begins, her voice returning to the calmer, steadier tone it had before. "I know that girl kobolds can grow to be pretty fuckin' gigantic. Your... Village Mother. Did she put up a fight?" Lyric doesn't answer immediately. "What do you care?" "Just humor me," she sighs. Her patience remains as... well, as thick as it'll ever be. Lyric takes a deep sniff and lets out a shaky sigh. "Yeah." "Yeah?" Arona repeats. "She take out any?" Another pause. "Like... four or five." "Your one kobold Village Mother killed five orc raiders? By herself?" "For all the good it did." Arona hums through pursed lips as she considers how to approach her next sentence. "Bear with me on this, I'm gonna try and make a point," she starts. Which makes a cold jolt run up your spine – opening a statement like that is never a good sign. "Kobolds are worth about eight grand a head[lyric.electrumRange 0 300 |. You... would probably get a little more, with the weight on you ]." Lyric's eyes dart back up to Arona's. Just a second ago, [lyric.heShe] had conceded defeat and just wanted the conversation to end. But with a sentence like that, the fight returns to [lyric.himHer] pretty quickly – that [lyric.heShe] and [lyric.hisHer] people could have their lives be... evaluated like that. "And your Village Mother? She would have been worth... man, hard to say. Tens of thousands." She whistles as she considers it. "She might have been impossible to sell, actually. A kobold that big and that fierce would be more of a commodity – something that would be traded between tribes rather than something we could reasonably sell on a market somewhere." [pc.isDK |You, again, say nothing, and continue to watch the conversation unfold from the sideline. "She is not a 'thing', you jerk!" Lyric bites, [lyric.hisHer] voice breaking from [lyric.hisHer] crying. |You tell Arona to [arona.isDom | |hurry and ]make her point before she makes things worse. And you remind her that kobolds aren't 'things'. Although Lyric still looks like [lyric.heShe]'d get physical with Arona if [lyric.heShe] thought [lyric.heShe]'d stand a chance, [lyric.heShe] relaxes very slightly knowing that [lyric.heShe] has you beside [lyric.himHer]. ] "How much do you think a single orc is worth?" Arona asks. "Serious question." The question takes [pc.isDK | |you and ]Lyric aback. "Uhh," [lyric.heShe] hums, [lyric.hisHer] bloodshot eyes staring at the space around Arona as [lyric.heShe] tries to answer it. "I don't know... I've never considered how much money a person is worth." "Orc slaves are worth a whole lot more than eight thousand," she answers for Lyric. "And, depending on the orc, more than a Village Mother." "Please make your point," Lyric whimpers. "Now that you know how much kobolds are worth, and how much orcs are worth, and how many orcs your Village Mother took out, do you think the orc raiders that kidnapped your village made a profit?" "Even if they didn't, is that supposed to make me feel better?" Arona grunts at Lyric diverting her question like that. "I say this as an orc, knowing that your village was kidnapped by orcs, but it's not orcs you should be blaming," she says with a low growl. "And it's not yourself and your kind for being weaker than orcs. You should be blaming the fact that there's a market for slaves at all. I guarantee that, if slave trading weren't worth so much money, no tribe in the world would have picked a fight with a Village Mother, or the village she was mothering, just for their own stock of slaves." Lyric pauses as [lyric.heShe] considers Arona's viewpoint. [lyric.HeShe]'s still a shaken, sodden, emotional mess, but the more casual tone – and, perhaps, remembering the fight that [lyric.hisHer] Village Mother put up – seems to have relaxed [lyric.himHer] enough that [lyric.heShe] can at least approach the conversation with a slightly more level head. And, knowing that you're standing next to [lyric.himHer] and ensuring that things don't escalate probably helps. "I don't know how easy it's going to be for me to direct my hatred from orcs to [silly |systemic capitalism |the concept of commerce ]," Lyric admits.[pc.ra orc | Then, [lyric.heShe] turns to you sheepishly. "Not counting you, [pc.name]." ] Arona laughs. "I don't blame you. I'd be fuckin' pissed, too. If some rival tribe managed to enslave all of Kervus overnight, but they missed me, the first thing I'd want is revenge. I'd rather level every other stronghold until I got them back than try and, I dunno, steal every coin ever made and melt them all down." Arona extends a finger and places it on Lyric's chin[lyric.isTall | |, lifting [lyric.hisHer] eyes back up to look into hers ]. "Look, Lyric, you don't have to like orcs. You don't have to like me. If you slit my throat in my sleep, I'd get it." She frowns. "You'd better make sure the first slice counts, though." It's one of those absurd, off-the-cuff, and inappropriate jokes that even Lyric can't help but giggle through [lyric.hisHer] wavering breathing. "And, yeah, this sucks to hear and it sucks to say, but orc slave trade isn't stopping[arona.isChief |. Kervus isn't about to stop buying them, and other tribes aren't about to stop selling them ]. We orcs, we're big, we're strong, and we're stupid. It's what we're best at. It's what brings in money. [arona.isChief |I can't just go back home and tell everyone |Even if I were chief, I couldn't just go back home to Kervus and tell everyone ] that the women are picking up sewing and the men are picking up personal training." You have to hand it to Arona: the tension in the air, while not fully evaporated, has eased. Lyric is still uncomfortable and still wants the conversation to be over, but the conversation isn't a total, unmitigated disaster anymore, and everyone can leave dour and frustrated as opposed to angry and hopeless. There's one thing that you've been wondering since you first saw Lyric approach Arona. You ask Lyric what, exactly, [lyric.heShe] hoped [lyric.heShe]'d get out of this conversation. Lyric sniffles again, rubbing [lyric.hisHer] nose with the back of [lyric.hisHer] arm. "I don't know..." [lyric.heShe] admits. "I was hoping... to know where my family was taken, at least." Arona shrugs. "Like I told you, as far as I know, Kervus hasn't dealt with any big shipments of kobolds, so I'm no good there. And even if [arona.isChief |we |they ] did, unless [arona.isChief |we |they ] kept the whole village for [arona.isChief |our |their ] camp, the kobolds would have sold off pretty quick." "I know we ain't friends, Lyric," Arona says with a sigh, her shoulders relaxing. From the tone in her voice, she's looking to wrap the conversation. "The slave trades aren't gonna stop just because one of the slaves didn't like it. Like I said before, you might as well get mad at farmers for raising cows for their meat. And I know you don't like being compared to cows and chickens, but, well..." She stutters as she tries to think of some way to finish that thought without riling Lyric up again. "The best thing I can think to say is that... there are worse evils in the world." "Worse than slavery? Like what?" Lyric asks incredulously. Arona frowns. "I don't know, don't put that shit on me. I'm trying to end this conversation without making things worse." The air hangs heavy and stale between your orc and your [lyric.isTall |dragon |kobold ] for a long moment. You can tell that Lyric is still emotionally [pc.isBimbo |tumul– tummytul– upset |tumultuous ], and that this conversation didn't go even remotely the way [lyric.heShe] wanted, and you don't know if Arona's finishing remarks made things better. Arona, for all her faults, recognizes the same thing: she's unrepentant, blunt, and unabashed about the realities of orc culture, but she's not unsympathetic, and she doesn't want to end this conversation in a worse way than it started. She places her hand on Lyric's [lyric.isTall |shoulder, giving [lyric.himHer] a friendly squeeze |head, giving [lyric.himHer] a reassuring pat, like a pet. ] "And like I said about farmers not naming their animals... I dunno what this means to you, coming from me, but [arona.isDom |[pc.name] is mine, and you belong to [pc.name], which means that you belong to me, too. And that |[pc.name] likes you, and if [pc.name] likes you, that ] means that you're under my protection, too. You don't have to worry about [arona.isDom |belonging to |being stolen by ] anyone else." Lyric hums... but the 'reassurance' does little to assuage [lyric.himHer][lyric.isTall | |. And the longer that Arona's hand rests on [lyric.hisHer] head and pats [lyric.himHer] like a dog, the more [lyric.heShe] gets visibly uncomfortable. It's a tangible relief for [lyric.himHer] when she finally lifts it away ]. [arona.isChief |"You're the chief of the Kervus tribe," [lyric.heShe] says. "Can you at least promise me that you'll... stop kidnapping kobolds?" "Nnnnnn," Arona starts, then has the last-second sensibility to pull back. She's already botched the landing on this conversation enough; denying Lyric this last bit would set her back completely. "Kervus doesn't actually, uh... 'obtain the inventory'. Kervus buys and trades, but we're not the ones that, you know, do the deed." Lyric recognizes the deflection for what it is. "Okay, then can you promise me that you won't do that, then?" Arona briefly hesitates. "I'll, uh... look into it." ] Without anything more to say, Lyric turns about and goes back the way [lyric.heShe] came, without so much as a farewell to either of you. '

rows.original:
You stand with Arona next to the heat of your campfire. She stands awkwardly, shuffling from one foot to the other as she tries to diffuse the tension in her body. Not that either of you expected things to get any wilder than some loud words, but even still, Arona, for all her strength and fortitude... it's easy to make her feel uncomfortable.

rows.original:
You tell Lyric that Ivris's shop seems awfully cramped for someone of [lyric.hisHer] size, and suggest that [lyric.heShe] might enjoy getting out into the fresh air with you for a little while.
    
    "No, I'm fine," Lyric replies with a genuine smile and a swish of [lyric.hisHer] tail. "I know I'm much bigger, now, and I sometimes bump my head on the door frame, but I'm actually pretty cozy right here, where I am. And Ivris is so nice and accommodating, too."
    
    You stare at Lyric. [lyric.HeShe] stares back, oblivious.
    
    "Oh!" [lyric.heShe] says, jolting in place as the realization hits [lyric.himHer] like a thunderbolt. "You want me to – right! Yes, sorry!" [lyric.HeShe] raps [lyric.hisHer] knuckles against [lyric.hisHer] own head, like [lyric.heShe] was knocking on a door. "I still got chemistry on the brain for a bit. And you asked me about Ivris, and I got all twisted and turned around. Yes, we can leave immediately!"
    
    Lyric turns towards [lyric.hisHer] little table to swipe a few vials, waterskins, and ingredients, stuffing things into various pockets along [lyric.hisHer] tunic and into the pockets on [lyric.hisHer] belts. "Okay!" [lyric.heShe] says with one last bounce on [lyric.hisHer] feet. "Onward, [pc.name]!"

    “不，我没事，”莉里克带着真诚的微笑回答道，同时轻轻挥了挥手。[lyric.hisHer]我知道我现在变得大很多了，有时候会撞到门框上，但在这里，我其实感觉挺舒服的。而且艾薇莉丝也非常友善，总是很体谅我。”

哦！[lyric.heShe]说道，声音陡然提高：[lyric.hisHer]脊柱挺直了，[lyric.hisHer]尾巴惊讶地竖了起来。[lyric.isTall|我们认识的时间已经够长了，以至于……他们把我变成了一条龙！ ]我没想到你会问我关于……我的事情。 [lyric.isTall|直到现在，它仍然会让我措手不及！|人们通常不会问我关于我自己的事情！] [lyric.isTall|在我还是个狗头人的时候，我遇到的大多数非狗头人生物……|我遇到过的大多数非狗头人生物……]通常会询问[lyric.isTall|ed]他们希望我能够为他们做些什么。嗯，他们通常情况下只是[lyric.isTall|告诉了|告诉]让我离开吧通常情况下用更直白的语言来说就是这样。 [lyric.isTall|即便到现在，依然是这样。仍然对我来说还挺新鲜的！|这对我来说真是新鲜事啊！]你耐心地等待莉里克开始回答你的问题。 “嗯，那个……首先，我其实并不是来自……这个地区叫什么来着？” “冰霜边境，”你回答道。 “对，我其实并不是来自这里。我来自遥远的南方，那里的气候温暖得多，一年中很少下雪。全年都是温暖宜人的；树木始终保持着绿色，空气的湿度也通常比这里高很多。……冰霜之地。” 你自然会问一个显而易见的问题：如果那就是[lyric.heShe]的故乡，那么，究竟是什么驱使着人们去做这些事情呢？[lyric.himHer]在这里，却如此遥远[lyric.hisHer]元素？” 听到这个问题，莉里克一反常态地犹豫了起来。[lyric.HeShe]突然想不起来了[lyric.himHer]要勇敢地直视你的眼睛，そして [lyric.hisHer]嘴唇开始颤抖。[lyric.HisHer]眼睑向上翘起，[lyric.hisHer]那双大大的、金色的眼睛开始泛起泪光[lyric.heShe]差点哭出来了。” “嗯，[lyric.heShe]结结巴巴地说：“我……被绑架了。被兽人抓走了。” 你插话对莉里克说：“如果[lyric.heShe]如果不想再继续下去的话，那就[lyric.heShe]没有必要。 [lyric.isTall|毕竟，这已经是既定事实了。|你可能会认为这是理所当然的。]不过，你会有一种这样的感觉[lyric.heShe]除非你下令停止，否则它们就不会停下来。[lyric.himHer]那就可以了。 [lyric.HeShe]深深地叹了口气，身体不禁颤抖起来。“我想，现在我可以谈论这件事了。我的意思是[lyric.isTall|在我们共同经历了这一切之后？在我变成了这样的一个人之后？|我现在就在你身边，对吧？]最终，一切都得到了解决！” 你暗自提醒自己：在冰川裂谷中，你发现莉里克几乎冻死了。情况本来就已经越来越糟了[lyric.himHer]所以，是的。[lyric.heShe]说道，努力让自己振作起来，强忍着泪水继续说下去。[lyric.hisHer]那些兽人袭击了我的村庄，绑架了我和我的族人。我们被关在一艘船上，然后一路向北航行，最终来到了……嗯，就是这里。关于这段旅程的细节，我就不详细说了。” 你完全可以理解。[lyric.himHer]但我必须说，他们给我们提供了铜作为维持生存的资源。我们可以吃铜，但这也并不意味着可口的，美味的。而且这种金属营养价值并不高。金属的质量越差，我们就需要吃下更多的这种金属，才能开始释放火焰。” “他们给我们的手铐是由青铜制成的，而各种合金材质太坚硬了，我们根本无法咬碎它们。在我们成功登陆之前，我设法通过囤积食物来维持生存，直到快要饿晕过去；然后有一天晚上，我以最快的速度吃光了所有食物，这样就可以用我的火息将手腕上的手环加热到炽热的状态。等它们变得通红之后，我就把它们浸入他们提供给我们的公共水槽里。我反复做了很多次，直到那块金属变得足够脆弱，即使是用我那双细瘦的手臂，也能把它扯开。 [lyric.HeShe]掀开[lyric.hisHer]护腕的布料，向你露出[lyric.hisHer]手腕内侧。它们的每一处手腕上都有长长的、宽宽的、深红色的烧伤疤痕。[lyric.hisHer]手铐曾经是[lyric.isTall|。 即使在现在，过了这么久之后[lyric.heShe]当它变成一条龙之后，那些伤痕也会永远留在它的身上。[lyric.hisHer]身体]这个过程其实并不完美，也没有那么顺利。[lyric.heShe]带着一丝俏皮的语气说道[lyric.hisHer]但是，它确实起作用了。[lyric.HeShe]把护腕重新折起来，说道：“我在半夜爬上了甲板，然后跳进了海里。” 半夜？他是怎么做到的？[lyric.heShe]知道这片土地的来历吗？他们甚至被发现的嗯，其实我的村庄位于最南端地区的西海岸，对吧？而那些兽人正把我们往北带。所以我知道东边就是陆地——只要进入水中，只要观察星星和月亮的方位，就能知道东方在哪里。我游了大概几个小时，终于到达了陆地。” 听到这里，你完全被这个故事吸引住了，于是让莉里克暂停一下，好让你能回顾一下刚才的内容。[lyric.HeShe]当时，我居住在这片大陆的南部地区。[lyric.heShe]被兽人绑架了。当时[lyric.heShe]正在准备出售的过程中。[lyric.heShe]通过绝食成功逃脱了。[lyric.himHer]自我限制与资源分配[lyric.hisHer]先把食物准备好，然后一次性全部吃掉；接着，利用这种突如其来的金属冲击力[lyric.hisHer]胆敢对……出言不逊[lyric.hisHer]把它们反复浸在水中，直到它们变得脆弱到足以折断为止。之后再给它们戴上手铐。那个， [lyric.heShe]在半夜悄悄爬上甲板，跳入海中，借助星星来确定东方在哪里，然后游了一个多小时直到[lyric.heShe]已经成功登陆了。 你询问莉里克，这一切是否都正确。 “没错！[lyric.heShe]说着，还摇着尾巴。[lyric.hisHer]尾巴。 [var0|…你问到是否[lyric.heShe]知道是谁[lyric.heShe]据我所知，是北方地区的另一个兽人部落。我不知道他们的部落名称或其他详细信息。” ……这很可能是你迟早会与阿罗娜进行的对话。] 你让莉里克继续说下去。那是怎么发生的呢？[lyric.heShe]最终落入了冰川裂谷？你可能会认为，第一个应该出现的地方应该是[lyric.heShe]我想去的方向是南方，而不是更往北。” 听到这个问题，莉里克再次犹豫了——不过，这一次，[lyric.heShe]望着远方，没有流露出任何情绪。“我……还在犹豫是否应该回去。[lyric.heShe]说：“那次袭击证明，住在那里并不安全。如果我继续留在那里，我就不得不面对这样一个事实：我是唯一一个成功逃脱的人。 [lyric.HeShe]打开[lyric.hisHer]想说更多，但却再也说不出任何话来。[lyric.HeShe]停止施法[lyric.hisHer]低头沉思，神情肃穆。[lyric.HisHer]尾巴静止地悬在身后[lyric.himHer]所以，嗯，我听说在更北边的某个地方，还有另一个……狗头人聚居地。他们把那个地方叫做幽暗山丘。那里有一位女王，据我所知，她的地位就和我们村里的村长差不多。那个地方在地下，一年到头都很热。最棒的是，那里有你想得到的所有黄金！黄金，这种金属真是太珍贵了！说实话，这听起来简直好得让人难以置信！” 一想到幽暗山丘，莉里克又变得兴奋起来，说话的语气也更加活跃了。[lyric.hisHer]先前的沮丧早已被兴奋与期待所取代。“我花费了大量的时间和精力进行研究，终于找到了！我成功找到了通往山腹深域的路，而且……真的，我做到了！[pc.name]，就是那样天堂啊！我被狗头人们包围了！那里的温度温暖极了……而且金币！那个地方点亮那些东西啊！我一进去就能看到它们在墙上闪闪发光呢！” 莱瑞克的身体慢慢放松下来，[lyric.hisHer]始终面带微笑[lyric.hisHer]面带微笑……但显然，这种兴奋感并没有持续太久。毕竟，莉里克在雪中等待，是有着原因的。 “这正是我梦寐以求的一切。[lyric.heShe]轻声说道：“我在那里本可以开始新的生活。再也不用为食物、陪伴或安全而担忧了。” 你沉默不语。莉里克的低头露出了[lyric.heShe]伸出爪子来[lyric.hisHer]擦去泪水，说道： “原来……那些黄金并不是用来吃的。我在那里待了一天，之后女王就把我赶走了。” 过了一会儿，莉里克的肩膀开始颤抖[lyric.heShe]偶尔会打嗝或流鼻涕。当[lyric.heShe]时终于又抬起头来。[lyric.hisHer]眼睛干涩，但[lyric.hisHer]脸颊湿润了。[lyric.HisHer]脸颊被强行挤成了一丝微笑。 “就在那之后不久，你在雪地里找到了我。[lyric.heShe]说道，[lyric.hisHer]声音颤抖且不稳定。“所以，只要结局好，一切就都值得了，对吧？
rows.raw: ' You ask Lyric to tell you a little bit about [lyric.himHer]self. [var0|You've run into kobolds before, but Lyric [lyric.isTall|seemed|seems] a bit... well, different from the chaff, and you don't mean that in a bad way. Even [lyric.hisHer] scales are a different color than what you've seen.|[lyric.isTall|You had never|You've never] seen a kobold before, and Lyric is quite the character – but you don't mean that in a bad way. Are all kobolds like [lyric.himHer]? Spritely, little, energetic, scientifically-minded, avaricious gremlins-but-you-mean-that-in-a-cute-way?] "Oh!" [lyric.heShe] says, perking upward: [lyric.hisHer] spine straightens and [lyric.hisHer] tail stands on-end in surprise. "[lyric.isTall|We've known each other for long enough that, well, we turned me into a dragon! ]I wasn't expecting you to ask me about... me. [lyric.isTall|Even now, it still catches me off-guard!|People don't usually ask me about me!] [lyric.isTall|Back when I was a kobold, most non-kobolds I had met|Most non-kobolds I've met] usually ask[lyric.isTall|ed] me for something I can do for them. Well, they usually just [lyric.isTall|told|tell] me to go away, and usually in more crass language than that. [lyric.isTall|Even now, this is still a bit new to me!|So this is new to me!]" You patiently wait for Lyric to start answering your question. "Well, um... to start with, I'm not actually from... what's this region called?" "The Frost Marches," you answer. "Yeah, I'm not actually from here. I come from way, way down south, where the climate is much warmer and it rarely snows at any time of the year. It's nice and warm all year ‘round; the trees stay green and the air is usually a whole lot more humid than here in the... the Frost Marches." You ask the obvious question: if that's where [lyric.heShe]'s from, then what brings [lyric.himHer] here, so far out of [lyric.hisHer] element? At the question, Lyric, rather uncharacteristically, hesitates. [lyric.HeShe] suddenly can't bring [lyric.himHer]self to look you in the eye, and [lyric.hisHer] lips begin to tremble. [lyric.HisHer] eyelids arch upward, and [lyric.hisHer] big, golden eyes begin to water – [lyric.heShe]'s nearly about to cry. "Um," [lyric.heShe] stumbles, "I was... kidnapped. Stolen. By orcs." You interject by telling Lyric that if [lyric.heShe] doesn't want to go any further, then [lyric.heShe] doesn't have to. [lyric.isTall|Which, by now, is a given|Which you'd think was a given], but you get the impression that [lyric.heShe] wouldn't stop unless you told [lyric.himHer] that it was okay. [lyric.HeShe] takes a deep, shuddering sigh. "I think I'm okay with talking about it. I mean, [lyric.isTall|after everything you and I have been through? After what I've become?|I'm here with you now, aren't I?] Everything worked out in the end!" You silently remind yourself that you found Lyric nearly frozen to death in the Glacial Rift. Things went from bad to worse for [lyric.himHer] in a hurry. "So, yeah," [lyric.heShe] says, trying to buck up and swallow [lyric.hisHer] emotions, "an orc tribe raided my village and kidnapped me and my kin. The lot of us were thrown onto a ship, and we sailed north until we got... well, here. I'm, uh, not going to go into details about how the trip was." You don't blame [lyric.himHer]. "But I will say that they fed us copper to keep us going. We can eat copper, but that's not to say it's palatable, and it's not especially nutritious. And the worse quality that the metal is, the more we need to eat before we can start breathing fire." "The cuffs they put us in were made of bronze, and alloys are too tough for us to chew through. Before we made landfall, I managed to escape by stockpiling my food rations until I was starving; then, one night, I ate all of it, as quickly as I could, so I could heat the cuffs around my wrists with my fire breath. And once they were red-hot, I dunked the cuffs into the communal water trough they gave us. I did that a bunch of times until the metal was weak enough to yank apart, even with my spindly-thin arms." [lyric.HeShe] pulls back the fabric of [lyric.hisHer] bracers, showing you the underside of [lyric.hisHer] wrists. They each have long, broad, deep-red burn scars where [lyric.hisHer] cuffs used to be[lyric.isTall|. Even now, after [lyric.heShe]'s become a dragon, the scars remain as a permanent fixture on [lyric.hisHer] body]. "It wasn't exactly a perfect, painless process," [lyric.heShe] says with a bit of a lilt in [lyric.hisHer] voice, "but it worked." [lyric.HeShe] folds the bracers back up. "I crawled above-deck in the middle of the night, then jumped overboard." In the middle of the night? How did [lyric.heShe] know where land was? Had they even spotted land? "Well, actually, my village was on the west coast of the far-southern regions, right? And the orcs were taking us north. So I knew that land was to my east – once I was in the water, all it took was looking at the stars and the position of the moon to know which direction was east. I swam for maybe a few hours before I made landfall." You're reeling at this whole story so far, so you ask Lyric to pause so you can recap. [lyric.HeShe] lived in the southern regions of the continent when [lyric.heShe] was kidnapped by orcs. While [lyric.heShe] was on the way to being sold, [lyric.heShe] managed to escape by starving [lyric.himHer]self and rationing [lyric.hisHer] food; then eating it all at once; then using the sudden burst of metal in [lyric.hisHer] gut to breath fire on [lyric.hisHer] handcuffs before dunking them in water over and over until they were weak enough to snap. After that, [lyric.heShe] snuck above-deck in the middle of the night; jumped overboard; used the stars to determine which way was east; and then swam for over an hour until [lyric.heShe] made landfall. You ask Lyric if that's all correct. "Yep!" [lyric.heShe] says, wagging [lyric.hisHer] tail. [var0|... you ask if [lyric.heShe] knew who [lyric.heShe] was being sold to. "As I understood it, another tribe of orcs in the northern regions. I don't know their tribe name or anything." ... this is probably a conversation you're going to have with Arona sooner or later.] You ask Lyric to continue. How did [lyric.heShe] end up in the Glacial Rift? You'd have thought that the first place [lyric.heShe]'d want to go was south, not farther north. At that question, Lyric once again hesitates – although, this time, [lyric.heShe] stares off into the distance rather than get emotional. "I'm... still trying to decide if I want to go back," [lyric.heShe] says. "The raid proved that it wasn't safe to live there. And if I did, I'd have to live with the fact that I was the only one to escape." [lyric.HeShe] opens [lyric.hisHer] mouth to say more, but no more words come out. [lyric.HeShe] stops, casting [lyric.hisHer] eyes downward in solemn thought. [lyric.HisHer] tail lies motionless behind [lyric.himHer]. "So, um, I had heard that there was another... gathering of kobolds somewhere farther north. In a place that they called Undermountain. They had a queen, which, from what I heard, sounded just like how we had a Village Mother. It was underground, where it was hot all year ‘round. And best of all, they had all the gold you could ask for! Gold, the most delicious of all the metals! It honestly sounded too good to be true!" Remembering the Undermountain causes Lyric to get more animated and excited once again; [lyric.hisHer] earlier despondence replaced with excitement and eagerness. "It took me a lot of effort and research, but I found it! I managed to find my way to the Undermountain, and... my word, [pc.name], it was paradise! I was surrounded by kobolds! It was warm as could be! And the gold! The place was lit with the stuff! I could see it gleaming off the walls as soon as I found my way in!" Lyric's body slowly begins to relax, and [lyric.hisHer] smile stays on [lyric.hisHer] face... but it's clear that the elation is short-lived. Lyric was freezing in the snow for a reason, after all. "It was everything I could have wanted," [lyric.heShe] says quietly. "I could have started a new life there. I'd never have to worry about food, or company, or security again." You stay silent. Lyric's face turns downward, and [lyric.heShe] raises a claw to [lyric.hisHer] eye, wiping away a tear. "Turns out... the gold wasn't for eating. I lasted a day before the queen banished me." A few moments pass; Lyric's shoulders shudder and [lyric.heShe] occasionally hiccups and sniffles. When [lyric.heShe] finally looks back up, [lyric.hisHer] eyes are dry, but [lyric.hisHer] cheeks are damp. [lyric.HisHer] cheeks are raised into a forced smile. "You found me in the snow not long after that," [lyric.heShe] says, [lyric.hisHer] voice wavy and unsteady. "So, all's well that ends well, right?" '

rows.translation: [lyric.HimHer]自己

rows.original: [lyric.isTall |Knowing that Lyric is no longer strictly all-kobold, you nonetheless |You ] ask Lyric about kobolds in general. They aren't an especially common species in this corner of Savarra, and you're sure [lyric.heShe]'d be a valuable resource on everything there is to know about [lyric.himHer] and [lyric.hisHer] scaly kind. "Well, I'll give you the cheat sheet answer first," [lyric.heShe] says with a laugh and a smile. "Do you want to get on a kobold's good side real fast? Give them food and warmth. We're very basic like that. Our favorite snack is metal, particularly gold and electrum. Give us food and a hug and you'll have a friend for life." That explains why [lyric.heShe] was so quick to profess [lyric.hisHer] love to you once you thawed [lyric.himHer] out[lyric.isTall |. You ask [lyric.himHer] if that's no longer strictly true, now that [lyric.heShe]'s a dragon. "I'm only a dragon because of you, [pc.name]," [lyric.heShe] reminds you with a smile. "You get a pass." That doesn't quite answer your question. [lyric.HeShe] laughs. "Well, platonically, if someone fed me and hugged me, I'm not about to push them away and tell them to leave me alone. Would you?" [pc.isDK |You don't answer that. |[lyric.HeShe] continues before you can answer. ] "Romantically or otherwise, you have no competition. But... yeah, if some stranger gave me some gold and a hug, I'd have a new friend, right there on the spot." [lyric.HeShe] continues, picking up from your diversion. ]"Having scales means we tend to get cold a lot faster than anyone with skin or fur or feathers[lyric.isTall |, and that's still true now that I'm a dragon ], so we generally prefer warmer areas and climates to what you'll primarily find in this region, which is why kobolds are so rare here. Myself, I'm from way down south; coming here was the first time I've ever actually seen snow. And, between you and me, I don't see the hype. Can't say I'm a fan." You tell Lyric that it may come as a shock for [lyric.himHer] to hear, but most races, including your own, aren't exactly big fans of colder climates either. "Then why live here?" [lyric.heShe] asks earnestly. Excellent question. But this isn't about you and your kind; you want to learn more about kobolds. [lyric.HeShe] just mentioned that kobolds like to eat metal? "Oh yes! Some types of metal are actually considered to be part of a staple diet for us. We can eat meat and fruit, which are much easier to come by, but you can tell if a kobold's gotten a steady input of the good stuff by the glow of their scales and the shape of their bodies. I think [pc.race]s are the same way, too?" You answer that, in your culture, the saying is that ‘abs start in the kitchen.' Eating healthy is as important to a strong, shapely body as proper exercise is. [lyric.electrumRange 0 100 |You ask what a ‘well fed' kobold that's been fed a steady diet of ‘the good metal' is supposed to be shaped like. [pc.isDK |You don't answer that. |[lyric.HeShe] continues before you can answer. ] "Romantically or otherwise, you have no competition. Myself, I'm from way down south; coming here was the first time I've ever actually seen snow. And, between you and me, I don't see the hype. Can't say I'm a fan." You tell Lyric that it may come as a shock for [lyric.himHer] to hear, but most races, including your own, aren't exactly big fans of colder climates either. "Then why live here?" [lyric.heShe] asks earnestly. Excellent question. But this isn't about you and your kind; you want to learn more about kobolds. [lyric.HeShe] just mentioned that kobolds like to eat metal? "Oh yes! Some types of metal are actually considered to be part of a staple diet for us. We can eat meat and fruit, which are much easier to come by, but you can tell if a kobold's gotten a steady input of the good stuff by the glow of their scales and the shape of their bodies. I think [pc.race]s are the same way, too?" You answer that, in your culture, the saying is that ‘abs start in the kitchen.' Eating healthy is as important to a strong, shapely body as proper exercise is. [lyric.electrumRange 0 100 |You ask what a ‘well fed' kobold that's been fed a steady diet of ‘the good metal' is supposed to be shaped like. "I'll give you three guesses, and the first two don't count," [lyric.heShe] answers with an overly-exaggerated sway of [lyric.hisHer] hips, causing the fat of [lyric.hisHer] thighs to jiggle, sway, and clap together at the apex of each swing. ... interesting to note. |You ask Lyric if eating metal makes every kobold's thighs explode with girth and mass like [lyric.mf |his |hers ] did. "Where I come from, yep," [lyric.heShe] answers, turning around and lifting [lyric.hisHer] tail, giving you an unimpeded look at [lyric.hisHer] fat [lyric.isTall |dragon |kobold ] ass, [lyric.hisHer] tail hiking up to expose more of [lyric.hisHer] thigh[lyric.isTall | – not that any of it was hidden in the first place ]. "Big booties like this baby," [lyric.heShe] says, slapping [lyric.hisHer] right ass cheek for emphasis, "are considered attractive to kobolds from my region, because it means they're well-off and that their mates and children would probably be well-fed, too.[lyric.electrumRange 0 150 | | [lyric.isTall |If I was still a kobold and I had a bum like this, then all you'd have to do is send me into a kobold camp or village |Send me into a kobold camp or village looking like this ], and we'd have a whole harem of little ankle-biters looking to get in on what we have, [pc.name]. ] I dunno if it's the same deal with your northern kobolds, but based on the Undermountain's queen and the bottom she's got, I'm gonna go with a yes." ... something to keep in mind for later. ] For your follow-up question, you ask Lyric what metals are the most delicious and nutritious for kobolds. "Gold. Gold, gold, gold, gold!" Lyric chants, [lyric.hisHer] tail wagging a mile a minute and a strand of drool dripping down the corner of [lyric.hisHer] mouth. "Gold is far and away the most delicious, the most nutritious, the most incredible of the metals for us to eat. It's like some kind of do-it-all superfood! Feeling tired and weak? Just eat some gold! Just got a bit of a sweet-tooth? Eat all the gold you want, it's not unhealthy for you! There's nothing it doesn't do and we can survive entirely on gold alone[lyric.isTall |. I am so thankful that I'm not the kind of dragon that wants to hoard it, because even the thought of having a bit of gold to snack on is, uuugghhh," [lyric.heShe] moans, almost sexually, as [lyric.heShe] wipes [lyric.hisHer] chin with the back of [lyric.hisHer] wrist ]." [lyric.HeShe] pauses, [lyric.hisHer] eyes drifting to one said and [lyric.hisHer] mouth twisting in thought. "Maybe that's why gold is so difficult to come by nowadays. Maybe we mighta, kinda, sorta ate it all." [lyric.HisHer] eyes go back to you. "A distant second is electrum. Still just as nutritious, and plenty tasty all on its own, but it just doesn't have that 'zing' that gold has, you know? There isn't a kobold alive that, if presented with gold and electrum, would choose the electrum." [lyric.HeShe] tilts [lyric.hisHer] head and rests [lyric.hisHer] chin on [lyric.hisHer] hand. "Silver is pretty hit-or-miss depending on things like where it was found, whether it was polished, and on and on. Nickel is [silly |probably a D on the tier list |pretty low-bar ], and at that point, you're probably just hungry for anything. Most 'brown' metals, like copper and brass, are edible but they're strictly a last resort – it'd be like you eating leaves off a tree to survive. And finally, we can't eat alloys like bronze, because they're too tough for us to chew through." Can kobolds eat anything other than metal? "Oh, yes. Metal isn't something you grow on a farm, after all – we'd be in a tough spot if our settlements ran out of metal to eat. As delicious and nutritious as it is, metal isn't actually our primary source of food. We can eat dairy, meat, and fruit just fine, but we can't digest grains and most vegetables, so feeding me bread is a good way to make me die. Well, figuratively. I'd wish I was dead with the stomach ache it'd give me." Well, now you know quite a bit about the dietary habits of a kobold. You want to get a bit into their culture next: what is it that kobolds do all day? They have a reputation for being sneaky thieves outside of their own settlements; you'd like to think they don't just steal from each other to get back all the time. "We're good at sneaking and stealing because the outside world isn't built for us to have an easy life in, not because we like it" [lyric.heShe] says with some disdain. "Just so you know." [lyric.HeShe] takes a deep breath through [lyric.hisHer] nose. "I don't know, I don't think it's too terribly different from what you're used to in your [pc.race] villages and settlements. Most of us are miners looking for metals to add to our stockpiles, but you also have your wet-nurses; your warriors; your occasional carpenters... every settlement has a village mother, but they sometimes go by different-but-the-same titles, like the queen of the Undermountain, and she's always the one in charge." It's always a queen? There's never a king kobold? "Kobolds get larger with every pregnancy they see through," Lyric explains. "But it's a pretty slow process. The village – sorry, the queens are always the largest, the strongest, and, very often, the oldest and most experienced. They're usually the protection and intimidation against raiders, along with our warriors. And in exchange, everyone underneath them does whatever they say." Sounds more like a beehive to you.[pc.hasCock |[lyric.mf | | So... how many pregnancies would she need to have in order to become a queen herself? [lyric.isTall | "At this point, becoming a Village Mother might actually be a downgrade," she laughs as she runs her hands over her exposed thighs. The action isn't meant to be sexual: it's meant to highlight that she's very different from how she was before. "But if I was still a kobold? ]Oh... a hundred, maybe? Maybe more?" she answers. And how often can kobolds be pregnant in a year? "Once a month. It takes another month for the egg to hatch, but we're good to go almost as soon as the egg is laid." [lyric.isTall |You ask her if she ever had any fantasies of being a queen herself. |You ask if she'd like to be a queen someday. ] "Yeah, sounds like a pretty nice lifestyle to me!" she answers, her eyes wandering and lighting up with fantasies of being waited on hand-and-foot. "All the attention you could ask for; all the food you could want; and everybody does whatever you say? Yeah, sign me up!" [lyric.isTall |What's to stop her from having both? Is it not possible for her to be both a queen and a dragon? |How soon would she like to get started? ] She hesitates at the question. "I don't know. [lyric.isTall |I'm kind of busy traveling with you right now. |Once I'm done traveling with you? ]" As soon as the words leave her mouth, she startles herself. "Oh, goodness... I've never thought that far ahead. I don't think I want to stop traveling with you, [pc.name]." Her brow furrows in thought. "So... never, I guess?" What if she could be a queen with you? She pauses, considering what it is you're asking. "But," she says haltingly, "I... I don't think I want to be your queen. I like what you and I have now, [pc.name]. I like to think I'm being good to you. I mean...." She pauses again, trying to put her thoughts into words. "I guess I'd make a good queen for you. You're already a good queen to me[pc.mf |," she says without a moment's hesitation. " |. ]Maybe nothing would change?" This is more difficult than you expected, so you change subjects. ] ] You ask if they do anything for recreation. "What do you mean?" Like, music, art, poetry? [lyric.HeShe] said that they had carpenters; have they ever built statues or commemorative buildings that served a purpose other than to just be a building? "No, nothing like that," Lyric answers. "We just like to live, is all." That... hardly sounds like living to you. That sounds like surviving. "Right. We just like to survive, is all." You aren't sure how to feel about that. "

rows.translation: 狗头人

rows.original: [lyric.isTall |Way back w |W ]hen you two first got acquainted with each other, [lyric.heShe] said that [lyric.heShe] was interested in the ‘sciences,' and then [lyric.heShe] started spouting some trivia about science that, honestly, just sounded like magic to you. You ask [lyric.himHer] if [lyric.heShe] could elaborate on what [lyric.heShe] was talking about. "See, the big difference between magic and science is that magic requires a focus of some kind. It could be a gemstone, or something as simple as a tattoo or whatever. A mage could conjure a fireball from between their hands or shoot lightning from their fingertips, but ask yourself: why is it that lightning strikes during a thunderstorm? [lyric.isTall |Why can dragons and kobolds breathe fire, but, say, humans cannot? ]Why is it that, when nature 'casts' magic, the rules for it are different?" You admit that you had never considered that angle. When something happens in nature that you can't explain and nobody was around to cast a spell, was it a magician that did it? "My fascination with the sciences started when I was much younger: I was playing in a field of grass, and then I touched a metal chunk that I got for my afternoon snack. I got such a shock, I can still feel it!" [lyric.heShe] laughs as [lyric.heShe] wrings [lyric.hisHer] fingers as if [lyric.heShe] was just shocked by something. "I remember asking myself, ‘why did that happen?' So, I tried doing everything that I did again, in order to replicate the shock when I touched the knob – and it worked!" "Ever since then, I've had two objectives to my life's mission: the first," [lyric.heShe] says, extending [lyric.hisHer] index finger, "is to learn how, on a more... 'mechanical' level, I guess? I want to learn how magic really works. We know a magician needs a focus, and that magic can take so many different forms, and that all you need to cast a bit of it is a focus and some knowledge on what you're doing. But I want to know how a focus and an understanding of the laws of our universe causes fire to be conjured between our palms, or for a summoner to create a primitive life form out of some rocks or something. Nature can cast lightning from some clouds in the sky, and it doesn't use a focus – if I can understand how it does that, I'll be one step closer to understand how we can do it from our fingertips and a pretty rock." "And the second," [lyric.heShe] says, extending [lyric.hisHer] middle finger, "is to see if there are other methods of magic that we haven't found yet." You ask [lyric.himHer] if [lyric.heShe] has any ideas on what a ‘new form of magic' could be. "Not a one!" [lyric.heShe] admits with a cheery laugh. "We already have people that can make golems from nothing with a basic form of sentience and we can already shoot fire, and cold, and lightning from our hands. I have no idea where we could go from here!" [lyric.HisHer] eyes light up, growing larger with excitement. "But that's what makes it so exciting to me, [pc.name]: there's so much that we don't know about the world already. All it would take is a small discovery – like, I don't know, maybe metal can still hold a charge of electricity after a bolt passes through it – and that'd start a snowball of discoveries towards a new, more exciting world." From the sounds of things, [lyric.heShe]'s very excited about this mission of [lyric.mf |his |hers ], and [lyric.heShe]'s really committed to seeing it through. You ask if [lyric.heShe]'s been keeping any notes on [lyric.hisHer] progress – discoveries, ideas, progresses, anything that [lyric.heShe] could reference later, and anything that someone else could reference and continue on from. "Nope!" [lyric.heShe] answers with a wide smile. "I can't read. Everything I know," [lyric.heShe] says, tapping at [lyric.hisHer] skull, "is in here." That's a shame, and [lyric.heShe] should really put [lyric.hisHer] effort into learning. It's a macabre thought, but it'd be a huge loss to the world if something happened to [lyric.himHer] before [lyric.heShe] managed to put [lyric.hisHer] discoveries to parchment. You offer to teach Lyric how to read and write someday. At the suggestion, Lyric's smile shrinks to nothing; [lyric.hisHer] golden eyes get as wide as can be; and [lyric.hisHer] tail starts thumping against the [atCamp |ground |floor ] at a remarkably fast pace. "I'd love nothing more," [lyric.heShe] says with no small amount of reverence and awe. "Me, learning how to read...?" The reaction catches you a bit off-guard, but, you suppose, reading is something that you've taken for granted ever since you've learned how to do it. For someone like Lyric, it makes sense that [lyric.heShe]'d be as excited for it as [lyric.heShe] is. [lyric.isTall |You have a few more questions in mind about [lyric.hisHer] focuses on the sciences |Before you wrap up, you ask Lyric one last question ]: if [lyric.heShe]'s as focused on [lyric.isTall |them |the sciences ] as [lyric.heShe] says [lyric.heShe] is, then what does [lyric.heShe] think of alchemy, a proven school of study for the not-strictly-magical? "Well, the reason why I don't focus on alchemy now is because I'm too deep into my studies to want to switch," [lyric.heShe] answers. "But the reason why I didn't focus on alchemy back then is because, where I come from, all things alchemy weren't very easy to come by: anything from equipment to reagents was a difficult find. But you know what we did have?" You say nothing, allowing Lyric to answer [lyric.hisHer] surely-rhetorical question for you. "D-do...," [lyric.heShe] stutters, "do... you not know what we had?" Oh, apparently it wasn't rhetorical. You think about it for a moment. "Metal?" you ask tentatively. "Yes!" [lyric.heShe] answers, breathing a sigh of relief that you were smart enough to answer. "It turns out, metal is a pretty good jumping point for getting started on learning the material beginnings to science and magic. And we had heaps of the stuff lying around – anything that we weren't using for food was fair game. So, I started with what I had." Makes sense to you. [lyric.isTall |Which brings you to your last question: Lyric is a dragon now. Does [lyric.heShe] attribute that to the sciences, or to alchemy? "It's because of alchemy," [lyric.heShe] answers, arching [lyric.hisHer] brow downward, confused why you would ask that. "Science... how do I explain this... science is more about the method. The journey. It's about understanding why, down to as minute a detail as possible, and replicating your results perfectly every time, because you understand it so completely." "And alchemy... puts less emphasis on the 'how's' and 'why's' and is more focused on the end result. Turning lead into gold, or, in my case, a kobold into a dragon. Consistency is important – what worked for me ought to work for any other kobold – but... I feel like trying to dissect alchemy down to its building blocks is kind of missing the point of alchemy. What matters is that I'm a dragon now." Lyric pauses, trying to put more of [lyric.hisHer] thoughts to words. It takes [lyric.himHer] a few seconds. "Let me... try to put it this way," [lyric.heShe] says. "Imagine you're walking down a beaten path in a forest. Science is... staring at the ground, counting your steps, and noting how many steps it took. Then doing it a day later and seeing if you take the same amount of steps, and if not, try to understand why. Was the humidity different? Were your strides longer or shorter, and if so, why? Were you, I don't know, wearing different boots that day?" "And alchemy," [lyric.heShe] says, lifting [lyric.hisHer] right hand, palm up, "is walking down that beaten path in the forest, looking at the green trees, the blue sky, breathing in the fresh air, letting your mind wander... and then you're at the end of the path. You barely remember the walk; you just remember that you enjoyed it." ... That's quite the answer you just got from [lyric.himHer]. You honestly weren't expecting it. Maybe Lyric should have been a philosopher, not a scientist. "Nah," [lyric.heShe] replies with a dismissive wave of [lyric.hisHer] hand. "I just need to know what I'm talking about. And by the way?" [lyric.heShe] continues without even pausing to breathe. "Turning lead into gold is the Promised Land for either science or alchemy." [lyric.HeShe] licks [lyric.hisHer] lips, then does it again. "Actually, that's probably something you don't want either dragons or kobolds to learn." ]
rows.translation: [lyric.isTall |很久很久以前…… |W ]当你们俩刚开始认识的时候[lyric.heShe]说道[lyric.heShe]对那些“科学领域”很感兴趣，然后[lyric.heShe]开始滔滔不绝地讲一些关于科学的冷知识，说实话，那些内容对你来说简直就像魔法一样神奇。你问道：[lyric.himHer]如果[lyric.heShe]可以详细说明一下[lyric.heShe]你看，魔法与科学之间的最大区别就在于，魔法需要某种媒介作为载体。这种媒介可能是一颗宝石，也可能像纹身这样的简单东西。法师可以从手中召唤出火球，也可以从指尖释放闪电，但你想想：为什么在雷雨天气里才会出现闪电呢？ [lyric.isTall |为什么龙和狗头人能够喷火，而人类却不能呢？ ]为什么当大自然施展‘魔法’时，其规则会与众不同呢？” “你承认自己之前从未从这个角度思考过这个问题。当大自然中发生一些你无法解释的现象，而且当时也没有人在进行任何魔法仪式时，难道真的是有魔术师在背后操纵这一切吗？” “我对科学的兴趣其实早在我很小的时候就产生了：那是在一片草地上玩耍的时候，我无意中触到了一块用来当下午零食的金属块。当时我受到了巨大的电击，那种感觉至今仍然历历在目！[lyric.heShe]笑着说[lyric.heShe]拧紧[lyric.hisHer]手指仿佛在动[lyric.heShe]我当时真的被这件事震惊了。我记得自己当时在想：‘为什么会发生这种事呢？’于是，我重新做了所有那些事情，试图重现当初触摸那个旋钮时所感受到的那种震惊——结果真的成功了！” “从那以后，我的人生目标就明确了两个：第一个目标就是[lyric.heShe]说道，并继续说道[lyric.hisHer]食指，我想，就是想要在更……“机械”的层面上了解如何运用它吧？我想真正弄明白魔法究竟是如何运作的。可行。我们知道，魔术师需要一个专注点，而魔法可以呈现出各种各样的形式。其实，要施展魔法，你所需要的仅仅是一个专注点，以及对自己所要做的事情有所了解而已。但我想知道如何当我们能够专注于并理解宇宙的法则时，我们就能够让火焰在手掌中浮现；或者让施法者用一些石头之类的物质创造出原始的生命形态。大自然也能从天空中的云层中释放闪电，而它并没有使用任何聚焦的手段——如果我能弄明白它是如何做到这一点的，那么我就离理解整个宇宙的运作机制又近了一步。我们可以轻而易举地做到这一点，只需要一个普通的石头而已。” “而第二点[lyric.heShe]说道，同时伸出了手。[lyric.hisHer]竖中指，其实是在试探是否还有其他我们尚未发现的魔法手段。[lyric.himHer]如果[lyric.heShe]对于“新的魔法形式”会是什么样，你有什么想法吗？ “一个想法都没有！[lyric.heShe]开心地笑着承认道：“我们已经有人能够凭空创造出具有基本感知能力的魔像，而且我们现在已经能够从手中释放火焰、寒冰和闪电了。我真的不知道接下来还能取得什么成就！[lyric.HisHer]眼睛亮了起来，因兴奋而变得更大。“恰恰因为这样，它才让我觉得如此兴奋。[pc.name]：有太多的事情我们需要去处理不要他们对这个世界已经有了相当多的了解。所需要的，只是一个小小的发现——比如，也许金属在电流穿过之后仍然能够保持电荷——而这个发现就会引发一系列进一步的探索，从而引领我们进入一个全新的、更加令人兴奋的世界。” 从目前的情况来看[lyric.heShe]对于这次任务，他感到非常兴奋。 [lyric.mf |他的 |她的 ]，以及[lyric.heShe]真的下定了决心要完成这件事。你问[lyric.heShe]一直在记录着些什么。[lyric.hisHer]进展——无论是发现、想法，还是各种形式的进步，任何这些都属于进展的范畴。[lyric.heShe]不行！[lyric.heShe]微笑着回答：“我不识字。我所知道的一切，都是别人告诉我的。[lyric.heShe]说着，一边轻敲着[lyric.hisHer]骷髅就在里面。” “真可惜[lyric.heShe]真的应该去做。[lyric.hisHer]投入在学习上的努力。虽然这个想法听起来有些可怕，但如果发生了什么，那对世界来说将是一大损失。[lyric.himHer]在[lyric.heShe]之前成功完成了[lyric.hisHer]将这些发现记录在羊皮纸上。你承诺有朝一日会教莉里克如何读写。 听到这个建议，莉里克的笑容立刻消失了。[lyric.hisHer]金色的眼睛睁得大大的；[lyric.hisHer]尾巴开始剧烈地抽打着[atCamp |地面 |地板 ]速度快得惊人。“我再没有比这更想要的了。[lyric.heShe]带着几分敬畏和惊叹说道：“我，竟然还在学习阅读……？” 这种反应让你有些措手不及，但仔细想来，阅读对于你来说应该是一件理所当然的事情——毕竟你从学会阅读的那一刻起，就再也没把阅读当作什么特别的事情。对于像莉里克这样的人来说，这种反应倒也在情理之中。[lyric.heShe]我会像其他人一样为它感到兴奋。[lyric.heShe]是。 [lyric.isTall |你还有几个问题想要询问。[lyric.hisHer]专注于科学研究 |在结束之前，你向莉里克提出了最后一个问题。 ]如果[lyric.heShe]专注于[lyric.isTall |他们 |自然科学 ]如同[lyric.heShe]表示……的意思[lyric.heShe]那么，究竟是什么呢？[lyric.heShe]想想炼金术吧，这可是一门经过实践验证的、与纯粹的魔法并无直接关系的学科啊。 “嗯，我之所以不专注于炼金术现在是因为我目前的学习任务实在太繁重了，因此没有精力去更换其他事情。[lyric.heShe]但我之前没有专注于炼金术的原因其实是然后原因在于，在我成长的地方，所有与炼金术相关的物品都很难获得：从设备到炼金材料，这些东西都极难找到。但是你知道我们当时确实拥有什么吗？” 你没有说话，于是莉里克便回答了。[lyric.hisHer]呃[lyric.heShe]结结巴巴地说：“你……你难道不知道我们曾经拥有过什么吗？” “哦，原来这不是在反问。”你仔细想了想，然后试探性地问道：“金属吗？” “是的！[lyric.heShe]答案就在这里，听到你能够聪明地想出答案，我真是松了一口气。原来，金属其实是了解科学和魔法的基本原理的一个很好的切入点。而且我们手头也有大量的金属——任何没有被用来制作食物的金属都可以用来研究。所以，我就从手头现有的材料开始研究。 [lyric.isTall |这就引出了你的最后一个问题：莉里克现在已经变成了一条龙了，对吧？[lyric.heShe]这是科学的作用，还是炼金术的成果呢？ “这是炼金术的功劳。[lyric.heShe]答案，呈拱形[lyric.hisHer]皱着眉头，不明白为什么你会提出这样的问题。“科学……我该怎么解释呢……科学更注重方法，注重探索的过程。它的本质在于理解。为什么甚至要细致到最小的细节，每次都能完美地重现你的实验结果，因为你对这个过程有着极其透彻的理解。” “而炼金术……则较少关注‘如何’和‘为什么’，它更注重最终的结果。将铅变成金，或者在我的例子中，把一只狗头人变成一条龙。一致性很重要——对我有效的方法，对其他狗头人也应该有效——但是……我觉得，如果试图把炼金术分解成它的基本构成要素，那就有点偏离了炼金术的真正意义了。重要的是，我现在已经变成了一条龙。” 莱瑞克停顿了一下，试图进一步表达自己的意思[lyric.hisHer]将想法转化为文字，这需要一定的时间。[lyric.himHer]几秒钟后，他说：“让我……试着这样表达吧。[lyric.heShe]想象一下，你正在森林里的一条小路上行走。科学，其实就是这样——它关注着你每一步的落脚点，记录着你走了多少步。然后第二天再重复这个过程，看看你走的步数是否还是一样的；如果不同，就要尝试找出原因。是当天的湿度不同了吗？还是你的步幅变长了或变短了，如果是这样，原因又是什么呢？又或者，那天你穿的靴子不一样了？” “而炼金术，也是如此。[lyric.heShe]说着，便抬起了手。[lyric.hisHer]右手掌心向上，想象着自己正沿着森林里那条熟悉的小路行走，欣赏着绿树、蓝天，呼吸着清新的空气，让思绪自由驰骋……最终，你走到了小路的尽头。你几乎想不起这一路的历程，只记得自己非常享受这段旅程。 ……你刚刚从[lyric.himHer]那里得到了一个相当不凡的回答，说实话，你完全没料到。也许莉里克应该成为一名哲学家，而不是科学家。 “嗯，也不是吧。[lyric.heShe]只是随意地挥了挥手作为回应[lyric.hisHer]我只需要知道自己在说什么而已。顺便问一下？[lyric.heShe]甚至没有停下来喘口气，就继续说道：“将铅变成金，对于科学而言，就是那片应许之地；而对于炼金术来说，也同样如此。[lyric.HeShe]舔食[lyric.hisHer]嘴唇动了动，然后又重复了一遍。“其实，那可能是你该做的事情不要希望龙族或狗头人都能学会这些技能。 rows.raw: ' [lyric.isTall |Way back w |W ]hen you two first got acquainted with each other, [lyric.heShe] said that [lyric.heShe] was interested in the ‘sciences,' and then [lyric.heShe] started spouting some trivia about science that, honestly, just sounded like magic to you. You ask [lyric.himHer] if [lyric.heShe] could elaborate on what [lyric.heShe] was talking about. "See, the big difference between magic and science is that magic requires a focus of some kind. It could be a gemstone, or something as simple as a tattoo or whatever. A mage could conjure a fireball from between their hands or shoot lightning from their fingertips, but ask yourself: why is it that lightning strikes during a thunderstorm? [lyric.isTall |Why can dragons and kobolds breathe fire, but, say, humans cannot? ]Why is it that, when nature 'casts' magic, the rules for it are different?" You admit that you had never considered that angle. When something happens in nature that you can't explain and nobody was around to cast a spell, was it a magician that did it? "My fascination with the sciences started when I was much younger: I was playing in a field of grass, and then I touched a metal chunk that I got for my afternoon snack. I got such a shock, I can still feel it!" [lyric.heShe] laughs as [lyric.heShe] wrings [lyric.hisHer] fingers as if [lyric.heShe] was just shocked by something. "I remember asking myself, ‘why did that happen?' So, I tried doing everything that I did again, in order to replicate the shock when I touched the knob – and it worked!" "Ever since then, I've had two objectives to my life's mission: the first," [lyric.heShe] says, extending [lyric.hisHer] index finger, "is to learn how, on a more... 'mechanical' level, I guess? I want to learn how magic really works. We know a magician needs a focus, and that magic can take so many different forms, and that all you need to cast a bit of it is a focus and some knowledge on what you're doing. But I want to know how a focus and an understanding of the laws of our universe causes fire to be conjured between our palms, or for a summoner to create a primitive life form out of some rocks or something. Nature can cast lightning from some clouds in the sky, and it doesn't use a focus – if I can understand how it does that, I'll be one step closer to understand how we can do it from our fingertips and a pretty rock." "And the second," [lyric.heShe] says, extending [lyric.hisHer] middle finger, "is to see if there are other methods of magic that we haven't found yet." You ask [lyric.himHer] if [lyric.heShe] has any ideas on what a ‘new form of magic' could be. "Not a one!" [lyric.heShe] admits with a cheery laugh. "We already have people that can make golems from nothing with a basic form of sentience and we can already shoot fire, and cold, and lightning from our hands. I have no idea where we could go from here!" [lyric.HisHer] eyes light up, growing larger with excitement. "But that's what makes it so exciting to me, [pc.name]: there's so much that we don't know about the world already. All it would take is a small discovery – like, I don't know, maybe metal can still hold a charge of electricity after a bolt passes through it – and that'd start a snowball of discoveries towards a new, more exciting world." From the sounds of things, [lyric.heShe]'s very excited about this mission of [lyric.mf |his |hers ], and [lyric.heShe]'s really committed to seeing it through. You ask if [lyric.heShe]'s been keeping any notes on [lyric.hisHer] progress – discoveries, ideas, progresses, anything that [lyric.heShe] could reference later, and anything that someone else could reference and continue on from. "Nope!" [lyric.heShe] answers with a wide smile. "I can't read. Everything I know," [lyric.heShe] says, tapping at [lyric.hisHer] skull, "is in here." That's a shame, and [lyric.heShe] should really put [lyric.hisHer] effort into learning. It's a macabre thought, but it'd be a huge loss to the world if something happened to [lyric.himHer] before [lyric.heShe] managed to put [lyric.hisHer] discoveries to parchment. You offer to teach Lyric how to read and write someday. At the suggestion, Lyric's smile shrinks to nothing; [lyric.hisHer] golden eyes get as wide as can be; and [lyric.hisHer] tail starts thumping against the [atCamp |ground |floor ] at a remarkably fast pace. "I'd love nothing more," [lyric.heShe] says with no small amount of reverence and awe. "Me, learning how to read...?" The reaction catches you a bit off-guard, but, you suppose, reading is something that you've taken for granted ever since you've learned how to do it. For someone like Lyric, it makes sense that [lyric.heShe]'d be as excited for it as [lyric.heShe] is. [lyric.isTall |You have a few more questions in mind about [lyric.hisHer] focuses on the sciences |Before you wrap up, you ask Lyric one last question ]: if [lyric.heShe]'s as focused on [lyric.isTall |them |the sciences ] as [lyric.heShe] says [lyric.heShe] is, then what does [lyric.heShe] think of alchemy, a proven school of study for the not-strictly-magical? "Well, the reason why I don't focus on alchemy now is because I'm too deep into my studies to want to switch," [lyric.heShe] answers. "But the reason why I didn't focus on alchemy back then is because, where I come from, all things alchemy weren't very easy to come by: anything from equipment to reagents was a difficult find. But you know what we did have?" You say nothing, allowing Lyric to answer [lyric.hisHer] surely-rhetorical question for you. "D-do...," [lyric.heShe] stutters, "do... you not know what we had?" Oh, apparently it wasn't rhetorical. You think about it for a moment. "Metal?" you ask tentatively. "Yes!" [lyric.heShe] answers, breathing a sigh of relief that you were smart enough to answer. "It turns out, metal is a pretty good jumping point for getting started on learning the material beginnings to science and magic. And we had heaps of the stuff lying around – anything that we weren't using for food was fair game. So, I started with what I had." Makes sense to you. [lyric.isTall |Which brings you to your last question: Lyric is a dragon now. Does [lyric.heShe] attribute that to the sciences, or to alchemy? "It's because of alchemy," [lyric.heShe] answers, arching [lyric.hisHer] brow downward, confused why you would ask that. "Science... how do I explain this... science is more about the method. The journey. It's about understanding why, down to as minute a detail as possible, and replicating your results perfectly every time, because you understand it so completely." "And alchemy... puts less emphasis on the 'how's' and 'why's' and is more focused on the end result. Turning lead into gold, or, in my case, a kobold into a dragon. Consistency is important – what worked for me ought to work for any other kobold – but... I feel like trying to dissect alchemy down to its building blocks is kind of missing the point of alchemy. What matters is that I'm a dragon now." Lyric pauses, trying to put more of [lyric.hisHer] thoughts to words. It takes [lyric.himHer] a few seconds. "Let me... try to put it this way," [lyric.heShe] says. "Imagine you're walking down a beaten path in a forest. Science is... staring at the ground, counting your steps, and noting how many steps it took. Then doing it a day later and seeing if you take the same amount of steps, and if not, try to understand why. Was the humidity different? Were your strides longer or shorter, and if so, why? Were you, I don't know, wearing different boots that day?" "And alchemy," [lyric.heShe] says, lifting [lyric.hisHer] right hand, palm up, "is walking down that beaten path in the forest, looking at the green trees, the blue sky, breathing in the fresh air, letting your mind wander... and then you're at the end of the path. You barely remember the walk; you just remember that you enjoyed it." ... That's quite the answer you just got from [lyric.himHer]. You honestly weren't expecting it. Maybe Lyric should have been a philosopher, not a scientist. "Nah," [lyric.heShe] replies with a dismissive wave of [lyric.hisHer] hand. "I just need to know what I'm talking about. And by the way?" [lyric.heShe] continues without even pausing to breathe. "Turning lead into gold is the Promised Land for either science or alchemy." [lyric.HeShe] licks [lyric.hisHer] lips, then does it again. "Actually, that's probably something you don't want either dragons or kobolds to learn." ] '

rows.raw: " You heft your pack up and set it across your back, ready to restart your journey. But after only a few steps, you feel an unusual rustling in your pack. It's not surprising – you have an entire kobold in there, after all – but [lyric.heShe] is usually inert and only comes out when you ask [lyric.himHer] to. Sure enough, after a few more seconds, Lyric's fingers break the opening of your pack and pry the mouth open, and [lyric.hisHer] head emerges from the opening. "Hey, [pc.name]?" [lyric.heShe] asks, [lyric.hisHer] mouth right next to your ear. "What is this? It feels, I dunno, kinda familiar, somehow." You look over your shoulder as [lyric.heShe] struggles to free [lyric.hisHer] arm; once [lyric.heShe] does, in [lyric.hisHer] open hand is [var0 |a dark red crystal, glowing faintly with an inner light, roughly the size of your thumbnail. Oh, that's... that's Dragonsblood. "What?!" [lyric.heShe] asks, jolting in your pack. "You have condensed dragon's blood, just... as a thing?" That's what you're told. [pc.ra dragon |It's what turned you into the [pc.isBimbo |sexy ]beast that you are right now. A few hits of that is all it takes to turn you into this.You're led to believe that, if you consume it, you'll be given the strength and [pc.isBimbo |sexiness |countenance ] of a dragon. ] "No way," [lyric.heShe] gasps, awed and wide-eyed at the little jewel sitting in the palm of [lyric.hisHer] upturned hand. Lyric stares at it, [lyric.hisHer] eyes wide as saucers; the glowing inner power of the jewel is consumed by the growing pitch-black pupils of [lyric.hisHer] eyes. Without breaking [lyric.hisHer] vision on it, Lyric asks, "[pc.ra dragon |is it yours? Like... is it your blood?" You answer that it isn't. "Oh, good. Then ]can I have it?" ... You're not against that, you suppose, but would it even do anything to [lyric.himHer]? Is consuming a dragon's blood all it takes for a kobold to become a dragon? [lyric.HeShe] breaks [lyric.hisHer] eye contact with the jewel and makes it with you instead. "Is that all it takes for [a] [pc.race]?" You're... different, and [lyric.heShe] ought to know that about you by now. "Well, the answer is no," [lyric.heShe] sighs forlornly. "There's a lot of truth about the stereotype about dragons having whole cabals of kobolds at their every beck and call. If drinking a dragon's blood was all it took, then every single kobold would have known about it. Unless it's, like, the universe's best kept secret. Kobolds aren't really the best secret-keepers." If it's true that dragons used to keep whole throngs of kobolds around, then, you suppose, other draconic fluids would be equally ineffective. "Right," Lyric replies quickly, seemingly oblivious to your insinuation. [lyric.HisHer] attention goes back to the crystal in [lyric.hisHer] palm. "But, like... things have changed. You, [pc.name], you can turn into just about any race, any sex, any person you want to be, just from having a weird diet. There's – there's gotta be a way that we could get this dragon's blood to work on me, right?" You note that Lyric seems awfully smitten with the idea of becoming a dragon. Is [lyric.heShe] not satisfied with what [lyric.heShe] is now? "That's–" [lyric.heShe] starts, then sputters, taken aback by the question. "That's an unfair question! Of course I'm satisfied with what I am, [pc.name]. It's because of what I am that I can travel with you like this." [lyric.HeShe] shuffles around in your pack, upsetting your balance slightly, to prove [lyric.hisHer] point. "But think of it from a kobold's perspective. rows.original: You heft your pack up and set it across your back, ready to restart your journey. But after only a few steps, you feel an unusual rustling in your pack. It's not surprising – you have an entire kobold in there, after all – but [lyric.heShe] is usually inert and only comes out when you ask [lyric.himHer] to. Sure enough, after a few more seconds, Lyric's fingers break the opening of your pack and pry the mouth open, and [lyric.hisHer] head emerges from the opening. "Hey, [pc.name]?" [lyric.heShe] asks, [lyric.hisHer] mouth right next to your ear. "Did you get this for me?" You look over your shoulder as [lyric.heShe] struggles to free [lyric.hisHer] arm; once [lyric.heShe] does, in [lyric.hisHer] open hand is [var0 |a long stalk, covered in ticklish hairs, lined with hexagonal auburn leaves. Oh, that's Cinderleaf. It's a common-enough weed with alchemical properties – and, if you remember right, it's considered a favorite snack for common lizards. You smirk: you would have thought kobolds were a step above a ‘common lizard'. "Hey, food is food," [lyric.heShe] replies, gently bopping the end of the stalk against your nose. "When you live out in the jungle or in a cave, sometimes, you don't have the luxury to be picky about your lunch. And Cinderleaf just happens to be yummy!" You tell Lyric that you have plans for that Cinderleaf. It's why you got it in the first place. You tell [lyric.himHer] that it's not for [lyric.himHer], and not to eat it. "Dang," [lyric.heShe] hums dejectedly as [lyric.heShe] lowers [lyric.hisHer] hand back into the pack. "Okay, whatever you say." |a crunched, wrinkled, discarded leaf, so nondescript that, frankly, it could have come from any tree that sprouts leaves. It's suspended in an equally nondescript fluid that clings to the leaf's pores, preventing further decay. Oh, that's an Ashen Leaf. You tell Lyric that, no, it's not for [lyric.himHer], and that you have plans for it. And that [lyric.heShe] should probably stop touching it. "Oh, uhh," [lyric.heShe] stutters. [lyric.HeShe] pulls [lyric.himHer]self away from [lyric.hisHer] own palm, as if [lyric.hisHer] hand wasn't attached to the rest of [lyric.himHer]self, then struggles to fit it pack into the pack without letting the leaf touch any other part of [lyric.hisHer] body. Your pack isn't that big; there's only so much space [lyric.heShe] can make for [lyric.himHer]self away from your cursed artifacts. You ask [lyric.himHer] why [lyric.heShe] asks. You would have figured that a kobold like [lyric.himHer] wouldn't have had any interest in vegetation. "Well, it's ‘cause that's a Cinderleaf," [lyric.heShe] answers. "Or, I mean, it was a Cinderleaf at one point. Cinderleafs are a good snack for any lizard and lizard-race. I thought you were offering me food." Food that's been suspended in some kind of weird, floating, unmoving liquid? "I thought it might have been juicy." Lyric's naïve [pc.isDK |"charm" is difficult to put up with sometimes. Thank whoever's listening that [lyric.heShe]'s such a willing little [lyric.hasVagina |cocksock |pocket-rocket ]. |charm is one of the reasons you keep [lyric.himHer] around. Only someone like [lyric.himHer] could have come to the conclusions [lyric.heShe] just did. ] |a long bluish-green stem covered in thin, ticklish hairs, covered in hexagonal sapphire leaves. Oh, that's Frostleaf. It's a common-enough weed with alchemical properties – and, if you remember right, it's considered a favorite snack for common lizards. You smirk: you would have thought kobolds were a step above a ‘common lizard'. "Hey, food is food," [lyric.heShe] replies, gently bopping the end of the stalk against your nose. "When you live out in the jungle or in a cave, sometimes, you don't have the luxury to be picky about your lunch. And while I don't think Frostleaf is as tasty as Cinderleaf, Frostleaf has this chill, refreshing foretaste to it that kinda reminds me of water. It's a nice snack!" You tell Lyric that you have plans for that Frostleaf. It's why you got it in the first place. You tell [lyric.himHer] that it's not for [lyric.himHer], and not to eat it. "Dang," [lyric.heShe] hums dejectedly as [lyric.heShe] lowers [lyric.hisHer] hand back into the pack. "Okay, whatever you say." ] ... Although, while Lyric is out and while the topic is on your mind, you ask: are the kobolds related to the salamander race at all? There are variants among the salamanders – namely, Cinderscale and Frostscale – just like how there are variants among the kobolds based on their geography. And Cinderleaf is a favorite snack that they both enjoy. "We're... related, yeah," [lyric.heShe] answers with an unusually unsteady tone. "In the same way that a human is related to an orc. They both have skin; they both stand on two feet; fingers, toes, teeth, hair, eyes... but you also wouldn't call a human an orc, you know? Not unless you're looking to pick a fight." Does that mean that you asking if kobolds and salamanders are the same were fighting words? "Not with me. I'm not much of a fighter," [lyric.heShe] laughs sheepishly. "A different kobold or salamander might have thought you were dumb, though." That's... okay. Cool. "Although, now that you bring it up," [lyric.heShe] continues, oblivious to your tone and sudden tension, "salamanders and kobolds are similar in that we have a common ancestor. I don't know if humans and orcs share a common ancestor like that. We came from dragons!" You pivot on the spot, trying to look further over your shoulder towards Lyric. Dragons are a thing of myth, and the myths say that they were the size of houses. They were fearsome, one-step-short-of-godlike creatures, capable of blotting out the sun with their wingspan, or [silly |burninating |[pc.isBimbo |burning |immolating ] ] a countryside with a single breath. And sitting in your pack, supposedly descended from such a monster, is a four-foot lizard[lyric.electrumRange 0 200 | | with a fat ass ]. It's a bit of a downgrade. "Now, I know it's a bit of a downgrade," Lyric continues, "but that's kinda what you get, I guess, when you breed outside your species for a few hundred generations. But there's a direct line from both kobolds and salamanders straight to dragons. If you believe the oral history, anyway." You aren't positive what to do with this trivia, that salamanders and kobolds are both directly descended from dragons. But... maybe it'll come in handy someday.

rows.original: "I just have to know," you confess. "How do you keep your clothes clean?" "Ahaha!" Evelyn laughs, her barely-concealed breasts shaking in her vibrant red dress. "It is quite the mystery, isn't it? Such a dirty village and yet not a speck of dirt to be seen across my clothing. I'm loathe to spoil the fun, but since you asked: they're enchanted." She smiles. "It simply wouldn't do to have my heels all covered in mud." Sure enough, she dips the tip of one heel into a muddy, carriage-created puddle and you watch as the liquid simply wicks away and drips back to the ground. "That makes so much more sense," you say, shaking your head. "Of course, I myself am distinctly non-magic," Evelyn titters. "So I often find myself having to be washed. Fortunate that there's no lack of willing attendants in Hawkethorne." "I can imagine," you murmur, glancing at the hem of her dress. It's hard to believe her considerable endowments can possibly be hidden away, but the proof is right before your eyes. "Well, have fun on your walk, Evelyn." "You too," she says, winking. "Do stop by my room later, [pc.name]." With that, she struts away and disappears into the throng of people.

    "I bet! First kidnappings, then raiders, now monsters from the woods... I wonder if [flags.TODO_BARON_DISPOSED|[pc.name]|the baroness] will ever call for a standing guard?"
    
    "Maybe. Maybe..."
rows.translation:
你看到镇上的炼金术士坐在她店铺的门阶上，正在研钵里研磨草药。兽人铁匠奥格里什靠在她身旁的墙上。两人正深谈着，你只听到零星几句：
    
    “多亏维伦，我们的药终于到货了！”艾薇莉丝叹道，“我本来真的很担心。山里那些掠夺者抢走了不少，不过我们现在有足够的量撑过冬天了。只要别出什么坏事……”
    
    奥格里什哼了一声。“真出了事也不要紧，现在有我的青铜了。今天早上刚有个贾西拉商人经过，拿一大堆锡换了石头和木材，货已经送到我这儿了。现在可以开始给民兵打造新武器了。加斯一直催得紧。”
    
    “可不是嘛！先是绑架案，然后是掠夺者，现在又是森林里冒出来的怪物……我在想，[flags.TODO_BARON_DISPOSED|[pc.name]|女男爵]到底会不会组建一支常备卫队？”
    
    “也许吧。也许……”

rows.translation: 下一步
桑德斯与莉娅登

rows.original:
Brother Sanders and Liaden are walking down the street opposite you, deep in conversation.
    
    "I just don't understand how you can set aside Lumia's light," the younger paladin laments, rapping her knuckles on her bronze breastplate. "Ma said you'd dedicated your life to her, didn't you?"
    
    Sanders casts his gaze down. "There are seven gods, Lia, and none of them demand — or even suggest — that we recognize only one of them. This village was dedicated in Velun's name, and it's the oak-father who provides all that they have. When I settled here, I decided it would not be right for the only priest in town to proselytize a different deity."
    
    Liaden gives her father a suspicious look. "Pa, I ain't judging, but... oh, hey [pc.name]!"
    
    You wave as the two clergy pass you by.
rows.translation:
桑德斯修士和莉娅登正在你对面的街道上边走边谈，聊得十分投入。
    
    “我就是不明白，你怎么能把卢米娅的光辉放到一边，”年轻的圣骑士抱怨道，指节敲着自己的青铜胸甲。“妈说你曾把一生都献给了她，不是吗？”
    
    桑德斯垂下目光。“世上有七位神祇，莉娅，没有一位要求——甚至暗示——我们只能信奉其中一位。这个村庄奉维伦之名建立，而他们拥有的一切都由橡树之父赐予。我在这里定居时便认定，镇上唯一的祭司不该向居民传扬另一位神祇。”
    
    莉娅登怀疑地看着父亲。“爸，我不是在评判你，只是……哦，嘿，[pc.name]！”
    
    两位神职人员从你身旁经过时，你朝他们挥了挥手。

rows.translation: 下一步
桑德斯与莉娅登

rows.original:
Liaden is sitting on the steps of the town chapel, nursing a mug of something steamy-hot. Her father is standing behind her, watching the stars. Sanders seems much older now, more world-worn in his unguarded personal time — especially when a young woman who looks just like him is so close by for contrast. 

    Liaden seems to be praying. "As the sun sets, we pray she come again to warm our hearts. We light our hearth-fires to remind ourselves of her embrace."
    
    "And we hold each other tight," Sanders finishes, reaching down and squeezing his daughter's shoulder. "For the night is [silly|dark and full of terrors|long and dark, but together, we shall endure]."
    
    "We shall endure," Liaden echoes, putting her hand over his. "Together."
    
    "Together."
    
    Aww.
rows.translation:
莉娅登坐在镇上小教堂的台阶上，手中捧着一杯热气腾腾的饮品。她的父亲站在她身后，凝视着夜空中的星星。桑德斯如今看起来成熟了许多，在那些不经意的私人时刻，他显得更加饱经世故——尤其是当有一个与他外貌一模一样的年轻女子就在他身边时，这种对比更加明显。 

    莉娅登似乎在祈祷：“当太阳落山时，我们祈祷她能再次归来，温暖我们的心灵。我们点燃炉火，以此来回忆她给予我们的温暖与拥抱。”
    
    “我们也紧紧相拥，”桑德斯接着说道，伸手捏了捏女儿的肩膀。“因为夜晚[silly|黑暗而充满恐惧|漫长而黑暗，但只要我们在一起，就一定能撑过去]。”
    
    “我们会撑过去的，”莉娅登应声道，把手覆在他的手上。“一起。”
    
    “一起。”
    
    哎呀……

阿兹兰与莉娅登

rows.original:
Liaden and Azyrran are walking the market, hand in hand, talking quietly with each other. Azzy [azzy.kdb
        |giggles every so often, clearly enchanted by the smaller paladin.
        |has draped one of her wings regally over the smaller paladin's shoulders, really emphasizing how much larger and more muscular your mighty hornet really is.
        |is giggling and buzzing her wings every so often, making her heaving honey-laden just bounce under her top... and Liaden can't take her eyes off them no matter how hard she tries. Not that Azzy minds!
    ]
    
    They spot you and both wave, smiling warmly. Seems like they're having a nice time.
rows.translation:
莉娅登和阿兹兰手牵着手在市场上散步，两人轻声地交谈着。阿齐[azzy.kdb
        |她偶尔会咯咯笑起来，显然被这位年轻的圣骑士迷住了。
        |她将自己的一只翅膀优雅地搭在那位较矮小的圣骑士肩上，这更加凸显出你那位强大的大黄蜂究竟有多么庞大、多么肌肉发达。
        |她时不时地咯咯笑着，还振动着自己的翅膀，让那对饱含蜂蜜、起伏不定的乳房在她上衣下不停弹动……而无论莉娅登如何努力，她的目光都无法从它们身上移开。不过，阿齐显然并不在意这些！
    ]
    
    他们看到了你，两人都微笑着向你挥手。看起来他们玩得非常开心。

rows.original: Just as you're wondering where to head next, a voice calls out to you from the statue in the middle of the town square, a rich and smooth tenor. "Ah! A new face! Mind if I have a moment of your time, my [pc.race] friend?" You turn to face the speaker, and find a pint-sized catfolk lounging on a wrought-iron bench by the foot of the statue; he tilts his head upwards to acknowledge you as your eyes meet. At first, you're not quite sure that he's not a child — his looks are certainly very childlike — but judging by the deepness of his voice, he's no youngling. And there's the matter of the lute propped up in his lap — a musician [pc.bg minstrel|like you|of some sort], then. As you step forward, the little catboy extends a hand which you take, and his fingers are surprisingly strong despite their fine appearance. [party.has cait |"Awww, aren't you the cutest little thing!" Cait gushes cheerily. "The temples back in Jassira are just packed with kittens like you!" The bard just chuckles. "I might be descended from Jassirans, but I've never been there, so I'll take your word for it." ] So, is something the matter? "Right, allow me to introduce myself. I'm River. River, the Singing Arrow, and it's a pleasure to see a new face around Hawkethorne. It can get really dreary up here sometimes, especially about wintertime. But that's what Garth keeps me around here for — to liven things up and get people thirsty; I've been around this village for as long as he has! Ah! And your name is?" [pc.name]. "Right, right, [pc.name], [pc.name]. I've heard a lot about you — you're the talk of the town, helping [party.has cait|Caitriss Zethra right over there|a poor kitten] with her problems, heading out into the cold and dark on a mission of bravery and derring-do. Yes, yes, I know the whole story. Garth supplied most of it, but I went up to the temple and investigated myself, along with several other accounts..." [party.has cait |Cait's eyes widen a bit. "Wait, how do you know my full name? I haven't — " |He certainly is the inquisitive sort, isn't he? ] River stops strumming his lute long enough to wave dismissively. "Musician aside, I'm what passes for the town crier, after a fashion — it's my job to know things and collect news from people passing through, and repeat that for a small fee. That, or if there's something you'd like everyone in town to know, I can make that happen for the same small fee." "So yes, of course I would know such a small detail." [party.has cait |Cait folds her arms at that, still not quite satisfied with River's explanation, but she can't argue with it in her current state of mind. ] So, he's a musician of some sort? "Exactly. Although I do prefer the word 'bard.' It has a certain romantic feel to it, and implies a lot more finesse than something as bland as 'musician.' 'Troubadour' is simply too flighty, and 'minstrel' evokes a courtly connotation that really isn't present here. Don't you agree?" If he wants to be called a bard, fine, he can be one. "Now then, you're on a quest, are you not?" That is... technically true, although you're a little overwhelmed as to where to begin. And what business is it of his, anyways, besides being the local busybody? "Well, my good [pc.mf|sir|madam], if you're on a great and arduous quest, it needs to be chronicled. Someone must preserve the deeds, great and small, of [pc.mf|heroes|heroines] for posterity, after all. I appear to be the most qualified local to do so, that is certain. So if you will allow me, I will spread word of your doings far and wide in song and spirit. I already am working on my first composition, but I'm sure you'll be performing more deeds worthy of immortalising in tune and verse." That's plenty of pandering he's doing right there... "Mm-hm. Mm-hmmm... mmm-mmm-mmm." River flicks his fingers in a blur and jams out a quick series of chords on his lute. "I have the feeling that we will be the best of friends, [pc.name], whether we like it or not. Garth has told me much about you — alas, I was not here on the day of the storm, but returning from Tychris and hence huddling in a hole by the side of the road. Never mind, though, for we will be seeing much of each other from here on out, I think." If he's going to be hanging out here in the middle of town, that's going to be a given. "Excellent! I shall see you around — if you need something of me, don't be afraid to ask!"
rows.translation: 就在你正在思考接下来该去哪里的时候，镇中心那座雕像里突然传来一个声音，那是一个浑厚而流畅的男高音。 “啊！有新面孔来了！能占用你一点时间吗，我的[pc.race]朋友？” 你转过身去，看到一个身材矮小的猫族正躺在雕像脚下的铁艺长椅上；他微微仰起头，与你对视。起初，你不太确定他是否真的是个孩子——他的外貌确实很像小孩子——但听他的声音，显然他已经不是个幼崽了。 还有他怀里的鲁特琴——看来他应该是个音乐家。 [pc.bg minstrel|喜欢你|某种形式]那么，当你向前迈步时，那个小猫男孩会伸出一只手，你握住了他的手，而尽管他的手指看起来很纤细，但实际上却出奇地有力。 [party.has cait |哇，你真是太可爱了！”凯特开心地赞叹道，“在贾西拉，那些山谷里到处都是像你这样的小猫呢！” 那位吟游诗人只是笑了笑：“虽然我可能是贾西拉人的后裔，但我从未去过那里，所以还是相信你的话吧。 ] 那么，是不是有什么事情发生了呢？ “好的，让我先介绍一下自己。我叫瑞弗，也就是‘会唱歌的箭’。能在鹰棘镇见到新面孔，真是件愉快的事。这里有时候会变得非常沉闷，尤其是在冬天。不过，正是加斯让我留在这里——就是为了让气氛活跃起来，让人们感到兴奋；我和他一起在这个村庄生活了这么久！啊！那么，您叫什么名字呢？ [pc.name]对，对，[pc.name]， [pc.name]我听说过很多关于你的事——你真是镇上的焦点人物，一直在帮助别人。 [party.has cait|就在那边的凯特·泽特拉。|一只可怜的小猫]尽管面临着种种问题，她还是毅然踏入了寒冷而暗影的环境，去执行一项需要勇气与冒险的任务。是的，这些故事我都知道。大部分内容都是加斯告诉我的，但我自己也亲自去了那座寺庙进行调查，同时还查阅了其他几份资料 [party.has cait |凯特的眼睛微微睁大了。“等等，你怎么会知道我的全名？我还没…… |他确实是个充满好奇心的人，不是吗？ ] 瑞弗暂时停止了拨弄琉特琴的动作，挥了挥手表示不用继续。“先不说我这个音乐家的事，其实我也可以算是个小镇的传令员吧——我的工作就是了解各种信息，从路过这里的人们那里收集新闻，然后收取一点费用后再把这些消息传播出去。当然了，如果你们有什么想让全镇的人都知道的事情，同样的费用，我也可以帮你们把消息传开。” “所以，嗯，这种小事我当然会知道。 [party.has cait |凯特这样抱着双臂，对瑞弗的解释仍然不太满意，但以她目前的心态，也无法对此提出异议。 ] 所以，他算是一种音乐家吗？ “没错。不过我更喜欢用‘吟游诗人’这个词。它带有一种浪漫的感觉，而且比‘音乐家’这样的说法要显得高雅得多。‘游吟诗人’这个词虽然有点浮夸，但‘吟游歌手’则会让人联想到宫廷生活的氛围，而实际上他并不属于那种类型。你不同意吗？” 如果他想被称为吟游诗人，那好吧，他就可以这么称呼自己。 “那么，你现在正在执行一项任务，对吧？” 从技术上来说，确实是这样……只不过你可能还不知道该从哪里开始行动。这跟他有什么关系呢？他不过是个爱管闲事的本地人罢了。 “嗯，我的好[pc.mf|先生|夫人]如果你正在进行一项伟大而艰巨的探索，那么这段经历就必须被记录下来。有人必须保留所有这些大事小事的记录。 [pc.mf|英雄们|女主角们]毕竟，这些都是为了后人。显然，我是最合适的人选来完成这项工作。所以，请允许我吧，我会通过歌曲和故事将您的丰功伟绩传播到四面八方。我已经在创作我的第一首作品了，但我相信，您还会做出更多值得用歌声和诗句来纪念的壮举。他这样做简直是在讨好别人啊……” “嗯嗯。嗯嗯嗯……”瑞弗快速地拨动手指，用鲁特琴弹奏出一连串音符。“我觉得我们一定会成为最好的朋友。[pc.name]，无论我们是否愿意，加斯已经跟我讲了很多关于你的事情——可惜在暴风雨发生的那天我并不在这里，当时我正在从提克里斯返回的路上，所以只能躲在路边的一个洞里。不过没关系，我想从现在开始我们会有很多机会见面吧。 如果他打算经常待在城里的这个地方，那肯定是不可避免的。 “太好了！以后我们会经常见面的——如果你需要我的帮助，随时都可以尽管开口！
