rows.original:
River is a tiny little kitten-boy of a bard — he can't be anywhere more than five foot two, with most of his body huddled against the cold in an oversized brown poncho sewn together from heavy wool from some kind of highland animal. He's seated on the wrought-iron bench at the foot of the statue that dominates Hawkethorne's main square, his feet dangling a little ways above the floor, and in his hands he strums a rather fine-looking lute, providing a gentle musical accompaniment to the atmosphere of the village's center. Beneath his poncho — it reaches down to his knees — you spot the ends of warm leggings and furred boots, simple, sturdy and practical.

        For a catfolk, he's pretty thin — no, not thin, for there's a bit of muscle on that bone. More lithe, perhaps — a recurve bow, scaled down to his size, as well as a quiverful of arrows suggests how he came by that wiry frame that rests on otherwise slender limbs. The bard himself is akin to a longhaired breed of cat compared to other catfolk — the almost comically sized ears that stick out from the top of his poncho's hood are covered in a thick layer of white fluff, as is his feline tail.
        
        As you study him, he lifts up his hood to return your gaze, and you spy his green, slitted eyes and long shock of soft, white hair that spills down the back of his shoulders. He gives you a lazy grin, pulls his hood back down over his eyes, then leans back against his seat in a pose of uniquely feline laziness, tail curling about one of the bench's legs as he continues his business. You notice that River's fingers are a little longer than most, quite the boon for a musician — and by how swiftly he plays, there's no question as to their dexterous nature.
        
        All in all, River looks like an easygoing fellow on the surface, and for someone who makes his living from performance art and being social you guess he has to be. The sort of guy who lives for the moment, perhaps, some good food, a little carousing, and a warm bed at night.
rows.translation:
瑞弗是个身材矮小的吟游诗人——他的身高顶多五英尺二英寸，大部分身体都被裹在一件用某种高原动物身上的厚羊毛缝制的棕色大披风里，以此来抵御寒冷。他坐在鹰棘镇主广场上那座雕像脚下的铁艺长椅上，双脚微微悬在地面之上，手中拨弄着一把外观颇为精致的鲁特琴，为这个村庄中心的氛围增添了一丝轻柔的音乐伴奏。在他的雨披下——那雨披一直垂到他的膝盖——你可以看到他穿着保暖的紧身裤和毛皮靴子的鞋尖，这些装备简单实用，而且非常结实。

        对于一个猫族来说，他的体型算是相当纤细的——不过，也不算真正意义上的纤细，因为他的骨骼上还是能看出一些肌肉的痕迹。或许应该说，他的身形更加灵活敏捷才对。一把根据他的体型量身打造的弯弓，以及一箭袋里的箭矢，都说明了他为何会拥有那样结实而柔韧的体格，即便他的四肢看起来相当纤细。这位吟游诗人本身，与其他猫族相比，更像是一种长毛猫品种——他披风兜帽顶部凸出的耳朵大得几乎有些滑稽，上面覆盖着一层厚厚的白色绒毛，他的猫尾巴也同样如此。
        
        当你注视着他时，他掀起兜帽与你对视，你看到了他那双绿色的、裂开的眼睛，以及那一头柔软的白发，它垂落在他的肩后。他懒洋洋地对你笑了笑，又将兜帽拉下来遮住眼睛，然后以一种只有猫才会有的慵懒姿态靠在椅背上，尾巴卷在长椅的腿上，继续做他的事情。你可以看出，瑞弗的手指比大多数人的都要长一些，对于一名音乐家来说，这无疑是一个巨大的优势——而从他演奏的速度来看，他的手指灵活性无疑是非常高的。
        
        总的来说，瑞弗表面上看起来是个随和的人，对于一个以表演艺术和社交活动为生的人来说，他确实应该是这样。他应该是那种活在当下的人，喜欢品尝美味的食物，享受短暂的狂欢，そして每晚都能睡在一个温暖的床上。

rows.original: "So, you'd like to change what you go by?" River scratches his chin. "A little harder than just changing your callsign, but it's something I can do. As an added bonus, everyone will think that's always been your name, so you don't have to go to the trouble of introducing yourself to people all over again!" He... he can do that? "Of course, of course." The little catboy waggles a finger at you. "Don't worry too much about how it works, just accept the services I provide for what they are. If you're certain about changing your name... just tell me what you want to be known as from here on out. I assure you, even the gods themselves won't be any the wiser... or maybe they'll just play along. And there's the matter of the fee..." [var0||Ah, yes. The fee, which you can't afford. River clicks his tongue at that. "Ah, you poor thing. All right, I'll waive the fee, because I like you and know you're really broke, as opposed to just pretending to be broke like some people do at Garth's. But don't keep on doing this..."]

rows.original:
"So, that's it? That's what you want people who live about these parts to know you as?"
        
        Indeed.
        
        "Mm-mm-mhm." River lays his lute on his lap and steeples his fingers. "Well then, I'll spread the word and let everyone know. Like I said, it'll be a little more work, but before you know it, everyone will know you by [pc.name] and always will have."
        
        How soon can he get the word out?
        
        "I already have!"
        
        What?
        
        The white-furred catboy leans back on his bench and picks his lute back up with a wink. "Like I said, everyone will know it before even you do. So relax, and don't think too hard about it. I have my ways, after all. Now if you don't mind, I think I'll relax a little with a good tune."
rows.translation:
“所以，就这样？这就是你想让这一带的人用来称呼你的名字？”
        
        没错。
        
        “嗯——嗯——哼。”瑞弗把鲁特琴横放在腿上，十指指尖相抵。“那好，我会把消息传开，让所有人都知道。就像我说的，这得多费一点功夫，不过用不了多久，人人都会知道你叫[pc.name]，而且在他们记忆中，你一直都叫这个名字。”
        
        他要多久才能把消息传开？
        
        “已经传开了！”
        
        什么？
        
        白毛猫男孩靠回长凳，眨眨眼，再次拿起鲁特琴。“就像我说的，在你意识到之前，所有人就已经知道了。所以放轻松，别想得太复杂。毕竟，我自有办法。现在，要是你不介意，我想弹首好曲子放松一下。”

rows.original:
The little bard-boy eyes you up and down. "But of course! I'd be glad to teach you what I know — [pc.bg minstrel
    |given that I've chosen to set down roots here in Hawkethorne, it'd be great to have another musician traveling out and about spreading the tunes that I've wrought. Of course, some of them would be quite literally singing your own praises, but that just makes it better, doesn't it
    |it's always encouraging to see someone take an interest in what I do and try to learn some of it for themselves. My dream, perhaps, is to have a student who will someday surpass me. Perhaps you will one day be that protege, hmm

    Maybe.

rows.original: Re-assign the Attribute points you gained from levelling up. You can't re-assign the points you started with at Level 1, nor any temporary points. Costs 300 Electrum Coins and a day of training time.
rows.translation: 你可以重新分配因升级而获得的属性点数。不过，你无法重新分配在1级时初始拥有的那些点数，也无法重新分配任何临时获得的点数。进行这项操作需要花费300枚琥珀金币，并且还需要消耗一天的训练时间。

rows.translation: 学习技能

rows.original: Train any Black Mage or Charmer power that you are high enough level to use. Costs 100 Electrum Coins per level of the power, and will take up the rest of your day.
rows.translation: 当你等级足够高时，可以学习任何黑魔法师或魅惑师相关的技能。学习每项技能需要消耗100枚琥珀金币，而且学习过程会占用你一整天的时间。
rows.raw: "Train any Black Mage or Charmer power that you are high enough level to use. Costs 100 Electrum Coins per level of the power, and will take up the rest of your day."

rows.translation: 学习技能

rows.original: There are no powers River can teach you right now.
rows.translation: 目前，瑞弗并没有什么能力可以教给你。
rows.raw: "There are no powers River can teach you right now."

rows.translation: 更换职业

rows.original: Change your class to a Charmer, a support and resolve combat class. Switching classes does not transfer or unlock new Talents, though it will give you the perks of your new class up to your current level. You would be well-advised to have the coin to buy additional talents afterwards. Switching classes costs 3,000 Electrum Coins, and will take one full week of time.
rows.translation: 将你的职业改为魅惑师——这个职业属于辅助型职业，能够帮助你在战斗中取得优势。虽然更换职业不会让你获得新的天赋或解锁新的能力，但你会立即享受到新职业在当前等级下所提供的优势。建议你在更换职业后尽快准备足够的金币来购买额外的天赋。更换职业需要花费3,000枚琥珀金币，而且整个过程需要整整一周的时间。
rows.raw: "Change your class to a Charmer, a support and resolve combat class. Switching classes does not transfer or unlock new Talents, though it will give you the perks of your new class up to your current level. You would be well-advised to have the coin to buy additional talents afterwards. Switching classes costs 3,000 Electrum Coins, and will take one full week of time."

rows.translation: 你没有所需的 3,000 琥珀金币。

rows.original:
comes to a close, and the two of you top it off by sharing a drink at the Frost Hound. You've never seen River drink anything but chilled milk, and the catboy likes it that way.
    
    "That'll be it for now. Go and get some rest; [party.som|you'll need it|[party.compNames] has been waiting for you|[party.compNames] have been waiting for you]. rows.original: "Oh sure," River says, a placid little smile crossing his face as he strums a little musical accompaniment to your conversation. "I'd be tempted to ask for a coin for my time — I am supposed to be working, after all — but since you're such a nice [pc.mf|fellow|lady], there's no charge for our budding champion. I'm a great little kitten like that. "So, you wanted to talk?"
rows.translation: “哦，当然可以，”瑞弗说道，脸上浮现出一丝平静的微笑，一边为你们的交谈轻轻拨弦伴奏。“我其实很想为我这点时间讨一枚硬币——毕竟我确实是在工作——不过既然你这么好心，[pc.mf|伙计|女士]，我们这位初出茅庐的冠军就分文不取。我就是这么一只大方的小猫咪。” “所以，你是想找我谈谈？”

rows.translation: 他自己

rows.original: You'd like to know a little more about the little kitten bard. Where did he come from, who is he, and where is he going? River raises an eyebrow at you. "Oh? I came into the square from the Frost Hound, I'm River, and after this, I'm heading back up to bed!" You scowl. Those answers, while technically correct, aren't exactly the most useful that he could have given. "But those are the ones I'm willing to give, friend." He gives you a cheeky grin[pc.isDK | of the sort that sorely tempts you to return it with a slap |, which you return with a disapproving glare ]. "Tell me — would you be inclined to give your life story, every single little detail of it, to anyone who just came up and asked? All the foils and foibles of your life up to this point?" Well... "Well?" You suppose not... "Exactly! And I'm not just anyone, I'm River, the Singing Arrow! I've got to have an aura of — " he stops strumming for a moment to waggle his fingers in the air — "mystery, you know. Gotta keep up appearances." Oh, really. "Well, it's that or [rand |the lizard wizard whose staff I nicked find me |that lovely kitten whom I knocked up under the bar two towns back catch up to me with her three burly brothers in tow |that big fat guy whom I was singing rude songs about hear about where I'm staying ], innit? I like the Frost Hound, shocking as that may sound, and I'd rather not have to leave again. While I know it's probably sacrilege for a bard to say he's tired of being a transient, I'm at that age where running around is getting a little tiring. "Now, if you don't mind, I'd really rather not discuss the subject any more. Like I said, I'm River, the Singing Arrow, I came in from the Frost Hound, and I'm going up to bed later. That's all I'm saying, and that's all you'll ever get out of me. Anything else I can do for you?"
rows.translation: 你想再多了解一点这位小猫吟游诗人。他来自哪里，他究竟是谁，又准备去往何方？ 瑞弗扬眉看着你。“哦？我是从霜犬酒馆来到广场的，我是瑞弗，等这边结束以后，我就要回楼上睡觉！” 你皱起眉头。严格来说，这些回答全都正确，但绝对算不上他能给出的最有用的答案。 “可我只愿意告诉你这些，朋友。”他冲你顽皮一笑[pc.isDK |；那副笑脸实在让你忍不住想扇他一巴掌作为回应 |，而你则回以不赞同的瞪视 ]。“告诉我——要是随便什么人走过来问你，你会愿意把自己的人生经历、其中每一处微不足道的细节全都告诉对方吗？把一路走来遭遇的阻挠和犯过的傻事全盘托出？” 嗯…… “所以呢？” 你想，大概不会…… “正是如此！况且我可不是什么无名小卒，我是瑞弗，歌唱之箭！我必须营造出一种——”他停下拨弦，腾出手指在空中晃了晃——“神秘的气质，明白吧。总得维持形象。” 哦，真的吗。 “那当然，不这样的话，[rand |那个法杖被我顺走的蜥蜴法师就会找到我 |我在两个镇子外的酒吧柜台下搞大肚子的可爱猫女，就会带着她三个魁梧的兄弟追上我 |那个被我编了下流歌曲嘲弄的大胖子，就会打听到我的住处 ]，不是吗？说来或许令人震惊，但我喜欢霜犬酒馆，也不想再被迫离开了。我知道，吟游诗人说自己厌倦漂泊，听起来或许有点大逆不道，可我已经到了四处奔波都会觉得疲惫的年纪。 “好了，如果你不介意，我实在不想再谈这个话题。就像我说的，我是瑞弗，歌唱之箭；我从霜犬酒馆来到这里，待会儿就要上楼睡觉。这就是我愿意说的一切，你永远也别想从我嘴里问出更多。还有什么是我能为你效劳的吗？”

rows.raw: "So, where did he come from, who is he, and where is he going?"

rows.translation: 见过吗？

rows.original: Have you seen him before? You can't quite place where you've seen River — or at least, someone like him, but there's a definite sense of deja vu about the little kitten bard. A lingering touch of familiarity that you can't quite place, lingering on the tip of your tongue, on the edge of your consciousness... the more you look at River, the more you're convinced that you've run into him somewhere before. "Oh, it's quite possible." River coaxes an appropriately dramatic chord from his strings and chuckles. "I get around while spreading my sound, so to speak — I wouldn't be surprised if you've heard me perform before and it simply slipped your mind until you've seen me again. And if not, well, there are many catfolk around who might reasonably look like me, yes?" Huh. You suppose. "It's a wide world, and it takes all sorts to make it. I'm sure there's someone out there who looks just a little like you, too, or maybe even more than a little like you." River waggles his hand in a gesture that's neither here nor there. "But come on, does it really matter if you've seen me before? What does matter is that I, the Singing Arrow, am here and prepared to move your heart and soul — for a small fee, that is. Heroes like you do deeds, I write songs, something something exclusivity clause, but yeah, easy!" [party.has cait | "I don't know about that," Cait whispers into your ear when River's occupied in greeting a passer-by. "He looks cute, to be sure, but there's something about him that's creepy and off. He makes the fur on my tail rise, and... I don't know. It's just a feeling." You know what she means. Still, without any concrete evidence, a feeling's just a feeling, and the little bard-boy's been around Hawkethorne for a while now, it seems. If he's trusted enough to be practically a town fixture, he can't be bad, can he? ]
rows.translation: 你以前见过他吗？你总觉得在哪里见过瑞弗——或者至少是见过像他这样的人，但就是想不起来具体是在哪里。对于这个小猫头鹰吟游诗人，你有一种强烈的似曾相识的感觉，这种熟悉感萦绕在心头，却始终想不起来具体来源。……你越是观察瑞弗，就越会确信自己之前在某个地方见过他。 “哦，很有可能。”瑞弗从琴弦上弹出了富有戏剧性的音符，然后轻笑着说道，“可以说，我在传播我的音乐的同时也在四处游历——如果你之前听过我的表演，而现在才想起来，那也并不奇怪。如果不是这样的话，嗯，周围也有很多猫族，他们的样子应该和我很相似吧？” “哈，你是这么认为的。” “这个世界很大，各种各样的人都有。我肯定也有其他人，他们的样子和你有点像，甚至可能非常像你。瑞弗挥了挥手，做出一个模棱两可的手势，说道：“不过说真的，你之前是否见过我，真的有那么重要吗？确实关键在于，我，这位“歌唱之箭”，就在这里，而且愿意用一点点代价来触动你的心灵——当然，这是有条件的。像你这样的英雄会做出伟大的事迹，而我则会创作歌曲。还有一些独家授权之类的条款，不过嘛，其实挺简单的！ [party.has cait | 我不太确定，”当瑞弗正忙着跟路过的行人打招呼时，凯特在你耳边低声说道，“他确实看起来挺可爱的，但他的身上有种让人觉得毛骨悚然、不对劲的地方……他真的会让我浑身不自在。……我也不确定。只是一种感觉而已。” 你应该明白她的意思。不过，如果没有确凿的证据，这种感觉终究只是感觉而已。而且，那个小吟游诗人似乎已经在鹰棘镇待了有一段时间了。如果他得到了足够的信任，甚至几乎成为了这个小镇的标志性人物，那么他肯定不会是个坏人，对吧？ ]

rows.translation: 乐器

rows.original: "You think I should play something else? Maybe my father's mandolin? The pipes with which I courted my first love? How about a stolen horn? An ancient fiddle from Estelore itself? Or maybe a songbook in a tongue only the gods can speak? Oh! Oh! I know, a one-man-band?" Okay, okay, you get the point. [pc.isDK|Please, he should stop before you give in to the urge to slap him in full view of everyone|You give him a most pointed and disapproving glare]. "Seriously, though. A lute is favored because it's practical, you see. You can wear it on a sling about you, you can use it to brain someone — although I don't recommend you do that too often, even if it makes a very satisfying noise — and it keeps your mouth free so you can sing, it's not too hard to repair if you can find some good horsehair for the strings, it gives a good range of music, you can carry it around easily... need I go on?" No, no, he doesn't. "Cliches are cliches for a reason, friend. Once you understand the whys and wherefores and don't follow them blindly, you're in the clear. Now, friend, was there anything else you wanted to discuss?"
rows.translation: “你觉得我应该演奏点别的吗？也许弹我父亲的曼陀林？用我当年追求初恋时弹的那对风笛？或者一把偷来的号角？一把来自埃斯托洛尔的古老小提琴？又或者一本只有神明才听得懂的语言写成的歌本？哦！哦！我知道了，来一场单人乐队怎么样？” 好吧，好吧，你明白我的意思了。[pc.isDK|拜托，他最好在你忍不住当众扇他一巴掌之前停下来|你投给他一个极其尖锐而充满不赞成的瞪视]。 “不过说真的。鲁特琴之所以受青睐，是因为它实用，你瞧。你可以用背带把它挂在身上，也可以拿它去敲别人的脑袋——虽然我不建议你太经常这么干，哪怕那声音听着很过瘾——而且它还能让你的嘴空出来好唱歌；只要能找到些好马毛做琴弦，修起来也不太难；它能奏出的音域很广，也方便随身携带……还需要我继续说吗？” 不，不，他不需要。 “陈词滥调之所以是陈词滥调，是有原因的，朋友。一旦你弄懂了其中的来龙去脉，不再盲目照搬，你就没问题了。那么，朋友，你还有什么别的事想聊吗？”
rows.raw: " "You think I should play something else? Maybe my father's mandolin? The pipes with which I courted my first love? How about a stolen horn? An ancient fiddle from Estelore itself? Or maybe a songbook in a tongue only the gods can speak? Oh! Oh! I know, a one-man-band?" Okay, okay, you get the point. [pc.isDK|Please, he should stop before you give in to the urge to slap him in full view of everyone|You give him a most pointed and disapproving glare]. "Seriously, though. A lute is favored because it's practical, you see. You can wear it on a sling about you, you can use it to brain someone — although I don't recommend you do that too often, even if it makes a very satisfying noise — and it keeps your mouth free so you can sing, it's not too hard to repair if you can find some good horsehair for the strings, it gives a good range of music, you can carry it around easily... need I go on?" No, no, he doesn't. "Cliches are cliches for a reason, friend. Once you understand the whys and wherefores and don't follow them blindly, you're in the clear. Now, friend, was there anything else you wanted to discuss?""

rows.translation: 乐器

rows.original: So, why a lute? Why not something else?
rows.translation: 那么，为什么选择鲁特琴呢？为什么不是其他乐器呢？
rows.raw: "So, why a lute? Why not something else?"

rows.translation: 音乐

rows.original: River looks around at the people in the town square, then shrugs. "It's a combination of whatever's appropriate for the situation, and whatever's been requested. A good performer's got to be able to read his audience and react accordingly, and of course, you don't want to rile them up so much that something unsavory happens and Garth's got to call up old man Sanders to put down the excitement with emergency measures." What emergency measures would those be? "You'll recognize them when you see them." The little kitten bard gives you a knowing nod. "But you don't want to be hanging around when he does. Either way, that means that I probably won't be able to give you an exact rendition of what you want me to play — if giving the entire length of 'The Hedgehog Who Couldn't Be Buggered' right out here in the square is going to turn the Frost Hound into any more of a doghouse that it is already, then I'm not doing it. Old Garth is already showing me more kindness than I deserve letting me ply my trade here, and I'm not going to turn around and bite him in the ass." "What this means for you is that if you pay me to do a request, you get to decide the general mood of what you'd like me to play, be it something lighthearted or serious. I read both the people in the barroom as well as old Garth's mood, then decide on what exactly I want to perform. Capish?" That kinda defeats the point of a request... "Could be." River shrugs. "Then again, where else can you get a good song like mine for just a couple coins?"
rows.translation: 瑞弗环顾了一下镇广场上的人们，然后耸了耸肩说道：“表演内容当然是要根据现场情况以及观众的需求来决定。一个优秀的表演者必须能够了解自己的观众，并据此做出相应的调整。当然，你也肯定不希望惹恼他们吧。所以虽然可能会发生一些不愉快的事情，但加思还是不得不打电话给桑德斯老人，让他采取紧急措施来平息这场骚动。” “那些紧急措施会是什么呢？” “等你看到了就知道了。那只小猫吟游诗人向你投来了会意的点头。“但当他这么做的时候，你肯定不想待在附近吧。无论如何，这意味着我可能无法准确地演奏出你想要听的内容——如果在这里的广场上完整演奏《那个根本不在乎别人看法的刺猬》这首歌，会让‘霜犬酒馆’变得更加糟糕的话，那我就不演奏了。老加斯已经对我表现出了远超我应得的善意，允许我在这里从事我的工作，我绝对不会反过来伤害他。” “这意味着你也就是说，如果你付钱让我表演某首歌，你就有权决定我希望营造的整体氛围——是轻松愉快的，还是严肃认真的。我会观察酒吧里其他人的情绪，以及老加思当下的心情，然后才会决定到底表演什么。明白了吗？” “这样反而违背了提出请求的初衷吧……” “也可能是吧。”瑞弗耸了耸肩，“不过话说回来，除了这里，哪里还能用这么少的钱听到像我这样的好歌呢？

rows.translation: 音乐

rows.original: So, what does he play over here?
rows.translation: 那么，他在这儿演奏些什么呢？
rows.raw: "So, what does he play over here?"

rows.translation: 鹰棘镇

rows.original: "Mmm," comes the reply from the little kitten bard. "Mm-mm-mmm. I've been here since Hawkethorne was founded, but people used to be here before, too. The village's built atop the ashes of the town that once stood here... has it really been fifteen years, give or take one or two? Or if you think about it another way, has it really only been fifteen years? The old castle was close, and we believed an old imperial city used to be around these parts, too. Don't let the wildness of these lands fool you, [pc.name]. There's a lot of rich history to be had... rich, dark and bittersweet, like chocolate." Which is why you're asking if he has anything to share. "Ah... I can't just give it all away, friend, but what I can give, you're more than welcome to have. Now then..." River leans back on his bench and strums his lute idly. "[rand |Did you know that the statue I'm sitting under is that of the baroness's father? He was a pretty dashing fellow in his prime, wasn't he? Too bad he's dead and buried." You squint at the statue. It's clearly been repaired and refurbished, making its exact age hard to guess at, but it looks pretty old. Of course, it must have been exposed to the elements before Hawkethorne was founded, and it's pretty harsh about these parts... "Cuts a fine figure, doesn't he?" Yeah, when he points it out, the fellow depicted by the statue [flags.ATUGIA_MET|does indeed resemble the baroness quite strikingly|looks quite handsome]. No doubt like with portraits, the sculptor must have made plenty of quiet touch-ups to the man to make his appearance more flattering, but even so. |Does River actually know what happened to Garth's wife? "Yes, I do. But that's one story that even I won't tell, friend. It's not mine to spill, and I won't betray Garth and Sanders' trust like that. If Garth ever feels like letting you know, he'll be the one to do so, not me. Until then, my lips are sealed." |The baroness... she is old money, and a lot of it. The family has a lot of wealth tied up in Tychris, both in the banks and various investments and properties. It's how the family got by out here even after the village was razed by the siege." There was a siege here? River waves a hand dismissively. "Couple centuries ago, maybe a bit more. The village proper was taken down to the foundations, but the castle still stood. Without any people around, all the money in the world wouldn't have helped repair the damage to the castle, either, which is why it sat that way for so many years. And as the baroness found out with the mercenaries she hired to keep the roads clear, money will only go so far, even with sellswords. "There's a difference between influence and power, a fine but important difference that many only learn far too late when they overextend themselves. Remember that, my dear [pc.title]. Always remember that." |This is a fine place we have here, isn't it?" Indeed. It looks like it's been here a long time. "And yet we're only roughly fifteen years old." It's kind of hard to believe — some of these buildings look ancient. "That's because they are. Several of the major landmarks are actually refurbished ruins. The most obvious one would be old man Sanders' pad — the place is old stone, old, old stone. The structure was still solid, so we gave it a fresh coat of plaster and several new tiles and he was fine with that. We all lived in the chapel for the first couple of months, just the handful of new settlers; when I arrived, it was just Garth, his wife, and Sanders." And yet there're so many buildings up within the walls... River shrugs. "What could be saved, we saved; no point wasting good masonry. Garth knows the best builders this side of the Marches; they don't usually come cheap, but they'll do it just for him. Throw together a serviceable home in days, those people. Hawkethorne is pretty comfy these days, but for the four of us, the first couple months or two in the old chapel were pretty rough. It was then that I got into the habit of wearing a woollen poncho, and never quite got rid of that habit... it's a sensible one to have." |The reason people come to this place today is mostly because of me. Four settlers in the ruins of an ancient village, up against the frontier — it's a bit of a hard sell, especially when you can't promise people much. Somehow, I managed to do it. We're actually in a pretty good place — food to the south, timber to the north, minerals to the eastern foothills. If this village gets any bigger, there're certainly the resources to support it. Of course, given the local troubles... but then, that's what someone like you is for, isn't it?" You kind of fell into this whole thing... Kasyrra was certainly not what you expected when you headed out that night with Cait. "Ah, but as the saying goes, the right [pc.mf|man|woman] in the wrong place can make all the difference. So... wake up, [pc.mf|mister|missus] [pc.name]. Wake up, because you're a hero now, whether you like it or not. And I'll be here to sing of your deeds to all who care to listen, be they salutary... or less savory. If I can sell a ruin in the wilderness, my friend, I can sell you. So don't worry about it and go out there and do deeds, feed fuel to my muse." ] "Now then, is there anything I can do for you?"
rows.translation: 嗯……”小猫吟游者回答道，“嗯嗯嗯……我从鹰棘镇建立之初就住在这里了，但在这之前，也早就有人居住在这里了。这个村庄是建在曾经存在于这里的城镇的废墟之上的……真的已经过去十五年了吗？或许还会多一两年吧？或者，换一种方式来思考的话……真的已经过去那么久了吗？只有十五年过去了？那座古老的城堡离我们很近，我们猜测这片地区曾经也有一座古老的帝国城市。千万不要被这些土地的荒凉景象所迷惑。[pc.name]其中蕴含着许多丰富的历史故事……那些故事充满色彩，充满暗影，同时也带着苦涩与甜蜜，就像巧克力一样。” 正因为如此，你才会问他是否有什么可以分享的。 “啊……朋友，我总不能把所有的事情都告诉你们吧，但那些我可以分享的内容，你们当然可以听。”瑞弗靠在长椅上，漫不经心地拨弄着他的鲁特琴，说道。[rand |你知道我现在坐着的这座雕像其实是女男爵父亲的像吗？他在年轻时可是个相当英俊潇洒的人，对吧？可惜他已经去世，被埋在了地下。 你仔细观察着这座雕像。很明显，它已经被修复和翻新过，因此很难判断它的确切年代，但看起来确实非常古老。当然，在鹰棘镇建立之前，它肯定已经经历了各种自然环境的考验，而这些地区的环境条件确实相当恶劣…… “这座雕像看起来真是威风凛凛，不是吗？” 是啊，当有人指出这一点时，这座雕像所描绘的那个人物[flags.ATUGIA_MET|确实确实与那位女男爵有着惊人的相似之处。|看起来相当不错]毫无疑问，就像绘制肖像画一样，雕塑家肯定也对这个男子进行了多次细致的修改，以便让他的形象看起来更加讨人喜欢。但即便如此…… |瑞弗真的知道加思的妻子发生了什么事吗？ “是的，我知道。但这个故事，就连我也不会告诉别人，朋友。这不是我应该泄露的秘密，我也不会那样辜负加思和桑德斯的信任。如果加思想让你知道的话，他会亲自告诉你的，而不是我。在那个时候之前，我的嘴唇会保持沉默。 |那位女男爵……她拥有巨额的财富。她的家族在泰克里斯拥有大量的资产，这些资产既包括银行存款，也包括各种投资和房产。正因为如此，即使在村庄被围攻摧毁之后，她的家族依然能够维持生计。这里曾经发生过围攻吗？” 瑞弗漫不经心地摆了摆手：“大概几个世纪前吧，也可能更久一些。村庄本身已经被毁得只剩下地基，但那座城堡依然矗立在那里。由于没有人居住在那里，再多的钱也无力修复城堡所受的破坏，因此它就这样闲置了这么多年。正如女男爵通过雇佣那些负责维护道路畅通的雇佣兵所发现的那样，即使是用雇佣兵，金钱也终究是有其限度的。 影响力与权力之间是有区别的，这种区别虽然细微，但却非常重要。很多人直到过度扩张自己的势力时，才终于意识到这一点。请记住这一点，亲爱的。[pc.title]永远要记住这一点。 |我们这里真是个不错的地方，不是吗？” “确实如此。这些建筑看起来似乎已经存在很久了。” “可实际上我们才成立大约十五年而已。” “真是难以置信——有些建筑看起来简直古老得不可思议。” “那是因为它们确实很古老。其中一些重要的地标其实都是经过修复的废墟。最明显的例子就是桑德斯老人的住所——那里用的都是古老的石材，真是非常古老啊。老的石头。那座建筑的结构依然坚固，所以我们给它重新抹了一层灰泥，还换上了几块新瓷砖，他对此也很满意。在最初的几个月里，只有为数不多的新移民住在那座小教堂里；当我到达的时候，那里只有加思、他的妻子以及桑德斯。然而，城墙里面还有那么多建筑物啊……” 瑞弗耸了耸肩：“能挽救的东西我们都挽救了；浪费优质的建筑材料实在没有意义。加斯知道边境这边最优秀的建筑师们；他们的收费通常都不低，但为了他，他们一定会愿意帮忙的。那些人真的在短短几天内就搭建出了一间可以居住的简陋房子。如今，鹰棘镇已经变得相当舒适了，但对于我们四个人来说，在那座旧小教堂里度过的最初一两个月确实非常艰难。正是那段时间，我养成了穿羊毛披风的习惯，而且这个习惯一直持续到了现在。……这是一个明智的决定。 |人们今天之所以来到这个地方，很大程度上都是因为我的缘故。在一片古老村庄的废墟中，只有四名定居者愿意来到这片位于边境地区的土地——这样的提议本来有点难以让人接受，尤其是当你无法向人们承诺太多东西的时候。然而，我最终还是成功说服了他们。我们的处境其实相当不错——南方有食物，北方有木材，东部山脚下还有矿产资源。如果这个村庄继续发展壮大，肯定有足够的资源来支撑它的发展。当然，也得考虑到当地存在的各种问题。但是，像你这样的人不正是为了这类事情而存在的吗？” 你某种程度上也是被卷入了这一切之中……那天晚上你和凯特一起出发时，肯定没有预料到会遇到卡希拉这样的人。 “啊，不过俗话说，合适的时机总会到来的。 [pc.mf|男人|女性]出现在错误的地方，可能会带来完全不同的结果。所以……醒醒吧。 [pc.mf|先生|夫人] [pc.name]醒醒吧，因为无论你愿不愿意，你现在都已经成为了一位英雄。而我，会在这里向所有愿意倾听的人讲述你的英勇事迹——无论这些事迹是值得赞颂的，还是不那么值得称赞的。我的朋友，如果我连荒野中的一片废墟都能卖出去，那么你，我也一定能说服你。所以别担心，勇敢地去行动吧，让你的故事成为我灵感的源泉吧。 ] 那么，有什么我可以帮您的吗？

rows.original: [rand |"Gweyr's fit right back into town," River acknowledges your question with a nod. "I was worried Hawkethorne had changed too much, or she'd have constant conflict with Sanders, but it would appear that the gods have blessed us for doing their work in this world. At least she may have the respite from the strife that has plagued her life up to this point." That, and she knows how to keep her head down. River acknowledges your reply with a nod, pulling the hood of his poncho over his brow. "It's a useful skill to have. Still, I'm glad that she's back — the wealth of experience such a woman has accumulated over her lifetime in all manner of strange and unusual circumstances is enough songwriting material for me to pad out the rest of my days, I feel. Neither of us are as young as we used to be, and I need to get her stories down and into a form which can be easily spread before one of us finally kicks the bucket. "It may be decades too late, but at least the old dog managed to get a satisfactory ending to her story, even if it wasn't completely happy. In this day and age, that's about the best of what we can hope for, and it's through our struggles that we can lay the foundations for those who come after us to perhaps indeed get happy endings..." |"I've written a couple of new songs based on Gweyr's exploits when she was younger. By all appearances, people like them more than the other stuff... I guess there is that appeal of hearing about someone still alive and living just next door instead of something that happened in the distant past. Chasing novelty, you know?" And has he perchance managed to come up with something about her last adventure? "Ah, not yet. That one's... tricky. I need some time to spin an appropriately epic yarn in order to do it justice; if I didn't know as many tales about certain things as I do and didn't know you personally, I might've dismissed whole parts of it as being made-up. But given everything... I'm going to have to play for an audience, and it needs to have that twinge of verisimilitude in it in order to be entertaining. You get what I mean?" [pc.bg minstrel |Sure, you do. You're — well, were a minstrel yourself, you know how the crowd goes. River raises an eyebrow. "Were a minstrel, you say?" Well, after everything that's happened to you up till now, you'd like to think you're something more. A smile. "That makes sense. |You can't be wholly sure... but you think you do. River nods. "Regardless of how much I embellish or downplay the facts, it's got to have the ring of truth to it. ] Either way, it means that I've got to take my time and think this out before I put it all down. Once you set the music free into the world, you can't take it back." |"I owe Gweyr my life, and old man Reverra here owes her the gem in his shield." River reaches over his shoulder and taps the statue's stone boot knowingly. "Without her, neither of us would be here today. You know, I was chatting with her not so long after she'd arrived back in town, and how I was sorry I didn't stand up for her more all that time ago given what she'd done for me before heading off to what would become her doom. And all that she did was to pat me on the head and tell me that I stood up for her more than anyone else did, so there was that to my name. That just made me feel even more guilty. "I know it's not productive to bemoan the past in this fashion, but I suppose I've got to be a bit of a romantic by virtue of my profession. Garth and Gweyr were amongst the first who joined up on our train heading up north to try and settle the frontier, and we've known each other for so long... I suppose I'm not one to be waxing nostalgic, am I?" |"Don't tell her, but I've been keeping an eye out for Gweyr since she returned to town. Smoothing things out ahead of her, asking people to be nice, making sure she doesn't get any rude or weird stares. I don't think she's noticed, but she's always been the kind to let it pass silently even if she did, so I honestly have no way to tell myself." That's very kind of him, especially given her history with the townspeople... not that many of those who were involved in that incident are still around these days. While you understand that he thinks this is the least he can do after he let her down, it's still more than what most would've done. It's appreciated — you would've at least expected some questions about how and why Garth suddenly has a wife whom he's been supposedly estranged from for the last twenty years, but if River is running around smoothing about things in the background then it all makes sense now. River nods. "If I'm able to get the word out quickly and discreetly, there's no point in my holding back, is there? Sure, it wasn't easy — what with Garth being who he is, people love to gossip about him and his. There was the whole thing when his daughter first got pregnant, when they were saying that either he or his son did it... it's hard to quash that kind of rumor once it gets out into the wild, regardless of how much truth or lack thereof there might be in there. "It took time and effort — and a lot of spending of what clout I've built up here in Hawkethorne over the years — but I eventually persuaded most of the major gossips here in town to hold their tongues for once. A lot harder than I thought it's be... if only I could just wave a magic wand or something and have everyone else fall into line, ha. I don't expect it to last forever, but by then I know Gweyr will have conducted herself in an upstanding enough fashion to wash away all the rumors of her past and what she's been doing in the meantime that are no doubt going to crop up." |"The night she was exiled, Gweyr asked me to keep in touch with her old mercenary company in case she ever needed to ask them to come up north for a spell. For a handful of months, I wondered if she meant to use them to take her revenge upon what was left of the village... but as none of the correspondence ever pointed to any sign of that over the years, I eventually stopped worrying so much about it. "Still, I don't get why she felt like she had to hound Tollus personally over those last two decades without seeking help from people in her old life. I don't know about you, but I think that having an experienced band of mercenaries who are loyal to your person would've been a great asset in trying to beat back the cult. Well, I guess it makes for a better story this way." ]
rows.translation: [rand |格维尔已经回到了镇上，”瑞弗点头回答了你的问题。“我原本担心鹰棘镇会变得太不一样，或者她会和桑德斯不断发生冲突，但看来诸神确实眷顾了我们，让我们能够顺利完成这项任务。至少，她可以摆脱迄今为止一直困扰她的生活中的那些纷争了。” 而且，她知道如何低调行事，不引人注意。 瑞弗点了点头，表示同意你的回答，然后将雨披的兜帽拉到了眉毛上。这是一项非常有用的技能。不过，我还是很高兴她回来了——这样一位女性在一生中，在各种奇怪而不寻常的处境中积累的丰富经验，对我来说，简直就是取之不尽的创作素材，足以让我有足够的内容来充实我的余生。我们俩都已经不再像从前那么年轻了，在我和她中的某一个人最终离世之前，我必须把她的故事记录下来，并整理成一种便于传播的形式。 “虽然可能为时已晚，至少这只老狗还是为自己的故事找到了一个令人满意的结局，尽管这个结局并不完全完美。在当今这个时代，这已经是我们所能期望的最好的结果了。正是通过我们的努力与奋斗，我们才能为后来的人奠定基础，让他们也能够拥有幸福的结局…… |我根据格维尔年轻时的经历写了几首新歌。显然，人们更喜欢这些歌，而不是其他的作品……我想，讲述一个仍然活着、就生活在我们身边的人的故事，总比讲述发生在遥远过去的事情更有吸引力吧。就是那种追求新鲜感的行为，你懂的吧？” 那么，他有没有设法为她上次的冒险故事编造出些什么呢？ “啊，还没有。那个故事嘛……有点棘手。我需要一些时间来编出一个足够精彩、足够史诗般的故事，才能把她的冒险经历恰当地呈现出来；要不是我对很多这类故事都非常熟悉，也不认识你这个人，我可能会认为其中很多内容都是编造出来的吧。但是，考虑到所有这些因素……我必须为观众而表演，而且表演内容必须具备一定的真实感，这样才能让人觉得有趣。你明白我的意思吧？ [pc.bg minstrel |当然可以。你本人——嗯，曾经是一名吟游诗人，你应该知道观众们会有怎样的反应。 瑞弗挑了挑眉毛。你说自己曾经是吟游诗人？” “嗯，经历了到现在为止发生的一切之后，你自然会希望自己能成为更了不起的人吧。” 他笑了笑：“这也说得通。 |你无法完全确定……但你觉得自己是确定的。 瑞弗点了点头：“无论我是如何夸大事实或淡化其严重性，这些话总得带有真实的色彩才行。 ]无论如何，这意味着在我把所有内容都写下来之前，我必须花时间仔细考虑清楚。一旦你将音乐释放到这个世界中，你就再也无法把它收回来。 |我的性命欠了格维尔的，而这位雷维拉老人，他的盾牌上那颗宝石也是欠她的。”瑞弗伸手搭在老人的肩上，故意敲了敲那座雕像石制制成的靴子。“如果没有她，我们今天都不会在这里。你知道吗？她回到城里不久后，我曾和她聊过，当时我真的很后悔，在她为我做了那么多之后，当初却没有更坚定地站在她那一边，直到后来她走上了那注定的悲剧之路。她所做的只是轻拍我的头，告诉我，比起其他人，我才是最支持她的人，所以这一点应该算在我头上。但这反而让我感到更加内疚。 “我知道这样沉溺于对过去的懊悔并没有什么意义，但我想，由于我的职业关系，我多少还是有点浪漫情怀的吧。加思和格维尔是最早加入我们这支向北方进发的队伍的人，他们和我们一起努力试图在边境地区建立定居点。我们相识已久……我想，我应该不属于那种会沉溺于怀旧情绪的人吧？ |别告诉她，不过自从她回到镇上后，我就一直在关注着她。我会提前处理好一些事情，让大家都对她友好一些，确保她不会受到任何粗鲁或奇怪的目光。我觉得她应该没有注意到这些，但她本来就是那种即使注意到了也会默默忍受的人，所以说实话，我也无法确定她是否察觉到了什么。 他真是太好了，尤其是考虑到她与镇上那些人的过往……毕竟，那些参与那件事的人，如今已经所剩无几了。虽然你理解他认为，在让自己让她失望之后，这是自己最起码能做的，但这样的举动已经远远超出了大多数人的预期。真的很感谢——你至少会预料到人们会问一些关于加斯怎么突然就有了一个妻子，而据传说他在过去二十年里一直与这个妻子处于断绝关系的状态这样的问题。但如果瑞弗在暗中协调处理这些事情，那么现在一切就都说得通了。 瑞弗点了点头：“如果我能迅速而谨慎地把消息传出去，那么我再隐瞒下去也就没有意义了，对吧？当然，这并不容易——毕竟加斯是那样一个人，人们总喜欢对他和他的事情闲言碎语。比如他女儿刚怀孕的时候，人们就纷纷猜测是他是还是他的儿子干的……这种谣言一旦传开，就很难被制止了，无论其中有多少真相或虚假成分。 这花费了大量的时间和精力，也耗费了我这些年来在鹰棘镇积累起来的影响力，但最终我还是说服了镇上大多数爱传闲话的人，让他们这次保持沉默。其实这比我想象的要困难得多。要是我能挥动一根魔法杖之类的东西，让所有人都乖乖听话该多好啊。我并不指望这种状况能永远持续下去，但到那时，我相信格维尔一定会表现出足够高的品行，从而彻底消除关于她过去的那些谣言，以及在此期间她所做的一切无疑会引发的各种议论。" |在她被流放的那个夜晚，格维尔让我继续与她原来的雇佣军团队保持联系，以防她日后需要他们北上帮忙解决某些问题。有几个月的时间，我都在想，她是否打算利用这些人来为村庄所遭受的破坏报仇。不过，这些年来，所有的通信内容都没有提到过任何与此相关的迹象，所以最终我也就不再为此过分担忧了。 “不过，我还是不明白，为什么在过去的二十年里，她不寻求自己过去生活中认识的人的帮助，非要去亲自追究托勒斯的责任呢。我不知道你们怎么想，但我觉得，拥有一支对你忠心耿耿、经验丰富的雇佣军队伍，对于击退那个邪教组织来说，无疑会是一大助力。嗯，这样看来，故事也会更加精彩了。" ]

rows.original: "Really, now." River leans back on his bench and eyes you, giving you a small, affable smile. "Have you seen me before?" Well, maybe not exactly him, but there's no doubt about it — River carries an air of familiarity about him, a sense of yearning and closeness that speaks to something in you like his music does. It's certainly quite the boon for a musician to have that kind of immediate appeal with his audience, that's for sure. So yes, if you haven't seen him exactly, you can't shake off the feeling that you've seen... you don't know, maybe a relative. Someone who looks distinctly like him or gives off the same feel, that's for certain. "That really means nothing. There are plenty of good musicians in this world, aren't there? And let's face it, manipulating the passions of the crowd is part of being any kind of performer — working one's audience isn't anything strange or suspicious." You said nothing about him being strange or suspicious. "Come now, I'm not stupid and you're not, either." River still has that little placid smile on his lips, friendly and disarming. "You wouldn't be pursuing this line of questioning otherwise. Let's say that you are correct — you've encountered someone who has the same kind of presence that I do. That really doesn't mean anything, does it? The world is wide, and I'm sure that even, say, you have perhaps a dozen kindred souls wandering around with a strikingly similar air to your person. [pc.name], you're just reading too much into all of this, my friend. "On the other hand..." Yes? River purses his lips and stops strumming his lute long enough to raise a finger to his lips. "You're quite an interesting person, and if word has it right, extremely persistent, too. I don't deny that I can't help myself but leave a little breadcrumb trail for those who are so inclined to ask the right questions. Call it a part of my nature, perhaps; it is who I am because of who you are." Whatever does he mean? "What I mean is... you've done well." The air about you suddenly takes on a slight pink hue, and you notice that the people about you in Hawkethorne square have suddenly stopped moving mid-stride, frozen in place.[party.som | | The same goes for [party.compNames] beside you — starting to panic, you reach out for [comp1.hisHer] hand, only to find it insubstantial and incorporeal, your fingers passing through [comp1.hisHer] arm without so much as the slightest resistance. | The same goes for [party.compNames] beside you — starting to panic, you reach out for [comp1.names] hand, only to find it insubstantial and incorporeal, your fingers passing through [comp1.hisHer] arm without so much as the slightest resistance. ] [pc.isDK |What the fuck's |Just what's ] going on here? You look back at River, expecting him to be the source of this mess, but the little catboy bard is just as frozen as everyone else is. His voice still continues to speak, though, although it's not coming from his lips any more, but echoing all about you. "For all the good that it did, you managed to talk your way around Nareva, take her down a peg or two. It does feel good to have that sneaky snake humbled — her domain and portfolio are what they are, but they also lend one to grandeur too easily." You whirl around, and in the blink of an eye a little black-haired catboy is sitting beside River on the bench, just as tiny as he is but wearing a lot less clothing and a lot more jewelry. Sprawled out in a very feline fashion, he eyes you nonchalantly, as if you were an old and familiar friend. Which, to be honest, you might very well be... "So if you don't mind — " the voice is now centered about the little catboy — "Please don't give River a hard time. He's really doing his best at his job, and while he does have a history I really don't bother manufacturing the facts down to the smallest detail. No one asks too much of wandering musicians like him, and yes, I know that he's settled down here in this village. With a mind like yours, I'm sure if you looked into his stated past you could find some discrepancies, but as far as River knows all his memories are perfectly true and he is being genuinely honest in dealing with you." ...And who is he supposed to be? You're certain of the answer, but the question has to be asked nonetheless. The little catboy picks at his jeweled thong before taking his tail in his hands and giving you a playful little smile. "Our pretty pink friend Cait worships me." [party.has cait |You look back over your shoulder at Cait, standing as still as a statue and staring off into empty space; it's not a great leap of logic to assume that she can't see Mallach as she is right now. Shaking your head, you look between her and Mallach several times, then sigh. "She is quite devout despite not having formally taken her vows, but that's alright with me — the vows part, that is. The whole formal clergy bit is just for show anyway; the passion's certainly there! But how much Caitriss believes in the real me and how much is merely her notion of me... well, that's something she has to work out for herself, and until then, it wouldn't do to show myself to her; would ruin her journey. I hope you can understand that. Part of the reason we — well, most of us — leave well enough alone and are loathe to step in is because you need to figure out your own problems a lot of the time; it's something we learned during the Godswar. What's the saying again? 'Give a man a fish', that was it. These days, we're just here to, uh, facilitate." [var0 |Actually, if you're speaking to her patron deity, something comes to mind if he's going to bring up the matter of facilitation. "Yes?" Could he... could he actually do something with her brand, let her have kittens? "Easily. But does she want to have them?" That... "I won't do it against her will. The Brand serves a useful purpose for a girl like her, after all. And it's not like she doesn't know how to solve that little problem if she wanted, though it might be a bit... awkward... after the whole running-off bit she and her sister pulled. But the possibility will always just be that so long as Caitriss doesn't want it." ] That's... well, you can't argue. Speaking of which, can he do something about Calla? Cait's really heartbroken about her sister, and... The catboy god's face turns serious. "[flags.WC_CLEAR |You saw what happened in the Winter City |That's a tough one ]. You can't go breaking portals open willy-nilly or we're all going to end up fucked, and not in the fun way. Haven't you wondered why portals are always brief things? Even we gods fear to open one for more than a moment. There're things out there, in the places between, drawn to breaches like moths to a flame. You don't want to give them a way in, not ever." "Even supposing I could open a portal safely, which I can't, and won't... you'd have to know what world she's gone to, and where she is exactly. She'd have to be in a state to survive the trip — portal-hopping is hard on the body and mind, you know. And of course, she would have to want to come back to begin with. I'm not saying it's impossible to get her back, but the odds aren't great, [pc.name], and as much as it pains me to lose a follower — even an apostate — the risk is too great. I'm afraid the gods can't step in to help. Really, the others are more likely to try and hinder you, especially Velun and Tira. They're rather obsessive about the natural order of things being preserved, and portals being breached is anything but." |It's a pity that she isn't here to see her patron deity in all his... well, this appearance doesn't quite inspire glory, but it is in line with the catfolk ideal anyway. Mallach's smile broadens. "I generally try to shape my appearance to what people expect me to look like. I've found that it helps others relate better. But no, even if Caitriss were here, that would change nothing; this discussion is for you and you alone." Well, aren't you honored. ]
rows.translation: 真的，就是现在。”瑞弗靠在长椅上，看着你，露出了一个亲切而温和的微笑。拥有你以前见过我吗？” “嗯，也许没有吧。正是如此他，但毫无疑问——瑞弗身上散发着一种让人感到熟悉的气息，那种渴望与亲近的感觉，能够触动你内心深处的某些东西，就如同他的音乐一样。对于一位音乐家来说，能够立刻吸引听众的注意，无疑是一大优势。所以，如果你还没有看过他确实，你会有一种感觉，觉得自己曾经见过这个人……也不知道，也许是个亲戚。某个和他长得很像的人，或者给人一种类似的感觉，这一点是肯定的。 “不过那其实没什么意义吧。这个世界上有很多优秀的音乐家，不是吗？说实话，操纵人群的情绪其实是任何表演者都必须具备的能力——与观众建立良好的互动关系根本没有什么奇怪或可疑之处。 你并没有说过他有什么奇怪或可疑的地方。 得了吧，我又不傻，你也不是。”瑞弗的嘴角依然挂着那抹平和的微笑，显得既友好又让人放松。“否则你也不会一直追问这个问题了。假设你是对的——你确实遇到了一个和我有着同样特质的人。那其实什么意思也没有，对吧？世界这么大，我敢肯定，就算说，也一定有那么十几个人，他们的性格和你极为相似，正在这个世界上四处游荡吧。[pc.name]，朋友，你其实是把这一切想得太复杂了。 “不过……” 嗯？ |你回头看了看凯特，她站在那里，一动不动，就像一尊雕像，目光呆滞地望着前方空无一物的地方；不难推测，她现在根本看不到马拉克。你摇了摇头，几次将目光在她和马拉克之间来回切换，然后叹了口气。 “我不会违背她的意愿去强迫她。毕竟，对于她这样的女孩来说，那个品牌确实有它的作用。而且，如果她真的想要解决那个小问题，她其实也是知道该怎么做的，只不过可能需要一些时间罢了。……真是尴尬……在她们姐妹俩搞了那么一出之后。不过，只要凯特不介意的话，这种可能性始终是存在的。 ] 那……嗯，确实没什么好争辩的。说起来，他能不能为卡拉做点什么？凯特为她妹妹感到非常难过，而且…… 猫族神的脸色变得严肃起来。[flags.WC_CLEAR |你们都看到了在冬城发生的事情。 |这可真是个棘手的问题。 ]你不能随便就打开传送门，否则我们所有人都会陷入麻烦，而且绝对不是什么好事。你有没有想过，为什么传送门的存在时间总是那么短暂？就连我们这些神明也不敢让传送门持续开启超过片刻。在外面的那些地方，有一些东西，它们会被那些裂隙吸引，就像飞蛾被火焰吸引一样。你绝对不能让它们进入来。” “就算我能够安全地打开一个通道，但实际上我既不能也不愿意这么做。你得知道她去了哪个世界，具体在什么地方。她必须处于能够顺利完成这次旅行的状态——毕竟穿越传送门对身心都是极大的考验。当然，她还得有回来的意愿才行。我并不是说不可能把她赢回来，但成功的几率并不大。[pc.name]，虽然失去一个追随者让我感到非常痛苦——哪怕他是一个叛徒——但这种风险实在太大了。恐怕连神明也无法介入来帮助我们。事实上，其他人更有可能试图阻挠你，尤其是维伦和蒂拉。他们非常执着于维护事物的自然秩序，而门户被破坏显然违背了这一秩序。 |真遗憾她没能在这里看到她的守护神呈现出这样的……嗯，这种模样实在算不上什么荣耀，但至少也挺有意思的吧。是无论如何，这也符合猫族的理想。 马拉克的笑容变得更加灿烂：“我通常会努力让自己的外貌符合人们的预期。我发现这样能让别人更容易与我建立联系。但是不，即使凯特在这里，也不会有什么改变；这次谈话是专门为你准备的，只与你有关。” 嗯，你真是感到荣幸啊。 ]
rows.raw: " "Really, now." River leans back on his bench and eyes you, giving you a small, affable smile. "Have you seen me before?" Well, maybe not exactly him, but there's no doubt about it — River carries an air of familiarity about him, a sense of yearning and closeness that speaks to something in you like his music does. It's certainly quite the boon for a musician to have that kind of immediate appeal with his audience, that's for sure. So yes, if you haven't seen him exactly, you can't shake off the feeling that you've seen... you don't know, maybe a relative. Someone who looks distinctly like him or gives off the same feel, that's for certain. "That really means nothing. There are plenty of good musicians in this world, aren't there? And let's face it, manipulating the passions of the crowd is part of being any kind of performer — working one's audience isn't anything strange or suspicious." You said nothing about him being strange or suspicious. "Come now, I'm not stupid and you're not, either." River still has that little placid smile on his lips, friendly and disarming. "You wouldn't be pursuing this line of questioning otherwise. Let's say that you are correct — you've encountered someone who has the same kind of presence that I do. That really doesn't mean anything, does it? The world is wide, and I'm sure that even, say, you have perhaps a dozen kindred souls wandering around with a strikingly similar air to your person. [pc.name], you're just reading too much into all of this, my friend. "On the other hand..." Yes? River purses his lips and stops strumming his lute long enough to raise a finger to his lips. "You're quite an interesting person, and if word has it right, extremely persistent, too. I don't deny that I can't help myself but leave a little breadcrumb trail for those who are so inclined to ask the right questions. Call it a part of my nature, perhaps; it is who I am because of who you are." Whatever does he mean? "What I mean is... you've done well." The air about you suddenly takes on a slight pink hue, and you notice that the people about you in Hawkethorne square have suddenly stopped moving mid-stride, frozen in place.[party.som | | The same goes for [party.compNames] beside you — starting to panic, you reach out for [comp1.hisHer] hand, only to find it insubstantial and incorporeal, your fingers passing through [comp1.hisHer] arm without so much as the slightest resistance. | The same goes for [party.compNames] beside you — starting to panic, you reach out for [comp1.names] hand, only to find it insubstantial and incorporeal, your fingers passing through [comp1.hisHer] arm without so much as the slightest resistance. ] [pc.isDK |What the fuck's |Just what's ] going on here? You look back at River, expecting him to be the source of this mess, but the little catboy bard is just as frozen as everyone else is. His voice still continues to speak, though, although it's not coming from his lips any more, but echoing all about you. "For all the good that it did, you managed to talk your way around Nareva, take her down a peg or two. It does feel good to have that sneaky snake humbled — her domain and portfolio are what they are, but they also lend one to grandeur too easily." You whirl around, and in the blink of an eye a little black-haired catboy is sitting beside River on the bench, just as tiny as he is but wearing a lot less clothing and a lot more jewelry. Sprawled out in a very feline fashion, he eyes you nonchalantly, as if you were an old and familiar friend. Which, to be honest, you might very well be... "So if you don't mind — " the voice is now centered about the little catboy — "Please don't give River a hard time. He's really doing his best at his job, and while he does have a history I really don't bother manufacturing the facts down to the smallest detail. No one asks too much of wandering musicians like him, and yes, I know that he's settled down here in this village. With a mind like yours, I'm sure if you looked into his stated past you could find some discrepancies, but as far as River knows all his memories are perfectly true and he is being genuinely honest in dealing with you." ...And who is he supposed to be? You're certain of the answer, but the question has to be asked nonetheless. The little catboy picks at his jeweled thong before taking his tail in his hands and giving you a playful little smile. "Our pretty pink friend Cait worships me." [party.has cait |You look back over your shoulder at Cait, standing as still as a statue and staring off into empty space; it's not a great leap of logic to assume that she can't see Mallach as she is right now. Shaking your head, you look between her and Mallach several times, then sigh. "She is quite devout despite not having formally taken her vows, but that's alright with me — the vows part, that is. The whole formal clergy bit is just for show anyway; the passion's certainly there! But how much Caitriss believes in the real me and how much is merely her notion of me... well, that's something she has to work out for herself, and until then, it wouldn't do to show myself to her; would ruin her journey. I hope you can understand that. Part of the reason we — well, most of us — leave well enough alone and are loathe to step in is because you need to figure out your own problems a lot of the time; it's something we learned during the Godswar. What's the saying again? 'Give a man a fish', that was it. These days, we're just here to, uh, facilitate." [var0 |Actually, if you're speaking to her patron deity, something comes to mind if he's going to bring up the matter of facilitation. "Yes?" Could he... could he actually do something with her brand, let her have kittens? "Easily. But does she want to have them?" That... "I won't do it against her will. The Brand serves a useful purpose for a girl like her, after all. And it's not like she doesn't know how to solve that little problem if she wanted, though it might be a bit... awkward... after the whole running-off bit she and her sister pulled. But the possibility will always just be that so long as Caitriss doesn't want it." ] That's... well, you can't argue. Speaking of which, can he do something about Calla? Cait's really heartbroken about her sister, and... The catboy god's face turns serious. "[flags.WC_CLEAR |You saw what happened in the Winter City |That's a tough one ]. You can't go breaking portals open willy-nilly or we're all going to end up fucked, and not in the fun way. Haven't you wondered why portals are always brief things? Even we gods fear to open one for more than a moment. There're things out there, in the places between, drawn to breaches like moths to a flame. You don't want to give them a way in, not ever." "Even supposing I could open a portal safely, which I can't, and won't... you'd have to know what world she's gone to, and where she is exactly. She'd have to be in a state to survive the trip — portal-hopping is hard on the body and mind, you know. And of course, she would have to want to come back to begin with. I'm not saying it's impossible to get her back, but the odds aren't great, [pc.name], and as much as it pains me to lose a follower — even an apostate — the risk is too great. I'm afraid the gods can't step in to help. Really, the others are more likely to try and hinder you, especially Velun and Tira. They're rather obsessive about the natural order of things being preserved, and portals being breached is anything but." |It's a pity that she isn't here to see her patron deity in all his... well, this appearance doesn't quite inspire glory, but it is in line with the catfolk ideal anyway. Mallach's smile broadens. "I generally try to shape my appearance to what people expect me to look like. I've found that it helps others relate better. But no, even if Caitriss were here, that would change nothing; this discussion is for you and you alone." Well, aren't you honored. ] "

rows.original: "Now then, you wanted to know about River, is that it? What his deal is?" You wouldn't have asked if you weren't curious about it. "River is..." the smile vanishes from Mallach's face as he presses his hands together and thinks. "I'm not sure there's an exact word for it in Belharan when you translate it from Jassiran, not one that captures the entire nuance of the idea. But the closest thing, I think, would be a homunculus. An entity whom I have created in his entirety without the slightest shred whatsoever of divine power to call his own, placed in a position to observe events and experience life and all its passions in the most authentic fashion possible." That's not quite right — how is he supposed to be able, say, to change your name instantly without any godly shenanigans? "Ah, that's me; all the fun stuff has nothing to do with him whatsoever. River as you know him is as perfectly mundane as he could be, given what he is. Even though I occasionally look out from behind his eyes, he is anything but a meat puppet despite being a creation. If nothing else, he has his own persona and passions. It wouldn't be an authentic experience of life and existence otherwise, would it?" Does he actually have a soul? Can the gods create life out of thin air, or are they fashioned through some other means? "At any one time, there are about two dozen such homunculi out there in the world, just... living life as normal people. Some, like River here, are fashioned out of thin air and have memories of their pasts fabricated. Others are sired or born of said fashioned homunculi for the most authentic experience. Just after the Godswar, I tried it out for myself, you know. The sixty-odd years I spent as the first River were far happier than what I was before, inasmuch as I was able to perceive anything approaching happiness. You know what I mean." You notice he sidestepped your question, not that you can blame him; that's an answer you'd be loathe to give were you in his shoes. Are all the creations named River, too? He shakes his head. "No, no. Men and women, young and old, rich and poor... these homunculi have existed in all forms, from poets to prostitutes. But there is always a River around, and I try to place him where he can observe the most important events of the day. Sentimental reasons, you see; he was the first. "Matter of the fact is, I am a deity of passions, and while I do have something of that from... ah, the manner I came into myself, I've always felt that it was insufficient. River and his ilk have genuinely contributed to that understanding over all these years — an authentic expression of all the passions of people from all walks of life, from great and selfless love to petty envies and jealousies. What you all take for granted and think normal in the course of things is actually quite rare and fascinating when viewed from the perspective of a fellow like me; the chaos and capriciousness of your often contradictory desires is what keeps this world from being boring! To use a little hyperbole, I do not quite agree with Nareva that existence should consist of balls moving around other balls in a predictable and orderly fashion, although I don't suppose I could hold that position even if I wanted to. It is part of who I am, after all, and that stems from the fact that it is part of who you are." ... "Well then, [pc.name]. You wanted to know if you'd seen River before, and there you have your answer — yes, but not in the way you imagined. River was... the first. The River you are familiar with, as I have fashioned him, is more or less an amalgamation of the best parts of all the other Rivers who have lived. You see fragments of other people who resonate with you in his persona, because there are so many that such an effect is frankly, unavoidable. Are you satisfied with what you've learned today?" ...At this rate, you'll never be able to meet someone new without wondering if they're another of Mallach's vessels. A shrug and coy smile. "I think you'll know if you run into another of them. Nareva assures me that you are quite perceptive. With that, I hope you're satisfied with the answer you have, friend. Well, you probably aren't and that knowledge's probably only raised more questions, but you'll just have to figure those out on your own. River won't know, that's for sure. "So... have at it. I don't care if you and yours make a story of triumph or utter hopelessness, it's all delightful drama to me." Before you can raise any objections, the pink tint fades from the air, and the world starts into motion once more. The sounds of Hawkethorne's hubbub flood back into your ears, and River's words continue as if nothing had ever taken place. "It's a wide world, and it takes all sorts to make it. I'm sure there's someone out there who looks just a little like you, too, or maybe even more than a little like you." River waggles his hand in a gesture that's neither here nor there. "But come on, does it really matter if you've seen me before? What does matter is that I, the Singing Arrow, am here and prepared to move your heart and soul — for a small fee, that is. Heroes like you do deeds, I write songs, something something exclusivity clause, but yeah, easy!" [party.has cait |"I don't know about that," Cait whispers into your ear when River's occupied in greeting a passer-by. "He looks cute, to be sure, but there's something about him that's creepy and off. He makes the fur on my tail rise, and... I don't know. It's just a feeling." You give Cait a long, hard look and wonder if you should try telling Cait that you just saw Mallach — or at least, you think you did. Would she believe you? Probably not... "Hey, [pc.name], you're looking at me funny. Did something happen?" No, no... |Yeah, easy indeed. Easy indeed... ]
rows.translation: 那么，你其实是想了解关于瑞弗的事情，对吧？想知道他到底在忙些什么。” 如果你不是对此感到好奇，就不会提出这样的问题。 “瑞弗其实是……”马拉克脸上的笑容消失了，他双手交叠，开始思考起来。我不确定在贝拉兰语中是否有一个确切的词汇可以用来表达这个概念，因为从贾西兰语翻译过来后，没有任何一个词能够完全涵盖这个概念的所有细微含义。但我觉得，最接近的词应该是‘人造生命体’。这种生命体完全是由我创造出来的，它们没有任何属于自身的神力，但却被置于能够以最真实的方式观察各种事件、体验生活以及其中的一切情感的位置上。那不太对吧——比如说，他怎么可能不借助任何神奇的手段，就立刻改变你的名字呢？ “啊，那都是我干的；所有这些有趣的事情其实都和他毫无关系。正如你所知道的，河在很多方面都显得极其平凡、普通。是尽管我偶尔会透过他的眼睛去看世界，但尽管他是一个被创造出来的存在，他却绝不是一个没有思想的肉体傀儡。至少，他拥有自己独特的个性和热情。否则，这样的生活体验也就失去了它的真实意义，不是吗？ 他究竟有没有灵魂？神明真的是凭空创造生命，还是通过其他方式造就了这些生灵？ “在任何时候，这个世界上都存在着大约二十几个这样的‘小人’。他们像普通人一样生活。其中一些人，比如这里的瑞弗，其实是凭空创造出来的，他们的过去经历也是被人为编造的。而另一些人，则是由这些被创造出来的人所生育或诞生的，这样就能获得更加真实的体验。在神战之后，我也亲自试过这种体验，你知道的。在我作为第一个“瑞弗”度过的六十多年时间里，我过得比以前快乐多了，因为那时我终于能够感受到接近幸福的那种感觉了。你们应该明白我的意思吧。 你注意到他避开了你的问题，不过这也不能怪他；如果处在他的位置，你也会很不愿意回答这个问题的。难道所有的这些创造物都被命名为“瑞弗”吗？ 他摇了摇头：“不，并不是这样。有男有女，有老有少，有富有穷……这些被创造出来的人形生物有着各种各样的形态，从诗人到妓女，应有尽有。但是，每个创造物身边总是会有一个‘瑞弗’存在，而我总是试图把他们安排在能够观察到当天最重要事件的地方。你知道，这是出于一些情感上的原因吧……毕竟，他是第一个被创造出来的。 事实上，我本身就是情感的象征。虽然我自身具有一些与情感相关的特质……嗯，这大概与我诞生方式有关，但我一直觉得这些特质还不够。这些年来，瑞弗以及他那一群人确实为人们更好地理解情感做出了贡献——他们真实地展现了各行各业人们的情感世界，从伟大而无私的爱，到那些琐碎的嫉妒与怨恨。在像我这样的角度来看，那些你们都认为理所当然、觉得再正常不过的事情，其实是非常罕见且令人着迷的；你们那些常常相互矛盾的欲望所带来的混乱与无常，正是让这个世界不会变得无聊的原因！套用一点夸张的说法，我并不完全同意娜瑞瓦的观点，即人类的存在应该仅仅是由一些球以可预测且有序的方式相互碰撞、运动所构成的。不过，我也不认为自己有什么不同的看法可以即使我想改变，我也无法改变这个事实。毕竟，这已经成为我自我认同的一部分了，而这一点的根源，其实也在于你本身也是如此。” …… “那么，[pc.name]你之前想知道自己是否曾经见过瑞弗，现在你得到了答案——是的，但并非以你想象中的那种方式。瑞弗其实是……第一个。而你现在所熟悉的瑞弗，其实是我在他身上融合了所有曾经存在过的瑞弗们的优点所创造出来的形象。在他的性格中，你能看到那些与你产生共鸣的其他人的影子，因为这样的影子实在太多了，以至于这种效果几乎是不可避免的。你对今天所学到的这些内容感到满意吗？ 照这样下去，你每次结识新朋友时，都会忍不住怀疑他们是不是马拉克的另一个化身。” 她耸了耸肩，露出一个俏皮的微笑：“我想如果你真的遇到了这样的人，你自己就会明白的。娜瑞瓦告诉我，你其实很有洞察力。那么，希望你对现有的答案感到满意吧，朋友……不过恐怕你并不满意，而这些疑问反而让你产生了更多的疑惑，不过这些你只能自己去弄清楚了。河绝对不会知道这些的。 那么……尽管开始吧。我不在乎你和你的同伴们会编出一个关于胜利的故事，还是一个关于彻底绝望的故事，对我来说，这一切都不过是精彩的戏剧罢了。” 你还没来得及提出任何反对意见，空气中的粉色光芒就已经消失了，世界再次恢复了生机。鹰棘镇的喧闹声重新传入你的耳中，而瑞弗的话也仿佛什么都没发生过一样，继续说着。 这个世界如此广阔，各种各样的人都有。我敢肯定，肯定有某个和你长得有点像的人，甚至可能非常像你。”瑞弗随意地挥了挥手，似乎并不太确定自己在说什么。“但是，说真的，你之前是否见过我，真的有那么重要吗？确实关键在于，我，这位“歌唱之箭”，就在这里，而且愿意用一点点代价来触动你的心灵——当然，这是有条件的。像你这样的英雄会做出伟大的事迹，而我则会创作歌曲。还有一些独家授权之类的条款，不过嘛，其实挺简单的！ [party.has cait |我不太确定，”当瑞弗正忙着跟路过的行人打招呼时，凯特在你耳边低声说道，“他确实看起来挺可爱的，但就是有点让人觉得毛骨悚然、不太对劲。他让我浑身都不自在……总之，就是有一种不好的感觉。” 你仔细地打量了凯特一番，心里在想：是不是应该告诉她，你刚才其实看到了马拉克——或者至少，你思考你做到了。但她会相信你吗？大概不会吧…… “嘿，[pc.name]，你看着我的样子好奇怪啊，是不是发生了什么事情？” “不，没有…… |是啊，确实很简单。真的非常简单…… ]
rows.raw: " "Now then, you wanted to know about River, is that it? What his deal is?" You wouldn't have asked if you weren't curious about it. "River is..." the smile vanishes from Mallach's face as he presses his hands together and thinks. "I'm not sure there's an exact word for it in Belharan when you translate it from Jassiran, not one that captures the entire nuance of the idea. But the closest thing, I think, would be a homunculus. An entity whom I have created in his entirety without the slightest shred whatsoever of divine power to call his own, placed in a position to observe events and experience life and all its passions in the most authentic fashion possible." That's not quite right — how is he supposed to be able, say, to change your name instantly without any godly shenanigans? "Ah, that's me; all the fun stuff has nothing to do with him whatsoever. River as you know him is as perfectly mundane as he could be, given what he is. Even though I occasionally look out from behind his eyes, he is anything but a meat puppet despite being a creation. If nothing else, he has his own persona and passions. It wouldn't be an authentic experience of life and existence otherwise, would it?" Does he actually have a soul? Can the gods create life out of thin air, or are they fashioned through some other means? "At any one time, there are about two dozen such homunculi out there in the world, just... living life as normal people. Some, like River here, are fashioned out of thin air and have memories of their pasts fabricated. Others are sired or born of said fashioned homunculi for the most authentic experience. Just after the Godswar, I tried it out for myself, you know. The sixty-odd years I spent as the first River were far happier than what I was before, inasmuch as I was able to perceive anything approaching happiness. You know what I mean." You notice he sidestepped your question, not that you can blame him; that's an answer you'd be loathe to give were you in his shoes. Are all the creations named River, too? He shakes his head. "No, no. Men and women, young and old, rich and poor... these homunculi have existed in all forms, from poets to prostitutes. But there is always a River around, and I try to place him where he can observe the most important events of the day. Sentimental reasons, you see; he was the first. "Matter of the fact is, I am a deity of passions, and while I do have something of that from... ah, the manner I came into myself, I've always felt that it was insufficient. River and his ilk have genuinely contributed to that understanding over all these years — an authentic expression of all the passions of people from all walks of life, from great and selfless love to petty envies and jealousies. What you all take for granted and think normal in the course of things is actually quite rare and fascinating when viewed from the perspective of a fellow like me; the chaos and capriciousness of your often contradictory desires is what keeps this world from being boring! To use a little hyperbole, I do not quite agree with Nareva that existence should consist of balls moving around other balls in a predictable and orderly fashion, although I don't suppose I could hold that position even if I wanted to. It is part of who I am, after all, and that stems from the fact that it is part of who you are." ... "Well then, [pc.name]. You wanted to know if you'd seen River before, and there you have your answer — yes, but not in the way you imagined. River was... the first. The River you are familiar with, as I have fashioned him, is more or less an amalgamation of the best parts of all the other Rivers who have lived. You see fragments of other people who resonate with you in his persona, because there are so many that such an effect is frankly, unavoidable. Are you satisfied with what you've learned today?" ...At this rate, you'll never be able to meet someone new without wondering if they're another of Mallach's vessels. A shrug and coy smile. "I think you'll know if you run into another of them. Nareva assures me that you are quite perceptive. With that, I hope you're satisfied with the answer you have, friend. Well, you probably aren't and that knowledge's probably only raised more questions, but you'll just have to figure those out on your own. River won't know, that's for sure. "So... have at it. I don't care if you and yours make a story of triumph or utter hopelessness, it's all delightful drama to me." Before you can raise any objections, the pink tint fades from the air, and the world starts into motion once more. The sounds of Hawkethorne's hubbub flood back into your ears, and River's words continue as if nothing had ever taken place. "It's a wide world, and it takes all sorts to make it. I'm sure there's someone out there who looks just a little like you, too, or maybe even more than a little like you." River waggles his hand in a gesture that's neither here nor there. "But come on, does it really matter if you've seen me before? What does matter is that I, the Singing Arrow, am here and prepared to move your heart and soul — for a small fee, that is. Heroes like you do deeds, I write songs, something something exclusivity clause, but yeah, easy!" [party.has cait |"I don't know about that," Cait whispers into your ear when River's occupied in greeting a passer-by. "He looks cute, to be sure, but there's something about him that's creepy and off. He makes the fur on my tail rise, and... I don't know. It's just a feeling." You give Cait a long, hard look and wonder if you should try telling Cait that you just saw Mallach — or at least, you think you did. Would she believe you? Probably not... "Hey, [pc.name], you're looking at me funny. Did something happen?" No, no... |Yeah, easy indeed. Easy indeed... ] "

rows.original:
You ask River if he can provide a spot of entertainment. The little kitten-boy gives you a smile and nod, then stops strumming his lute long enough to extend an open palm towards you.

    "Sure can do, so long as you've got the coin."
    
    You toss a couple of electrum pieces to River, who deftly catches them out of the air. "Many thanks, friend. So, what do you want to hear? Something lighthearted to rouse the spirits, or something somber to give one pause?"
rows.translation:
你问瑞弗能不能来一段助兴表演。那个小猫男孩朝你笑着点了点头，然后停下拨弄鲁特琴，向你摊开一只手掌。

    “当然可以，只要你有钱。”
    
    你把几枚琥珀金币抛给瑞弗，他灵巧地在半空中接住。“多谢了，朋友。那么，你想听点什么？来点轻松快活的提提神，还是来点沉重哀伤的让人静一静？”

rows.original:
River finishes his music with a small flourish, and the town square erupts into a series of raucous cheers from the passersby present. The catboy lets his tune die down to strumming, and at length, the people begin to disperse, a fair few changing their course towards the Frost Hound. At length, Garth emerges from his establishment, carrying a tall glass of something golden and foaming out to the bench by the statue.

    "Cheers." River eagerly takes the glass and downs it in a quick series of gulps. For such a small kitten, he's sure got a large stomach on him. "Thanks, old friend."
    
    Garth grunts as he retrieves the glass and turns his back on the both of you. "You keep them coming and drinking, and there'll be more where that came from."
    
    "Haha, of course!" River throws a sidelong glance at you. "I think I'm done for now, friend. I'll sing you another song later... for another couple of hawks, if you like."
rows.translation:
瑞弗以一小段华丽的演奏结束了他的音乐，此时镇广场上，路人们爆发出一阵阵喧闹的欢呼声。那个猫人少年让旋律逐渐减弱，转为轻轻弹奏，最终，人们开始散去，其中有不少人改变了方向，朝着霜犬酒馆的方向走去。终于，加斯从他的住所走了出来，手里拿着一杯金黄色的、冒着泡沫的饮料，走向雕像旁的长椅。

    “干杯。”瑞弗迫不及待地接过杯子，一口气喝了个精光。对于这么一只小小的小猫来说，它的胃容量还真不小啊。谢谢，老朋友。”
    
    加思哼了一声，拿起了杯子，然后转身离开了你们俩。“你们继续让他们来喝酒吧，还会有更多的酒出现的。”
    
    “哈哈，当然啦！”瑞弗侧眼看了你一眼。我想我现在暂时忙完了，朋友。等会儿我会再为你唱一首歌……当然，如果你愿意付更多的钱的话。

rows.original:
Once the music dies down, the passersby who've gathered to listen start moving off, muttering and sighing amongst themselves. A couple head into the Frost Hound, perhaps to drown recently surfaced sorrows, and the two of you watch the scene play out.

    "Ah, nothing like a bit of soft and slow to get the spirits moving, in more sense than one." River chuckles. "A dash of melancholy can help, too. The music wants to be free, but I'm done for now."
rows.translation:
当乐声渐渐平息，那些聚拢来聆听的路人开始陆续散去，彼此低声嘟囔着、叹着气。有几个人走进了霜犬酒馆，或许是想借酒浇灭刚刚泛起的愁绪，而你们俩看着这一幕落幕。

    “啊，没什么比一段轻柔舒缓的曲子更能让人心神摇动——而且不止一种意义上。”瑞弗轻笑着说，“掺一点忧郁也有帮助。音乐想要自由，可我现在先到此为止了。”

rows.original:
"I like this one," River muses. "This one was from a time when dragons ruled the world, or so they say."

    Sylistraxia was an empress who was haughty and vain
    And especially proud of her despotic reign.
    But conceit of this sort isn't proper at all
    And soon the old tyrant was doomed for a fall.
    One day as she viewed her subjects from 'high,
    A virile young drake caught the dragon slut's eye.
    Bending over to see, that oversexed bitch
    Let her gold crown slip, and fall into the ditch.
    With a cry of sheer terror, she jumped like a fool,
    And rushed to the moat which reeked like a cesspool.
    She leaped in! Kersplash! And sank like a stone.
    (Everyone hoped for a new ass 'pon the throne.)
    But alas she came up and staggered from the sewer,
    Her garments reeked of offal, her breath of manure.
    "Why did I do that? What possessed me today?
    I smell almost as bad as the drakes which I lay!"
    "And if anyone sees me, oh what a disgrace,
    I'd better leave if I want to save face!"
    But a crowd had assembled and stared, amazed,
    The sight confused them, the stench left them dazed.
    Then with a shriek, a kobold began to laugh,
    Giggling and pointing at the Empress' fecal bath.
    Becoming enraged, she suddenly turned wild,
    She looked like she wanted to strangle the child!
    Her hand turned to fist, and she struck lightning fast,
    But the old whore missed, slipped, and fell on her ass.
    Not holding back, the crowd soon roared,
    The laughter was deafening. It grew till it soared.
    But the Empress was dour and called for her guard,
    The arrival of violence quickly silenced the herd.
    "You who found humor in my sorrow and misfortune
    Will soon find the rack! And pain! And contortion!
    Then I will cackle as you stew and boil,
    In a pot full of lard, sauce and bubbling oil.
    And for those who survive but would rather be dead,
    I'll pluck out their eyes, and chop off their heads!
    Finally at my feast, roasted bodies will swing,
    And I'll take delight in devouring your spleens!"
    All were led away at the point of a sword,
    While old Syli took a dip in a ford.
    Then she laughed at the cries that screamed through the night,
    She chuckled at their anguish, she cackled at their plight.
    In the Empire today, none dare to tell this tale,
    Lest they find themselves thrown in the pits' darkest jail.
    But here amongst ourselves this song can be sung,
    The tale of how the Empress acquired her faint smell of dung.
rows.translation:
“我喜欢这一首，”瑞弗沉吟道，“据说它来自巨龙统治世界的年代。”

    西利斯特拉克西亚女皇傲慢又虚荣，
    尤以自己的暴虐统治为荣。
    可这般自负实在不成体统，
    老暴君很快便注定一跤栽重。
    一日她从高处俯瞰臣民，
    一头年轻雄龙引得荡妇龙女动心。
    那好色母龙弯下腰想看得真切，
    金色王冠却滑落，掉进沟渠不见。
    她惊恐尖叫，像傻瓜般纵身一跃，
    冲向那臭如粪坑的护城河边。
    她跳了进去！扑通！像石头般下沉。
    （众人都盼王座上的屁股换人。）
    可惜她又浮上来，踉跄爬出下水道，
    衣衫臭如内脏，呼吸尽是粪肥味道。
    “我为何这么做？今天究竟中了什么邪？
    我闻着快跟那些同我上床的雄龙一样恶劣！”
    “若有人看见我，哦，那该多丢脸，
    想要保住颜面，我最好赶快走远！”
    可围观人群早已聚拢，惊愕地凝望，
    眼前景象令他们困惑，恶臭令他们昏茫。
    随着一声尖叫，一个狗头人笑了起来，
    咯咯发笑，指着女皇洗过的粪池。
    女皇勃然大怒，霎时陷入狂暴，
    她看起来简直想把那孩子掐掉！
    她攥紧拳头，以闪电般速度出击，
    可老娼妇打偏脚滑，一屁股摔倒在地。
    人群不再忍耐，顷刻哄笑如雷，
    笑声震耳欲聋，愈来愈响，直冲天际。
    女皇却阴沉着脸，召来自己的卫兵，
    暴力一到，喧闹人群立刻鸦雀无声。
    “胆敢从我的悲伤与不幸中取乐之人，
    很快就会尝到刑架！痛苦！身体扭曲变形！
    待你们在锅中炖煮翻滚，我便放声怪笑，
    那锅里装满猪油、酱汁与沸腾的油膏。
    若有人幸存却宁愿一死了之，
    我便挖出他们的双眼，再把脑袋砍掉！
    最后，在我的宴会上，烤熟的尸体高高悬吊，
    我会尽情享受吞食你们脾脏的美妙！”
    所有人都在刀锋逼迫下被押走，
    老西莉则去浅滩里洗净污垢。
    随后她聆听彻夜回荡的惨叫，开怀大笑，
    因他们的痛苦轻笑，为他们的厄运狂笑。
    如今帝国之中，无人胆敢讲述这个故事，
    免得自己被扔进深坑里最黑暗的牢狱。
    可我们私下相聚，仍能将这首歌传唱，
    它讲述女皇如何染上那股淡淡的粪臭芳香。

    Finally at my feast, roasted bodies will swing,
    And I'll take delight in devouring your spleens!"
    All were led away at the point of a sword,
    While old Syli took a dip in a ford.
    Then she laughed at the cries that screamed through the night,
    She chuckled at their anguish, she cackled at their plight.
    In the Empire today, none dare to tell this tale,
    Lest they find themselves thrown in the pits' darkest jail.
    But here amongst ourselves this song can be sung,
    The tale of how the Empress acquired her faint smell of dung.'

rows.original:
"This one's pretty common in what's left of Old Belhar," River says as he begins. "Not quite as much up here, but them's the breaks."
    
    Come all, you artisans and tradesmen,
    And my fellow revelers and fools.
    Remember each day that your trade would decay
    If a maid did not look to your tools.
    The blacksmith, the sooty old blacksmith,
    Truly a solid and stoic old fellow.
    But his iron would burn old, and his fire grow cold,
    If a maid did not blow up his bellows.
    Then there's the fine young chandler,
    He works up the tallow so quick.
    But his craft would be marred, and his works not get hard,
    If a maid did not stiffen his wick.
    The ploughman, the jolly spry ploughman,
    He follows the plow in the silt.
    But the fields would be unturned, if a maid had not learned
    To take in his blade to the hilt.
    The brewer, the merry red brewer,
    He makes a very fine ale.
    But his brew would be waste, if there's no maid to taste,
    And make sure that it doesn't grow stale.
    So come all you journeymen, craftsmen,
    And all that are apprenticed to trade.
    For there'd never be a screw, nor a nut busted too,
    If it weren't for the help of a maid!
rows.translation:
“这首在旧贝尔哈残存的地区相当常见，”瑞弗开口唱道，“在这儿就没那么流行了，不过世事就是这样。”
    
    来吧，所有的工匠与手艺人，
    还有我的酒友与傻瓜们。
    请记住，你的手艺终会荒废，
    若没有姑娘照看你的工具。
    那铁匠，满身烟灰的老铁匠，
    真是个结实又坚忍的老家伙。
    可他的铁终会烧损，炉火终会变冷，
    若没有姑娘帮他吹旺风箱。
    还有那俊俏的年轻蜡烛匠，
    他搓起油脂来手脚真快。
    可他的手艺会走样，成品也硬不起来，
    若没有姑娘帮他把烛芯弄硬。
    那农夫，快活又利落的老农，
    他跟着犁头走在淤泥里。
    可若没有姑娘学会这一手，田地就永远翻不过来，
    将他的犁刀整根吞入至柄。
    那酿酒师，快活的红脸酿酒师，
    他酿的麦酒真是好。
    可若没有姑娘来尝，他的酒就白酿了，
    还得保证它不会放陈变味。
    所以来吧，所有短工、工匠，
    还有所有在手艺行里当学徒的人。
    因为永远不会有拧动的螺丝，也不会有被拧坏的螺母，
    若不是有姑娘来帮忙！

rows.original:
"I like this one," River muses. "They say a paladin composed it."
    
    If all the young ladies were little white rabbits,
    I'd be a hare, and teach them bad habits!
    If all the young ladies were bricks in a pile,
    I'd be a mason and lay them in style!
    If all the young ladies were hens in the hay,
    I'd be a cock, and ensure a good lay.
    If all the young ladies were bells in a tower,
    and I were a clapper, I'd ring every hour!
    If all the young ladies were doors of stout wood,
    and I were a knocker, I'd bang them up good!
    If all the young ladies were peaches so sweet,
    I'd suck out their juices and chew on their meat.
    If all the young ladies were birds in their nests,
    I'd be an egg, and lie on their breasts.
    If all the young ladies were mares of good breeding,
    I'd be the prize stallion and give them a seeding!
    
    If all the young ladies were this, and I were that,
    I'd be all over them, at the drop of a hat!
    But since they aren't here and I can't be arsed,
    Bartender, go on and fill up my glass!
rows.translation:
“我喜欢这一首，”瑞弗若有所思地说，“据说是一位圣骑士创作的。”
    
    如果所有年轻的女士都是一只只小白兔，
    我就会变成一只野兔，把坏习惯都传染给她们！
    如果所有年轻的女士都是一堆砖块……
    我要成为一名石匠，把它们砌得漂亮无比！
    如果所有年轻姑娘都像是干草堆里的母鸡，
    那我就会变成公鸡，保证让她们被好好操上一顿！
    如果所有年轻姑娘都像是塔楼里的铃铛，
    而我就是那根钟锤，那我一定会每小时都敲响一次！
    如果所有年轻姑娘都是一扇扇结实的木门，
    而我是一副门环，那我一定会把它们敲得砰砰作响！
    如果所有年轻姑娘都像那样甜美可口的桃子，
    我一定会吸干它们的汁液，然后品尝它们的果肉。
    如果所有年轻姑娘都像那些在巢中的小鸟……
    我愿意变成一颗蛋，躺在她们的胸前。
    如果所有年轻姑娘都是血统优良的母马，
    那我就会成为那匹最优秀的种马，让她们都能怀孕！
    
    如果所有年轻姑娘都是这样的，而我又是那样的，
    那我一定会立刻扑向她们，毫不犹豫！
    但她们又不在这里，而我也没心情管这些，
    酒保，快把我的杯子倒满吧！
