rows.original: [rand |Was he born into the temple the same way that Cait and Salwah were? "I wasn't born into the Temple, but I was raised in it." Yusra sighs and clasps his hands together. "It happens in the poorer parts of the land, especially when there's famine, drought, the likes — sometimes a small village temple will find a box in a courtyard with a kitten or two in it. I happened to have such a beginning." Oh. You're sorry. "Don't be, it's just one of those unfortunate facts of life; people plan expecting times of plenty and then get seven years of lean instead. For centuries, the Temple of Mallach has shouldered the duty of caring for Jassira's orphans and foundlings, in association with the Lumian temple, of course. The latter helps a lot, but the former is where all the wealth and resources lie, so a partnership to care for the unfortunate is necessary. "It was an okay life, I suppose. A small village temple has not even one-twentieth of the wealth and splendour of those in the big cities, but we were fed, watered, sheltered from the worst of the sandstorms and worked to the bone. Not that any of the half-dozen of us complained, because we could clearly see the link between the work we were doing and how it kept us alive. Existence in the inner desert is hard. I have the temple matron to thank, really — I remember there was one time when a visiting spicetender offered to buy me and another kitten, and she refused." The way Yusra says it so matter-of-factly... yes, Jassira is the world's greatest exporter of its own people through such means, but to hear it coming from his mouth... "Kittens taken in by the temple are supposed to be under the holy protection of the Prince of Passions, which is why people have the confidence send foundlings to the temple steps in hard times, knowing they'll be cared for as best as circumstances allow. But corruption is like rats — something to be kept down, but never truly exterminated, and it permeates any and every institution to some degree. I was fortunate." So, he took his vows when he came of age? "Not at first. Like many in my position, I thought temple life too stuffy with its rules and strictures, and ached to be free; I was out the gates the moment I could be. I won't go into details, but the next two years of my life proved well enough that the other end of the oasis was hardly as verdant as I'd imagined it to be. "I've been lucky, but Tira tires of carrying the same person on her back for too long. After some thought, I returned to the temple that had raised me and took my vows. Didn't stay there long, though, wound up being dispatched soon enough... and the rest is, well." He taps his brand of the harlot. "One thing leading to another." |Is there any reason he became a paladin in particular? Or was it even a choice that he could make to begin with? Neither Cait or Sally have gone too deeply into how their vocations were assigned, although it seems that they started years before they took their vows. "No such luck for me, I'm afraid. Partly because I didn't have the good fortune to live in the capital, partly because when I was that age I was determined to leave the temple when I reached my majority." Yusra chuckles sadly. "But yes, when I returned to the temple and took my vows, I was presented with some options. "I could've been a comfort boy, you know; I've certainly got the goods for it. And I won't deny that it was very, very tempting. But as nice as a life of comfort would've been, I know what happens to those who lean just a bit too hard on their looks and wind up with not much left when those start to fade. Let's face it — you only have a handful of years of being a prime fuckboy, and then the wear and tear starts to show, even with all of the Temple's knowledge behind you. The life doesn't leave you with much time to prepare yourself for what comes after, either." So it was that or be a paladin? There were no other choices open to him? "Oh no, there were plenty. But being a paladin... I'd have an excuse to be outside the temple gates when things got too stuffy inside, and still be able to duck back in when it got too hot outside. That, and it appealed to my sense of adventure while I was still a kitten. Being on the front line of holy struggle and taking the most direct action in the name of the Prince of Passion, that kind of thing. It's been fun, and more than one temple matron has appreciated me pitching in with the comfort boy routine while I was billeted with them. Best of both worlds, you know?" |So, prior to all this demon business, what did he do as a Mallachite paladin? The world hasn't completely settled down from the Godswar, but there is this tenuous peace, inasmuch as one can have peace. "Pilgrim escort is one of the biggest ongoing duties of Mallachite paladins in peacetime, and there's never any lack of work in that regard. Mallachites live all over the world, and those who still consider themselves observant make it a point to at least try to make a pilgrimage to a major temple." Given how much more dangerous the world is after the Godswar, an escort makes sense. But you'd imagine that only the wealthy and well-connected would be able to leave their homes for extended periods of time, kind of like Cait and her family, come to think of it. "Oh, yes, it's a custom of old that's had to adapt to darker times. It used to be that everyone would try to make it to a major temple, but that's just not practical — the old roads may still exist, but not all of them are safe and many monsters wear the shapes of people. There's also the fact that common people can't afford to leave their homesteads unattended — it's one of the reasons why your temple is so popular, being an easy outlet for every observant catfolk in the region to fulfill their holy obligations. Bringing the faithful to the Prince of Passions and returning them safely... there aren't that many truly higher callings, I feel." You can guess. There are perks to the job, you take it? "I wouldn't call it a benefit, but any Mallachite temple is obliged to billet me and any pilgrims while they're making the journey, more than just the customary bath and night in the courtyard for anyone. The freedom of being able to travel within and without Jassira, that's another... but most of all, getting to know the rich and powerful from various parts of the world, sometimes carnally! Make a trip with a group in tow, pick up people heading home, pick up another group and so forth... I'd just finished my fourth such round trip and first one beyond Jassira when the call came in to head up here." |Hmm. His gear is quite fancy — it was assigned to him by the temple, wasn't it? "Oh, of course it was; you won't be able to get this sort of thing off the street. It's quite a serious thing to even get too close to a paladin's regalia — impersonation of an authority figure and all that, you see. In some places in the desert, a wandering paladin is about all the law and order you're going to get, and so it's important that people can trust their eyes instead of having to double-guess themselves." Yusra's eyes glint, and the catboy grins. "Why, what's with that look? Perhaps my armor is a little too revealing to be practical?" Well... "Ah, I jest, I jest. But it indeed is very, very eye-catching, and intentionally so. There's a reason why the symbol of my particular order is the desert rose — strength in beauty and all that. Being effective in a fight doesn't mean you can't look good while at it, and doing something in style is really good for morale. That, and being underestimated because your armor 'shows too much skin' helps a whole bunch; you've got to stay in style." |How long has he been out of Jassira, now? "About a year, give or take a month. Last time I stayed was about until the end of the dry season until my bones got restless enough for me to take another escort commission out of the nation." Does he miss the homeland? "Well, yes and no. Like I said, when I'm there, my bones wind up restless; when I'm out on business, I wind up hankering for the warmth and sun back home. It's not really a bad thing, keeps me on the move — I think this scouting assignment is the first real task I've had which has required me to stay in one place for an indefinite amount of time. "It's like when I was young, I suppose. Growing up in the temple, I hated being subjected to its strictures; once let loose out into the world, I wanted the comfort and safety Mallach's halls provided. And no sooner had I taken my vows and had my brand inscribed that I was thinking of heading out again." He laughs. "I guess it's just my lot in life, my passion to desire something as impossible as boiled ice." |Is it awkward, being a paladin of Mallach? Usually when people hear the word the stereotype that comes to mind is Lumian or Tiran, who have more established martial traditions. Then there's, say, Sorrans, who while not actively being all smite-y on the other hand also don't have anything against it. "Well, depends on who's asking." He gives you a wink. "Those who can't quite believe that my weapon isn't just used for dancing change their tune pretty quick after a few smacks upside the head with a glaive — not that I'm in the habit of being short-tempered, of course. A paladin of Mallach has to know what temperance is, but that doesn't preclude a good old consensual bout. "That aside... once the initial shock's done with, it's good to be flashy. When you stick out, people remember the nice Mallachite paladin who helped with an embarrassing disease much easier, and it's easier to build a reputation that way. We're the first line of defence against any threats that might crop up, especially in the more rural regions, and it makes our jobs a lot easier if people are inclined to trust us to begin with." You can see where he's coming from. It doesn't hurt that Yusra presents himself as a bit of a brat — that kind of mischievous, energetic demeanor sticks out and leaves an impression on people. Attitude, looks and ability, he's got it all. "Really, you don't need to flatter me to get in my pants. That being said, I can't say that I don't enjoy flaunting what I have. Being able to walk in and grab the center of attention if you so chose... it's an addictive feeling, and one that you shouldn't get too used to. Just so you know, ha!" ]
rows.translation: [rand |他也是像凯特和萨尔瓦那样在寺庙中出生的吗？ “我并不是在寺庙中出生的，但我在那里长大的。”尤斯拉叹了口气，双手交握在一起说道，“在那些较为贫困的地区，尤其是在发生饥荒、干旱之类的灾害时，有时一些小村庄的寺庙里会发现院子里有个盒子，里面有一两只小猫。我的命运就是这样的。” 哦，你感到很抱歉。 “别这样，这只是生活中那些不幸的事情之一罢了；人们总是期待着丰饶的时光，但却往往要经历七年的艰难时期。几个世纪以来，马拉克神殿一直肩负着照顾贾西拉地区的孤儿和弃儿的职责，当然，这也得到了卢米亚神庙的协助。后者的帮助确实很大，但所有的财富和资源都掌握在前者手中，因此，为了共同照顾这些不幸的人，这种合作是必不可少的。” “我想，这样的生活也算不错吧。虽然小村庄里的寺庙远没有大城市的寺庙那么富有、那么宏伟，但我们有饭吃、有水喝，也能躲避最猛烈的沙尘暴，还得累死累活地干活。我们这六个人中并没有人抱怨，因为我们都清楚地看到，自己所做的工作与维持生存息息相关。在内陆沙漠中生存本来就非常艰难。真的，我得感谢那位寺庙的女主管——我记得有一次，有位路过的香料商提出要买下我和另一只小猫，但她拒绝了。” 尤斯拉说得如此理所当然……没错，贾西拉确实是通过这种方式成为世界上“输出人口”最多的地方，但听到这种话出自他的口中…… “被寺庙收留的小猫应该受到‘激情王子’的神圣保护，正因如此，人们在艰难时期才会放心地把弃儿送到寺庙门口，因为他们知道这些孩子会得到尽可能好的照顾。但是腐化就像老鼠一样——必须加以遏制，却永远无法彻底根除，而且它在某种程度上渗透到了每一个机构之中。我很幸运。” 那么，他成年后就立下了誓言吗？ “并不是立刻。和很多处于我这种处境的人一样，我认为寺院的生活充满了规则和束缚，太过于压抑了，我渴望获得自由；一有机会，我就立刻离开了那里。具体细节我就不赘述了，但接下来的两年让我清楚地认识到：绿洲的另一边并不像我想象中那么美好。” “我确实很幸运，但蒂拉也受不了长期背负同一个人。经过一番思考，我回到了抚养我长大的那座寺庙，立下了自己的誓言。不过我在那里待的时间并不长，很快就被派往了别的地方……剩下的，嘛，你也知道。”他轻敲着自己那枚娼妓的烙印，“一系列的事情就这样发生了。” |他之所以会选择成为圣骑士，究竟有什么原因吗？还是说，这本来就是他可以自主做出的选择呢？无论是凯特还是莎莉，都没有深入探讨过自己的职业是如何被确定的，不过看起来，她们在正式宣誓之前，就已经开始了相关的准备和训练。 “恐怕我没什么这样的运气。一部分原因是我没有福气生活在首都，另一部分原因则是，在我那个年纪时，我就已经下定决心，等到成年后就要离开寺庙。”尤斯拉悲伤地笑了笑，“不过，当我回到寺庙并立下誓言后，确实得到了一些选择。” “你知道，我本可以成为一个所谓的‘慰安男孩’；我确实具备做这个角色的所有条件。我也不否认，这样的生活确实非常诱人。但是，尽管这样的生活很惬意，我也清楚：那些过于依赖外貌的人，一旦外貌开始衰退，他们会面临什么。说实话，你能当那种最抢手的浪荡子的年头也就那么几年，之后，各种问题就会开始显现出来，即便有神庙提供的所有知识作为支持。而且，生活本身也不给你太多时间来为未来做好准备。” 所以，要么干那个，要么就当圣骑士？他就没有别的选择了吗？ “哦，不，并不是没有其他选择。但是成为圣骑士的话……当庙内的气氛变得过于压抑时，我就有借口离开庙门；而当外面天气太热时，我也可以随时再回到庙里去。而且，这在我还是小猫的时候就激发了我对冒险的向往。站在神圣斗争的最前线，以‘激情王子’的名义采取最直接的行动——这种感觉真的很有趣。有好几位寺庙的女主管也很感激我在她们那里住宿时，帮着一起做慰安男孩的活儿。两全其美，你懂我的意思吧？” |那么，在所有这些关于恶魔的事情发生之前，作为马拉克信徒圣骑士，他到底做了些什么呢？自从神战之后，世界尚未完全恢复平静，但还存在着一种脆弱的和平——如果这也能算和平的话。 “在和平时期，护送朝圣者是马拉克信徒圣骑士最重要的职责之一，因此这方面的工作从来都不缺。马拉克信徒遍布世界各地，而那些仍然自认虔诚的人，至少会努力前往一座重要的寺庙进行朝圣。” 考虑到神战之后这个世界变得如此危险，配备护送人员确实是必要的。但你可以想象，只有那些富有且人脉广泛的人，才有可能长时间离开自己的家——说起来，就像凯特和她的家人那样。 “哦，是的，这是一种古老的习俗，只是随着时代的变化，它也不得不做出一些调整罢了。过去，每个人都会设法前往一座大型神庙，但那实在不现实——那些古老的道路或许仍然存在，但并非所有道路都安全无阻，而且许多怪物会伪装成人类的形态。此外，普通民众也负担不起让家人独自留在家中不设防的风险。正因如此，你们的寺庙才如此受欢迎，对于该地区所有虔诚的猫族来说，这里都是履行他们神圣义务的便捷场所。将信徒们引见到激情之王身边，并确保他们安全归来……我觉得，真正有更高使命的事情并不多吧。” “你应该能猜到，这份工作确实有一些好处，对吧？” “我不敢称之为好处，但任何马拉克信徒神庙都有义务在我和那些朝圣者赶路期间为我们提供住宿，而不只是像对待一般人那样，按惯例给一次沐浴、让他在院子里过一夜。能够在贾西拉境内自由往返，这也是另一种乐趣……但最重要的是，能够结识来自世界各地的富有权势的人，有时候甚至还能与他们发生一些亲密关系！可以和一群人一起出发旅行，途中遇到准备回家的人，再带上他们继续旅程，然后再结识另一群人，以此类推。就在我完成第四次这样的往返旅程、也是第一次走出贾西拉的时候，传来了要我北上此地的召唤。” |嗯，他的装备相当精致——这些应该是寺庙分配给他的吧？ “哦，当然是的；这种装备在市面上是买不到的。光是靠得离圣骑士的服饰太近，就已经是件相当严重的事了——那等于假冒权威人物之类的，你明白吧。在沙漠的某些地方，游荡的圣骑士几乎就是你能得到的全部法律与秩序，因此人们能够相信自己的眼睛、而不必反复怀疑自己才是非常重要的。”尤斯拉的眼睛闪烁着光芒，而那个猫族男孩也露出了微笑。“哎呀，你那是什么表情？也许我的护甲太过暴露，不太实用吧？” “嗯……” “啊，我开玩笑的，开玩笑的。不过它的确非常非常引人注目，这也是有意为之的。我们这个组织选择沙漠玫瑰作为象征，就是寓意着‘美丽之中蕴含力量’这样的含义嘛。在战斗中表现出色并不意味着你就不能同时保持良好的形象，而以一种时尚、有风格的方式行动确实能够提升士气。另外，因为你的护甲‘暴露了太多皮肤’而被低估，这一情况也会大有帮助——你必须保持风格。” |他离开贾西拉已经有多久了？ “大概一年吧，前后可能差一个月。上次我在那里的时候，一直待到旱季结束，直到我的骨头开始不安分了，才决定再次离开这个国家，去接受其他的护送任务。” 他会想念故乡吗？ “嗯，可以说会，也可以说不会。就像我之前说的，当我在故乡的时候，我的骨头就会感到不安分；而当我在外面执行任务的时候，我又会怀念故乡的温暖和阳光。这其实并不完全是件坏事，它让我不停奔波——我想，这次侦察任务应该是我接到的第一个真正需要我在同一个地方不知待到何时的任务。” “大概就像我年轻的时候吧。在寺庙中长大，我厌恶那里的种种束缚；一旦来到外面世界，我就渴望享受到马拉克殿堂所带来的舒适与安全。而就在我立下誓言、让自己的烙印被刻上去之后，我立刻又想着要离开那里了。”他笑了，说道：“我想，这大概就是我命中注定的命运吧——总是热衷于去追求那些根本不可能实现的东西，就像想要煮沸的冰一样。” |成为马拉克的圣骑士，这会不会让人觉得有些奇怪呢？通常人们听到这个词时，首先想到的往往是卢米亚人或蒂拉人——那些拥有更为悠久尚武传统的种族。当然，还有索兰人，他们虽然不会主动去打打杀杀，但对此也并不反对。 “嗯，这得看是谁在问。”他向你眨了眨眼，“那些无法相信我的武器并不只是用来跳舞的人，只要被长柄刀在脑袋上敲几下，态度就会立刻转变——当然，我并不是个容易发脾气的人。作为马拉克的圣骑士，当然应该懂得什么是克制，但这并不妨碍来一场你情我愿的老式较量。” “除此之外……当最初的冲击过去之后，展现出一些引人注目的特点其实是件好事。当你脱颖而出时，人们会更容易记住那位帮助人们战胜那种令人尴尬的疾病、善良的玛拉基特圣骑士，这样你也更容易建立起自己的声誉。我们是抵御任何可能出现的威胁的第一道防线，尤其是在那些较为偏远的地区。如果人们一开始就愿意信任我们，那么我们的工作也会变得容易许多。” 你完全可以理解他的立场。尤斯拉表现得有点调皮捣蛋，这种顽皮又充满活力的形象确实很容易让人留下深刻印象。无论是态度、外貌还是能力，他样样俱备。 “说真的，你用不着靠奉承我来跟我上床。话虽如此，我并不能说自己不喜欢炫耀自己所拥有的东西。如果能随心所欲地走进人群、成为众人瞩目的焦点……这种感觉确实很让人上瘾，不过你也最好别太习惯。只是想让你知道而已，哈哈！” ]
rows.raw: " [rand |Was he born into the temple the same way that Cait and Salwah were? "I wasn't born into the Temple, but I was raised in it." Yusra sighs and clasps his hands together. "It happens in the poorer parts of the land, especially when there's famine, drought, the likes — sometimes a small village temple will find a box in a courtyard with a kitten or two in it. I happened to have such a beginning." Oh. You're sorry. "Don't be, it's just one of those unfortunate facts of life; people plan expecting times of plenty and then get seven years of lean instead. For centuries, the Temple of Mallach has shouldered the duty of caring for Jassira's orphans and foundlings, in association with the Lumian temple, of course. The latter helps a lot, but the former is where all the wealth and resources lie, so a partnership to care for the unfortunate is necessary. "It was an okay life, I suppose. A small village temple has not even one-twentieth of the wealth and splendour of those in the big cities, but we were fed, watered, sheltered from the worst of the sandstorms and worked to the bone. Not that any of the half-dozen of us complained, because we could clearly see the link between the work we were doing and how it kept us alive. Existence in the inner desert is hard. I have the temple matron to thank, really — I remember there was one time when a visiting spicetender offered to buy me and another kitten, and she refused." The way Yusra says it so matter-of-factly... yes, Jassira is the world's greatest exporter of its own people through such means, but to hear it coming from his mouth... "Kittens taken in by the temple are supposed to be under the holy protection of the Prince of Passions, which is why people have the confidence send foundlings to the temple steps in hard times, knowing they'll be cared for as best as circumstances allow. But corruption is like rats — something to be kept down, but never truly exterminated, and it permeates any and every institution to some degree. I was fortunate." So, he took his vows when he came of age? "Not at first. Like many in my position, I thought temple life too stuffy with its rules and strictures, and ached to be free; I was out the gates the moment I could be. I won't go into details, but the next two years of my life proved well enough that the other end of the oasis was hardly as verdant as I'd imagined it to be. "I've been lucky, but Tira tires of carrying the same person on her back for too long. After some thought, I returned to the temple that had raised me and took my vows. Didn't stay there long, though, wound up being dispatched soon enough... and the rest is, well." He taps his brand of the harlot. "One thing leading to another." |Is there any reason he became a paladin in particular? Or was it even a choice that he could make to begin with? Neither Cait or Sally have gone too deeply into how their vocations were assigned, although it seems that they started years before they took their vows. "No such luck for me, I'm afraid. Partly because I didn't have the good fortune to live in the capital, partly because when I was that age I was determined to leave the temple when I reached my majority." Yusra chuckles sadly. "But yes, when I returned to the temple and took my vows, I was presented with some options. "I could've been a comfort boy, you know; I've certainly got the goods for it. And I won't deny that it was very, very tempting. But as nice as a life of comfort would've been, I know what happens to those who lean just a bit too hard on their looks and wind up with not much left when those start to fade. Let's face it — you only have a handful of years of being a prime fuckboy, and then the wear and tear starts to show, even with all of the Temple's knowledge behind you. The life doesn't leave you with much time to prepare yourself for what comes after, either." So it was that or be a paladin? There were no other choices open to him? "Oh no, there were plenty. But being a paladin... I'd have an excuse to be outside the temple gates when things got too stuffy inside, and still be able to duck back in when it got too hot outside. That, and it appealed to my sense of adventure while I was still a kitten. Being on the front line of holy struggle and taking the most direct action in the name of the Prince of Passion, that kind of thing. It's been fun, and more than one temple matron has appreciated me pitching in with the comfort boy routine while I was billeted with them. Best of both worlds, you know?" |So, prior to all this demon business, what did he do as a Mallachite paladin? The world hasn't completely settled down from the Godswar, but there is this tenuous peace, inasmuch as one can have peace. "Pilgrim escort is one of the biggest ongoing duties of Mallachite paladins in peacetime, and there's never any lack of work in that regard. Mallachites live all over the world, and those who still consider themselves observant make it a point to at least try to make a pilgrimage to a major temple." Given how much more dangerous the world is after the Godswar, an escort makes sense. But you'd imagine that only the wealthy and well-connected would be able to leave their homes for extended periods of time, kind of like Cait and her family, come to think of it. "Oh, yes, it's a custom of old that's had to adapt to darker times. It used to be that everyone would try to make it to a major temple, but that's just not practical — the old roads may still exist, but not all of them are safe and many monsters wear the shapes of people. There's also the fact that common people can't afford to leave their homesteads unattended — it's one of the reasons why your temple is so popular, being an easy outlet for every observant catfolk in the region to fulfill their holy obligations. Bringing the faithful to the Prince of Passions and returning them safely... there aren't that many truly higher callings, I feel." You can guess. There are perks to the job, you take it? "I wouldn't call it a benefit, but any Mallachite temple is obliged to billet me and any pilgrims while they're making the journey, more than just the customary bath and night in the courtyard for anyone. The freedom of being able to travel within and without Jassira, that's another... but most of all, getting to know the rich and powerful from various parts of the world, sometimes carnally! Make a trip with a group in tow, pick up people heading home, pick up another group and so forth... I'd just finished my fourth such round trip and first one beyond Jassira when the call came in to head up here." |Hmm. His gear is quite fancy — it was assigned to him by the temple, wasn't it? "Oh, of course it was; you won't be able to get this sort of thing off the street. It's quite a serious thing to even get too close to a paladin's regalia — impersonation of an authority figure and all that, you see. In some places in the desert, a wandering paladin is about all the law and order you're going to get, and so it's important that people can trust their eyes instead of having to double-guess themselves." Yusra's eyes glint, and the catboy grins. "Why, what's with that look? Perhaps my armor is a little too revealing to be practical?" Well... "Ah, I jest, I jest. But it indeed is very, very eye-catching, and intentionally so. There's a reason why the symbol of my particular order is the desert rose — strength in beauty and all that. Being effective in a fight doesn't mean you can't look good while at it, and doing something in style is really good for morale. That, and being underestimated because your armor 'shows too much skin' helps a whole bunch; you've got to stay in style." |How long has he been out of Jassira, now? "About a year, give or take a month. Last time I stayed was about until the end of the dry season until my bones got restless enough for me to take another escort commission out of the nation." Does he miss the homeland? "Well, yes and no. Like I said, when I'm there, my bones wind up restless; when I'm out on business, I wind up hankering for the warmth and sun back home. It's not really a bad thing, keeps me on the move — I think this scouting assignment is the first real task I've had which has required me to stay in one place for an indefinite amount of time. "It's like when I was young, I suppose. Growing up in the temple, I hated being subjected to its strictures; once let loose out into the world, I wanted the comfort and safety Mallach's halls provided. And no sooner had I taken my vows and had my brand inscribed that I was thinking of heading out again." He laughs. "I guess it's just my lot in life, my passion to desire something as impossible as boiled ice." |Is it awkward, being a paladin of Mallach? Usually when people hear the word the stereotype that comes to mind is Lumian or Tiran, who have more established martial traditions. Then there's, say, Sorrans, who while not actively being all smite-y on the other hand also don't have anything against it. "Well, depends on who's asking." He gives you a wink. "Those who can't quite believe that my weapon isn't just used for dancing change their tune pretty quick after a few smacks upside the head with a glaive — not that I'm in the habit of being short-tempered, of course. A paladin of Mallach has to know what temperance is, but that doesn't preclude a good old consensual bout. "That aside... once the initial shock's done with, it's good to be flashy. When you stick out, people remember the nice Mallachite paladin who helped with an embarrassing disease much easier, and it's easier to build a reputation that way. We're the first line of defence against any threats that might crop up, especially in the more rural regions, and it makes our jobs a lot easier if people are inclined to trust us to begin with." You can see where he's coming from. It doesn't hurt that Yusra presents himself as a bit of a brat — that kind of mischievous, energetic demeanor sticks out and leaves an impression on people. Attitude, looks and ability, he's got it all. "Really, you don't need to flatter me to get in my pants. That being said, I can't say that I don't enjoy flaunting what I have. Being able to walk in and grab the center of attention if you so chose... it's an addictive feeling, and one that you shouldn't get too used to. Just so you know, ha!" ] "

rows.original: [party.has cait |Yusra glances between Cait and you, then turns his palms skyward in a good-natured shrug. "You would have me gossip about the temple matron to her face? Shame, shame." Cait giggles. "Oh, come on. Everyone gossips about temple matrons — it's only to be expected with the title! Surely I'm no exception!" "With all due respect, there's a difference between them and you. My conscience could not bear wagging my tongue about you to your face as opposed to some cranky crone, my dear." "Oh, so it'd be okay if you did it just between [pc.name] and you, without me around?" Nah, you don't think Yusra means that. He's obviously saying that Cait's wonderful presence is so uplifting that people can't help but speak honeyed words in her presence, whether they mean to or not. That can come across as flattering — oh no, it's happening right now! That gets Cait to laughing in earnest, and it goes on for a good half-minute before she gets all wheezy and has to clap the both of you on your shoulders for support before she doubles over from giggling too hard. "All right, you two, I think you've made your point well enough. Let's talk about something else for now, and then once my back is turned you're free to gossip as you please about me. Deal?" |[rand |"I must say, the temple matron herself is possessed of considerable enthusiasm and faith, quite the asset when faced with an endeavor like running a temple in such a remote part of the world. There's more zeal in her than crabby old women thrice her age, which is saying something." He isn't wrong. Cait tries to remain bubbly and friend-shaped to just about everyone she meets, and she isn't above getting her hands dirty when it comes to her particular interpretations of her faith. "Quite so. It's that particular brand of energy that makes her all the more compelling — leading by living the word, as it were, and not shying from any part of it." He smiles. "That energy is infectious, and I find myself being more involved at my duties in her presence. Ah, it's rare that someone like her comes along — she is truly a treasure." He's not too bad himself. "Which isn't wrong... but she's a natural." Yusra chuckles. "It's true that we all receive hospitality training from the temple, my friend, but some take to it more than others. "Still, to return to your question, no, I didn't know the temple matron before arriving any more than a monastic scholar knows a lay priest in the sticks just because they're both Lumians, and I think it's better this way." "It gives me something to do and is a good opportunity to let others know what Mallach really is all about, from the Jassiran point of view." He laughs. "It's not like he's unrecognized in this part of the world or anything — there's even a statue of him in the village below — but different peoples have different perceptions of deities. And speaking of that, the temple matron has a very pure idea of what Mallach, and hence his followers, should be like. It's very endearing." She is indeed quite the idealist, going so far as to give away just about everything in service of her faith, herself included. "We have a word in Jassiran for such people, an approximate translation of which would be 'friend-shaped.' Whatever shape the temple matron takes, it's that of a friend." |"Ah, it must be nice for the temple matron — she is so far removed from the politics that usually accompanies such a station, and is comfortable delegating daily matters to her best friend when out on adventure, for days or even weeks at a time. Back home, such a cavalier attitude would quickly land her in trouble, here, it's a boon that enables her to fully explore all aspects of her passions as our god intends. Isn't it absolutely marvelous?" Well, it's how things are done in the Marches, by all means. Carmen [flags.CARMEN_KILLED |didn't lift a finger during her tenure as baroness |doesn't do anything despite being baroness ], Garth is pretty off-hands as unofficial village alderman, and yet somehow everything still manages to work despite there being the barest of direction in anything. rows.translation: [party.has cait |尤斯拉将目光在凯特和你之间来回扫视，然后友好地耸了耸肩，双手朝天说道：“你们想让我当着她的面去议论寺庙的女主管吗？太不好意思了，真的。” 凯特轻声笑了起来：“哦，别这样嘛。所有人关于寺庙女主持人的闲言碎语——这个身份本来就难免会招来这些议论吧！我当然也不例外！ “尽管我非常尊重你，但她们和你之间还是有区别的。亲爱的，我的良心不允许我在你面前说你的坏话，而不会去对某个脾气暴躁的老妇人说这些。” “哦，所以如果你只是在一些人背后说这些话，那就没问题了[pc.name]那你呢，没有我在身边，你会怎么样？” “不，你不会认为尤斯拉是这个意思的。他显然是在说，凯特的存在实在太令人振奋了，以至于人们在她面前都不由自主地说些甜言蜜语，无论他们是否真的这么想。这听起来可能会让人觉得是在夸赞——哦不，现在这种情况正在发生呢！ 这一下把凯特逗得哈哈大笑，她笑了足足半分钟，直到笑得喘不过气来，还不得不拍拍你们的肩膀让你们帮她支撑一下，否则她就会因为笑得太厉害而弯下腰来。 好吧，你们两个，我觉得你们已经把观点表达得够清楚了。现在我们先聊点别的吧，等我走开后，你们就可以随便议论我了。这样行吗？ |[rand |我必须承认，这位寺庙的女管理者本身就充满了热情与信念，这对于在世界上如此偏远的地区管理一座寺庙来说，确实是一大优势。她的热情甚至超过了那些年龄是她三倍、性格刻薄的老年妇女，这一点确实值得肯定。他并没有错。凯特总是试图对遇到的每一个人都保持开朗友好的态度，而在她对自己信仰的理解上，她也不介意采取一些强硬的手段。 确实如此。正是那种独特的能量让她显得更加吸引人——她用自己的行动践行着自己的信念，从不回避其中的任何一部分。”他微笑着说，“这种能量具有感染力，在她面前，我会不由自主地更加认真地履行自己的职责。啊，像她这样的人实在难得——她真的是个珍宝。” “他自己也还不错。” “这倒也没错……但她就是有天赋。”尤斯拉轻笑道，“没错，我们所有人都在寺庙里接受过待客礼仪的训练，我的朋友，但有些人就是比其他人更擅长这些。总是对他人保持热情与开朗的态度，往往会让自己付出代价……但对他人而言，这种态度却能给他们带来力量。这位寺庙的女管理者，正是那些受到“情感之君”恩赐的人之一。 |你感到好奇…… “是的，我的朋友。” 他在来这里之前就认识凯特吗？ “啊哈，并不是这样的。其实我来自贾西拉的一个比较偏远的地区——”他轻咳了一声——“就在阿努比人那些水晶屋顶的洞穴里种植香料的地方。在那里，根本没人知道苏丹娜的名字，更不用说她家族中那些鲜为人知的分支了。当然，每个人都知道那位当地香料商的详细情况。 rows.original: [rand |"Ah, her. The girl may be grand cleric of this temple in name, but if her job title were to follow what she actually does, bursar or treasurer would be more appropriate." [pc.bg scholar |Ohh, just the word %"bursar" sends shivers down your spine, a remnant of your academic life that will never leave you for all eternity. You don't think she's that terrifying, though, is she? |Well, that's not an incorrect assessment, but he says it like it's some kind of mark against her. ] "Oh, don't get me wrong. Everything needs money to run, and so every temple needs to have someone like her. The matron is prone to giving things away in the name of the faith, which while commendable also means that if carried out to extremes, there won't be anything left to give in short order. Hence, the need for a bean-counter. The girl's pleasant enough most of the time, but to see her go through a ledger sends shivers down one's spine." |You've been meaning to ask... is the full-body style of doing tattoos popular in Jassira? While the head-to-toe adornment of leaves and branches on Sally's skin is certainly aesthetic, it can't have been easy on her. "It does depend on where in Jassira you speak of, and it's not necessarily a rural and urban divide. Having tattoos means you're showing off bare skin, and you have to stay indoors most of the day in order to be flaunting that much of yourself, lest the sun do a number on your careful art." Yusra chuckles and shakes his head. "The rich, mostly, and those who can afford to try and mimic them." Oh. Well... Sally is from the main temple in the capital, same as Cait. You don't get much more indoors and well-to-do than that. "It's not anything hard and fast, just my own observations. Tattoos like the grand cleric's is hardly something that's done in one sitting or even three, and the amount of willpower it must've taken is rare in your average pampered brat. Still! I'm sure my thoughts will change should I ever encounter sufficient evidence to the contrary, ha!" |"The grand cleric has been kind to me during my stay here so far. Brusque and brief, but kind nevertheless. I am here to help everyone out, after all, and not just a squad of passing holy warriors demanding room and board as is our right. The little kindnesses do not go unnoticed... which is more than I'd expect from a bean-counter like her. I really do think she's warmed up to me somewhat." Sally? Cold? Well... you remember meeting her when she first arrived in Hawkethorne, and she felt a lot friendlier then. Taking care of the temple, especially in Cait's absence, and the whole renting out her womb as a surrogate thing has hardened her a bit in a comparatively short time. Yusra grins. "Girl's not that way naturally, but collecting debts hardens the heart, as they say. You don't suppose she could be a little more seductive when convincing petitioners to pay up after getting dead drunk on temple grounds, could she?" Well, they do say that honey is good for attracting flies. "But vinegar is even better than honey in that regard." A snicker. "Oh, yes, I do get what you're saying, and I've seen her work up the reluctant in the Mallachite way. But sometimes people do get recalcitrant, and Imad's not always around. Necessity and duty change people, my friend, and not always for the better. For a definition of 'better', at any rate. "A young woman being thrust into a role for which she was hardly trained... she told me that she followed the matron up here expecting to do missionary work, and in a sense she found it, didn't she? Only it was bigger and grander in scope than the little two-room affair that most such efforts wind up being. All things considered, she's actually adapted pretty well to the sudden twist her life's taken — reminds me a little of myself, really." |"She does her job well," Yusra says after a moment's thought. "Donations and payments for services go in, maintenance is performed, and there's excess to accommodate unforeseen circumstances like me showing up out of the blue. It's actually quite impressive, given that the traditional source of income — pious catfolk immigrants — are in short supply up here at the roof of the world!" Well, it also helps that Garth knows people and hence was able to arrange for everything from building to upkeep at a fraction of the cost. "Not to discount the effort of the locals in supporting the temple, of course," Yusra adds hurriedly. "Which should show just how much she and the temple matron have been able to sell the idea by setting a good example. Many of the laity outside of Jassira have the mistaken idea that Mallachite temples are merely glorified whorehouses — we're other things in addition to being that." Mmm... the temple's main attraction does continue to be sexual, from where you're standing. "And drugs. And music. And beauty. But arguably, it all comes down to sex for a certain kind of mentality." A laugh. "Well, I suppose you don't get to see very much of it otherwise[silly | — this is a porn game, after all ]. As easy as it'd be to coast upon the sex part for as long as possible, perhaps I should speak to the grand cleric about emphasizing other aspects of our god's domain. Wouldn't that be nice." |"It's a wonderful brand of practicality the grand cleric exhibits, isn't it? Perfectly balancing out the temple matron's idealism to create a functional yet inspiring temple. Would more temples back home in Jassira be this way." Salwah didn't always use to be like this, at least not from what you saw of her while she was still living in the Frost Hound, and from Cait's stories of their childhood. Running the temple, especially while Cait's gone, has doubtlessly hardened her. "Ah, a sacrifice so that the matron can keep her innocence. What nobler gesture of friendship can there be?" Yusra turns up his palms and raises his eyes skyward. "Such a noble gesture capable of making even the Prince of Passions himself weep. Girl's quite chatty when we get to doing our morning gymnastics together — oh yes, we've taken to that when time allows. Having a partner allows for forms that wouldn't be possible alone... and it's all the better for keeping two people limber instead of one, wouldn't you say?" ]
rows.translation: [rand |啊，那个女孩。虽然名义上她是这座寺庙的大祭司，但如果根据她的实际工作内容来给她定职位的话，‘司库’或者‘财务主管’才更合适吧。 [pc.bg scholar |哦，只要听到“财务主管”这个词，就会让你不寒而栗——这可是你学生时代留下的痕迹，永远也不会从你的记忆中消失。你不会认为她那个不过，她真的那么可怕吗？ |嗯，这种评价倒也不算错误，但他说这话的时候，给人的感觉却像是这是在指责她什么似的。 ] 哦，别误会我的意思。一切运作都需要资金，所以每座寺庙都需要像她这样的人。那位女管理者总是以信仰的名义赠送各种物品，这种行为虽然值得称赞，但如果走极端的话，很快就会没有什么东西可以赠送了。因此，才需要有人来负责管理财务。这个女孩大多数时候都挺不错的，但看到她认真地核对账目，还是会让人不寒而栗。 |你一直想问……在贾西拉，全身都纹身这种风格真的流行吗？虽然莎莉身上从头部到脚部都纹满了树叶和树枝的图案，看起来确实很美观，但这样的纹身对她来说肯定不会太容易忍受吧。 这确实取决于你是在贾西拉的哪个地区谈论这个问题，而且这种区分并不一定是城乡之间的差异。纹身意味着你要暴露自己的皮肤，而在大多数时间里，你都不得不待在室内，这样才能展示自己的纹身，否则阳光会破坏你精心制作的纹身图案。尤斯拉轻笑了一声，然后摇了摇头，说道：‘主要是那些富人，以及那些有能力模仿他们行为的人。’” 哦……好吧……莎莉是就像凯特说的那样，从首都的主神庙开始，再没有比这更豪华、更舒适的室内环境了。 “这并不是什么绝对的结论，只是我的个人观察而已。像那位大祭司那样的纹身，绝对不可能一次就完成，甚至三次也做不到。要承受这样的痛苦和意志力的考验，对于那些被宠坏的年轻人来说，实在是太难了。不过！如果我以后遇到了相反的证据，我的看法肯定也会改变的，哈哈！ |在我在这里的这段时间里，这位高级牧师对待我一直很友善。虽然她说话直率简短，但本质上还是挺善良的。毕竟，我是来帮助大家的，而不仅仅是一群路过此地的神圣战士，他们只是理所当然地要求得到食宿而已。这些小小的善意并没有被我忽视……对于她这样一个精于计算的人来说，我已经觉得她对我有所改观了。 莎莉？变冷了？嗯……你应该还记得她刚来到鹰棘镇的时候，那时她显得要友善得多。由于要负责管理寺庙的事务，尤其是在凯特不在的情况下，再加上还要承担代孕的任务，她在相对较短的时间内变得坚强了许多。 尤斯拉笑了起来：“女孩子本来不是这样的，但俗话说，欠债会让人心肠变硬。你不会觉得，在神庙里喝得酩酊大醉之后，她应该能用更迷人的方式去说服那些欠债的人还钱吧？” 嗯，毕竟也有句话说，蜂蜜确实能吸引苍蝇啊。 但在这方面，醋甚至比蜂蜜更有效。”有人轻声嘲笑道，“哦，我明白你的意思，我也见过她用那种固执的方式让那些顽固的人屈服。但有时候人们就是会变得倔强起来，而伊马德也不总是在身边。朋友，需要和责任会改变一个人，只不过这种改变并不总是往好的方向发展。至少，对于‘变好’这个定义来说是这样吧。 一位年轻女性被强行推到了一个她几乎没有任何准备的角色中……她告诉我，她本来是跟着那位负责人来到这里的，以为自己会从事一些慈善工作，从某种意义上说，她确实做到了，不是吗？只不过，这次她所从事的工作规模要比大多数类似的工作都要大得多、重要得多。综合考虑来看，她其实已经很好地适应了自己生活发生的这种突然变化——这让我有点想起自己呢。 |她把工作做得很好，”尤斯拉思考片刻后说道，“捐款和服务费用都收进去了，维护工作也得到了妥善处理，而且还有剩余的资金可以用来应对一些意外情况，比如像我这种突然出现的人。事实上，这真的相当了不起——因为在这里，这个世界的顶端，传统的收入来源——那些虔诚的猫族移民——已经变得十分稀少了！ 当然，加斯人脉广泛，这也帮助他以极低的成本安排好了从建筑到维护的所有事宜。 当然，我们也不能忽视当地人为支持这座寺庙所付出的努力，”尤斯拉急忙补充道，“正是他们的行动，以及她和寺庙管理者们以身作则，才让这个理念得到了广泛的传播。在贾西拉以外的许多地方，人们都误以为马拉克信徒寺庙只不过是披着神圣外衣的妓院罢了——事实上，我们还有许多其他的意义加法事实上，确实如此。” 嗯……从你现在的位置来看，这座寺庙的主要吸引力确实与性有关。 “还有毒品、音乐和美貌。但可以说，对于某种特定的心态而言，这一切最终都归结为性。”他笑了笑，“嗯，我想否则你也看不到太多与性相关的东西吧。[silly | — 毕竟，这是一款色情游戏啊。 ]虽然靠性这方面来维持现状也挺容易的，但或许我应该和那位大祭司谈谈，让他强调我们神明信仰中其他方面的内容。那样不是更好吗？ |这位大祭司所展现出的这种务实精神实在令人赞叹，不是吗？他巧妙地平衡了寺庙女主管的理想主义，从而打造出了既实用又富有启发性的宗教场所。如果贾西拉国内的更多寺庙都能如此运作该多好啊。萨尔瓦以前并不总是这样的，至少从你在她还住在寒霜猎犬镇时所看到的情况，以及从凯特讲述的他们童年时期的故事来看，她是这样的。如今负责管理这座寺庙，尤其是在凯特不在的情况下，这些责任无疑让她变得更加坚强了。 啊，这样的牺牲，只是为了让那位女主人能够保持她的清白。还有比这更高尚的友谊之举吗？”尤斯拉摊开双手，仰望天空，“这样的高尚行为，甚至能让‘激情王子’本人也为之动容落泪。但他们确实组成了一支非常出色的团队——他们的性格中那种双重性以及为了适应新角色而发生的深刻变化，确实引起了我的注意。这一点非常引人深思。 “不过，生活的严酷现实以及突然肩负起管理寺庙的重任，也并没有打击到这位高阶牧师的精神或什么。当我们一起做晨间体操时，这个女孩会变得特别爱说话——没错，只要时间允许，我们就会一起做这个运动。有一个人陪着做，就可以完成一些单独做的话根本做不了的动作……而且，两个人一起做体操，肯定比一个人做效果更好，你说呢？" ]

rows.original: [rand |"Oh, the greeter? She's just about perfect for the job. Easy on the eyes, comfortable with wearing so little even in this chill, effortlessly happy, and cheerful to everyone she meets. Also completely vapid and empty-headed, but that's a positive in this line of work." Yusra chuckles and scratches his ears before bursting out into a genuine belly laugh. "I've known girls who started off as temple greeters fresh after their induction when they came of age and stayed that way for the next forty years or so. So long as your smile is genuine, people will be drawn to it. There's something about that good-natured innocence that... well, I shouldn't dwell too much on it. "It's absolutely hilarious how she charges people for holding hands, though. I get a laugh out of that every time she manages to pull it off." There are people who do nothing but serve as door greeters for the entirety of their lives? "If there's one thing the Temple's good at, it's matching people to their temperaments and capabilities. It takes all kinds to make a world, and there are more people who aren't really good for much more than work others would find demeaning than you'd imagine. In its benevolence, the Temple matches people to roles which they aren't just suited for, but find fulfilling and meaningful — which is how people like Rune wind up being temple greeters for the rest of their lives. Certainly nothing wrong with that, and while it's less glamorous than being a paladin it's also no less important for what we do." |"That outfit of Rune's isn't traditional Jassiran, I'd know. Wonder who she got to design it, because it's rather unique — haven't seen something quite like it anywhere. Maybe that's why she wears it, to lure in people with a taste of novelty. What do you think?" You think that Yusra's probably overthinking it. He laughs. "True, I guess. It's conceivable that she could've come up with it herself... she's just that air-headed that I could believe it. An idiot savant, possibly?" Well, if you might be blunt, given his own paladin gear you don't really see what's the big difference between the novelty in Yusra's and Rune's getups. They're just different flavors of exotic to you. "Ah, but one is accepted exotic by a lot of people, and the other is simply exotic to one air-brained kitten. But as I said, that's not necessarily a bad thing. Novelty, right? Her being the first thing that people see when they drop by the entrance is absolutely great — speaks to the familiar while still being exotic enough." |"I was speaking with Rune the other day, and just a few words exchanged had me laughing and for just a moment, forgetting my worries," Yusra says. "I was wondering how she did it, but then realized that she herself didn't know — it was like asking a bird how it flies, or a fish how it swims. With a demeanor like that, I can almost — almost — believe that she's as extensively traveled as she claims to be despite being so airheaded." Really? Yusra smiles and puts his hands together. "I wouldn't believe it if I hadn't encountered such people for myself. You're not from around these parts either, [pc.name] — you should be well aware of the rigors of travel, even in relatively safe lands. But there are those who exhibit such obliviousness and cheerfulness, yet come away unscathed from it all, to the point where I can only conclude that the gods are watching over these people somehow and arrange matters so that no harm comes to them. It can't be sheer luck — mere fortune would eventually flip the other way with how often such people test it." He has actual evidence of this? "No, but I don't see any other reasonable explanation. People like Rune just happen to live a blessed life, and while I know it's sinful that fragment of envy is still there whether I like it or not." He sighs. "Sometimes I wonder if such people exist to remind us what we could be life if we didn't stray further from the gods every day." |"When I first heard of Rune's hand-holding thing, I couldn't quite believe that she was serious. People in this part of the world are so starved for simple passionate contact like that? It got better when I figured what she was really up to... but it's still handholding and not that risque to begin with. And here I thought she was up to something truly scandalous. "It's quite sad, really. That there're people who actually pay the money just to be able to hold hands with a temple greeter for a while... but more often than not, it's about the passions, the emotions, rather than the sex, isn't it? Yes, you could go into the temple proper, pay a little more to be attended to... but it just isn't the same as holding hands with a ditzy bimbo who by all appearances is truly glad to see you and interested in whatever little inanities one's prone to spouting." |"Ah, Rune. That kind of bubbly happiness, that overflowing passion... that good-naturedness is worth protecting and cherishing. Girl really does remind me of one of the reasons I became a paladin... you want to keep those bright-eyed, bouncy kittens that way for as long as possible before the wear of the world finally gets to them. There are those who would take pleasure in specifically despoiling beautiful flowers... most frustrating. But Rune is too silly to notice, which is why others like Salwah must watch out for her." ]
rows.translation: [rand |哦，那个接待员？她简直太适合这份工作了。她长得漂亮，即使在这种寒冷的环境里也几乎不怎么穿衣服，却依然显得很舒适；她总是面带笑容，见到每个人都会显得很高兴、很开朗。当然，她也很空洞、没什么头脑，但在这种工作中，这反而是件好事啊。尤斯拉轻声笑了起来，挠了挠他的耳朵，然后突然放声大笑起来。‘我认识一些女孩，她们在成年后刚被录用，就开始担任寺庙的迎宾工作，之后四十多年里一直保持着这个职位。只要你的笑容是发自内心的，人们就会被它吸引。那种天真的、善良的态度……嗯，我不太应该过多地去思考这些。 不过，她居然因为别人牵手而向他们收费，这真的太搞笑了。每次她成功做到这一点的时候，我都会被逗得哈哈大笑。” 难道真的有人一生中只是扮演着迎宾员的角色吗？ 如果说神殿有什么擅长的事情，那就是根据人们的性格和能力来为他们安排合适的岗位。创造一个丰富多彩的世界需要各种各样的人，而那些其实并不擅长做什么特别事情的人，也比你想象中要多得多。对于他们来说，做一些别人认为低贱的工作，反而可能是最适合他们的选择。出于善意，这座神庙会为人们安排那些不仅适合他们，而且能让他们感到有成就感、有意义的工作——正因如此，像露恩这样的人才会选择终生担任神庙的接待员。这当然没有任何不妥，虽然这份工作没有成为一名圣骑士那么光鲜亮丽，但对我们来说，它的意义同样重要。" |露恩那身装束显然不是传统的贾西兰风格，我一眼就能看出来。不知道是谁为她设计的，因为这套服装确实非常独特，我在其他地方从未见过类似的款式。也许她之所以穿这身衣服，就是为了吸引那些喜欢新奇事物的人吧。你怎么看？” 你认为尤斯拉可能是想得太多了。 他笑了：“嗯，大概吧。确实有可能是她自己想出来的这个主意……她就是有点犯傻，所以我才会相信这种可能性。也许是个天才傻瓜吧？” 嗯，说实话，考虑到他本人也穿着那些骑士装束，你其实很难看出尤斯拉和露恩的装扮有什么本质区别。对你来说，它们只不过是不同风格的异国风服饰罢了。 啊，但其中有一个是被接受了对很多人来说，这种设计确实显得很新颖、很奇特；而对某个天马行空的家伙来说，它也只是显得有点与众不同罢了。但正如我所说，这并不一定是坏事。新颖性，就是它的魅力所在吧？当人们走进入口时，首先看到的就是这个设计，这简直太棒了——它在让人感到熟悉的同时，依然保持着足够的独特性。 |前几天我和露恩聊天，仅仅寥寥几句话就让我开怀大笑，有那么一刻，我完全忘记了所有的烦恼，”尤斯拉说道。“我一直在想她是怎么做到的，但后来才意识到，她自己其实也不明白——这就好比问一只鸟它是如何飞行的，或者问一条鱼它是如何游泳的。拥有这样的气质，我真的觉得几乎真觉得她像自己说的那样游历过那么多地方吗？尽管她看起来那么糊涂。” “真的吗？” 尤斯拉笑了笑，然后双手合十说道：“要不是我自己也遇到过这样的人，我也不会相信的。你也不是这个地方的人吧？[pc.name] — 你应该很清楚旅行的艰辛，即使是在相对安全的地区也是如此。但总有一些人表现得如此毫不在意、如此开心愉快，最终却能毫发无损地度过一切，以至于我只能认为，一定是神明在以某种方式守护着这些人，安排了一切，让他们不会受到任何伤害。这绝不可能是纯粹的运气——毕竟，这种事情反复发生，单纯的运气最终总会用尽的。” “他真的有证据支持这一观点吗？” “没有，但我想不出其他合理的解释。像露恩这样的人，似乎天生就拥有幸福的人生。虽然我知道，无论我是否愿意，那种嫉妒的情绪依然存在，但这确实是一种罪过。”他叹了口气，“有时候我会想，是不是正是因为有这样的人存在，才让我们意识到，如果不再每天远离神明，我们的生活本可以是什么样子。" |当我第一次听说露恩会主动牵手别人时，我真的不敢相信她是认真的。在这个地方，人们竟然如此渴望这种简单而充满情感的肢体接触吗？后来当我明白了她的意图之后，我就觉得这一切都变得可以理解了。真的真的挺可悲的。居然有人愿意花钱，就只是为了能和寺庙里的迎宾员握握手、待上一会儿而已。…但事实上，更多时候，这些行为背后的动力其实是激情与情感，而非性本身，对吧？没错，你可以走进真正的寺庙，多花一些钱来享受更好的服务……但那与和一个看起来真的很高兴见到你、并且愿意倾听你那些琐碎无聊的话的傻姑娘手拉手，体验的感觉毕竟是不一样的。" |啊，露恩。那种充满活力的快乐，那种溢于言表的热情……还有那种天性中的善良，确实值得我们去保护、去珍惜。这个女孩真的让我想起了自己当初选择成为圣骑士的原因之一……你肯定也想让那些天真无邪、充满活力的孩子们永远保持这样的状态，直到这个世界的种种磨难最终影响到他们。确实有些人专门喜欢破坏那些美丽的花朵……真是让人恼火。不过露恩太天真了，根本注意不到这些，因此像萨尔瓦这样的人就必须时刻照顾着她。 ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"Oh, the greeter? She's just about perfect for the job. Easy on the eyes, comfortable with wearing so little even in this chill, effortlessly happy, and cheerful to everyone she meets. Also completely vapid and empty-headed, but that's a positive in this line of work." Yusra chuckles and scratches his ears before bursting out into a genuine belly laugh. "I've known girls who started off as temple greeters fresh after their induction when they came of age and stayed that way for the next forty years or so. So long as your smile is genuine, people will be drawn to it. There's something about that good-natured innocence that... well, I shouldn't dwell too much on it. "It's absolutely hilarious how she charges people for holding hands, though. I get a laugh out of that every time she manages to pull it off." There are people who do nothing but serve as door greeters for the entirety of their lives? "If there's one thing the Temple's good at, it's matching people to their temperaments and capabilities. It takes all kinds to make a world, and there are more people who aren't really good for much more than work others would find demeaning than you'd imagine. In its benevolence, the Temple matches people to roles which they aren't just suited for, but find fulfilling and meaningful — which is how people like Rune wind up being temple greeters for the rest of their lives. Certainly nothing wrong with that, and while it's less glamorous than being a paladin it's also no less important for what we do." |"That outfit of Rune's isn't traditional Jassiran, I'd know. Wonder who she got to design it, because it's rather unique — haven't seen something quite like it anywhere. Maybe that's why she wears it, to lure in people with a taste of novelty. What do you think?" You think that Yusra's probably overthinking it. He laughs. "True, I guess. It's conceivable that she could've come up with it herself... she's just that air-headed that I could believe it. An idiot savant, possibly?" Well, if you might be blunt, given his own paladin gear you don't really see what's the big difference between the novelty in Yusra's and Rune's getups. They're just different flavors of exotic to you. "Ah, but one is accepted exotic by a lot of people, and the other is simply exotic to one air-brained kitten. But as I said, that's not necessarily a bad thing. Novelty, right? Her being the first thing that people see when they drop by the entrance is absolutely great — speaks to the familiar while still being exotic enough." |"I was speaking with Rune the other day, and just a few words exchanged had me laughing and for just a moment, forgetting my worries," Yusra says. "I was wondering how she did it, but then realized that she herself didn't know — it was like asking a bird how it flies, or a fish how it swims. With a demeanor like that, I can almost — almost — believe that she's as extensively traveled as she claims to be despite being so airheaded." Really? Yusra smiles and puts his hands together. "I wouldn't believe it if I hadn't encountered such people for myself. You're not from around these parts either, [pc.name] — you should be well aware of the rigors of travel, even in relatively safe lands. But there are those who exhibit such obliviousness and cheerfulness, yet come away unscathed from it all, to the point where I can only conclude that the gods are watching over these people somehow and arrange matters so that no harm comes to them. It can't be sheer luck — mere fortune would eventually flip the other way with how often such people test it." He has actual evidence of this? "No, but I don't see any other reasonable explanation. People like Rune just happen to live a blessed life, and while I know it's sinful that fragment of envy is still there whether I like it or not." He sighs. "Sometimes I wonder if such people exist to remind us what we could be life if we didn't stray further from the gods every day." |"When I first heard of Rune's hand-holding thing, I couldn't quite believe that she was serious. People in this part of the world are so starved for simple passionate contact like that? It got better when I figured what she was really up to... but it's still handholding and not that risque to begin with. And here I thought she was up to something truly scandalous. "It's quite sad, really. That there're people who actually pay the money just to be able to hold hands with a temple greeter for a while... but more often than not, it's about the passions, the emotions, rather than the sex, isn't it? Yes, you could go into the temple proper, pay a little more to be attended to... but it just isn't the same as holding hands with a ditzy bimbo who by all appearances is truly glad to see you and interested in whatever little inanities one's prone to spouting." |"Ah, Rune. That kind of bubbly happiness, that overflowing passion... that good-naturedness is worth protecting and cherishing. Girl really does remind me of one of the reasons I became a paladin... you want to keep those bright-eyed, bouncy kittens that way for as long as possible before the wear of the world finally gets to them. There are those who would take pleasure in specifically despoiling beautiful flowers... most frustrating. But Rune is too silly to notice, which is why others like Salwah must watch out for her." ] "

rows.translation: 露恩

rows.original: [rand |"Ah, the temple's primary claim to not being just a whorehouse," Yusra says with a twinkle in his eye. "Ah, I kid, I kid. Even if she won't put herself out to be picked up, the girl's music is often the backdrop to which the sacred harlots work." It's... well... everyone works together to keep things running, you suppose. And her music? "Her music has the mark of the coast, from what I've heard of it. That region of Jassira which actually receives regular rain blown inland from the sea... a place where people don't have to worry that much about water. You can tell by how lively and energetic it is, how much influence there's been on that musical tradition from all kinds of peoples carried from all over the sea. Truly a breath of fresh air over the slow, meandering tunes of the more inland provinces, ha! "But yes! She's a reminder that temples aren't supposed to be all about sex, as easy as it might be to lean into that aspect of Mallach's passions for a new temple like this one is. Sex is an easy draw and money maker, but the temple matron and grand cleric at least remember their lessons well enough to at least try and attend to the other means of expressing one's passions. Painting and sculpture might be lost on the locals here, but I think anyone can appreciate a good tune." |"Yes, that's correct — if those two are indeed from the coastal regions of Jassira, then I can understand the desire to come all the way up here to the roof of the world, especially if Amina knew the temple matron. That part of our glorious nation is rather cutthroat, a side effect of the local mercantile culture, and that extends to the local Temple as well. Rising through the ranks on one's merit can be hard when vacancies are hard to come by and successors to any important jobs are often hand-picked and trained years or even decades before they'll hold the position...I can see the impetus to leave for proverbial greener pastures. "Sometimes it's not so bad to be a big fish in a small pond. It all depends on what kind of opportunities are around you — and for someone as talented and slightly unorthodox as Amina is in music, coming all the way here where her playing's more likely to be applauded as exotic and mystical rather than being booed for not being perfectly in line with the audience's tastes is certainly the right choice. Here, dear Amina can be who she wants to be and get applauded for it. Quite the no-brainer to make the trip, wouldn't you say?" |Most people think that Jassirites are all about catfolk, so to see Imad and Amina as Jassirite Mallachites is a little surprising. "That's a common misconception, really. Yes, the majority of Jassirites are indeed catfolk, but that's mostly because Jassira is the home of catfolk. Even so, that doesn't forbid other peoples from serving the Prince of Passion in that nation. If anything, Imad and Amina are simply amongst an outsized proportion of anubians in the Temple compared to how many there are amongst the population." Interesting. Is there a reason for this? "It's unfortunate — the antics of the spicetenders and by extent, the moneylenders and slave traders who are downstream from them are what give the anubians a bad name, but all of that people shoulder the burden while the true villains are much less reviled than they ought to be. It's a sticky situation and one that's persisted for a long, long time, partly because of the simple necessity of spice to the way of life over there, partly because of corruption, and partly because of the spicetenders' immense wealth. And all of those bring the matter to such a strong simmer that there are those anubians in the temple who seek some kind of respectability by serving the Prince of Passion and setting themselves apart from their more unscrupulous kin." [pc.isDK |Or at least, that's what they say. Yusra sighs and rubs his temples, but doesn't contradict you. "Cheerful [pc.mf |fellow |girl ], aren't you? That is... corruption exists everywhere, and while it can't be eradicated we do our best to keep it down. There are already enough jokes about the Temple and sultanate being literally incestuous; there're too many tongues wagging about the same thing happening with the Temple and the spicetenders." Hey, you didn't mention anything about anubians being plants in the temple — he just spilled that out of his own accord. "And most of them aren't," Yusra snaps, his cheerful demeanor gone. "There's no need to be contrary for the sake of it." Fine, if he would continue? |Does it work? "Somewhat. The primacy that Mallach holds over Jassira aside, even if they were servants of the other Seven, it's still seen as a noble calling. The two just about cancel each other out, I'd say. They may think differently, though." Anything else? ] "There's not much left to say. I expect it's just one of many reasons why brother and sister would leave Jassira to be with the temple matron; the roof of the world is about as different a place from Jassira as one can reasonably get. Both brother and sister want to be judged on their own merits, albeit in different ways... I can understand and approve of this desire." |"I rather enjoy Amina's playing. It uses traditional Jassiran music as a base, but has various other styles blended in, no doubt from what she's picked up by the port. The end result is familiar yet unique, delightful in its own way. I'm hoping it catches on more than it already us, truth be told." |Is it common for those who're part of a Jassirite-style temple to not be up for, uh, service, as Amina is? "Quite common, actually. Sacred harlots are, at a bare minimum, trained in the ways of pleasure; there's a reputation to uphold. Then, they may have a specialisation they dabble in, as evidenced by the shape and color of their brand... just wandering into a temple and asking for the nearest temple denizen to be a warm hole or prick is something rude people from Tronarii do." He makes it sound like instead of most temple staff being up for hire, the opposite is true. "That's right. An established temple like the one the matron here is from has musicians, artists, cleaners, retired harlots who cook and care for the guests and kittens, clerics who attend to the sick, and more. Sacred harlots would actually be a fairly small proportion of those in the temple. "Now... there's nothing stopping, say, a traveling paladin like me from offering myself, let alone some of the temple staff who might be willing to do something on the side for favors, gifts and the like. But such are usually special arrangements, discreetly inquired about through the matron or grand cleric, and the one being asked is perfectly within his or her right to refuse. That way special care and attention can be given to the matter, especially since it's not one's usual vocation." Well, Cait's temple is the only one you've ever been to in the Jassirite tradition, so things are unfortunately a little skewed. Yusra nods and flashes you a smile. "People around the world worship the Prince of Passion in their own way, of course. But yes... this temple doesn't have that many people around, and the easiest way to get petitioners interested is with the sex. It's just what it is — I fully expect that the focus will gradually shift as more join and the matron and grand cleric are better able to fill out these halls. I suppose that one might complain that it takes appealing to the base passions to drum up interest in the finer arts, but things are what they are. From that perspective, a temple having but a single Mallachite who doesn't put out on request like Amina does is actually the oddity here." ]
rows.translation: [rand |“啊，这座神殿最大的招牌，就是它不只是个妓院，”尤斯拉说着，眼里闪着光。“啊，我开玩笑的，开玩笑的。就算她不愿主动招揽客人，那女孩的音乐往往也是那些神圣妓女干活时的背景音乐。” 这个嘛——怎么说呢——你猜想，这里大概是大家齐心协力，才让一切运转起来的吧。那她的音乐呢？ “据我所知，她的音乐带着海岸的印记。贾西拉那片地区确实能经常得到从海上吹向内陆的雨水……是个人们不必太担心水的地方。从它多么活泼、多么有活力，从各路渡海而来的人们对那种音乐传统产生过多大影响，你就能听出来。比起内陆省份那些缓慢、迂回的小调，这真是一股清新的空气，哈！” “不过，没错！她提醒了我们：神殿本不该只围着性打转——尽管对于这样一座新神殿来说，很容易就会一头扎进马拉克那股激情的这一面。性爱是很容易招徕人、也很赚钱的手段，但至少这位神殿的女主事和那位大祭司还记得自己学过的功课，至少试着去顾及其他表达激情的方式。绘画和雕塑这里的本地人也许欣赏不来，但我认为任何人都能欣赏一段好曲子。” |“是的，没错——如果那两位确实来自贾西拉的沿海地区，那我就能理解他们为什么愿意一路来到这个世界的屋脊，尤其是阿米娜还认识那位神殿的女主事。我们这辉煌国度的那个地区相当残酷，这是当地商业文化带来的副作用，而这也延伸到了当地的神殿。当空缺难得一见、要职的继任者往往在接任前好几年甚至几十年就被挑中培养时，单靠本事往上爬是很难的……我完全能理解他们想去找传说中更肥美的草场的冲动。” “有时候，在小池塘里当条大鱼也不算太坏。这全看你身边有什么样的机会——而对像阿米娜这样在音乐上既有才华又略显离经叛道的人来说，一路来到这里，让她的演奏更可能被赞为异域而神秘，而不是因为不完全合观众口味就被喝倒彩，无疑是正确的选择。在这里，亲爱的阿米娜可以成为她想成为的人，并因此赢得喝彩。跑这一趟根本不用多想，你说是不是？” |大多数人以为贾西拉人特人尽是猫族，所以看到伊马德和阿米娜是贾西拉人特的马拉克信徒，会有点意外。 “这其实是常见的误解。没错，贾西拉人特人多数确实是猫族，但这主要是因为贾西拉是猫族的家园。即便如此，那也不妨碍其他族人在那个国家侍奉激情王子。真要说的话，伊马德和阿米娜只是碰巧赶上了神殿里阿努比亚人比例远高于其在总人口中占比的情况。” 有意思。这其中有什么原因吗？ “说来不幸——正是那些香料商，以及依附于他们的放债人和奴隶贩子，让阿努比亚人背上了恶名，但这一切却要由整个族群来背负，而真正的恶人受到的唾骂远少于他们应得的。这是个棘手局面，而且已经持续了很久很久，部分是因为香料在当地生活方式中不可或缺，部分是因为腐化，还有部分是因为香料商的巨额财富。这一切把这潭水熬得滚烫，于是神殿里有些阿努比亚人便通过侍奉激情王子来寻求某种体面，好把自己和那些不那么讲道义的亲族区分开来。” [pc.isDK |或者至少，他们是这么说的。 尤斯拉叹了口气，揉了揉太阳穴，但没有反驳你。“挺高兴的嘛，[pc.mf |伙计 |姑娘 ]，不是吗？这个嘛……腐化无处不在，既然无法根除，我们就尽力把它压下去。关于神殿与苏丹宫廷简直亲如一家的笑话已经够多了；如今又有太多人在嚼舌根，说神殿和那些香料商之间也在发生同样的事。” 嘿，你之前可没提过阿努比亚人在神殿里是内线——是他自己主动说出来的。 “而他们大多并不是，”尤斯拉厉声说道，愉快的模样一扫而空。“没必要为了唱反调而唱反调。” 好吧，那他愿不愿意接着说？ |有用吗？ “多少有点用。撇开马拉克对贾西拉拥有的那种至高地位不谈，即便他们是其他七位神的仆从，那也仍被视为一种高尚的使命。要我说，这两者差不多正好相互抵消。不过，他们也许不这么想。” 还有别的吗？ ] “没什么好说的了。我想，这不过是兄妹俩离开贾西拉、去投奔那位神殿女主事的众多原因之一；这个世界的屋脊和贾西拉，可以说是天差地别了。兄妹俩都希望凭自己的本事受到评判，只是方式不同……我理解并且赞同这种愿望。” |“我倒是挺喜欢阿米娜的演奏。它以传统的贾西拉音乐为基础，又混入了各种别的风格，无疑都是她在港口学来的。最后出来的效果既熟悉又独特，自有其动人之处。说实话，我希望它能比现在更受欢迎。” |在贾西里特风格的神殿里，像阿米娜这样不参与，呃，服务的人，常见吗？ “其实相当常见。神圣妓女起码都受过取悦之道的训练；名声总得维护。然后，她们可能还会涉猎某项专长，这从她们烙印的形状和颜色就能看出来……而像特洛纳里人那样，随随便便走进一座神殿，要求最近的神殿成员给你当个暖洞或者肉棒，那是没礼貌的人才干的事。” 他把话说得好像大多数神殿人员都不是随便能雇的，而事实恰恰相反。 “没错。像这里这位女主事出身的那种成熟神殿，有乐师、画师、清洁工、退休后给客人和小猫们做饭、照看他们的老妓女，还有照料病人的祭司，等等。神圣妓女其实只占神殿里相当小的一部分。” “如今……没有什么能拦住，比如说，像我这样云游的圣骑士自荐枕席，更不用说有些神殿人员可能愿意私下做点什么，换些人情、礼物之类的东西。但这类事通常是特殊安排，要通过女主事或大祭司谨慎地询问，而被问的人完全有权拒绝。这样就能对这件事给予特别的照料和关注，尤其是因为这并非那人的本职。” 嗯，凯特的神殿是你在贾西里特传统里唯一去过的一座，所以很不巧，你的印象有点偏。 尤斯拉点点头，冲你笑了笑。“当然，世界各地的人都在以自己的方式敬拜激情王子。不过，没错……这座神殿人不多，而要引起请愿者的兴趣，最容易的办法就是靠性。事情就是这样——我完全预计，随着更多人加入、女主事和大祭司更有能力充实这些殿堂，重心会逐渐转移。我猜有人会抱怨，说为了激起人们对高雅艺术的兴趣，竟得先迎合最底层的激情，但事情就是这样。从这个角度看，一座神殿里只有一位像阿米娜这样不会应要求献身的马拉克信徒，反倒才是这里的怪事。” ]
rows.raw: " [rand |"Ah, the temple's primary claim to not being just a whorehouse," Yusra says with a twinkle in his eye. "Ah, I kid, I kid. Even if she won't put herself out to be picked up, the girl's music is often the backdrop to which the sacred harlots work." It's... well... everyone works together to keep things running, you suppose. And her music? "Her music has the mark of the coast, from what I've heard of it. That region of Jassira which actually receives regular rain blown inland from the sea... a place where people don't have to worry that much about water. You can tell by how lively and energetic it is, how much influence there's been on that musical tradition from all kinds of peoples carried from all over the sea. Truly a breath of fresh air over the slow, meandering tunes of the more inland provinces, ha! "But yes! She's a reminder that temples aren't supposed to be all about sex, as easy as it might be to lean into that aspect of Mallach's passions for a new temple like this one is. Sex is an easy draw and money maker, but the temple matron and grand cleric at least remember their lessons well enough to at least try and attend to the other means of expressing one's passions. Painting and sculpture might be lost on the locals here, but I think anyone can appreciate a good tune." |"Yes, that's correct — if those two are indeed from the coastal regions of Jassira, then I can understand the desire to come all the way up here to the roof of the world, especially if Amina knew the temple matron. That part of our glorious nation is rather cutthroat, a side effect of the local mercantile culture, and that extends to the local Temple as well. Rising through the ranks on one's merit can be hard when vacancies are hard to come by and successors to any important jobs are often hand-picked and trained years or even decades before they'll hold the position...I can see the impetus to leave for proverbial greener pastures. "Sometimes it's not so bad to be a big fish in a small pond. It all depends on what kind of opportunities are around you — and for someone as talented and slightly unorthodox as Amina is in music, coming all the way here where her playing's more likely to be applauded as exotic and mystical rather than being booed for not being perfectly in line with the audience's tastes is certainly the right choice. Here, dear Amina can be who she wants to be and get applauded for it. Quite the no-brainer to make the trip, wouldn't you say?" |Most people think that Jassirites are all about catfolk, so to see Imad and Amina as Jassirite Mallachites is a little surprising. "That's a common misconception, really. Yes, the majority of Jassirites are indeed catfolk, but that's mostly because Jassira is the home of catfolk. Even so, that doesn't forbid other peoples from serving the Prince of Passion in that nation. If anything, Imad and Amina are simply amongst an outsized proportion of anubians in the Temple compared to how many there are amongst the population." Interesting. Is there a reason for this? "It's unfortunate — the antics of the spicetenders and by extent, the moneylenders and slave traders who are downstream from them are what give the anubians a bad name, but all of that people shoulder the burden while the true villains are much less reviled than they ought to be. It's a sticky situation and one that's persisted for a long, long time, partly because of the simple necessity of spice to the way of life over there, partly because of corruption, and partly because of the spicetenders' immense wealth. And all of those bring the matter to such a strong simmer that there are those anubians in the temple who seek some kind of respectability by serving the Prince of Passion and setting themselves apart from their more unscrupulous kin." [pc.isDK |Or at least, that's what they say. Yusra sighs and rubs his temples, but doesn't contradict you. "Cheerful [pc.mf |fellow |girl ], aren't you? That is... corruption exists everywhere, and while it can't be eradicated we do our best to keep it down. There are already enough jokes about the Temple and sultanate being literally incestuous; there're too many tongues wagging about the same thing happening with the Temple and the spicetenders." Hey, you didn't mention anything about anubians being plants in the temple — he just spilled that out of his own accord. "And most of them aren't," Yusra snaps, his cheerful demeanor gone. "There's no need to be contrary for the sake of it." Fine, if he would continue? |Does it work? "Somewhat. The primacy that Mallach holds over Jassira aside, even if they were servants of the other Seven, it's still seen as a noble calling. The two just about cancel each other out, I'd say. They may think differently, though." Anything else? ] "There's not much left to say. I expect it's just one of many reasons why brother and sister would leave Jassira to be with the temple matron; the roof of the world is about as different a place from Jassira as one can reasonably get. Both brother and sister want to be judged on their own merits, albeit in different ways... I can understand and approve of this desire." |"I rather enjoy Amina's playing. It uses traditional Jassiran music as a base, but has various other styles blended in, no doubt from what she's picked up by the port. The end result is familiar yet unique, delightful in its own way. I'm hoping it catches on more than it already us, truth be told." |Is it common for those who're part of a Jassirite-style temple to not be up for, uh, service, as Amina is? "Quite common, actually. Sacred harlots are, at a bare minimum, trained in the ways of pleasure; there's a reputation to uphold. Then, they may have a specialisation they dabble in, as evidenced by the shape and color of their brand... just wandering into a temple and asking for the nearest temple denizen to be a warm hole or prick is something rude people from Tronarii do." He makes it sound like instead of most temple staff being up for hire, the opposite is true. "That's right. An established temple like the one the matron here is from has musicians, artists, cleaners, retired harlots who cook and care for the guests and kittens, clerics who attend to the sick, and more. Sacred harlots would actually be a fairly small proportion of those in the temple. "Now... there's nothing stopping, say, a traveling paladin like me from offering myself, let alone some of the temple staff who might be willing to do something on the side for favors, gifts and the like. But such are usually special arrangements, discreetly inquired about through the matron or grand cleric, and the one being asked is perfectly within his or her right to refuse. That way special care and attention can be given to the matter, especially since it's not one's usual vocation." Well, Cait's temple is the only one you've ever been to in the Jassirite tradition, so things are unfortunately a little skewed. Yusra nods and flashes you a smile. "People around the world worship the Prince of Passion in their own way, of course. But yes... this temple doesn't have that many people around, and the easiest way to get petitioners interested is with the sex. It's just what it is — I fully expect that the focus will gradually shift as more join and the matron and grand cleric are better able to fill out these halls. I suppose that one might complain that it takes appealing to the base passions to drum up interest in the finer arts, but things are what they are. From that perspective, a temple having but a single Mallachite who doesn't put out on request like Amina does is actually the oddity here." ] "

rows.original: "Most certainly," Yusra replies. "After you tell me why exactly you'd like to know. I have a few guesses, of course, but I'd like to hear it from your mouth for the record." Cautious, isn't he? "Your reputation precedes you, [pc.name]; your deeds speak for themselves, so it's less a matter of caution and more one of understanding your angle. Please, if you don't mind." Well, you've been involved in this whole demon thing from the get-go, right when the portal opened up and spat Kasyrra out onto you. Given that you've already made your own inroads into the matter and are investigating the situation in Khor'minos right now while offering what aid you can, you want to know what Yusra's up to so that you won't get in each other's way and perhaps might even be able to help each other in your endeavors. There's also the matter of Cait, of course. She didn't leave the Temple on the best of terms, and here comes along someone to... well, you don't know anything yet, but it's best to be on the lookout. If nothing else, you do wonder what will happen when the main host of Mallachites does finally arrive in the Marches. Yusra doesn't look offended in the least by this statement. "Well, at least you're honest and unafraid to speak your mind. Although if I were someone who intended the temple matron harm, telling me that to my face would be counterproductive, wouldn't it?" Or a warning to not try anything funny. "Indeed. Well, given that you're the adventuring sort, I think you might be able to help with some of these. "First and foremost, I'll need to get together the supplies needed to base an army out of this temple — there's no way a supply train is going to be stretching all the way from Jassira to here. As resourceful as the grand cleric may be, tens of thousands of holy warriors and their camp followers descending upon this land is going to cause some problems with the local logistics; the temple and its environs may be suited to housing them, but they need more than that. Securing provisioning will primarily fall to Salwah, but if you could help her in any way, that'd be appreciated. "Secondly, I'm here to gain information about the enemy we face. The Prince of Passions himself has briefed the leaders of the host what he and the other divines know about this new threat the world faces, but that's still painfully little to form a coherent strategy on. I'll need to come up with some ideas to learn more about the enemy, and relay that back to the host." How will he do that, if they're so far apart? "The same way I was informed of my new assignment: we met up in our lord's dream and exchanged pleasantries." Your memories are drawn back to your sojourn in Mallach's palace and the garden party in particular. The mess of clerics, paladins and other religous notables all engaged in one massive orgy of sex, drugs and other pleasures... guess that gathering isn't just for indulging oneself in a massive fit of hedonism. "Anything material will be delivered by... other means I can't disclose, provided it's not too large, but I don't think it'll come to that," Yusra continues, too lost in his own thoughts to notice yours. "And finally, I'll need to inform the religious groups whose gods have primacy in the region of our intended arrival, as late to the party as we will be. Doubtlessly they'll be informed through other means, but still, formally declaring one's intent can't hurt." His goals are relevant, but quite vague. You take it that he has a lot of autonomy to do as he pleases, then? Given that there are so many unknowns about the threat, the only reasonable thing to do would be to give Yusra as free a hand as possible, until he has some leads to go off on. He is supposed to be a scout, after all. "That I am, and that I'll be doing. I'll need a while to assess the situation, talk to the temple matron and to the locals in the village below, then plan a course of action. If you're still interested in lending a hand, talk to me about the matter when the both of us are ready."
rows.translation: 当然可以，”尤斯拉回答道，“不过在你告诉我你究竟为什么想知道这个之前，我先有一些猜测。不过，我还是想亲耳听你讲出来，以便把你的说法记录下来。” 他真是很谨慎啊…… “你的名声早已远播四方了[pc.name]；你的行为已经说明了一切，所以现在的问题不在于谨慎行事，而在于理解你的立场。如果你不介意的话，请吧。” 嗯，从一开始你就参与了这件事，对吧？从那个传送门打开，把卡希拉带到你面前的那一刻起，你就已经卷入了其中。既然你已经在这一问题上采取了一些行动，目前正在调查科尔米诺斯的局势，并尽你所能提供帮助，那么你自然想知道尤斯拉在忙些什么，这样你们就不会互相干扰，甚至还有可能在各自的努力中互相帮助。 当然，还有凯特这个家伙。她离开神殿的时候关系并不太好，而现在又出现了一个人……嗯，你懂我的意思吧。知道目前还没有什么新的进展，但最好还是保持警惕。不管怎样，人们确实很好奇：当马拉克信徒们的主要首领最终来到边境地区时，会发生什么呢？ 尤斯拉对此话丝毫没有感到被冒犯。“嗯，至少你很诚实，也不害怕说出自己的想法。不过，如果我是那些想要伤害神庙女祭司的人，直接当面跟我说这样的话，反而会适得其反，不是吗？ 或者，这也是一个警告，提醒大家不要尝试任何奇怪的事情。 “确实如此。不过，既然你是个喜欢冒险的人，我想你或许能够帮助解决其中的一些问题。 “首先，我需要收集一些必要的物资，以便在这座寺庙里建立一支军队——毕竟，不可能有一条补给车队从贾西拉一直延伸到这里啊。尽管这位大祭司足智多谋，但成千上万的圣战士及其随从涌入这片土地，无疑会给当地的物流带来诸多麻烦；虽然神庙及其周边地区足以容纳他们，但他们所需要的远不止这些。确保各项配置工作的顺利进行主要将由萨尔瓦负责，但如果你能在任何方面帮助她，那将非常感谢。 其次，我来这里是为了收集关于我们所面对的敌人的信息。‘情感之王’本人已经向军队的领导们介绍了他和其他神明们所了解的关于这一新出现的威胁的情报，但这些信息仍然远远不够，我们无法据此制定出有效的战略。我需要想出一些办法来进一步了解敌人，然后把这些信息传达给军队。 他们相隔那么远，他要怎么做到呢？ “就像我得知自己新任务的那次一样：我们在领主的梦境中相遇，互相寒暄了几句。” 你的记忆被带回了你在马拉克宫殿里的那段时光，尤其是那场花园派对。那些神职人员、圣骑士以及其他宗教要人，全都参与了一场疯狂的性爱、毒品和其他享乐活动的狂欢……看来，那场聚会确实不是一般意义上的聚会啊只是任何实物都会通过……一些我不能透露的其他方式送达，只要物品不是太大就行。不过我觉得应该不会用到那种方法吧，”尤斯拉继续说道，他完全沉浸在自己的思绪中，根本没有注意到你在想什么。最后，我还需要通知那些在该地区拥有至高无上地位的宗教团体，告知我们即将抵达的消息。虽然我们来得有点晚，但毫无疑问，他们也会通过其他途径得到这个消息。不过，正式地宣布自己的意图总没有坏处。他的目标确实很重要，但同时也相当模糊。那么，你可以认为他有很大的自主权，可以随心所欲地行动吧？鉴于目前对于这种威胁还存在许多未知因素，最合理的做法就是尽可能给予尤斯拉自由发挥的空间，直到他获得一些可以进一步行动的线索为止。他是毕竟，我本应该是一名侦察员的。 “我确实是，也会继续履行这个职责。我需要一些时间来评估当前的情况，与寺庙的负责人以及下面村庄的当地人进行沟通，然后才能制定出行动方案。如果你仍然愿意帮忙的话，等我们双方都准备好了，再跟我讨论这件事吧。

rows.original: No sooner have the words left your mouth that Yusra's smile widens, and the bratty catboy's eyes glint. No doubt he's been asked this question many times before, and is more than willing to tell the tale. Still, one has to go through the motions, and it's something that he obviously takes great delight in. "Why, is it strange to see a Mallachite with one of these? It is a kink some have, you know, enough that some come to the temple to ask for it specifically." Well, these cages have been used as... unorthodox punishments before. You personally know someone who [etheryn.isCaged |has |had ] the misfortune to be stuck in such a situation, caught in such a cage imposed by an abusive sister. That certainly isn't what Yusra was expecting — his smile vanishes, replaced by a look of serious consternation as he curls his tail around and fiddles with it. "Unfortunate, and my commiserations for your friend. That being said, my situation is nowhere near as distasteful." You motion for him to go on. "I put this on voluntarily — it's more akin to one of those vows of silence that Narevans take, where they don't say a word for as long as the vow lasts. So's the same thing here — I simply undertook a vow of sorts to not receive pleasure through my prick until the end of this year or more, then I can choose whether to continue or have it removed." Why, though? "Have you heard the saying, 'absence makes the heart grow fonder'?" Yes... "That's the long and short of it; you can ask me about the theology separately if you're that interested. I guess it also helped me wind up picked for this scouting assignment, since someone probably figured that the demons wouldn't be getting to my balls or something if I had them covered up. Too many Tronariian romances for those folks, I think — their women sometimes actually put on chastity belts in the rural areas to avoid getting raped by marauding orcs and centaurs. I don't really think it helps, to be honest; nevertheless, there're enough stores about demonic spawn that I guess they decided better safe than sorry." So long story short, no usage of his kitty-prick for him. Is that right? "Yes and no. I'm supposed to be depriving myself with my vow, not others, so there's a ghostlight attached to the cage should I need it." Yusra rolls his eyes, grins, and shakes his head. "That's temple logic for you, and in a way it makes sense. Just because I want to restrain my own passions doesn't mean others have to join me. The clerics who enchanted this thing knew what they were doing — as far as I can tell, it handles the motions just as if I weren't wearing anything, so don't worry about it." So, can he take off his chastity cage if he wanted to, or does he have to go somewhere special to have it removed? "The latter would be more in the spirit of the thing, and that's what I originally opted for. Then again, unforeseen circumstances can crop up in my line of work as opposed to that of a comfort boy, so I got denied for that; I do know how to remove it if necessary. If necessary is the key phrase here — holy vows are made to be kept, and if I do so I'd better have a really good reason." Or else? He nods and sticks his tongue out at you. "Or else. Not saying any more, holy vows are kind of a touchy subject, if you don't mind." Well, fine, if he's going to be that way. Maybe you can talk about something else. [party.has cait |"Hey, lighten up, you two," Cait says, playfully elbowing the both of you in turn. "There's no need to get grumpy with each other — [pc.name], there's no need to push Yusra, and Yusra, [pc.name] was clearly ribbing you, so there's no need to get all bratty and pouty about it.
